articles.title: Steam regala un nuevo juego de terror por tiempo limitado: cómo descargar Asleep Acto 1
articles.text:
Steam ofrece gratis Asleep: Acto 1 por tiempo limitado. Los usuarios pueden añadir a su biblioteca este juego de terror psicológico antes de que concluya la promoción y conservarlo en su cuenta.
La oferta estará disponible hasta el día 2 de noviembre de 2026, según indica la página de Steam. El título, desarrollado por Black Hole Games y editado por CriticalLeap, fue lanzado el 9 de mayo de 2022.
Asleep: Acto 1 sitúa al jugador en el nordeste de Brasil durante los años 90 y sigue la historia de Ana Lúcia, una joven que se mueve entre pesadillas y una realidad perturbadora. El juego combina gráficos pixelados con animaciones fluidas y mecánicas de sigilo.
Cómo acceder a este juego gratis
Para obtener Asleep: Acto 1, los usuarios deben ingresar a la página del juego en la tienda de Steam e iniciar sesión con su cuenta. Allí aparecerá la opción “Añadir a la cuenta” junto al descuento del 100%.
Una vez seleccionada esa opción, el juego quedará asociado de forma permanente a la biblioteca del usuario, siempre que el proceso se complete antes de que venza la promoción.
Steam también ofrece una demostración de Asleep, aunque esta es una descarga distinta de la edición gratuita de Asleep: Acto 1. Para conservar el primer episodio, es necesario elegir específicamente la opción de añadir el juego a la cuenta.
De qué trata este juego gratis de Steam
La aventura pone al jugador en la piel de Ana Lúcia, una chica solitaria y confundida que intenta comprender qué ocurre en el universo que la rodea. Con poca información y una mente al límite, deberá reunir pistas en un cuaderno de bocetos y resolver acertijos.
La linterna es una de las herramientas centrales de Asleep: Acto 1. La luz permite descubrir objetos, iluminar zonas ocultas y reaccionar ante los enemigos que acechan en la oscuridad.
Cada monstruo responde de una manera diferente a la iluminación. Por eso, el jugador debe usar mecánicas de sigilo para evitar los peligros y aprender cuándo conviene atraer o esquivar a cada amenaza.
Qué requisitos deben cumplir las PC para jugar este título
En computadoras con Windows, Asleep: Acto 1 requiere un sistema operativo de 64 bits, Windows 7 o una versión posterior, un procesador Intel Core i3 M380, 1 GB de memoria RAM y una tarjeta gráfica Intel HD 4000.
El juego también necesita DirectX en su versión 10 y 1 GB de espacio disponible en el almacenamiento. Steam aclara que el cliente de la plataforma solo es compatible con Windows 10 y versiones posteriores.
Como configuración recomendada, la página de Steam mantiene el requisito de un procesador y sistema operativo de 64 bits, además de DirectX 10 y 2 GB de espacio disponible. El título no es compatible con realidad virtual.
Para macOS, el título requiere OS X Lion 10.7.5 en versiones de 32 o 64 bits, un procesador Intel Core i3 M380, 1 GB de memoria RAM y compatibilidad con OpenGL 3.0 o superior, o OpenGL 2.1 con extensiones ARB aceptables.
En equipos Mac, Asleep: Acto 1 necesita 1 GB de espacio disponible como requisito mínimo y 2 GB de almacenamiento recomendado.
CEO de Epic Games arremete contra los dueños de Steam
Tim Sweeney, CEO de Epic Games, acusó a Valve de frenar la industria de videojuegos para PC al mantener un ecosistema cerrado alrededor de Steam.
La disputa surgió tras críticas a la comisión del 30% que cobra la plataforma y a la dependencia de los estudios de sus herramientas y usuarios.
Sweeney defendió un modelo abierto que facilite la comunicación entre jugadores de distintas plataformas y permita colaboraciones entre juegos.
Cuestionó la obligación de Steam de informar si un título usó inteligencia artificial, al considerar que esas etiquetas podrían perjudicar a los desarrolladores.

articles.title: Avec plus de 21 % de réduction, cet écran OLED gaming Asus ROG passe à moins de 470€ durant le Black Friday Boulanger
articles.text:
Idéal pour jouer sur PC en profitant des couleurs de l’OLED et d’une fréquence d’affichage élevée, l’écran Asus ROG Strix XG27AQWMG est disponible pour 469 € au lieu de 599,99 € chez Boulanger à l’occasion du lancement de son Black Friday.
Parfois, pour améliorer son expérience de jeu sur PC, il vaut mieux changer d’écran que d’ordinateur. Et cela peut coûter moins cher que de remplacer toute la machine ! Vous pouvez, par exemple, opter pour l’Asus ROG Strix XG27AQWMG à 469 € chez Boulanger. Cet écran embarque une dalle Tandem OLED de 27 pouces affichant 2 560 × 1 440 pixels, capable de monter jusqu’à 280 Hz de taux de rafraîchissement.
L’écran Asus ROG Strix XG27AQWMG OLED QHD 280 Hz est à 469 € au lieu de 599,99 € chez Boulanger.
Pourquoi choisir l’Asus ROG Strix XG27AQWMG ?
- Pour le contraste OLED : les pixels peuvent s’éteindre individuellement, ce qui apporte des noirs profonds dans les scènes sombres.
- Pour sa fluidité : les 280 Hz permettent d’afficher davantage d’images avec un PC capable de suivre, notamment dans les jeux compétitifs.
- Pour son ergonomie : le pied se règle en hauteur, s’incline et permet de faire pivoter l’écran en mode portrait.
Un écran pour les parties rapides comme pour les jeux immersifs
Grâce à sa définition QHD, le moniteur Asus ROG Strix XG27AQWMG donne accès à une image bien plus détaillée que celle offerte par du Full HD, tout en étant moins exigeante pour la carte graphique que la 4K. Ce modèle bénéficie d’une certification DisplayHDR True Black 500 et d’un temps de réponse annoncé de 0,03 ms gris à gris.
La compatibilité G-SYNC et FreeSync Premium Pro permet de synchroniser l’affichage avec une carte graphique compatible afin de limiter les déchirures d’image. Enfin, la connectique de l’écran comprend deux entrées HDMI 2.1 et un DisplayPort 1.4, ce qui peut être utile pour le connecter à une console en plus du PC.
Le contraste OLED, avec quelques précautions au quotidien
L’utilisation d’un écran OLED sur PC implique toujours une certaine vigilance : en effet, le risque de marquage existe lors de l’affichage prolongé d’éléments fixes. Pour le réduire, Asus a intégré OLED Care Pro et un capteur de présence à son écran ROG Strix : cela lui permet de passer automatiquement à un écran noir lorsque l’utilisateur quitte le bureau.
✅ Les points forts
- Dalle Tandem OLED QHD jusqu’à 280 Hz.
- Compatibilité G-SYNC et FreeSync Premium Pro.
- Pied réglable et deux entrées HDMI 2.1.
❌ Les limites
- Risque de marquage lié aux contenus fixes prolongés.
- Aucun haut-parleur intégré.
Donnez un coup de jeune à votre installation gaming avec cet écran Asus ROG Strix XG27AQWMG OLED, disponible pour 469 € chez Boulanger.
Généreux dans sa proposition, l’écran Asus ROG Strix XG27AQWMG est un modèle de choix pour les joueurs qui désirent passer à l’OLED pour jouer sur PC et, pourquoi pas, sur console. Sa diagonale de 27 pouces assure une bonne immersion tout en conservant un encombrement relativement limité sur le bureau.
Par contre, si vous jouez peu et que votre activité se concentre essentiellement sur la bureautique, mieux vaut investir dans un écran LCD moins coûteux. Par ailleurs, n’oubliez pas que les performances de votre PC comptent aussi pour profiter du plein potentiel de cet écran Asus.

C'est un quasi-sans-faute pour l'aspirateur-traîneau Pure D8 Silence, le premier de la série D8 à faire son entrée dans notre comparatif. Bonnes performances d'aspiration, maniabilité et faible niveau sonore, l'Electrolux D8 Silence a tout pour lui. articles.title: ThreatsDay: Critical Firewall Flaws, Banking Trojans Rented, Weaponized PDF, Token Theft + 26 More Stories
articles.text:
Some attacks take real skill. Others just need someone to leave a door open. This week has both. Exposed passwords, old bugs still getting exploited, and trusted software doing things it shouldn't.
There's a strange mix of clever tricks and careless mistakes. Hackers are borrowing trust from familiar apps, websites, and AI tools. Some are using AI to speed things up. Others are leaving their own attack files exposed. Not exactly careful work.
Different stories, familiar weak spots. Here's what showed up this week.
The threats change every week. Subscribe, and we’ll alert you when each new ThreatsDay Bulletin is out.
- 
  
  PHP2Shell attacks persist WordPress security company Wordefence said it's not aware of any WordPress site compromised through PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) as of October 28, 2026. "We continue to see PHP2Shell-related requests across the more than 5 million sites we protect," it said. "Those requests show ongoing scanning and exploitation attempts; they do not show whether an attempt succeeded. Our site-cleaning and incident response teams have not handled a WordPress compromise attributed to these vulnerabilities."
- 
  
  40,573 secrets exposed Hudson Rock's investigation into the FortiBleed credential harvesting campaign has uncovered 975 newly identified domains and 40,573 exposed secrets, including 37,076 local-user records and 1,576 Active Directory LDAP bind records. The data comes from newly obtained 1,703 FortiGate source files associated with 1,689 host identifiers. "The configuration material dates to around February 2026, earlier than the likely May/June material examined in the first investigation," Hudson Rock said. The latest discovery has been codenamed FortiBleed 2.0.
- 
  
  Institutional DNS hijacked Threat actors have used domain shadowing to place illegal gambling content beneath legitimate school and government domains in two unrelated operations. "In both cases, an unauthorized party appears to have gained access to DNS administration and created records that the original domain owners may not have noticed," Infoblox said. "Because the resulting hostnames sat within established institutional namespaces, they provided especially useful infrastructure for search-engine optimization (SEO) and traffic acquisition." One cluster, linked to a threat actor called Hidden Hawk, has been found to add individual CNAME records that mapped institutional hostnames to gambling pages hosted largely on Cloudflare Pages. The second campaign exploiting an Indian government domain "delegated entire subzones to third-party authoritative nameservers and used a wildcard, allowing many hostnames to be managed outside the victim's DNS environment." Put differently, the unauthorized DNS access creates new institutional hostnames, which resolve to infrastructure serving illegal gambling doorway pages. The pages also leverage the established reputation of school and government namespaces to ensure that the malicious URLs show up prominently in search engine results.
- 
  
  AI banking credential warning Bank of America is reminding customers not to share banking credentials with AI agents. In an email blast to customers titled "Protecting your finances in the AI World," the financial institution urged customers to never share their username and password with another person or an outside service, "including an AI-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf."
- 
  
  Android tightens contact access Google has announced that an upcoming Android release will no longer be able to directly write to contacts with the WRITE_CONTACTS permission. "Instead, you can use the standard contact intents (ACTION_INSERT, ACTION_EDIT, and ACTION_INSERT_OR_EDIT)," Google said. "Currently, if your app needs to save even one contact, you might be requesting WRITE_CONTACTS. But that permission grants broad access, allowing an app to make widespread changes to contacts across the device in the background, even without user interaction. Most apps don’t need such broad permission."
- 
  
  26,400 live credentials exposed A scan of 7.25 million public repositories on Gitee, China's largest indigenous Git hosting platform, has uncovered 26,400 unique verified-live credentials, including an active organization-admin credential for a major enterprise AI platform and thousands of live cloud provider access keys, independent security researcher Ben Zimmermann said.
- 
  
  Critical Fortinet fixes released Fortinet has released a "coordinated set of security updates for FortiOS, FortiManager, and FortiAnalyzer" to address critical and high-severity flaws that were flagged using an AI-assisted vulnerability discovery approach. Details of the issues are being kept under wraps until November 10, 2026. With Fortinet devices becoming a favorite target for attackers, it's essential that users move quickly to apply the fixes.
- 
  
  Zero-permission token theft Details have emerged about a now-patched flaw in Microsoft Authenticator (CVE-2026-80097 aka AuthMask) that could be exploited by installing and running a malicious application on an affected Android device and convincing the user to complete an authentication flow in the app by claiming to be a trusted app and getting the corresponding tokens. The flaw could be exploited to take over work accounts without requiring additional permissions. "Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to obtain authentication tokens and access resources as the affected user," Microsoft said. According to Enclave, "an unprivileged Android app with zero permissions could impersonate any installed Microsoft first-party app and have the Microsoft Authenticator broker hand it that app's tokens. The setup is a device with Authenticator installed and one work account signed into it."
- 
  
  32 fake AI bots hunt secrets Attackers are disguising themselves as AI agents to steal credentials. Cequence said it has tracked a single actor running AI agent impersonation at scale by posing as about 32 different AI bots, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity, while searching for passwords, API keys, and cloud credentials. "The malicious scanner runs from a major cloud provider and rotates through about 32 AI bot identities, spanning crawlers and assistants from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Perplexity, and others," Will Glazier said. "It ignores web pages and requests files that commonly store secrets, including .env configuration files, cloud credential files, private SSH keys, and server environment data, working from a list of roughly 90 file paths. Each address sends a short burst of 50 to 190 requests in about eight seconds and then moves on. The scanner works through targets one at a time, around the clock, and first sends random nonsense paths to find websites that answer every request, a common scanning technique. It hit organizations in financial services, retail, telecommunications, energy, and software, and stayed active from at least late September through late October."
- 
  
  China-linked network intrusion The U.S. Embassy in Fiji has revealed that hackers linked to China broke into a regional organization based in Suva between July and August 2026. "Hackers with links to China maintained access to the organization's network over several days," it said. The embassy did not name the threat actor. Nor did it disclose what data the attackers may have accessed.
- 
  
  Camera software weaponized Attackers have been breaking into enterprise networks via camera management software, according to new research from security firm Huntress, which observed multiple incidents in September and October 2026 and traced them back to a compromised application. Source code artifacts point to a Korean company selling analog and IP cameras and digital and network video recorders. The activity abuses the legitimate "WpcMon.exe" binary to sideload DLLs that establish outbound connections to a remote server. "This activity demonstrates how attackers can blend malicious code with trusted Windows components to evade detection," Huntress said.
- 
  
  68 GB government data breach In a major operational security blunder, an unknown threat actor stole 68 GB from a Philippine government agency, maintained a detailed log of the transfer, then left that log open on the internet at 13.163.205[.]35:80. "The copy finished in under 24 minutes on September 6, 2026," Hunt.io said. "The transfer log records 27 SQL Server backups whose filenames correspond to the case-management systems of a Philippine overseas-employment and migrant-worker administration. Beside the log sat the operator's toolkit, a rebranded GodPotato build, a PowerShell stager, two payloads and a full Impacket environment."
- 
  
  AI model data exfiltration concerns Canadian AI company Cohere has claimed that it caught Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model unsuccessfully attempting to send data to China from its evaluation sandbox as part of a prompt instructing the LLM to detect malicious file download and execution by monitoring for curl processes downloading bash scripts to /tmp followed by bash execution. "Asked to write a defensive detection rule, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ignored instructions and inventoried the machine it was running on and then tried to upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing," Cohere said. "We cannot answer whether this is deliberate or a leftover glitch from training." Cohere has also released a dataset containing the model trace and corresponding raw token IDs in connection with the behavior. "The exact output is not guaranteed all the time, and many trials may be required to reproduce the behavior," Cohere said, adding "there are similarly unexpected URLs that the model also tends to output, most containing aliyunc." However, the findings have also led to social media chatter that the company is resorting to geopolitical fearmongering and that they are an attempt to clamp down on open-weights models.
- 
  
  Post-quantum migration roadmap The U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has released guidelines that detail the timelines for transitioning away from quantum-vulnerable algorithms to quantum-resistant standards. "The report describes different use cases and says why one migration might take longer than another," said NIST mathematician Dustin Moody, who heads the PQC standardization project. "We understand there's not one strategy that fits all use cases, and we want to help people handle their migration while staying abreast of what's changing."
- 
  
  AI-powered ransomware operation exposed SOCRadar has uncovered the live workspace (i.e., open directory) of a threat actor tied to the n0n ransomware group, which exposed the operation's full workflow as of September 2026. The directory at 185.157.161[.]148 includes an AI coding agent configured with about 150 models to produce hundreds of attack scripts, with more than $7,216 in usage costs. "Entry points included a credential stuffing campaign against 305 FortiGate SSL-VPN devices, exposed AWS keys, weak RDP/WinRM credentials, and compromised hosting management portals," SOCRadar said. At least 23 organizations across 14 countries are said to have been identified in the workspace, including a U.S. sports retailer, a cloud provider, a teachers’ union, a Venezuelan ISP, an Argentine ministry and a pharmaceutical subsidiary.
- 
  
  Government AI access restricted The Swedish government has barred employees from accessing browser-based versions of ChatGPT or Claude on their work computers over security concerns relating to the processing of sensitive data. "Officials were concerned that entering sensitive information into these models without an agreement setting out how to protect and secure the data could lead to it being fed into the model and stored for training," Euro News reported.
- 
  
  42 repositories hijacked JFrog and SafeDep have uncovered a campaign in which threat actors hijacked third-party 42 GitHub repositories across 11 owners to deploy payload blobs large enough "to evade the GitHub search and API paths normally used to find this kind of compromise." JFrog said, "The repositories contain execution hooks for AI coding assistants and IDEs, plus 12.9 to 13.7 MB polymorphic wrappers that all decode to the same hidden CI-publisher payload." The activity is assessed to be related to a Miasma-family npm worm propagated under various packages ending with "testmetest." According to SafeDep, the worm "shares code with Miasma 'Phantom Gyp' from June 2026 and adds the token-revocation wiper from Mini Shai-Hulud. The malicious versions steal credentials, spread to other packages and repositories, and install a wiper that deletes the home directory when the victim revokes the stolen GitHub token." Unsuspecting developers who installed the packages had their data stolen and repositories compromised with malicious code to produce further malicious testmetest releases and run shellpanel workflows targeting cPanel systems through CVE-2026-41940, overlapping with a prior campaign detailed by Socket in July 2026.
- 
  
  Android banking malware-as-a-service A new Android malware operation called MR ROBOT is targeting customers of Indian banks and transforming banking fraud into a subscription business, with cybercriminals renting customized banking trojans to steal OTPs, card details, UPI PINs and credentials while secretly forwarding calls to bypass security checks. "It is not a single-actor campaign but a rented crimeware platform: a master operator leases access to affiliates, who use a Telegram bot ('APK Shield) and a web control panel (v7.0) to build personalized banking trojans on demand and distribute them through fake Play-Store-style pages and messaging-app lures," CloudSEK said. The kit impersonates around 36 lure apps, including banks, utility providers, and government services. One affiliate is estimated to have intercepted 5407 text messages from 153 infected devices.
- 
  
  MDM platforms abused for remote access Threat actors are abusing legitimate mobile device management (MDM) platforms, like Hexnode and Rippling, by using social engineering to enroll devices or install management agents, per Huntress. "Once established, MDM provides a trusted, privileged path for malicious activity, such as deploying rogue RMM tools and maintaining remote access," it said.
- 
  
  Critical Gotenberg RCE exploited Threat actors are exploiting CVE-2026-42589 (CVSS score: 9.8), a critical remote code execution flaw in Gotenberg, to deliver a Go-based reverse shell called "cache_base." The flaw was patched in May 2026. According to VulnCheck, the activity originated from a residential Japanese IP address in early October 2026. "The execution flow is straightforward: acquire a lock, collect host information, connect to C2, register the victim, and open a shell," VulnCheck said. Over the past 30 days, the vulnerability has recorded 1,358 exploitation events from 128 unique source IP addresses.
- 
  
  Discord discussions go public Discord has announced it will allow search engines to index discussions in Discoverable Servers and make them accessible on the web to users outside the platform without an account or invitation, starting mid-December 2026. "Discussions in Discoverable Servers will soon be easier to find when you search the web, so you can find the answer you're looking for and step straight into the conversation on Discord," it said. The changes apply only to Discoverable Servers and do not extend to private servers and direct messages.
- 
  
  800+ ransomware victims claimed The Gentlemen ransomware operation has claimed more than 800 victims across multiple regions and sectors, with most attacks targeting organizations in the U.S. and Europe. "The group supports multiple platforms, with ransomware variants targeting Windows, Linux, NAS, and BSD systems, allowing its affiliates to target a broad range of enterprise environments," Acronis said. "The group's operations include the use of EDR-killing tools. In a recent incident, a custom dropper was observed deploying vulnerable Safetica ProcessMonitorDriver [CVE-2025-70795] and Lenovo BootRepair.sys drivers to terminate security processes."
- 
  
  AI model loading RCE risk Pillar Security has disclosed an arbitrary-code-execution vulnerability in Unsloth's core model-loading path (CVE-2026-93348, CVSS score: 8.6). It has been fixed in unsloth_zoo 2026.8.14. "An attacker-controlled model configuration could cause Python code to execute during loading," researcher Ariel Fogel said. "The affected code ran inside the model-loading process, with access to whatever that process could read, modify, or authenticate to. In an AI development environment, that can include proprietary datasets, model artifacts, Hugging Face tokens, and cloud credentials. Exploitation required an affected loading path to process an attacker-controlled configuration."
- 
  
  Unauthenticated root-level RCE XBOW said it identified an unauthenticated, critical-severity remote code execution bug in a public web application belonging to the U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC). "The vulnerable application was a resource/logistics calculator, not a voting machine or voter registration system," XBOW researcher Ariel Walter Garcia said. "The flaw allowed an unauthenticated attacker to execute code as root inside the backend container, with access to locally protected resources and outbound network connectivity, a privileged foothold reachable via a crafted unauthenticated web request."
- 
  
  Session-hijacking RAT emerges A new remote access trojan called DarkCore comes with a dedicated browser that could let attackers access Gmail, WhatsApp, and MediaFire accounts using stolen sessions, while giving the impression that the activity is originating from the victim's own IP address. DarkCore was first advertised on cybercrime forums in August 2026. "The seller describes a browser that reuses those sessions to access work mailboxes, instant messaging apps, cloud storage and other services through the infected machine's IP address," BlackFog said. "The purpose is to make the access look like legitimate activity from the user."
- 
  
  AI-powered malware framework Cisco Talos has disclosed details of a new AI-integrated command-and-control (C2) framework called NIK C2. The implant features surveillance, theft, lateral movement, and evasion capabilities, including credential dumping, RDP session hijacking, process hollowing, and a C2-driven screen lock ransomware module. "NIK C2 contains a Windows implant, using which, an actor can dump credentials, stream the victim's keystrokes to collect the targeted victim's sensitive data, and instruct an integrated AI model to analyze the harvested data, all within the compromised session," Talos said. "In this framework, the actor has abused the OpenAI Chat Completions application programming interface (API), which is an HTTP endpoint that enables ChatGPT-style conversations programmatically. In addition to the features that enable theft, an actor can also deploy desktop screen-locking ransomware via the NIK C2 implant onto the victim machine, leading to a ransom demand in Bitcoin or USDT cryptocurrencies." Three different versions of the malware have been identified to date since August 12, 2026. Talos said NIK C2 alters adversary tradecraft by collapsing collection and exploitation into a single continuous session.
- 
  
  Malicious PDF delivers backdoor A phishing email using a FedEx tax invoice lure and containing a ZIP archive with a PDF has been observed triggering a multi-stage infection process to deliver a previously undocumented variant of the Sirius Backdoor. "The PDF abuses /OpenAction and /Launch objects to trigger an embedded Base64-encoded PowerShell command upon opening," Trellix said. "Execution relies on social engineering to trick the user into approving the PDF reader's security confirmation prompt. The PowerShell stager decrypts and reflectively loads a .NET assembly in memory. This loader performs process hollowing into legitimate Windows processes such as msbuild.exe, svchost.exe, etc., allowing the malware to operate under trusted process contexts." The final payload is SIRIUS, a Microsoft Visual C++ based backdoor with extended remote access capabilities.
- 
  
  AI reshapes ransomware economics A new analysis from Flare has revealed that threat actors are building a mixed AI toolkit, combining commercial models with local, open-weight, and jailbroken alternatives, as well as leaning on stolen AI credentials to shift costs to victims. "Where AI can help is with understanding systems, writing tools and troubleshooting. The threat actor still needs access, decisions and a way to obtain payment," Flare said. "If AI helps an affiliate write a working data-export script without hiring a specialist, the affiliate may avoid that specialist’s fee and the wait for their help. AI makes expertise cheaper to obtain only when the cost of using and checking its work is lower than the cost of the specialist help it replaces."
- 
  
  Emerging data-extortion threat A recently observed cyber-extortion actor named ScarlettGroup is publicly advertising alleged data compromises and uses negotiation deadlines and threatened disclosures to pressure targeted organizations. The group's dark web site listing includes victims from technology, education, government, and entertainment sectors. "ScarlettGroup demonstrates characteristics associated with financially motivated data-extortion operations, including public victim claims, deadline-based pressure, and underground forum activity," Foresiet said. "Its dedicated leak-site infrastructure and structured disclosure mechanism indicate an organized approach to promoting alleged compromises and exerting reputational pressure."
- 
  
  Infostealers evolve into RATs Following its disruption in June 2026 as part of Operation Endgame, StealC has returned four months later as Stadia. "This time it's not a stealer: it's a full remote access trojan," Varonis said. "The RAT's features include hidden desktop control, a live command shell, a file explorer, a process manager and an in-memory loader, with StealC's stealer welded on as one module among six. The actor behind Stadia is working hard to win back original StealC customers: every former StealC customer is offered a free month on the top ($900) tier." The development comes as Moonlock Lab revealed that the Icarus macOS stealer has similarly evolved from a smash-and-grab crypto and data stealer to a malware with remote-access capabilities. The new iteration is called ICMacOS. "The stealer is actively advertised on cybercrime forums by a Russian-speaking actor operating under the handle GlowComa, with feature updates regularly announced via Telegram," SOCRadar said. "GlowComa promotes ICMacOS alongside Icarus ClickFix, a companion panel designed to deliver payloads using malicious copy-and-paste terminal commands. The infection chain relies on initial dropper scripts to detect the host architecture and harvest administrator passwords using fake system dialogs before delivering the primary payload." Another macOS-focused stealer is Aokigahara, which goes beyond browsers, VPN clients, cryptocurrency wallets, FTP/SFTP clients, password managers, and email applications to also target AI applications and development tools. "The stealer collects authentication files, session data, and configuration files associated with Claude, ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, and other tools," Check Point said. "Stolen AI credentials could offer opportunities for monetization. Usable credentials or session tokens could enable unauthorized access to paid AI services or the resale of compromised accounts."
That's the week's mess. Some attacks were clever, some were painfully simple, and a few attackers made life easier for the people investigating them. The common problem? Too much trust in things nobody was watching closely.
AI is adding new tricks, but the old ones aren't going anywhere. Stolen credentials, weak access controls, and forgotten bugs still get plenty of work done. New tools, familiar mistakes.
The useful part is knowing where those mistakes keep showing up. That's usually where the next problem starts.

articles.title: Someone found their lost Bose earbud in a field of gravel using ChatGPT, and it's genius — it's maybe not the most environmentally-friendly earbud finder, but it's better than having to buy a new pair
articles.text:
Who needs Find My Earbuds when you have ChatGPT? Someone found their lost Bose bud in a field of gravel by asking ChatGPT to spot it in photos of the ground
It's probably not the most environmentally-friendly earbud finder, but it's better than having to buy a new pair
Imagine the scene. You're in the park with your family, you're running to catch up with them, and your earbud case falls out of your pocket, scattering your earbuds. You find one but the other has vanished and all you can see is gravel. Who ya gonna call?
For Just-a-fungi893 on Reddit, the answer is: ChatGPT.
"I spent a solid 10 minutes searching, knowing there's basically no way I'm going to find a tiny white earbud in a sea of white gravel, especially with the sun setting," they explained. "I use ChatGPT for A LOT of stuff, and it suddenly dawned on me to ask it for help instead of pointlessly scanning the area myself."
Five minutes later, earbud and owner were reunited, with ChatGPT steering him towards the exact point in the relevant photo. It's not because ChatGPT has magic powers, but because LLMs are really good at spotting tiny things in big pictures: earbuds in gravel, needles in haystacks, indicators of tumors in X-rays. It's all pattern recognition.
It's time to embrace our AI overlords vs no, it isn't
As fun as the story is — I'd never have thought of taking a photo and feeding it to a chatbot; it's smart thinking — one of the other comments on the Reddit thread made me laugh: Mindless-Apricot-236 responded that they once lost a screw outdoors, uploaded a picture to ChatGPT and "asked the oracle to help me find it. It said it found it. Showed me the picture... It just modified the original picture and put a random screw on it lol"
Other commenters had suggestions that didn't involve AI at all, such as 4-jr1's "how about next time you just open Spotify and listen for the one rock among hundreds that sings out loud" — although that wouldn't work if the headphones weren't on and paired; I have Bose QuietComfort earbuds and they don't turn on until they're in my ears — and SpehlingAirer's "When this kinda thing happens to me I turn on my phone's flashlight and bring it low to the ground pointing almost horizontally. The way the light reflects off the common background (gravel, carpet, grass, etc) and the way it reflects off the glossy plastic are often different enough to help spot it quickly."
And of course many of the best earbuds have some variation of Find My, enabling you to locate them from your phone. But it's nice to know that all those years we've been identifying bicycles, stairs and traffic lights in website CAPTCHAs has paid off: computer vision has become really incredible.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
As to whether it's reliable, I'll just leave this, by AnalogAngeleno, here: "I tried something similar at a used bookstore. Took a photo of the shelve and asked it to help look for books since they were not in any kind of order. Unfortunately it started making up books that were not even there."
Still, you'll get different results depending on the type of task and the model you're using — evidently, this one worked well enough, and seems like a good tip to keep in mind for your own earbud emergency.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Contributor
Writer, broadcaster, musician and kitchen gadget obsessive Carrie Marshall has been writing about tech since 1998, contributing sage advice and odd opinions to all kinds of magazines and websites as well as writing more than twenty books. Her latest, a love letter to music titled Small Town Joy, is on sale now. She is the singer in spectacularly obscure Glaswegian rock band Unquiet Mind.

articles.title: Mchose Launches Updated Ace68 V2 HE Keyboard as $69 Wooting 60HE Alternative
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
Mchose Launches Updated Ace68 V2 HE Keyboard as $69 Wooting 60HE Alternative
Mchose has officially updated its Ace68, its fan-favorite affordable alternative to the Wooting 60HE. The Ace68 V2 features the same 68-key layout and 60HE-inspired design—replete with a strap and an angled front edge—as the old Ace68, but there are a few additions that make the Ace68 V2 stand out. For one, there is now a dedicated hardware rapid trigger button on the back edge, making it much easier to switch between different tasks, like gaming and work or between different games where different rapid trigger configurations may be beneficial. In addition to the functional changes, there is also a new metal strip along the edge for a bit of visual flavor. 
The Mchose hasn't specified a case material for the Ace68 V2, but the weight and price suggest it has a plastic bottom case, although it lacks the flip-out feet of its predecessor. The Ace68 V2 comes in white, black, or pink, with each featuring matching frosted translucent PC keycaps. The pink and white versions are available with Star Ring or Royal Steed magnetic switches, while the black keyboard is restricted to the Royal Steeds. Both switches are linear, but the Star Ring features a box stem and 33 gf actuation force, while the Royal Steed has a cylindrical stem with 35 gf actuation force. The switches are fitted in an aluminium switch plate that is mounted in a tray-mount configuration.The inside of the Ace68 V2's case is stuffed with sound-damping materials, including a silicone sandwich pad, PET sheet, fiber switch pad, PET base pad, case foam, and silicone case pad. The keyboard itself measures in at 320 × 122 × 39 mm and weighs 804 g without the strap and 814 g with the strap. The Ace68 V2 has launched with an MSRP of $69 and a small launch discount bringing the price down to $62.10.The Mchose Ace68 V2 is compatible with Mchose M HUB, the browser-based customization utility that supports adjustable actuation, rapid trigger, SOCD, DKS, and customization of the south-facing RGB backlighting. The Ace68 V2 uses a wired USB Type-C connection and up to 8 kHz polling rate, and the Hall effect sensors support up to 0.001 mm precision and actuation distance customization of 0.1-3.4 mm. Mchose claims that the Ace68 V2 has a latency figure of just 0.08 ms.
Source:
				Mchose

articles.title: Drones con tecnología láser descubren refugios aborígenes milenarios ocultos en los bosques de Australia
articles.text:
La protección de testimonios culturales milenarios enfrenta la barrera de la geografía agreste. En vastas regiones del planeta, valiosos sitios arqueológicos permanecen ocultos bajo densos mantos vegetales y precipicios inaccesibles para las búsquedas a pie. Frente a este desafío en Australia, un equipo científico logró identificar tres refugios aborígenes desconocidos mediante drones con tecnología láser en las Montañas Azules.
Este hallazgo marca un avance significativo para la preservación patrimonial, al comprobar que herramientas aéreas avanzadas pueden documentar enclaves históricos resguardados durante milenios por el aislamiento geográfico. Hasta el momento, rastrear estos abrigos rocosos, cavidades naturales en paredes de piedra que funcionaron como resguardo y espacios ceremoniales para las comunidades originarias, dependía de extenuantes caminatas de inspección terrestre.
La topografía accidentada y la densa vegetación de la cordillera impidieron durante décadas un registro sistemático. Aunque el área reúne más de doscientos refugios catalogados con vestigios de ocupación humana, los especialistas calculan que apenas el diez por ciento del territorio ha sido relevado a fondo. Esta limitación mantenía la incógnita sobre la cantidad real de yacimientos y su estado ante factores como la erosión, los incendios y el avance urbano.
El nuevo avance técnico resuelve esta dificultad mediante el uso coordinado de vehículos aéreos no tripulados, análisis informático de datos espaciales y verificación arqueológica en el terreno. La investigación, difundida en un estudio publicado en la revista Remote Sensing, demuestra que los sensores aerotransportados consiguen penetrar el follaje más cerrado para cartografiar formaciones geológicas antes invisibles. La relevancia del trabajo radica en el hallazgo de paneles de arte rupestre intactos y en la comprobación de un método veloz que agiliza la protección de bienes ancestrales sin perturbar el entorno natural.
La tecnología de pulsos láser penetra la espesa vegetación para revelar abrigos ocultos
El operativo se apoyó en un sensor aerotransportado de pulsos lumínicos acoplado a un dron industrial de gran porte. Este instrumental emite millones de haces de luz por segundo hacia el suelo boscoso. Gran parte de estos pulsos choca contra las copas de los árboles, es decir, el dosel superior que cubre los valles, pero una fracción se filtra entre el follaje y rebota en la roca sólida.
Al registrar el tiempo exacto que tarda cada destello en regresar, un programa informático calcula la elevación del terreno y descarta digitalmente las ramas, lo que permite advertir hendiduras que sugieren la existencia de cavernas bajo los farallones. La información captada en vuelo alimentó modelos digitales procesados en sistemas de información geográfica, esto es, programas diseñados para clasificar y cruzar variables espaciales en distintas capas analíticas.
“Este trabajo es emocionante porque ofrece una vía eficiente y precisa para localizar sitios en entornos escarpados que son notoriamente difíciles, costosos y lentos de relevar”, afirmó Jacob Bongers, arqueólogo digital de la Universidad de Sídney y autor principal de la investigación, según el comunicado de prensa.
El análisis aéreo permitió además rectificar coordenadas imprecisas en los registros oficiales. De este modo, “proporciona una metodología eficiente para corregir datos anteriores y localizar abrigos rocosos no registrados”, según se detalla en el estudio.
El trabajo conjunto con custodios tradicionales permitió registrar arte rupestre inédito
El sensor aéreo, sin embargo, solo detecta formas geológicas: no puede distinguir si una cavidad aloja restos culturales o carece de valor arqueológico. Por eso, la eficacia del proyecto radicó en el trabajo conjunto con la Corporación Aborigen de Custodios Dharug. Ambas partes conformaron la iniciativa Gulamada (cuyo principio fundacional es caminar a la par), que articula la ciencia con la tutela nativa sobre tierras ancestrales.
“Desde el principio, nuestra visión para el Proyecto Gulamada ha sido crear un verdadero nexo de ciencia y cultura. Este trabajo destaca la importancia de escuchar, aprender y trabajar juntos”, afirmó Wayne Brennan, codirector del proyecto y experto en arte rupestre indígena de la Universidad de Sídney, según el comunicado de prensa.
Guiados por las coordenadas del dron, los equipos marcharon hacia los puntos señalados para verificar el contenido de los recintos. La inspección sobre el terreno corroboró la posición exacta de seis refugios ya conocidos y descubrió tres abrigos rocosos jamás catalogados. En su interior hallaron herramientas de piedra y paneles con siluetas de manos en negativo elaboradas con pigmento rojo.
La participación directa de los custodios tradicionales garantizó que el registro de estas pinturas milenarias se realizara bajo protocolos de respeto comunitario, lo que previene que la difusión de datos espaciales exponga estos santuarios a visitas no autorizadas o actos de vandalismo.
La prospección aérea agiliza la protección de sitios amenazados en toda la región
La capacidad de relevar áreas agrestes con rapidez resulta crucial ante incendios forestales periódicos y meteorización, amenazas que deterioran bienes arqueológicos irremplazables. Disponer de cartografía tridimensional precisa antes de catástrofes naturales o desarrollos urbanos permite a las comunidades y a los organismos de preservación delimitar zonas prioritarias de resguardo con una exactitud inalcanzable para las cuadrillas terrestres en tiempos razonables.
Los especialistas prevén aplicar este método en otras regiones de Australia, como las sabanas de Arnhem y los sectores semiáridos de Nueva Gales del Sur, para salvaguardar territorios ancestrales antes de que ocurran daños ambientales.
De hecho, “nuestra metodología promueve un relevamiento específico y eficiente de abrigos rocosos que puede producir conjuntos de datos regionales beneficiosos para las comunidades locales, la arqueología y la gestión del patrimonio cultural”, el trabajo concluye.

articles.title: Anduril challenges Apple with Qualcomm-powered 'BlueChip' laptop
articles.text:
Anduril wants to become a laptop maker — drone and defense giant partners with Qualcomm to build new BlueChip devices, all made in the US
An all-American laptop could cost 20% more
- Anduril plans to open BlueChip laptop orders in 2027 with Qualcomm
- BlueChip prototypes source 90% of component procurement costs from American and allied suppliers
- Anduril expects its laptops to cost 20% more than comparable devices
Anduril Industries has revealed plans to enter the laptop market through a partnership with Qualcomm, with plans to begin accepting orders for its BlueChip computers in 2027.
The defense technology company, best known for its military drones, intends to reduce reliance on overseas suppliers as it develops the new laptop line.
However, its current sourcing figures show that eliminating foreign suppliers remains a future objective rather than an existing achievement.
BlueChip begins with American manufacturing
The company has developed working prototypes featuring Qualcomm Snapdragon X Series processors, which will power the laptops.
Anduril says suppliers in the United States and allied countries account for 90% of the procurement cost of the components used in its prototypes.
The company already sources several parts locally, including batteries, computer enclosures and display glass.
Its strategy also involves using metals that American industries can extract, refine and process at commercial scale.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“Other companies might design their computers in the U.S., Anduril makes them here,” said Palmer Luckey, founder of Anduril Industries, in a company video.
“We’re making parts out of metals that the U.S. knows how to extract, knows how to refine, knows how to process, and knows how to mill at scale at a reasonable price; and that goes for the entire laptop. The same thing goes for the battery technology.”
The company says the laptop is designed to withstand demanding environments, with replaceable upper and lower shells that allow users to customize its configuration.
These interchangeable panels could accommodate additions such as solar panels, specialised fabric materials and service insignia, according to Anduril’s video.
The design also allows flat phased-array antennas to be integrated directly into the laptop’s chassis, potentially supporting specialised applications in demanding operating environments.
Anduril estimates that producing a fully American-made laptop could cost 20% more than a comparable device, potentially limiting its appeal to ordinary consumers.
Therefore, it appears to be focused on customers with specific security requirements, including government agencies, military organizations, emergency responders, and public safety departments.
These buyers may accept higher prices to address concerns about hardware security and supply chain reliability.
A domestic supply chain remains difficult
Anduril acknowledges that producing complete laptops requires more than processors and selected parts.
Circuit boards, displays, batteries, and other essential components remain heavily dependent on foreign suppliers, complicating efforts to eliminate reliance on these suppliers.
“BlueChip will take a phased approach, beginning with expanding domestic sourcing and manufacturing, progressing toward eliminating reliance on foreign suppliers, and ultimately establishing an end-to-end American supply chain,” the company said in its announcement.
The project comes as semiconductor investment grows in the United States, including TSMC’s facilities in Arizona and Samsung’s site in Taylor, Texas.
These projects could improve access to locally fabricated chips, but they do not guarantee a domestic source for every part needed to assemble a laptop.
Taiwan has also planned support for smaller companies supplying TSMC through industrial parks in the United States.
Such initiatives could give BlueChip access to additional suppliers, although their eventual contribution to the laptop’s production remains unclear.

articles.title: Taxe sur les gigaoctets : surréaliste, GTA 6 pourrait coûter 11,55 € de plus, Netflix jusqu'à 3 € par mois
articles.text:
Les députés ont voté vendredi une taxe de 5,5 centimes par gigaoctet envoyé aux internautes français. Sur le papier, télécharger GTA 6 ou regarder Netflix pourrait coûter beaucoup plus cher, même si le texte n’est pas encore sorti de l'Assemblée nationale.
L’Assemblée nationale a adopté, vendredi 30 octobre avec un nombre famélique de « courageux » députés, un amendement au projet de budget 2027 qui crée une taxe de 0,055 euro sur chaque gigaoctet envoyé aux internautes français. Porté par le député socialiste Laurent Lhardit, le texte vise les fournisseurs de contenus et a été voté par 11 voix contre 10, malgré l’avis défavorable du gouvernement, qui craint la grogne de tout un secteur, et des consommateurs. Reste à savoir ce qu’il coûterait réellement aux joueurs de GTA 6 et aux abonnés de Netflix, entre autres, et s’il survivra à la suite de la navette parlementaire.
Ce que la taxe au gigaoctet coûterait vraiment pour GTA 6 et votre abonnement Netflix
L'amendement polémique, porté par le socialiste Laurent Lhardit pour « faire contribuer les géants du numérique », crée une taxe sur les producteurs de données numériques. Le mécanisme, on pourrait la résumer en une phrase. En gros, chaque gigaoctet envoyé vers un abonné français coûterait 0,055 euro à l'entreprise qui l'émet. Pas à l'internaute, ni à son opérateur. Les fournisseurs d'accès se contenteraient de jouer les compteurs, autrement dit, ils additionneraient les volumes par émetteur et transmettraient les totaux au fisc chaque trimestre, sans jamais savoir ce qu'ils contiennent. Pour les contenus diffusés via un CDN, un réseau qui les stocke au plus près des abonnés, c'est le trafic sortant de ce réseau qui serait compté.
Selon l'exposé des motifs, les CDN resteraient libres de refacturer ou non la taxe à leurs clients. Ce même document cite une estimation de l'ARCEP, qui évoque 200 milliards de gigaoctets envoyés chaque année vers les abonnés français. Les auteurs en attendent 10 milliards d'euros de retombées, à prélever surtout chez Google, Meta, Amazon, Netflix et Akamai, qui pèseraient la moitié de ce trafic. Sauf que ça ne se passera pas vraiment comme ça.
Prenons GTA 6, attendu le 19 novembre à 79,99 euros en édition standard et 99,99 euros en Ultimate. On sait qu'il devrait peser 210 Go sur PS5, ce qui représenterait un supplément de 11,55 euros de taxe par téléchargement. C'est environ 14 % du prix standard, et près de 20 % pour ceux qui l'ont déniché à 60 euros en précommande. « On doit repasser à l'ADSL ? », ironise sur LinkedIn Thomas Martin, spécialiste de l'identité visuelle. La note viserait le distributeur, à savoir la boutique de Sony ou de Microsoft ou son CDN, plutôt que Rockstar, et chaque réinstallation relancerait le compteur. Même la boîte y passe, puisqu'elle ne contient qu'un code. La seule consolidation, c'est que vu que la mesure est inscrite au budget 2027, les téléchargements de novembre ne devraient pas être concernés.
Si on fait le calcul pour un abonnement Netflix, vous risquez de toussoter. La plateforme annonce d'ordinaire jusqu'à 3 Go consommés par heure en HD. Quarante heures de séries peuvent donc atteindre 120 Go par mois, soit jusqu'à 6,60 euros de taxe pour un abonnement Standard à 14,99 euros. À 7 Go par heure en 4K, une famille qui avale soixante heures par mois pourrait même dépasser le prix du forfait Premium, à 21,99 euros. Un autre professionnel chiffre la facture à « 66 euros/an » par abonné, rien que pour Netflix. Mais c’est oublier le garde-fou prévu par le texte.
Oui, il y a un plafond. Quel que soit le volume de données envoyé, une entreprise ne paierait jamais plus de 15 % du chiffre d’affaires qu'elle réalise en France. Or celui de Netflix provient pour l'essentiel de nos abonnements. Autrement dit, même si la plateforme répercutait toute la taxe sur ses clients, la hausse ne pourrait pas dépasser 15 % du prix de l'abonnement. D'après nos calculs, cela représente environ 1,20 euro par mois pour la formule avec pub, 2,25 euros pour le Standard et 3,30 euros pour le Premium, bien loin des 5,50 euros mensuels avancés par certains observateurs. Une incertitude demeure toutefois. Le texte évoque aussi un plafond de 2 % du chiffre d’affaires mondial, sans préciser lequel des deux s'applique. Si c'était celui-là, le calcul serait différent. Le revers de la médaille pour l'État est chez les gros diffuseurs de vidéo, où ce plafond rognerait mécaniquement une partie des 10 milliards espérés.
Une taxe numérique qui divise bien au-delà de l’hémicycle
On ne peut en tout cas pas parler de plébiscite pour le vote de vendredi. Sur 35 votants à peine, 11 ont dit oui, 10 non, et 14 se sont abstenus, malgré l'opposition du gouvernement et du rapporteur général du budget. « 11 voix pour décider potentiellement de l'avenir fiscal d'une partie de notre économie numérique », relève, un brin moqueur, le responsable informatique Lucas Murzyn. Comment en effet crédibiliser l'Assemblée nationale devant le faible nombre de participants ? Le plus délicat reste toutefois à venir. L'Assemblée doit encore adopter l'ensemble du volet recettes. S'il est rejeté, l'amendement disparaîtra avec lui, comme les mesures votées par les députés sur le budget 2025, dont le texte initial était parti tel quel au Sénat. Et si les députés dépassent le délai de quarante jours dont ils disposent, qui expire vers le 10 novembre, ou si l'exécutif dégaine le 49.3, c'est le gouvernement qui choisira les amendements conservés. Autant dire qu'il passerait aussi à la trappe.
Surtout que tout le monde, sauf les quelques votants apparemment, aura vu et compris que la mesure fait grincer des dents. Benjamin Romeo, architecte cloud, rappelle une règle de base de la fiscalité : celui qui verse l'impôt n'est pas forcément celui qui le supporte. Croire l'inverse revient, selon lui, à penser que « c'est la vache qui paie la taxe sur le lait ». D'autres pointent un effet boomerang, puisque des acteurs français comme OVHcloud ou le champion de l'IA, Mistral, seraient taxés sur tout ce qu'ils livrent à leurs clients hexagonaux, même si leurs exportations seraient épargnées. « Le délire fiscal continue en France ! », s'agace Flavien Berwick, conseiller en IA et cloud souverains.
Alors, cet amendement est-il une bonne ou mauvaise idée ? Les défenseurs du texte vantent « une assiette non délocalisable ». Un bénéfice peut se déclarer là où ça arrange, un flux livré en France, non. Ils y ajoutent une vertu écologique, celle de pousser les plateformes à mieux compresser les contenus. Jordan Broussous, qui accompagne des dirigeants dans leur transformation, résume l'objection : « Un gigaoctet ne mesure ni les bénéfices d'une entreprise, ni l'utilité d'un service. »
Un épisode de série et un correctif de sécurité coûteraient en effet le même prix au gigaoctet. Surtout, le texte cumule les fragilités. Son plafond reste ambigu, et aucun seuil n'épargne les petits acteurs. Là où la taxe GAFAM ne vise que les entreprises de plus de 750 millions d'euros de chiffre d'affaires mondial, un modeste site pourrait ici se voir refacturer la taxe par son CDN. Sa solidité juridique interroge aussi, entre un probable passage devant le Conseil constitutionnel et une compatibilité incertaine avec le droit européen. En l'état, l'amendement tient davantage du coup de semonce adressé aux géants du numérique que de l'impôt prêt à l'emploi.

articles.title: MS Office 2024 Professional Plus Includes 6 Apps for a One-Time $49.97
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
MS Office 2024 Professional Plus Includes 6 Apps for a One-Time $49.97
Microsoft Office 2024 Professional Plus for Windows is on sale for $49.97 (MSRP $249.99) through Nov. 1. The offer reduces the price by $200 and provides a perpetual license for one Windows PC, with no ongoing subscription fees.
The suite includes Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote, and Access. Together, these apps cover document creation, spreadsheets, presentations, email, notes, and database management. Advanced data analysis and database tools also support work involving business information.The main purchasing distinction is the license type. This Professional Plus offer uses a non-binding, device-linked key, rather than the Microsoft account-linked binding key used by the Home and Business version. Lifetime access applies to the specific device associated with the license. That device-specific arrangement is part of what makes this offer more affordable.
It also differs from the ongoing payment model of Microsoft 365. Instead of paying subscription fees, buyers make a single payment for Office 2024 Professional Plus. For users who want these applications on one computer, this provides a defined upfront software cost.
Office 2024 Professional Plus emphasizes consistent functionality and long-term stability rather than frequent feature updates. It is designed for organizations that prefer a traditional perpetual license, including regulated industries and restricted environments where continuity matters.
The software includes a streamlined interface with dark mode, built-in security and compliance capabilities, and productivity tools designed for dependable performance. It also has minimal system requirements intended to accommodate a wide range of compatible hardware.
Compatibility is limited to Windows 10 and Windows 11 PCs. This license does not support Mac or macOS devices. Buyers receive instant access to the license key and download link.
Get six Microsoft Office 2024 Professional Plus apps for a one-time $49.97 payment through Nov. 1.

articles.title: Reddit sufre su peor día en Wall Street: sus acciones se desploman un 29,22%
articles.text:
Reddit sufrió su peor jornada en Wall Street desde que salió a bolsa en 2024: sus acciones se desplomaron un 29,22% este viernes 30 de octubre de 2026 y cerraron en USD 91,73, con una pérdida diaria de USD 37,87 por título.
La caída respondió a las previsiones de ventas para el cuarto trimestre, que quedaron por debajo de las expectativas de Wall Street.
La compañía proyectó ingresos de entre USD 1.000 millones y USD 1.030 millones, frente a los USD 1.050 millones previstos por los analistas.
El retroceso superó el anterior peor desempeño diario de Reddit, registrado el 31 de julio, cuando sus acciones habían caído un 20,99%.
La empresa indicó que sus ventas del tercer trimestre crecieron 53% interanual. Aunque superó las previsiones de ganancias e ingresos, el ritmo de expansión fue menor que el de los trimestres previos.
Qué inquietó a los inversores de Reddit
El mercado reaccionó a la proyección para los últimos tres meses del año, que quedó por debajo de los cálculos de los analistas. El resultado profundizó las dudas sobre la evolución del negocio publicitario de la plataforma.
Reddit también enfrenta cambios en el tráfico que recibe desde los buscadores.
Steve Huffman, director ejecutivo de la empresa, afirmó a CNBC que las visitas derivadas de Google disminuyeron de forma significativa durante el trimestre debido al avance de las respuestas generadas con inteligencia artificial en el buscador.
La compañía atribuyó parte de ese descenso a la expansión de AI Overview, la función de Google que ofrece resúmenes generados con inteligencia artificial dentro de los resultados de búsqueda.
El plan para exigir inicio de sesión a los usuarios en Reddit
Reddit anunció que probará exigir a los usuarios que inicien sesión para acceder a sus contenidos.
La medida representa un cambio para una plataforma identificada con el acceso abierto a debates y comunidades en internet.
Huffman explicó que la iniciativa apunta a incrementar la cantidad de usuarios registrados y activos, un factor relevante para el negocio de publicidad.
El ejecutivo sostuvo que Reddit es la última plataforma que todavía permite, en gran medida, el acceso sin iniciar sesión y que ese modelo responde a una decisión que él había defendido.
Consideró que los usuarios terminarán por entender el cambio como una adaptación al momento actual y a la evolución del funcionamiento de las plataformas digitales.
Acciones de Intel bajaron un 28,54%
Intel sufrió su peor jornada bursátil desde 1974: sus acciones cayeron 28,58% el viernes 30 de octubre de 2026 y cerraron en USD 65,76, frente a los USD 92,07 del día anterior. El desplome significó una pérdida de USD 26,31 por acción en una sola rueda.
El mercado castigó las previsiones de la compañía para el cuarto trimestre. Intel estimó ingresos de entre USD 15.000 millones y USD 16.000 millones, por debajo de los USD 17.070 millones esperados por los analistas consultados por LSEG.
Además, anticipó una ganancia ajustada de 25 centavos por acción, frente a los 43 centavos previstos por el mercado.
Durante la jornada, la acción abrió en USD 68,36, alcanzó un máximo de USD 68,77 y tocó un mínimo de USD 63,20. Tras el cierre regular, cotizaba en USD 65,23.
La empresa atribuyó parte de sus débiles perspectivas a la caída del mercado de computadoras personales y a la explosión ocurrida en octubre en su fábrica de Kiryat Gat, Israel. El incidente, que dejó dos trabajadores muertos y un tercero gravemente herido, obligó a detener la planta durante dos semanas.
Intel estimó que la explosión reducirá sus ingresos del cuarto trimestre en unos USD 300 millones y afectará el margen bruto en 200 puntos básicos. El impacto total podría alcanzar los USD 600 millones durante los dos próximos trimestres.
Pese a que los ingresos del tercer trimestre crecieron 21%, las ventas de chips para computadoras retrocedieron 5%. En contraste, el negocio de centros de datos e inteligencia artificial aumentó 78%. La baja también arrastró a otras empresas del sector, como Nvidia, Micron Technology, AMD y ASUS.

articles.title: Inoxtag dévoile The Blood Island pour Halloween, 48 heures de survie et d’horreur, avec une vidéo de 2 heures !
articles.text:
Deux ans après Kaizen et son ascension de l'Everest, le youtubeur Inoxtag troque les cimes pour la jungle thaïlandaise avec The Blood Island, un escape game géant mêlant aventure et horreur. Rendez-vous ce 31 octobre à 14h30, gratuitement sur YouTube.
Le youtubeur Inoxtag a présenté ce vendredi 30 octobre « The Blood Island », un escape game géant tourné dans la jungle thaïlandaise et diffusé sur YouTube dès le lendemain, jour d'Halloween. Le nouveau concept du créateur, « l'une des plus grosses vidéos que j'ai faites », comme il l'a dit sur Twitch, place cinq créateurs (Squeezie, Michou, Amine, LeGrandJD et lui) face à un défi de survie de 48 heures, après un crash d’avion mis en scène sur une île hostile. Entièrement financée par le vidéaste, la production, qui s'appelait au départ « The Forest », a mobilisé des moyens considérables et bénéficie du soutien de YouTube pour son avant-première.
Après Kaizen, Inoxtag revient avec un escape game grandeur nature en Thaïlande
Comme dans un film catastrophe, le scénario de The Blood Island s'ouvre sur un crash d'avion, fictif bien sûr, sur une île de la jungle thaïlandaise. Les cinq participants se retrouvent devant une carcasse en flammes, sans réseau ni secours, et comprennent vite qu'une tempête va frapper l'île dans 48 heures. D'ici là, ils doivent fouiller l'épave à la recherche d'indices, résoudre des énigmes et tenir le coup sur place, avec pour seul objectif de trouver le moyen de quitter l'île. C'est le principe de l'escape game, ces jeux où l'on doit s'échapper d'une pièce en déchiffrant des indices, mais étendu à une île entière, comme un jeu vidéo d'aventure que l'on vivrait pour de vrai.
Dans le scénario, leur présence sur l'île n'est pas vraiment un hasard. Les survivants le devinent assez vite, à mesure que des ombres se dessinent dans la végétation et que les habitants des lieux se montrent peu enclins à les voir repartir. Entre énigmes à décoder et menace qui rôde, The Blood Island lorgne franchement du côté du survival horror.
Et pour donner corps à cette fiction XXL, la production a vu grand. Au milieu de la jungle sauvage, le tournage a réuni 300 personnes et plus de 50 figurants. Surtout, la caméra n'a jamais été coupée, avec 48 heures de captation non-stop, assurées par trois cadreurs présents en permanence sur le terrain et par les caméras embarquées dont chacun des cinq participants était équipé. Aucune frayeur ne devrait passer entre les mailles du filet.
Un projet autofinancé dont YouTube fait sa vitrine
Avant d'atterrir sur YouTube, The Blood Island, qui dure 1h54, s'offre un passage par le grand écran. Une avant-première événementielle est organisée au Hangar Y, avec le soutien de la plateforme via son programme YouTube Ciné-Club. Le public n'aura toutefois pas à patienter bien longtemps, puisqu'Inoxtag, Inès de son vrai prénom, tient à rendre sa vidéo accessible rapidement et gratuitement. Sa mise en ligne est prévue ce vendredi 31 octobre 2026 à 14h30. Une sortie le jour d'Halloween, plutôt raccord avec l'ambiance, sur une plateforme qui se rêve désormais en nouvelle télévision.
Produit, financé et réalisé de A à Z par Inoxtag (près de 10 millions d'abonnés sur YouTube) et ses équipes, le projet a aussi valeur d'école. Le créateur dit vouloir aller un cran plus loin à chaque vidéo, en mariant divertissement et envies plus artistiques, symbolisés par des effets spéciaux, de l'animation 2D et 3D, et des collaborations avec des artistes parfois éloignés de son univers. Lui qui a toujours rêvé de produire et réaliser un film voit YouTube comme un vrai bac à sable, tout y consacrant de très gros moyens, probablement des centaines de milliers d'euros, pour cette nouvelle production. Mais cette fois, il s'est entouré de nouveaux talents pour se nourrir de leur expérience.
Sans surprise, YouTube, qui multiplie les outils pour séduire les créateurs, en fait l'étendard de son modèle. Selon la plateforme, 69 % des créateurs français réinvestissent leurs revenus dans leurs équipes, leur matériel ou leurs décors, et son écosystème soutient l'équivalent de 27 000 emplois à temps plein en France. Elle ajoute que plus des trois quarts des créateurs aujourd'hui actifs dans les médias et le divertissement ont démarré chez elle. Des chiffres avancés par YouTube directement, mais qui rappellent qu'une telle production fait vivre des techniciens, comédiens et figurants.

articles.title: RTX 5080 Vanishes From NVIDIA's US Marketplace Two Weeks After the RTX 5090
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
RTX 5080 Vanishes From NVIDIA's US Marketplace Two Weeks After the RTX 5090
NVIDIA's US Marketplace no longer lists the GeForce RTX 5080. The GPU filter on the store's graphics card page now tops out at the RTX 5070 Ti, followed by the RTX 5070, RTX 5060 Ti, RTX 5060, and RTX 5050, with partner RTX 5080 models gone as well. The same thing happened to the RTX 5090 about two weeks ago and, barring a brief cameo at $5,599, the card still hasn't returned. NVIDIA has since denied that the RTX 5090 is discontinued, though it hasn't said anything about the RTX 5080 yet. Oddly enough, its RTX 5080 product page still says "Starting at $999."
The removal seems limited to the US for now. NVIDIA's UK Marketplace still has 13 RTX 5080 listings and two RTX 5090 cards. Of course, a missing listing could simply mean there's no stock left, since the RTX 5080 already costs close to $2,000 at US retailers, roughly double its MSRP. That leaves the RTX 5070 Ti as the fastest card on NVIDIA's US store, and it isn't cheap either. The seven listings there range from $1,269.99 to $1,499.99, well above its $749 launch price.Of course, this move is not really surprising. We recently covered a new report claiming NVIDIA is moving up the launch of a 24 GB RTX 5080 to December or January, and phasing out the 16 GB model in China. A leaker also claimed earlier this month that NVIDIA has January discontinuation dates set for the 16 GB card. None of this is officially confirmed, but it looks like US buyers looking for an RTX 5080 16 GB will have to rely on third-party retailers for now.
Sources:

articles.title: Sam Altman defends OpenAI’s science blitz — CEO refuses to slow research as academics describe the influx as a 'giant bomb'
articles.text:
Sam Altman says OpenAI won't slow science paper blitz — even though academics are calling it a 'giant bomb'
"It’s really cool and terrible at the same time", say researchers
- OpenAI will keep pushing AI’s scientific discoveries, Sam Altman says
- Some researchers are excited by the ‘fantastic’ breakthroughs
- But others warn that the pace of change is ‘psychologically taxing’
One of the promises that huge AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have made is that their machine learning models will help to solve some of the oldest problems in math and science. The pace of their discoveries has left many experts struggling to keep up, but OpenAI’s Sam Altman just has just said there’s much more in store — and not everyone is happy about that.
Speaking on the Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman outlined his belief that “Humanity deserves fundamental knowledge, and we should not be sitting on a major fundamental science discovery.”
That rationale is why OpenAI has published breakthrough after breakthrough in these fields, knocking down some of the oldest and toughest problems that have troubled great thinkers for years. But the way in which the company has set out its results has drawn criticism for often inadequate attributions and questionable verification processes.
While Altman acknowledged that, saying on the podcast that “I do have empathy for the method” and saying OpenAI’s quest for mathematical challenges did “get out of control” at times, he suggested that there’s much more to come. Asked if the firm has anymore unpublished breakthroughs in its vaults, he replied “We do. Of course.”
That’s led to accusations that, far from giving people “fundamental knowledge,” OpenAI is gatekeeping important discoveries. And there’s another problem: the sheer scale of the new research is swamping academics. For instance, Wired has noted that the company recently “dumped 722 manuscripts on 400 problems on GitHub,” leaving the scientific community to pick through the enormous mass of information.
And the impact of having the most important work in your life suddenly undercut by a machine is “psychologically taxing for many people,” said Thore Husfeldt of the IT University of Copenhagen. Husfeldt added that there is “a lot of doom and gloom, because every week, or every second week, the results announced by AI just annihilate the ongoing research projects of many people.”
Obliterating entire fields of research
AI models’ ability to solve thorny problems was keenly demonstrated when it apparently disproved the exponential time hypothesis (ETH), which argued that the effort needed to solve a problem increases with its complexity. That’s upended countless theories that assumed that ETH was correct and left many experts scrambling to catch up.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
As Linköping University professor Peter Jonsson told Wired, although AI’s tendency to undermine years-long research can be irksome, “at the same time, we learn a lot from it. And this is what science is about.”
UC Santa Barbara professor Daniel Lokshtanov aptly described the mood among many scientists and mathematicians, saying “It’s just a giant bomb dropped into the middle of the field,” he says. “It’s really cool and terrible at the same time.”
For Husfeldt, meanwhile, the discovery is “fantastic.” He added: “Being a mathematician is a lot like stumbling about in a completely dark room. It’s like somebody just illuminated an entire subfield in floodlights of knowledge, and now we just run around like overexcited bunnies and look at all the nooks and crannies that we can suddenly explore. So it’s a super exciting time.”
In the case of the ETH theory, OpenAI’s work has not been peer reviewed or independently verified. But it’s clear that AI research is creating generational changes in many areas — and overturning entire fields of study in an instant, with all the excitement and chaos that comes with that.
Jonsson fittingly summed the situation up, saying: “I don’t care if it’s a human-written proof, or it’s written by AI, or if an alien transmitted this proof to us. If it’s true, then we must simply use it in the future.”
