articles.title: Qué es la ansiedad por inteligencia artificial y por qué preocupa a los expertos
articles.text:
La ansiedad por la inteligencia artificial se instala en los consultorios de los terapeutas y los datos lo confirman: en una encuesta del Pew Research Center realizada en 2026 a más de 3.400 adultos en Estados Unidos, el 52% de los consultados dijo sentirse más preocupado que entusiasmado por el avance de la IA en la vida cotidiana, frente al 37% que expresó esa misma inquietud en 2021.
El fenómeno tiene nombre propio: ansiedad por IA. Según informó el Washington Post, los especialistas en salud mental advierten que llegó para quedarse. Los miedos van desde perder el trabajo hasta no poder distinguir lo real de lo fabricado por una máquina, y los terapeutas ya tienen respuestas concretas para quienes lo padecen.
La psiquiatra Tracy Foose, terapeuta en el Área de la Bahía de San Francisco, lo vivió en carne propia. Cuando empezó a publicar videos en redes sociales, algunos seguidores insistían en que era una influencer generada por computadora, algo que al principio le resultó halagador.
La sensación cambió cuando se puso a investigar. Descubrió que existen múltiples compañías que ofrecen crear dobles digitales capaces de replicar la voz y el rostro de cualquier persona.
“Me di cuenta de que alguien podría hacer un video que se apropiara tan completamente de mi imagen, mi voz, mi cara, que incluso yo podría creer que soy yo”, le dijo al Washington Post. El halago se transformó, según sus propias palabras, en “una forma de terror existencial”.
El 52% de los estadounidenses teme más de lo que se entusiasma con la IA
Ese terror no es un caso aislado. Sha Sajadieh, quien lidera el Índice de IA en el Instituto Stanford para la IA Centrada en el Ser Humano, explicó al medio que la mayor exposición a la tecnología produce un doble efecto: entusiasmo y alarma, casi a partes iguales.
“Con una adopción más amplia viene una mayor comprensión de lo que esta tecnología es capaz de hacer, lo cual puede ser muy emocionante como herramienta para muchos de nosotros, y también puede ser increíblemente abrumador cuando pensás en algunos de los posibles impactos a largo plazo”, señaló.
Un informe de Pew de 2025 refuerza esa tensión: cerca del 75% de los estadounidenses acepta que la IA los asista en tareas cotidianas, pero más de la mitad califica como alto el riesgo social que implica la tecnología.
Ese equilibrio frágil se sacudió aún más la semana pasada, cuando una publicación de un investigador de Anthropic (la empresa creadora del asistente Claude) se viralizó en la red social X al advertir que existe una probabilidad superior al 10% de que “la IA podría matar a todos los humanos”.
Hasta ese momento, las preocupaciones sobre una inteligencia superior que domine el mundo habían sido, en general, territorio de los propios especialistas del sector. Sajadieh aclaró, sin embargo, que la mayoría de las angustias vinculadas a la IA son más inmediatas: “más reales aquí y ahora”.
El miedo a perder el empleo y la identidad está en el centro de la angustia
La más extendida de esas preocupaciones concretas es el temor a la pérdida del trabajo. Vaile Wright, psicóloga y directora sénior de innovación en salud de la Asociación Americana de Psicología (APA), explicó al Washington Post que quedarse sin empleo no solo implica perder el sustento económico, sino también el propósito. “Muchas veces tu identidad está envuelta en la cantidad de inversión que pusiste en tu carrera”, afirmó.
A ese miedo se le suma otro, más difuso pero igual de corrosivo: ver a la IA ejecutar tareas consideradas propias de los seres humanos, como generar ideas o resolver problemas, puede sacudir la autoestima de forma más profunda. “Hay una parte de nosotros que quiere defender la creatividad y la inteligencia humanas y decir: ‘Soy mucho mejor’, pero frente a frente con la máquina, puede que no siempre se sienta así”, reconoció Foose.
Hay, además, un tercer factor que alimenta la angustia: la dificultad creciente para distinguir lo real de lo artificial. Thea Gallagher, psicóloga clínica y profesora asociada de psiquiatría en la Escuela de Medicina Grossman de la Universidad de Nueva York, señaló que la proliferación de contenido generado por IA desorienta a las personas y les genera miedo a ser estafadas o víctimas de una falsificación digital.
El informe de Pew de 2025 pone cifras a esa incertidumbre: el 53% de los estadounidenses no se siente capaz de detectar si algo fue producido por una persona o por una máquina.
La velocidad del fenómeno tampoco ayuda. La IA avanza en publicidad, contratación laboral y salud, muchas veces sin que la regulación pueda seguirle el ritmo. “Para la mayoría de nosotros, realmente no sabemos cómo funciona. A veces ni los propios desarrolladores lo saben”, indicó Wright. “Estar golpeados por tanta incertidumbre nos recuerda lo poco que podemos controlar”.
Los terapeutas recomiendan informarse, conectar con otros y ejercitar las habilidades propias
Frente a este panorama, los especialistas consultados por el Washington Post ofrecen herramientas concretas. El primer paso, según Wright, es mejorar el conocimiento sobre la IA: experimentar con versiones gratuitas de herramientas como ChatGPT o Claude, o tomar cursos introductorios. Conocer la tecnología ayuda a percibirla como un recurso utilizable, en lugar de una amenaza difusa.
La recomendación es preguntar en el trabajo cómo se usa la IA y reflexionar sobre el valor que cada persona aporta. Para los padres, hablar con docentes sobre la tecnología en el aula y medidas para preservar el pensamiento crítico.
Un segundo eje pasa por reconectar con el cuerpo y los sentidos. Foose subrayó que, a diferencia de la IA, los seres humanos son “seres vivos que respiran en un mundo físico”. Atender necesidades básicas como moverse, alimentarse y salir al aire libre ancla la mente en el presente y frena la espiral de pensamientos catastróficos.
“No tiene que ser una caminata de varios días en la naturaleza. Puede ser simplemente caminar por una calle de la ciudad con todo el ruido de los taxis”, ejemplificó. Gallagher, en la misma línea, subrayó el valor de “volver a la naturaleza, estar en el mundo” y recuperar el contacto con lo que se puede ver, tocar y sentir.
Cultivar vínculos reales y redescubrir las capacidades humanas es parte del antídoto
El tercer pilar es la conexión social. Wright advirtió que la tendencia a no querer cargar a los demás con los problemas propios es, en realidad, un obstáculo, porque “en realidad necesitamos buscar apoyo social”. Foose apuntó que el contacto presencial, “donde podemos tocarnos, vernos, olernos, por más extraño que suene”, puede ser restaurador.
Crear rituales, como ejercicio semanal o llamadas quincenales, sostiene la conexión. Si el círculo social se redujo, reconectar con viejos amigos o hacer voluntariado ayuda a ampliarlo.
Los terapeutas sugieren reivindicar las propias capacidades. Gallagher alienta a sus pacientes a “crear, hacer, producir”, algo que la IA no puede quitar. Foose invita a resolver problemas físicos, como reorganizar un cajón u ordenar el garaje, para recuperar la propia agencia.
Cuando el desánimo se instala, propone recordar la magnitud del cerebro humano: “Hace cuatrillones de cálculos por minuto y no depende de una planta de energía para hacerlo. Podemos llevarlo a la naturaleza. Podemos llevarlo bajo el agua. Podemos conectarlo a otros cerebros simplemente usando el lenguaje”, dijo. “La IA recién está aprendiendo a hacer eso”.

articles.title: This week in Tom's Hardware Premium: October 31, 2026 — Vera CPUs available on Oracle clusters, building an agentic CPU benchmark and a primer to LLMs
articles.text:
This week in Tom's Hardware Premium: October 31, 2026 — Vera CPUs available on Oracle clusters, building an agentic CPU benchmark and a primer to LLMs
Catch up on everything we published this week.
In case you're not yet subscribed to our Tom's Hardware Premium subscription service, here's what you've been missing out on this week. We detail our thoughts on Anthropic's filings pre-IPO, Cadence's new suite of LLMs to power its EDA tools, how Nvidia is securing its entire supply chain to serve AI data center demand, how Vera CPUs are landing in the cloud, an update to the ongoing TP-Link saga, and more. Remember, to access any of the articles listed here, you'll need to arm yourself with a subscription.
We've been hard at work behind the scenes to determine exactly how locally-run AI models and workloads stress consumer-level components. While throughput and tokens per second are indeed important factors, our resident CPU expert Jake Roach has begun laying out his vision for how Agentic workloads tax CPUs, and how we're building benchmarks in this newfangled AI world that the PC hardware space finds itself increasingly entrenched in. It's not often that readers get the chance to look at our behind-the-scenes work, and this piece offers a look at some of the foundational exploration we're doing around how to define what an agentic AI CPU benchmark might look like in the future.
As the rise of Artificial Intelligence increasingly becomes attached to powerful, locally-run hardware, you might encounter terminology and nomenclature that you may otherwise not be familiar with. So, we've published a primer on all of the basic terminology that you need to know moving forward. Currently, you get breakdowns of how inference works, details on quantization, context, KV cache, and more. We're striving to update this page as our exploration with local AI grows, to serve as a handy bookmark. It's not a mere dictionary either, as we contextualize how each of these things relates to the larger overall model, how it might be served, or where you might encounter it when trying to run an AI model of your own.
Nvidia's Vera CPUs were a salient part of a swath of Oracle announcements this week. The chip, usually found alongside Nvidia's NVL72 rack, is now generally available, but curiously, standalone Vera instances are also available on OCI superclusters. The CPU is specifically designed with Agentic AI workloads in mind, and it just so happens that we've benchmarked an Nvidia Vera server just this week to highlight the efficacy of how well Vera might perform under certain workloads.
Last week, we covered TP-Link's proposal to allow the router manufacturer to sell its Wi-Fi 8 products in the U.S. Now, according to a new report, it's alleged by the FCC that TP-Link's own reports contain "false or incorrect information in its applications" related to equipment authorizations for four different models of Wi-Fi 8 routers that the company hopes to sell stateside. As the saga continues to develop, we attained a statement from TP-Link on the subject, as the situation continues to develop.
Anthropic's large and sprawling S1 filing made headlines this week as the company prepares for an IPO. Within the document, it details many (but not all) of the numbers driving one of the world's foremost AI labs. Once you get past the mind-bogglingly high $800 billion in GPU and TPU contracts, the company has shown that most of its compute capacity isn't actually served to customers, and is instead dedicated to R&D for new models, features, and testing. There's a huge amount of information to sink your teeth into here, and despite what many might believe, the company's revenue per compute dollar spent is actually in Anthropic's favor, shattering the myth that tokens cost more in compute than they do for a user.
As neoclouds and hyperscalers (who rent compute out to companies like Anthropic) scale up and scale out, domains become exceedingly important. With copper materials coming up to their natural limits, eyes have turned to the photonic domain to alleviate bandwidth bottlenecks. Now, PsiQuantum has entered the domain, showcasing a prototype photonic switch that loses less light than other devices on the market, and the company expects to develop and mature its solution and is likely to enter the photonic switch market.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Cadence has revealed Maestro, a suite of tuned LLM's, designed specifically to work in EDA flows using the company's in-house suite of agentic tools. We've covered the rise of agentic EDA tools closely, and Cadence's Maestro suite appears to be the company's own shot across the bow in helping its customers automate elements of their own chip designs. In initial results compared with general-purpose AI models, Cadence claims up to a 30% improvement in the quality of results and that Maestro effectively uses fewer tokens for the same task, with up to 5x the token efficiency compared to off-the-shelf AI models.
But all of those new AI chips have to come from somewhere. With the ongoing, ceaseless AI buildout, firms are looking to secure their supply chains, with Nvidia one of the chief companies among them. As demand continues to soar, the very real limitation of fabs is particularly highlighted in the realm of the substrates used to create PCBs. Ajinomoto Build-up Film, or ABF, is one of the hottest commodities in the chipmaking industry as a result, and Nvidia has announced plans to secure the material from Ibiden, in addition to other critical materials used in chip packaging, testing, and more. Of course, Nvidia isn't doing this out of the goodness of its own heart; it's doing it in exchange for reserved production capacity.
The ramifications of AI are still being felt across the globe, but if you've been on social media over the past several weeks, you may have found that there's one particular trend: Decompilation and recompilation of video games, recompiled to work natively on PCs. We detail how additional software tools like Reverse Engineer Anything and Ghidra are powering the boom.

To read any of the articles we mention above, as well as unlock Bench, you'll need to purchase a Tom's Hardware Premium subscription. Your support goes a long way in helping us to publish deeper, more insightful articles that might not otherwise be covered.
Sayem Ahmed is the Subscription Editor at Tom's Hardware. He covers a broad range of deep dives into hardware, both new and old, including the CPUs, GPUs, and everything else that uses a semiconductor. articles.title: Petits mais très costauds, des remorqueurs de nouvelles générations rejoignent la Marine française
articles.text:
La Direction générale de l’armement a notifié aux chantiers Piriou un marché de seize remorqueurs-pousseurs nouvelle génération pour la Marine nationale. Adaptés à la manœuvre des sous-marins nucléaires, ces RP30NG sont attendus dès 2028.
La Marine nationale poursuit le renouvellement de sa flotte de remorqueurs. La Direction générale de l'armement (DGA) a indiqué, jeudi 29 octobre, avoir notifié aux chantiers Piriou, entreprise française spécialisée dans la construction et la réparation navales de navires en acier et aluminium, le marché d’acquisition de seize remorqueurs-pousseurs de nouvelle génération, désignés RP30NG. Quatre navires sont commandés ferme, les douze autres restant en option. Ils sont destinés aux bases navales de l'Hexagone et d'Outre-Mer et assureront les manœuvres des sous-marins nucléaires au port, mais aussi des missions de lutte antipollution, de surveillance maritime et d’action de l'État en mer.
Des remorqueurs taillés pour les sous-marins nucléaires
Sur le papier, le remorqueur RP30NG n'est pas un colosse, avec ses 26 mètres de long pour 370 tonnes en charge complète. On est évidemment loin des 261 mètres du Charles de Gaulle et de ses 42 500 tonnes à pleine charge. Il est plutôt du genre petit, mais costaud. Ses 30 tonnes de traction désignent par exemple l'effort qu'il peut fournir en tirant un autre navire. Et il ne reste pas cantonné au port, car il peut s'éloigner jusqu'à 200 milles nautiques des côtes, environ 370 kilomètres, pendant plusieurs jours.
La première mission listée par la DGA, et non des moindres, c'est toutefois celle des manœuvres de port. Les sous-marins nucléaires lanceurs d'engins (SNLE), sous-marins nucléaires d'attaque (SNA) et bâtiments de surface de premier rang, c'est-à-dire les plus gros navires de combat de la flotte, pourront compter sur ces remorqueurs pour évoluer dans l'enceinte portuaire.
Ces navires ont aussi des allures de couteau suisse. Ils peuvent être sollicité dans différents cadres, comme la lutte contre les incendies, les opérations antipollution, et la mise en place de barrages protégeant l'accès aux ports. La servitude portuaire figure à leur programme. Au large, ils participeront à la surveillance de la Zone économique exclusive et prêteront main-forte à l'action de l'État en mer, du contrôle des pêches à l'assistance.
Un ADN civil pour gagner du temps
Plutôt que de repartir d'une feuille blanche, les RP30NG reprennent le design de la gamme civile de remorqueurs Piriou. Il a toutefois été adapté à un exercice très spécifique, à savoir la manœuvre des sous-marins nucléaires. Un choix pragmatique, puisque s'appuyer sur une gamme existante permet de produire ces navires en série et de réduire les délais de livraison.
Le contrat conclut par la DGA se déroule en deux temps. En fait, dans l'immédiat, seuls quatre navires sont réellement commandés. C'est ce qu'on appelle une commande ferme, et ces remorqueurs seront d'ailleurs construits à Concarneau, dans le Finistère. Les douze autres restent en option, ce qui signifie que l'État pourra les commander plus tard, s'il le souhaite. Il en va de même pour le maintien en condition opérationnelle, autrement dit l'entretien et les réparations qui permettent aux remorqueurs de rester prêts à intervenir.
Ce marché fait partie du programme de renouvellement de la flotte de remorqueurs de la Marine nationale. Il fait suite à un premier contrat signé en 2020, qui avait abouti à la livraison de quatre RP30. Dès 2028, la version « NG » rejoindra à son tour les Services de moyens portuaires des bases navales, dans l'Hexagone mais aussi en Outre-Mer.

articles.title: OpenAI restringirá lo que ChatGPT responde a adolescentes sobre armas, aunque la pregunta parezca inocente
articles.text:
OpenAI anunció el 30 de octubre que limitará la información sobre armas que ChatGPT entrega a usuarios menores de 18 años, incluso cuando la pregunta parezca inofensiva. La medida forma parte de un paquete de salvaguardas contra la violencia real, que la empresa empezará a aplicar en las próximas semanas.
Según la publicación oficial de la compañía, la versión de ChatGPT para adolescentes restringirá la información práctica sobre armas y sistemas de seguridad que pueda usarse para facilitar actos violentos. El límite rige aunque no haya señales de intención violenta en la conversación.
Las políticas de OpenAI ya prohibían ayudar a cualquier persona a planear o ejecutar actos de violencia, y limitaban la ayuda a adolescentes para conseguir armas. La nueva regla amplía esa protección a datos prácticos que antes no estaban cubiertos.
Los adolescentes podrán seguir usando ChatGPT para prevenir o desescalar la violencia, buscar apoyo y contactar a un adulto de confianza, precisó la empresa.
Cómo decidirá ChatGPT quién es menor de edad
OpenAI dijo que reforzó su sistema de predicción de edad, lanzado el año pasado. El sistema analiza varias señales, como los patrones de comportamiento, para estimar si un usuario es menor de 18 años, y traslada a los adolescentes a la experiencia con más protecciones.
Quien sea clasificado como menor por error podrá confirmar que es adulto con un trámite rápido a través de Persona, el socio de verificación de edad de la empresa. Así se le retirarán las protecciones adicionales.
La compañía agregó que busca aplicar los límites más estrictos también cuando prevea que una persona es menor, aunque sus conversaciones no muestren intención violenta.
Cambios que alcanzan a todos los usuarios
Para todos los usuarios, sin importar la edad ni el motivo de la consulta, ChatGPT dará menos detalle sobre ataques masivos del pasado. Eso incluye las armas y el equipo utilizados, cómo se obtuvieron y las comparaciones de magnitud del daño que puedan aumentar la notoriedad del atacante.
OpenAI aclaró que los usuarios podrán seguir pidiendo ayuda para entender esos hechos, el impacto en las víctimas y las señales de alerta que permiten prevenir nuevos casos.
Además, cuando una conversación muestre que alguien está obsesionado con la violencia o con causar un daño grave a otra persona, ChatGPT podrá cerrar el chat de forma automática. Si ocurre varias veces, la empresa podrá pausar la cuenta de manera temporal.
Con el control parental, los padres vinculan su cuenta a la de sus hijos. En julio, OpenAI amplió las alertas para avisarles si la cuenta del adolescente era desactivada por violar las normas sobre violencia. Ahora trabaja en notificarles también cuando la cuenta se pause por hablar de forma reiterada de violencia.
La empresa informó que realizó más de 200 denuncias a las autoridades en el tercer trimestre de 2026 por amenazas inminentes de violencia, y afirmó que esos avisos ayudaron a frustrar planes violentos.
El anuncio llega, según Reuters, en medio del escrutinio creciente a las empresas de IA por los riesgos de los chatbots para los jóvenes. La agencia recordó que este mes la organización sin fines de lucro Common Sense Media halló que la versión para adolescentes de ChatGPT avisaba a los padres tarde o nunca cuando las cuentas registraban conversaciones sobre suicidio, autolesiones o trastornos alimentarios.
OpenAI publicará su primer informe de seguridad comunitaria a principios de 2027, con datos del segundo semestre de 2026, y lo actualizará cada seis meses.

articles.title: AutoFull Unveils the C3 Pro Gaming Chair Series
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
AutoFull Unveils the C3 Pro Gaming Chair Series
AutoFull, a leading esports peripherals brand, today announced the launch of the C3 Pro Series, a new line of gaming chairs designed for a new generation of gamers. Guided by the idea of "The Gaming Chair to Start With," the series combines distinctive gaming aesthetics with adjustable lumbar support and a choice of configurations to suit different comfort needs and preferences.
The C3 Pro Series features two models: C3 Pro Standard and C3 Pro Advanced. While the Standard focuses on essential lumbar support for everyday gaming, the Advanced adds active seat ventilation and heating, a larger upgraded seat, and a retractable footrest for a more feature-rich comfort experience.Cool. Cozy. Custom Fit. Core Features of the C3 Pro Series
Cool: Lightning-Inspired Design
Inspired by the energy of a lightning strike, the C3 Pro Series features a bold silhouette and embroidered lightning motifs that extend across the backrest's side wings, bringing a dynamic, futuristic look to the gaming chair.
The series launches in two colorways: Flash, featuring a silver-and-black combination, and Flare, featuring black and gold. Both share the same distinctive design language, offering different expressions of the series' bold gaming aesthetic.
Cozy: Active Seat Ventilation and Heating
Available on the C3 Pro Advanced, the integrated seat ventilation and heating system gives players more control over their seating comfort across changing temperatures.
Dual fans circulate air through the seat to help reduce heat buildup during extended gaming sessions, while dual graphene heating pads provide adjustable warmth when the room gets chilly. Three ventilation levels and three heating levels let users tailor their experience. A 15-minute automatic shutoff and overheating protection provide additional safety features.
The C3 Pro Advanced also features a larger upgraded seat and a retractable footrest, giving players more room to settle in and another way to relax between matches.
Custom Fit: Adjustable Lumbar Support
Support is central to the C3 Pro Series. Adjustable lumbar support lets players fine-tune the position of lower-back support to suit their preferred sitting position, whether they are gaming, studying, or spending time at a desk.
The C3 Pro Standard focuses on essential lumbar support and everyday comfort, making it a practical starting point for first-time gaming chair buyers and those upgrading from a basic chair. The C3 Pro Advanced builds on that foundation with additional comfort features for players who want more flexibility in how they sit and relax.Choose Your C3 Pro
The C3 Pro Series offers two configurations designed around different needs and priorities.
- C3 Pro Standard—Essential Support: Designed for first-time gaming chair buyers and upgraders who want core lumbar support, distinctive styling, and the essentials for everyday gaming.
- C3 Pro Advanced—Enhanced Comfort: Adds active seat ventilation and heating, a larger upgraded seat, and a retractable footrest for players seeking a more feature-rich comfort experience.
Both models share the series' lightning-inspired design, while their distinct configurations help shoppers choose the features that matter most to them.
Availability
The AutoFull C3 Pro Series is now available in the United States through the AutoFull official website and Amazon, with availability in the EU beginning November 2, 2026. Both C3 Pro Standard and C3 Pro Advanced will be available through the respective regional stores.

articles.title: 'Online exams are now a waste of time': Top UC Berkeley professor calls time on homework grades as students are increasingly cheating using AI
articles.text:
'Online exams are now a waste of time': Top UC Berkeley professor calls time on homework grades as students are increasingly cheating using AI
Who did your homework?
- Berkeley professor Richard Borcherds says he no longer grades homework
- The renowned mathematician stated that it is amost impossible to spot a human written submission among those created with AI
- Grading in Borcherds’ classes are now conducted with in-person exams, completed without resorting to electronic devices
Professor Richard Borcherds of the University of California, Berkeley, has revealed he has abandoned grading homework for his math students.
The decision appears to have been made following an improvement in AI-produced homework, which has left educators unable to spot human-penned submissions from those completed using AI.
British-born Borcherds – whose award-winning work includes infinite-dimensional algebras and is currently researching quantum field theory – has determined that his students will be assessed using traditional exams, without reliance on electronic devices.
The decision follows Berkeley’s previous evaluation of AI detection software that it found was unreliable, and prompted the university to allow professors to formulate their own AI policies within the course syllabus.
"Grading for correctness"
AI has changed the game as far as educators are concerned. While some appear content to let students submit work produced however they see fit, others are taking a more determined approach. Professor Borcherds has clearly seen a change in scores as the use of AI among his math students has increased.
“Online exams are now a waste of time as several students just use AI to answer the questions. I cannot tell which students are using AI, but I notice the average score increases a lot in online exams.”
Borcherds explained that what he calls “grading for correctness” essentially pushes students towards using AI. They’re employing a tool that can be guaranteed to produce the correct answer.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“Grading for correctness just adds a huge incentive for them to use AI for homework instead of doing it themselves and penalizes students for honesty. And paying to grade AI generated answers is a waste of time and money.”
Difficult assessments
Other educators have expressed similar concerns about AI, although to date none seem to have taken Borcherds more traditional stance on the technology. Some have found, however, that giving students the time and space to use AI has skewed their results, and limiting access to the technology provides more realistic grades.
Berkeley has previous explored the use of AI detection and found it lacking. By putting its professors in charge of determining departmental expectations of AI use in students, the university has given its educators the power to expect better from their students.
Professor Borcherds could be set to lead the way on this, and perhaps once this story attracts attention, more educators will take a stronger view of AI assistance in homework and assessments.

articles.title: Google, Anthropic and others to support new AI crawling opt-out standard - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google, Anthropic and others to support new AI crawling opt-out standard
Google LLC, Microsoft Corp., Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC today announced plans to support an upcoming website crawling standard.
The technology will enable website operators to block artificial intelligence developers from using their content to train their models.
Many websites contain a text file titled “robots.txt” that informs crawlers what content they may access. A publisher can use the file to block scraping across the board or only make specific webpages inaccessible. It’s also possible to include certain other instructions. For example, a company can ask crawlers not to visit its website too often.
Website operators historically used robots.txt files to manage how search engines interact with their properties. Nowadays, the technology also helps regulate the activity of the scrapers with which AI providers collect training data.
A company that wishes to disallow training-related scraping must make multiple edits to its website’s robots.txt file. In particular, it needs to add a separate entry for every single AI provider. If an AI provider uses multiple scrapers to collect data, each scraper requires its own robots.txt entry.
The crawling standard Google, Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI are backing aims to simplify the process. It would allow website operators to block all scrapers that collect training data for generative AI models with a single robots.txt entry. The setting wouldn’t apply to models that “perform exclusively non-generative tasks.”
The structure of robots.txt files follows a standardized format called the Robots Exclusion Protocol. Google, Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI plan to incorporate their crawling standard into the format. They have already submitted a draft version of their proposal to the Internet Engineering Task Force, the nonprofit that maintains the Robots Exclusion Protocol.
Microsoft stated in a blog post that it will also provide a crawling setting called AI Grounding. It’s designed for situations where an AI model seeks to access a webpage in order to answer a user question rather than to collect training data.
Microsoft’s setting will enable website operators to prevent its services from sending such requests. The feature will also extend to third-party AI tools that use Microsoft technologies to process prompts.
OpenAI plans to offer similar controls. Both the ChatGPT developer and Microsoft intend to add support for the crawling standard in the coming months, while Google will follow suit sometime next year. Meta Platforms Inc. expressed support for the idea behind the technology but hasn’t yet committed to implementing it.

articles.title: El peor día de Intel desde 1974: cayeron sus acciones 28,58%
articles.text:
Las acciones de Intel se desplomaron 28,58% al cierre de la jornada de este viernes 30 de octubre de 2026 y terminaron en USD 65,76, frente a los USD 92,07 del jueves.
La baja respondió a un pronóstico para el cuarto trimestre inferior a las expectativas: la empresa prevé ingresos de entre USD 15.000 millones y USD 16.000 millones, cuando los analistas consultados por LSEG esperaban USD 17.070 millones.
Intel también anticipó una ganancia ajustada de 25 centavos por acción, por debajo de los 43 centavos previstos por el mercado. La caída equivalió a una pérdida de USD 26,31 por acción en una sola sesión.
El gráfico de Google muestra que Intel abrió a USD 68,36, alcanzó un máximo de USD 68,77 y tocó un mínimo de USD 63,20. Durante gran parte del día, la acción osciló entre USD 64 y USD 68, lejos de los USD 92,07 del cierre anterior. Tras la rueda regular, cotizaba a USD 65,23.
El peor día de Intel desde 1974
La caída de 28,58% fue la más pronunciada para Intel desde 1974, de acuerdo con Yahoo Finance. El mercado castigó las proyecciones de la empresa para el cuarto trimestre, que quedaron por debajo de las expectativas de los analistas.
La presión sobre la acción había comenzado en las operaciones posteriores al cierre del jueves 29 de octubre, cuando Intel anticipó ingresos y ganancias inferiores a lo esperado, según Reuters.
La empresa atribuyó parte de ese escenario a la debilidad del mercado de computadoras personales y a la explosión registrada en octubre en una fábrica de Kiryat Gat, Israel.
Los chips para PC bajan, mientras crecen los centros de datos
Los resultados del tercer trimestre, terminado el 26 de septiembre, habían mostrado ingresos de USD 16.510 millones, un aumento interanual de 21% y una cifra alineada con las previsiones.
La ganancia ajustada fue de 52 centavos por acción, por encima de los 40 centavos estimados.
Sin embargo, las ventas de la división de chips para computadoras cayeron 5%, hasta USD 8.100 millones, por debajo de los USD 8.980 millones que esperaba el mercado. El negocio de centros de datos e inteligencia artificial, en cambio, creció 78% y alcanzó USD 7.300 millones, según CNBC.
El director financiero, David Zinsner, advirtió: “Vemos que la desaceleración de las PC continuará al menos durante la primera mitad del próximo año”. Intel proyecta, de acuerdo con Quartz, que el mercado de computadoras personales caerá 12% en 2026 y otro 10% en 2027.
Explosión en Israel y la falta de capacidad de producción
Zinsner señaló a Reuters que la explosión de octubre en la planta de Kiryat Gat restará unos USD 300 millones a los ingresos del cuarto trimestre y reducirá el margen bruto en unos 200 puntos básicos.
La empresa espera un impacto similar en el primer trimestre, por lo que el efecto total ascendería a unos USD 600 millones en ventas.
La fábrica estuvo detenida durante dos semanas y produce principalmente chips para centros de datos.
CNBC indicó que el accidente provocó la muerte de dos trabajadores y dejó a un tercero gravemente herido. Intel todavía evalúa cuántas obleas, los discos de silicio utilizados para fabricar chips, pueden aprovecharse.
Intel elevó su inversión prevista para 2026
Intel elevó su previsión de inversión de capital para 2026 desde USD 18.000 millones hasta USD 20.000 millones y anticipó que el gasto aumentará de forma considerable en 2027. En agosto, la compañía había reunido USD 23.000 millones mediante una oferta de acciones.
El impacto en otras empresas del sector
La caída de Intel también se reflejó en otras compañías vinculadas a los semiconductores. Según el panel de empresas relacionadas del gráfico de Google, Advanced Micro Devices perdía 10,88%, Nvidia retrocedía 4,22%, Micron Technology caía 5,30% y ASUS bajaba 4,63%.

articles.title: Como cancelar o Kindle+ (antigo Kindle Unlimited) • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Como cancelar o Kindle+ (antigo Kindle Unlimited)
Assinatura do Kindle Unlimited, agora chamado de Kindle+, pode ser cancelada pelo celular ou computador em poucos passos
Se você deseja cancelar o Kindle Unlimited ou Kindle+, precisará usar o navegador do celular ou do PC para acessar a página de gerenciamento do serviço da Amazon. Se você cansou, precisa parar de pagar ou não vê mais utilidade no Kindle+, siga os passos abaixo para interromper as futuras cobranças mensais da assinatura.
Se você acessou a página de assinaturas da Amazon e não conseguiu encontrar a opção de cancelamento do Kindle Unlimited, pode ser que você tenha feito a adesão pela Play Store do celular.
Nesse caso, você precisará acessar as opções de assinaturas da Play Store e procurar pelo Kindle Unlimited ou Kindle+ entre as inscrições para cancelar o serviço.
Não é possível cancelar o Kindle+ (Kindle Unlimited) pelo próprio dispositivo Kindle ou app de leitura Kindle. Mas você pode usar o próprio celular que tem o aplicativo instalado para fazer o cancelamento usando o navegador.
Sim, mas não instantaneamente. Os livros que você emprestou do Kindle+ ainda ficarão disponíveis durante a vigência da assinatura, ou seja, até a próxima data em que seria feita uma nova cobrança. Após esse período, os livros serão devolvidos automaticamente.
Já os livros comprados individualmente permanecerão na sua biblioteca, independentemente de ter ou não uma assinatura do Kindle+ ativa.

articles.title: Intel shifts production capacity from consumer to server CPUs in face of 'unprecedented' AI demand — company navigating 'one of the most significant supply shortages in history'
articles.text:
Intel shifts production capacity from consumer to server CPUs in face of 'unprecedented' AI demand — company navigating 'one of the most significant supply shortages in history'
Client platforms struggle to get memory anyway, right?
Although the consumer PC market is shrinking and will continue to shrink in the coming quarters, Intel is confident that the overwhelming demand from the AI industry for everything that can compute or store data will offset declines in the client space. To that end, the company is reallocating some of its capacity from client to data center CPUs, expanding its Fab 24 in Ireland to make more Xeons, has begun equipment installation into Fab 62 in Arizona ahead of schedule and vows to make 18A chips there, and is expanding its advanced packaging capacity in New Mexico and Malaysia.
"The industry continues to navigate one of the most significant supply shortages in history, driven by the unprecedented demand for Super Intelligence," said Lip-Bu Tan, chief executive of Intel, during the company's earnings call. "Against this backdrop, I am pleased by the progress we made growing our server supply in Q3. I am mindful about the ongoing challenges we face in the future quarters to keep pace with server demand."
More Intel 3-based Xeons
Intel's manufacturing expansion comes as demand for server processors continues to exceed supply despite substantial production increases over the next several quarters. The company's Data Center and AI (DCAI) business generated $7.3 billion in revenue in the third quarter of 2026, up 17% sequentially and nearly 80% year-over-year. Intel expects demand for data center CPUs to remain strong in 2027 – 2028 as AI infrastructure operators deploy more CPU-intensive agentic and inference workloads.
To meet demand for Xeon CPUs in the coming years, one of Intel's immediate priorities is to increase output of Xeon 6 'Granite Rapids' processors, which are made using its Intel 3 process technology. The company recently began expanding production capacity at its Fab 24 manufacturing complex near Leixlip, Ireland, but this capacity will only come online by the end of 2027, unless the move can be accelerated.
To further increase its Intel 3 capacity, Intel plans to convert some manufacturing resources at its Oregon facilities from Intel 18A to Intel 3. These resources were originally intended to manufacture Panther Lake client processors, but weaker PC demand has allowed Intel to prioritize higher-demand data center products. The company expects the additional Intel 3 capacity in Oregon to enter production in the second half of 2027.
"What we are taking offline to put Intel 3 into Oregon is 18A wafers, which we are generally going to build Panther Lake products," said Dave Zinsner, chief financial officer of Intel. "We see the opportunity with some of that capacity freed up to go produce more data center wafers."
Granite Rapids has already become Intel's fastest ramping server processor family, but demand continues to exceed available supply, according to the company's management. Intel is also improving manufacturing yields and reducing production cycle times to extract more usable processors from its existing capacity. According to the company, Intel 3 manufacturing costs have declined by approximately 15% since the first quarter of 2026.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Prepping for Diamond Rapids, Nova Lake
Intel is also accelerating the expansion of its leading-edge manufacturing operations in Arizona. The company is ramping Intel 18A production at Fab 52 and is accelerating equipment installation into the adjacent Fab 62, which is set to become the company's second high-volume manufacturing facility for 18A, 18A-P, and derivative process technologies.
These investments will support future Intel 18A/18A-P-based products, including server CPUs, although the company has not disclosed the precise allocation of manufacturing capacity between client and data center products at the facility. While the latter is natural, Intel said during the conference call that it expects to win some market share in the client space with its Core Ultra 400-series 'Nova Lake' CPUs, which will require the company to produce these parts in high volumes.
To support its capacity expansion, Intel aggressively procured new tools in the third quarter.
Not only wafers
While expanding production of Intel 3 and Intel 18A/18A-P wafers is a must to increase output of data center CPUs, producing more wafers will not necessarily solve Intel's supply problems. The company also faces shortages of advanced organic substrates required to package its multi-chiplet processors (or rather system-in-packages, or SiPs?) that rely on EMIB and/or Foveros 3D packaging technologies. Intel has been working with substrate suppliers to expand their production capacity and expects approximately 40% additional substrate capacity to become available in the second half of 2027.
"We are not only constrained on the wafer side, we are also constrained on the substrate side," Zinsner said. "So, it is important we get the substrate piece of this ramped up to be able to meet the demand."
In addition, Intel is expanding its advanced packaging operations in New Mexico and Malaysia to support growing demand from internal product groups and external customers. The company already uses its EMIB technology to connect multiple compute dies in Granite Rapids processors, while its newer Clearwater Forest Xeons combine EMIB with Foveros Direct 3D and hybrid bonding to stack Intel 18A compute dies on Intel 3 base dies. Additional packaging capacity will be essential as Intel increases production of these processors and introduces more complex multi-die products as well as assembles advanced system-in-packages using EMIB, EMIB-T, Foveros 3D, and other technologies for external clients.
"On Advanced Packaging, we are pleased by the progress we are making with EMIB and EMIB-T for our internal products," Tan said. "Both continue to see significant external customer traction as well. We continue to improve on execution, working with our supply chain to secure the capacity to meet the needs of our Advanced Packaging customers. We are also seeing robust progress in the readiness of Hybrid Bonding Interconnect (HBI), which is an enabler of 3D chip stacking for our upcoming server products."
Capital needed
Intel's expansions will require substantial capital. Intel expects its capital expenditure (CapEx) budget to reach approximately $20 billion in 2026 and increase significantly in 2027 (though it did not reveal any firm numbers). The company said firm purchase orders to semiconductor equipment suppliers increased by nearly 40% sequentially as it secured tools for its manufacturing expansion. Intel is also evaluating opportunities to accelerate construction of its semiconductor manufacturing complex in Ohio, where the first major structural truss was recently installed.
"We have made good progress securing the equipment required to support our growth plans with firm purchase orders to equipment suppliers increasing nearly 40% sequentially," Zinsner said. "We are also accelerating clean room build-outs, including Fab 62 in Arizona and exploring opportunities to accelerate in Ohio.
Yet Intel's capacity expansion will take time to produce results. New equipment must be installed and qualified, additional wafers must pass through lengthy manufacturing cycles, and substrate suppliers must increase their output (which will likely require them to procure new tools and install them) before Intel can ship more finished processors. Consequently, the company expects supply constraints to remain particularly severe during the first half of 2027, even as the client PC market is set to continue contracting.
Nevertheless, Intel expects its data center business to continue growing and believes that additional manufacturing capacity, higher yields, and improved substrate availability will enable it to capitalize on demand for AI infrastructure in the second half of 2027 and beyond.

articles.title: Intel Fab 28 Shutdown to Cost $600 Million in Lost Revenue, Production to Restart Soon
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
Intel Fab 28 Shutdown to Cost $600 Million in Lost Revenue, Production to Restart Soon
Intel's global foundry operations are crucial to the company's revenue generation, and impacting any part of the supply chain directly harms the business. When explosions occurred at Fab 28 in Kiryat Gat, Israel, Intel's operations there briefly halted 10 nm node production for two weeks. During this time, the assessment of both equipment and production output is estimated to result in about $300 million of lost revenue in the upcoming Q4 2026, as well as another $300 million in Q1 2027. Just two weeks of downtime has destroyed a massive amount of 10 nm wafers that Fab 28 has been manufacturing.
Intel CFO David ZinsnerWe have been shut down for about two weeks. We feel like we are going to be starting up production here by the end of this week. While we are doing that, we are trying to assess all the wafers that are in the line and what is usable and what is not usable from those materials. This is somewhat of an early assessment, both really of 4Q and of 1Q. But I think the current thinking is that we will have about a $300 million impact to the fourth quarter. That is likely to be similar in the first quarter.
Intel's Fab 28 in Israel has been manufacturing I/O dies for Xeon 6 "Granite Rapids" as well as compute tiles for Xeon 5 "Emerald Rapids" CPUs. Intel has rebranded the node name to Intel 7, but it is still essentially the 10 nm technology. Just two weeks of downtime is destroying a massive amount of wafers, as it takes roughly six months for leading-edge nodes to complete wafer production from start to finish. Hence, interrupting that has resulted in significant losses spread over two quarters.
Source:
				Intel Q3 2026 Earnings			
	
	
	
		
	
		
6 Comments on Intel Fab 28 Shutdown to Cost $600 Million in Lost Revenue, Production to Restart Soon
Also the explosion had nothing to do with any geo-political issues.
There is a reason TSMC also needs to pull all the stops to populate those new fabs. And I remember quite a few articles about workforce from the US having 'different' demands ;) That's cultural alignment for ya. Its not like the US magically opens a can of fab workers overnight. And then, you might have the numbers, but do you have the seniority in the work force too? You can't run a plant on juniors.^

articles.title: F1, Top 14 et films récents : CANAL+ tombe à 15,99€/mois pendant 2 ans ce weekend
articles.text:
Jusqu’au 2 novembre, Canal+ relance une vente flash qui ramène son abonnement de base sous la barre des 16 € pendant deux ans. L’offre CANAL+ à 15,99 €/mois pendant 24 mois, puis 24,99 €/mois, réunit cinéma récent et grands championnats, mais elle engage sur deux ans et laisse de côté Netflix comme HBO Max.
Canal+ n’a pas touché au contenu de son offre d’entrée de gamme, seulement à son prix. Pendant cette vente flash, l’abonnement CANAL+ passe de 24,99 € à 15,99 € par mois pour les 24 premiers mois, soit 9 € d’économie mensuelle et 216 € sur la durée de l’engagement.
L’offre flash CANAL+ à 15,99 €/mois est réservée aux nouveaux abonnés, sans abonnement Canal+ le mois précédent. Elle vise d’abord ceux qui veulent un seul abonnement pour le cinéma récent et le sport de la semaine, sans empiler les plateformes.
L’abonnement CANAL+ est à 15,99 € par mois pendant 24 mois au lieu de 24,99 €, directement chez Canal+, pour les nouveaux abonnés.
Pourquoi choisir l’offre CANAL+ ?
- Des films six mois après la salle : Les films sortis au cinéma arrivent sur Canal+ six mois après leur sortie en salles. Pour qui va peu au cinéma, c’est le moyen de rattraper les films de l’année sans les louer un par un.
- Plusieurs sports sous le même toit : Le match du mercredi de la Ligue des champions, la Formule 1, le MotoGP, la Premier League et le Top 14 figurent dans l’offre. Un fan de rugby et un amateur de sports mécaniques y trouvent leur compte dans le même abonnement.
- Direct, replay et deux écrans : Les programmes se regardent en direct ou en replay, sur deux écrans en même temps. Un foyer peut suivre un Grand Prix dans le salon pendant qu’une série tourne sur une tablette.
Du Grand Prix du dimanche au film du samedi soir
L’offre donne accès aux chaînes Canal+, Canal+ Box Office, Canal+ Grand Écran, Canal+ Sport 360, Canal+ Docs et Canal+ Kids, ainsi qu’aux séries et documentaires maison. Le replay est le vrai confort : un programme manqué en direct se regarde plus tard, à l’heure qui vous arrange. Comme le détaille notre avis sur Canal+, l’application fonctionne sur le web, les smartphones, les tablettes, les consoles PlayStation et Xbox, les téléviseurs connectés et des boîtiers comme l’Apple TV 4K ou le Fire TV, avec une lecture hors ligne. Nous y jugions l’interface bien pensée, même si elle reste sujette à quelques bugs.
Le profil idéal regarde à la fois du sport et du cinéma, et préfère une seule facture à trois abonnements. Les amateurs de Top 14, de Formule 1 ou de MotoGP y trouvent un rendez-vous régulier, et les films de l’année arrivent sans surcoût. L’intérêt baisse si vous voulez toute la Ligue des champions : l’offre mentionne le match du mercredi, pas l’ensemble de la compétition. Elle convient mal aussi à qui cherche surtout des séries américaines, puisque Netflix, HBO Max et Paramount+ ne sont pas inclus.
Ce que cette formule ne remplace pas
Cette offre est l’entrée de gamme de Canal+ : les catalogues de Netflix, HBO Max ou Paramount+ demandent une formule supérieure comme Canal+ Ciné Séries. Face aux plateformes de streaming seules, son atout reste le cinéma récent, qui y arrive bien plus tôt que chez les autres services. En contrepartie, nous relevions un prix plus élevé que la concurrence et assez peu de productions exclusives, deux points que la remise atténue sans les effacer. Pour situer Canal+ face à Netflix, Prime Video ou Disney+, notre comparatif des meilleures plateformes de streaming détaille les forces de chacune.
✅ Les points forts
- 216 € d’économie sur les 24 mois d’engagement
- Les films disponibles six mois après leur sortie en salles
- Formule 1, MotoGP, Premier League et Top 14 inclus
- Direct, replay et deux écrans simultanés
- Une application disponible sur la plupart des écrans
❌ Les limites
- Un engagement de 24 mois, puis 24,99 € par mois
- Une offre réservée aux nouveaux abonnés
- Netflix, HBO Max et Paramount+ non inclus
- Peu de contenus en 4K, selon notre avis
La vente flash court jusqu’au 2 novembre : vérifiez le tarif de 15,99 € par mois et les conditions d’engagement sur la page de l’offre avant de souscrire.
À 15,99 € par mois, cette vente flash rend l’abonnement Canal+ plus abordable, sans rien retirer du cinéma récent ni du sport annoncé. Les 216 € économisés sur deux ans sont réels, puisque le tarif remonte ensuite à 24,99 €, son prix habituel. Pour un foyer qui suit la F1, le Top 14 ou la Premier League et regarde les films de l’année, l’abonnement couvre beaucoup pour un tarif contenu.
L’engagement reste le vrai point à peser : vingt-quatre mois, c’est deux saisons sportives complètes. Si vous regardez surtout des séries Netflix ou HBO Max, ou si le sport ne vous intéresse pas, une plateforme seule vous servira mieux. Si au contraire vous hésitiez à revenir sur Canal+ pour la F1 ou les films récents, la fenêtre ouverte jusqu’au 2 novembre mérite d’être regardée de près.

articles.title: Google X co-founder Sebastian Thrun raises $130M for AI engineering startup Dulo - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google X co-founder Sebastian Thrun raises $130M for AI engineering startup Dulo
Dulo Inc., a startup co-founded by prominent artificial intelligence researcher Sebastian Thrun, has raised $130 million in funding.
The Information broke the news of the investment on Thursday. Dulo co-founder Adrian Aoun confirmed the report in a post on X.
Before launching Dulo with Thrun (pictured) earlier this year, Aoun sold an early natural language processing startup called Wavii Inc. to Google LLC for over $30 million. He has also invested in companies such as Pinterest Inc. Thrun, in turn, co-founded Google’s X research lab. He led the X program that later became Waymo and helped establish Google Brain, a precursor to Google DeepMind.
Dulo’s round included contributions from former Google Chief Executive Officer Eric Schmidt and Ram Shriram, one of the search giant’s first investors. They were joined by Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff, famed venture capitalist John Doerr and more than a half-dozen startup funds. Dulo didn’t disclose its valuation.
The company’s one-page website states that it’s developing foundation models optimized for hardware design tasks. In August, Thrun listed robotics among Dulo’s focus areas. It’s possible the company’s AI is meant to speed up the development of industrial robots and autonomous vehicles.
Thrun joined Google in 2007 after leading the development of Stanley, an early self-driving vehicle that helped kickstart the autonomous driving market. He later founded a flying taxi startup with financial backing from Google co-founder Larry Page.
It’s unclear what hardware design tasks Dulo’s models will automate. One possibility is that the startup hopes to optimize engineering simulations, which hardware teams use to check their product designs for flaws before manufacturing them. Dulo’s website says it’s looking to facilitate “manufacturing at lightspeed.”
Several other engineering-focused AI startups are also working to optimize simulations. One recently funded player, Vinci4D Inc., has built a platform that automates the so-called meshing phase of simulation projects. Meshing is a process through which engineers turn a product’s blueprint into a collection of small, three-dimensional shapes. That arrangement reduces the amount of hardware needed to run simulations.
Other AI startups are working to speed up partially differentiated equations. Simulators rely on such equations to predict the behavior of hardware systems under real-world conditions.
Dulo’s most prominent venture-backed rival is Prometheus Inc., an engineering AI startup co-led by Amazon.com Inc. founder Jeff Bezos. The company raised $12 billion in funding earlier this year from Bezos and a group of financial institutions. Like Dulo, Prometheus is using AI to speed up the development of complex hardware systems such as robots.

articles.title: Developer builds a complete Intel 486 PC emulator in a browser — 100% pure-JavaScript Retro486 includes modular tabs for screen, motherboard, storage, expansion cards, and more
articles.text:
Developer builds a complete Intel 486 PC emulator in a browser — 100% pure-JavaScript Retro486 includes modular tabs for screen, motherboard, storage, expansion cards, and more
There’s FreeDOS and classic games like Doom ready to play around with, or you can use your own disk images.
Developer Jan de Jager has created a full Intel 486 PC system in a browser. On the e486-web GitHub page, de Jager boasts that the emulator is coded in 100% pure JavaScript. The project’s fuller title is the Retro486 Modular Browser PC. Claude gets a development credit, so we guess you could say e486-web was (partially) vibe-coded.
The live demo you can boot with a single click is impressive, with tabs to interact with and configure your browser-based, dependency-free Intel 80486DX2-66 PC in a browser. The first tab is dubbed the CRT monitor, and this is where you will spend the most time using the command line, apps, and games. However, it is also very appealing to be able to adjust your PC configuration in the tabs for Motherboard & Slots, Storage Bay, Custom Card Studio, and System & Diagnostics.
I couldn’t resist taking the e486-web for a spin using the live demo. The CRT monitor screen is totally charming, with various display options including color and scanlines, and tributes to classic CRTs with green phosphor, amber, or paperwhite displays. This is the screen where you will also type DOS commands and interact with whatever you get to run.
The next tab in this comprehensive 486 PC system emulator lets you pick a motherboard design and, probably more importantly, add and remove expansion cards. The default system comes with a VLB graphics card, Sound Blaster 16 ISA card, a multi-I/O controller, network card, and more. All the cards seem to be configurable. A Custom Card Studio tab lets you create and test more cards, and it looks quite advanced.
I spent quite a lot of time in the Storage Bay tab, switching through the OS and software disks inside the “1-Click bundled & Cached Disks” collection. FreeDOS started fine, but I got some errors when I wanted to test some of the games in the library, which includes Doom, Wolfenstein 3D, and more. Though tempted to find and install Syndicate on the hard disk that the emulator can create and configure, I didn't get around to it yet. However, the Bullfrog classic is one of the first games I played on an actual 486DX2 system in the 1990s, and I also played it on Amiga. This browser-based emulator features browser persistence, so e486-web settings can be maintained between sessions, and it automatically caches ROMs, floppy images, and custom uploaded .img/.iso files for your convenience.
Another tab in this extensive system emulator is called System & Diagnostics. Here you can switch the CPU to a different model, view the CPU registers, and nose around in RAM, VRAM, storage, BIOS, boot sectors, and so on.
Currently e486-web is in version 0.1, and the GitHub shows that most files were uploaded/updated about a week ago. Some files are just two days old, though, so hopefully wrinkles are busily being ironed out by de Jager and Claude. The presentation of this no-downloads live emulator, and the conveniently tabbed interface and configuration options, show lots of promise.

articles.title: Samsung pode lançar tablet dobrável com tela de 17 polegadas • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Samsung pode lançar tablet dobrável com tela de 17 polegadas
Rumores indicam que projeto avançou e pode dar origem ao Galaxy Z Tab. Dispositivo teria 8 polegadas quando fechado.
A Samsung parece realmente disposta a trazer sua tecnologia de display dobrável para outros segmentos mobile. Agora, rumores indicam que a companhia sul-coreana teria avançado no fabricação de um um tablet dobrável, com tela de 17 polegadas.
Segundo o vazamento, o aparelho fechado já se aproximaria do tamanho alcançado pelo Galaxy Z Fold 8 quando aberto, 8 polegadas. De acordo com o GSMArena, os primeiros relatos sobre o projeto surgiram no fim de agosto, quando a mesma fonte afirmou que um dobrável de 17 polegadas estaria em desenvolvimento na Samsung.
Há divergências, porém, sobre o formato da dobra. Uma das possibilidades seria usar uma única tela de 17 polegadas que dobraria no sentido oposto do que costumamos ver nos smartphones, desativando um dos lados. Nesse cenário, a tela permaneceria exposta e poderia facilitar danos em uma queda, por exemplo.
Outra seria adotar uma construção semelhante aos celulares, com uma tela grande na parte interna e um segundo display externo de aproximadamente 8 polegadas. Não há detalhes sobre especificações nem previsão de lançamento comercial.
Essa ideia não é nova dentro da Samsung. Durante a SID Display Week de 2021, a Samsung Display, divisão de telas da empresa, apresentou um conceito de dispositivo com painel OLED dobrável de 17 polegadas e proporção 4:3.
O protótipo podia ser usado totalmente aberto ou parcialmente dobrado, em uma posição semelhante à de um notebook. A tecnologia continuou aparecendo em demonstrações da divisão nos anos seguintes, sendo que, em 2023, rumores chegaram a apontar um possível Galaxy Z Tab. Antes disso, a companhia lançou um “tablet dobrável”, o Galaxy View, com apenas uma tela.
O possível tablet aparece em um momento no qual a Samsung testa novos formatos para sua linha de aparelhos dobráveis. A geração atual inclui o Galaxy Z Fold 8, em formato passaporte, e o Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, que mantém o design comprido das gerações passadas.
Vazamentos recentes já apontam o desenvolvimento de uma nova geração mais extensa para 2027. Espera-se que a Samsung lance um Galaxy Z TriFold 2 e um terceiro modelo da família Galaxy Z Fold 9, que pode ser uma versão mais larga ou com configurações mais básicas.
A expansão ocorre na esteira do lançamento do iPhone Duo, primeiro smartphone dobrável da Apple. Sob a liderança de John Ternus, a empresa também pode lançar outros dobráveis nas próximas gerações.

articles.title: El satélite de centro de datos de Google ya se comunica con la Tierra: este fue su primer mensaje
articles.text:
Google recibió la primera respuesta de un chip de IA de tipo centro de datos que funciona en órbita. Ingenieros enviaron al satélite del proyecto Suncatcher la orden de escribir un haiku sobre el espacio y el modelo Gemma 4 lo devolvió a la Tierra, según informó la empresa este 30 de octubre.
El poema dice: “Blue marble below / Data streams in silent grace / Starlight feeds my core” (“Canica azul abajo / Datos que fluyen en silenciosa gracia / La luz de las estrellas alimenta mi núcleo”). Google lo recibió cuando el satélite pasaba sobre Svalbard, Noruega. Después, el equipo probó limericks (versos humorísticos de cinco líneas) sobre el espacio y consultas sobre el estado técnico del equipo.
Google lanzó el prototipo el 1 de octubre. Tardó unas tres semanas en revisar sus sistemas antes de enviar la primera consulta. Travis Beals, director sénior del área que dirige el proyecto, llamó a este paso el hito “Hello World” (“Hola, mundo”, la primera prueba que se hace con un sistema nuevo).
Un vocero de Google dijo a TechCrunch que el satélite funciona con normalidad. Gemma 4 es un modelo abierto de Google DeepMind, el laboratorio de IA de la empresa, y viajó cargado en el satélite desde antes del lanzamiento.
Cuatro chips, pero solo uno encendido a la vez
El satélite lleva cuatro unidades de procesamiento tensorial (TPU, los chips de IA diseñados por Google) y genera hasta 1 kilovatio de electricidad. TechCrunch informó que esa potencia solo alcanza para encender un chip durante unos 20 minutos seguidos, lo que complica además la comunicación con la Tierra.
El satélite despegó en un cohete Falcon 9 de SpaceX junto con más de 100 naves. Google lo concibe como el primer paso para formar redes de satélites que vuelen muy cerca unos de otros y ejecuten en órbita tareas pesadas de IA.
Las pruebas que siguen medirán cómo rinden los chips bajo estrés térmico y exposición a la radiación del espacio. La radiación puede provocar errores en la memoria que alteran datos sin activar los sistemas habituales de control. TechCrunch señaló que las pruebas en la Tierra sugerían un efecto menor en tareas de uso de modelos ya entrenados y más problemas al entrenarlos.
Dos satélites conectados llegarán en 2027
Si los chips responden bien, el siguiente paso son dos satélites con TPU, programados para 2027. Tendrán más capacidad de generar energía y probarán enlaces ópticos entre ellos, es decir, comunicación por luz directa entre una nave y otra.
Según TechCrunch, Suncatcher es el único plan de centros de datos espaciales que prevé enlaces de alta velocidad entre satélites. Los centros de datos de SpaceX también usarían láseres, pero orbitarían demasiado lejos entre sí para compartir el procesamiento. Starcloud y Cowboy Space planean tareas de IA en satélites individuales.
Alphabet, la empresa matriz de Google, tiene una participación significativa en SpaceX. TechCrunch indicó que ambas compañías necesitarán Starship, el cohete pesado de SpaceX aún en desarrollo, para lanzar sus centros de datos con costos viables.
Un análisis revisado por pares publicado este mes, según TechCrunch, estimó que SpaceX tendría que volar Starship 1.800 veces para lograr las reducciones de costo que alcanzó con sus cohetes anteriores.
El medio también recordó que las acciones de Alphabet cayeron esta semana, después de que la empresa informara que la IA en su buscador frena el crecimiento de los ingresos por publicidad.

articles.title: BrainChip Launches AKD1500 Raspberry Pi 5 Development Kit
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
BrainChip Launches AKD1500 Raspberry Pi 5 Development Kit
BrainChip Holdings Ltd (ASX: BRN, OTCQX: BRCHF, ADR: BCHPY), a global leader in ultra-low-power, fully digital, event-based neuromorphic AI, today launched the AKD1500 Raspberry Pi 5 Development Kit. The kit pairs a Raspberry Pi 5 with BrainChip's AKD1500 M.2 board, giving the millions of engineers, makers and product teams who already build on Raspberry Pi an off-the-shelf way to develop low-power, always-on AI applications - and a clear path to production on the same AKD1500 chip.
Brian Beyer, CEO, Hellbender"As an American Tier 1 for physical AI, Hellbender looks for edge technologies that can move cleanly from prototype to production. BrainChip's AKD1500 Raspberry Pi 5 kit makes it easy for engineering teams to evaluate low-power, always-on AI on familiar hardware, and we see it as a promising option for the robotics and vision applications our customers are building."
The challenge: always-on AI strains power, privacy and the path to production
A growing class of edge devices - sensors, monitors, wearables, industrial equipment and smart home products - must listen, watch or measure continuously. Running AI on these devices with conventional processors means analyzing every frame and sample, whether anything has changed, which drains batteries and adds heat. Sending the data to the cloud instead adds latency, bandwidth cost and privacy risk. And once a model is deployed, teaching it something new typically means collecting data, retraining in the cloud and pushing an update.
Developers face a second hurdle: the hardware used to build a proof of concept is often not the hardware that ships. Moving from a prototype to a production design can mean re-porting models, re-validating performance and starting over on a new platform.
The solution: event-based AI that learns on the device
AKD1500 uses BrainChip's event-based, neuromorphic architecture to process only meaningful events rather than every piece of incoming data, making it well suited to power always-on workloads such as sensing, monitoring and detection. All processing happens on the device, so applications avoid the latency, bandwidth cost and privacy exposure of the cloud.
AKD1500 also supports on-chip learning, so models can learn new classes directly on the device without cloud retraining. A developer can teach a Raspberry Pi 5 application to recognize a new keyword, gesture or object in the field, and the data stays local.
Steve Brightfield, chief product officer, BrainChip"Raspberry Pi is where many edge AI products begin. This kit puts neuromorphic AI where developers already work and gives teams a fast, low-cost way to validate applications on streaming data. Kit support will include Docker images that can be preloaded to simplify benchmarking and demos and that serve as a reference for custom neuromorphic application containers. Developers who already have a Raspberry Pi 5 with an M.2 HAT can add the production AKD1500 M.2 card and use the same software.""
From prototype to production on one chip
The kit is off the shelf and quick to set up. Teams evaluate their application on Raspberry Pi 5, then design the same AKD1500 chip into their own product with a PCIe or SPI interface to suit their system without switching to new silicon. The kit joins the AKD1500 PCIe card and AKD1500 M.2 board in BrainChip's family of AKD1500 development platforms, and teams can prototype on any of them.For developers, the kit offers:
- A familiar platform: Build and test edge AI on Raspberry Pi 5 hardware and workflows developers already know.
- Always-on efficiency: Event-based processing handles continuous sensing workloads without processing every input.
- Local learning and privacy: Add new keywords, gestures or objects on the device, with no cloud retraining and no data leaving the device.
- Free tools and models: BrainChip's MetaTF software tools and models are available at no charge through the BrainChip Developer Hub.
- One chip, prototype to product: The AKD1500 chip that runs on the kit is the same one teams design into production.
Strategic significance for BrainChip
According to MarketsandMarkets, the global edge computing market is projected to grow from $111.34 billion in 2026 to $317.39 billion by 2031, fueled by organizations prioritizing faster data processing, low-latency applications and decentralized digital infrastructure.
The AKD1500 Raspberry Pi 5 Development Kit reflects BrainChip's commitment to executing its product roadmap and delivering the production-ready tools developers need today. It advances three priorities:
- Broader developer adoption: Putting Akida in front of the Raspberry Pi community expands the pipeline of engineers who design with Akida.
- AKD1500 commercialization: Alongside the PCIe card and M.2 board, the kit completes an accessible lineup built on one chip, covering prototyping through production and creating a direct path from evaluation to chip design-ins.
- Edge AI leadership: AKD1500 brings BrainChip's event-based processing and on-chip learning to a mainstream developer platform.
Availability
The AKD1500 Raspberry Pi 5 Development Kit is available now through the BrainChip Shop. MetaTF software tools and models are available at no charge through the BrainChip Developer Hub.

articles.title: Ce Roomba lave son rouleau à 80 °C et perd 200 € pour le Black Friday de Boulanger
articles.text:
Boulanger n’a pas attendu le 27 novembre pour ouvrir son Black Friday, et les robots aspirateurs figurent en bonne place. Parmi eux, l’un des derniers Roomba d’iRobot, qui s’attaque aux taches tenaces avec un prétraitement par pulvérisation avant de passer un rouleau lavé à l’eau chaude, perd 200 € quelques mois seulement après sa sortie.
Présenté en mai avec la gamme 2026 d’iRobot, le Roomba Plus 675 Combo se place juste sous les modèles Max de la marque et a été lancé à 799 € avec sa base AutoWash. Il associe une aspiration de 30 000 Pa à un nettoyage humide en deux temps, pensé pour décoller les salissures sèches.
Boulanger l’affiche aujourd’hui à 599 € au lieu de 799 €, soit 25 % de remise sur un produit neuf vendu et expédié par l’enseigne, avec paiement en trois fois sans frais et retours prolongés jusqu’au 31 janvier 2027.
iRobot Roomba Plus 675 Combo à 599 € au lieu de 799 €
Pourquoi choisir le Roomba Plus 675 Combo ?
- Un jet sous pression qui prétraite les taches détectées, pour un nettoyage jusqu’à 40 % plus efficace selon iRobot.
- Une base qui lave le rouleau à 80 °C et le sèche à 55 °C pour éviter les odeurs.
- Un profil bas de 9,98 cm, sans tourelle, pour passer sous la plupart des meubles.
- Des seuils franchis jusqu’à 3,5 cm.
- Un indice de réparabilité de 8,2 et des pièces détachées disponibles pendant 9 ans.
Un Roomba qui reprend des couleurs
Le Roomba Plus 675 Combo reprend une bonne part des technologies du Roomba Max 875 Combo, vendu bien plus cher. Sa navigation combine un LiDAR ClearView Pro et une caméra IA capable de reconnaître plus de 300 types d’obstacles, et l’application Roomba Home gère jusqu’à trois étages, le nettoyage pièce par pièce et les zones d’exclusion. Après 25 cycles, Maniaques salue une aspiration efficace sur sols durs comme sur tapis et une brosse principale qui reste propre, sans cheveux enroulés, en ne pointant véritablement que l’application comme point faible.
Il faut aussi tenir compte de quelques limites pratiques. Le réservoir d’eau du robot, de 135 ml, est jugé idéal jusqu’à 50 m², et l’ensemble peut monter à 63 dB. Enfin, l’autonomie de 90 jours annoncée pour la base concerne le sac à poussière : filtre, brosses et rouleau restent à remplacer tous les trois à six mois selon iRobot.
Prétraiter, laver, s’entretenir seul
Une tache traitée avant d’être frottée
C’est la vraie originalité de ce modèle. Plutôt que de compter sur le seul rouleau pour ramollir une salissure sèche, le robot commence par la réhydrater avec un jet ciblé, puis passe son rouleau PowerSpin, qui s’autonettoie en continu pendant le lavage. Sa caméra repère les zones sales pour y insister, et le rouleau se relève jusqu’à 10 mm à l’approche des tapis.
Une base qui fait le gros de l’entretien
La base AutoWash plonge le rouleau dans un bain d’eau à 80 °C, élimine l’eau sale à l’aide d’une raclette, puis le sèche à l’air chaud à 55 °C. Elle vide aussi la poussière dans un sac scellé, recharge le robot en eau propre et dose automatiquement le détergent grâce à ses réservoirs de 4 litres d’eau propre et 3,3 litres d’eau sale.
✅ Les points forts
- Prétraitement des taches et rouleau lavé à l’eau chaude.
- Base AutoWash très complète, avec dosage automatique du détergent.
- Profil bas de 9,98 cm et seuils jusqu’à 3,5 cm.
- Réparabilité de 8,2 et pièces disponibles 9 ans.
❌ Les limites
- Application perfectible selon les premiers tests.
- Réservoir du robot limité à 135 ml.
- Consommables à renouveler tous les trois à six mois.
iRobot Roomba Plus 675 Combo à 599 € au lieu de 799 €
Le Roomba Plus 675 Combo marque un vrai retour en forme d’iRobot sur le lavage, avec une approche du nettoyage des taches qui le distingue de la concurrence. À 599 €, il devient une option sérieuse pour qui veut un robot autonome au quotidien.

articles.title: Hackers steal $6.3B from Binance in biggest-ever crypto heist - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Hackers steal $6.3B from Binance in biggest-ever crypto heist
Hackers have stolen about $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance, a major cryptocurrency exchange operator.
The heist is more than four times bigger than the previous largest crypto theft. TRM Labs Inc., a venture-backed blockchain intelligence startup, believes that both cyberattacks were carried out by a North Korean state-backed hacking group tracked as TraderTraitor.
About 40% of the stolen sum comprised stablecoins issued by three major crypto companies: Circle Internet Group Inc., Ripple Labs Inc. and Tether Ltd. They managed to freeze most of the funds before the hackers moved them out of reach. Binance, for its part, has set aside over $6.34 billion to cover users’ losses.
The hackers stole the funds by compromising several of the company’s wallets. One of them powers the infrastructure that Binance uses to process customers’ Ethereum transactions. According to TRM, the hackers breached the wallet late Thursday and sent its entire balance to a wallet they controlled.
TraderTraitor compromised Binance’s wallet by exploiting an Ethereum feature called EIP-7702 that the blockchain’s maintainers released last year. It enables a snippet of code called a smart contract to temporarily control a wallet. EIP-7702 only activates smart contracts if they receive authorization to run from the wallet’s operator. That authorization takes the form of an encrypted message.
The hackers used a malicious smart contract to take over Binance’s Ethereum wallet. It’s currently unclear how they obtained the authorization necessary to run such code.
According to Binance, an internal investigation determined that TraderTraitor had compromised a laptop belonging to one of its DevOps engineers. The company says that it has also “uncovered additional points of breach.”
“Developer and DevOps machines sit close to organizations’ most sensitive systems and hold credentials, tokens and deployment access,” said Kobi Sivilya, chief information security officer of cybersecurity company Checkmarx Ltd. “The question for any organization is how far an attacker could get from a single compromised workstation. Teams should review who has standing access to what systems, whether that access is appropriately limited and whether one machine can reach critical services without a second control.”
TRM determined that TraderTraitor had rehearsed the cyberattack for at least 36 hours before the theft. On Wednesday morning, the hackers deposited a small amount of funds into a malicious crypto wallet. Early Thursday, they tested some of the code that they used in the cyberattack on three different wallets.
According to Binance, the malware contained a “self-destruct mechanism” that deleted the tools the hackers installed on its infrastructure and the activity logs they generated. The mechanism made it more difficult for the company to investigate the attack. Binance did, however, determine that the hackers bypassed the approval workflows it uses to process crypto outflows.
“Organizations that rely on exchanges, custodians or any critical financial counterparty should ask what continuous visibility they have into those relationships,” Rand Davis, chief technology officer at SecurityScorecard, told SiliconANGLE in an email. “They should also ask what their playbook is when a counterparty pauses withdrawals or services. Security leaders can use this moment to map which third parties sit on their critical paths, pressure-test contingency plans, and watch for the phishing and social-engineering follow-on that typically trails a headline event of this scale.”
Binance suspended crypto deposits and withdraws on its exchange after it discovered the breach. The company has since restored deposits, but its withdrawal processing system remains offline. Binance plans to reactivate the feature on Monday.
