articles.title: “Todos nos enriquecemos” si el gobierno grava el valor del trabajo de los robots: Larry Ellison, cofundador de Oracle
articles.text:
El cofundador de Oracle, Larry Ellison, planteó durante la reciente conferencia AI World de la compañía que la inteligencia artificial podría hacer a todas las personas “más saludables y más ricas”, siempre que los gobiernos modifiquen su esquema impositivo para adaptarse a una economía dominada por la automatización.
En una sesión de preguntas y respuestas durante el discurso de cierre del evento, Ellison describió un escenario en el que los sistemas de inteligencia artificial y los robots reducirían de manera drástica el costo de bienes y servicios. El empresario rechazó la idea de que la tecnología terminará por reemplazar a los trabajadores en su totalidad y sostuvo que, en cambio, servirá para aumentar la productividad humana.
Larry Ellison descarta que la IA reemplace a todos los trabajadores
“Creo que eso es bastante absurdo”, afirmó Ellison sobre las predicciones que anticipan que la inteligencia artificial sustituirá a la totalidad de la fuerza laboral. El directivo reconoció que la automatización desplazará inevitablemente algunos empleos y puso como ejemplo los servicios de transporte compartido, en referencia a la aprobación creciente de vehículos autónomos en Las Vegas y otras ciudades.
Sin embargo, remarcó que no todos los puestos de trabajo sufrirán el mismo impacto. Durante su intervención, reveló que posee licencia de piloto y señaló que el piloto automático, pese a ser una tecnología con décadas de existencia, no ha reemplazado a los pilotos humanos.
Según su planteo, los humanos continuarán ocupando roles de supervisión en numerosas industrias, aun cuando algunas funciones de trabajadores del conocimiento evolucionen hacia la gestión de agentes de inteligencia artificial.
Para ilustrar su argumento, Ellison planteó el caso hipotético de una vivienda construida íntegramente por robots, en un escenario donde la automatización sustituyera por completo la mano de obra humana. Si el trabajo humano representaba, por ejemplo, el 80% del costo de una casa, esa proporción se abarataría de manera instantánea gracias al impacto de la automatización.
Con ese ejemplo, el empresario sentó las bases de un concepto que denominó “ingreso alto universal”, una idea que otros referentes de la industria tecnológica, entre ellos Elon Musk, ya habían planteado con anterioridad.
Gravar el valor agregado en lugar del trabajo humano
“Necesitamos pasar de gravar el trabajo humano a gravar el valor agregado”, sostuvo Ellison. “Así, cuando los robots agreguen valor, todo ese valor que agregan los robots es gravado, y podríamos tener un ingreso alto universal”.
El ingreso alto universal constituye, según el planteo del directivo, una evolución del concepto de ingreso básico universal, que consiste en un pago regular a los ciudadanos para cubrir sus necesidades esenciales. Ellison sugirió que las ganancias de productividad que generaría la inteligencia artificial podrían crear suficiente riqueza como para sostener ingresos mucho más altos, pese a una eventual disminución de la actividad laboral humana.
El empresario citó la propuesta del economista Milton Friedman sobre el impuesto negativo a la renta, a la que describió como un “impuesto a la renta inverso” capaz de contribuir a distribuir parte de la riqueza generada por la inteligencia artificial. “Los robots están agregando valor. El gobierno grava ese valor... Todos nos volvemos ricos como resultado”, expresó.
Un cambio que tomaría más de una década en concretarse
El propio Ellison admitió que su visión requeriría una transformación profunda de los sistemas fiscales actuales y que su implementación demandaría más de diez años. Pese a lo ambicioso del planteo en el contexto económico actual, el cofundador de Oracle insistió en su postura optimista: “Todo eso es viable”, concluyó.
El contraste entre el discurso de Ellison y la situación del mercado laboral tecnológico resulta relevante: el sitio especializado layoffs.fyi registró más de 135.000 despidos en el sector tecnológico durante 2026, cifra que incluye alrededor de 21.000 empleados de Oracle despedidos entre junio de 2025 y junio de 2026, además de miles adicionales durante septiembre de 2026.

articles.title: NYT Connections hints and answers for Saturday, October 31 (game #1238)
articles.text:
NYT Connections hints and answers for Saturday, October 31 (game #1238)
My clues will help you solve the NYT's Connections puzzle today and keep that streak going
A new NYT Connections puzzle appears at midnight each day for your time zone – which means that some people are always playing 'today's game' while others are playing 'yesterday's'. If you're looking for Friday's puzzle instead then click here: NYT Connections hints and answers for Friday, October 30 (game #1237).

I was on the right track with STARTING WITH DOG COMMANDS, as I saw the link between DOWNFALL, SITCOM and STAYCATION — but I thought KILLER was the fourth; something, in hindsight, that would take canine training to a whole new (and wrong) level.
After winning a Purple First for connecting the hardest group of the game, I made another error putting together the easiest/yellow group, including DIRTY among the WORDS MEANING GOOD THAT SOUND BAD.
After switching with GNARLY, another meaning for DIRTY came to mind and I was able to cobble together MARTINI SPECIFICATIONS.

What is NYT Connections?
NYT Connections is one of several increasingly popular word games made by the New York Times. It challenges you to find groups of four items that share something in common, and each group has a different difficulty level: green is easy, yellow a little harder, blue often quite tough and purple usually very difficult.
On the plus side, you don't technically need to solve the final one, as you'll be able to answer that one by a process of elimination. What's more, you can make up to four mistakes, which gives you a little bit of breathing room.
It's a little more involved than something like Wordle, however, and there are plenty of opportunities for the game to trip you up with tricks. For instance, watch out for homophones and other word games that could disguise the answers.
It's playable for free via the NYT Games site on desktop or mobile.

A man of few talents, his career is rich and various and includes the highs of interviewing Elton John and Blur; and the lows of interviewing Right Said Fred, appearing on a Channel 5 documentary about Peter Kay, and fact-checking the instruction manual for a German cooker. Somehow still affording to live in North London he is at his happiest riding his bicycle and shouting at pigeons.

articles.title: Review da Sabala DR-500: uma caixa para festas em alto e bom som • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Review da Sabala DR-500: uma caixa para festas em alto e bom som
Caixa de som Bluetooth da Sabala se destaca pelos 500 W de potência, proteção contra água e bateria gigante; confira a análise
A Sabala DR-500 é uma caixa de som Bluetooth que promete experiência completa e extremamente potente para quem precisa de volume e qualidade de áudio em diversos ambientes, desde reuniões em casa até grandes encontros ao ar livre.
O modelo se destaca ao entregar 500 W de potência em um sistema de áudio de três vias, com uma bateria colossal de 81.000 mAh, capaz de funcionar inclusive como power bank para carregar outros dispositivos.
O Tecnoblog testou a Sabala DR-500 nos últimos dias e traz todos os detalhes sobre a qualidade de som e se vale a pena o investimento.
Aviso de ética
Esse é um conteúdo patrocinado. Isso quer dizer que a marca encomendou a nossa análise, mas não comprou o resultado dela. Por isso, mantemos os pontos positivos e negativos da Sabala DR-500 de forma clara e precisa, com o objetivo de ajudar você a tomar a melhor decisão de compra.
Para mais informações, acesse a nossa Política Editorial.
A embalagem da Sabala DR-500 impressiona pelo tamanho avantajado. Ao abrir o pacote, encontramos apenas a caixa de som, o cabo de energia para carregamento e o manual de instruções.
É importante destacar que não acompanham o produto cabos auxiliares do tipo P2 e nem microfone para uso na função de karaokê, exigindo que você utilize ou compre esses acessórios separadamente.
Para atender à proposta de mobilidade, o equipamento conta com uma alça integrada para transporte. Na parte superior, fica posicionado o painel de controles físicos.
As dimensões e peso são:
Durante os meus testes, senti que o peso compromete bastante a experiência com mobilidade. Se a sua intenção for ficar alternando a caixa de cômodo a todo momento ou transportá-la a pé por longas distâncias, como em trilhas, por exemplo, esse peso pode dificultar as coisas.
Os botões são emborrachados e bem distribuídos, permitindo ligar e desligar o aparelho, realizar o pareamento Bluetooth, acionar o modo Auracast, ajustar o volume, pausar ou dar play nas músicas.
Você também pode ativar o modo estéreo sem fio, alternar os efeitos de iluminação e mudar os modos de equalização.
Na traseira do dispositivo ficam instaladas as conexões físicas, todas protegidas por uma tampa de borracha vedada.
Essa proteção garante à caixa a certificação IP66 de resistência contra poeira e jatos fortes de água, permitindo o uso tranquilo à beira da piscina ou na praia sem medo de respingos.
O design conta ainda com iluminação RGB nas laterais, que oferecem efeitos luminosos dinâmicos alternando de cor conforme o ritmo da música ou de acordo com a sua escolha.
A qualidade de som cumpriu o esperado para um dispositivo com 500 W de capacidade. O aparelho entrega som estéreo 360 com excelente definição entre graves, médios e agudos, sem distorção mesmo com o volume no máximo.
Toda essa potência da caixa pode ser controlada pelos modos de equalização oferecidos tanto no app quanto no próprio produto. O modo interno ajusta a reprodução das músicas para que o som alto não incomode quem estiver escutando dentro de casa.
Já no modo externo, é possível notar um aumento na definição do som pra que todo mundo consiga escutar com clareza o que tá sendo reproduzido ao ar livre, por exemplo.
Segundo a marca, a DR-500 conta com um sistema de som de três vias:
Ela também possui três amplificadores de áudio, dedicados exclusivamente para cada canal sonoro. No geral, é um modelo voltado para diferentes perfis de uso, seja para escutar em casa, em encontros entre amigos, na praia ou em festas, tranquilamente.
A autonomia é outro destaque positivo da Sabala DR-500: são 81.000 mAh de capacidade. Isso permite até 46 horas de reprodução de músicas sem parar. Claro, isso pode variar — com o volume no máximo, foi possível chegar a aproximadamente oito horas de som.
Já o carregamento da caixa é relativamente demorado por conta dessa alta capacidade de bateria. Para carregar de 0 a 100%, são necessárias cinco horas na tomada.
Esses 81.000 mAh também permitem que você conecte seu celular, utilizando a caixa como um powerbank.
Mas o modelo vem equipado com apenas uma porta USB-A na parte traseira. Na prática, isso limita o uso simultâneo de acessórios.
Por exemplo: se você conectar um pendrive com músicas, não terá outra entrada disponível para carregar a bateria do seu celular ao mesmo tempo — exigindo que você escolha entre uma função ou outra.
No quesito conectividade sem fio, a caixa vem atualizada com o padrão Bluetooth 6.0. Durante todo o período de testes, a conexão se manteve estável em distâncias de até 10 metros, sem engasgos, atrasos ou quedas de sinal.
A DR-500 traz suporte às tecnologias Auracast e TWS. O recurso TWS permite parear duas caixas sem fio em modo estéreo.
Já o Auracast possibilita a transmissão simultânea do mesmo áudio para diversas caixas compatíveis em um mesmo ambiente.
No painel traseiro, há um pacote completo de conexões físicas: uma entrada auxiliar P2 tradicional, a porta USB-A para leitura de pendrives ou uso como power bank e uma entrada P10 para microfone ou para conexão de instrumentos musicais.
Aplicativo da Sabala permite usar todas as funções presentes no modelo remotamente, como o equalizador de ambiente, controle do Auracast e as personalizações de iluminação. Tudo com boa responsividade no Android ou iPhone (iOS).
Você também pode conferir a bateria, configurar um timer ou fazer o desligamento da caixa de som diretamente pelo celular.
Esses recursos, apesar de básicos, são importantes principalmente em festas ou confraternizações, já que você não precisa ficar indo até a caixa de som para aumentar ou diminuir o volume, por exemplo, ou fazer outros ajustes.
A Sabala DR-500 é uma escolha bastante atraente no mercado de áudio de alta potência.
Custando na faixa de R$ 2.300, o grande trunfo do modelo está na relação entre preço e potência bruta. Nessa mesma faixa de preço, concorrentes diretas como a JBL Boombox 4, entregam um nível de potência consideravelmente menor.
Com a DR-500, você leva impressionantes 500 W e um sistema de três vias pagando um preço menor que opções rivais. Além disso, a bateria gigante de 81.000 mAh com função power bank e a certificação IP66 contra água e poeira são importantes para quem organiza festas e eventos ao ar livre.
No entanto, o peso de 11,5 kg tornam o transporte constante um desafio, a recarga completa leva 5 horas e a embalagem não inclui cabos auxiliares ou microfone.
Se a sua prioridade for o volume mais alto e a maior autonomia, sem se importar com o peso para trasportar, a Sabala DR-500 entrega bom custo-benefício nesta categoria.
Agora, eu quero saber de você: o que achou da caixa de som? Deixe sua opinião na Comunidade do Tecnoblog!

articles.title: Anthropic's Claude AI blocks video game cloning and reverse-engineering — sweeping new restrictions also hit legitimate developers and basic troubleshooting tasks
articles.text:
Anthropic's Claude AI blocks video game cloning and reverse-engineering — sweeping new restrictions also hit legitimate developers and basic troubleshooting tasks
Many game developers are reporting Claude's refusal to work on their own projects.
Reverse-engineering games for converting them between systems is currently a hot topic, and it's getting messier by the day. According to multiple user claims, Anthropic's Claude Code and/or Opus 5.5 model are blocking attempts at innocuous reverse-engineering, including but not limited to those using the popular Reverse Engineer Anything (REA) tool. That issue may be linked to a text rule that's now in force, which allegedly instructs the model to avoid "[recreating] a specific existing game."
According to Twitter user Chasm, the game-related textual rule is "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original." There is no official or additional confirmation if this is the actual rule text, but it's plausible enough given the very clear refusals that devs have been encountering over the past week.
This situation is tricky to analyze due to the varying types of reports. First, the existence of a game-related rule is real, as Claude Code's GitHub is seeing an influx of issues complaining about refusals to do standard game work halfway through development, when replicating a game mechanic, and patching a tabletop-like game. It's possible that some of those reports have been made by users with nefarious purposes, but at least one is a bona fide developer with a real track record.
As for reverse engineering, there had already been a smattering of user reports across Reddit and other platforms, wherein Claude refused to perform tasks like (allegedly) analyzing a simple Windows crash dump, clearing up junkware on a Samsung TV, or just using REA altogether.
The simultaneous timing of both game- and cyber-security restrictions may be a coincidence, and yet there are complaints from purported game developers saying that Claude blocked their own games' anti-cheat development and security reviews, under the justification that its safeguards were triggered.
Anthropic introduced its Cyber Verification Program on October 6, essentially saying that access to its frontier models' advanced cybersecurity capabilities would be limited to entities covered by Project Glasswing, taking effect immediately.
It's possible that whichever ruleset was applied is the same one that's causing the cybersecurity-related refusals. Still, it's odd to see that 24 days have passed since then, and yet reports of bot refusal are only coming in since the last week or so.
As for possible motivations behind these restrictions, they are twofold. The first and most obvious one is that Anthropic — and, by extension, other AI players — are preemptively protecting themselves from potential lawsuits from software companies, including game studios, for offering the means to reverse-engineer their software.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
There is no official statement on these matters from Anthropic or other AI companies so far. Anthropic isn't the only one playing this game, too, as recently OpenAI deactivated the account of another person trying to clean up their TV's software.
The recent rash of AI-powered clones of application suites like Adobe's suite and Microsoft Office 365, as well as the countless recomps and decomps of console games, likely has most every software company on earth rethinking their life choices. And probably also in frequent contact with their legal teams.
The online reaction was swift, suggesting that users looking to perform reverse-engineering work simply use Chinese, open-weight, or local LLMs instead of Claude or GPT. This, at the same time, highlights the irony of frontier AI companies that copied the world's information and art for their training sets and are now concerned with copyright infringement.
And yet there are situations that merit some discussion, like the recent controversy about the Steam Next Fest being chock-full of AI slop copied from existing titles. That particular situation is getting particularly nasty, as game developers are reportedly being extorted under threat that their game demos will be cloned into complete games before they have a chance to finish and release the original.
Adding insult to injury, this is seemingly being done to small studios whose main priority is usually "having food," rather than big publishers looking to microtransaction everything into a new yacht for shareholders.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.
- Jabberwocky79 I wouldn't be surprised if Adobe is the main player behind this development. They have the biggest purse strings and some of the most to lose.
But yeah, it's totally ironic that AI companies essentially rape the internet to train their models and now they are worried about people using their acquired knowledge to circumvent copyright LOL. Reply

articles.title: Une taxe sur chaque gigaoctet téléchargé : les députés viennent de voter une mesure qui pourrait coûter cher
articles.text:
L’Assemblée nationale vient d’adopter un amendement instaurant une taxe de 5,5 centimes sur chaque gigaoctet de données transmis aux internautes français. Si la mesure venait à entrer en vigueur, les fournisseurs de contenus devraient passer à la caisse, avec un risque de répercussion sur le prix de nos abonnements.
Regarder une série sur Netflix, télécharger un jeu vidéo de 100 Go ou simplement passer quelques heures sur YouTube pourrait bientôt coûter plus cher aux plateformes qui nous fournissent ces contenus. Ce vendredi 30 octobre, les députés ont adopté un amendement au projet de loi de finances pour 2027 qui propose de taxer les données circulant sur Internet. Une idée pour le moins originale, défendue au nom d’une meilleure contribution des géants du numérique aux finances publiques. Mais derrière les milliards d’euros espérés par ses auteurs, plusieurs questions se posent, à commencer par celle qui nous intéresse tous : qui finira par payer ?
Une taxe de 5,5 centimes par Go, payée par les plateformes
L’amendement déposé par le député socialiste Laurent Lhardit prévoit la création d’une taxe sur les données numériques envoyées aux internautes français. Le texte a été adopté de justesse, par 11 voix contre 10, malgré l’opposition du gouvernement et du rapporteur général du budget.
Le principe est simple : chaque gigaoctet de données transmis serait taxé à hauteur de 0,055 euro, soit 5,5 centimes.
Prenons un exemple concret. Le téléchargement d’un jeu vidéo de 100 Go représenterait théoriquement 5,50 € de taxe pour l’entreprise qui distribue les données. Avec 200 Go, la taille estimée de GTA VI, la facture grimperait à 11 €. Et pour une plateforme de streaming diffusant des milliards de gigaoctets chaque année, les sommes pourraient rapidement devenir considérables.
Précision essentielle : ce ne sont pas les internautes qui seraient directement taxés, ni les fournisseurs d’accès à Internet. La contribution serait due par les entreprises qui émettent les données, qu’il s’agisse des plateformes vidéo, des réseaux sociaux ou des distributeurs de contenus numériques.
Les opérateurs, eux, seraient chargés de mesurer les volumes transmis et de communiquer les résultats à l’administration fiscale. Le dispositif prévoit une collecte agrégée, sans examiner le contenu des échanges ni identifier les habitudes individuelles des abonnés. Ses modalités techniques devront toutefois être précisées par décret.
Pour éviter une taxation disproportionnée, l’amendement prévoit également un plafonnement lié au chiffre d’affaires des entreprises : 15 % de leurs revenus français ou 2 % de leur chiffre d'affaires mondial.
Dix milliards espérés, mais qui paiera réellement la facture ?
Les auteurs de l’amendement estiment que cette taxe pourrait rapporter jusqu’à 10 milliards d’euros par an à l’État. Ils s’appuient notamment sur les quelque 200 milliards de gigaoctets de trafic annuel évoqués dans leur exposé des motifs.
Leur objectif est de faire davantage contribuer les grands acteurs internationaux du numérique, qui représentent une part considérable du trafic Internet français.
La mesure aurait également, selon ses défenseurs, un intérêt environnemental : en donnant un coût aux données transmises, elle encouragerait les plateformes à mieux compresser leurs vidéos, images et autres contenus.
Mais ce raisonnement laisse plusieurs interrogations en suspens. D’abord, la taxe ne concernerait pas uniquement les géants américains. Des entreprises françaises pourraient également être touchées, notamment dans les secteurs du streaming et du jeu vidéo.
Ensuite, rien ne garantit que les plateformes absorberaient intégralement ce nouveau coût. Certaines pourraient choisir d’augmenter leurs tarifs, de réduire leurs marges ou de modifier leurs offres. Une hausse des abonnements Netflix, Disney+ ou des services de jeux reste donc une possibilité, pas une conséquence automatique.
La proposition rappelle d’ailleurs les précédents débats autour d’une taxation de la bande passante des grandes plateformes, même si le mécanisme retenu cette fois repose sur les volumes réellement transmis.
Enfin, cette taxe n’est pas encore en vigueur. L’adoption de l'amendement ne constitue qu’une étape dans l’examen du budget 2027. Le dispositif peut encore être modifié ou supprimé avant l'adoption définitive de la loi.
Pour le moment, votre facture Internet ne change donc pas. Mais le vote ouvre un débat particulièrement sensible : faut-il taxer les entreprises numériques en fonction de la quantité de données qu’elles nous envoient, au risque de leur donner une raison supplémentaire d'augmenter leurs prix ?

articles.title: Critique Ted Lasso saison 4 : la série Apple TV réussit son retour sans changer sa recette
articles.text:
| Réalisateur | Bill Lawrence, Jason Sudeikis | 
| Acteurs | Jason Sudeikis, Hannah Waddingham, Jeremy Swift, Nick Mohammed, Juno Temple, Brett Goldstein | 
| Genre | Comédie, Comédie dramatique, Drame, Évènement Sportif | 
| Durée | 35 min | 
| Date de sortie | 05/08/2026 | 
| Episodes | 10 | 
Malgré une troisième saison qui avait tout d'une conclusion, la populaire série Ted Lasso d'Apple TV est revenu avec une quatrième saison, aujourd'hui disponible en intégralité. Voici notre avis, garanti sans spoilers.
Trois années après une saison 3 qui semblait pourtant avoir clos l'histoire de Ted Lasso, la célèbre série d'Apple TV est revenue avec une inattendue saison 4, disponible aujourd'hui en intégralité sur la plateforme de streaming de la firme à la pomme.
Un nouveau chapitre qui nous fait remettre les crampons avec plaisir, et qui place l'entraîneur incarné par Jason Sudeikis face à un challenge inédit. Les Numériques a pu voir cette saison 4, et voici notre avis garanti sans spoilers.
Cette quatrième saison de la série voit Ted retourner à Richmond pour relever son plus grand défi : entraîner une équipe féminine de football de deuxième division. Tout au long de la saison, Ted et l’équipe vont devoir apprendre à se lancer les yeux fermés, et à prendre des risques qu’ils n’auraient jamais imaginés.
Succès d'audience de la plateforme de streaming Apple TV et lauréate de 13 Emmy Awards, la série Ted Lasso a su trouver la délicate formule pour séduire à la fois le public et les critiques. Il n'est donc pas étonnant que cette nouvelle saison, que personne n'avait réellement demandée, joue la carte de la sécurité en ne changeant pas (beaucoup) sa précieuse recette.
Cette saison 4 débute alors comme une machine à la mécanique bien huilée, où on retrouve Ted aux États-Unis près de son fils, alors que Rebecca, Leslie et Keeley viennent le chercher pour le ramener à Richmond. Le temps de mettre l'histoire en place, le premier épisode a ainsi tout de la petite madeleine nostalgique.
Les personnages n'ont pas bougé d'un iota en trois années, chacun reprenant sa partition et ses gimmicks sans fausse note, et on repasse même par les lieux emblématiques de la série.
Ce n'est pas désagréable en soi et ça fonctionne toujours, mais on pouvait craindre que Ted Lasso ne soit revenu que pour faire du réchauffé. Heureusement ce n'est pas le cas, et l'ensemble prend enfin du relief et de l'intérêt dès le deuxième épisode qui pose les passionnants enjeux de cette saison, autour du foot féminin.
Là où les précédentes saisons de Ted Lasso s'intéressaient à la masculinité toxique, l'ego ou encore l'aspect moral dans le foot, cette quatrième saison aborde frontalement les problématiques liées au foot féminin : les préjugés sexistes, les aspects financiers et commerciaux, ou encore la difficulté de faire coexister son rôle de mère avec son envie de jouer...
Pour donner du corps à ces thématiques, cette saison 4 se dote d'une galerie de personnages qui n'a rien à envier à Jamie Tartt, Dani Rojas et Sam Obisanya, entre une paire de sœurs défenseuses qui s'écharpent à la moindre occasion ou une gardienne qui refuse de porter des gants
Des protagonistes hauts en couleur, mais fidèles à "l'esprit Ted Lasso", et qui font des étincelles face aux "anciens" que sont Roy Kent ou Coach Beard. Dans le lot de ces nouveaux visages, on note quelques belles performances d'actrices.
La présence notamment de l'excellente Faye Marsay (Andor, Adolescence) et surtout de Tanya Reynolds (Sex Education, The Decameron), qui est la véritable réussite de cette saison 4. Son personnage d'assistante de Ted très secrète mais aussi très ambitieuse évolue joliment durant les premiers épisodes, et promet de le faire encore plus par la suite.
On était un peu sceptique sur cette prolongation peu attendue, mais ce nouveau chapitre de Ted Lasso amuse et émeut, jouant à la fois sur la nostalgie des fans avec le même humour et ce ton doux-amer si particulier, tout en proposant aussi de nouveaux personnages touchants et des enjeux renouvelés autour du foot féminin.
Si la série souffre toujours d'un esprit "tout le monde est beau, tout le monde est gentil" un peu niais, qui n'arrivera toujours pas à convaincre les plus cyniques, on peut assurer que cette quatrième saison plaira sans aucun doute aux fans (comme nous).
Ted Lasso réussit son retour sur la pelouse, avec certes une même recette, mais des ingrédients joliment revisités, et on ne serait pas contre une nouvelle flopée d'épisodes dans une potentielle (mais encore non-annoncée) saison 5.
Pour rappel, les programmes Apple TV sont disponibles via le site officiel, mais aussi dans les Prime Video Channels de Prime Video, et ils sont inclus dans l'offre de Canal+.
Cette saison 4 de Ted Lasso prouve que le retour de la série n'était pas qu'une simple opération nostalgique. Si elle reprend une formule bien connue, elle parvient à lui donner un second souffle grâce à ses nouveaux personnages et aux enjeux du football féminin, sans rien perdre de son humour ni de sa tendresse. Une nouvelle saison attachante et réjouissante, qui ne convaincra pas les plus réfractaires à son optimisme débordant, mais qui devrait ravir les fans de la première heure.

articles.title: GIGABYTE Advances Local AI Infrastructure with WRX90 AI TOP Motherboard
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
GIGABYTE Advances Local AI Infrastructure with WRX90 AI TOP Motherboard
GIGABYTE, a global leader in high-performance computer hardware, today announced the WRX90 AI TOP workstation motherboard, supporting AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO series processors. Engineered specifically for local AI workloads and intensive computing, the motherboard features multi-GPU PCIe 5.0 expansion slots, high-capacity ECC memory support, and enterprise-grade BMC remote management. It provides a robust, highly extensible hardware foundation for professionals to deploy dedicated local AI platforms and manage model development on-premises.
Scale Up for AI Development
To support evolving AI applications, the WRX90 AI TOP allows organizations to configure and expand their hardware as computational workloads grow. Equipped with seven PCIe 5.0 x16 slots and two MCIO 8i connectors, the motherboard offers extensive bandwidth capable of supporting up to nine GPU devices through compatible expansion hardware. Complementing this expansion capacity, eight-channel DDR5 memory support accommodates up to 2 TB of ECC RDIMM for large datasets and memory-intensive applications. The inclusion of Error-Correcting Code (ECC) memory automatically detects and corrects data corruption, ensuring data integrity during prolonged AI computing sessions.Engineered for Reliability
Sustained performance requires a foundation engineered for heavy continuous loads. The WRX90 AI TOP features a 32+3+3+3-phase digital power design paired with a 14-layer server-grade PCB and a full-metal backplate, ensuring stable power delivery, signal integrity, and structural rigidity. Thermal engineering plays a vital role in preventing throttling under sustained operation. To tackle heat buildup around closely spaced memory modules, the included DDR Wind Blade XTREME Duo fans improve airflow to reduce average memory temperatures by up to 43°C compared to unassisted setups. Dedicated SYS Wind Blade fans and extensive heatsinks cover the power delivery and chipset areas, maintaining optimal thermal control during heavy processing runs.
Manage Smarter. Connect Faster.
For streamlined operational management, the WRX90 AI TOP integrates an onboard BMC and a dedicated IPMI LAN port. This enables IT administrators to perform remote hardware monitoring, power control, and troubleshooting at any time. These capabilities significantly simplify maintenance workflows for IT teams while ensuring long-term operational stability for local computing environments. Additionally, dual server-grade 10GbE LAN ports enable rapid data transfers to centralized storage arrays without the need for an add-in network card, while dual USB4 Type-C ports offer high-speed connectivity for external storage and peripherals.The WRX90 AI TOP expands GIGABYTE's AI TOP portfolio with a workstation motherboard that bridges extreme computing power with practical management tools. Its combination of expandable architecture and durable hardware design empowers enterprise users and developers to build systems optimized for long-term AI development.

articles.title: Meta, TikTok y X perdieron en un tribunal de Londres su pelea contra los pedidos de datos del regulador
articles.text:
El Tribunal Superior de Londres rechazó el recurso de Meta, TikTok y X contra Ofcom, el regulador de las comunicaciones del Reino Unido, por los pedidos de datos sobre moderación de contenido que les hizo bajo la ley de seguridad en línea. Es una de las primeras pruebas del nuevo régimen, según Reuters.
La sentencia se dictó el viernes 30 de octubre de 2026. El tribunal descartó el argumento central de las tres plataformas: que los pedidos de información eran desproporcionados. Reuters no detalló en su despacho los fundamentos del fallo ni si las empresas podrán apelar.
Ofcom envió las notificaciones en febrero del mismo año. Exigían cifras detalladas de moderación: cuántas publicaciones se eliminaron o vieron restringida su visibilidad, y a cuántos usuarios llegó contenido dañino.
La Ley de Seguridad en Línea de 2023 impone a redes como Facebook, Instagram, TikTok y X estándares más estrictos, sobre todo para proteger a los menores.
Un portavoz de Ofcom celebró la decisión: “Reunir información de las empresas es fundamental para nuestra capacidad de hacer el trabajo”. Meta dijo estar “decepcionada” con el fallo, y TikTok informó que analiza la sentencia. X no respondió de inmediato a las consultas de Reuters.
Las plataformas dijeron que el costo era desmedido
Meta sostuvo que recopilar información “a esta escala” excede lo necesario y lo proporcionado, y afirmó que ella y otras empresas del sector presentaron el recurso por esa razón. X calificó su notificación como “el pedido de información más costoso” que recibió de cualquier regulador y estimó que le costaría millones de libras.
Según el estudio de abogados Wiggin LLP, Meta describió su notificación como una “lista de deseos” sin base legal. La firma recogió esa frase de informes previos y la citó en un análisis publicado el 19 de octubre sobre los litigios contra Ofcom.
La ley respalda los requisitos del regulador con multas de hasta el 10% de la facturación global de una empresa en las infracciones más graves. Según Wiggin, el tope es el que resulte mayor entre ese porcentaje y 18 millones de libras.
Meta tiene otros dos frentes abiertos contra Ofcom
El fallo del 30 de octubre de 2026 no cierra la disputa. Reuters señaló que todavía falta una decisión, potencialmente más importante, sobre otro recurso de Meta: el que cuestiona cómo Ofcom calcula las tarifas que pagan las plataformas y las multas máximas que podría aplicar.
Ese caso se discutió en un tribunal de Londres a mediados de octubre. La BBC informó en mayo que Meta considera “desproporcionado” el método de cálculo, que se basa en los ingresos mundiales y alcanza a las empresas que facturan más de 250 millones de libras al año.
Según los documentos judiciales citados por la BBC, el sistema hace que “un puñado de empresas” cubra “la gran mayoría” de los costos de Ofcom. La abogada de Meta, Monica Carss-Frisk, planteó que el cálculo no está ligado a los ingresos por servicios en el Reino Unido.
Ofcom respondió entonces que actuó según “una lectura simple de la ley”. Su representante legal calificó de “descabellado” el cuestionamiento de Meta a la experiencia del regulador, según el servicio MLex.
Meta también impugna la categoría que Ofcom asignó a WhatsApp dentro del régimen. Además, en octubre pasó a ser el blanco de la primera investigación formal de Ofcom bajo la ley de seguridad en línea, precisó Reuters.
La sentencia sobre las tarifas y las multas de Meta sigue pendiente, sin fecha anunciada en las fuentes consultadas.
Meta posterga fecha en la que iniciará a usar el contenido web de empresas para entrenar su IA
Meta postergó del 30 de octubre al 20 de noviembre de 2026 la aplicación de términos que le permiten utilizar contenido de sitios vinculados a cuentas empresariales de Facebook e Instagram.
La medida llegó tras cuestionamientos de editores y reguladores europeos. Aunque eliminó la referencia explícita a “entrenar” inteligencia artificial y acotó la cláusula a productos publicitarios y comerciales, especialistas advierten que aún habilitaría rastreo masivo.
Meta afirma que los propietarios pueden expresar sus preferencias mediante robots.txt, algo que la redacción no garantiza expresamente. La Comisión Europea analiza una denuncia, mientras la CMA británica evalúa posibles medidas de intervención futura.

articles.title: AI semiconductor industry trends: from chips to systems - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
6 insights from the GSA Women’s Leadership Initiative: AI semiconductor industry trends turn the chip race into a systems race
For decades, the semiconductor industry competed on one thing: the individual chip. One of the biggest AI semiconductor industry trends now under way is the shift toward treating chips as components of much larger systems. Performance, cost and reliability are now determined across the package, the rack and the supply chain, not inside a single die.
That shift moves the hardest problems upstream. Packaging, connectivity, yield, sourcing and verification used to come after design, but now they shape it from the first day. AI is shortening development cycles at the same time as it adds to the complexity engineers have to manage. The next phase will be defined by how well companies coordinate across that whole system.
“I think the AI system is our new chips,” said Letizia Giuliano, vice president of product management and marketing at Qualcomm Technologies Inc. “If we were optimizing everything for the silicon in the past, now these days we’re optimizing everything for the system.”
Giuliano and other industry experts spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and co-host Alison Kosik at the GSA Women’s Leadership Initiative event in Palo Alto, California. The interviews covered AI semiconductor industry trends, optical interconnects, advanced packaging, AI-driven yield learning, physical AI, strategic sourcing and AI-assisted chip design.
Here are six standout insights from the event:
1. Connectivity overtakes compute as the bottleneck in AI infrastructure.
Moving data between chips, memory and racks now limits AI performance more than raw compute, according to Giuliano. At 200 gigabits per second per lane, half of the signal budget goes just to getting out of the package. That is pushing optical interconnect from rack-to-rack links into the rack, the blade and the package itself, with copper and optics in use side by side. Qualcomm has just launched High Bandwidth Compute, a low-power way to attach compute to memory that is tuned for tokens per watt. Building such products at hyperscale volume means product engineering has to join design-for-test, manufacturing and reliability planning early, explained Sophie Wang, senior director of product engineering at Marvell Technology Inc.
Check out theCUBE’s complete interview.
2. Advanced packaging moves from afterthought to system architecture.
The boundary of an AI system is shifting from the chip to the package, emphasized Nisha Ananthakrishnan, senior director of advanced packaging at Intel Corp. Intel uses its EMIB bridge technology to link chiplets and to scale packages from 3x to more than 10x form factors. Outsourced assembly and test providers are becoming system integrators, noted Patricia MacLeod, senior director of corporate communications and industry partnerships at Advanced Semiconductor Engineering Inc. She pointed to ASE’s VIPack platform, which supports technologies ranging from fan-out chip-on-substrate to co-packaged optics. Many of the chips AI depends on, such as power management chips and voltage regulators built at 12 to 28 nanometers, use mature nodes, added Tazrien Kamal, senior director of technology and innovation at GlobalFoundries Inc.
Watch the full interview from theCUBE.
3. AI-driven yield learning turns speed to volume into a competitive edge.
About 70% to 80% of the problems found when scaling up volume manufacturing could have been caught before tapeout, highlighted Preeti Prasher, chief operating officer of Stathera Inc. Using AI to analyze characterization, simulation and inline manufacturing data lets teams start new wafers before a bad lot reaches test. Adaptive testing also cuts test time. Lattice Semiconductor Corp. has released Lattice Prompt, its first AI design assistant, which turns a plain-language request into a field-programmable gate array design and recommends the best part for the form factor and cost, according to Iliana Chen, senior director of program management at Lattice. Demand from robotics and other markets has made volume Lattice’s biggest challenge, Chen noted.
See theCUBE’s full coverage.
4. Physical AI becomes a system-level challenge, not a chip war.
Physical AI is much broader than humanoid robots and covers any autonomous system that senses its surroundings, reasons and acts in the physical world, explained Gina Longoria, VP of external communications at Arm Ltd. The market is in its first inning, and no single company can build the architecture, security and safety standards it needs on its own, she stressed. Firmware is becoming the layer that ties GPUs, CPUs, network cards and Compute Express Link devices into one fleet-scale system, shared Lakshmi Ramagiri, partner for firmware engineering at Microsoft Corp. Security has to move beyond secure boot to continuous trust while a system is running, and the Open Compute Project and DMTF are the standards bodies to watch, Ramagiri added.
Don’t miss the full interview on theCUBE.
5. Strategic sourcing becomes a product decision as AI strains the supply chain.
Sourcing now goes well beyond negotiating prices and shapes product development, risk and customer experience, emphasized Alisa Wang, AVP of global planning and procurement at Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd. Because AI-driven demand can change within a year, suppliers have to be treated as strategic partners that receive product roadmaps early, she noted. Leading-edge logic capacity at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. is the tightest constraint, followed by packaging, specialty materials and critical equipment. In response, Credo is qualifying second-source suppliers and spreading its manufacturing footprint across more regions. Stathera’s Prasher highlighted dual sourcing for key segments and using supplier feedback during new product introduction to develop lower-cost products together.
Hear the full story on theCUBE.
6. AI agents compress chip design as development cycles shrink to six to nine months.
AI is moving from a productivity assistant to a built-in part of electronic design automation flows, explained Rimi Dasgupta, chief of staff for product management and markets at Synopsys Inc., and Vidya Neerkundar, director of product management at Siemens Digital Industries Software. Synopsys has seen verification closure on register-transfer-level designs accelerate as much as 50-fold and debug time drop by 40%, according to Dasgupta. Demand for workload-optimized custom silicon has also cut development cycles from 18 months to six to nine months. AI is probabilistic, but chips must be deterministic, so Synopsys pairs AI with multiphysics solvers from its Ansys acquisition and is working with OpenAI Group PBC on a dedicated GPT-Synopsys model. Multi-die design is the next big shift as chips hit reticle limits, Neerkundar noted.

articles.title: AI agent used to perform controversial brain surgery on a mouse, Anthropic Sonnet-controlled motorized surgery rig — Opus 5.5 refused to conduct biological experiment, Sonnet given free rein to treat epilepsy with a range of gene therapy vectors after
articles.text:
AI agent used to perform controversial brain surgery on a mouse, Anthropic Sonnet-controlled motorized surgery rig — Opus 5.5 refused to conduct biological experiment, Sonnet given free rein to treat epilepsy with a range of gene therapy vectors after
This raises a lot of ethical questions, though.
Exin Therapeutics, a biotech startup focusing on next-generation neurotherapeutics, claims it has successfully conducted brain surgery on a mouse using an AI agent. Its co-founder and CEO, Gabriel Ocana-Santero, shared the entire procedure on X, showing how the AI agent chose the gene therapy vector and dosage and the brain region where it would be applied. The AI agent also drove the robotic arms that injected the medication into the mouse’s brain. Thankfully, the operation seems to have been a success, with the mouse recovering well and recorded moving around in its enclosure.
“Autonomous surgical robots exist and they are better at the mechanics than our bench rig, [to be honest]. But in every one of them, a human decided what operation to perform, and the robot executed it,” Ocana-Santero said. “Nobody told this agent what to give or where to put it. It got a phenotype and a shelf of candidates and had to work out the therapy and the coordinates itself. I am not aware of an agent previously choosing a treatment and a brain target and then delivering it into a living mammal.”
The team used Anthropic Sonnet, which received a mouse model of epilepsy, control of a motorized surgery rig, and 19 gene therapy vectors in a spreadsheet. Aside from that, it also had access to three research papers, allowing it to choose the brain region where it should apply the treatment. Nevertheless, a licensed veterinarian was purportedly overseeing the entire operation, with every irreversible step requiring approval before the AI agent could proceed. Aside from that, the entire system also had an emergency stop button that would cut the power to every motor in the surgery rig.
The only thing that the vet surgeon on duty did was to do the craniotomy procedure to expose the brain, as the AI agent wasn’t allowed to do that yet for safety reasons. There were also several safeguards that the AI agents were banned from overriding, which even the human operators couldn’t bypass, necessitating a manual fix to the agent’s code during the operation.
What’s interesting, though, is that the startup only used Anthropic’s mid-range Sonnet model for the operation. It initially tried using Opus 5.5, but it immediately refused to do any work after it detected that it was working on a biological experiment. The older Opus 5 model was able to run the entire procedure on paper but refused to do live surgery. “The block isn't the rig and isn't the inputs. It's me. My own output was stopped when I started writing the plan for this surgery... if I try, it gets cut off the same way, and the worst version of that is me cut off partway through a live procedure with a needle somewhere in the brain,” the LLM reportedly told the Exin Therapeutics team. “Starting something I can't finish on an anesthetized animal is worse than not starting.”
Despite the seeming success of the operation, some people are concerned about the ethics of such a procedure. While AI LLMs have been useful in medical research, adding them to sinus surgery has seen malfunctions skyrocket by more than 12 times. Aside from that, relying on an AI to make every decision in such a risky procedure puts accountability in question, especially if something goes wrong. We also haven’t even touched the long-standing ethical question of animal experimentation in the medical setting. Still, some users applauded the experiment, with one comment saying that they’re excited about the possibilities of these integrated technologies, as their son has been suffering from drug-resistant epilepsy for 19 years.

articles.title: OLED TVs over 100 inches might finally be coming, and it might help bring the price of 77 and 83-inch sizes down too — LG Display and its partner are reportedly investing 1 billion extra yuan to upgrade large OLED panel production
articles.text:
The dream home theater TV? 111-inch OLED TVs might be coming, as LG finally explores going beyond the 97-inch limit — but what will the performance be like?
Giant OLED TVs could finally become affordable as LG Display commits to truly enormous OLEDs — but does bigger mean better?
- LG Display is investing heavily in OLED production up to 111 inches
- Current LG OLEDs top out at 97 inches
- Today's 97-inch panel is much older tech than smaller panels
If you're looking for home theater-size OLED TVs, you'll soon encounter two hard limits: availability and affordability. You can't currently buy an OLED larger than 97 inches because nobody makes them.
And you probably can't afford a 97-inch OLED TV because it's terrifyingly expensive: today LG is listing its 97-inch OLED for $19,999 (reduced from $24,999) / £15,999. But it looks like both of those things are about to change.
LG Display is reportedly investing big money in big OLED, though: it and its partner Guangzhou Development Zone Holding Group are reportedly investing an extra 1 billion yuan to upgrade its production facilities for giant OLED displays.
As FlatpanelsHD reports, the market analysis company TrendForce says that the announced upgrades mainly target "large-size OLED module manufacturing, with products covering 77-inch, 83-inch, 97-inch, and 111-inch," with the ability to debut a 111-inch panel being a "major highlight of the project."
Bigger and potentially more affordable TVs are always welcome. But we do have some questions.
What panel is LG intending to use?
The big question for us is whether the investment will mean improvements to the existing 97-inch panel's technology.
The 2026 version of LG's 97-inch OLED TV is a 4K native panel with a native refresh rate of 120Hz, but while the model is the LG G6, its panel is not the same as its smaller siblings: they all get LG's Primary RGB Tandem 2.0 panel, but the 97-inch is an older, non-Tandem panel — in fact it dates back to the LG G2 from 2022, so it's several generations behind. That means it isn't as bright and doesn't have the same color accuracy as the other models.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
That difference is important, because these large OLEDs are up against some of the best mini-LED and increasingly, RGB mini-LED TVs — and those TVs are exceptionally bright and accurate as well as increasingly affordable. It's possible to buy high-quality 98-inch Hisense TV for just $3,999, which is a lot for a TV but not a lot for a 98-inch one — and is obvious just a fraction of the 97-inch OLED price.
We're keeping our fingers crossed here: if LG Display breaks the size barrier and makes ultra-large Tandem RGB TVs that are less expensive to manufacture, that'd be great. The worst case scenario is that we get the same kind of panel that's currently in the 97-incher, but a bit bigger — but it seems like that the aim is to upgrade the technology, given that production of smaller sizes was mentioned as a goal as well.
And that might be the bigger win from the project for most of us: if the project succeeds in making producing 111-inch OLED viable, and therefore improves the process and lowers the cost of 77-inch and 83-inch models too, that's probably the real benefit.

articles.title: La taxe au gigaoctet prend sa revanche à l’Assemblée et pourrait faire exploser le prix du streaming
articles.text:
L’idée de faire payer les plateformes pour les octets qu’elles déversent sur les réseaux circule depuis des années, des couloirs de Bruxelles au programme du Parti socialiste. Ce vendredi 30 octobre, l’amendement du député Laurent Lhardit au budget 2027 l’a concrétisée : une taxe sur les « producteurs de données numériques », votée par 11 voix contre 10 en première lecture. Le rapporteur général du budget et le gouvernement avaient pourtant appelé à la rejeter quelques minutes plus tôt, comme la commission des finances l’avait déjà fait le 9 octobre.
Qui paiera ces 0,055 euro par gigaoctet ?
Le texte institue, selon ses propres termes, « une taxe assise sur les flux de données numériques émises par les fournisseurs de contenu et acquittée par ces derniers ». Chaque gigaoctet expédié vers un abonné français coûterait ainsi 0,055 euro à l’entreprise qui l’émet, un péage au volume dont les fournisseurs d’accès seraient les releveurs de compteur. Orange, Free, Bouygues Telecom et SFR devraient relever, de façon anonymisée et consolidée, les volumes qui transitent vers leurs clients, sous la supervision de l’Arcep. Les contenus mis en cache chez des diffuseurs comme Akamai entrent aussi dans le calcul.
L’exposé des motifs vise sans détour Google, Meta, Amazon, Netflix et Akamai, cinq acteurs qui concentrent à eux seuls la moitié du trafic mesuré par l’Arcep. En séance, Laurent Lhardit a chiffré le rendement attendu à 10 milliards d’euros par an : « La taxe serait principalement acquittée par les géants mondialisés du numérique, puisqu’ils émettent l’immense majorité des flux adressés aux abonnés internet en France ». Un double plafond, 15 % du chiffre d’affaires réalisé en France ou 2 % du chiffre d’affaires mondial, ménage les secteurs qui émettent énormément pour chaque euro encaissé, vidéo à la demande et jeu vidéo en tête.
Philippe Juvin, rapporteur général de la commission des finances, a rendu un premier avis défavorable : les géants visés répercuteraient selon lui le poids de la taxe sur leurs annonceurs. Côté gouvernement, David Amiel a suivi. Le ministre de l’Action et des Comptes publics juge le dispositif difficile à mettre en œuvre sans capteurs de flux, voire sans mesure « au niveau des terminaux individuels de réception ». Il estime aussi que la moitié du produit, soit 5 milliards d’euros, retomberait « sur des fournisseurs de contenus de plus petite taille, notamment sur des fournisseurs français ». Laurent Lhardit a balayé l’objection avec un exemple maison : la diffusion des cinq chaînes du groupe TF1 sur les box des opérateurs représenterait 200 000 à 300 000 euros de taxe, un poids qu’il juge faible pour les acteurs français.
Et maintenant, qui peut encore l’enterrer ?
Dès 2021, Orange, Deutsche Telekom et Telefónica réclamaient à Bruxelles une contribution des plus gros générateurs de trafic au financement des réseaux. La Commission européenne avait ouvert une consultation début 2023, avant de ranger le dossier faute de consensus. À une différence près : dans la version votée vendredi, les milliards iraient au budget de l’État, là où le programme socialiste de cet été fléchait 0,10 euro par gigaoctet vers le financement des infrastructures.
Pour l’abonné, cent gigaoctets de vidéo consommés dans le mois, un ordre de grandeur courant pour un foyer adepte des plateformes, représenteraient 5,50 euros de taxe, que rien n’interdirait aux services concernés de répercuter sur leurs tarifs ou leurs écrans publicitaires. Les porteurs du texte y voient même une vertu écologique, la taxe incitant à compresser et optimiser les volumes transmis.
Avant d’en arriver là, l’amendement doit d’abord survivre au vote de la première partie du budget, celle des recettes, dans une Assemblée où rien n’est acquis. Suivront un Sénat à majorité de droite, peu susceptible de la voter, puis l’hypothèse d’un 49.3. Yaël Braun-Pivet a publiquement appelé Sébastien Lecornu à l’utiliser, et le gouvernement garderait alors la main pour écarter la mesure du texte final.

articles.title: Acer Swift Air 14 : Boulanger allège de 300€ le prix de cet ultrabook poids plume pour le Black Friday
articles.text:
Avec son châssis léger et son écran de 14 pouces, l’ordinateur portable Acer Swift Air 14 est un modèle de portabilité. Même son prix est léger chez Boulanger : il passe de 899,99 € à 599,99 € pour le Black Friday.
Personne n’a envie de transporter un ordinateur portable lourd et encombrant lors de ses déplacements quotidiens. C’est pourquoi l’Acer Swift Air 14 se présente comme un modèle de choix pour les travailleurs nomades : il ne pèse que 1,19 kg. À l’occasion du lancement de son opération Black Friday, Boulanger le propose à 599,99 € au lieu de 899,99 €. C’est la version SFA14-I31-59JG du PC qui est concernée par cette offre : elle embarque un processeur Intel Core 5 320, 8 Go de mémoire vive et un SSD de 512 Go. Cette configuration bureautique fonctionne sous Windows 11.
L’Acer Swift Air 14 SFA14-I31-59JG est à 599,99 € au lieu de 899,99 € chez Boulanger.
Pourquoi choisir l’Acer Swift Air 14 ?
- Pour sa légèreté : ses 1,19 kg et son épaisseur d’environ 1,3 cm le rendent particulièrement facile à transporter au quotidien.
- Pour son écran fluide : la dalle IPS de 14 pouces monte à 120 Hz, ce qui améliore notamment la fluidité du défilement.
- Pour son stockage : le SSD de 512 Go permet de stocker de nombreux documents et d’installer vos logiciels de bureautique.
Un petit format qui soigne le confort de travail
L’écran du Swift Air 14 d’Acer est une dalle IPS qui affiche une définition de 1 920 × 1 200 pixels au format 16:10. Cette configuration permet de profiter d’un peu plus de hauteur pour lire les documents qu’un écran 16:9 plus classique, à largeur égale. La présence d’un traitement mat est également utile en déplacement, puisqu’il limite les reflets. Quant à son clavier rétroéclairé, il facilite la saisie en basse luminosité. Sa connectique comprend deux ports USB4 au format USB-C, un port USB-A et une prise casque. Pour les connexions sans fil, on trouve du Wi-Fi 6E et du Bluetooth 5.3.
Un ultraportable dont les 8 Go de RAM imposent des limites
Ce Swift Air mise sur la mobilité et l’affichage, mais il offre un peu moins de confort en ce qui concerne les usages multitâches. Notre test de l’Acer Swift Air 14 a d’ailleurs confirmé qu’avec 8 Go de RAM seulement, des ralentissements peuvent être constatés sous Windows 11.
✅ Les points forts
- Format léger de 1,19 kg.
- Écran IPS mat au format 16:10 et à 120 Hz
- Clavier rétroéclairé et connectique USB 4.
❌ Les limites
- 8 Go de RAM contraignants sous Windows 11.
- Chargeur secteur vendu séparément.
Pour le Black Friday, l’ultrabook Acer Swift Air 14 passe à 599,99 € chez Boulanger avec la livraison offerte.
L’Acer Swift Air 14 peut convenir aux étudiants et aux utilisateurs mobiles qui font de la transportabilité et du confort de lecture leurs priorités lorsqu’ils utilisent un ordinateur portable. Son clavier rétroéclairé est également un vrai atout.
Cependant, les utilisateurs qui ont l’habitude de jongler entre de nombreuses applications ou d’utiliser des logiciels créatifs risquent de se heurter bien vite aux limites de cette configuration, qui aurait mérité un peu plus de mémoire vive.

articles.title: Evercade Nexus Handheld Console Now Available
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
Evercade Nexus Handheld Console Now Available
Blaze Entertainment is proud to announce that the Evercade Nexus, the newest retro gaming handheld console from Evercade, is now available on Amazon, Funstock, Best Buy and GameStop, as well as other Evercade retailers across Europe and the US. Evercade continues to champion physical cartridges as the medium to relive the classic gaming experience. Buyers will receive RARE's 64-bit classic titles BANJO-KAZOOIE and BANJO-TOOIE with the console.
Andrew Byatt, CEO Blaze Entertainment LtdThe Evercade Nexus has arrived, marking a huge moment for us and an exciting new chapter for Evercade. We've spent years building a platform that celebrates great games, and Nexus takes that vision further than ever before. To launch with legendary names like Banjo-Kazooie and DOOM, alongside hundreds of games available on physical cartridges, is a fantastic achievement for the team. Nexus brings together everything we believe in: great games, physical ownership and the joy of discovering something new. We can't wait for players to experience it, and there's plenty more to come."
The Evercade Nexus is built to play with an ultra-bright 5.89" screen, the biggest ever screen on an Evercade, with a peak brightness of over 500nits. The new, larger design allows for dual analogue sticks, giving Evercade players the full experience of 64 and 32-bit games, and helping recreate the feel of arcade-style gaming in your hands. All of this in a new larger form factor that is still light and comfortable to use and travel with, and a sleek new look with a black colour scheme and a customisable RGB light-up logo.
At the centre of this new console is the heart of Evercade - the physical cartridge slot. Giving best-in-class emulation from over five decades of gaming, all presented in real physical gaming cartridges. Each one is a window into the best of gaming. It can highlight the works of a publisher like ACTIVISION, TAITO or RARE. Or the history of a franchise like TOMB RAIDER, DUKE NUKEM, LEGACY OF KAIN or DOOM. No downloads or wait times, just physical ownership, a full colour manual, and collectability with over 80 cartridges and 700+ games released since Evercade's launch in 2020.With Evercade Nexus, local multiplayer gaming on handheld is now possible thanks to EverSync! This new feature will allow players to share their game wirelessly to another Evercade Nexus console so both players can play the same game at the same time on their own screen. This new feature connects directly from console to console, and does not need WiFi or an internet connection. Only one game cartridge is required as well, meaning players can share their game even if the other player doesn't own that particular cartridge.
Many features return from previous Evercade devices, including TATE Mode, which allows for vertical screen orientation for authentic arcade gameplay, a custom user interface with full display ratio and scanline options, the Evercade library to track cartridge ownership, and wireless updates, including bonus features like the Indie Heroes Game of the Month. Combined with USB-C charging, our critically acclaimed D-Pad and responsive controls, this makes Evercade Nexus the ultimate Evercade experience.
Pricing
The Evercade Nexus comes with the console, the BANJO-KAZOOIE Double Pack cartridge, a USB-C to USB-A charging cable and quick start guide, and is available at Amazon, Funstock, Best Buy and GameStop, as well as other Evercade retailers across Europe and the US. 
PRICE: £169.99 | $199.99 | €199.99
In addition, accessories will be available to purchase separately, including an official Hard Shell EVA Carry Case with space for 6 cartridges, and a screen protector kit.

				Evercade

articles.title: Qué hacía MrBeast anter de ser millonario y alcanzar más de 500 millones de suscriptores en YouTube
articles.text:
MrBeast es actualmente el youtuber con más suscriptores del mundo. Su canal principal tiene 524 millones de suscriptores y su patrimonio neto asciende a USD 2.600 millones, de acuerdo con Fortune. Pero ¿a qué se dedicaba el creador de contenido antes de ser millonario y famoso?
Jimmy Donaldson, de 28 años, comenzó a subir videos a internet a los 13 años. Sus inicios estuvieron marcados por una adolescencia común en Carolina del Norte, Estados Unidos: creció en un hogar de clase media con dificultades económicas, junto a una madre soltera que trabajaba en varios empleos, según CNN.
A qué se dedicaba MrBeast antes de la fama y el dinero
Antes de la fama y el dinero, MrBeast construyó su carrera con videos caseros, horas de análisis sobre YouTube y desafíos de resistencia que buscaban captar la atención de la audiencia.
Jimmy Donaldson comenzó a publicar contenido a los 13 años. En febrero de 2012 subió su primer video bajo el nombre de MrBeast6000 y, durante los siguientes cuatro o cinco años, experimentó con distintos formatos.
Sus primeros contenidos incluyeron gameplays (videos en los que jugaba videojuegos), vlogs, análisis sobre las ganancias de otros creadores y retos de menor escala. En paralelo, dedicaba largas horas a estudiar el algoritmo de YouTube, las visitas, las miniaturas y las tendencias de la plataforma.
Donaldson también ingresó a la Universidad de Carolina del Este, aunque abandonó sus estudios dos semanas después para dedicarse por completo a la edición de videos. En esa etapa, llegó a vivir o trabajar desde su propio automóvil.
El punto de inflexión llegó en 2017, cuando publicó un video en el que contaba hasta 100.000. El desafío le demandó cerca de 40 horas de grabación.
Ese contenido se volvió viral y cambió el rumbo de su canal. A partir de entonces, los retos de resistencia comenzaron a convertirse en una de las marcas de sus videos.
MrBeast dará asesoría financiera a creadores de contenido
MrBeast se alió con Mastercard para impulsar herramientas financieras y oportunidades de negocio destinadas a creadores de contenido y consumidores.
La iniciativa, desarrollada junto con Beast Industries, la compañía fundada por Jimmy Donaldson, contempla programas de tarjetas de marca compartida, beneficios exclusivos, recursos de educación financiera y experiencias vinculadas con la comunidad del youtuber.
El objetivo de la colaboración es ayudar a que las personas conviertan sus ideas y su presencia en línea en proyectos sostenibles.
Según Jeff Housenbold, director ejecutivo de Beast Industries, el acuerdo permitirá ofrecer habilidades prácticas y confianza para llevar adelante iniciativas propias.
Jill Kramer, directora de marketing y comunicaciones de Mastercard, sostuvo que la nueva generación está creando formas de comercio mientras moldea la cultura digital.
Donaldson pasó de publicar videos en YouTube a construir una empresa con presencia en medios de comunicación, productos de consumo, plataformas tecnológicas, servicios móviles y propuestas financieras.
La alianza busca aprovechar ese alcance para conectar cultura y comercio mediante servicios orientados a quienes buscan desarrollar negocios.
MrBeast pide un Tesla Roadster volador
MrBeast pidió a Tesla un Roadster con capacidad de vuelo para grabar un video, tras la presentación del nuevo deportivo eléctrico de la compañía. Jimmy Donaldson publicó la solicitud el 17 de octubre en X, pero Elon Musk y Tesla no respondieron públicamente.
El vehículo que interesó al creador es el Roadster Rocket, un monoplaza disponible solo por invitación.
Tesla afirmó que puede volar con 10 propulsores de gas frío, alerones activos y un sistema de succión bajo la carrocería. Sin embargo, el modelo no estará habilitado para circular en vías públicas y Musk advirtió que no fue optimizado para la seguridad.
La empresa prevé iniciar la producción en 2028. Musk también anunció una pista de pruebas con loopings en Texas, donde los propietarios podrían ensayar maniobras, incluidas funciones autónomas.

articles.title: Voitures électriques : au Portugal, elles pourraient bientôt être financées à 80% par l'État. Et en France ?
articles.text:
Les États veulent pousser le plus possible leurs citoyens vers les véhicules électriques. Au point de réfléchir à massivement aider au niveau financier !
Il faut le plus rapidement possible faire passer le parc automobile du thermique à l'électrique. Voilà l'idée générale en Europe. Mais pour y arriver, les stratégies sont multiples, des interdictions aux subventions. Dans ce domaine, si l'on a déjà de bonnes aides en France, on pourrait vite apparaître comme des petits joueurs avec ce qui pourrait se passer au Portugal !
Le Portugal voudrait subventionner jusqu'à 80% du prix d'un véhicule électrique pour les ménages les plus modestes
Au Portugal, on pourrait sortir l'artillerie lourde au niveau des aides pour les voitures électriques. À l'occasion des débats sur le budget 2027, la ministre de l'Environnement et de l'Énergie Maria da Graça Carvalho a ainsi indiqué que le gouvernement réfléchit à augmenter spectaculairement les aides.
Ainsi, les ménages les plus modestes du Portugal pourraient bien bénéficier d'un soutien qui représentera jusqu'à 80% du prix d'un nouveau véhicule électrique. Une façon de mettre fin au barrage représenté par le prix pour de nombreuses personnes.
Un plafond à 15 000 € HT imposé
Cette aide exceptionnelle pourrait concerner environ 20 000 véhicules. Il faut tout de même noter que les potentiels bénéficiaires ne pourront pas faire leur choix parmi tout ce qui existe. Ce soutien est réservé à l'acquisition d'un véhicule coûtant moins ou 15 000 € HT - ce qui pourrait par exemple inclure la Renault Twingo E-Tech.
À noter que le Portugal a aussi d'autres aides plus classiques, qui touchent elles l'ensemble de la population - le gouvernement veut ainsi allouer 50 millions d'euros aux enveloppes dédiées à l'ensemble des Portugais. La France pourrait-elle prendre exemple sur ce pays du sud de l'Europe, et doubler les aides actuelles avec un subventionnement beaucoup plus fort pour les ménages les plus modestes, qui peuvent à ce jour avoir jusqu'à 7700 euros d'aides ?
Source : Automobile Propre

articles.title: Extreme Networks wants the network to run AI, not just be run by it - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Extreme Networks wants the network to run AI, not just be run by it
At its recent AI Summit in Amsterdam, Extreme Networks Inc. shared early Agent ONE Coworker results and previewed Exchange zones, which put spare access points and switch compute to work as on-premises artificial intelligence infrastructure. Here’s what it means and what information technology pros should do about it.
Most of the conversation about AI and networking has flowed in one direction. AI comes in, examines the network and helps the network team run it better. That’s useful, but it treats the network as the patient, not as a resource.
At the summit, the company argued that there is a better way. The network should be managed by AI and serve as a place where AI runs, using data that most organizations currently throw away. This would let network teams stop being the people who merely keep the Wi-Fi up for the AI project and become the people who host it.
The news
Extreme made two announcements. The first was a progress report on Extreme Agent ONE Coworker, the ambient AI agent built into Extreme Platform ONE. In its first month, Extreme says, customers saved about 1,000 hours of troubleshooting, 41% of Platform ONE customers used it for daily tasks, and users responded to 98% of critical “nudges,” the proactive alerts the agent raises after running its own pre-investigation. Engagement was roughly 10 times that of Extreme’s first-generation conversational assistant.
The second was a preview of Extreme Exchange zones, planned for the first half of 2027. A zone combines an Extreme Universal Compute Platform or a customer-owned server with spare capacity from Extreme access points and switches already installed at a site. AI applications from the Extreme Exchange marketplace run locally on open-weight models by default, with cloud inference used only when policy allows and logged every time. Agent ONE Operator mode, the autonomous tier, also arrives in the first half of 2027.
Ambient beats conversational
The first wave of AI in networking wasn’t a smashing success because it relied on a chatbot built on fragmented data. During his talk, Nabil Bukhari (pictured), Extreme’s chief technology officer and president of AI platforms, called it a design flaw. “Conversational AI requires the user to have the question and the context, and you will be surprised how difficult that is when it comes to technology domains,” he said.
In Extreme’s focus groups, many administrators asked a powerful AI assistant how many devices they had, even though the number was already on the dashboard. Coworker flips that. “We have moved to the world where instead of you prompting AI, AI prompts you,” Bukhari said.
The best evidence came from a customer. Kevin Rocha, chief information officer at Hill College, described a wireless outage in a building housing HR, finance and enrollment. “Agent ONE Coworker told me exactly where to look: One access point needed attention, and several more were due for firmware upgrades. We resolved the issue in about 20 minutes rather than an entire morning,” he said. Platform ONE, he added, “is like having two or three more network engineers on staff.”
That’s the value of AI for networking in most enterprises. It doesn’t replace the network team. It gives a small team the reach of a larger one. Bukhari also admitted that there is more work to be done. He explained that 58% of support cases opened by Agent ONE arrive with all the evidence support needs. “Fifty-eight is pretty good, but 58 is still 58 and not 100.”
Governance has to live outside the agent
Andrew Grill, the opening keynote speaker and author of “Digitally Curious,” discussed the stakes. “When a chatbot gets it wrong, you might have a bad paragraph. If an agent gets it wrong, you have a bad Tuesday,” he said. His test for any deployment: “If your agent does something wrong at 2 in the morning, whose phone rings?”
Extreme’s Operator demo is subject to guardrails. Each of the 268 tools can be configured to auto-authorize, ask first or never use. Four baseline rules apply to everything: do no harm to the network, never expose a credential, never act outside your role and never act in another tenant. Every task has a full audit trace.
An important design criterion is that governance reside within Extreme Exchange, not Platform ONE. “You can’t govern something from within,” Bukhari said. “That is how you get rogue agents.” If the system running the agent also controls its permissions, you don’t have a control plane. You have an honor system.
Exchange zones are the bigger bet
Networks generate dense, real-time telemetry on location, movement and behavior that far exceeds what operations needs, and cloud platforms drop most of it because moving it is expensive. Bukhari said the valuable uses tend to hit four walls: sovereignty, localization, survivability and economics.
The innovation is where the compute comes from. Higher-end access points have four to eight cores and typically use only one, so organizations already pay for and power idle compute hanging from their ceilings. In one healthcare demo, a fall-detection app that combined camera feeds, Wi-Fi location and paging to find the closest responder ran entirely on access points. A second demo used Seattle Seahawks game data to predict gate congestion and showed that some fans faced a seven- to eight-minute walk to the nearest pro shop.
“This is not a network management use case,” Bukhari said. “These use cases are impossible without that rich, real-time telemetry.” That’s the strategic point. The return goes to operations, facilities and fan experience, giving network leaders something they’ve rarely had: a revenue story.
Zones will ship in 2027, and the demo apps were built in collaboration with design partners. The model needs a real application catalog, so Extreme is pairing it with a free, invitation-only forward-deployed engineering program. Pricing will be consumption-based, measured in “agent actions.” As Grill noted, most organizations haven’t priced the cost of their tasks today, so they’ll struggle to judge value.
Sovereignty is about permission
As expected, the most valuable insights came from the customer panel. Jonathan Monk, CIO of the Institute of Cancer Research in London, manages roughly 9 petabytes of data, but performance isn’t his primary reason for building sovereign AI. “When we ask people in our organization what’s the biggest thing that holds them back from using AI, it’s that I’m not sure if I’m allowed to,” he said.
Andrew Beynon, chief enterprise architect at Extreme partner ARO, linked that to shadow AI. The goal, he said, is “to make the journey for legitimate adoption of AI easier than the move to illegitimate adoption.” Monk called it building “paved roads.” The industry treats sovereignty as a compliance cost, but these customers see it as an adoption accelerator.
David O’Neill, director of IT operations at Liverpool Football Club, offered a balanced take on AI. “While AI is an answer, it’s not necessarily the answer.” Bukhari highlighted the next challenge: “Adoption is no longer the problem. It’s the optimization of adoption.” After AI-generated product specs ballooned to 200 pages, Extreme capped them at three pages.
Advice for IT pros
Include the network team in the AI plan. If it isn’t involved, decisions about traffic, inference location and data residency will be made without the people who understand them.
Separate governance from execution. Check whether agent permissions, audit logs and the kill switch are outside the system the agent runs in.
Inventory the data your network discards. Identify the location and occupancy telemetry you already generate, and which business units would pay to use them.
Pressure-test the edge-compute math. Ask how workloads are prioritized during RF demand spikes and which model sizes realistically fit on an access point.
Price your tasks first. Without a baseline cost for today’s work, it’s impossible to evaluate consumption-based AI pricing.
Final thoughts
Extreme can’t outspend its larger competitors, so it’s betting on speed and focus as a pure-play networking company. The Agent ONE numbers suggest that’s paying off on the operations side.
Exchange zones are the bolder idea. Turning installed access points and switches into a distributed, centrally governed inference fabric is more ambitious than anything I’ve seen from Extreme’s larger rivals. It’s also unproven, and 2027 is a long way off in AI time. As Beynon put it, “today’s knowledge has got an expiry date.”
The direction Extreme is headed is the right one. For 30 years, the network has been the most important infrastructure, yet nobody wanted to talk about it until it broke. AI makes the network the system that connects data, compute and people, and possibly the one that runs the AI, too. Network pros who see that early will have a much bigger role in where their organizations go next.
