articles.title: As Anthropic finally files for IPO, rising risks aren't slowing the AI buildout - yet - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
As Anthropic finally files for IPO, rising risks aren’t slowing the AI buildout – yet
The other artificial intelligence shoe dropped this week, as Anthropic filed for what surely will be the second blockbuster AI initial public offering of stock this year.
Nearly 70,000 words in the filing list a ton of risks, but in short, it’s making unimaginably huge bets on buying computing power, it’s uncertain on how long customers will keep spending on AI in the face of dubious returns — and of course there’s the really-not-unusual “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.” And as Jason Bloomberg writes, the unmentioned risk is that AI as of today doesn’t have the economies of scale that made software so lucrative.
But it’s hard to imagine it won’t be crazily successful if and when it happens before Thanksgiving. They’ll join the 70% of Nvidia employees who are millionaires. Shed another tear for anyone looking for affordable housing in the Bay Area — we’re not building our way out of this, no matter what YIMBY folks hope.
One interesting wrinkle: SpaceXAI, the other AI IPO earlier this year, will be hoping Anthropic’s offering is successful, since it’s supplying a large chunk of that compute. Same with other AI partner/rivals such as Google and Microsoft.
And Anthropic isn’t alone in amassing cash to continue buying and building more AI infrastructure. Meta this week said it will issue $95 billion in nonvoting stock to build even more. Few, least of all universal backstop Nvidia, seem to think the AI and data center backlash will dent this investment. But that doesn’t mean everyone will win. As SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said this week, self-servingly but perhaps not wrongly (Gartner agrees), a lot of AI neoclouds are going to go belly-up.
Investor worry extends to the big cloud providers too. Despite a continued boom in its cloud business, Google parent Alphabet saw its stock swoon more than 12% Thursday, vaporizing more than $500 billion in market value as it reported a slow quarter for search and ads — perhaps because AI chatbots are siphoning off people’s attention. Microsoft fared better thanks to its resilient application layer on which it can apply AI. But despite strong cloud revenue growth, Amazon stock fell on concerns it could be spending too much on infrastructure. All that came to a head Friday, when the Nasdaq tanked, down almost 3%.
Seems like investors are just generally skittish. On a tear this year until now, Intel stock plunged almost 30% after its Thursday earnings report, on concerns the PC business is slowing. Fortinet also fell more than 20% following its report that included a slightly lower outlook.
Don’t relax yet. Next week there’s another earningspalooza, including Apple, AMD, Supermicro, Qualcomm, Arm and Palantir.
So an apparent Chinese spy for some time has been hanging around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who evidently didn’t know she was more than a customer executive. Lordy. The New York Times laid out the bones of the U.S. government’s concern, but read it carefully and it sure seems like there are some missing dots throughout. Perhaps this kind of espionage is more common than we know where there’s a nexus of big money and geopolitics, but this may not be the last we hear of it, even if the Trump administration is shrugging.
Oh, and there’s an election next week that might change things… in unpredictable, not necessarily great ways for the economy. Fasten those seatbelts. And vote (but not for the wrong people, thanks).

articles.title: Here's why the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite gaming headset remains the best gaming headset I've ever tested — and wins our Gaming Device of the Year award
articles.text:
There are only so many ways I can say how good the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite is, but perhaps the simplest way is the best: it is the greatest gaming headset I have ever tested and reviewed.
Yup, it still looks very familiar, and very SteelSeries Arctis on the outside, but this headset is like no other in the brand's lineup, or the wider market. Everything, every minute detail, has had time and consideration poured into it, and it really is the fullest realization of what a gaming headset can be, and a natural winner at the TechRadar Product of the Year Awards 2026.
First and foremost, as I laid out in my full SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite review, it's got that brilliant out-of-the-box SteelSeries audio — but not quite as we all know it. The brand-new custom-made carbon fiber audio driver, held in place by a brass surround ring, makes for a different, but still breathtaking, flavor.
Combine that SteelSeries Arctis tuning with the new hardware combination, and you get unbelievable immersion, supremely accurate sound reproduction of anything and everything, and excellently rich and detailed certified Hi-Res Audio for a wireless gaming headset.
While I could talk about the audio alone for ages, the Elite backs up its brilliant sound with a faultless feature set.
Firstly, building on the brilliant DAC unit the Arctis Nova Pro headsets introduced, the Elite's GameHub with OmniPlay means you can be connected to every platform type, basically simultaneously.
It's fabulous. Utilizing this, as well as the headset's Bluetooth connection, you can actually connect to up to four different sources, and mix and listen to them altogether. You might never need four, but being connected to my console and PC, and having Bluetooth on to take phone calls, has been really useful for me.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
You've got two different microphone modes (a retractable boom, which is fantastic quality, and built-in ones for convenience), the 'infinite' battery supply due to a spare being charged in the GameHub all the time, and a host of EQ and other controls in the GameHub.
The Nova Elite feels fantastically premium, and joyous to wear and use. The cold-rolled steel and aluminum materials are superb, the leatherette cushions are sublime, the metallic volume wheel is a tiny but glorious touch, and every button and material finish feels worthy of the headset's lofty price tag.
Other headsets might tickle different fancies, or appeal to different priorities that folks might have; but for anyone looking for a premium, do-it-all headset for all of their devices that excels in every way, it has to be the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite. You simply will not find a better headset offering the same combination of design, features and audio quality. Buy it, and you will never look back.

articles.title: Attention à ce message WhatsApp, il permet aux pirates de prendre le contrôle de votre compte
articles.text:
La gendarmerie nationale alerte sur la prolifération d’une arnaque qui cible les utilisateurs de WhatsApp. L’objectif des arnaqueurs : prendre le contrôle de votre compte WhatsApp. Pour y parvenir, l’arnaqueur se fait passer pour l’un de vos proches et vous invite à voter pour la fille d’une connaissance qui participe à un concours de danse. En réalité, il n’y a aucun vote, seulement une arnaque bien ficelée.
Un faux concours de danse pour pirater votre compte WhatsApp
Tout commence par un message semblant provenir de l’un de vos proches. En réalité, un pirate a pris le contrôle du compte de ce proche et se fait passer pour lui. Le message vous invite à voter pour une jeune fille qui participe à un soi-disant concours de danse. Dans toutes les arnaques de ce type repérées en ligne, les noms Sophie et Eliska sont mobilisés.
Dans l’exemple ci-dessous, nous pouvons lire : « Coucou ! Tu as passé une nuit confortable ? J’ai un petit service à te glisser : accorde ton vote à Sophie, la fille de mes amis. Elle est engagée dans un concours, et l’enjeu, c’est une bourse d’études plus la possibilité de fouler la scène ».
Qui ne serait pas prêt à aider une enfant qui a la possibilité de réaliser l’un de ses rêves et de toucher une bourse d’études ? Justement, les arnaqueurs misent sur ce message qui semble aussi touchant qu’anodin pour arriver à leurs fins.
Nous arrivons ici au cœur de l’arnaque : le lien mis en avant qui permettrait soi-disant de voter pour la jeune fille. En réalité, la victime est redirigée vers un faux site de vote qui prétend avoir besoin de son numéro de téléphone pour valider sa participation. Elle reçoit ensuite un code de vérification qui, lorsqu’il est partagé, permet aux arnaqueurs de connecter son compte WhatsApp à leur propre appareil. Une fois le compte piraté, ils seront en mesure de contacter les proches de la victime pour les arnaquer (demande d’argent, tentative de phishing, etc.).
Rappelons au passage que les messages frauduleux semblant venir de proches présentent des variantes du type « j’ai retrouvé des photos de toi petit [lien frauduleux] » ou « je suis tombé sur des photos de toi compromettantes [lien frauduleux] ».
Comment ne pas tomber dans le piège ?
Le premier conseil est de ne cliquer en aucun cas sur le lien mis en avant et de ne jamais partager un code de vérification. Par ailleurs, n’approuvez sous aucun prétexte une connexion que vous n’avez pas demandée. Et comme le rappelle la gendarmerie nationale, veillez également à activer la vérification en deux étapes.
Faites aussi attention à certains détails : les liens frauduleux repérés dans ces arnaques renvoient vers les sites « academybalet.lat » et « fibsdance.site », soit des noms qui ne correspondent à aucune académie de danse. En cas de doute, contactez directement votre proche via un autre moyen de communication pour vous assurer qu’il est bien à l’origine du message (par appel téléphonique de préférence). Si le mal est déjà fait, rendez-vous dans la section « Appareils connectés » de WhatsApp et déconnectez tout appareil inconnu. Enfin, alertez au plus vite vos proches de la situation.

articles.title: Javier Calvo, director de 'La Bola Negra': "Se ha podido hacer con menos de 15 millones de euros porque tiene dos directores"
articles.text:
En una entrevista con CNN en Español, Javier Calvo respondió a la pregunta que más le repiten desde Cannes: cómo una película de época con tres líneas temporales y miles de figurantes ha costado "menos de 15 millones de euros". Su explicación fue que "la han podido hacer entre dos personas". Y eso que la película no es precisamente barata. Repasemos y comparemos cifra a cifra.
Pero cuánto ha costado. La resolución del ICAA que en octubre de 2025 concedió a la película un millón de euros en ayudas generales recoge un presupuesto de 9,9 millones, pero solo contando la parte española. La ficha del catálogo del ICAA atribuye a España el 90% de la coproducción y a Francia el 10%, así que el coste total del film rondaría los 11 millones. Desde ahí, se podría redondear hacia arriba hasta 14 millones al sumar promoción y distribución, o con el cambio de divisa, hablar de 15 millones de dólares, como cuando empezó a distribuirse en Estados Unidos. Calvo apunta a "menos de 15".
Cuánto dinero es. En España, 9,9 millones para producir una película es mucho dinero. El coste medio de un largometraje español de 2024 es de unos 2,8 millones. Solo la parte española de 'La bola negra' multiplica esa media por 3,5. Tampoco todo ese dinero sale del mismo bolsillo. El solicitante de la ayuda es la empresa Los Esquiadores, A.I.E., que concentra el 98,32% de la parte española.
Cuánto dinero gana. Si 'La bola negra' parece una ganga es porque la taquilla ha sido espectacular. Esta semana sumaba 34,3 millones de euros y 5,1 millones de espectadores, convirtiéndose en la cuarta película española más taquillera de la historia en salas nacionales. En Estados Unidos Netflix, que la estrena allí, publicó su taquilla, algo que no hacía con ningún estreno desde hacía diez años, para presumir de un primer fin de semana cifrado en 277.619 dólares en solo cuatro salas.
Por qué es más fácil. Calvo y Ambrossi describen para CNN cómo se hizo un reparto de horas de trabajo. Ambrossi contó que eligieron "uno a uno" a los miles de extras, revisando vídeos y castings, y que mientras él hacía eso Calvo podía preparar con la dirección de fotografía cada jornada. "Un director no puede estar eligiendo miles y miles de extras", dijo.
Lo hacen todo. Los dos, además, producen. La ficha del ICAA acredita a Ambrossi como productor y sitúa entre las productoras a Suma Content Films, la empresa que comparten. Pero la película figura como escrita, dirigida y producida por los dos, es decir, que el multiplicador de Calvo se cuenta en jornadas: dos personas que hacen varias funciones, y que pueden estar en dos sitios a la vez.
Equipo. Curiosamente, no siempre las parejas de directores son contabilizados como una sola cabeza. En Estados Unidos, desde el convenio de 1978, el Sindicato de Directores (DGA) solo admite un director por película, como una forma de protección frente a productores y estrellas. Las excepciones existen, entre ellas los llamados bona fide teams, que el sindicato reserva a quienes ya han dirigido antes y han demostrado funcionar como un solo director. Por ejemplo, hasta 'Ladykillers', en 2004, los hermanos Coen no solicitaron la exención de codirección y Robert Rodriguez abandonó el sindicato para poder acreditar a Frank Miller como codirector de 'Sin City'.

articles.title: Ce TV Mini LED Samsung de 2026 ouvre le Black Friday de Boulanger sous les 450 €
articles.text:
Le Black Friday ne tombe que le 27 novembre, mais Boulanger a déjà ouvert le bal, et l’une des premières offres porte sur un téléviseur sorti cette année. Le TU50M72H fait entrer le MiniLED dans le bas du catalogue Samsung 2026 et repasse sous la barre des 450 € dans sa version 50 pouces, de quoi moderniser un salon sans viser le haut de gamme.
Avec la gamme M72H, Samsung propose sa technologie MiniLED dans l’entrée de gamme de son catalogue 2026. Le modèle de 50 pouces, mis en ligne fin avril 2026, s’adresse avant tout aux foyers qui veulent un vrai gain de contraste pour les films, les séries et le sport.
Pour le lancement de son Black Friday, Boulanger l’affiche à 449 € au lieu d’un prix de référence de 529 €, soit 15 % de remise, sur un produit neuf vendu et expédié par l’enseigne. C’est moins que les 499 € relevés chez Boulanger en juillet, et moins que les prix pratiqués actuellement chez Cdiscount, Darty ou la Fnac, autour de 500 €.
TV Samsung MiniLED TU50M72H à 449 € au lieu de 529 €
Pourquoi choisir le téléviseur Mini LED Samsung ?
- Un rétroéclairage MiniLED, qui apporte des noirs plus tenus et des hautes lumières mieux maîtrisées qu’un téléviseur LED d’entrée de gamme.
- Trois ports HDMI 2.1 compatibles VRR et ALLM, assez pour brancher une console et deux autres appareils.
- Sept ans de mises à jour gratuites, sécurisées par Knox.
- Les applications des box Bouygues, Free, Orange et SFR, ainsi que la compatibilité AirPlay 2.
- Un indice de durabilité de 8,2 sur 10.
Un 50 pouces taillé pour le salon, pas pour la compétition
Le TU50M72H a un profil assez clair : remplacer un vieux téléviseur Full HD par un modèle 4K qui apporte un vrai gain de contraste, sans viser le haut de gamme. Tizen centralise le streaming et donne accès aux applications des principaux opérateurs, ce qui permet de se passer du décodeur de sa box pour regarder la télévision, tandis qu’AirPlay 2 et le Bluetooth facilitent le partage depuis un téléphone ou l’envoi du son vers un casque. Les tuners TNT, satellite et câble sont aussi de la partie.
Le jeu vidéo est en revanche son point faible. Malgré trois ports HDMI 2.1, le VRR et l’ALLM, Boulanger annonce une fréquence de balayage native de 50 Hz, et la fonction Motion Xcelerator ne monte à 120 Hz qu’en 2K. La rédaction de Clubic estimait déjà que la gamme M72H est bien plus à l’aise avec les films, les séries et le sport qu’avec le jeu à haute fréquence. Côté son, les 20 W intégrés risquent de paraître justes dans une grande pièce, et les amateurs de cinéma noteront l’absence de Dolby Vision et de Dolby Atmos, habituelle chez Samsung. Enfin, le téléviseur ne propose pas de prise casque.
Le Mini LED descend en gamme, et ça se voit à l’écran
Un rétroéclairage plus fin pour mieux tenir les noirs
L’intérêt principal du TU50M72H tient à sa technologie Mini LED Pure Spectrum Vision AI. Le rétroéclairage, composé de diodes bien plus petites que sur un téléviseur LED classique, est piloté plus finement, ce qui permet d’afficher en même temps des noirs profonds et des blancs très lumineux. La dalle 10 bits affiche jusqu’à 1,07 milliard de couleurs, et le processeur Mini LED 4K se charge de la mise à l’échelle des contenus de plus basse définition, un point important quand une bonne partie de la télévision et du streaming n’est pas encore diffusée en 4K.
Sept ans de suivi pour durer
L’autre argument, moins visible mais tout aussi utile, est la durée de suivi. Samsung promet sept ans de mises à jour gratuites et sécurisées par Knox, et Boulanger indique une disponibilité des pièces détachées pendant sept ans à compter de la fabrication. L’assistant Vision AI Companion répond aux questions et propose des suggestions directement depuis le téléviseur, tandis que Bixby se charge des commandes vocales.
✅ Les points forts
- Rétroéclairage MiniLED rare à ce niveau de gamme chez Samsung.
- Trois ports HDMI 2.1 avec VRR et ALLM.
- Sept ans de mises à jour et indice de durabilité de 8,2.
- Applications des box opérateurs et AirPlay 2 intégrés.
❌ Les limites
- Fréquence native de 50 Hz, peu adaptée au jeu exigeant.
- Pas de Dolby Vision ni de Dolby Atmos.
- Son de 20 W un peu juste dans une grande pièce.
- Pas de prise casque.
TV Samsung MiniLED TU50M72H à 449 € au lieu de 529 €
Le TU50M72H ne s’adresse pas aux joueurs ni aux cinéphiles exigeants, mais il coche l’essentiel pour un salon de taille moyenne qui veut profiter du MiniLED et d’un suivi logiciel long. À 449 €, il fait partie des offres à surveiller de ce Black Friday anticipé, et les retours prolongés jusqu’à fin janvier laissent le temps de l’offrir ou de changer d’avis après les fêtes.

articles.title: Modo Halloween en WhatsApp: cómo activarlo en iPhone y Android
articles.text:
Con la llegada de Halloween, los usuarios de WhatsApp pueden personalizar la apariencia de la aplicación para darle un estilo relacionado con la celebración del 31 de octubre. Aunque la plataforma no cuenta con una función oficial denominada “modo Halloween”, permite combinar diferentes herramientas para modificar la foto de perfil, los fondos de los chats y los colores de las conversaciones.
Estos cambios están disponibles tanto en teléfonos Android como en iPhone y no requieren instalar aplicaciones externas ni utilizar versiones modificadas de WhatsApp. La personalización se realiza desde los ajustes habituales de la plataforma y permite incorporar imágenes de calabazas, fantasmas, casas embrujadas y otros elementos asociados con la fecha.
Además, quienes tengan acceso a Meta AI pueden utilizar la inteligencia artificial para generar imágenes temáticas que luego pueden emplearse como fondos de conversación o compartirse con otros contactos.
Antes de comenzar, es recomendable actualizar WhatsApp desde Google Play Store o App Store para comprobar que estén disponibles las opciones de personalización más recientes. Algunas herramientas pueden variar según el modelo del teléfono, la versión de la aplicación y la región.
Cómo cambiar la foto de perfil de WhatsApp por una imagen de Halloween
Uno de los primeros pasos para personalizar la cuenta consiste en reemplazar temporalmente la fotografía del perfil por una imagen relacionada con la celebración.
Para hacerlo, tanto en Android como en iPhone se debe abrir WhatsApp e ingresar a Configuración. En Android, esta opción aparece en el menú de los tres puntos ubicado en la parte superior de la pantalla. En iPhone, se encuentra en la barra inferior de la aplicación.
Después, hay que tocar la fotografía de perfil y seleccionar la opción para modificarla. El usuario puede elegir una imagen almacenada en la galería, tomar una fotografía nueva o utilizar un avatar, si tiene habilitada esa función.
Entre las alternativas se encuentran ilustraciones de calabazas, personajes disfrazados, fantasmas o diseños con colores oscuros. También es posible editar una fotografía antes de utilizarla como imagen de la cuenta.
El nombre del perfil también puede modificarse temporalmente para incorporar alguna referencia a Halloween. Sin embargo, conviene tener en cuenta que los contactos podrán visualizar estos cambios, por lo que es recomendable mantener una identificación reconocible si se utiliza WhatsApp para cuestiones laborales.
Cómo colocar fondos de Halloween en las conversaciones
Otra alternativa consiste en modificar el fondo de pantalla de los chats. Esta herramienta permite reemplazar la imagen habitual por una ilustración temática sin alterar los mensajes ni los archivos compartidos.
En Android y iPhone, el procedimiento comienza al abrir una conversación y acceder a su menú de opciones o información. Allí se debe buscar el apartado de tema o fondo de pantalla, seleccionar la imagen deseada y ajustar su posición antes de guardar los cambios.
Los usuarios pueden elegir fotografías o ilustraciones de bosques oscuros, lunas llenas, casas embrujadas, calabazas iluminadas y otros elementos relacionados con la celebración.
Es importante seleccionar imágenes que no tengan demasiados detalles o colores que dificulten la lectura. Un fondo demasiado recargado puede reducir el contraste de los mensajes y hacer menos cómoda la visualización de las conversaciones.
Cómo cambiar los colores de los chats para Halloween
WhatsApp también incorpora opciones de personalización que permiten modificar los colores y la apariencia de las conversaciones mediante los temas de chat.
Para acceder a esta herramienta, hay que ingresar a una conversación y buscar el apartado de tema o apariencia. Según las opciones disponibles en cada dispositivo, se pueden elegir distintas combinaciones de colores y diseños.
Para conseguir una estética de Halloween, los tonos naranja, violeta, negro y verde oscuro permiten crear una apariencia relacionada con la celebración. La configuración puede aplicarse a conversaciones individuales, de manera que cada chat tenga un diseño diferente.
Estos ajustes son exclusivamente visuales: no modifican el funcionamiento de WhatsApp, la privacidad de los mensajes ni las medidas de seguridad de la cuenta.
Cómo utilizar Meta AI para crear imágenes de Halloween en WhatsApp
Los usuarios que tengan disponible Meta AI dentro de WhatsApp pueden recurrir a esta herramienta para generar imágenes personalizadas relacionadas con Halloween.
Para ello, pueden escribir una instrucción que describa el diseño que desean obtener. Por ejemplo: “Crea una ilustración de una calabaza iluminada frente a una casa antigua, con un bosque oscuro y una luna llena”.
La inteligencia artificial puede utilizar esa descripción como punto de partida para producir una imagen que luego podrá compartirse en conversaciones o utilizarse como recurso visual.
También es posible solicitar diseños con fantasmas, murciélagos, cementerios o personajes disfrazados. La calidad y disponibilidad de estas funciones dependen de la versión de WhatsApp, el dispositivo y la región.
Al utilizar Meta AI, es recomendable evitar compartir información personal, fotografías de terceros sin autorización o datos que permitan identificar a menores de edad.
De esta manera, los usuarios pueden crear su propio modo Halloween en WhatsApp mediante las herramientas de personalización disponibles en Android y iPhone, sin modificar el funcionamiento de la aplicación ni comprometer la seguridad de sus cuentas.

articles.title: Cursor diz que extensão falsa do Claude Code afetou até 5 mil usuários • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Cursor diz que extensão falsa do Claude Code afetou até 5 mil usuários
Versão maliciosa tentava roubar dados do computador e abrir acesso remoto por SSH.
A Cursor, responsável pelo editor de código de mesmo nome, identificou e removeu uma versão adulterada da extensão Claude Code, da Anthropic, que pode ter afetado até 5 mil usuários. O pacote malicioso tentava coletar informações do computador e instalar um backdoor por SSH para permitir acesso remoto à maquina.
A versão corrompida, Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.313, ficou disponível no marketplace de extensões da plataforma entre 6h27 a 17h35 de 29 de outubro, no horário de Brasília. Após identificar o incidente, a empresa, que pertence à SpaceX, de Elon Musk, retirou a extensão do ar e chegou a suspender temporariamente o marketplace.
Segundo a companhia, não há evidências de adulteração em outros pacotes. A Cursor também reconstruiu o marketplace antes de colocá-lo no ar novamente. Usuários potencialmente afetados pelo problema devem ser contatados diretamente pela plataforma.
Segundo o alerta publicado pela Cursor, a versão maliciosa não foi criada pela Anthropic, mas se passava pelo pacote do Claude Code contendo um código que comprometia a máquina de quem a instalasse. Depois da instalação, o programa coletava informações como nome do usuário e do PC, sistema operacional, arquitetura do processador, diretórios de trabalho, e-mail do Git e endereço IP.
Em seguida, a extensão tentava adicionar ao computador uma chave SSH controlada pelo invasor, identificada como svc-telemetry, para criar uma porta de entrada que pudesse ser usada posteriormente. Usando a mesma chave, o malware procurava estabelecer um túnel reverso até um servidor externo, o que permitiria acessar a máquina remotamente.
Para manter esse acesso mesmo depois de uma reinicialização, o código ainda instalava mecanismos de persistência no Windows e no macOS. As rotinas eram programadas para tentar restabelecer a conexão aproximadamente a cada 60 segundos.
Parte das informações coletadas e o estado da conexão com o servidor também eram enviados para a infraestrutura controlada pelo invasor.
A tentativa do acesso remoto, porém, não funcionou como planejado na maior parte dos computadores. Segundo a plataforma, o código continha erros e dependia de permissões elevadas para ativar o serviço SSH. Dessa forma, o risco era maior apenas em máquinas que deram permissões de administrador ou root ao Cursor.
Mesmo nesses casos, a empresa recomenda que qualquer pessoa que tenha instalado a versão comprometida faça uma verificação do sistema. A orientação vale para quem instalou ou atualizou a extensão Anthropic.claude-code para a versão 2.1.313 durante o período em que ela esteve disponível.
Uma das formas de verificar a máquina é procurar pela chave svc-telemetry, adicionada pelo malware às configurações de SSH.

articles.title: 3D-printed ghost guns may now have a way to be traced to their source — Australian researchers correctly identify 26 out of 28 printed PLA samples to their filament product
articles.text:
3D-printed ghost guns may now have a way to be traced to their source — Australian researchers correctly identify 26 out of 28 printed PLA samples to their filament product
It only tests for PLA, but it's a starting point.
A study published on October 22 in the journal Forensic Science International reports that researchers from Curtin University in Perth, Australia, have developed a forensic method to analyze 3D-printed PLA parts and match them to their respective filament, correctly matching 26 out of 28 samples of PLA. This potentially provides a way to link seized 3D-printed “ghost-guns” with other seized filament, allowing police to form a clearer network for the manufacturing and distribution of the 3D-printed firearms.
3D-printed firearms have become a big problem worldwide, as they are untraceable and even compostable in the case of PLA, with tools like this AI 3D-printed gun generator making it scarily accessible. Serial numbers, registration, and a network of licensed distributors are usually the first line of investigation when it comes to crime involving firearms, but easily manufacturable, untraceable, disposable plastic firearms are a new threat with no clear way to crack down on them yet.
However, this research, by Dr. Georgina Sauzier et al. from Curtin University's School of Molecular and Life Sciences, along with forensics experts from ChemCentre, has devised a way to trace a printed object to a specific filament product, down to the brand and type.
The process of 3D printing changes the filament’s physical properties, and this change can be measured. In this research, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) is used, a thermoanalytical technique that lets the sample go through a range of temperatures, and the instrument measures how heat flows through the sample. It measures how much energy or power is used to keep the sample at a certain temperature or to change its temperature, giving us a graph of its thermal properties.
The sample’s thermal properties can then be cross-referenced with its unprinted filament, creating an association between them. As of now, the tested PLA products are the only successfully identified material, with PETG and ABS not providing enough information to link them to their filament product. Sauzier blames the amorphous nature of those filaments, giving very similar results with no clear identifiers linking them to their respective filament products. PLA has a semi-crystalline molecular structure, which provides clearer temperature transition points under the temperature tests as the crystalline structures break down and rearrange.
However, ABS and PETG did show some promise when tested using ATR-FTIR (Attenuated Total Reflectance-Fourier Transform Infrared), which uses infrared to identify chemical bonds and material composition. The team did find differences in additives using this method, but still did not give enough information to link them back to their respective filament products.
The research is still very early, with more rigorous testing to be done, as the team printed using only one machine, printed small sample tiles cut with scissors, and left them for a year in monitored office conditions before testing. Properties could further change as cooling rates vary greatly depending on what the printer is printing: Faster cooling and slower print speeds on overhangs, or slower cooling and faster print speeds on infill sections. Different printers may also affect the physical properties, adding one more factor in the chain.

So far, correctly identifying 26 out of 28 samples is a great start to cracking down on dangerous, untraceable illegal firearms. When the research matures and can reliably identify a broad range of materials, it could potentially trace 3D-printed firearms to the printer and filament, potentially creating a list of where they were purchased and who purchased them.

articles.title: EA Cancelled Mass Effect To Fund Star Wars: Battlefront 3
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
EA Cancelled Mass Effect To Fund Star Wars: Battlefront 3
Not long after the news broke that EA was giving Mass Effect and BioWare the axe, it was revealed that LucasFilm was looking for a development partner for its next Star Wars: Battlefront game, ostensibly Battlefront 3. In that rumor, it was claimed that LucasFilm was considering either Sony's Bungie or EA's DICE for the project. Now, it appears as though EA move to shut down BioWare and cancel Mass Effect was part of a bet on Star Wars: Battlefront 3, according to a new report from Bloomberg's Jason Schreier. 
The report claims that, following EA's acquisition by the PIF group, which has already resulted in multiple rounds of layoffs, the executives at the gaming giant evaluated potential upcoming game projects and decided that Star Wars was the safer bet, with both Mass Effect and Battlefront 3 expected to cost hundreds of millions of dollars to produce. Part of the motivation for picking Star Wars over Mass Effect also appears to have been EA's historic preference for and experience with shooters, like Battlefield 6.The report also cites poor commercial performance of BioWare's Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which is described as "a last chance" for the studio. Mass Effect: Andromeda also had a messy launch and poor sales figures, and, along with the monumental Anthem disaster, added fuel to EA's cost-cutting decisions.
Source:
				Bloomberg			
	
	
	
		
	
		
9 Comments on EA Cancelled Mass Effect To Fund Star Wars: Battlefront 3
As well, given the leaked details of "ME5" following BioWare's closure showed it was just entering the concept phase with just a showcase teaser for the upper heads or investors, it wouldn't be any loss to cancel the project outright.Glad to see that even EA saw there was no saving BioWare. They would be much better off making some money back just licensing out ME and DA to other studios and letting others do the work of making a game that would actually sell.
Heck, at this point, with nothing left to lose, they could even go for the low effort Collabs with gatcha games, Fortnite, or even with competing games just to include characters or costumes inspired by DA1-3 or ME1-3. Crimson Desert and Black Desert Online could easily fit the DA aesthetic, maybe work with Sandfall Interactive on a mini-expansion into the Painting of Dragon Age and rewarding DA-themed gear and costumes. Or heck, paid costumes/skins in their Battlefield and Battlefront games. It'd be certainly better than leaving both ME and DA for dead, and EA does need the money as well.
Now ME has a bit more presence as a brand and its merch was still selling well, so I could see that farmed out.
Also looking back, it's humorous how DA2 was made because the devs at the time claimed DA1 was too stressful to make again, hence narrowing the focus and "telling a more personal story", but after the players revolted, the devs figured out how to make Inquisition closer to DA1 and recovered enough player good will to start on a DA4, which ended how it ended. The series really did suffer a rollercoaster of development and player emotion, ending with a crash and potentially permanent end. DA1 really was a lightning in a bottle moment that BioWare never recaptured.
Sigh. I pity the devs that have to work on this shitstain. I mean, you have to somehow figure out something to get players connected ALL OVER AGAIN. Forget building on foundations. New community. New sale. New everything. Its like a new school class every year except the class is the entire world, and they DO know what you taught them last year.
Insanity to think this can keep working out well, but apparently, it somehow does.
It also doesn't dawn on any of these bean counters that WoW, a single game with a string of expansions, has been and remains one of the most player-connected service games in the (western) gaming world. 10-15 $ of sub money every month from a dozen or two million players. Just like that; keep the servers running and add a boss or two every time. Over several decades now. If any company has gained trust in that sense.... and a dedicated customer base. How hard is it to just sell an expansion to that existing experience. I don't get it. Build on what you had. Make it insanely awesome. But no... we get the tutorial every single fucking goddamn time, and some 'easter eggs' to remind you that devs know you already played sixteen earlier installments and its Yet Again The Same Shit But Different.
There could just be a Battlefront update that they market as much as a new game, and I reckon players would be a lot happier. Just spoonfeed like they were used to getting it... There are countless examples of games that do this perfectly fine for many years.
Unironically, Mass Effect 1-3, despite 'starting over' with your progression 3 times, did have an overarching story. Star Wars, the trilogy... need I say more. They already know this shit works and gets people locked in... but nope. Just keep sticking numbers behind every yearly reskin and keep wondering why player attachment remains low - its like they want to slowly erode the faith people have in live service games they actually make buck on. Ubisoft is another such champion at this, and boy, are they doing well lately!
Destiny 1 for example, needed Destiny 2 because D1's engine just didn't have the capability for expansion and growth, and D2's engine did. However, they also chose to reset everything because it was too much tech debt to port over existing equipment and weapons based on save files.
You're right that some games like CoD and Battlefield (and Battlefront) should just be a live-service game that keeps getting updated as old content is brought up to standard or replaced just like classical MMOs, or even online games like Destiny (which also sees a regular change to the meta and content), Fortnite, or Overwatch/Marvel Rivals. Charge a DLC cost of like 40 USD, and it'd still sell. Moreso if new stuff is locked to the DLC leaving players with only the older content (again, pulling from Destiny's expansions) that gradually thins out on players because more and more bought the new DLC and moved to the new game modes or newer maps/guns. Then add the Battle Pass, Seasonal Content for Halloween, St. Patrick's, Valentine's, Winter Holidays, etc, and limited time events to keep player paying.
As well, some games are now able to outright update the game engine by basically deleting and redownloading the game, so there's even less need for a sequel just for a minor or major engine update.
Destiny though I'm not sure applies; let's not turn around cause and effect. Destiny, from the get-go, was marketed as a lie. The persistence of player progress for example, was initially presented as persistent but come D2, that suddenly just got a hard reset. And its not like 'the engine' is the reason - if they had actually built the right engine from the start. This situation only underlines how that entire game's premise has been a big fat lie from the start: game wasn't even equipped to deliver what it implied to be.
We also see that on-the-fly engine revamps happen in live service games. Look at WoW. In the end, you just keep that sub, you buy an expansion below game price (softening the blow for consumer perception) and in everything the game tries to keep you tied to that same, continuous sub, and it implies continuous persistence and progress. The reality is that every new tier of content, you actually get that reset anyway, but its a soft reset, you keep your gold. Your levelling. Your old gear. It just feels so much better even though its effectively the same thing. But feelz matter in a live service that is built to play with your emotions and attachment :) The fragmentation of playerbase due to all these different games can be largely avoided... I think the companies would be making more money instead of less.

articles.title: Vous jonglez entre Claude Code, Codex et Copilot ? Vous allez apprécier ce petit logiciel gratuit
articles.text:
Les assistants de programmation IA ont chacun leurs plafonds et leurs compteurs. AI Limits les rassemble dans un widget pour Windows 11, histoire de savoir combien de marge il reste avant la prochaine réinitialisation.
Les outils de développement assisté par IA imposent des limites variables : sessions de cinq heures, plafonds hebdomadaires ou quotas propres à certaines fonctions. Pour connaître son solde, il faut consulter plusieurs interfaces. AI Limits propose de centraliser ces informations sur Windows 11.
- Pourcentages et échéances visibles
- Trois niveaux de détail
- Jetons réutilisés en lecture seull
Claude Code, Codex, Copilot et Antigravity dans un seul widget
AI Limits réunit les quotas de Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot et Google Antigravity. Il présente des jauges de consommation et les délais avant leur remise à zéro. Pour Claude Code, il suit notamment les fenêtres de cinq heures, les plafonds hebdomadaires et certains quotas par modèle. Copilot dispose de compteurs de requêtes et de complétions, tandis qu'Antigravity affiche des limites partagées entre modèles.
L'interface prend la forme d'un panneau flottant et translucide. Trois niveaux de détail, des jauges horizontales ou verticales et plusieurs palettes permettent de le personnaliser. On peut aussi le masquer : un indicateur prend alors le relais dans la zone de notification ou sur la barre des tâches. Une estimation du temps restant avant l'épuisement d'un quota est proposée en option.
L'application exploite les identifiants déjà enregistrés sur le PC par les outils officiels en ligne de commande. Si Claude Code, Codex CLI ou GitHub CLI sont connectés, nul besoin, en principe, de ressaisir ses accès. Les chiffres proviennent des fournisseurs concernés, et non d'un comptage local des requêtes.
Un utilitaire gratuit, avec quelques limites à connaître
AI Limits est gratuit et open source, sous licence GPLv3 ou ultérieure. Disponible notamment sur le Microsoft Store et en version portable, cet utilitaire en Rust sert de tableau de bord commun, comme les jauges d'un véhicule regroupées devant le conducteur plutôt que sur quatre écrans.
Cette simplicité suppose de passer par les outils pris en charge. AI Limits ne mesure pas toutes les conversations menées dans ChatGPT ou Claude depuis un navigateur : il suit les comptes connectés aux outils de programmation. Une clé API Claude ajoutée manuellement renseigne, quant à elle, les plafonds de l'API, pas les quotas d'un abonnement Pro ou Max.
Côté confidentialité, le programme lit les jetons d'authentification existants sans les modifier. Son développeur assure ne collecter aucune télémétrie. Le code public peut être examiné, mais l'accès à ces jetons reste à prendre en compte avant installation.
Les chiffres ne sont toutefois pas toujours actualisés. Quand un jeton expire ou qu'un fournisseur limite les consultations, AI Limits conserve le dernier relevé et le grise pour signaler son ancienneté. Mieux vaut cela qu'un faux compteur en temps réel.

- Trois niveaux de détail

articles.title: The hidden threat in Anthropic’s prospectus: diseconomies of scale - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
The hidden threat in Anthropic’s prospectus: diseconomies of scale
As potentially the largest IPO in history, Anthropic PBC is breaking new ground. Its prospectus lists 88 risk factors covering 93 pages alone. From artificial intelligence posing an existential threat to humanity to the possibility AI will blackmail people, the company lists a litany of risks that should make any potential Anthropic investor wary.
One potentially company-sinking risk factor, however, does not explicitly appear in the prospectus: diseconomies of scale.
Diseconomies of scale occur when a company’s average cost of producing each unit of output increases as the company grows.
You would think that given the time and effort that Anthropic devoted to ensuring its list of risk factors was complete that they would have included this one. There is a reason, however, that they missed it, despite the fact that diseconomies of scale is the elephant in the room.
We’ve been down this road before with cloud computing. The fundamental economic driver of the hyperscaler clouds was economies of scale: the larger they became, the lower their cost of each unit of output, leading to massive growth and profitability over time.
Since the AI boom requires massive data center buildouts just as cloud computing does, it might be reasonable to assume that AI will experience the same economic benefits of massive growth that cloud computing enjoyed.
This assumption, however, is likely to be false. To understand why, we must take a look at how the software and cloud businesses scale – and why AI is so different.
The economics of scaling software
Throughout the history of enterprise computing, software has benefited from its negligible marginal cost.
With physical goods, from automobiles to chicken nuggets, every unit has a raw materials and production cost. The more widgets you make, the more those costs add up.
Software is fundamentally different. Once a vendor has spent the money to build an application, it can sell that application to as many customers as it can find, where the cost of delivering additional copies of that application is negligible compared to the original cost of developing it.
This negligible marginal cost enables software vendors to become immensely profitable as their business scales.
The economics of scaling the cloud
Computer hardware, in contrast, is nothing more than more widgets – the more you deploy, the greater your materials and production costs.
Cloud computing combines both software and hardware in its offerings. The software may have negligible marginal cost, but each cloud provider must shell out money for each physical server.
To address this cost challenge, cloud providers take advantage of economies of scale.
The hyperscalers built their clouds by deploying massive numbers of commodity servers. As each firm expanded its business, the cost of each unit of output – say, the cost of providing a server instance or a unit of cloud storage – decreased.
As a result, the cost of servers went down as they scaled, and the cloud computing firms became increasingly profitable as they grew, despite the fact that their business models depended on hardware as well as software.
How the economics of AI differs from both software and the cloud
Back to Anthropic and the rest of the frontier large language model providers: Ostensibly, AI is just a type of software, and Anthropic is running its software in hyperscaled data centers that are essentially clouds. This underlying assumption is implicit in the company’s prospectus.
This assumption, however, is flawed. Frontier model vendors require graphics processing units and other premium, expensive hardware from day one – and their specialized processor requirements continue to accelerate as they rapidly innovate their software.
This advancing specialized processor requirement didn’t impact the rise of the cloud. True, each cloud provider eventually added various specialized hardware instance types as they grew, but those instances didn’t change the fundamental economics of the cloud business.
Anthropic, in contrast, doesn’t have the luxury of deploying commodity hardware to achieve economies of scale. Instead, it must build out expensive servers that only get more expensive as LLMs’ processor requirements continue to advance.
Adding humans to the economic argument
There are also diseconomies of scaling the human side of the AI boom that contrast with the growth of the cloud.
The hyperscalers certainly require an experienced workforce with deep expertise to deploy their clouds and keep them running. But as they grew, they were able to leverage such personnel more efficiently. An admin who managed a thousand physical servers could easily manage 10,000 or a million as the underlying cloud platforms matured.
Unlike the cloud providers, however, Anthropic and the other frontier model vendors must continually scale up the expertise of their teams. New LLMs aren’t simply scaled-out versions of older ones. Each one requires new expertise from expert humans.
Anthropic is battling its competitors to innovate quickly and roll out increasingly powerful models on unprecedented timeframes. As a result, frontier LLM vendor teams experience diseconomies of scale that the hyperscalers never had to face.
Software and hardware and people, oh my!
Anthropic and the rest of the frontier LLM vendors suffer from a fundamentally novel economic reality, because they must continue to increase their hardware capabilities while upskilling their workforce so they can competitively innovate their software.
They can’t simply run increasingly powerful models on commodity hardware – or even the same hardware they ran the previous generation model on. They must increase their investments in hardware at a pace that keeps up with the pace of software innovation.
The end result is a diseconomy of scale the technology industry has never seen before. We are so used to the negligible marginal cost of software and the massive economies of scale of the cloud, that we are simply unprepared for the diseconomies of scale that frontier LLM vendors like Anthropic must negotiate.
The Intellyx take
Even though the frontier model marketplace is still quite new, we’re already seeing the impact of its inherent diseconomies of scale as token costs become an increasingly significant expense for consumers of AI.
As LLMs become more powerful and the hardware they require becomes an increasingly expensive bottleneck, it’s just a matter of time until token costs become prohibitively high for a range of AI-based applications.
Anthropic and the other LLM model vendors can try to respond by increasing the efficiency of their more powerful LLMs or rolling out less powerful, and thus less expensive models – assuming their customers buy into these moves.
We may also eventually reach a plateau where the models are sufficiently powerful and the hardware is sufficiently performant, thus enabling more familiar economies of scale to take over. However, no such plateau is in sight.
The question potential Anthropic investors must ask, therefore, is whether the company’s leadership position in the LLM market is a strength or a weakness? Just how far can it innovate and grow before its offerings are too expensive? And what does it do then?
Jason Bloomberg is founder and managing director of Intellyx, which advises business leaders and technology vendors on their digital transformation strategies. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE. articles.title: Tech sleuth claims to have found the oldest GUI application that still works with Windows 11 — 34-year-old CDPLAYER.EXE from Windows NT in November 1992 wins the prize
articles.text:
Tech sleuth claims to have found the oldest GUI application that still works with Windows 11 — 34-year-old CDPLAYER.EXE from Windows NT in November 1992 wins the prize
However, if you cheat and enable 16-bit apps in Win11, you can still enjoy REVERSI.EXE, as distributed with Windows 1.01 in 1985.
A technology enthusiast claims that the oldest GUI application that still runs on Windows 11 is CDPLAYER.EXE from November 1992. The app had to run on Microsoft’s newest consumer OS without modifications or emulation involved to be chosen as the ‘winner’ of their experiment. Blogger Enlyth expected something from the early NT era, as Windows 11 doesn’t support 16-bit apps, despite its strong backward compatibility. Finding an app that is almost 34 years old that still works with a simple double-click is a remarkable result.
At the beginning of their journey to find the oldest Windows UI app that just works on Microsoft’s newest OS, Enlyth confirmed FREECELL.EXE from February 1993 would still run without issues. This game was distributed alongside the Win32s environment, designed to allow some 32-bit applications to run on the 16-bit operating systems like Windows 3.1 and 3.11. Win32s was made available in beta in October 1992, but went mainstream in July 1993.
A tip Enlyth received via a tech forum suggested that FREECELL.EXE was a candidate for the oldest GUI app remaining compatible with Windows 11. However, the blogger wasn’t satisfied with this easy win and dug through “some early NT 3.1 pre-release versions that seemed promising.” Build 347 caught the detective’s eye, specifically CDPLAYER.EXE, linked on Nov 16, 1992. That indeed seems to be the earliest GUI app that works without modification or emulation on Windows 11. But this knowledge almost defied Enlyth’s eye as their system is, like many modern systems, optical-drive-less. Luckily, adding a small DLL (cdemu.dll) allowed Enlyth to emulate a CD drive and demonstrate that the 1992-era application still functions as intended.
I wanted to verify that CDPLAYER.EXE was still usable on the latest Windows 11 release. Unfortunately, the multi-part.ARJ archive of Windows NT 3.1 that I found on Archive.org threw up errors when I tried to pick through its contents. I have a USB-attached optical drive that plays CD audio in Windows 11, so I thought I could get CDPLAYER.EXE to run without any extra DLL.
Lastly, Enlyth wanted to push the envelope a little and see what even more ancient Windows apps might work if they got some help from the Winevdm project on 64-bit Windows. “Using otvdm does feel like cheating,” admitted the digital sleuth, and we’d agree. However, being able to run 16-bit apps in Windows 11 ratcheted back the wheels of time. The result was that Enlyth managed to enjoy “a fully playable version of REVERSI.EXE dated 15-Nov-1985.” That’s a GUI-driven game distributed as part of Windows 1.01 and is roughly 41 years old.

articles.title: I’m a certified barista, and these are the essential off-grid espresso makers I recommend for your emergency prepping kit if the power fails
articles.text:
Civilization may crumble, but bad coffee is optional — I test coffee makers for a living, and these off-grid espresso machines are perfect for preppers
So you've got your water, cash, canned food, and a wind-up radio, but something is missing from your prepping supplies. If the power goes out and your water supply is cut, how will you make your morning coffee? Put down that jar of instant granules — basic services might have failed, but your tastebuds haven't.
Drip coffee is an easy way to perk yourself up and boost your morale in a crisis (just pick up a ChemEx brewer or a simple dripper with some filter papers), but if you're aiming to conserve water then a shot of espresso is a better way to get your caffeine fix, so here I've focused on brewers for preparing shorter drinks.
Consider how you're going to store your emergency coffee supply, too. Whole beans will hold their flavor better than ground, and I recommend keeping them in an opaque, airtight container in a cool place (light, heat, air, and moisture are the enemies of aroma compounds). You'll need a grinder, too — look for one with burrs rather than blades so your coffee isn't chopped up in rough pieces.
If all that sounds like too much hassle in a crisis, opt for foil-sealed coffee pods instead. Both the Nanopresso and Dreame Ecceluxe Go below have adapters for brewing with single-serve capsules.
The Ecceluxe Go heats its own water, but if you pick a more basic brewer then you'll need a different way to get it up to temperature. As the former editor of an outdoor gear website, I recommend a simple gas camping stove like the MSR Pocket Rocket 2, which will get your water up to around 203F / 95C in approximately 3.5 minutes. Now, onto the brewers...
Wacaco NanoPresso
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
No power? No problem. The Wacaco Nanopresso generates up to 18 bars of pressure using nothing but elbow grease. It's small enough to tuck inside a pocket, and is hand-powered, so all you need is a source of hot water to create properly extracted espresso with thick crema (even if you have to use a flashlight to see what you're doing).
The standard Nanopresso uses ground coffee, which you can tamp down using the scoop (the brewer has a valve to release pressure if you accidentally tamp it too hard), but if you'd rather use pods then the NS adaptor allows you to use Nespresso Original style capsules instead.

It feels robust and solid in the hand, and is packed with thoughtful little features like an insulated water tank and cup to protect your hands from heat, and an easy-clean portafilter that needs minimal maintenance.

The Dreame Ecceluxe Go is a battery-powered brewer with a miniature boiler built-in. Just pour room-temperature water into the reservoir on top (measuring lines engraved inside will prevent you overfilling it and wasting precious resources), then pick the right adapter — Nespresso Original, Nestlé Dolce Gusto, ESE (Easy Serve Espresso), or fresh grounds — and you're ready to brew.
Preparing an espresso with room temperature water takes about six minutes from start to finish, and you can prepare two or three drinks before the Ecceluxe Go needs recharging (from a portable battery or solar generator during a power outage). The brew unit itself is smaller than a thermos flask, and comes in a compact carry case that you can tuck away with the rest of your emergency supplies.
The Dreame Ecceluxe Go is due to go on sale in Spain and Portugal very soon, with the US following shortly after. There's no plan for a UK launch yet, but it charges via USB-C, so there's no reason British preppers can't import one.
AeroPress and Manual Coffee Grinder

If you're planning to keep whole coffee beans in your emergency supplies, you need the AeroPress Manual Coffee Grinder. I've tested a lot of manual grinders in my time, and this is easily the best. It has proper burrs rather than cheap blades so coffee is ground rather than shredded, and they're adjustable so you can optimize the grind size to suit your brewing method.
The default setting is optimized for the AeroPress brewer, which you can use to make a short, strong shot of coffee to keep you awake, or a longer, smoother drink if you have water to spare. I have a plastic AeroPress in my locker at work (you never know what might happen), but if you want something extra tough then take a look at the rugged AeroPress Steel. If you're part of a whole family of coffee-lovers there's also the king-sized AeroPress XL, and if you need something you can also use on the road, the bijou AeroPress Go packs down into a compact travel cup.

articles.title: La future Peugeot 208 se précise : voici ce que l'on sait déjà
articles.text:
Un nouveau design
Peugeot devrait profiter du lancement de la troisième génération de la 208 pour inaugurer un nouveau style, qui a déjà été préfiguré avec le concept Polygon, mais aussi plus récemment au Mondial de l’Auto avec les concepts E-T16 et RCZ.
La prochaine Peugeot 208 devrait miser sur l’horizontalité, avec une signature lumineuse avant et arrière sous la forme de trois bandes horizontales traversant la voiture. Ces bandes remplaceront les griffes du lion de l’actuelle Peugeot 208, qui ont elles-mêmes remplacé les dents de lion de la phase 1 de la deuxième génération de 208.
Si les dimensions ne devraient pas changer, avec une voiture d’environ 4 mètres de long, la prochaine Peugeot 208 paraîtra plus large en raison de cette nouvelle signature lumineuse. Ainsi, la 208 gagnera en prestance, et il en faut. En effet, avec la concurrence qui s’est affûtée parmi les citadines, notamment avec la Cupra Raval, agressive à souhait, la Volkswagen ID. Polo, chic et moderne, et la Renault 5 E-Tech, qui mise sur la nostalgie, la Peugeot 208 va devoir sortir le grand jeu pour séduire.
Et a bord Peugeot devrait lancer une nouveauté attendue, son i-cockpit dernière génération intégrant un volant rectangulaire “Hypersquare” avec une direction Steer-by-Wire, sans lien mécanique. Les commandes au volant seront bien intégrée sur ce volant à la forme singulière, directement dans les 4 trous ronds permettant la prise en main.
Une nouvelle plateforme pour la 208
La prochaine génération de Peugeot 208 devrait utiliser la nouvelle plateforme STLA Small, uniquement dans des déclinaisons électriques. La stratégie est la même que celle de Volkswagen, qui a lancé les Cupra Raval et Volkswagen ID. Polo uniquement en électrique, tout en gardant les Seat Ibiza et Volkswagen Polo thermiques. Et oui, Peugeot devrait continuer la commercialisation de l’actuelle 208 avec des motorisations thermiques et micro-hybrides pour proposer un accès abordable à la gamme.
Cette deuxième génération de Peugeot 208 pourrait avoir droit à un troisième restylage, qui sera le bienvenu. Si elle n’accuse pas tant les années sur le plan stylistique, la 208 marque le pas à bord, avec une présentation assez datée qui se remarque particulièrement sur la e-208 GTI, vendue 42 900 euros.
Pour revenir à la Peugeot 208 III, le constructeur au lion pourrait en dire plus dès l’année prochaine, avec une présentation au second semestre 2027 pour un lancement en 2028.

articles.title: La "snackficación" de la dieta española: el sector de los aperitivos y frutos secos crece casi un 5% hasta los 3.253 millones de euros
articles.text:
En España no comemos igual ahora que en la época de nuestros padres o abuelos. Ni siquiera lo hacemos igual que hace una década. Lo saben bien Mercadona y el resto de cadenas que han visto un filón en el negocio de los mercaurantes, espacios a medio camino entre el súper y el restaurante de toda la vida en los que devorar platos recién cocinados. Prima la rapidez, la comodidad, el ahorro de tiempo. También la búsqueda de alternativas fáciles, económicas y saludables a cocinar en casa. No es una ecuación fácil, pero hay una industria que está sabiendo aprovecharla: la del snack.
De hecho, cada vez hay más pistas (y voces) que nos hablan de una progresiva “snackficación” de nuestra dieta.
La cifra: 4,6%. 2025 no fue un mal ejercicio para la industria de los aperitivos y frutos secos. Así lo refleja el último balance anual de la Asociación de Snacks, que deja dos cifras sobre la mesa. En 2025 las ventas del sector alcanzaron en nuestro país los 3.254 millones de euros, un 4,6% más que en 2024. Aunque parte de ese porcentaje se explica por la subida de precios, la industria también despachó más snacks. Su volumen de comercialización subió un 1,5%, lo que sitúa sus ventas en 392.866 toneladas.
El reinado del fruto seco. Por supuesto, no todos los snacks se venden igual de bien. Ni su comercialización avanza a la misma velocidad. Los más exitosos son los frutos secos, que en 2025 acapararon el 37,7% de las ventas (toneladas). El resto de la ‘tarta’ sectorial se la reparten las patatas fritas, que acaparan el 32,39%, y ‘otros snacks’ (27,39%).
Si hablamos de la evolución, en 2025 el negocio de los frutos secos creció un 8,12% en términos de valor (euros) y 0,88% en volumen (toneladas). Las patatas fritas movieron un 2,84% menos de facturación, pero la industria lo compensó gracias a la demanda del resto de aperitivos, que creció un 4,54% en valor y cerca de un 9% en toneladas comercializadas.
¿Por qué es importante? Los datos de la Asociación de Snacks son interesantes porque no solo nos hablan de la marcha del sector. También revelan cómo está cambiando nuestra forma de comer. De hecho, el informe de la patronal está en sintonía con otros estudios sobre la alimentación en España, como el anuario de 2025 del Ministerio de Agricultura. Sus técnicos calculan que el consumo de aperitivos fuera del hogar ha aumentado un 3,6%. Pedimos y comemos snacks con más frecuencia fuera de casa, aunque cuando nos los sirven ingerimos cantidades menores. Más picoteo, menos empacho.
El informe del ministerio muestra sin embargo una ‘foto’ más compleja que el de la patronal. Los españoles comemos menos chocolatinas, bombones y patatas fritas fuera de casa, pero cada vez estamos más interesados en los frutos secos. Su volumen de compras se ha disparado un 12% en los últimos años. Eso explica que el balance general del sector sea difuso, con un retroceso general que coincide con una pérdida de peso de fritos y dulces y una subida de los frutos.
Importa qué comes… y cómo comes. Esos datos no son casuales. Los españoles (igual que ocurre en otros países) estamos cambiando nuestra forma de alimentarnos. Y eso no pasa solo por un cambio del menú, en el que han perdido peso los pescados, el pan fresco o el alcohol. También varía nuestro patrón de comidas, la frecuencia y el planteamiento de las ingestas. El esquema tradicional ‘desayuno-almuerzo-cena’ se flexibiliza, dejando hueco para una dieta más distribuida a lo largo del día con pequeñas cantidades de alimento.
No es solo teoría. En Estados Unidos han detectado una clara tendencia hacia el reemplazo de las comidas centrales del día por pequeñas ingestas de snacks. En 2020 admitía ese cambio el 38% de los encuestados. En 2024 eran ya el 56% y en 2025 el 62%. Muchos lo hacen solo de forma ocasional, pero los porcentajes muestran que algo está cambiando.
¿Y en España? Hay pistas que apuntan en una dirección similar: en 2004 el INE calculó que el 58% de la población solía realizar tres comidas al día. En 2022 Mapfre volvió a abordar el tema y descubrió que, al menos durante los días laborales, el porcentaje de quienes hacían tres comidas no llegaba al 39%.
El 30% realizaba cuatro y el 23% se alimentaba cinco veces a lo largo de la jornada. Son diferentes estudios realizados por diferentes organismos (INE y Mapfre), con lo que deben compararse con cierta cautela, pero aun así sugieren un cambio de hábitos.
Una palabra: “snackficación”. A la vista de esos cambios hay quien ya habla de una “snackficación” de la alimentación, un cambio paulatino que rompe con el patrón tradicional de tres bloques de ingesta al día (desayuno, almuerzo, cena) y lo sustituye por picoteos espaciados a lo largo de la jornada. ¿La razón? No solo cambia nuestra alimentación, también lo hace cómo la planificamos y nuestras prioridades, entre las que gana fuerza la gestión eficaz del tiempo.
Queremos comida saludable, pero cada vez estamos menos dispuestos a encerrarnos en la cocina para prepararla y tenemos menos hábito de ir al mercado para comprar productos frescos. No solo eso. También reducimos el tiempo que dedicamos a la comida en sí. De ahí el éxito de los mercaurantes (que permiten una ingesta rápida), el take away o que cada vez más hosteleros estén cambiando el menú tradicional de tres platos por opciones más comprimidas.
El atractivo del picoteo. La industria de los snacks es consciente de ese escenario. De ahí que cada vez sea más frecuente encontrarse productos que el sector presenta como alternativas de alimentación rápidas y saludables. Ya no apela únicamente al estómago. Lo hace también al cerebro.
Incluso a la búsqueda de pequeñas recompensas y “momentos de felicidad”, un nicho de negocio sobre el que advertía hace poco Circana. En el mismo estudio europeo, por cierto, la consultora desliza otro dato revelador: el 13% de los encuestados reconoce que ya consume snacks en vez de la comida principal y el 28% compagina ambos. Gran parte lo hace además convencido de que ese picoteo es una forma de cuidarse.

Black Friday 2026 – Le défroisseur vapeur SteamOne SteamCube "5 étoiles" à 399,00 € (-20%)
Le défroisseur vapeur SteamOne SteamCube passe sous les 400 € chez Fnac.com, Cdiscount Marketplace et Darty.com soit une baisse d'environ 20% sur le prix habituellement constaté. C'est actuellement le meilleur produit de notre comparatif.
Expert français du steamer, SteamOne propose SteamCube, un appareil hybride aux compétences accrues, pouvant s’apparenter à une centrale vapeur. Sa plaque est chauffante et peut défroisser à l’horizontale comme à la verticale, avec un débit vapeur annoncé de 125 g/min.

articles.title: SpaceX quer comprar casas de vizinhos incomodados com seus data centers • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
SpaceX quer comprar casas de vizinhos incomodados com seus data centers
SpaceXSI estaria comprando casas próximas a uma usina que gera energia para seus data centers para tentar evitar queixas por ruído.
Não é incomum que pessoas que vivem próximas a data centers reclamem sobre esses lugares causarem transtornos. Para lidar com isso, a SpaceX parece ter encontrado uma solução, digamos, radical: estaria comprando casas localizadas nas proximidades de uma usina de energia que alimenta justamente data centers.
O caso em questão envolve, na verdade, a SpaceXSI, empresa resultante da incorporação de xAI pela SpaceX. A xAI foi fundada por Elon Musk em 2023 para desenvolver tecnologias e serviços de inteligência artificial, com destaque para o Grok, vale relembrar.
Pois bem, não é novidade que aplicações de IA demandam data centers dedicados. Por conta disso, a SpaceXSI construiu em 2024, ainda sob o nome xAI, instalações do tipo na região de Memphis, nos Estados Unidos.
Data centers demandam muita energia. Para atender a essa necessidade, a SpaceXSI montou uma estrutura de geração de energia com 69 turbinas temporárias movidas a gás na cidade de Southaven. O problema é que essas turbinas produzem muito barulho, incomodando enormemente os moradores da região (sem contar outros transtornos gerados, como a poluição do ar).
De acordo com o jornal The Guardian, a SpaceXSI passou a enviar corretores de imóveis a moradores das redondezas da usina de energia para oferecer uma proposta de compra de suas residências.
Um corretor teria dito a um dos moradores que o plano da companhia de Elon Musk consiste em comprar 418 casas da região, sendo que 18 já teriam sido negociadas. Outras cinco já teriam sido compradas pela MZX, subsidiária da SpaceX que opera a estrutura de energia.
Ainda de acordo com o jornal, as residências adquiridas serão usadas para abrigar funcionários da companhia. Ao que tudo indica, as propostas de aquisição têm valores próximos a US$ 180.000, que é a estimativa média de preço das casas da região.
Mas há uma condição: o morador que quiser vender a sua casa deve concordar em não processar a SpaceXSI por conta dos incômodos causados pela usina elétrica.
Na verdade, uma ação judicial coletiva contra a SpaceXSI está em curso desde junho desde ano. Nela, moradores da região reclamam que a usina gera um ruído constante e que, muitas vezes, se assemelha ao barulho de um avião. Nesse sentido, a compra das casas seria uma estratégia para não tornar o embate judicial um problema maior.
No mês seguinte, a empresa fechou um acordo com órgãos reguladores estaduais para transformar a usina em uma instalação permanente de geração de energia a gás. Essa mudança traria uma estrutura mais moderna que, como tal, diminuiria o ruído que hoje é gerado pelas turbinas temporárias.
A SpaceXSI também já havia se manifestado sobre a implementação de medidas de contenção dos transtornos, como construção de barreiras acústicas e ajustes de potência na geração de energia.
Mas a suposta estratégia de comprar casas na região levanta dúvidas sobre se, de fato, a companhia de Elon Musk pretende ser uma “boa vizinha”, como deu a entender.

articles.title: Mid-market ERP: How Intuit uses AI to avoid failed migrations - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Intuit targets the mid-market ERP gap with AI
Growing companies that outgrow entry-level accounting software face a hard choice: Stay put or gamble on a mid-market ERP that promises automation but often brings cost and disruption. Artificial intelligence is now giving financial software providers a way to close that gap without forcing businesses through a risky migration.
Intuit Inc. is pushing finance toward automation, and its mid-market strategy targets companies caught between small-business tools and legacy systems. Those businesses face the problems of success, such as more customers, more entities and more currencies, and need technology to help them scale, according to Ashley Still (pictured), executive vice president and general manager of mid-market at Intuit.
“Actually, 50% of mid-market ERP implementations fail,” Still said. “So, 50% of businesses that leave their existing financial platform to go to what they think will be a better platform for them actually fail in that implementation. It typically costs $60,000 and six months.”
Still spoke with Alison Kosik and Christophe Bertrand at Intuit Connect, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed why mid-market ERP migrations fail, how Intuit Enterprise Suite fills the gap and how AI agents are taking on routine finance work. (* Disclosure below.)
Closing the mid-market ERP gap with AI
Intuit’s answer is Intuit Enterprise Suite, which lets growing companies scale on the platform where their data already lives instead of starting over. Intuit has added industry-specific editions for construction, manufacturing and nonprofits. Still described the product as the CFO’s command center.
“First, they actually can see a complete view of the business for the first time ever, all of their entities in one place, consolidated financials,” she said. “That really is game-changing because it gives them the ability to make real-time decisions.”
Accounting firms are central to the plan, since 70% of mid-market businesses work with an accountant or advisor, according to Still. Intuit is automating routine work such as categorizations and reconciliations, while its new Agent Studio lets a business or firm build a customizable agent just by describing what it needs. Accounting firms Citrin Cooperman and Sorren have already put agents into production through the tool, she noted.
“The point is the expectation is that more and more of the tedious work is done for a finance team or done for a firm rather than them having to do everything themselves,” Still said.

articles.title: US police forces could soon get a major tech upgrade thanks to DT Research's new rugged laptops, which pack in Nvidia graphics and AI processing
articles.text:
US police forces could soon get a major tech upgrade thanks to DT Research's new rugged laptops, which pack in Nvidia graphics and AI processing
DT Research's LT365PA brings Nvidia RTX graphics to police crime scenes
- DT Research unveils the LT365PA, a 15.6-inch rugged laptop offering Nvidia RTX A2000 or RTX 5000 Ada graphics
- It targets crime scene, crash reconstruction, and command post work, and reaches resellers worldwide in Q1 2027 but has no published price yet
- Much of the design carries over from 2023's LT355, and PNY lists an end-of-life window for RTX A2000 modules in that same quarter
Police crash investigators could soon be processing 3D scans and drone footage at the roadside instead of back at the station, if DT Research gets its way.
The California company has unveiled the LT365PA, a 15.6-inch rugged laptop with optional discrete Nvidia graphics, aimed at crime scene investigators, crash reconstruction teams, and military command posts.
The pitch for potential customers is simple enough: the ability to crunch video, drone imagery, 3D scans, and sensor feeds where the data is collected, rather than waiting on a network connection or a distant data center.
A workstation GPU in a rugged shell
The official DT Research's product page says the LT365PA runs on an Intel Core Ultra 5 225H or Core Ultra 7 255H with 16GB to 32GB of LPDDR5 memory, up to 2TB of storage, and Windows 11 IoT Enterprise.
The 15.6-inch touchscreen is rated at 1,200 nits, with a 4K panel and two MIL-STD-3009 Class B night-vision displays (one for naked-eye use, one for night-vision goggles) available as options. The chassis is IP65 rated and MIL-STD-810H certified, and a CAC reader, RFID and NFC readers, GPS, 4G LTE, and a NIST-compliant BIOS round out the extras public-sector buyers often tend to prefer.
DT Research offers an Nvidia RTX A2000 or what it calls an "RTX 5000A," which appears to be the Ada Lovelace-based RTX 5000 Ada Generation. The gap between the two is large: PNY's embedded MXM line card lists the A2000 module with 2,560 CUDA cores and 8GB of memory, while the RTX 5000 Ada has 9,728 CUDA cores and 16GB at a 115W power rating, giving it more than four times the peak FP32 throughput.
That GPU does most of the AI processing in DT Research's pitch; the NPU inside Intel's Arrow Lake-H chips is rated at just 13 TOPS, as we noted when Intel announced the family, so the heavy video analytics and 3D work DT Research describes will fall to the Nvidia silicon.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Same premise, a different model number and upgrades under the hood
Agencies with long memories may recognize the LT365PA. DT Research's LT355, launched in 2023, was also a 15.6-inch rugged laptop with a 1,200-nit screen and embedded Nvidia RTX A1000 or A2000 graphics, and it too was pitched to law enforcement and the military. At the time, Tsai said DT Research had listened to customers and "developed the next version of our rugged laptop to include an NVIDIA graphics card."
Compare the two spec sheets side by side, and a lot carries over: display brightness, the night-vision options, the operating temperature range, the enclosure materials, and the ratings of the hot-swappable battery packs are identical, and the GPU version still ships with a 230W power adapter.
What has changed is the newer Intel platform, the RTX 5000 Ada option, a 1.1lb (0.5kg) weight saving, and 4K and IR camera options. There is a step back, too, at least on paper: the LT355's two memory slots supported up to 64GB, while the LT365PA tops out at 32GB of LPDDR5.
"Today's field teams need the same high-performance AI computing capabilities at the edge," DT Research president Daw Tsai said in the company's announcement, which says the LT365PA will reach authorized partners and resellers worldwide in the first quarter of 2027. Pricing has not been disclosed.
A crash investigation pitch is arguably the most persuasive part of DT Research's launch. According to the Federal Highway Administration, "every minute of incident delay multiplies traffic queues by a factor of four," and the likelihood of a secondary crash climbs 2.8% for each minute the original incident remains a hazard. Anything that lets investigators confirm their scans and photos are complete before a road reopens has real value.
Despite leaning on such a specific example, the laptop itself doesn't capture anything. Laser scanners and drones do that, and DT Research names no software partners or processing-time figures to show how much faster the LT365PA makes the job.
There are practical trade-offs as well. At 8.6lb (3.9kg), the LT365PA is heavier than our top-rated rugged laptop, the Panasonic Toughbook 40, at 7.4lb, and its IP65 rating is a notch below the IP66 rating of the Toughbook 40 and Getac's B360X lineup. DT Research cites MIL-STD-810H for shock and vibration but publishes no drop height or a fuller list of test methods, whereas Durabook itemizes a long list of 810H tests behind the Z14I-DX3, from altitude to explosive atmosphere.
DT Research also publishes no battery life figure. The two standard packs work out to roughly 123Wh combined, and the GPU model ships with a 230W adapter, nearly double the 120W unit supplied with the standard version, which suggests those hot-swappable batteries will earn their keep under sustained GPU load.
Whether US police forces actually get this upgrade is a separate question. As MIT Technology Review's James O'Donnell has written, "police departments in the US have extraordinary independence," with more than 18,000 of them each deciding what technology to buy, so there is no single customer to win here.
The AI angle deserves a bit of pushback: DT Research pitches on-device video analytics without saying which applications it has validated or tested against, and that is where police technology matters most. The same MIT Technology Review reporting covered an AI tool that tracks people by clothing and body attributes in a way that sidesteps local facial recognition bans. The LT365PA is only hardware, but what agencies run on it will determine how welcome it is.
For crash and forensic teams still working on 2023-era gear, an LT365PA with the RTX 5000 Ada would be a genuine step up. The RTX A2000 version is a far more modest refresh, however, and with shipments not starting until 2027 and procurement cycles to follow, most investigators will not be unpacking one for a while yet.
