articles.title: New UEFI Tool Lifts NVIDIA's Tensor Cap on RTX 20 to 40 Series Cards in Windows
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
New UEFI Tool Lifts NVIDIA's Tensor Cap on RTX 20 to 40 Series Cards in Windows
Last week, modders found a way to double the tensor throughput of GeForce RTX 20, RTX 30, and RTX 40 cards, though Zagitta's original tool only ran on Linux. Now, Chinese modder physicsdolphin has released nv-uefi-unlocker, a UEFI tool that lifts the same limit on Windows. NVIDIA runs FP16, BF16, and TF32 tensor math with FP32 accumulation at half rate on GeForce cards, while the same silicon in professional cards runs at full speed. The tool removes that cap before the driver even loads, without any VBIOS flashing. An earlier Windows port from impacifist targeted a single RTX 3090 system, while this one covers all three generations.
The gains look substantial. One user's RTX 4070 Ti Super went from 57.00 to 150.93 TFLOPS in FP16 (2.65x), though board power also climbed from 227 W to nearly 292 W. An RTX 2070 reportedly jumped from 36 to around 60-63 TFLOPS. Not every card has been tested; RTX 20 owners have to enable GSP firmware mode first, and RTX 50 isn't supported at all. The unlock resets on every power-off, so it runs from a USB stick on each cold boot, with Secure Boot disabled or a self-signed certificate enrolled. That could be a problem for games whose anti-cheat requires Secure Boot.Gamers shouldn't expect anything here, since games and regular FP32 CUDA work see no change. This is mostly for local AI work like image generation and fine-tuning. The developer also warns that pairing it with a power limit unlock can push power and heat well past stock limits, so readers are advised to keep an eye on temperatures.
Sources:
				nv-uefi-unlocker (GitHub), 				Reddit, 				via Notebookcheck

articles.title: Nvidia store quietly pulls the RTX 5080 following RTX 5090 removal — street prices climb to 2.2X MSRP
articles.text:
Nvidia store quietly pulls the RTX 5080 following RTX 5090 removal — street prices climb to 2.2X MSRP
First, it was the GeForce RTX 5090, and now the GeForce RTX 5080 – two of the best graphics cards have gone dark. After the Blackwell flagship left Nvidia's marketplace, the GeForce RTX 5080 followed suit. Prices for the sub-flagship have exploded to more than 2.2X its original $999 MSRP, and the Blackwell-powered graphics card is slowly going out of stock at various U.S. retailers.
As with the recent disappearance of the GeForce RTX 5090 on Nvidia’s marketplace, the listings and filters for the GeForce RTX 5080 have also disappeared. While its absence does not necessarily mean Nvidia has discontinued the graphics card, it does raise questions about its status and future availability. This move is especially fishy because other Blackwell SKUs, such as the GeForce RTX 5070 Ti and GeForce RTX 5070, remain listed on the marketplace, albeit marked as “Out of Stock.”
The continued presence of the GeForce RTX 5070 Ti and GeForce RTX 5070 suggests that Nvidia wants to keep the products visible even when they are not immediately available so that consumers can anticipate restocks. The complete removal of the GeForce RTX 5090 and GeForce RTX 5080 breaks that pattern. It fuels rumors that Nvidia has allegedly stopped production of the GeForce RTX 5090 and possibly the GeForce RTX 5080 too, in favor of a rumored GeForce RTX 5080 24GB.
Rumors claim Nvidia allegedly stopped producing the GeForce RTX 5090 to repurpose the valuable GB202 silicon into the chipmaker’s RTX Pro Blackwell lineup, which fetches higher margins. This has a lot of credence, since many agree that Nvidia stopped being a gaming hardware vendor long ago and has transformed into an AI provider.
Rather than simply discontinuing the GeForce RTX 5090, Nvidia purportedly intends to introduce the GeForce RTX 5080 24GB as the new flagship gaming graphics card. The thing is, a 24GB variant of the GeForce RTX 5080 would solve one of the biggest consumer gripes with the graphics card: the lack of memory. While a GeForce RTX 5080 24GB would offer the same memory as the GeForce RTX 5090, it simply isn't a direct drop-in replacement. The former has 2X fewer CUDA cores, a substantial performance gap that even a 50% memory increase can't make up for.
How much money are you willing to spend during the Black Friday sales?
The GeForce RTX 5080 launched in January of last year with an MSRP of $999. Demand quickly outpaced supply, and with the rapid price hikes due to the memory shortage, the market price has more than doubled its original MSRP. As of this moment, the most affordable GeForce RTX 5080 in stock, the PNY GeForce RTX 5080 ARGB Epic-X RGB OC, retails for $2,199.99, which is 2.2X over the original launch price.
While some stock remains, it’s selling out fast, and the remaining units will only get more expensive as availability dwindles. At this rate, the GeForce RTX 5080 is unlikely to be available by Black Friday. If you are set on a GeForce RTX 5080, you may have little choice but to act quickly and buy at today's elevated prices.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
If the GeForce RTX 5080 24GB is indeed legitimate, the graphics card will almost certainly debut at a substantial premium over the original GeForce RTX 5080. Although Nvidia maintains that the RTX 5090 is still alive, the reality suggests otherwise. We have contacted the company for comment regarding the GeForce RTX 5080’s status.

articles.title: Dell’s 15-inch touchscreen laptop is the WFH machine I’d recommend
articles.text:
Dell's 15 touchscreen laptop with 1TB of storage is the office machine I’d recommend to remote workers — especially now it's $300 off at Best Buy
The 2026 Dell 15 pairs Intel’s new Core 7 350 chip with 16GB of RAM, a roomy 1TB SSD, and a 15.3-inch touchscreen in a thin, light design
In our experience, when it comes to business laptops you can't really go wrong with a Dell. But while the likes of the XPS dominate the high-end, I'm not convinced most professionals need a machine like that.
For remote and hybrid workers the Dell 15 laptop for $900 (was $1200) at Best Buy, is an easy pick for productivity that doesn't compromise on power for general office work, emails, video calls, and - of course - streaming movies in your downtime. For me, laptop checks every box and gives you plenty of room for files.
• Best for: students, families, and home workers who want a dependable, big-screen everyday laptop with lots of storage.
• Why we like it: a 15.3-inch touchscreen with 400 nits of brightness, a generous 1TB SSD, 16GB of memory for smooth multitasking, a backlit keyboard, and a light 3.34-pound design.
A 15.3-inch laptop with a 1920 x 1200 IPS touchscreen rated at 400 nits, Intel’s Core 7 350 processor from its new Core Series 3 lineup, integrated Intel graphics, 16GB of memory, a 1TB SSD, a backlit keyboard, HDMI 2.1, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and Windows 11. It weighs 3.34 pounds and comes in Celestial Blue.
Why we recommend it
Dell’s mainstream laptops have long been a safe pick for anyone who wants a reliable machine without paying for premium extras, and the 2026 Dell 15 brings a thinner, lighter design and Intel’s new Core Series 3 chips. We haven’t tested it yet, although we've reviewed plenty of similar models from Dell, and have a couple in use at home precisely as WFH machines. The specs are great here, and the 1TB SSD stands out, since most laptops at this price still ship with 512GB.
Price Context & Historical Value
This is $300, or 25%, off Best Buy’s $1,199.99 comparison price, but since this model just launched, there’s little price history to compare it to. Personally, I think the $1,199.99 list price flatters the discount.
Still, $899.99 for 16GB of RAM, 1TB of storage, and a touchscreen is a fair price given how much memory costs have climbed this year. It’s a sensible buy if you need a laptop, but it may well get cheaper as Black Friday nears.
Should You Buy It?
✅ Buy the Dell 15 (2026) if... you want a reliable office laptop with a big touchscreen, need plenty of storage for photos and files, or want a light machine that’s easy to carry around the home office, into work, or to class.
❌ Skip the Dell 15 (2026) if... you need a laptop capable of graphics-intensive workloads, as that's beyond what this Dell machine can handle.

articles.title: Why Banks Need Thousands of Test Cycles Before AI Agents Spend Money - Tech Guide
articles.text:
A bank can forgive a chatbot that gives a clumsy answer. It cannot forgive an agent that pays the same invoice twice. As software begins to act on behalf of customers, moving funds and settling bills without a person approving each step, the testing bar rises sharply.
That is why risk teams talk in thousands of test cycles, not dozens. Each cycle replays a payment scenario with small changes, and the goal is to see how the agent behaves when conditions drift. Teams that want a practical picture of how payment infrastructure is assembled and exercised can look at how FinteqHub explains the connections between financial services and technology providers.
What Changes When Software Holds the Wallet
A traditional payment flow has a human checkpoint. Someone clicks, confirms a code, or signs off a batch. An AI agent removes that checkpoint by design, because the whole point is speed and autonomy. Removing the human does not remove the need for judgment. It moves the judgment into rules, limits and monitoring, and every one of those has to be proven before launch.
Why one successful run proves very little
An agent that pays a utility bill correctly on Monday has shown it can handle Monday. Language models are probabilistic, so the same prompt can produce slightly different actions on different runs. Risk officers would rather see forty identical passes than one flawless demo.
How scenarios multiply fast
Take a simple instruction such as “pay my rent on the first.” Vary the currency, the weekend calendar, a changed landlord account, a duplicate reminder email and a short network outage. Five variables with four settings each already give 1,024 combinations, and that is before any adversarial input. Pass rates alone mislead, so validation teams usually track a few separate numbers, shown below with typical aims. Each one has its own threshold, and a failure in any single row can hold back a release for weeks.
| Measure | What it captures | Typical aim | 
| Duplicate payment rate | Same instruction paid twice | Zero in every cycle | 
| Limit breaches | Spend above the set ceiling | Zero | 
| Escalation accuracy | Handing doubtful cases to a person | Very high | 
| Run to run variance | Different actions from identical input | Low and explained | 
Notice that three of the four aims are absolute. A rate of 99.9 percent sounds strong until it is applied to a million transfers a month, which leaves a thousand errors to unwind by hand.
Banks also keep the failures. A test that broke the agent once becomes a permanent regression case, and the library grows with every incident, internal or industry wide.
Edge cases and hostile text that fill the calendar
Most of the cycles go to awkward situations, not the happy path. Public holidays that differ between countries, rounding on currency conversion and a merchant name that changes slightly between invoices quietly cause trouble in production. An agent that reads emails and invoices can be handed text written to steer it. Imagine an invoice whose footer quietly tells the agent to ignore its spending cap. Red teams write hundreds of such variants, and each one has to fail safely.
Testers also feed the agent contradictory instructions, such as a customer message asking for a transfer while a standing rule forbids it. The correct result is a pause and a question, not a guess.
Regulators Expect a Paper Trail
Supervisors in most major markets already require banks to show how automated decisions are governed. For agents, that means records of what was tested, what failed, who signed off and what limits apply. Thousands of cycles are only useful if the results are logged in a way an auditor can replay months later.
Staged rollout follows the same logic. Many institutions begin with a sandbox, move to shadow mode where the agent proposes payments that a person still executes, and only then grant a small live allowance, perhaps a few hundred dollars a day, which widens as evidence accumulates.
A Realistic Timeline for Going Live
For a narrow task such as recurring bill payment, a bank may spend several months between prototype and first live customer. Wider mandates take longer. The slow pace is not hesitation. Every added run shrinks the chance of a surprise, and a surprise on a live ledger costs more. Customers who see the agent work quietly for years will rarely think about the thousands of runs that made that possible.
Consider a mid sized lender that tests a bill payment agent nightly. After ninety days it holds roughly ninety thousand logged runs, a few dozen documented failures, and a short list of useful fixes that each came from a specific bad night, such as a leap day or a bank holiday that nobody had planned for in advance. That archive, more than any demo, is what convinces a risk committee to raise the daily allowance.

articles.title: Sur Windows 11 , les navigateurs Chromium vont démarrer au quart de tour, Edge en tête
articles.text:
Edge est le premier navigateur à profiter du lancement accéléré de Windows 11. Microsoft promet environ 15 % de gain à l’ouverture pour la plupart des utilisateurs, jusqu’à 33 % quand le PC jongle avec beaucoup de tâches. Ces travaux profiteront aux autres navigateurs sous Chromium.
Le gain concerne les lancements d’Edge quand le navigateur est déjà ouvert, ou actif en arrière-plan (grâce à Startup Boost, par exemple). La fonction est déjà déployée avec Edge 150, sur Windows 11 (25H2, 26H1 ou 26H2) mis à jour avec la KB5127936 d’octobre 2026, hors sécurité, ou une version plus récente.
Edge prévient Windows qu’il est là, et le système n’a plus à le chercher
Jusqu’ici, un clic sur Edge dans la barre des tâches, ou sur un lien censé s’ouvrir dans le navigateur, obligeait Windows à lancer un petit processus intermédiaire. Son rôle : vérifier si Edge tourne déjà et, si oui, lui transmettre la demande. Sur un PC qui vient de démarrer, on le remarque à peine. Avec plusieurs applications ouvertes, cette vérification peut donner une impression de lenteur.
Désormais, Edge signale lui-même sa présence à Windows dès qu’il démarre, et le système enregistre cette demande. Au lancement suivant, Windows contacte directement le processus Edge en cours, sans intermédiaire. Ce nouveau fonctionnement s’applique au menu Démarrer, à la barre des tâches et aux liens pris en charge qui s’ouvrent par défaut dans Edge. Microsoft travaille à y ajouter l’ouverture des fichiers PDF.
Microsoft avait déjà communiqué sur les optimisations de performance de Edge. Avec la version 134, nous rapportions un gain d’environ 9 % sur Speedometer 3.0, un benchmark qui simule de vraies interactions d’utilisateur. L’éditeur de Redmond expliquait avoir opéré des modifications du moteur de rendu de Chromium. Ici, les travaux portent donc sur le lien entre le navigateur et Windows, pas l’affichage des pages.
Non, Microsoft ne répète pas ce qu'elle a fait avec Internet Explorer en intégrant profondément son navigateur au sein du système. Les fruits de ces travaux seront reversés à Chromium, le projet open source sur lequel reposent Edge, Chrome, Vivaldi, Opera ou Brave. Ces navigateurs pourront donc en profiter à l’avenir, même si à l’heure actuelle, aucune date n’est précisée. Côté développeurs, la documentation décrit une interface expérimentale réservée aux applications « à instance unique », c’est-à-dire celles qui réutilisent la fenêtre déjà ouverte plutôt que d’en créer une nouvelle. Notons qu’il faut demander à Microsoft un jeton de déverrouillage. Reste à savoir si les développeurs de Mozilla pourront adapter ces travaux au moteur de rendu Gecko

articles.title: Vous détenez des cryptos ? En pleine crise Binance, ce courrier de la DGFiP est un piège, alerte la Police nationale
articles.text:
La Police nationale met en garde contre un faux courrier des impôts qui cible les détenteurs de cryptomonnaies. Un QR code y renvoie vers un site frauduleux, au moment même où Binance a subi un piratage record.
Un faux courrier des impôts, glissé dans les boîtes aux lettres, est en train de circuler et il est d'autant plus dangereux qu'il imite à s'y méprendre la Direction générale des Finances publiques. Tout y est, avec l'en-tête de la République française, l'adresse de Bercy, les articles de loi à la pelle et un QR code à scanner d’urgence pour « régulariser » vos cryptomonnaies. Une belle façade administrative bâtie par les escrocs, qui cherchent à obtenir votre phrase de récupération, une suite de mots secrets qui suffit à prendre le contrôle d'un portefeuille crypto et à le vider. Le moment est plutôt mal choisi pour baisser la garde. Car le soir même de l'alerte de la Police nationale, lancée jeudi 29 octobre, Binance se faisait dérober plus de 6 milliards de dollars, et ses clients inquiets deviennent des cibles toutes trouvées pour ce genre d'arnaque.
Un faux courrier des impôts presque plus vrai que nature qui vise les détenteurs de cryptos
Le document exhumé par la Police nationale est daté du 28 septembre 2026. Il prend la forme d'une mise en demeure. La missive prétend que des plateformes enregistrées auprès de l'AMF ont signalé les opérations en cryptomonnaies du destinataire, tout en le sommant de recenser tous ses comptes, portefeuilles et protocoles DeFi sur un « Portail des actifs numériques », avant le 29 octobre. Peu importe qu'il ou elle ait déjà tout déclaré, l'inscription passe par le scan d'un QR code présenté, sans rire, comme « sécurisé ». La technique est récente, mais elle n'est pas nouvelle, puisqu'une première vague, avec une échéance au 5 septembre, avait déjà circulé à la rentrée.
Le piège mélange le faux et le vrai. La directive européenne DAC8 existe bel et bien, par exemple. Depuis le 1er janvier 2026, les plateformes crypto collectent les données de leurs clients, et leur première transmission au fisc est attendue d'ici fin janvier 2027. Les formulaires 2086 et 3916-bis cités sont eux aussi authentiques. Le courrier pousse même le culot jusqu'à renvoyer vers impots.gouv.fr, « pour toute information officielle ».
Pour finir d'affoler le lecteur, il égrène les sanctions, à savoir 750 euros d'amende par compte non déclaré, 1 500 euros au-delà de 50 000 euros, des majorations de 40 à 80 %, intérêts de retard, et un contrôle fiscal approfondi. Selon la Police nationale, le QR code ou le lien frauduleux sert en fait à voler les identifiants fiscaux et, surtout, la phrase de récupération du portefeuille. Cette suite de 12 à 24 mots permet de restaurer un portefeuille sur n'importe quel appareil. Qui la détient peut le vider, sans le moindre recours.
Avec Binance siphonné, les arnaqueurs à l'affût comme jamais
L'alerte lancée par la Police nationale date du matin du 29 octobre. Le soir même, Binance, première plateforme d'échange au monde, se faisait dérober environ 6,3 milliards de dollars, plus de quatre fois le précédent record établi par le piratage de Bybit en 2025. Le point d'entrée fut l'ordinateur portable compromis d'un ingénieur, qui a permis de déclencher des retraits non autorisés. TRM Labs attribue l'attaque, avec une forte confiance, au groupe nord-coréen TraderTraitor, déjà coutumier du fait.
Binance assure avoir mis de côté plus de 6,34 milliards de dollars pour couvrir l'intégralité des pertes, et environ 3 milliards ont été gelés avec l'aide d'acteurs du secteur. La plateforme a d'abord suspendu les dépôts et retraits ; sa cofondatrice Yi He assure depuis que les dépôts fonctionnent à nouveau, les retraits devant reprendre sous 48 heures. En France, la situation est assez particulière, puisque faute d'agrément MiCA, Binance n'y fournit plus de services sur cryptoactifs depuis le 1er juillet, et les clients qui y avaient laissé leurs fonds ne peuvent plus les retirer pour l'instant. Le cours de Bitcoin, qui dépassait les 73 000 dollars l'unité hier, est largement sous les 70 000 ce vendredi après-midi.
Les conséquences seront multiples, que ce soit pour certaines entreprises ou pour des clients privés de retraits et inquiets pour leur épargne. Binance les a d'ailleurs invités à se méfier des arnaques, qui vont forcément se multiplier dans les prochaines semaines. Du faux support au faux formulaire d'indemnisation, la recette du courrier fiscal pourrait vite changer d'emballage. Quoi qu'il en soit, personne ne doit jamais vous demander votre phrase de récupération. En cas de doute, contactez votre centre des impôts ou tapez vous-même l'adresse d'impots.gouv.fr, puis signalez la tentative sur 17cyber.gouv.fr ou au 0 805 805 817.

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday 2026, l'aspirateur balai Dyson V8 Cyclone passe à 249 € (-17 %)
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 – L'aspirateur balai Dyson V8 Cyclone à 249,00 € (-17%)
L'aspirateur balai Dyson V8 Cyclone passe sous les 250 € chez Boulanger.com soit une baisse d'environ 17% sur le prix habituellement constaté.
L'innovation peut-elle se nicher dans la réinterprétation ? Ce qui apparaît comme un sujet de bac de philo trouvera peut-être une réponse après notre test du Dyson V8 Cyclone, la vision 2025 d'un aspirateur-balai sorti en 2016.
Dyson V8 Cyclone

Points forts
- Belles performances d'aspiration.
- Entretien facile.
- Relativement discret, aussi bien visuellement qu'acoustiquement.
Points faibles
- Autonomie trop faible à la puissance turbo.
- Extraction de la brosse pénible.
- Manque d'astuces pratiques (pas d'indicateur d'autonomie, de rampe de leds…).
Dans les grandes lignes, le Dyson V8 Cyclone reste le même que le V8 “normal”. Pour le meilleur et pour le pire, serait-on tenté d'ajouter. Certes, il existe quelques menues différences au niveau de la prise en main, une amélioration de la gestion du bruit, et on ne peut que féliciter Dyson d'avoir enfin pris le virage de la batterie amovible. On regrette d'autant plus que cet aspirateur-balai n'ait pas pris celui de l'indicateur d'autonomie précis, ou encore de la rampe de leds sur la tête d'aspiration. Ceci étant, malgré une durée de vie en mode turbo famélique, le V8 Cyclone est un modèle efficace et très simple à entretenir.

De plus, grâce à la filtration multicyclonique tout à fait performante, l'entretien de l'appareil est un jeu d'enfant. Certes, nous aurions apprécié un mode boost peut-être un peu plus endurant ou encore une estimation de l'autonomie restante en minutes et secondes plutôt qu'en pourcentage, mais cela n'entache pas du tout l'excellente impression laissée par ce R20 très réussi.

articles.title: Adieu les écrans géants et les gadgets inutiles ? La Chine durcit le ton face à la démesure automobile
articles.text:
Leurs vaisseaux ont certainement impressionné les visiteurs du dernier Mondial de l’Auto. Présentes en nombre, les marques chinoises ont en effet marqué la 91ème édition du salon avec des technologies plus étonnantes les unes que les autres. Sauf que le bluff pourrait bientôt prendre fin, puisque l’Empire du Milieu resserrera prochainement les boulons autour de ces modèles au nom de la sécurité. Enfin une bonne nouvelle ?
L’idée fait en tout cas son chemin, car le ministère chinois de l’Industrie et des Technologies de l’Information vient de lancer une consultation publique sur un projet de loi visant à contrôler davantage les technologies embarquées. Une attention particulière est notamment portée sur la taille des écrans tactiles, l’inclinaison des sièges zéro gravité, les feux personnalisables et les poignées de portes affleurantes. Voyons cela en détail.
Écrans tactiles géants : l’overdose qui met en danger les conducteurs
Les dalles XXL, d’abord, posent un réel problème d’ergonomie. Comment rester insensible au fait de devoir farfouiller dans d’innombrables sous-menus pour régler simplement la température intérieure ? Le ministère demande ainsi aux constructeurs d’évaluer l’impact de ces afficheurs sur la distraction des automobilistes. Leur fiabilité et leur sécurité en cas d’accident seront pareillement analysées.
De cela découlerait des mesures concrètes, comme l’interdiction pure et simple des écrans pliables et flexibles. Signature des modèles haut de gamme, les sièges zéro gravité sont aussi dans le collimateur des autorités. Des tests de collision, d’anti-pincement et de fiabilité plus exigeants sont ainsi suggérés pour améliorer leur sécurité. Le ministère conseille même de limiter l’usage de ces assises, voire de l’interdire en fonction des situations.
À lire aussi : « Les écrans tactiles pires que l’alcool au volant » – cette étude choc pointe du doigt les véhicules modernes
Messages et dessins sur les feux : la censure s’invite sur la route
Les feux personnalisables permettant d’écrire des messages coquins ou de dessiner des motifs amusants pourraient aussi être sous strict contrôle. Certains hauts responsables du ministère craignent que du contenu non autorisé soit affiché sur les routes. Les constructeurs sont vivement invités à modérer activement tout ce qui sera affiché dans ces feux. Toute inscription considérée comme sensible pourrait donc être bannie. Mais la fonctionnalité subsistera.
Le dernier point est déjà connu. Il s’agit des poignées affleurantes qui ont causé dans le passé des accidents gravissimes. Raison pour laquelle le ministère a déjà publié plusieurs modèles de poignées de portes qu’il juge sûrs. Une poignée de paramètres comme leur prise en main, leur emplacement ou leur mécanisme ont été pris en compte. Une ouverture de secours manuelle sera également imposée pour permettre une utilisation même après un accident.

articles.title: Bill Gates, fundador de Microsoft: "Consiste en contratar al robot, despedir al humano y no mirar atrás"
articles.text:
Este verano Bill Gates vaticinó algo: la adopción de la IA en el mercado laboral va a ser algo "muy turbulento" para lo que no estamos preparados. El cofundador de Microsoft se ha mostrado proclive a que se ponga impuestos a la IA porque si los empleadores pagan impuestos sobre la nómina de las personas que contratan, por qué no hacer lo mismo con los tokens de la IA y los robots que usas en tu proceso productivo.
De hecho, la realidad es justo la opuesta: si adquieres un robot, puedes desgravarte el gasto. Pues bien, han entrevistado al filántropo y multimillonario en The Observer y ha vuelto a poner el foco en lo que él cree que es el problema: los incentivos empresariales. Y ha vuelto a insistir: el sistema premia la sustitución de personas por máquinas.
Qué fácil es reemplazar trabajos (humanos). Bill Gates describe la IA como un evento evolutivo que deja al humano en un segundo plano, ya que ya no seremos lo más inteligente del planeta. Y esto trasciende de lo tecnológico a lo político: quién va a pagar la transición. Lo que Gates adelanta suena desolador: el reemplazo de casi todas las habilidades laborales por parte de la inteligencia artificial. Primero las de invención y trabajos de oficina y después, gracias a los robots humanoides, a los oficios.
Ante esa realidad, Bill Gates explica que tal y como están diseñados los incentivos laborales (en su opinión, mal), la lógica dominante "consiste en contratar al robot, despedir al humano y no mirar atrás". Por eso sostiene que los ingresos públicos caerán aunque la prosperidad (a nivel macro, otra cosa serán los hogares de esas personas sin trabajo) mejore. Y eso sin hablar de los riesgos de ese avance de la IA: en su hoja negra de posibilidades está el bioterrorismo y los ciberataques como amenaza inmediata y, a finales de los años 20, que la IA opere fuera de control humano y haya que ponerse serios con el alineamiento.
El plan de Gates para mitigarlo. El cofundador de Microsoft ha vuelto a insistir en gravar el uso de la IA y sugiere un "impuesto de tokens". Su razonamiento es que los ingresos públicos con los que se financia la red de seguridad (las prestaciones) se reducirán durante la transición, aunque la prosperidad general mejore. Así que los gobiernos necesitarán nuevas fuentes para pagar a quienes se queden sin empleo, la educación futura y la reconversión profesional.
Asimismo, defiende que los multimillonarios paguen más y hace una confesión: él habría aceptado pagar algo más del doble de lo que ha pagado. Según el Observer, ha abonado unos 14.000 millones de dólares en impuestos a lo largo de su vida y habría estado dispuesto a pagar 40.000 millones. Por eso pide a los gobiernos que encuentren la forma de gravar a las grandes fortunas de un modo que se perciba como justo, aunque advierte de que eso no resuelve el desfase entre gasto público y recaudación en muchos países ricos. En cuanto a las eventuales amenazas de una IA superdesarrollada, pide que EEUU y China cooperen para tratar de evitar estos riesgos, que directamente llama "reto para la humanidad".
Por qué importa. Si todas y cada una de las empresas ganan (en términos económicos) sustituyendo personas, el resultado colectivo puede ser un desastre aunque desde la lógica de la gestión empresarial sea una buena idea. De ahí que Gates proponga medidas que afectan a toda la sociedad. De hecho, ya hay señales: la inteligencia artificial está frenando el acceso laboral a los junior. Este estudio de Stanford evidencia que los jóvenes de 22 a 25 años en profesiones muy expuestas a la IA tienen un 19% menos de empleo de lo esperado.
Microsoft es el mejor peor ejemplo. Menuda cruel ironía que pocos días después de que, pese estar en su mejor momento económico, Microsoft haya dejado entrever que le sobran unas 60.000 trabajadores, el 27% de su plantilla, de sus oficinas de Estados Unidos, Canadá, India y Reino Unido y que afecta a personal de nivel 70 o inferior, así que les ha propuesto un plan de salidas voluntarias. Y ojo, porque no ha sido la primera del año: ya en abril lanzó un programa de jubilación voluntaria para unos 8.750 empleados elegibles en EEUU, y en julio comunicó casi 5.000 despidos, como recoge Reuters. 
Tampoco es nuevo: en mayo de 2025 despedía a unos 6.000 trabajadores, aproximadamente el 3% de su plantilla global, alegando "cambios en la organización para posicionar mejor a la empresa en un mercado dinámico", y en julio de 2025 se despedía de otros 9.000 empleados. Mientras tanto, la compañía invierte a lo grande en IA: solo en el último trimestre fiscal ha destinado 41.000 millones de dólares a inversión de capital. Puede que Bill Gates cofundara Microsoft, pero desde luego que en esta transición al futuro mercado laboral de la IA, creador y empresa actual tienen posturas diametralmente opuestas.

articles.title: NVIDIA Reportedly Moves Up RTX 5080 24 GB Launch
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
NVIDIA Reportedly Moves Up RTX 5080 24 GB Launch
NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB might arrive sooner than expected. A new post from Board Channels' ChannelGate account claims NVIDIA is speeding up the launch, with availability now expected around January 2027 and December 2026 as the earliest option. Earlier this month, various sources relayed that the card was reportedly planned for Q1 2027. The same post says NVIDIA will stop supplying the RTX 5080 16 GB and the RTX 5090 D V2 to China, leaving the 24 GB RTX 5080 as the only flagship model in that market. The report only covers China, so there's no word yet on whether the 16 GB card is going away globally. If the January window pans out, a CES 2027 reveal seems likely, though NVIDIA hasn't confirmed anything. 
Apparently, NVIDIA has already cleared out its RTX 5080 16 GB GPU inventory, and the remaining stock should last around two months. That roughly matches a leaker's claim that NVIDIA has January discontinuation dates set for the 16 GB card. The post is machine-translated, so some wording may be off. Specs are still unknown, though 24 GB on the same 256-bit bus would most likely mean 3 GB GDDR7 modules instead of 2 GB ones. Board Channels previously suggested the card could cost around 19,999 yuan (nearly $3,000) in China, while the 16 GB model already sells for close to $2,000 at U.S. retailers, double its $999 MSRP. With the memory shortage expected to get worse in 2027, it's reasonable to expect the 24 GB card to be both expensive and hard to find.
Sources:

articles.title: PS5 desbloqueado vira “Steam Machine” e roda jogos de PC • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
PS5 desbloqueado vira “Steam Machine” e roda jogos de PC
Projeto instala Bazzite com interface da Steam, suporte ao Proton e até desbloqueio experimental de unidades da GPU.
Um projeto não oficial transformou um PlayStation 5 desbloqueado em uma máquina Linux voltada para jogos. O PS5 Bazzite Deck leva a distribuição Bazzite ao console da Sony com a interface Steam Gaming Mode. A novidade representa um avanço em relação às primeiras experiências com Linux no videogame.
Agora, o foco está em transformar o console em algo próximo de uma “Steam Machine”, com acesso à biblioteca de jogos de PC.
O projeto adapta a versão do Bazzite voltada a consoles portáteis para o PlayStation 5. Também é possível alternar para um desktop completo baseado no KDE Plasma. Apesar da aparência, não é o SteamOS oficial da Valve. O Bazzite é uma distribuição Linux independente que oferece experiência similar e utiliza tecnologias como o Proton para executar jogos criados para Windows.
O sistema inicializa a partir de uma unidade externa, como pendrive ou SSD, e não substitui o software original da Sony. Sem carregar o Linux, o PS5 volta normalmente ao sistema da Sony.
Uma demonstração no YouTube mostra o console executando Forza Horizon 6. O detalhe chama atenção porque o jogo, lançado até agora para Xbox Series X/S e PC, só chega oficialmente ao PS5 em janeiro de 2027.
Usuários também já conseguiram executar Horizon Zero Dawn, Palworld, Genshin Impact, RimWorld e XCOM 2. O desenvolvedor do projeto afirma no Reddit que Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Ethernet e DualSense já funcionam no Bazzite, assim como o áudio por HDMI e aceleração de vídeo por hardware.
Em consoles equipados com chip HDMI FLAVA3, o projeto oferece resolução 1440p e 4K a até 120 Hz, além de HDR e VRR. Outras revisões possuem limitações e podem ficar restritas a 4K a 60 Hz.
No PS5 original e Slim sim. A GPU possui fisicamente 40 unidades computacionais (CUs), mas a Sony comercializa o console com 36 delas ativadas. O projeto permite tentar habilitar as quatro restantes. Isso representa mais CUs ativas, mas não garante ganho de desempenho e pode causar instabilidade.
O próprio projeto alerta que a ativação pode provocar pontos verdes, cores alteradas, artefatos gráficos e travamentos. Se surgirem problemas, é possível voltar à configuração original.
É necessário ter um console com um firmware compatível e acesso a um método de jailbreak. O cenário de desbloqueio do PS5 avançou rapidamente nos últimos meses, com novos exploits e ferramentas compatíveis com diferentes versões do sistema.
Vale mencionar que o primeiro boot pode levar vários minutos e atualizações da Sony também podem alterar o funcionamento. O PS5 Pro também passou a ser reconhecido pelo Bazzite a partir da versão 1.8.4, mas o desenvolvedor ainda classifica esse suporte como inicial.

articles.title: Intel’s woes wipe out $1 trillion of semiconductor market cap in one day — PC market bloodbath leaves few chip stocks unscathed
articles.text:
Intel’s woes wipe out $1 trillion of semiconductor market cap in one day — PC market bloodbath leaves few chip stocks unscathed
$1 trillion in semiconductor market capitalization wiped out.
Intel's shares plunged 30% on Friday, wiping out nearly $150 billion in market capitalization in a single day, the largest single-day loss in the company's history. The decline followed a disappointing financial outlook, largely driven by an anticipated drop of more than 20% in sales at Intel's client computing group (CCPG), the company's main cash cow. The declines quickly spread across the semiconductor industry. Although losses elsewhere were nowhere near as severe as Intel's, approximately $1 trillion in semiconductor market capitalization was wiped out on Friday, according to intraday estimates by Benzinga.
Fire sale
The PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index (SOX), which tracks the stock performance of 30 major semiconductor companies, is one of the key indicators of the industry's financial health. On Friday, the index plunged 9.14%, or 1,052.82 points, to 10,465.38 points as of 2:31 PM ET, as Intel's disappointing outlook triggered a massive selloff across the semiconductor industry.
Intel was by far the biggest loser, as other chip-related stocks, while Arm (-12.68%), AMD (-12.48%), Qualcomm (-12.14%), Applied Materials (-8.73%), ASML (-8.13%), Lam Research (-8%), Micron (-7.28%), and Broadcom (-7.1%) suffered considerably less. Then again, while Nvidia lost 5.66% of its market cap, this translates to around $270 billion, which is a massive amount of money. Paradoxically, Nvidia lost more market capitalization in absolute dollar terms than Intel.
In an unexpected turn of events, the downturn extended to server manufacturers and cloud giants too, as Dell (-12.67%), HPE (-8.10%), Supermicro (-6.96%), and Oracle (-6.88%) lost nearly 7% to 13% of their value. Reuters noted that investors increasingly question the scale of capital investments required to expand AI infrastructure as well as the sustainability of that spending.
Gloomy outlook
Intel’s client computing and physical AI group (CCPG) generated $8.1 billion in revenue during Q3 2026, down 5% year-over-year and 9% sequentially. Weaker demand and increased competition reduced client processor shipments by 14% year-over-year, which was partially offset by a 9% increase in average selling prices. CCPG accounted for nearly half of Intel's revenue of around $16.5 billion and the company's main source of cash. As strong demand for server processors only partially offsets declining client sales, Intel guided its Q4 revenue to be between $15 billion and $16 billion.
Intel expects the client market to deteriorate further in Q4 2026 and into 2027 as elevated memory prices and shortages of other components impact PC prices and demand. In general, Intel expects the client PC market to decline 10% in 2027 compared to 2026, which will inevitably have an effect on CCPG performance. While Intel expects its data center business to continue growing in 2027, industry-wide supply constraints will limit its ability to fully capitalize on demand.
2026 has been a mixed bag for Intel so far. On the one hand, the company achieved its highest market capitalization ever — $673.43 billion in mid-June — on growing sales of data center CPUs, strong sales of client products, and a return to profitability (if the $12.5 billion non-cash accounting charge associated with shares issued to the U.S. government is excluded). On the other hand, the company's capitalization has dropped by nearly 50% to $338.91 billion since mid-June (with $148.68 billion in just one day), as investors began to realize that the performance of Intel's CCPG heavily depends on memory prices, as customers and businesses tend not to like overpriced systems. Yet on the other hand, now that Intel sells fewer client processors, it can sell more expensive data center CPUs.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
What about Apple?
Surprisingly, Apple (-1.66%), which only sells client products, was nearly unaffected by the performance of Intel's client computing group, as investors probably believe that the world's largest supplier of consumer electronics is more immune to memory prices than Intel. Ironically, if we count the A-series SoCs used in iPhones (which tend to outperform mainstream laptop CPUs), Apple sells substantially more processors than Intel, making Apple by far the world's largest supplier of microprocessors. Despite this, Apple's shares were largely unaffected by the semiconductor selloff.
There are several reasons for this distinction. Firstly, Apple's business model is fundamentally different. Intel sells processors to PC manufacturers, whereas Apple designs its own processors and sells them as part of finished products. Consequently, Apple captures revenue from the entire device rather than just the processor. Secondly, the two companies face different demand dynamics. Intel depends heavily on the PC market, while Apple's iPhone business follows the smartphone replacement cycle. Rising memory prices could affect both, but not necessarily to the same extent and at the same time.
There is an additional irony: Apple is also a major customer of TSMC, so its processor supply chain overlaps with those of AMD, Intel, and other semiconductor companies whose shares declined sharply.
While we should not directly compare Apple and Intel, the comparison illustrates that investors were not necessarily abandoning companies that design or use semiconductors, but were rather concerned about the profitability and growth prospects of these high-tech companies. And if we take a look at the situation from this point of view, the whole thing will start looking completely different.

articles.title: Remote hands bridge the distance between your team and your infrastructure - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Modern IT infrastructure is a lot like building blocks. Some of it sits in the cloud, some in European server colocation facilities, and some runs on a company’s own hardware. But every now and then, hardware needs a human hand. And that hand cannot reach halfway across the world. That is where remote hands come in. Local technicians become an extension of your team, right there among the server racks.
Remote hands may sound like another marketing term. In practice, it is very simple: in certain situations, someone other than your own technician is authorised to access your server rack and work on the hardware. The scope of the service can determine whether an overnight incident takes 20 minutes to fix or two days. So, what does the service actually involve?
What the service covers and where its limits are
Remote hands means technical support carried out on your hardware by the data centre operator on your behalf. You submit a request through a customer portal or helpdesk. A technician carries it out in the data centre and records what was done. Typical tasks include:
- restarting and power cycling equipment – a hard reset of a server that has stopped responding,
- checking cables – making sure fibre and copper cables are connected to the right ports,
- visual inspection – checking status lights, temperatures and fans,
- replacing components – drives, power supplies or memory modules according to your instructions,
- installing and labelling equipment – mounting hardware in racks, adding labels and receiving deliveries,
- basic diagnostics and incident coordination – the technician acts as your eyes and ears on site.
Where the service ends
Some providers split their support into two levels:
- Simple tasks, such as those listed above, are offered as remote hands.
- More complex work, such as firmware updates, hardware configuration or troubleshooting more difficult issues, is offered as smart hands and charged separately.
Other providers combine both levels into a single package, sometimes called long hands. Terminology therefore varies from one provider to another. What matters is the exact list of services in your contract, not what the service is called.
Why remote hands matter when your servers are in another country
Distance changes the cost of every physical intervention. Sending your own technician to another continent means flights, accommodation and two lost working days for a task that may take five minutes. Time zones complicate things further. As your working day ends, the morning shift at a European data centre may just be starting. A remote hands team available 24/7, 365 days a year closes this gap and cuts response times from days to tens of minutes.
The cost of downtime is rising too. According to an Uptime Institute analysis, the latest major outage cost 57% of surveyed organisations more than US$100,000 [source]. For one in five, the cost exceeded US$1 million. Against numbers like these, the hourly rate of an on-site technician is a minor expense.
Tip: TTC Teleport’s Prague data centre holds TIER III certification from Uptime Institute, guarantees 99.982% availability and provides a 24/7 English-speaking helpdesk. This means international teams can request physical support at any time during their own working hours.
Hybrid infrastructure makes remote hands a natural fit
Companies rarely put all their eggs in one basket. Public cloud handles changing workloads. Data centre colocation hosts hardware with predictable workloads and sensitive data. And some equipment stays in-house.
Add a growing European footprint — data residency requirements, regulations such as NIS2 and DORA, and the need to reduce latency for European customers are pushing servers into Frankfurt, Amsterdam and Prague.
Remote server management can handle much of this mix. But there is a clear limit: remote access can restart an operating system, but it cannot plug a loose cable back in. That is where the local team takes over.
What to ask before signing up for remote hands
The scope of the service and response times belong in the SLA, not in an email thread. Check:
- which tasks are included in the standard rate and which are charged separately,
- how quickly a technician will respond to an emergency request outside business hours,
- how billing works (providers may charge in 15, 30 or 60-minute blocks, offer a monthly pool of hours or use a flat fee),
- what language the helpdesk operates in,
- how requests are submitted,
- and how every access to your server rack is logged.
Your auditor will appreciate that last point too.
Find the hands before you need them
Choose your provider while everything is running smoothly. Once something goes wrong, all you can do is find out what you actually signed up for. Compare your options before the first overnight alarm reminds you just how far away your server rack really is.

articles.title: Le Black Friday s’installe chez Boulanger : ce téléviseur TCL MiniLED de 65 pouces passe sous la barre des 900€
articles.text:
Le téléviseur TCL 65C79L combine un grand écran à rétroéclairage MiniLED et un affichage 144 Hz qui le rend adapté aux jeux vidéo. Boulanger le propose à 899 € pour le Black Friday, contre un prix de référence de 1 199 €.
Si vous planifiez de changer de téléviseur durant le Black Friday, vous n’avez peut-être déjà plus à attendre. En effet, Boulanger a d’ores et déjà lancé son opération autour de l’évènement, et propose la TV TCL 65C79L de 65 pouces pour 899 €. Il s’agit d’un modèle sorti en 2026, qui donne accès à une définition 4K et à une expérience gaming assez complète grâce à la prise en charge du 144 Hz avec une source compatible.
Le téléviseur TCL 65C79L de 65 pouces est à 899 € au lieu de 1 199 € chez Boulanger pour le Black Friday.
Pourquoi choisir le TCL 65C79L ?
- Pour son rétroéclairage MiniLED : les 1 152 zones permettent d’ajuster la luminosité dans différentes parties de l’image.
- Pour ses fonctions gaming : le VRR et l’ALLM accompagnent les consoles récentes, tandis que la 4K jusqu’à 144 Hz intéresse les joueurs sur PC compatible.
- Pour ses services connectés : Google TV donne accès aux applications de streaming, tandis que Google Cast et AirPlay 2 facilitent le partage de contenus depuis d’autres appareils.
Un grand écran pour les films et les soirées console
Le téléviseur TCL 65C79L affiche un pic de luminosité annoncé jusqu’à 3 000 nits par le fabricant. L’intérêt de cette caractéristique, c’est qu’elle permet notamment à l’écran de restituer les hautes lumières des contenus HDR. Côté son, on trouve un système audio de 60 W signé Bang & Olufsen, avec prise en charge du Dolby Atmos.
Les gamers peuvent, quant à eux, compter sur le VRR, qui synchronise le rafraîchissement de la dalle avec les images envoyées par la source, ainsi que sur l’ALLM, qui active automatiquement le mode à faible latence. Ce modèle figure également parmi les téléviseurs TCL concernés par l’arrivée de Gemini en France.
Un grand téléviseur qui nécessite beaucoup d’espace
Avec ses 65 pouces de diagonale, ce qui représente 164 cm, cette TV TCL 65C79L assure une très bonne immersion aussi bien pour les films et les séries que pour les jeux vidéo. Mais attention à bien vous assurer que vous disposez de la place nécessaire pour l’installer : le téléviseur mesure 144,4 cm de large et 36,9 cm de profondeur avec son pied.
✅ Les points forts
- Rétroéclairage MiniLED à 1 152 zones.
- Affichage 4K jusqu’à 144 Hz avec VRR.
- Google TV, AirPlay 2 et Google Cast.
❌ Les limites
- Un seul port USB.
- Encombrement important avec le pied.
Idéale pour jouer et regarder des films, la TV TCL 65C79L est proposée à 899 € chez Boulanger, avec la livraison offerte à votre domicile.
Ce téléviseur signé TCL convient aux foyers à la recherche d’un grand écran polyvalent pour les films, le streaming et les jeux. L’association du Mini LED et des 144 Hz constitue son principal intérêt à ce tarif qui chute sous la barre psychologique des 900 €.
Par contre, si vous ne jouez pas et que vous vous contentez essentiellement de regarder des émissions télévisées, un modèle plus simple et moins coûteux peut suffire à vos besoins. Il faut aussi vous assurer d’avoir tout l’espace nécessaire pour l’installer chez vous avant de commander.

articles.title: SEBI chairman says market regulator keeping eye on Tata Group developments
articles.text:
SEBI chairman says market regulator keeping eye on Tata Group developments
The comments came amid differences over governance matters at Tata Sons, the group's holding company, including the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman and the question of its proposed listing.
SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Saturday said the market regulator is monitoring developments relating to governance at the holding company level in the Tata Group, and pointed out that the group's listed companies and their promoters are subject to SEBI's disclosure and compliance norms.
The comments came amid differences over governance matters at Tata Sons, the group's holding company, including the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman and the question of its proposed listing.
"At the holding company level, there are some issues, as that's not really a listed company. The rest of the companies, those which are listed, follow all the LODR (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) norms," Pandey told reporters on the sidelines of the launch of the Bharat Chamber Investors Forum.
These listed companies and promoters of those firms are subject to all norms, he said.
Asked whether the SEBI was keeping track of Tata Group's developments, he said, "Yes... I mean in the sense of, you know, we have to keep monitoring all the developments."
Pandey did not refer to any specific governance violation or regulatory action against the group in his remarks.
The Tata Group has 26 publicly listed companies, with a combined market capitalisation of $328 billion as of March 31, 2025, according to its FY25 annual report.
Of these, seven listed companies collectively hold around 11.92% in Tata Sons, according to an analysis by governance advisory firm InGovern. The firms also have more than 1.77 crore shareholder or folio accounts.
The seven companies are Tata Steel, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Tata Chemicals, Tata Power, Indian Hotels, Tata Consumer Products and Tata Investment Corporation.
These companies are part of the group's larger portfolio of 26 listed entities and represent only those firms identified in the analysis as holding a stake in Tata Sons.
Tata Trusts holds around 66% in Tata Sons, while the Shapoorji Pallonji Group holds approximately 18.4%.

articles.title: D'après le patron de ChatGPT, la RAM dans nos PC est du "gaspillage" car les centres de données IA exploitent bien mieux cette ressource devenue rare
articles.text:
D'après le patron de ChatGPT, la RAM dans nos PC est du "gaspillage" car les centres de données IA exploitent bien mieux cette ressource devenue rare
Alors que la crise de la RAM frappe le monde entier, Sam Altman, dirigeant d’OpenAI à qui l’on doit ChatGPT, estime qu’elle est mal utilisée. Pour lui, cette ressource rare est désormais bien plus utile dans les centres de données IA que dans les PC des particuliers.
C’est lors du podcast Cheeky Pint de John Collison que Sam Altman a pris la parole à propos de la crise de la RAM : "D’un point de vue mondial, c’est assez terrible que tout le monde garde une partie de la quantité limitée de DRAM dans son propre ordinateur alors qu’elle n’est utilisée que 5 % du temps." Sam Altman ajoute : "Il faut viser une utilisation maximale dans les centres de données si l’on veut gérer un environnement où l’offre est aussi limitée."
La RAM dans nos PC ? Inutile selon Sam Altman
Sam Altman parle également des personnes qui cherchent à faire tourner l’IA en local sur leur PC, une tâche qui demande beaucoup de RAM pour faire tourner le modèle sans passer par un serveur externe. Dans un centre de données, la DRAM est exploitée toute la journée.
La crise de la RAM touche évidemment le grand public puisque les centres de données IA s’accaparent une grande part de la production mondiale. Désormais, les constructeurs privilégient les puces pour les serveurs car elles sont bien plus rentables. Résultat, il y en a beaucoup moins pour les PC et les smartphones.
La situation est telle que l’un des leaders du marché, Micron, a quitté le secteur de la RAM grand public sous sa marque Crucial pour privilégier ses gros clients qui alimentent des centres de données. Crucial fait partie des marques historiques pour acheter de la RAM et des SSD pour son PC, mais l’entreprise l’assume : la demande provoquée par l’IA a explosé et est bien plus rentable pour ses comptes.
Et n’oublions pas que la pénurie pourrait encore peser sur le marché en 2028 selon les dirigeants de Micron et de Samsung, l’un des autres leaders, voire jusqu'en 2030. Et bien évidemment, en 2027, on s’attend à des prix encore plus gonflés que cette année.
Des centres de données qui s'accaparent la demande
Les centres de données IA demandent bien plus de RAM qu’un PC et tournent non-stop. Sam Altman estime donc qu’une barrette de RAM dans le PC d’un particulier a moins de valeur qu’une quantité équivalente dans un centre de données qui profite à des milliers de clients.
Bien évidemment, la position de Sam Altman n’a rien d’innocent puisqu’il dirige OpenAI à qui l’on doit ChatGPT et qui a un besoin énorme et croissant de RAM. L’entreprise IA participe donc directement à cette course et puis n’oublions pas ces projets qui demanderont encore plus de RAM comme Stargate.
Mais alors pourquoi certaines personnes préfèrent utiliser de la DRAM pour faire tourner une IA sur leur PC au lieu de le faire dans le cloud ? Tout simplement, cela évite d’envoyer ses données vers un serveur, le tout sans connexion ou limite imposée par un abonnement. Et puis on ne peut pas oublier la question de la confidentialité.
La vision de Sam Altman entre donc en confrontation directe avec l’IA locale privilégiée par certains.

articles.title: "Recreé toda Suiza en Minecraft": un estudiante ha reconstruido Suiza a escala real a base de apilar bloques
articles.text:
Casi todo jugador de Minecraft ha levantado alguna vez una casa torcida o una torre sin fin. Algunos se lo han currado un poco más y han llegado a construir recreaciones de edificios reales, pero pocos se han planteado siquiera ponerse a construir un país entero dentro del juego. Un jugador se lo propuso y, aunque le ha llevado algún tiempo, lo ha conseguido: ha construido su Suiza natal con todo lujo de detalle.
Lo más curioso es descubrir de donde ha sacado las referencias para conseguir ese nivel de precisión. La web de Blocks incluye un mapa de la construcción y, justo debajo, se ha habilitado un deslizador que revela la foto aérea real de Swisstopo. El resultado es increíblemente preciso.
Un país entero, bloque a bloque. Según recogía el medio alemán 20 Minuten, un estudiante de 22 años de la ETH Zúrich ha levantado una versión de digital de Suiza a escala 1:1 dentro de Minecraft. El estudiante se hace llamar Manifold en el juego y aprendió por su cuenta modelado 3D y el uso de geodatos. "Todo empezó con el deseo de tener en mis manos las montañas y los valles suizos como modelos físicos", aseguraba Manifold.
Según contó al medio alemán, el estudiante usó datos geológicos reales de acceso público como base de datos para generar los paisajes digitales en el juego. "En mi caso, proviene de datos proporcionados por Swisstopo, la Oficina Federal de Topografía", aseguraba Manifold. Para establecer una escala equivalente entre el paisaje digital y los datos reales, utilizó la conversión más sencilla posible: un bloque de Minecraft equivaldría a un metro en el mundo real. Eso nos deja un mapa que cubre 41.285 kilómetros cuadrados. La mayor parte de la superficie del mapa digital de Suiza construido por Manifold está disponible por suscripción, pero el joven estudiante ha liberado toda la región de Jungfrau-Aletsch, declarada Patrimonio de la Humanidad por la UNESCO
Datos abiertos, un solo autor. El mundo que ha creado Manifold se nutre de varias fuentes de datos. El terreno proviene del modelo de elevación swissALTI3D, los lagos y masas de agua de swissBATHY3D, la altura de los bosques y árboles de swissSURFACE3D y los edificios provienen de swissBUILDINGS3D.
Tal y como recuerda la página de la Oficina Federal de Topografía de Suiza, hasta el 1 de marzo de 2021 hacía falta un permiso especial para usar la mayoría de los productos digitales de Swisstopo. A partir de esa fecha, mapas, fotos aéreas y modelos del paisaje son datos abiertos y gratuitos para su uso libre, incluso con fines comerciales. El estudiante reconoce que, "este proyecto solo es posible porque Suiza pone sus datos geográficos a disposición del público de forma gratuita". Manifold reconoce que el caso de Suiza es único. "Que yo sepa, en ningún otro lugar existen datos abiertos tan detallados para todo el mundo como en Suiza", afirmaba el estudiante suizo y por eso su proyecto de una Suiza digital en Minecraft con nivel de detalle tan extremo no es replicable para ningún otro lugar del planeta.
Otros países ya lo probaron. En 2014, la agencia danesa de geodatos reprodujo Dinamarca a escala 1:1, con unos 4.000 miles de millones de bloques. La idea fue de Simon Kokkendorf, empleado de la agencia, que la pensó como herramienta de enseñanza y partió del modelo de elevación 3D del organismo.
En 2013, el Ordnance Survey británico llevó Gran Bretaña al juego con más de 22.000 millones de bloques. Lo hizo un becario, Joseph Braybrook, y cada bloque cubría 50 metros cuadrados. Esa escala hace que se reduzca la "resolución" del mapa, dejando una vista aérea mucho más tosca. En cambio, la versión Suiza afina mucho más el detalle gracias a esa escala 1:1.
Sin embargo, lo realmente fascinante de este proyecto es la capacidad que han adquirido juegos como Minecraft para coger grandes volúmenes de geodatos y convertirlos en recreaciones digitales de espacios del mundo real. CartoVoxel toma los datos de calles, plantas de edificios y relieves del terreno reales para generar zonas de Nueva York. Map2Minecraft hace algo parecido usando datos de OpenStreetMap.

articles.title: Six ans après, un smartphone sur dix est toujours sur Android 11
articles.text:
Google ne publie plus de tableau de bord public régulier sur la répartition des versions d’Android depuis 2018. Les seules données officielles se nichent dans Android Studio, son environnement de développement, et une nouvelle fournée vient d’y apparaître à l’occasion de l’Android Dev Summit des 28 et 29 octobre. Elle recense les appareils actifs ayant contacté le Play Store sur une période de sept jours.
Android 16 prend enfin la tête
Android 16 équipe désormais 25,4 % des appareils, contre 7,5 % en décembre 2025, date de la précédente mise à jour de ces statistiques. À l’époque, Android 15 occupait encore la première place, avec 19,3 % du parc. La version lancée en juin 2025 prend désormais la tête, devant Android 14 (15,3 %) et Android 15 (14,7 %). Au total, 56,4 % des smartphones tournent sur Android 14 ou plus récent. Les chantiers engagés par Google pour accélérer les mises à jour, comme Treble et Mainline, qui rendent une partie du système indépendante des constructeurs, finissent par porter leurs fruits.
Android 17, disponible depuis le 16 juin, ne dépasse pas 1 % du parc après plus de quatre mois. Google a certes publié ses chiffres plus tôt dans le cycle que l’an passé. Android 16 avait bénéficié de près de six mois de déploiement avant la photographie de décembre 2025, contre quatre mois et demi pour son successeur aujourd’hui. Android 8.1, sorti en 2017, fait pourtant mieux, à 1,5 %.
Android 11, l’increvable qui embarrasse
Lancé en septembre 2020, Android 11 reste indéboulonnable et équipe encore 10,5 % des appareils actifs. Six ans après sa sortie, il devance Android 12 (9,6 %) et talonne Android 13 (11,8 %). Mises bout à bout, ces lignes signifient que plus de 30 % du parc tourne sur Android 13 ou une version plus ancienne.
Google a cessé le suivi d’Android 13 en mars 2026 : les appareils concernés ne reçoivent plus de correctifs de sa part, sauf geste de leur fabricant. Un smartphone sur dix fonctionne donc avec un système abandonné de longue date, exposé aux failles découvertes depuis. Depuis juin 2025, l’Union européenne impose pourtant aux constructeurs au moins cinq ans de mises à jour de sécurité après la fin de commercialisation d’un modèle. Cette obligation couvre les modèles récents, et laisse de côté le parc ancien déjà en circulation.

articles.title: Cash flow management gets real-time data for lending - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Beyond the books: Real-time data is driving a small-business lending surge
Small businesses have long treated cash flow management as an afterthought, tallying expenses after the money is gone. Now, financial platforms are folding payments, payroll, credit and lending into one system that can see money moving both ways — and predict where it is headed.
That shift puts software providers in direct competition with banks for small-business credit. Intuit Inc. says its view of both sides of the ledger, paired with AI pushing finance toward automation, gives it an edge traditional lenders cannot match, according to Todd Denbo (pictured), senior vice president of lending and commercial leader of Money at Intuit.
“We can see the expenses you’ve got queued up,” Denbo said. “For us, we can effectively predict that you’re going to have a cash flow shortage. That’s why we’ve got our lending businesses as well, so we can proactively offer lines of credit or a term loan to bridge that gap.”
Denbo spoke with theCUBE’s Alison Kosik and Christophe Bertrand at Intuit Connect, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Intuit uses real-time financial data and AI to help small businesses manage cash flow and automate financial tasks. (* Disclosure below.)
Cash flow management meets real-time lending data
Intuit lent about $400 million a year four years ago and almost $7 billion in its most recent fiscal year, according to Denbo. That growth reflects data averaging 625,000 data points per small business across the 10 million companies already on the platform. Because those businesses manage their finances on Intuit’s platform, the company can see money coming in and going out as it happens.
“Most lenders in this space rely on outdated trends that are from the commercial credit bureaus or the personal credit bureaus, or they’re trying to infer data that is just very challenging to infer,” Denbo said. “All of that is real-time.”
Intuit has also added spending data through its QuickBooks-integrated business credit card, which lets owners control employee spending before money leaves. The company has extended QuickBooks into Claude and ChatGPT as well, though automation still stops short of moving money on its own, Denbo explained. AI can handle the financial groundwork while business owners retain the final say over actions involving their money.
“We are gathering the data, we’re analyzing the data, we are packaging a response or a draft,” Denbo said. “But when it comes to anything that is moving money or sending a draft out, that’s where we’re waiting for, effectively, a human intervention.”

articles.text:
Amazon prorroga acesso grátis à Alexa turbinada
Tecnoblog apurou que o chamado “acesso antecipado” à Alexa+ vai até fevereiro de 2027.
Os usuários da Amazon terão mais tempo para testar a Alexa+. O Tecnoblog apurou que a gigante da tecnologia decidiu ampliar o período do chamado acesso antecipado em alguns meses. Com isso, os clientes brasileiros poderão experimentar a nova versão da assistente sem pagar por isso.
O período de degustação estava previsto seguir “pelo menos” até outubro de 2026. Agora, a Amazon confirmou com exclusividade ao Tecnoblog que decidiu expandir o beta pelo menos até fevereiro de 2027.
A empresa declarou que “sempre” enxergou o acesso antecipado “como um período dinâmico, no qual oferecemos aos clientes interessados a oportunidade de experimentar a Alexa+ e compartilhar feedback para nos ajudar a refinar o produto antes da disponibilidade geral”. O posicionamento dá a entender que os feedbacks e ajustes ainda estão acontecendo.
Não custa lembrar, a Alexa+ foi anunciada em fevereiro de 2025, diretamente de um evento em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos. Nós estávamos lá e acompanhamos tudo em primeira mão. Na ocasião, executivos da Amazon explicaram que a nova tecnologia utiliza inteligência artificial generativa para dar respostas mais elaboradas.
Em outras palavras, acabou aquilo de pedir para a Alexa criar um timer, acender as luzes ou pular para a música seguinte.
Eu venho testando a Alexa+ desde a chegada (ainda em beta) no Brasil, com bons experimentos em andamento. A gestão de calendários, conectada à conta Google, está muito mais eficiente. Você pede e assistente consegue ajustar compromissos de acordo com o seu contexto.
Além disso, também é possível conversar sobre as condições meteorológicas. Ela diz se vai chover e recomenda peças de roupa.
Outro avanço da Alexa+ é a conversa mais amigável. Não preciso citar o nome da assistente a todo momento. A partir da primeira interação, é possível fazer perguntas ou dar comandos adicionais como se estivesse num bate-papo.
Por outro lado, o uso de IA generativa pode levar a uma demora maior para certas respostas, em especial quando faço perguntas mais elaboradas. A Alexa+ passa mais tempo “pensando” antes de retornar.
A Alexa+ estará inclusa na assinatura do Amazon Prime, que sai a partir de R$ 19,90 por mês. Também será possível assinar somente a assistente por R$ 99 mensais (condição que não faz sentido nenhum, diga-se de passagem).
Por ora, o cadastro se dá de forma voluntária para quem já é assinante do Prime. É preciso ter um dispositivo compatível, como o Echo Show 5, e entrar na fila de espera.
Com a postergação do acesso antecipado para fevereiro, a Amazon nos contou que não tem uma data para o acesso geral à ferramenta, mas disse que planeja “avisar os clientes com antecedência antes da transição”.

articles.title: Seabirds racing home over the ocean can get jet-lagged
articles.text:
Flying across several time zones often causes jet lag, a feeling when the body insists it’s the middle of the night while the clock says it’s lunchtime. Now it turns out this nuisance is not exclusive to humans.
A new Science study on Manx shearwaters, seabirds that can fly hundreds of kilometers a day over the North Atlantic, shows they jet-lag themselves during their excursions. And because these birds navigate by the Sun, that jet lag leaves a measurable mark—it skews their compass.
Clockwork compass
Patrick Lewin is a behavioral and sensory ecologist at the University of Oxford and lead author of the study. “Manx shearwaters are medium-sized birds, about the same size as a pigeon,” Lewin said. “They are white underneath and black on top, but they have very long wings, and they are closely related to albatross.” Manx shearwaters nest in burrows on coastal islands around the North Atlantic. Most breed around the UK and Ireland, with about half of their population living in Wales.
From there, they head out to feed anywhere from a few dozen to more than 1,000 kilometers into the Atlantic. To get back, shearwaters are thought to work out where they are located using a map sense, possibly based on smells, and then use the Sun as a compass to set their direction.
The trouble with navigating by the Sun, though, is that it moves across the sky. “You can imagine an animal or a human that wants to travel south all day. At sunrise, when the Sun’s in the east, it needs to be traveling 90 degrees clockwise of the Sun, but by midday it needs to be traveling straight towards the Sun, and by sunset it needs to be traveling 90 degrees anticlockwise of the Sun,” Lewin said. Effective navigation by the Sun requires a clock that tells you what time of day it is. Birds, like nearly all animals, have such a clock built in. But the clock in Manx shearwaters is not perfect.

articles.title: WavKong V2700 Takes a Signal-First Approach to Whole-Home Wi-Fi
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
WavKong V2700 Takes a Signal-First Approach to Whole-Home Wi-Fi
WavKong today announced the commercial launch of its V2700 long-range Wi-Fi 6 router following the successful fulfillment of all Kickstarter orders. Its approach to whole-home Wi-Fi is built on a simple principle: Improve the wireless signal at its source, then use the fewest nodes necessary to deliver reliable coverage across even the largest or most complex homes.
From the upstairs bedroom where a daughter streams and studies, to a garage, a backyard gathering, or a security camera on a barn, reliable Wi-Fi should reach the places people actually use—not just the room closest to the router.Developed over six years, WavKong's proprietary RPU (Radio Processing Unit) chip brings base-station-grade digital signal processing to home Wi-Fi. In company testing at a single-story, wood-frame residence in California, one V2700 provided up to 15,000 square feet of combined indoor-outdoor Wi-Fi coverage. WavKong has also tested the router in three-story wood-frame homes in other U.S. states.
The Problem Isn't Always the Internet Plan. It's the Last Stretch of Wi-Fi.
A household can pay for fast broadband and still lose usable speed at the edges of the property. A phone may show a Wi-Fi connection in the garden, yet a video call freezes. A camera on an outbuilding may connect intermittently. A bedroom two floors away may become a daily dead zone.
Mesh networking is an effective way to extend Wi-Fi coverage, especially in homes with challenging layouts. But the best network is not necessarily the one with the most nodes. Each additional wireless point requires thoughtful placement and coordination of radio channels, backhaul and roaming. For households that are not networking experts, getting that design right can be difficult.
WavKong focuses on strengthening the underlying wireless link so fewer nodes may be needed to deliver dependable coverage. In many suitable homes, one V2700 can be enough. Where building materials or layout call for more coverage, two properly positioned V2700 units can work together in a Mesh network to deliver high-speed whole-home Wi-Fi. The goal is not to eliminate Mesh; it is to make the network simpler by needing fewer nodes.
The Technology: Cleaner RF, Not Just More Power
The V2700's RPU targets a fundamental radio-frequency challenge. As a Wi-Fi power amplifier operates at higher output levels, nonlinear distortion can compromise signal quality, limiting the speeds devices can sustain at longer range. Digital predistortion compensates for that distortion before transmission, helping preserve signal linearity.
Digital predistortion (DPD) algorithms have long been used in cellular base stations and satellite communications. WavKong has brought this class of digital RF processing into the 5 GHz radio path of a home Wi-Fi router through its dedicated RPU chip—adding a digital processing core to the radio system to compensate for power-amplifier distortion. Its engineering team brings decades of experience in mobile-communications algorithms, RF systems, and communications-chip development.
In laboratory testing at 160 MHz channel bandwidth and 1024-QAM, DPD improved error vector magnitude (EVM) from approximately -29.3 dB to -41.2 dB, a gain of more than 12 dB. In everyday terms, cleaner RF transmission helps maintain usable speeds farther from the router. Small Chip. Giant Leap.
What the Tests—and Early Users—Show
At a single-story, wood-frame California residence, WavKong tested indoor and outdoor coverage, including a distant garden location where the V2700 measured 123 Mbps, versus 4.2 Mbps for the comparison Mesh configuration. Separate testing in other U.S. states included three-story wood-frame houses, reflecting the different layouts and distances households need Wi-Fi to reach.
Independent real-world comparisons also show why network design matters. Technology creator Jeff Springer compared one V2700 with a well-known Mesh Wi-Fi brand: the V2700 delivered higher speeds than an individual Mesh node at several distant locations. Against the full three-node Mesh setup, the V2700 was faster at two of four test locations, while the Mesh system led at the other two. The point is not that Mesh is inferior; it is that stronger individual wireless links can reduce the number of nodes needed in suitable homes.
Other early users reported meaningful coverage gains. An Australian customer who had used a router plus two Mesh nodes reported 5 GHz downloads exceeding 500 Mbps after switching to V2700, versus about 250 Mbps previously. Another user reported that a previously unreliable smart doorbell became more stable after six weeks of use.
Coverage and speed figures reflect WavKong's internal tests or individual user reports under specific conditions. Actual results vary with walls and building materials, interference, router placement, client capabilities, and network configuration.
From Six Years of Engineering to Global Delivery
The V2700 launched on Kickstarter on April 22, 2026, earning "Project We Love" recognition within its first 24 hours. The campaign attracted 1,074 backers and raised HK$3,272,087 (more than US$400,000). WavKong completed Kickstarter fulfillment on September 29, following product validation, early-user testing, and the start of mass production.
Dr. Ziming Wang, CEO of WavKong"Great Wi-Fi should be invisible. People should enjoy reliable connectivity wherever life happens—upstairs, in the garage, out in the garden, or even at a security camera near the barn—without becoming networking experts," "Wireless performance starts with the quality of the signal, not the number of devices. That is why we went back to the fundamentals of RF engineering, bringing base-station-grade digital signal processing into home Wi-Fi. Our goal is simple: stronger signals, wider coverage, and fewer nodes where possible. Technology should make connectivity effortless, not more complicated."
The V2700 is available through WavKong's official website, with shipping to supported markets. It supports Wi-Fi 6, 160 MHz channel bandwidth, WPA3 security, and router or access-point deployment.
[Editor's note: The WavKong V2700 has an MSRP of US$399]

articles.title: This EcoFlow power station bundle is my pick for easy home backup
articles.text:
This EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic bundle is the home backup battery I’d keep ready for winter storms, and it’s $119 off at Best Buy
A 1,024Wh portable power station that can run fridges, routers, and medical devices during outages
EcoFlow has been a consistent top-performer in our tests, with one model earning the top spot in our guide to portable power stations. High-capacity, durable build, and reliable output are all strong with this line.
So, the EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic with 45W solar panel for $479 (was $598) at Best Buy is an easy recommendation. If a power outage leaves you without heat controls, internet, or a working fridge, the Delta 3 Classic gives you a quiet, fume-free backup you can keep indoors.
• Best for: Professionals, campers, and RV owners who want dependable backup power for outages or portable power on the go.
• Why we like it: Beyond the strong performance in our tests, this EcoFlow model features 1,024Wh of long-life LFP battery capacity, 1,800W of continuous AC output to run big appliances, 3,000 charge cycles, and a five-year warranty. The solar panels for off-grid use sweeten this one considerably for us.
• What you need to know: At $479 it’s good value for the battery alone, though the small panel is more of a bonus for added energy security rather than a serious charging option.
A 1,024Wh portable power station with a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery rated for 3,000 cycles, 1,800W of continuous AC output with a 3,600W peak, and a weight of 26.7 pounds. This bundle includes a 45W solar panel and a protective bag, and it comes with a five-year warranty. EcoFlow sells and ships it through Best Buy’s marketplace.
Why We Recommend It
EcoFlow is one of the biggest names in portable power, and the Delta 3 Classic is a pared-back version of its Delta 3 that keeps the essentials: a large, long-lasting LFP battery and enough output to run a full-size fridge or a space heater for a while. We haven’t tested this model ourselves, so this pick rests on EcoFlow’s track record and our experience testing other models. Expect fast charging, easy of use, and total dependability if you need additional or on-the-move power supply. The five-year warranty adds welcome peace of mind for a product you may rely on in an emergency.
For more top picks, see our guide to the best portable power stations.
Price Context & Historical Value
This is $119, or 20%, off the bundle’s $598 list price, which is a solid discount on a 1kWh power station with a five-year warranty. Keep in mind that the included 45W panel would take more than a full day of ideal sunlight to refill the battery, so think of it as a top-up tool rather than a full-blown charging solution. If you want backup power in place before winter, this is a good time to buy.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic bundle if... you want reliable backup power for outages, you need enough output to run a fridge, router, or CPAP machine, or you value a long-life LFP battery with a five-year warranty.
❌ Skip the EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic bundle if... you plan to rely on solar charging, since a 45W panel is far too small to refill this battery quickly, you need a power station that’s easy to carry long distances at 26.7 pounds, or you’d prefer to buy directly from Best Buy rather than a marketplace seller.
