articles.title: PsiQuantum turns its photonics know-how into an optical switch for supercharging AI data center GPU networks — 8x8 lab prototype loses less light than rivals, with plans to develop larger devices
articles.text:
PsiQuantum turns its photonics know-how into an optical switch for supercharging AI data center GPU networks — 8x8 lab prototype loses less light than rivals, with plans to develop larger devices
Google’s mirror switches have 136 ports; PsiQuantum’s chip has eight, with larger devices in development.
PsiQuantum, a quantum computing company, announced in a release earlier this week that it has turned its low-loss silicon photonics into an optical switch for use in AI data centers. Every optical switch typically comes with loss of light: the more light a switch receives, the less reaches the other side, with the amount of light lost measured in decibels. Typical data center optics can tolerate half the light (3 dB) being lost. PsiQuantum's switch debuted with a demo that typically loses only 1.2 dB of signal, or about a quarter of the light in lab tests, and the all-optical switch can achieve it without an amplifier. The prototype is, however, comparatively small, with eight inputs and outputs (8x8) against competitors’ 32 to 300, but the company says larger devices are in development.
The optical circuit switch (OCS) passes light straight through, from fiber to fiber, without converting it to or from electrical signals. Regular data center switches make that conversion at every hop, which takes power and adds latency. An OCS, instead, uses a fixed light path that it maintains until a change is ordered. Its main penalty comes down to how much light is lost when passing through the switch. PsiQuantum’s switch, which uses circuits etched on a silicon chip with no moving parts, unlike Google’s and Lumentum’s tiny mirrors, or microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), would be used alongside regular packet switches.
Skipping those conversions matters more as AI clusters grow, because moving data between GPUs is quickly becoming a bottleneck. Optics are a high-bandwidth improvement over copper, which has limitations in reach, although a shortage of lasers is a problem for the alternative. Improving communication bandwidth and distance is the goal, so that different racks of GPUs can talk at speed and act as one.
Switches similar to PsiQuantum’s made by Salience Labs and iPronics use built-in amplification and, at least in the former case, are also rated at under 2 dB, or under 37% of the light lost. Google’s mirror-based switch, Palomar, can also typically stay under 2 dB and has 136 ports. Salience’s switch sits at 32 and Lumentum’s at 300, which leaves the eight-port prototype a ways behind on how many fibers it can handle.
| Optical circuit switches by loss and size |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Switch | Ports (in × out) | Insertion loss, and what the figure is | Reconfiguration | How it switches | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PsiQuantum 8×8 demo | 8×8 | 1.2 dB (about 24% of the light lost), typical in the company’s lab tests | Under 3 ms | Silicon photonics chip, no amplification, no moving parts | 
| Google Palomar | 136×136 | Typically under 2 dB (under 37% lost) across all port pairings; 2 dB worst case | Milliseconds | MEMS mirrors (moving parts) | 
| Lumentum R300 | 300×300 | Close to 1.5 dB (about 29% lost), typical at start of life, Lumentum’s switching GM told Gazettabyte | Not stated | MEMS mirrors (moving parts) | 
| Salience Labs OC-32M | 32×32 | Under 2 dB (under 37% lost) port to port, a ceiling, after built-in amplification | Under 300 µs | Silicon photonics chip with amplification | 
| iPronics ONE-32 | 32 (layout not stated) | Not published | Under 300 µs | Silicon photonics chip with optical amplifiers | 
PsiQuantum's switch is an 8x8, meaning eight in and eight out, and “every input can reach every output.” It’s also “strictly non-blocking,” so a new connection never disturbs ones already in place. In the lab, it measured a typical 1.2 dB insertion loss, 40 dB of crosstalk (about 0.01% of the light leaking to other ports), and under 3 ms of reconfiguration time, all of which exceed “initial targets set for these devices.” The loss figure is measured fiber to fiber, which includes getting light onto and off the chip but not connector losses, PsiQuantum told Tom’s Hardware Premium.
The platform loses very little light at each component, which matters because a quantum computer can tolerate only so much lost light. PsiQuantum’s 2025 Nature paper reports silicon nitride waveguides losing as little as 0.5 dB per meter (about 11% of the light per meter), splitters 0.5 millidecibels, and crossings 1.2 millidecibels, the last two a few hundredths of a percent of the light or less each.
The company also says chip-to-fiber coupling has reached about 60 millidecibels, roughly 1.4% of the light lost, in its best published lab results, although without a full fiber array attached. Those figures set a best case, not a worst case, for a 64-port switch, since light crosses more components as ports are added and the losses add up.
How much loss is acceptable varies with the optics at the end of each link. Coherent, an optics maker, says that using an OCS can add “up to 3 dB additional insertion loss,” but its transceivers are able to work with that. Lumentum told Gazettabyte that 3 dB is good enough to work with off-the-shelf FR4, DR4, and DR8 optical modules using the switch; those are the standard plug-in options used to link GPU servers and switches, at distances of 500 meters to 2 kilometers. PsiQuantum’s 8x8 is built for the O-band, the wavelength range those modules use. PsiQuantum told Semafor that, to be workable, its switch needed insertion loss under 2 to 3 dB.
The 8x8 prototype was designed for conventional data center traffic and comes in well below the 3 dB loss target in a request from Nvidia for proposals, the company says. The port count marks it as a demonstration vehicle, but PsiQuantum has a 64x64 version taped out with a 72x72 underway and is “actively developing larger devices.” With crossings that lose so little light, the scale-up might hold. PsiQuantum declined to share details on future products, though it says the loss, which may be slightly higher, will stay very low.
Speed remains less important than insertion loss for how OCSes are currently used. Google, which has the most deployments, numbering in the “tens of thousands,” uses its switches to resize TPU pods or to route around failed chips, a job its “millisecond-scale” MEMS switches handle. PsiQuantum’s under 3 ms is within that class, but Salience and iPronics claim less than 300 microseconds for their amplified chip switches, which iPronics highlights for mid-workload network rewiring to hide the switch time while chips compute.
There is quite a lot of room for speed to improve, and PsiQuantum already has a material for that, used in an existing 64-port switch for its quantum systems, which need to switch light at gigahertz rates. The material, barium titanate (BTO), changes how it bends light when a voltage is applied, and the company chose it over lithium niobate, a more common selection, because BTO had the strongest effect it could find. This keeps switching elements short and losses low at speeds roughly a million times faster than the demo. BTO is “not required for the demonstration vehicle or initial products,” which use a thermally switched silicon nitride platform, but it is “an additional path to faster, more advanced future products.”
An argument for starting now is that building thousands of such switches for conventional applications would reduce the risk for the packaging, assembly, and supply chain of parts PsiQuantum builds for quantum computing. AI and quantum computing are “complementary technologies,” it says, and this is the chance to put its technology into action. When PsiQuantum hired Rob Soderbery as an executive vice president in July, it said he would advance its silicon photonics platform, “accelerating its application across AI networking and other next-generation computing infrastructure,” hinting at the roadmap. The company’s CHIPS award was finalized in September for “high-performance optical switches,” among other components.
Co-founder Pete Shadbolt praised Google’s alternative MEMS switch but would prefer to have similar-quality switching on a monolithic chip that needs no moving parts. Nvidia has a stake through its venture arm, NVentures, and collaborates with PsiQuantum on “GPU-QPU integration,” that is, graphics and quantum processing units, as well as silicon photonics. Nvidia also joined rival iPronics’ $125 million round in September to develop its second-generation optical switch.
Right now, inside Google, OCSes rewire AI clusters, and research firm Cignal AI expects most deployments to stay there through the end of the decade; outside of Google, OCS is still at “proof-of-concept and early trial.” The firm raised its market estimates earlier this year, though, roughly threefold for 2026 and by more than 40% for 2029. An opening exists for PsiQuantum in GPU networks, which ties into Nvidia’s interest, though adoption there is expected to be limited until then. The company says samples and testing kits have already gone to several computing companies, including GPU vendors and hyperscalers.
PsiQuantum should have commercial products “announced in the coming months,” along with updates on larger devices, while competitor Salience has already demonstrated 64 ports at this year’s European Conference on Optical Communication. Salience’s roadmap already has 128- and 256-port products. Scaling is always an issue, but if PsiQuantum’s figures, which haven’t been independently verified, hold up at 64 ports without amplifiers, then larger monolithic OCSes are on the way.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison thinks AI could make us all rich through a universal high income – but governments will need to change
articles.text:
Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison thinks AI could make us all rich through a universal high income – but governments will need to change
Ellison says AI will make the world "healthier and wealthier"
Speaking on-stage at the company's recent AI World conference, Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison declared AI could eventually make everyone "healthier and wealthier".
Apparently unfazed by the technology's impacts on humanity, Ellison does acknowledge that governments need to have a shift in mindset to adapt to this new future.
In a Q&A during the conference's hotly anticipated final keynote, Ellison outlined a future where AI systems and robots could dramatically reduce the cost of goods and services. But rather than accepting the suggestion that AI would end up replacing us all, he argued that the technology would ultimately serve to make us more productive, allowing workers to achieve things that simply weren't possible before.
AI won't replace us, but it will change the economics of work in a lasting way
"I think that's kind of nonsensical," Ellison said about predictions that AI will eventually replace everyone.
The multi-billionaire accepted AI and automation will inevitably displace some jobs, pointing toward rideshare services in a hint to ongoing approval of driverless cars in Las Vegas and other cities.
But he also stressed not all jobs would be impacted equally, revealing his pilot qualifications on-stage and stressing that autopilot hasn't replaced human pilots despite being a decades-old technology.
Although humans will continue to play supervisory roles in many industries (we're already seeing human knowledge worker roles evolve into AI agent managers in some cases), Ellison argued that the overall benefits would be positive, providing governments get involved to support the humans they represent.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Painting a picture of what he meant, he described a hypothetical house being constructed entirely by robots in a scenario where automation had replaced human labor. Whereas human labor would have accounted for, say, 80% of the cost of a house before, four-fifths of the house instantly becomes cheaper because of the impact of automation.
He used this example to set the foundation for the idea of 'universal high income' – a concept already floated by other tech billionaires, including Elon Musk.
Taxation needs to change to enable the provision of a universal income
"We need to change from taxing human labor to taxing value added," he said. "So when the robots add value, all that value that the robots add is taxed, and we could have universal high income."
Universal high income is an evolution of the universal basic income concept, which provides citizens with a regular payment that covers essential living costs. Instead, he suggested that the enormous productivity gains that AI could eventually unlock could create enough wealth to support much higher incomes, despite declining human work activity.
He referenced economist Milton Friedman's negative income tax proposal, describing it as a "reverse income tax" that could help distribute some of the wealth generated by AI.
"The robots are adding value. The government's taxing the value... We all become wealthy as a result."
However, Ellison's vision is a wildly ambitious one that would require a colossal change to today's systems. It would take more than a decade, he admitted. While a future of AI-induced human wealth with less work might sound far-fetched at best in today's economy, Ellison's optimism remains on track.
"All of that is doable," he concluded.

articles.title: Flesh-eating screwworms spread to third state and are attacking pets
articles.text:
For a genuine fright this Halloween, you can turn your gaze to the southern border, where ravenous, flesh-eating maggots are festering and have taken to eating people’s pets.
This week, the country’s New World Screwworm (NWS) infestation spread to a third state, Arizona, which joins New Mexico and Texas in being plagued by the horrifying parasites. To date, 74 animal cases have been identified in the US since the flies re-invaded the country in June.
The flies lay hundreds of eggs in wounds and moist orifices of animals, and the resulting voracious maggots feast on their victims. The maggots resemble screws and tortuously bore and twist into living flesh, causing severe, sometimes fatal wounds, before dropping to the ground to develop into adults.
Because of their ability to ravage livestock, the flies were eliminated from the country in the 1960s through aerial releases of sterile male flies, which thwart successful breeding. For years, they were held at bay using a biological barrier along the Darién Gap at the border of Panama and Colombia. But the barrier was breached in 2022, and the flies have made their way back to the US through Central America.
No one is safe
While they are largely seen as a threat to the livestock industry, they can also devastate wildlife, domestic pets, and in rarer cases, humans. According to the latest data from Mexico’s Ministry of Health, the country has confirmed 806 cases of human screwworm infestations since the flies reemerged. Nine people died from the savage maggots.

articles.title: Reddit Will Protect its "Extremely Valuable Corpus of Data" from Google's AI Search With Forced Logins
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
Reddit Will Protect its "Extremely Valuable Corpus of Data" from Google's AI Search With Forced Logins
Since before the advent of AI-powered web search, Google has leaned heavily on Reddit in particular, often with mixed results, and this was, by-and-large, a mutually beneficial relationship, with Google's AI Overview driving traffic to the forum site. However, as of Reddit's latest Q3 2026 financial results, this arrangement appears to be changing. Following the release of the financial results, there was a Q&A session in which Reddit's CEO, Steve Huffman explained that Reddit would be locking its data behind a login requirement in order to protect it from a changing web landscape.
Web search is evolving from a gateway to the web to becoming an AI-powered destination itself. While extraordinarily useful and powerful, AI search solves a different problem than Reddit. AI does not fulfill people's fundamental need for community, connection, and belonging with other people, and it lacks context and nuance... Logged in and app dial are our most valuable users, and they are our primary focus.
The Reddit experience captures the human experience in a way that no other platform can replicate. Only Reddit can help people navigate life's journey through the lens of other people's lived experiences. Only Reddit can help you feel both like a multifaceted, unique individual and a part of a greater whole, and do so without needing to reveal your real-world identity. That's why Reddit is, and always has been, a distinct and direct destination. People seek out Reddit because we meet a universal need they simply can't get anywhere else online. Our work now is about doubling down on what makes Reddit Reddit, and making Reddit more of a daily habit. We come into that work with clear advantages and revenue momentum in the business, and you can see that in the exceptional commercial results we delivered in the third quarter.
Huffman goes on to explain that Reddit has seen an average decline of over a million weekly referrals from search traffic, and he largely attributes this to Google's changing relationship with the web and how it handles search and referrals. Reddit's shift to a logged-in experience will start rolling out in the US, but the platform will also be testing to see if there is any value in a "lite" version of Reddit that does not require a login.
The biggest impact was on logged out and web traffic, but some of the impact flows through to logged in and app traffic, since search referral is a common source of re-engagement for users. The company helped to offset the declines by both driving reach, primarily through user marketing, and also by continuing to improve the product. These declines have continued into the early part of Q4. During October, we have seen that search traffic has dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week. If this rate of decline continues, current trends would suggest that total DAUq could fall in Q4 by a low double-digit percentage from our current base of 130 million DAUq. However, search referral trends do not determine our relevancy, and they do not define our future. Logged in and app dial are our most valuable users, and they are our primary focus.
Addressing a question about the driver behind the changes, Huffman explained Reddit's view of the repercussions of Google's push for AI Overviews:
Thanks, Josh. On the change from Google, our hypothesis is twofold. The biggest one is the AI Overviews or AI Mode. Both have evolved a lot, and particularly recently, they appear to be expanding them quite aggressively in the U.S. and outside. What started as a feature is now the full search experience, and at the minimum, it pushes everyone down the search page. Then on top of that, the experiences themselves are not traffic drivers. These things combined with the rollout just means Google has really shifted in their relationship with the rest of the internet. There is a second factor, which we believe our machine translation content is also being ranked lower. This primarily would affect us outside the U.S.
Sources:
				Reddit Investors, 				via PC Gamer, 				via Stock Analytics

articles.title: Apple’s Mac mini M4 makes the newer M6 hard to justify
articles.text:
I still think the Mac mini M4 is 'the best small form factor PC in the world' — and it’s $150 off at Best Buy
The cheapest way into the Mac ecosystem
The Apple Mac mini M6 may be catching all the headlines right now, but I still think for most people looking for a stylish and powerful mini PC, the Mac mini M4 is the optimal choice. It might lack the extra oomph of the M6, but for daily office tasks and content creation, it's way better value.
Case in point. The Apple Mac mini M4 is currently $650 (was $799) at Best Buy. If you want a fast, compact desktop for work, photo editing, or everyday use, and you already own a monitor and keyboard, the Mac mini M4 is the best-value Mac you can buy. Meanwhile, Best Buy has the Mac mini M6 for $799 (was $899).
• Best for: Professionals and creators upgrading an older Mac or Windows mini PC to a powerful, near-silent desktop without paying M6 prices. .
• Why we like it: We scored this machine 5 stars in our review, and wondered if it might actually be the best Mac ever. For most people, it will be. Apple’s speedy M4 chip, 16GB of unified memory for smooth multitasking and Apple Intelligence, a tiny five-inch-square design, and handy front-facing USB-C ports and a headphone jack.
A compact desktop with Apple’s M4 chip, 16GB of unified memory, and a 256GB SSD, with front USB-C ports and a headphone jack, plus Thunderbolt, HDMI, and Ethernet on the back. It supports Apple Intelligence and comes in silver.
Why we recommend it
In our Mac mini M4 review, our expert Matt awarded it an Editor’s Choice badge and full marks for value, praising its strong performance, much smaller design, and convenient front ports. He called it the cheapest way into the Mac ecosystem, though he noted it struggles with modern games and that its power button sits awkwardly on the underside. Our review unit had a 512GB SSD rather than this model’s 256GB, but it used the same M4 chip and 16GB of memory.
Price Context & Historical Value
Apple raised the Mac mini’s starting price to $799 earlier this year as memory costs surged, so this $150 discount is measured against Apple’s real current price rather than an inflated list price. It’s still more than the $599 the M4 Mac mini launched at, and well above the sub-$500 deals we saw before the price hike. Given today’s pricing, though, $649 is a strong deal and a good time to buy.
For comparison, the Mac mini M6 is currently down to $799 at Best Buy. For some workloads, it may be better. For general office tasks, the M4 is still worth considering for its value.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Apple Mac mini M4 if... you want an affordable, powerful Mac desktop, you already have a monitor, keyboard, and mouse, or you want a near-silent machine for work, photo editing, or music production.
❌ Skip the Apple Mac mini M4 if... you need lots of local storage, since 256GB fills quickly; you want to play the latest PC games; or you don’t already own a monitor and accessories, which add to the total cost.

| Warranty | 3 years | 
The 27C2A Pro’s core tech is an IPS variant TCL calls HFS Shoot. It combines an ultra-bright FALD backlight with Quantum Dot color and very quick response. Native resolution is 4K 3840x2160 pixels for a density of 163ppi. This is about as fine as it gets unless you move up to 5K or more. And those panels are still quite rare and expensive.
Brightness is honestly reported here, with my tests matching TCL’s claims. I saw almost 650 nits from a full white field pattern in SDR mode with the dimming turned off. HDR ran that up to almost 1,700 nits when I measured a 25% window with dimming on High. At that setting, I couldn’t measure the black levels at all. With 2,304 dimming zones, you won’t see any halo artifacts like panels with just a few hundred zones.
The Quantum Dot layer delivers just over 100% of the DCI-P3 gamut. You also get accurate picture modes with presets for DCI-P3, sRGB, Rec.709, and Adobe RGB, which is something rarely found outside the professional realm. Accuracy is superb with little to no need for calibration. I found similarly good performance in HDR mode, where you can adjust grayscale tracking and brightness if you wish.
The 27C2A Pro offers premium gaming too, with 160 Hz in 4K and 320 Hz in FHD resolution with a dual-mode switch. And there’s precise overdrive, Adaptive-Sync, and MPRT backlight strobing. This is one of the few monitors that lets you use all its video processing options at the same time. You can have MPRT, Adaptive-Sync, and overdrive all active at once.
Styling is outside the norm as well, with a white aesthetic for the stand and panel’s backside. LED lighting shines in the back with two large bracket shapes that show an array of colors and effects. There are gaming aids like reticles, timers, and a frame rate indicator. And you get a full complement of I/O ports with HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, and a USB-C, plus USB for your peripherals.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Assembly and Accessories
The 27C2A Pro ships in blocks of crumbly foam in its three main parts: base, upright, and panel. They assemble without tools. Under the snap-on fulcrum is a 100mm VESA mount with fasteners included if you'd rather use an arm, and you might want to after you read the next section of this review. The power supply is an external brick, and you get cables for DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-A/B, and USB-C.
Product 360
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
I said the 27C2A Pro is a white monitor, but from the front, everything is black except the base. This is good for distraction-free use, especially in low-light situations where you want to stay focused on the image. There’s plenty of white plastic in the back, though, on the stand and on the panel.
The back features ventilation across the top and two large LED banks shaped like reversed parentheses. The shapes are angular with soft corners and no sharp edges. The screen has a flush bezel 9mm thick on the top and sides with a 15mm strip across the bottom. All you see there is a tiny TCL logo. The control joystick is underneath the center and is backlit.
The stand offers full ergonomics with 5/15 degrees tilt, 20 degrees swivel, and a 90-degree portrait mode. The height range is 4.8 inches. This was my only complaint about the 27C2A Pro. Though the base and upright are solid together, the panel’s fulcrum point is very small and wobbly, which makes positioning it difficult. If you game intensely and have your keyboard on the desk, it will jiggle a bit.
Up and under the center is a well-stocked I/O panel with one DisplayPort 1.4, two HDMI 2.1, and a USB-C with 90 watts of power. You also get one upstream and two downstream USB 3.0 ports. There is a pair of five-watt internal speakers, and you get a 3.5mm headphone jack.
OSD Features
In 4K resolution, the 27C2A Pro’s OSD is very small. It was hard to read the tiny text unless I got up close. The FHD version is larger, of course. Press the joystick and click left to summon it.

View Original
Player mode refers to the nine picture modes you see in the first photo above. All you need is the default one, Standard, and I’ll tell you why in a moment.
Moving on to Game Settings, the 27C2A Pro has every video processing option currently available for an LCD panel. The overdrive has three speeds, with fast being the best. MPRT-Plus (backlight strobe) has two levels, which correspond to pulse width. The higher one cuts brightness by around 50%, but you can easily compensate with the brightness slider because there’s more than enough luminance headroom. You can use both with Adaptive-Sync if you wish, which is something very few monitors can do. I found the best motion quality with overdrive on Fast and Adaptive-Sync engaged. MPRT reduces motion blur to almost nothing but introduces a slight phasing artifact, so I didn’t use it for my gaming tests. Also in this menu are a set of aiming points, timers, and controls for the LED lighting.
The Display menu starts with Local Dimming and its three levels. Standard barely does anything, only increasing contrast to around 1,800:1. Medium and High are more aggressive, and they shut off the backlight completely at light level zero for theoretically infinite contrast. Dimming is available for both SDR and HDR content.
In the Color menu, you’ll find color temp presets and a gamut selector. It offers sRGB, Rec.709, DCI-P3, and Adobe RGB. All are very accurate, more so than the Original option, in fact. You’ll see how this works in my tests on page four. The 27C2A Pro is a very accurate monitor when set up correctly.
The remainder of the OSD is focused on conveniences like PIP/PBP, KVM options, OSD controls, and the like. If you want to reset everything to factory defaults, that option is in the Settings menu.
TCL 27C2A Pro Calibration Settings
I was initially disappointed with the 27C2A Pro during my first round of tests. It comes set to Standard mode, Original color space, warm color temp, and gamma 1. Gamma and grayscale measured well, but color tracking was a bit wonky. Luckily, you can select any of the available gamuts, sRGB, Rec.709, DCI-P3, or Adobe RGB, and get much better accuracy with near-perfect gamma and grayscale. I made small tweaks to the RGB sliders, and that was it. My settings are below.
In HDR mode, you get two presets, Display and Cinema. Their color is the same, but the EOTF curves are slightly different. My pick was Display, and with that, you get RGB sliders and a brightness control. You can also change the local dimming, though I recommend High for the deepest blacks and best contrast.
| Picture Mode | Standard | 
| Brightness 200 nits | 43 | 
| Brightness 120 nits | 21 | 
| Brightness 100 nits | 17 | 
| Brightness 80 nits | 11 | 
| Brightness 50 nits | 4 (min. 39 nits) | 
| Contrast | 50 | 
| Gamma | 1 | 
| Color Space | DCI-P3, Rec.709, sRGB, Adobe RGB | 
| Color Temp User | Red 49, Green 49, Blue 51 | 
Gaming and Hands-on
Gaming on the 27C2A Pro was a treat. I’m spoiled by premium OLEDs, but TCL has found a great combination of brightness, color, speed, and smoothness that mostly replicates that experience with an LCD panel. The only thing you won’t get is those infinite blacks, but the 27C2A Pro comes close with its 2,304 dimming zones and extremely bright highlights.
You’ll see later in the test notes just how bright it can get, and that capability is used to full effect. I always set up review displays to 200 nits, and that was only a third of the 27C2A Pro’s SDR brightness range. I found that I could use its local dimming for both SDR and HDR content, which was nice. Often, there is only dimming for HDR.
Color was also a strength, with vivid hues and excellent accuracy. I found some unusual behavior during initial tests, but once I discovered the secret, it was pro-level color all the way. Just pick the gamut you want and avoid the Original option in the OSD’s color space menu.
My GeForce RTX 4090-equipped PC had no problem maintaining 160fps in 4K. I tried the FHD/320 Hz option and found that it worked fine and delivered that frame rate. Since the downscale is an exact multiple, the picture wasn’t as soft as you might expect. The dual-mode feature is a viable option for users with consoles or less stout video cards.
I also noted that I could use overdrive and MPRT backlight strobing in concert with Adaptive-Sync. That’s something only a few high-end monitors offer, so it was nice to see from a $600 display. If you’re relegated to frame rates below 144 Hz, MPRT is a good option for eliminating motion blur. The overdrive on its own is also very effective at its middle setting, Fast.
Lag was low enough that I didn’t perceive any delay in control response. Backgrounds and moving objects stayed sharp, and my inputs were instantly translated to action. The 27C2A Pro has that addictive quality that all fast and smooth monitors have.
For productivity, the 27C2A Pro shines as a photo and graphics display. Its color modes include sRGB, Rec.709, DCI-P3, and Adobe RGB. That last one is a rarity outside the professional realm. They are spot-on, as you’ll see in my test results; no calibration needed. If you need a print reference monitor, this one qualifies.
I also noted that the 27C2A Pro is a complete package with LED lighting, internal speakers, USB ports with KVM, and a slick white aesthetic. My only complaint is that the stand is too wobbly. The base and upright are solid, but the panel’s attachment point has some jiggle. I would probably spend some of the money I saved over an OLED on an arm.
Takeaway: The 27C2A Pro is a complete package for gaming and productivity. It’s fast and smooth with excellent video processing and the ability to run Adaptive-Sync along with overdrive and backlight strobing. It’s colorful and sharp and has deep contrast thanks to 2,304 local dimming zones. It’s also much brighter than any OLED. It delivers tremendous bang for the buck.

articles.title: Home Battery vs Generator vs Grid: What Keeps Your Home Running in a Blackout? - Tech Guide
articles.text:
A blackout can occur at any time, without warning. There are several reasons for a blackout, such as issues with the electrical grid, severe weather, and other local problems. When the electricity goes out, home appliances stop working. To maintain your daily routine during a blackout, a backup power supply can help you run your home appliances.
To prevent a home from a blackout, there are three options: an electricity grid, a solar battery, and a backup generator. These three options work completely differently from one another.
Does Solar Power Work During a Blackout?
Yes, solar power works during a blackout, but only when you add a solar battery to your solar system. Most homeowners misunderstand that installing solar panels automatically means energy independence, but it’s true if you pair your rooftop panels with a solar battery from a trusted solar panel installer like Solar 365.
In general, when solar systems are grid-connected, the solar inverter shuts down when the grid goes offline for safety reasons. To prevent electricity from being sent back into the network while electrical workers are doing line work or repairing electrical wires in any other area.
To provide home backup, a solar system needs a suitably sized battery and backup equipment installed by a licensed solar panel installer, capable of safely disconnecting the home or property from the grid.
This is where batteries and generators can become useful.
Solar Battery Backup
A solar battery stores excess electricity generated by solar panels and is used when electricity is needed to support your normal operations.
A battery can continue supplying electricity to selected circuits or appliances when the grid goes down.
Advantages of a home battery
- Quiet operation
- No fuel required
- Can charge from rooftop solar
- Can provide automatic backup when properly installed
- Can reduce reliance on the grid
- Can be used every day, not only during blackouts
The amount of electricity for backup depends on your solar battery’s usable capacity and household energy consumption.
For example, a household using only essential appliances during an outage will generally get more backup time from the same battery than a household running air conditioning, electric cooking, heating, and other high-demand appliances.
A battery works with compatible solar inverter and equipments. Not only does a solar battery provide backup to your property.
Backup Generator
A generator produces electricity by using an external fossil fuel source, such as petrol, diesel, or gas, depending on the generator type.
Unlike a solar battery, a generator does not store electricity. It generates electricity by burning fossil fuels, which costs you money and affects the environment.
Advantages of a generator
- Can provide power for extended periods with sufficient fuel
- Suitable for higher electricity loads depending on generator capacity
- Does not depend on sunlight
- Can be useful when an outage lasts longer than expected
However, generators also have some disadvantages.
They can be noisy, require regular maintenance, and need fuel storage and refueling. They also produce exhaust gases.
Generators require a suitable area to produce electricity, whereas a solar battery can be installed indoors or outdoors, depending on your requirements. But the generator should be positioned in a safe, well-ventilated location.
What About the Electricity Grid?
The electricity grid is used every day and remains the primary source of power for most connected homes.
It provides continuous electricity without homeowners needing to manage fuel or battery capacity. However, a standard grid connection cannot supply electricity when the network itself is experiencing an outage.
This means the grid and backup systems serve different purposes.
The grid is designed for everyday supply, while a battery or generator can provide an alternative source when the grid is unavailable.
Home Battery vs Generator vs Grid
There isn’t one solution that is best for every household.
| Feature | Home Battery | Generator | Grid | 
| Works during blackout | Yes, with a suitable backup setup | Yes | No | 
| Fuel required | No | Yes | No | 
| Noise | Very low | Can be noisy | None at home | 
| Can recharge from solar, applicable | Yes, depending on the system | No | Not applicable | 
| Long-duration backup | Depends on capacity and charging | Yes, with fuel | Not during the outage | 
| Everyday use | Yes | Usually backup only | Yes | 
A solar battery is useful for every household that has installed a solar system and wants to use solar power and reduce its dependence on the grid.
A generator may be more suitable for situations where long-duration backup is the priority and fuel availability is not a major concern.
Some properties may even use more than one backup method depending on their electricity requirements.
What Appliances Should You Keep Running?
Backup power does not always need to supply the entire house.
Many homeowners choose to prioritize essential loads such as:
- Refrigerator and freezer
- Lights
- Internet equipment
- Security systems
- Garage doors
- Selected power outlets
- Essential medical equipment
- Some heating or cooling equipment
High-power appliances such as electric ovens, large air conditioners, hot-water systems, and pool pumps can consume considerably more electricity.
Knowing which appliances are essential can help determine the amount of backup capacity.
How Long Can a Home Battery Run During a Blackout?
There is no single answer because it depends on the battery capacity and the home’s electricity consumption.
For example, a battery might last considerably longer if it is supplying a refrigerator, lights, and internet equipment than if it is also powering an air conditioner and electric hot-water system.
A simple way to think about it is:
Backup time = usable battery capacity ÷ average power consumption
Actual performance can vary because of inverter efficiency, battery reserve settings, appliance start-up loads, and other system limitations.
Which Backup Option Is Right for Your Home?
The choice among a battery, a generator, and a grid connection depends on what you are trying to achieve.
If your main priority is everyday energy management and blackout protection, a suitably configured home battery can provide both.
If your priority is keeping a property powered through a long outage, a generator may offer a practical alternative.
For normal operation, the electricity grid remains the simplest power source when available.
The most important thing is to understand how the system will behave before a blackout occurs. Check which circuits are backed up, how much power the system can provide, how long it is expected to operate, and whether solar can recharge the battery during an outage.
A backup system is only useful during a blackout if it has been properly designed, installed, and configured for that purpose.

articles.title: L'ancien patron d'Intel croit avoir trouvé une solution à la crise de la RAM
articles.text:
Avec le soutien de Pat Gelsinger, Nagare Labs développe une mémoire qui pourrait offrir cinq fois plus de capacité sur une même surface. Une promesse encore expérimentale, dont la commercialisation pourrait prendre de nombreuses années.
La crise des composants mémoire et la hausse des prix continuent d'impacter durement les divers appareils informatiques grand public. Smartphones, tablettes, PC… Tout a augmenté, même les consoles ! Cette crise, pas près de se terminer, pourrait toutefois trouver une issue grâce à une nouvelle technologie baptisée Z2RAM.
Développée par Nagare Labs, une entreprise cofondée par les professeurs Suman Datta et Shimeng Yu du Georgia Institute of Technology, elle bénéficie d'un financement de 5 millions de dollars mené par Playground Global, dont Pat Gelsinger, ancien PDG d'Intel, est un associé.
Une architecture combinant trois technologies de mémoire
La Z2RAM ambitionne de réunir la rapidité de la SRAM, la densité de la DRAM et les possibilités d'empilement vertical de la NAND, avec une consommation énergétique réduite et une fabrication nettement simplifiée.
La SRAM, utilisée dans les caches des processeurs, est rapide mais occupe beaucoup de place. La DRAM, utilisée dans les si chères barrettes de RAM, offre une densité supérieure, mais une vitesse moindre. Quant à la NAND des SSD, elle privilégie la densité grâce à son empilement vertical, au détriment des performances.
Contrairement à la DRAM traditionnelle, qui exploite un transistor et un condensateur par bit, la Z2RAM repose quant à elle sur deux transistors. La charge est stockée dans la capacité du second, supprimant le condensateur physique. Cette architecture autorise également une lecture non destructrice, sans réécriture systématique des données.
Nagare Labs prévoit de fabriquer plusieurs couches de mémoire sur une même puce, puis de relier celle-ci à la puce de calcul par collage hybride, une technique déjà employée par AMD pour le 3D V-Cache. Selon l'entreprise, cette conception offrirait une densité plus de cinq fois supérieure à celle de la SRAM, à bande passante équivalente. À surface équivalente, une zone qui accueille actuellement 64 Mo de SRAM pourrait alors contenir 320 Mo de Z2RAM.
Des applications ciblées sur l'intelligence artificielle
Alors, tout le monde va devoir changer les barrettes de mémoire de son PC ? Absolument pas, loin du grand public, cette technologie vise principalement les datacenters dédiés à l'intelligence artificielle. Ces derniers sont contraints à certaines limites de bande passante mémoire et de capacité.
Les LPU de Groq 3 de NVIDIA embarquent environ 500 Mo de SRAM par puce. Une mémoire plus dense pourrait permettre de répartir certains grands modèles sur moins d’accélérateurs, mais l’ampleur de ce gain reste à démontrer.
Une commercialisation encore lointaine
La Z2RAM demeure au stade des prototypes de laboratoire. Nagare Labs recherche un partenaire industriel pour poursuivre son développement et vise des premiers exemplaires fonctionnels d'ici quatre ans. La commercialisation pourrait toutefois prendre une dizaine d'années.
Des obstacles subsistent concernant la fiabilité des semi-conducteurs à oxyde et l'absence d'interface standardisée pour les accélérateurs. Nagare Labs pourrait donc devoir développer sa propre solution.
Pour Pat Gelsinger, ancien PDG d'Intel, l'expansion des infrastructures d'IA favorise l'émergence de nouvelles mémoires. Si la Z2RAM n'est pas la réponse immédiate aux pénuries de RAM pour le grand public, son potentiel développement pourrait libérer certaines lignes de production, afin de retrouver une offre et un tarif corrects pour nos tablettes, smartphones, et ordinateurs personnels.
Source : NeoWin

articles.title: Il remplace l'autocuiseur et l'air fryer : le Ninja Foodi avec SmartLid est à -55 % jusqu'à ce soir — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le Ninja Foodi Multicuiseur avec SmartLid joue un peu les Transformers de la cuisine. Son couvercle unique change de mode grâce à un simple curseur. Vous passez ainsi de l’autocuiseur à la friteuse sans huile sans toucher à rien d’autre. Avec ses 11 modes de cuisson, il vise clairement ceux qui veulent libérer le plan de travail de deux ou trois appareils. Bonne nouvelle, Amazon le fait passer sous les 150 euros en avant-première du Black Friday, jusqu’à ce samedi 31 octobre au soir.
Les atouts du Ninja Foodi Multicuiseur avec SmartLid
- 11 modes de cuisson, dont autocuiseur, friteuse sans huile et yaourt
- Un couvercle SmartLid unique piloté par un simple curseur
- Une cuve antiadhésive de 6 litres, passant au lave-vaisselle
Affiché habituellement à 329,99 euros, le Ninja Foodi avec SmartLid descend à 149 euros chez Amazon. Cela représente une remise de 55 % sur le prix de référence. Il faut faire vite, l’offre s’arrête ce samedi 31 octobre au soir.
Un couvercle pour les gouverner tous
Tout le principe du SmartLid tient dans un curseur posé sur le couvercle. Vous le faites glisser, et paf, l’appareil bascule entre trois familles de cuisson : sous pression, Combi-vapeur (la vapeur combinée à la convection) et friture à l’air. Aucun second couvercle à ranger dans un placard déjà plein. Franchement, c’est un bon point pour une cuisine où la place est comptée.
Dans le détail, la liste des modes est longue : cuisson sous pression, friture à l’air, gril, four, déshydratation, saisie, vapeur, mijotage et même yaourt, plus deux programmes Combi-vapeur (vapeur + four et vapeur + friture à l’air). Ninja livre aussi un panier Cook & Crisp de 3,7 litres pour les frites et autres plats croustillants, une grille réversible et un guide de recettes. Bon, avec autant de modes, comptez quand même quelques essais avant de trouver vos réglages.
Six litres pour quatre, et une place à lui trouver
Ninja annonce une cuisson sous pression jusqu’à 70 % plus rapide qu’une cuisson lente, à feu doux ou en braisage. Pour un bœuf bourguignon un mardi soir, ça peut carrément changer la donne, même s’il faut ajouter le temps de montée en pression et de décompression. En friture à l’air, la marque revendique jusqu’à 75 % de matières grasses en moins face à des frites cuites dans l’huile.
La cuve de 6 litres permet de nourrir jusqu’à quatre personnes, selon Ninja. Au-delà, il faudra enchaîner les fournées, surtout en mode friture où le panier se limite à 3,7 litres. L’autre limite tient à son gabarit, 36 x 35 x 33 centimètres pour 10,7 kilogrammes. Le sortir du placard tous les soirs tourne vite à la séance de musculation. articles.title: Diving into the PROLED MacBook and the $15M Rogers fine [SyrupCast]
articles.text:
On this episode of the SyrupCast, EIC Jon Lamont and devices editor Dean Daley dive into the new MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR display, along with some of the other new Apple hardware.
We talk about the PROLED XDR, its exuberant Canadian price tag, the light-up logo, and we wonder why bother with a touch screen after all these years. We also quickly go over all of the new Apple devices like the iPad mini, iMac M6 and MacBook Pro M6.
Later, they dive into the flurry of telecom news this week, which included news about a new hold time petition, the Canadian Government’s plan to increase telecom competition, Rogers shifting auto-pay to only Rogers’ credit card owners, and pre-authorized debit cards. Of course, they also touched on everything from the $15M Rogers fine for deceptive unlimited plans.
Tune into this week’s episode of the SyrupCast.

articles.title: Patient Records on Shared Tablets: Privacy Basics for Clinics and Small Health Practices - Tech Guide
articles.text:
In today’s healthcare environment, the use of shared tablets in clinics and small health practices is becoming increasingly common. These devices offer convenience and efficiency, allowing healthcare professionals to access patient records quickly and provide timely care. However, with these benefits come significant privacy challenges. Ensuring patient data remains secure on shared tablets is critical to maintaining trust, complying with regulations, and protecting sensitive health information.
More clinics and small health practices are turning to shared tablets to improve workflow and reduce paperwork. According to a 2023 survey by the Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society (HIMSS), 68% of small healthcare providers reported using mobile devices such as tablets for patient data access, up from 45% in 2019. This rapid adoption highlights the importance of understanding and managing the privacy risks associated with shared device usage.
Healthcare providers are legally obligated to protect patient data under regulations such as HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) in the United States and similar privacy laws worldwide. Compliance requires organizations to implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards to secure electronic protected health information (ePHI).
Understanding these requirements can be daunting for smaller practices with limited IT resources. Leveraging resources like True North’s experts on HIPAA can provide valuable guidance on meeting HIPAA obligations effectively.
Understanding Privacy Risks with Shared Tablets
Shared tablets can be a double-edged sword. While they enable multiple staff members to access patient information seamlessly, they also create opportunities for data breaches if not properly managed. Some of the primary risks include:
– Unauthorized Access: Without stringent access controls, anyone with physical access to a tablet could potentially view sensitive patient information.
– Data Leakage: Shared devices increase the chances of accidental data exposure or intentional misuse, especially when multiple users log in and out frequently.
– Inadequate Device Security: Tablets that lack encryption, strong authentication, or regular updates are vulnerable to hacking and malware attacks.
These risks are amplified in small health practices where IT resources and security oversight may be limited. For example, a 2022 report found that 43% of small healthcare providers experienced at least one data breach linked to mobile device vulnerabilities. This statistic underscores the urgent need for effective privacy safeguards on shared tablets.
Best Practices for Securing Patient Records on Shared Tablets
To mitigate privacy risks, clinics and small health practices should adopt a comprehensive approach that includes technical controls, policies, and staff training. Below are some essential best practices:
- User Authentication and Access Control
Implement strict user authentication mechanisms such as unique usernames and strong passwords or biometric verification. Role-based access controls ensure that users can only access the information necessary to perform their duties, reducing the risk of unauthorized data exposure.
- Device Encryption
Encrypting data stored on tablets protects patient records even if a device is lost or stolen. Full disk encryption or encrypted containers for healthcare applications can prevent unauthorized users from accessing sensitive information.
- Automatic Logouts and Session Timeouts
Configure tablets to log users out automatically after a period of inactivity. This limits the window during which an unattended device could be accessed by the wrong person.
- Regular Software Updates and Patch Management
Keeping the tablet’s operating system and applications up to date is critical to defending against vulnerabilities and exploits. Establishing a routine patch management process helps maintain security integrity.
- Secure Network Connections
When accessing patient records remotely or through wireless networks, ensure that connections are protected using VPNs or encrypted Wi-Fi protocols. Public or unsecured networks should be avoided to prevent interception of data.
- Employee Training and Awareness
Staff must understand the importance of patient privacy and the specific procedures for using shared tablets securely. Regular training sessions can reinforce best practices and highlight emerging threats.
- Managed IT Support
Many small health practices lack the capacity to manage complex IT security needs internally. Partnering with a reliable managed service provider can make a significant difference. For example, practices that choose UV&S to handle IT benefit from expert management of their IT infrastructure, proactive monitoring, and rapid response to security incidents.
The Importance of Training and Culture in Privacy Protection
Beyond technical controls, fostering a culture of privacy awareness among clinic staff is crucial. Human error remains one of the leading causes of data breaches in healthcare. A 2021 study found that 27% of healthcare data breaches were due to employee negligence or mistakes.
Regular training programs tailored to the specific workflows of clinics and small practices can empower staff to recognize phishing attempts, properly handle shared devices, and follow logout protocols diligently. Encouraging an environment where privacy concerns can be reported without fear of reprisal also helps identify and address vulnerabilities proactively.
Case Study: How a Small Clinic Enhanced Privacy on Shared Tablets
Consider a small clinic that transitioned to using shared tablets for patient record access during consultations. Initially, the clinic faced challenges such as inconsistent logout habits and outdated software, leading to several near-miss privacy incidents. By implementing a multi-layered security approach-including user authentication, automatic logouts, and encryption-the clinic significantly reduced risks.
Additionally, the clinic engaged a managed IT services provider to oversee device updates, monitor network security, and provide ongoing staff training. This partnership ensured continuous compliance with privacy regulations and improved overall data protection.
The clinic also adopted mobile device management (MDM) software, allowing remote enforcement of security policies and rapid response in case of device loss. As a result, the clinic reported zero data breaches related to shared tablet use over the following 18 months, demonstrating the effectiveness of a comprehensive privacy strategy.
The Role of Technology in Supporting Privacy
Emerging technologies can further enhance privacy on shared tablets. For instance, mobile device management (MDM) solutions allow clinics to enforce security policies remotely, track device usage, and wipe data if a tablet is lost or compromised. Biometric authentication methods, such as fingerprint or facial recognition, offer convenient yet secure access controls.
Artificial intelligence (AI) tools also assist in detecting unusual access patterns or potential breaches, enabling rapid intervention before patient data is exposed. AI-driven analytics can flag anomalous login attempts or data downloads, helping clinics respond proactively to threats.
Investing in these technologies not only strengthens security but also supports compliance with evolving regulatory requirements, which increasingly emphasize proactive risk management.
Measuring the Impact of Privacy Improvements
Investing in privacy controls for shared tablets is not only a compliance necessity but also a business imperative. According to a report by IBM, the average cost of a healthcare data breach reached $10.1 million in 2022, underscoring the financial risks associated with inadequate data security. Additionally, 89% of patients surveyed expressed concern about the privacy of their electronic health records, indicating that strong privacy protections can improve patient trust and retention.
Beyond cost avoidance, clinics that demonstrate a commitment to protecting patient information often see increased patient satisfaction and loyalty. Privacy is a key factor in patient choice of healthcare providers, especially for sensitive health issues.
By proactively addressing privacy on shared tablets, clinics and small health practices can avoid costly breaches and enhance their reputation for safeguarding patient information.
Conclusion
Shared tablets offer undeniable advantages in streamlining healthcare delivery, but they also introduce significant privacy challenges that clinics and small health practices must address. Adhering to regulatory requirements, implementing robust security measures, and partnering with knowledgeable IT professionals are critical steps to protect patient records effectively.
Utilizing resources like for compliance expertise and for managed IT support can empower healthcare providers to navigate the complex landscape of data privacy confidently. Ultimately, safeguarding patient information on shared devices is essential for fostering trust, ensuring regulatory compliance, and delivering high-quality care in today’s digital healthcare environment.

articles.title: Bill Gates (70 años), fundador de Microsoft, advierte sobre la IA: "Nunca ha existido un arma tan poderosa" y exige límites obligatorios por seguridad
articles.text:
La IA está avanzando a tal velocidad que plantea nuevas dificultades para controlar sus posibles usos maliciosos. Aunque las grandes compañías tecnológicas continúan desarrollando modelos cada vez más capaces, algunas de las figuras más importantes de la industria consideran que confiar exclusivamente en las empresas para garantizar su seguridad ya no es suficiente, y Bill Gates ha sido el último en sumarse a esta corriente.
El cofundador de Microsoft habló sobre esta cuestión en una entrevista concedida a NBC News en la que reclamó una mayor intervención de los gobiernos. Así, el empresario considera imprescindible establecer mecanismos de vigilancia y protección que las compañías estén obligadas a incorporar en sus sistemas.
Bill Gates cree que las empresas no pueden controlar la IA por sí solas
Durante la conversación, Gates aseguró que "nadie piensa que la autorregulación sea suficiente". Para el empresario, tanto los responsables políticos como las fuerzas de seguridad deben participar en la definición de las medidas de protección, sobre todo si existe la posibilidad de que estas herramientas se utilicen para cometer delitos o desarrollar ataques informáticos.
Cuando habla de las consecuencias que podría tener un uso malintencionado de la tecnología, su advertencia va un paso más lejos. Gates defiende que nunca ha existido un arma tan poderosa como la combinación de personas con malas intenciones y herramientas avanzadas de IA, así que menciona riesgos como los ciberataques contra infraestructuras como resultado de esto. Además, también habla de la posibilidad de que grupos pequeños adquieran capacidades que antes estaban reservadas a grandes Estados.
Pese a todo lo que compartió, Gates no propone paralizar el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial. De hecho, su planteamiento consiste en incorporar sistemas de supervisión que permitan conocer qué están haciendo los modelos mientras se establecen medidas de seguridad obligatorias. Tal y como detalló, estas exigencias supondrían un coste adicional para las empresas sin frenar de forma considerable sus avances.
La dificultad estará en conseguir que gobiernos y compañías adopten criterios comunes, especialmente en un contexto de competencia tecnológica internacional. Gates considera que alcanzar acuerdos globales podría resultar incluso más complicado que las negociaciones sobre armamento nuclear durante la Guerra Fría. Su advertencia apunta a una cuestión fundamental para el futuro de la inteligencia artificial: quién debe supervisar sus capacidades y hasta dónde debería permitirse que actúe sin intervención humana.

articles.title: Qué hacer si la pantalla del iPhone Duo se rompió o dejó de funcionar: Apple inicia la reparación
articles.text:
Apple reconoció que algunas unidades del iPhone Duo presentan fallas en su pantalla plegable interna, un problema que puede provocar la aparición de grietas y una línea brillante que atraviesa el panel desde el centro hacia el lado derecho. Ante los reportes de los primeros compradores, la compañía recomendó a los usuarios afectados comunicarse con su servicio de atención AppleCare para gestionar el reemplazo del dispositivo.
La empresa confirmó el inconveniente después de recibir consultas de medios especializados como Bloomberg y 9to5Mac. En un comunicado compartido por Alex Kirschner, vocero de Apple, con The Verge, señaló que está al tanto de un defecto que afecta a un número reducido de equipos.
La compañía también aclaró que la mayoría de los iPhone Duo no presenta este problema y que, en los dispositivos afectados, las fallas suelen manifestarse rápidamente. Por ello, quienes detecten anomalías en el panel interno deben iniciar el procedimiento de atención técnica en lugar de continuar utilizando el teléfono con normalidad.
Qué falla en la pantalla plegable del iPhone Duo
Los primeros reportes de usuarios describen un comportamiento similar: la bisagra del dispositivo comienza a sentirse más rígida de lo habitual y, al desplegar el teléfono, aparecen grietas en la pantalla interna acompañadas de una línea luminosa.
Este defecto afecta al panel flexible, uno de los componentes más importantes del primer celular plegable de Apple. A diferencia de los teléfonos tradicionales, el iPhone Duo incorpora una pantalla que debe doblarse cada vez que el usuario abre o cierra el equipo.
El problema también fue analizado por iFixit, sitio especializado en reparaciones y desmontaje de dispositivos electrónicos. Durante una revisión del teléfono, sus especialistas plantearon que la pantalla podría estar ejerciendo presión contra una barra ubicada en la zona central de la estructura. Esta interacción podría explicar las marcas y daños detectados en algunas unidades.
Sin embargo, esta explicación corresponde a una hipótesis técnica del sitio y no a una causa confirmada oficialmente por Apple.
La compañía indicó que los usuarios con problemas deben contactar a AppleCare para solicitar un reemplazo. Incluso se conoció el caso de un comprador en Australia que recibió otro equipo directamente en una tienda Apple Store.
Cómo solicitar un reemplazo del iPhone Duo
Los propietarios que detecten grietas, líneas brillantes o problemas de funcionamiento en la pantalla interna pueden iniciar el proceso mediante tres canales oficiales.
1. Desde la aplicación Soporte de Apple
Una de las alternativas es utilizar la aplicación Soporte de Apple, disponible en la App Store. El procedimiento puede realizarse desde el propio iPhone Duo, utilizando su pantalla externa, o desde otro dispositivo Apple asociado a la misma cuenta.
Una vez dentro de la aplicación, se debe seleccionar el teléfono en la lista de dispositivos y acceder a la categoría «Reparaciones y daño físico». Después, hay que elegir «Daño de pantalla» o «La pantalla no funciona como debería».
El último paso consiste en solicitar atención mediante un chat o programar una llamada con un asesor de Apple.
2. Desde la página web de soporte
Otra opción es ingresar al portal oficial de soporte técnico de Apple e iniciar sesión con el Apple ID. Allí se debe seleccionar el iPhone Duo, buscar la sección relacionada con el hardware o la pantalla y comenzar una solicitud de reparación.
El sistema puede ofrecer una llamada telefónica con un especialista o permitir que el usuario programe una cita en un centro de servicio autorizado.
3. Mediante una llamada telefónica
Los usuarios también pueden comunicarse directamente con el servicio de atención de Apple. Durante la conversación, es importante describir si el problema apareció espontáneamente en el pliegue central o si se manifiesta mediante grietas y líneas luminosas.
Esto permitirá que el asesor identifique el inconveniente y determine el procedimiento correspondiente para el modelo.
Qué ocurre si el usuario tiene AppleCare+
Los propietarios que cuentan con una suscripción activa a AppleCare+ pueden consultar por el Servicio de reemplazo exprés, una modalidad que permite recibir otro dispositivo antes de enviar el equipo defectuoso.
En este caso, Apple despacha un iPhone Duo de reemplazo y proporciona el embalaje y las etiquetas necesarias para devolver el teléfono afectado por correo. Así, el usuario puede continuar utilizando un dispositivo mientras se completa el procedimiento.
La disponibilidad y las condiciones del servicio dependen de la cobertura contratada y de las condiciones aplicables en cada país.
Por ahora, Apple no ha informado cuántas unidades presentan el defecto ni ha detallado si realizará cambios adicionales en la fabricación del dispositivo. La compañía sostiene que se trata de un problema limitado a una pequeña cantidad de equipos y recomienda acudir a AppleCare para recibir asistencia.

articles.title: Salesforce’s M&A spree continues with a reported $375M deal for defense tech startup Rune | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Salesforce has agreed to acquire Rune Technologies, a startup that builds AI software to help the U.S. military predict supply needs and manage logistics from the field, for $375 million in cash and stock, Resilience Media reported.
The acquisition underscores Salesforce’s push into defense tech through Missionforce, its business unit serving national security and defense agencies. Since Missionforce launched last year, its business has grown 80% year over year, driven in part by a new 10-year, $5.6 billion contract with the U.S. Army, the company said in a blog post. By integrating Rune’s frontline logistics data, Missionforce will extend beyond back-office administrative planning to support battlefield operations.
Since its founding in 2024, Rune has raised a total of $30 million from investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Point72 Ventures, and IQT, a CIA-backed nonprofit venture firm formerly known as In-Q-Tel. The startup was last valued at $127 million when it raised a Series A led by Human Capital last year, according to PitchBook.
Salesforce has been on an acquisition spree this year. In addition to Rune, the CRM giant agreed to buy AI agent platform Fin (formerly Intercom) for $3.6 billion, bought Qualified for $1.2 billion, and signed an agreement to buy Listen Labs after the startup walked away from a $125 million Series C term sheet at a $1.5 billion valuation, as TechCrunch reported.
Salesforce didn’t respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: Intelligence agency misplaced 'a very significant number' of removable drives — storage media have been missing for years, but exact number of lost devices remain unknown
articles.text:
Intelligence agency misplaced 'a very significant number' of removable drives — storage media have been missing for years, but exact number of lost devices remain unknown
The missing drives number in the thousands.
The UK’s Investigatory Powers Commissioner’s Office (IPCO) has flagged “a very significant number” of General Communications Headquarters (GCHQ) storage drives that have been missing for years and have yet to be found. According to The Register, the lost storage media have been known to GCHQ officials for years now, but they’re still unsure about the scope of the problem.
"I remain concerned that GCHQ has not yet established a sufficiently clear understanding of the scale, location, and recoverability of lost removable media that may contain IPA-related data, notwithstanding that the underlying issues were first drawn to my attention several years ago. While I recognize the technical and practical challenges involved, the passage of time without a comprehensive account heightens the importance of sustained senior focus and assured remediation. Given the potential sensitivity of the material involved, I will continue to monitor progress closely,” investigatory powers commissioner Lord Brian Leveson wrote in the report.
GCHQ acknowledged to The Register that the tracking system for its removable media had been insufficient, but it has since taken steps to prevent it happening in the future. "We recognize the importance of security of removable media in our systems and have a range of measures to mitigate the risks posed by these items. The findings in the report have been addressed comprehensively, and all necessary steps to correct this issue have been taken," a GCHQ spokesperson told the publication. It has also launched a program to help locate as many of the lost storage media as possible and will have an automated asset-tracking system up and running before 2027.
The GCHQ is the UK’s equivalent to the National Security Agency (NSA), making it the country’s primary signals intelligence and cybersecurity agency. Its primary mission is governed by the Investigatory Powers Act (IPA), which was passed in 2016 and lays out the legal framework for government surveillance, data collection, and intercepting communications. While neither agency has exactly confirmed what data the missing drives contained, it could potentially have information about GCHQ operations, administration, and other crucial data.
While the UK’s premier signals intelligence and cybersecurity agency losing thousands of removable drives may sound alarming, it’s not alone in running into blunders like this. The publication reported that Britain’s Ministry of Defence has lost 87 classified USB drives from 2003 to 2008, and that the UK police have also dealt with officers losing their assigned tech gadgets. Other governments have also made considerable tech missteps — for example, the South Korean government lost 858TB of data after a catastrophic fire destroyed a data center, and it discovered that it had no backups. Indonesia discovered the same issue when it was hit with a ransomware attack, with one government official calling the lack of backups “stupid.”

articles.title: The Google Nest Wifi Pro is the simplest Wi-Fi 6e mesh router I know
articles.text:
The Google Nest Wifi Pro is the simplest Wi-Fi 6E mesh router I’d set up for non-techy family members — and it’s half price at Best Buy
Refreshingly easy to set up and manage through the Google Home app, and a single unit covers up to 2,200 square feet.
I don't know about you, but I'm sort of the gadget-man of the family. The tech-head. The makeshift IT consultant that gets called upon whenever there's an issue with technology. If you fall into the same category (or you never want to call on your family IT support again), I'd definitely recommend checking out the Google Nest Wifi Pro 6e Wi-Fi mesh router for $100 (was $200) at Best Buy.
The half-price deal makes it incredibly tempting. It's ridiculously simple to set up and manage, making it the ideal no-fuss mesh router pick if you or your family need better connections while working from home. If your home Wi-Fi is spotty and you don’t want to wrestle with complicated router settings, Nest Wifi Pro delivers fast, reliable coverage with minimal setup.
• Best for: home workers and families in small to midsize homes needing fast, easy-to-manage Wi-Fi with the option to add more units later.
• Why we like it: tri-band Wi-Fi 6E with a 6GHz band for less congestion, up to 2,200 square feet of coverage from one unit, effortless setup through the Google Home app, and support for adding more units to build a mesh.
A single tri-band Wi-Fi 6E (AXE5400) mesh router covering 2.4GHz, 5GHz, and 6GHz bands, with up to 2,200 square feet of coverage, support for up to 100 connected devices, WPA3 security, parental controls, and two Gigabit Ethernet ports. It’s managed through the Google Home app and also works as a Thread border router and Matter controller for smart home devices. Sold by Best Buy.
Why We Recommend It
Google built the Nest Wifi Pro for people who want Wi-Fi to simply work, and its app-based setup and automatic updates make it one of the least intimidating routers to own. We haven’t reviewed the Nest Wifi Pro, so this pick rests on Google’s track record with mesh networking and the router’s specs. Its 6GHz band is a real plus if you have newer phones and laptops that support Wi-Fi 6E, since it’s far less crowded than the older bands.
Price Context & Historical Value
Half off its $199.99 launch price is a strong deal, and $99.99 puts a Wi-Fi 6E mesh router within reach of almost any budget. Keep in mind that it launched in 2022, so it lacks the newer Wi-Fi 7 standard and multi-gig Ethernet found on pricier routers. For most homes with internet plans under 1Gbps, though, it’s a great buy at this price.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Google Nest Wifi Pro if... you want fast Wi-Fi that’s easy to set up and manage, your home is under about 2,200 square feet or you plan to add more units, or you use Google Home and want a router that doubles as a smart home hub.
❌ Skip the Google Nest Wifi Pro if... you want Wi-Fi 7 or multi-gig Ethernet ports for a very fast internet plan, you need lots of wired ports, or you already own older Google Wifi or Nest Wifi units, which can’t join a Nest Wifi Pro mesh.

articles.text:
Ce boîtier photo présente le meilleur rapport qualité / prix de notre comparatif
Le boîtier photo Nikon D7500 s'affiche aujourd'hui à 999,00 € chez Boulanger.com. C'est actuellement le meilleur rapport qualité / prix de notre comparatif, selon les 20 modèles testés dans notre laboratoire.
Remplaçant du D7200 ? Non, pas vraiment. Le Nikon D7500 vient plutôt, officiellement, s'intercaler entre ce dernier et le bien plus récent D500, en empruntant des composants aux deux. Vous pouvez donc voir le D7500 comme un D500 professionnel light, ou comme un D7200 très expert fortement amélioré. Au choix. Dans tous les cas, Nikon parvient à rendre une belle copie, propre et soignée, à défaut de se montrer originale ou avant-gardiste.

Points faibles

Avec le D7500, Nikon rend une très belle copie, mettant en avant son savoir-faire en termes d'autofocus, de suivi du sujet, de traitement d'image. Pour un tarif nettement inférieur à celui du D500, il offre des prestations très proches tout en proposant de nets progrès par rapport au D7200. Pas forcément le plus original, le D7500 s'inscrit dans l'air du temps (écran orientable et tactile, vidéo 4K/UHD) sans forcer plus qu'il ne le faut. Un boîtier équilibré taillé pour l'image d'action, voilà sa raison d'être.
