articles.title: Noel writes to Tata Sons to take biz recast, SP Group’s funding plea at Nov 26 meet
articles.text:
Noel writes to Tata Sons to take biz recast, SP Group’s funding plea at Nov 26 meet
Noel Tata's letter asks for a discussion on the September 11 letter from RBI, which makes a listing of Tata Sons mandatory by rejecting the application for de-registration.
Noel Tata has written to Tata Sons to take up a business reorganisation plan presented by him to avert listing of the conglomerate's holding company, and Shapoorji Pallonji group's part-exit to raise Rs 25,000 crore at the next board meet scheduled for November 26.
Noel, who chairs Tata Trusts, has sent two separate letters to Tata Sons secretary Suprakash Mukhopadhyay in his capacity as a board member, sources privy to the development said, adding that any member can convey an item to be included in the agenda with 15-day notice.
Emails sent to both Noel Tata and Tata Sons for a response on the development did not elicit a reply immediately.
First of the letters asks for a discussion and a vote on the reorganisation plan, under which it plans to amalgamate Tata Electronic Systems and Tata Consulting Engineers into Tata Sons Private Limited that can help avoid listing the group's holding company, which is considered by RBI as a core investment company and not an operational one.
Noel's letter asks for a discussion on the September 11 letter from RBI, which makes a listing of Tata Sons mandatory by rejecting the application for de-registration. It informs that subsequent to the letter, two of the biggest trusts under Tata Trusts had sent the reorganisation proposal on September 26.
As per the proposal, Tata Sons will become an operating company with the merger of electronics and engineering businesses, and cease to be an NBFC-CIC, which attracts the regulator's listing mandate.
The issue of Tata Sons' listing is core to the differences between Noel and the board of Tata Sons, which outvoted the head of the biggest owner group in the company by favouring for a compliance with the RBI mandate at its meeting on September 17.
Noel's side has been maintaining the need to preserve the character of the over-150-year grouping, advocating that the private character keeps investor pressure on delivering returns at bay and helps it take long term bets. The management of Tata Sons, however, says that it will have to follow the mandate of the regulator.
If the reorganisation plan gets adopted by Tata Sons, the amalgamation proposal will have to get nods from the RBI, National Companies Law Tribunal and also the Central government's Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
The two letters from Noel's side come at the end of a very hectic week, which started with truce talks between Noel and Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran at the former's South Mumbai residence on Sunday. This was followed by a letter from Noel to Tata Sons on Monday challenging Chandrasekaran's reappointment as chairman, and the issue taking a political turn with Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi lambasting the government for interference in the matter.
In the second letter to Tata Sons, Noel seeks information from the Tata Sons management on the progress on the letter from SP Group involving part-exit of its holdings to raise Rs 25,000 crore. He has asked for details on how the proposal has been evaluated and has also presented a draft resolution in the annexure.

articles.title: Prime Video : les 5 meilleures séries d'horreur pour une livraison de terreur en 24h
articles.text:
Loin des productions lissées conçues pour plaire au plus grand nombre, le genre horrifique trouve sur le petit écran un espace de liberté salutaire. Qu’il s’agisse de disséquer la folie humaine, d’explorer le malaise social par le prisme du surnaturel ou de moderniser des mythes fondateurs, Prime Video réunit des propositions radicales.
On vous a aussi sélectionné les meilleures séries d’horreur sur Netflix. Si vous préférez les films, on a dressé un top des meilleurs films d’horreur sur Prime Video, et un autre sur la plateforme Disney+.
Carrie (2026)
Quand le maître moderne de l’horreur télévisuelle s’attaque à la toute première œuvre publiée de Stephen King, le résultat ne pouvait être qu’un véritable séisme visuel. Oubliez les souvenirs assagis ou le simple vernis culte du film de Brian De Palma (1976) : Mike Flanagan (The Haunting of Hill House, Midnight Mass) réinvente la tragédie de Carrie White sous la forme d’une série incisive, étouffante et profondément dérangeante. Dans notre critique de Carrie, on la confronte au film culte.
En étirant le récit sur plusieurs épisodes, la série prend le temps de disséquer la psychologie brisée de son héroïne, en plongeant au cœur de l’enfer du harcèlement scolaire moderne et du fanatisme religieux familial.
The Strain
Loin des vampires romantiques, ténébreux et élégants à la Twilight ou Vampire Diaries, The Strain réinjecte du pur monstrueux, du crasseux et du parasite visqueux dans le mythe du suceur de sang. Imaginée par Guillermo del Toro et Chuck Hogan, la série démarre lorsqu’un Boeing 777 se pose à l’aéroport JFK de New York avec 206 morts à bord et seulement quatre survivants. C’est le point de départ d’une épidémie d’une violence inouïe, propagée par des vers parasites. Les créatures ici n’ont rien d’humain : ce sont des hôtes déformés, dotés d’un appendice buccal rétractile dégoûtant qui infecte leurs victimes sans la moindre pitié.
Avec sa direction artistique poisseuse, la série livre un body horror généreux, sur fond de panique pandémique claustrophobique.
Rosemary’s Baby (2014)
S’attaquer au monument cinématographique de Roman Polanski et au roman fondateur d’Ira Levin était un pari hautement risqué, mais cette mini-série de NBC réalisée par Agnieszka Holland et emmenée par Zoe Saldana réussit l’exploit d’imposer son propre malaise étouffant. En transposant l’intrigue de New York vers un Paris gothique, feutré et faussement rassurant, la série réinvente le calvaire de Rosemary. Cette jeune femme s’installe avec son mari dans un appartement haussmannien au passé trouble, puis tombe enceinte.
Très vite, l’emprise toxique d’un voisinage aristocratique trop bienveillant se transforme en une véritable conspiration satanique orchestrée dans l’ombre. La mini-série tient en deux épisodes d’environ deux heures chacun.
EUX
Créée par Little Marvin et produite par Lena Waithe, EUX (Them en version originale) compte parmi les séries d’horreur les plus éprouvantes et les plus politiques de ces dernières années. Située en 1953, en pleine Grande Migration, la première saison suit une famille afro-américaine qui quitte la Caroline du Nord pour emménager dans un quartier résidentiel blanc de Los Angeles. Mais ce qui devait être un havre de paix se transforme instantanément en un double cauchemar : d’un côté, la haine raciale pure et le harcèlement sadique des voisins du lotissement ; de l’autre, l’émergence de forces démoniaques et de visions macabres au sein même de leur demeure.
Bates Motel
Préquelle du Psychose d’Alfred Hitchcock, Bates Motel rend la relation fusionnelle, presque incestueuse et toxique entre le jeune Norman Bates (Freddie Highmore) et sa mère Norma (Vera Farmiga) à la fois fascinante, humaine et profondément terrifiante. Étalée sur cinq saisons d’une régularité exemplaire, la série dissèque la lente décomposition mentale d’un adolescent brisé par ses traumatismes, glissant inéluctablement vers la folie meurtrière.

articles.title: Le mystère d’Artemis : personne ne sait de combien de ravitaillements Starship aura besoin pour viser la Lune
articles.text:
Pour rejoindre la Lune, Starship doit d’abord faire le plein en orbite, mais personne ne sait vraiment combien de lancements cela demandera. Et le calendrier d’Artemis, lui, ne laisse presque aucune marge.
Starship occupe une place centrale dans le programme Artemis, puisque la NASA l’a sélectionné, aux côtés de Blue Moon de Blue Origin, pour poser ses astronautes sur la Lune. Et le 23 octobre dernier, l’agence a de nouveau ajusté sa feuille de route, tout en maintenant son objectif d’un retour sur notre satellite en 2028. Mais pour que ce plan tienne, SpaceX doit encore réussir une manœuvre qui n’a jamais été réalisée à cette échelle, rappelle Bloomberg.
Une station-service en orbite, et beaucoup d’inconnues
L’idée paraît simple sur le papier, elle l’est beaucoup moins dans les faits. Starship consomme tellement de carburant pour quitter la Terre qu’elle ne peut pas rejoindre la Lune d’une traite. SpaceX prévoit donc de faire décoller en premier un Starship « dépôt », une sorte de station-service vide en orbite, puis des Starship « citernes » viendront ensuite le remplir au fil de plusieurs lancements. Enfin, la fusée chargée de transporter les astronautes doit s’y amarrer pour se ravitailler avant de prendre la direction de notre satellite.
Mais combien de variantes citernes seront nécessaires ? C’est un sujet de discorde : la semaine dernière, un comité consultatif de la NASA a évoqué 22 vols. Un chiffre aussitôt contesté par Elon Musk, qui estime qu’il en faudrait entre 6 et 8. Problème, Jeremy Parsons, chef du programme Artemis, juge l’objectif du milliardaire d’« assez agressif », tout en estimant que « ce serait génial « de l’atteindre.
Cette approximation ne date pas d’hier. En 2023, un responsable de la NASA évoquait un chiffre » dans la haute dizaine », tandis qu’un cadre de SpaceX avançait « une dizaine environ » un an plus tard. À un an de la mission Artemis III, ce mystère ne semble toujours pas résolu.
Un calendrier qui ne laisse aucune marge
Plusieurs inconnues expliquent cet écart, à commencer par la capacité réelle de Starship. Elon Musk promet que la V3, celle qui est actuellement en phase de test, pourra emporter plus de 100 tonnes en orbite, mais ce n’est pas avéré pour le moment. De même, le carburant, conservé à très basse température, s’évapore en partie pendant le transfert comme pendant le stockage, ce qui pourrait obliger à lancer des citernes en plus.
La première démonstration de transfert de carburant entre deux Starship est visée début 2027, alors que la mégafusée vient simplement d’atteindre l’orbite pour la première fois. Cet essai devrait enfin donner un ordre de grandeur, encore faut-il qu’il soit tenu à temps. Car Blue Origin se tient en embuscade : son atterrisseur se passe de ravitaillement en orbite.

articles.title: Über 30 Jahre alt: Programmierer zeigt ältestes Programm, das unter Windows 11 noch läuft
articles.text:
Über 30 Jahre auf dem Buckel: Dieses Programm läuft noch heute problemlos unter Windows 11
Was ist eigentlich das älteste Programm mit grafischer Oberfläche (GUI), das ohne Emulation oder Modifikation noch unter Windows 11 läuft? Dieser Frage widmete sich der Programmierer Boris Popik und kam zu einigen überraschenden Erkenntnissen.
Keine 16-Bit-Unterstützung in Windows 11
Wie Popik in seinem Blog erklärt, bietet Windows 11 keine native Unterstützung von 16-Bit-Anwendungen. Das bedeutet, dass die Suche erst in der frühen Windows-NT-Ära Anfang der 1990er-Jahre beginnen kann. Das von Microsoft entwickelte 32-Bit-Betriebssystem kam im Juli 1993 auf den Markt.
In einem Forum wurde Popik auf Win32s aufmerksam gemacht, einer Erweiterung für Windows 3.1 und Windows 3.11 und einer Art Brückentechnologie für den Übergang in das 32-Bit-Zeitalter. Mit Win32s war es möglich, bestimmte 32-Bit-Programme auf dem älteren 16-Bit-Windows zum Laufen zu bringen.
Freecell von 1993 zum Laufen gebracht
Zu den bekanntesten Anwendungen, die eine installierte Win32s-Umgebung voraussetzten, gehörte das Kartenspiel Freecell. Und genau hier wurde Popik fündig. Er brachte eine aus dem Februar 1993 stammende Freecell-Version unter Windows 11 zum Laufen, ohne irgendwelche Änderungen vornehmen zu müssen.
Damit gab sich der Programmierer aber nicht zufrieden. Er machte in frühen Windows-NT-Versionen ein weiteres Programm ausfindig, das am 16. November 1992 das Licht der Welt erblickte: eine CD-Player-Anwendung. Das Problem: Popiks Rechner verfügt über kein CD-Laufwerk, wodurch das Programm zunächst crashte. Mit einem virtuellen Laufwerk konnte er dieses Problem aber beheben – und hatte eine noch ältere Anwendung für Windows 11 gefunden.
Gut 40 Jahre altes Game auf Windows-PC
Weiter zurück ging es allerdings tatsächlich nur mit Schummeln. Denn aufgrund der oben erwähnten fehlenden 16-Bit-Unterstützung in Windows 11 endet das Suchfenster eigentlich Anfang der 1990er-Jahre. Nutzt man aber eine entsprechende Komponente wie OTVDM, lassen sich 16-Bit-Anwendungen auf modernen 64-Bit-Versionen von Windows ausführen.
Genau das gelang Popik dann mit Reversi, einem schon in den 1880er-Jahren von dem Engländer Lewis Waterman entwickelten Brettspiel. Dessen Computerspiel-Variante vom 15. November 1985 ist – bis zum Beweis des Gegenteils – das wahrscheinlich älteste Programm, das sich auf einem modernen Windows-Computer zum Laufen bringen lässt. Allerdings nur unter Einsatz eines Emulators.
„das wahrscheinlich älteste Programm, das sich auf einem modernen Windows-Computer zum Laufen bringen lässt. Allerdings nur unter Einsatz eines Emulators.“
Was für ein Quatsch!
Mit einem Emulator lassen sich alle programme zu laufen bringen.

articles.title: LocalStack for Azure Enters Public Preview with Security Settings Stored but Not Enforced
articles.text:
LocalStack has put its Azure emulator into public preview, free and self-serve, with general availability expected in early 2027. Its own documentation is candid about the gap between emulating a resource and emulating its behavior.
The product runs Azure services on a developer machine and accepts existing ARM and Bicep templates, Terraform modules, Pulumi programs, and Azure CLI scripts without rewrites. The pitch is to test applications, as LocalStack puts it, "without waiting on a dev subscription or paying for every iteration." The service list is broad, covering AKS, Container Apps, Functions, App Service, Cosmos DB, Service Bus, Event Hubs, Key Vault, App Configuration, Managed Identity, API Management and more, and is wider than the announcement itself suggests. Each developer gets an isolated sandbox, and LocalStack positions it for development and testing rather than as a replacement for Azure.
The project is led by Paolo Salvatori, a Microsoft principal for 28 years before joining LocalStack and the creator of Service Bus Explorer. He sets the fidelity contract in one line:
If your solution runs perfectly on Azure but fails on our emulator, that is our bug to fix.
The documentation covers 24 resource providers and reports how much of each API is implemented. Storage Accounts covers 13 of 81 operations. App Service covers 143 of 616. Virtual Network covers 10 of 29.
The more useful pattern is what happens to the operations that are implemented. Configuration is frequently accepted, stored, and returned without taking effect. On App Service:
Keys, access restrictions, authentication settings, and publishing credential policies are not enforced.
The same page records that httpsOnly is not enforced and the emulator serves HTTP, that custom host-name bindings are stored and listed while the app answers only on its default names, that VNet integration is stored and returned with no network effect, and that backup configuration is stored while backup and restore are not implemented.
Networking follows suit. The Virtual Network page states plainly that "the emulator does not route network traffic or enforce security rules," that peering is unsupported, and that VPN gateways, ExpressRoute circuits, Load Balancer, Application Gateway, and Network Watcher are not implemented. Private DNS zones accept only A records.
Several Storage divergences land on authentication. Data-plane requests with a bearer token succeed whenever a token is present unless RBAC enforcement is enabled. A user delegation SAS does not re-check the principal’s RBAC when used. A SAS restricted to the caller’s public IP is refused because the emulator sees a Docker or loopback address. Unsupported request headers are silently accepted rather than rejected, and the x-ms-version header is not validated at all.
That promise is about code that runs in Azure and fails locally. The documented gaps mostly describe the reverse: an app with httpsOnly set serves HTTP here, and a data-plane request carrying any bearer token gets through. Both pass locally, and nothing in the run flags the difference.
Three behaviors will surprise people before any of that does. A web app created on a Windows plan runs its code in the Linux runtime. The Oryx build image ships for amd64 only, so on Apple Silicon a code deployment’s build fails, and the app starts without its dependencies. App Service state is held in memory and lost when the emulator stops.
Microsoft’s own local tooling is narrower and older. Azurite emulates Blob, Queue, and Table storage, the Cosmos DB emulator covers that database, and Azure Functions Core Tools runs Functions locally. None compose into a single environment where an ARM or Bicep deployment can be exercised end to end, which is the gap LocalStack aims to fill.
LocalStack also pitches the sandbox at AI agents, somewhere they can "deploy, break, and retry" without live credentials. An agent iterating there gets access restrictions stored rather than applied, and any bearer token accepted. Both come back as passes.
Developer experience features, including App Inspector, snapshots, and the chaos APIs, are not in preview. Pricing arrives at general availability, and preview access ends there. The transition terms are not settled: the product page still carries "[30 days]" as a literal placeholder and an unfilled next-steps section.

articles.title: Parece que han encontrado a la culpable de la rotura de la pantalla de algunos iPhone Duo. Y esto pone la campaña navideña a tiritar
articles.text:
El iPhone Duo se puso a la venta hace justo una semana y no hemos tenido que esperar demasiado para ver los primeros errores. Al margen de apps de terceros sin optimizar, algo lógico y que se irá solucionando, durante el primer fin de semana aparecieron usuarios que compartieron fotos de pantallas rotas en sus dispositivos. Todas tenían el mismo patrón de rotura y pronto se apuntó al mecanismo que podría tener la culpa.
Ahora parece que ya han encontrado esa pieza.
Qué ha pasado. Primero fue en Reddit, pero luego se fue extendiendo. Varios usuarios han reportado que, durante los primeros usos, el flamante iPhone Duo se rompía. Que haya unidades que salgan con fallos de fábrica, da igual que sea una nueva generación o no, es algo habitual porque se fabrican millones y es normal que algunas pasen bajo el radar de las pruebas de calidad, pero aquí el patrón era raro.
Una línea horizontal de píxeles muertos que cruza la parte derecha de la pantalla interior y una línea vertical justo en la bisagra que podía ser más o menos visible, pero que también estaba presente. Lo curioso del asunto es que esa línea horizontal era igual en todos los modelos con la pantalla rota, lo que llevó a pensar que detrás quizá había algo más que un problema de control de calidad en un lote..
La culpable. iFixit pronto hizo un vídeo en el que mostraban, usando radiografías y simulación, la posible pieza culpable. Comentaron que había un refuerzo estructural para mantener la zona central estable cuando extendemos la pantalla, pero que al doblarla, genera una enorme tensión sobre el panel y las conexiones, lo que podía terminar provocando el error.
Ahora, un youtuber surcoreano se ha dejado de radiografías y ha compartido este vídeo en el que podemos ver exactamente la pieza en cuestión:
iFixit ha hecho otro vídeo en el que se apoyan en lo que cuenta ese youtuber y aportan imágenes que muestran cómo, con la pantalla apagada, se puede ver en alguna unidad esa pieza que está causando el error. El medio especialista en reparación de dispositivos ratifica el vídeo del youtuber surcoreano, aportando nuevas simulaciones y escáneres que nos permiten ver el funcionamiento de esa pieza y cómo causa el error.
Prisas. El propio medio comenta que es temprano para hablar de cuántas unidades están afectadas, ya que tampoco es que haya demasiadas en el mercado, y no se aventura a decir que sea un fallo de diseño generalizado como fue el de la Xbox 360 original, el del teclado de mariposa del MacBook 2017 o el del Galaxy Note 7, pero sí que está afectando a cierto número de modelos.
A través de GSM Arena, podemos leer un informe del medio chino Jiemian News en el que un trabajador anónimo de Foxconn comenta que Apple habría reducido sus estándares de inspección de calidad con el objetivo de tener todas las unidades posible a tiempo tanto para el lanzamiento como para una campaña navideña que peligra. Ese empleado también comenta que la línea de producción del iPhone Duo
No es la primera vez que eso de las prisas por sacar el iPhone plegable sale a relucir. A comienzos de septiembre, antes de que se presentara el plegable, desde Nikkei Asia apuntaron que Apple no estaba pudiendo fabricar todos los plegables que quería. De hecho, se decía que no era un problema de diseño o de componentes, sino consecuencia del exigente nivel de calidad autoimpuesto.
Consecuencias. Si se han visto con el agua al cuello es algo que no podemos saber, pero lo cierto es que, si hoy entras en la web de Apple a por un plegable, la fecha que te dan para recogerlo es a meses vista. El 25 de enero, para ser exactos, por lo que se pierden la jugosísima campaña navideña.
Más allá del stock, está la consecuencia más directa, y es la posible crisis reputacional si el número de móviles afectados continúa aumentando. La bisagra es el componente más complejo de un plegable y un fallo de diseño en la misma no es algo que se solucione de la noche a la mañana.
Qué dice Apple. La compañía mantiene el comunicado temprano que hizo a comienzos de semana:
"Somos conscientes de un problema que afecta a la pantalla interior en un pequeño número de unidades del iPhone Duo. Si los usuarios experimentan problemas con la pantalla de su iPhone Duo, deben ponerse en contacto con AppleCare para obtener un reemplazo"
Por nuestra parte, hemos preguntado directamente a Apple debido a la actualización de la información sobre la pieza protagonista de esta historia y actualizaremos tan pronto como tengamos novedades. En nuestro análisis del iPhone Duo no tuvimos ningún problema, pero si estuviera interesado en comprar uno, esperaría a ver qué pasa.

articles.title: Netflix, HBO Max, évènements sportifs : Canal+ casse le prix de son offre Ciné Séries
articles.text:
24,99 € par mois pour profiter de Netflix, Apple TV, Paramount+, HBO Max et de plusieurs chaînes Canal+ : c’est la nouvelle promotion proposée sur l’offre Ciné Séries. Attention toutefois, ce tarif n’est appliqué que durant les 12 premiers mois. Ensuite, la facture augmente de 10 euros pour passer à 34,99 € par mois. Dans tous les cas, cette promotion a de quoi retenir l’attention.
Canal+ lance une promotion pour son offre Ciné Séries
Alors que les prix des différentes plateformes de streaming augmentent régulièrement, Canal+ vient de lancer une nouvelle promotion pour son offre Ciné Séries. Concrètement, il est question d’un engagement sur 24 mois. Durant les 12 premiers mois, l’abonné bénéficie d’un tarif réduit de 24,99 € par mois, au lieu de 29,99 €. Les 12 mois suivants, le prix passe à 34,99 € par mois. Pour rappel, l’offre Ciné Séries donne accès à Apple TV, HBO Max (abonnement Standard), Netflix (Standard avec Pub), Paramount+ (Standard), Ciné+ OCS et Insomnia (la plateforme de streaming dédiée au cinéma d’horreur). Côté chaînes, cette offre intègre Canal+, Canal+ Box Office, Canal+ Grand Écran, Canal+ Sport 360, Canal+ Docs, Canal+ Kids et Canal+ Cinéma(s).
Les abonnés à cette offre peuvent donc profiter des films et séries proposés sur les principales plateformes de streaming, tout en ayant accès aux événements sportifs retransmis par Canal+. Le groupe précise que tous ces services, pris séparément, reviendraient à 74 € par mois. À noter que cette offre est valable jusqu’au 9 novembre 2026 inclus.
Une offre très intéressante, mais il faut retenir un point
Comme nous l’avons précisé, l’offre est proposée à 24,99 € par mois durant les 12 premiers mois, avant de passer ensuite à 34,99 € par mois. Sur deux ans, cela représente donc une moyenne de 29,99 € par mois. Dans tous les cas, ce prix reste assez attractif vu le nombre de services auxquels l’offre donne accès. À noter qu’un abonnement sans engagement à Ciné Séries est également proposé à 34,99 € par mois.

articles.title: Intel stock plunges nearly 30%, its worst day in 52 years
articles.text:
What just happened? Intel was one of the stock market's biggest surprises this year. Its shares nearly quadrupled between January and a record high in late June – a run fueled by demand for the CPUs behind agentic AI. But on Friday, the chipmaker gave back a huge chunk of those gains in a single session. The stock closed down almost 29% at $65.76, its worst day since 1974.
Oddly enough, the quarter itself went well. Intel beat Wall Street's earnings estimates. Its data center revenue jumped nearly 80% from a year earlier to $7.3 billion, too. But its forecast for the last three months of the year landed well short: analysts had penciled in about $17 billion in revenue. Intel only expects $15 billion to $16 billion.
The weak spot is PCs. AI data centers are buying up so much of the world's memory that laptops and desktops have gotten a lot pricier this year. So fewer of them are selling. Intel now expects PC shipments to drop about 12% in 2026 and another 10% in 2027. It doesn't see things improving until memory supply and prices get back to normal.
The forecast also has to absorb a shutdown at the company's fab in Kiryat Gat, Israel. That's where an explosion killed two workers earlier this month.
Going by Yahoo Finance's count of closing prices back to 1973, only a nearly 30% slide in July 1974 was worse than Friday. Bank of America, D.A. Davidson, Seaport and Roth all downgraded the stock to neutral the same day. The US government felt it too, since its roughly 10% stake lost about $12 billion in paper value. Even so, Washington's shares are still worth over three times the $20.47 apiece it paid last year.
Intel's slide came a day after Alphabet's worst session ever. The Google parent shed roughly $500 billion in market value on Thursday after its quarterly report showed AI infrastructure spending had pushed free cash flow $9.07 billion into the red.
Meta's earnings didn't land much better. Both it and Alphabet now sit more than 20% below their 52-week highs, according to Yahoo Finance data. Even Nvidia is about 12% off its peak, mostly because investors fear its biggest customers will have to scale back spending in 2027.
Over in Seoul, SK Hynix fell 7% and Samsung lost 3% on Friday. That pulled South Korea's KOSPI down nearly 3.5%. Both companies make the memory that AI data centers have been soaking up, so the same boom squeezing Intel's PC business is now rattling investors in the boom's biggest winners.
For anyone shopping for a PC, none of this points to cheaper hardware soon. Memory prices could keep climbing through next year. Some forecasts don't have real relief arriving until 2028.

articles.title: GTA 6 revela a sus protagonistas: quiénes son Jason, Lucia y los personajes que llegarán a Vice City
articles.text:
Rockstar Games confirmó nuevos detalles sobre los personajes que darán vida a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), el próximo lanzamiento de una de las franquicias más populares de la industria de los videojuegos. La historia tendrá como protagonistas a Jason Duval y Lucia Caminos, una pareja que intentará construir una nueva vida en medio del crimen organizado, los negocios ilegales y los conflictos que dominan Vice City.
El elenco también incluirá narcotraficantes, atracadores profesionales, empresarios vinculados al entretenimiento nocturno y artistas que buscan hacerse un lugar en la escena musical. Estos personajes tendrán diferentes conexiones con los protagonistas y ayudarán a desarrollar una trama que combinará robos, ambición, relaciones personales y violencia.
El videojuego llegará el 19 de noviembre de 2026 a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S. Aunque Rockstar todavía no ha confirmado una versión para PC, ya ha presentado información sobre buena parte de los personajes que participarán en esta nueva aventura.
Jason Duval y Lucia Caminos: los protagonistas de GTA 6
Jason Duval es uno de los dos personajes principales de GTA 6. Creció rodeado de delincuentes y estafadores, pero intentó alejarse de ese entorno cuando ingresó al ejército. Sin embargo, su pasado terminó llevándolo nuevamente al mundo criminal.
Después de abandonar la vida militar, se instaló en los Cayos, donde trabaja para narcotraficantes de la zona. Su situación cambia cuando conoce a Lucia, una mujer que podría representar una oportunidad para comenzar de nuevo o convertirse en el origen de nuevos problemas.
Por su parte, Lucia Caminos ha enfrentado dificultades desde pequeña. Su intención de proteger a su familia terminó llevándola a la penitenciaría de Leonida, de la que finalmente consiguió salir.
Ahora busca tomar el control de su futuro y alcanzar la estabilidad económica que siempre deseó. La relación con Jason aparece como una posible oportunidad para conseguirlo, aunque ambos deberán enfrentarse a situaciones peligrosas para cumplir sus objetivos.
La historia de los dos personajes recuerda a la dinámica criminal de Bonnie y Clyde: una pareja que construye su camino a través de robos y decisiones arriesgadas.
Los personajes que rodearán a Jason y Lucia
Además de los protagonistas, Rockstar presentó a varios personajes que tendrán vínculos con el mundo criminal y los negocios de Vice City.
Cal Hampton: es amigo de Jason y socio de Brian Heder. Prefiere mantenerse en casa, donde pasa el tiempo vigilando comunicaciones de la guardia costera y navegando por internet. Su personalidad está marcada por las teorías de conspiración y la desconfianza.
Boobie Ike: es uno de los empresarios más conocidos de Vice City. Consiguió transformar su pasado en las calles en un negocio que incluye propiedades inmobiliarias, un club nocturno y un estudio de grabación. Aunque suele mostrarse sonriente, su actitud cambia cuando debe negociar.
Dre’Quan Priest: es un aspirante a empresario musical que busca dejar atrás sus actividades ilegales. Su objetivo es impulsar Only Raw Records, el sello discográfico que comparte con Boobie Ike, y conseguir el éxito dentro de la escena musical de la ciudad.
Real Dimez: el dúo está integrado por Bae-Luxe y Roxy, dos amigas que encontraron en la música y las redes sociales una manera de ganar dinero. Después de conseguir popularidad con sus canciones de rap, firmaron con Only Raw Records y buscan recuperar el éxito.
Raul Bautista: es un atracador profesional que destaca por su carisma y capacidad para organizar golpes. Su ambición aumenta con cada robo, por lo que busca personas dispuestas a asumir riesgos cada vez mayores para conseguir grandes recompensas.
Brian Heder: es un narcotraficante que opera desde un astillero en los Cayos junto a su esposa Lori. Después de pasar años en el negocio, ahora deja que otros realicen buena parte del trabajo ilegal. También mantiene una relación cercana con Jason, a quien permite vivir en una de sus propiedades a cambio de colaborar en algunas actividades.
Qué papel tendrán los personajes en la historia de GTA 6
El conjunto de personajes muestra que GTA 6 no estará centrado únicamente en los delitos que cometan Jason y Lucia. Rockstar plantea una historia en la que los negocios, la música, las relaciones personales y el crimen organizado estarán conectados.
Los protagonistas comenzarán desde una posición económica y personal complicada: Lucia acaba de salir de prisión y Jason depende de los vínculos que mantiene con narcotraficantes para sostenerse. A partir de esa situación, ambos buscarán oportunidades para mejorar sus vidas, aunque deberán enfrentarse a personas con intereses diferentes.
Los personajes secundarios también permitirán explorar distintos sectores de Vice City, desde los negocios nocturnos hasta las actividades ilegales que se desarrollan fuera del centro urbano.
Por ahora, Rockstar no ha detallado cómo se relacionará cada personaje con las misiones principales ni qué decisiones podrán tomar los jugadores durante la historia. Lo confirmado es que GTA 6 llegará el 19 de noviembre de 2026 a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S, mientras que su lanzamiento en PC continúa sin fecha oficial.

articles.title: Após jailbreak, jogos de Nintendo Switch 2 rodam em PC e até iPhone • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Após jailbreak, jogos de Nintendo Switch 2 rodam em PC e até iPhone
Projetos de código aberto permitem rodar títulos exclusivos em outras plataformas, mas exigem uma cópia original dos games.
Uma semana após o primeiro jailbreak do Nintendo Switch 2 via software, diversos jogos exclusivos da Nintendo já rodam em outras plataformas. Publicações no X/Twitter mostram títulos do console funcionando em PCs, no iPhone 18 Pro e até em um computador com macOS.
Ferramentas de código aberto têm facilitado o processo, como o software ns2jb, disponibilizado em 22 de outubro. Jogos como Mario Kart World, Dragon Age e Zelda foram disponibilizados em ports no GitHub sob a licença MIT, que permite o acesso ao código para pesquisa e testes. São projetos que não incluem os jogos em si: para executá-los, é necessário ter uma cópia original de cada título.
Por isso, a disponibilização dos ports, por si só, não configura pirataria. A infração ocorre quando há distribuição ou download não autorizado das imagens ISO dos títulos.
A Nintendo, porém, tem um histórico de ações contra emuladores e ferramentas de acesso a seus jogos. Em 2024, a empresa conseguiu derrubar o Yuzu, conhecido emulador de Nintendo Switch, e pediu a remoção de outras ferramentas semelhantes hospedadas no GitHub.
Mais recentemente, um usuário do Reddit foi condenado a pagar US$ 4,5 milhões (pouco mais de R$ 24 milhões) por violações envolvendo mais de 30 jogos exclusivos do Switch.
No fim de setembro, dois jailbreaks funcionais para o PlayStation 5 foram publicados e provocaram uma onda de ports distribuídos pela internet. Também surgiram aplicativos que oferecem gratuitamente milhares de jogos para rodar no console.
A facilidade com que os sistemas da Sony foram desbloqueados levantou suspeitas sobre o uso de inteligência artificial no processo de análise e exploração do código do console. É possível que o primeiro jailbreak do Switch 2 também tenha contado com ajuda de IA, embora isso ainda não esteja confirmado.
Em meio ao jailbreak do Switch 2 e relatos de games rodando em outras plataformas, novas ferramentas que levam exclusivos do Switch original para PC e celulares ganharam destaque. É o caso do nxnative, projeto open source disponível via GitHub que permite rodar jogos da Nintendo direto no iPhone.
Segundo o TechSpot, isso acontece porque tanto o celular da Apple quanto o console têm chips ARM, facilitando a tradução das informações entre sistemas.
Outros projetos também aproveitam a semelhança para rodar os games exclusivos no celular e mesmo no PC. Dois deles, d2r-mobile e MacNativeGames, estão disponíveis na plataforma de desenvolvedores e têm licença do MIT.

articles.title: Oh captain, our captain: Ars staff remembers Patrick Stewart
articles.text:
Along with the rest of the world, we at Ars are mourning Sir Patrick Stewart—the beloved award-winning actor best known as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men franchise—who died yesterday at the age of 86.
A statement released by Stewart’s representatives said:
We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia. He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all. We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.
Born in Yorkshire, England, in 1940, the acting bug bit Stewart at the age of 12, when his English teacher handed out scripts for Shakespeare’s The Merchant of Venice and asked young Patrick to read the part of Shylock—a role the adult Stewart would later play for the Royal Shakespeare Theater (RSC), among many other parts. His signature bald head emerged early, around 19, thanks to alopecia. He briefly worked as a cub reporter and a furniture salesman before winning a scholarship to the Bristol Old Vic Theater School, and he landed his first professional role in 1959, playing a marooned pirate in a production of Treasure Island for the Lincoln Repertory Company.
Stewart worked regularly in theater and on British television, and his big break came in his late 40s. The actor was conducting master classes on Shakespeare at the University of California, Los Angeles, when a TV producer developing TNG heard him lecture and thought he would make a perfect captain for the Enterprise-D. Creator Gene Roddenberry wasn’t initially keen on the choice, but Stewart’s audition changed his mind. The rest is television history.
On Instagram, fellow thespian Sir Ian McKellen—who first met Stewart when both were young actors with the RSC and co-starred as Magneto in the X-Men films—recalled the day Stewart told him about the Star Trek offer.
“’But Patrick, think of your stage career in the UK,'” McKellen recalled saying. “‘Do you really want to risk—getting lost in Hollywood for years and years?’ Well, he took the risk and thank goodness for us all that he did.”
Stewart himself never expressed anything but pride in the role. “For huge numbers of people, I will always be Jean-Luc Picard, and that’s fine,” he told The Independent in 2003. “I really believe we created an admirable individual.”
TNG ended in 1994, but it wasn’t long before Stewart created another iconic role, starring as Professor Charles Xavier in 2000’s X-Men, alongside McKellen as Magneto. He reprised the role in six more films and voiced the character in multiple video games.
He was a serious actor who never took himself too seriously, relishing Shakespeare, Ibsen, and Beckett but also throwing himself into comedic TV appearances on Saturday Night Live, The Daily Show (he was a “special correspondent” for several segments in 2012), and Sesame Street. Who could forget his timeless “Soliloquy on B,” channeling Hamlet? Or his daily readings of Shakespearean sonnets that helped us all get through the COVID-19 pandemic? He voiced Napoleon in 1999’s Animal Farm, CIA Deputy Director Avery Bullock on American Dad and, earlier this year, Sir Nitchfield in the delightful Sheep Detectives.
In between acting gigs, Stewart found time for charity work, advocating for such causes as domestic violence prevention and PTSD awareness among members of the armed forces, drawing on his own childhood being raised by an abusive father. All of this made Stewart one of the most beloved actors of our time. Tributes to Stewart are all over social media today, as celebrities and regular folk alike reflect on everything the actor’s work has meant to them over the years, including these heartfelt words from his lifelong friend McKellen:
Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end. You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love.
Ars staffers share their own reminiscences about Stewart and what he meant to them below.
Ken Fisher, founder and editor-in-chief:
I had the good fortune to literally bump into Sir Patrick Stewart outside Bond 45 in Midtown Manhattan (when it was on 45th Street). I was coming out of the restaurant with a couple of colleagues one evening when I turned right into him. When my eyes met his, I entered a state of total confusion. I knew he loved and even played Broadway, but it didn’t register why he was here, right next to me.
Fortunately, I recovered—but then, for some unknown reason, I said in a pirate voice, “Scuse muh, Capt’n!” But he didn’t miss a beat, smiled, and took a posture of “after you good sir!” I immediately chuckled like a fool and then added that I loved his work both on and off the stage. He thanked me, and we kept on rolling. I am thankful to this day that I didn’t say something corny like “two to beam up.”
What struck me about the exchange was that, as brief as it was, he did not appear annoyed in the slightest. And while I know he is a world-class actor, he also seemed genuinely appreciative of the comment. I am grateful today that I got to share my appreciation with him, awkward though it was.

Eric Berger, senior space editor:
Warmth. Humanity. Decency. Honesty. Integrity. Intellectualism. These are but a few of the traits I associate with Captain Jean-Luc Picard. At a time when our leadership in the United States, and many other countries around the world, regularly showcases the opposite of these characteristics, is it any wonder that we dearly miss the captain of the Enterprise-D? Picard first graced our TV screens in the late 1980s, a super impressionable time for me. As a result, for a time, that is how I expected most leaders would behave. Alas, no.
I’m sure everyone has their favorite Picard scenes, but for me it came at the very end of The Next Generation; we had all gotten to know and love the bridge crew so well, and it felt so bittersweet that it all was ending. There was Jean-Luc, who had maintained his professional distance for seven years, joining his crew at the poker table. And now, not just the series is over, but so too is the era in which Patrick Stewart was alive and making the world a better place. It’s a little darker outside.
Kyle Orland, senior gaming editor:
With Patrick Stewart’s death, there will be plenty of people remembering all of the Star Trek: The Next Generation moments when he ably portrayed Captain Picard as the moral and diplomatic core of the show. And for sure, Stewart’s meaty and memorable monologues in episodes like The Drumhead, The First Duty, Darmok, Chain of Command, and more will be long remembered by sci-fi fans and studied by actors honing their craft.
But the most lasting Captain Picard moments for me are often the ones where Stewart got to let his hair down (so to speak) and show some rare emotional vulnerability in what was usually such a composed and professional character.
It’s these smaller emotional character moments—and Stewart’s ability to make so much of them—that added depth and roundness to Captain Picard’s character over the years. And that continued all the way up to Next Generation‘s very final moments, where Stewart captures the wistfulness and regret of Picard finally deciding to join the senior staff poker game. “Five card stud, nothing wild… and the sky’s the limit.”
Jeremy Hsu, technology reporter:
As a very casual Star Trek viewer, I only really began to grasp the depth of Patrick Stewart’s acting when I became enthralled by the silver screen chemistry between him and co-star Ian McKellen in the X-Men film franchise. The love-hate relationship and emotional vulnerability that Stewart and McKellen instilled in their roles as old-friends-turned-rivals has resonated with me throughout the years, and I still have deep appreciation for how the actors’ real-life friendship grew from that acting experience.
I also count myself extremely fortunate to have seen Stewart and McKellen perform together in a Broadway stage revival of the play Waiting for Godot in 2014. I’m sad they won’t be performing together again, but whenever they had the opportunity, they shone brightly indeed.
Jacob May, copy editor:
Hope and altruism are central themes in Stewart’s iconic roles, and they resonated most with me during one of my lowest moments.
Ever the one to inspire, Stewart’s role as Professor X in many X-Men films encouraged people and mutants to see the best in themselves and in each other. In 2014’s Days of Future Past, his pep talk extended to new ears: a younger, disillusioned version of himself (played by James McAvoy), and he may have well been speaking to me, too. Professor X’s telepathic abilities transcend space, time, and reality—don’t question it too much.
Upon the film’s release, I was freshly laid off from my hometown newspaper after the copy desk saw its numbers cut in half. (What was already a skeleton crew became less than that.) It wasn’t lost on me that being a cynic and malcontent was partly why I wasn’t picked to remain at the paper. In my late 20s, I questioned many of the decisions that set me on my journalism path, unsure what would happen to my career.
The younger Charles Xavier finds himself in a similar spot: angry with himself, with other people, and with the general state of things—and he’s seemingly out of a job. The older Professor X reminds his younger self that people can overcome their self-defeating flaws. “Just because someone stumbles and loses their way doesn’t mean they’re lost forever.”
Younger Chuck laments being tormented by people’s accounts of their pain, something a person who reads the news for a living can relate to. I try to unplug from Cerebro—er, my computer—when I’m off the clock. Xavier doesn’t have that luxury. The constant voices have driven him to despair and left him increasingly jaded.
But older Xavier calls him out, saying it’s his own mindset that’s holding him back. “We need you to hope again,” he says.
Therein lies the answer to Xavier’s malady: hope. And, as it turns out, the advice was also applicable to a young journalist in a crumbling industry. Incidentally, Stewart also found himself at a career crossroads as a young man, though he wasn’t too far along a chosen path, according to the Hollywood Reporter.
At 15, he got a job at the local newspaper, The Dewsbury Reporter, where he was tasked with interviewing bereaved family members when someone in town died. Journalism turned out not to be his passion, and he spent much of his free time with drama groups. His editor finally told him he had to choose between acting and journalism—and he quit on the spot.
Maybe if I had an Englishman’s commanding baritone, I would have made the same choice.

Ryan Whitwam, senior technology reporter:
Patrick Stewart was a prolific actor, but I will always associate him most with Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation, a show that made a real impression on me as a nerdy kid. It was refreshing to see a leader who valued science and reason—someone who didn’t immediately reach for their phaser. Despite the sometimes silly sci-fi subject matter, Stewart never seemed like he was too good to be spouting technobabble, even though he was famously skeptical of the role at first. Stewart’s portrayal of Picard elevated the series and helped it to age into a classic that I (and I’m sure many of you) still enjoy.
I also appreciate that he took so many different roles in movies and TV during his post-Trek career. Whenever I saw Patrick Stewart pop up on my screen or heard his voice unexpectedly come out of a cartoon character, it was a reminder of how happy TNG made me over the years. I’ll miss that, and I’ll miss knowing that Patrick Stewart is out there being a kind, thoughtful guy off screen.
Lee Hutchinson, senior technology editor:
The version of Patrick Stewart that lives in my head will most often be the noble starship captain who taught us life lessons every Friday night at 7 pm on channel 39. But while Stewart was obviously fantastic at portraying Picard’s stentorian and often stuffy formality, I was surprised when I discovered that the man behind the uniform was… surprisingly hilarious.
I tuned into his early 1994 Saturday Night Live appearance expecting an endless series of Trek riffs, but what I got instead was a sketch about an erotic cake shop run by a weirdly scatological baker. My confusion gave way to giggles—it was a one-note joke, but the image of Stewart in an apron talking about “sexy cakes” has stuck in my head for decades. He committed to it every bit as hard as he committed to following the Prime Directive, and at 16, it made me realize that anyone who could go from “The first duty of a Starfleet officer is to the truth!” to that and sell them both with equal intensity and sincerity was not a one-note actor. This was a man with a hell of a lot of range!
The performance that brought me the most joy, though, was his turn on Ricky Gervais’ Extras, where he played a version of himself as an actor, delivering career advice to Gervais. The scene is a masterclass in expectation subversion, something Stewart often seemed to revel in. I won’t spoil it for the two or three readers who still haven’t had the pleasure, but I will say that to this day my wife and I still say, “I’ve seen everything, I’ve seen it all!” at each other regularly in conversation.
Farewell, Sir Patrick. You gave us so much. Thank you.
Jason Marlin, technical director:
Like many Gen Xers, I grew up loving the original Star Trek series. But The Next Generation held a special place in my heart. From the moment it premiered, I was captivated by the mind-bending concepts it explored. Jean-Luc Picard quickly became one of my favorite characters. I admired his intelligence, leadership, and moral integrity. He was the quintessential Starfleet captain, and he made balding cool in a way only Michael Jordan could rival.
Years later, I discovered what would become my favorite Patrick Stewart performance: his formidable portrayal of Ebenezer Scrooge on Broadway and in the 1999 adaptation of A Christmas Carol.
For me, the movie remains the definitive version of Dickens’ classic, and watching it has become a cherished family holiday tradition. During the COVID lockdowns, we eagerly tuned in to Stewart’s readings of Shakespeare, and of course, his solo multipart rendition of A Christmas Carol. A roaring fire, some warm drinks, and his perfect Shakespearean accent made everything seem right with the world.
Sir Patrick Stewart will be greatly missed in the Marlin household.
Nick Indge, senior technology reporter:
Growing up in the US, raised by Brits, there was something quietly thrilling about seeing a Yorkshireman handed the captain’s chair. Better still, it made TNG legitimate in the eyes of my parents—a classically trained Shakespearean actor wouldn’t be involved in anything unserious, surely. As I came of age in 2000, there he was again as Professor X. Of course he was. Who else could it have possibly been? Beyond the roles, though, he just seemed to be a genuinely good man, the Mr. Rogers and Weird Al tier of human being. And when the world was upside down at the height of COVID, there he was, reading me a daily sonnet.
Jennifer is a senior writer at Ars Technica with a particular focus on where science meets culture, covering everything from physics and related interdisciplinary topics to her favorite films and TV series. Jennifer lives in Baltimore with her spouse, physicist Sean M. Carroll, and their two cats, Ariel and Caliban.
Stewart's death obviously has, and for pretty explainable reasons. I consider myself a proud "second-generation Trekkie". My parents watched TOS in their college dorms in the 1960s. My older brother grew up watching TOS re-runs and TAS in the 1970s, and introduced me to the TOS-cast films when I was a kid in the 1980s.
TNG premiered when I was eight years old. For the remainder of the 1980s and most of the 1990s, watching 'Star Trek' once a week (TNG, and then later DS9 and VOY) was just what my family did. It was a ritual.
Jean-Luc Picard and the crew of NCC-1701-D were companions to me through some of the most turbulent years of my life — the death of my best friend when I was ten years old, the rocky adolescence that followed as I wrestled with epistemological and phenomenological questions that my young mind didn't have the tools to answer, and much more.
When 'Star Trek: Picard' premiered its third season in 2023, I was enraptured. Sure, it was a pretty obvious nostalgia play. But I don't think nostalgia is inherently a bad thing. And the season did seem to serve as closure for much of the cast, who generally felt like their last outing in 2002's 'Nemesis' didn't do their characters justice (a sentiment with which I very much agree).
The climax of that third season, with all of my old friends reunited on the bridge of the Enterprise-D for one last adventure, was cathartic and beautiful and made my heart soar. I could not be happier that Patrick Stewart lived to see that happen.
While the observation of his passing has mostly been in the tone of unreserved praise and adoration (which I feel is very much deserved), some have noted that Stewart had flaws. Of course he did, he'd be the first to point that out. When he was a young father and husband, he'd tell you himself that he'd not performed terribly well in either role. The man had a lot of demons from his own abusive upbringing to conquer, and that took some time. It's not an excuse, but is an explanation.
I learned a lot of valuable lessons from Jean-Luc Picard:
— Being curious about the unknown is better than fearing it.
— Seeking to understand our fellow-creatures is better than seeking to mistrust them.
— Reason and compassion are compatible.
— Principle and duty can coexist with warmth and humanity.
— True leadership is about guardianship, not overlordship.
But here's another thing that I learned from Patrick Stewart himself, which I think is no less valuable:
You will fail in your life. You will do things that you shouldn't do, things that will hurt other people. Sometimes you will do them by mistake. Sometimes you will do them because you experienced a lapse in your moral judgment. What's important is how gracefully you accept your failure, offer sincere penance to those you've harmed, and work to better yourself and the world around you in the aftermath.
He did that, and he taught me that doing that is one of the hallmarks of goodness.
I didn't just learn that lesson from Patrick Stewart, though. I also learned it from my own father. Like Jean-Luc Picard, my dad has demonstrated every day of his life that strength and compassion are not mutually-exclusive traits. He's demonstrated that quiet devotion to the people you love, and exercising authority by way of stewardship and kindness is the mark of a "real man", not bluster and bullying.
My dad's 80 years old, and just like Sir Patrick, he has Alzheimer's. He's doing okay. I don't think we expect to lose him any time soon. But that dimension has certainly amplified the emotional weight of Stewart's death for me.
If I can live into my 80s and be half the good influence that Patrick Stewart, or my own father, has been, I'll consider to to have been a life very well-lived indeed.

articles.title: Ollie, a privacy-focused AI assistant, is shutting down | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Ollie, a startup whose mission was to deliver an AI assistant that respected its users’ privacy, says that it will be shutting down in a week. Bill Lennon, the company’s co-founder and CEO, took to X on Friday to deliver the news, noting that the app will officially shut down on November 6.
“I’m really proud of what we accomplished,” Lennon said. “We built an incredible personal assistant with a small team, and learned a ton. I’m grateful to our amazing team, our users, our investors, and everyone who supported us on this journey.”
The text-based AI assistant market has exploded over the past year, as the increasingly powerful models that undergird such applications have made them significantly more useful for daily tasks.
Ollie, which discussed its $7.5 million seed round led by Khosla Ventures with TechCrunch in September, offered a subscription-based model. The assistant was focused on helping families stay connected and organized. The app connected to a user’s email and calendar, while also providing integrated functions to help with appointment bookings, meal planning, and bill payments. The company had also planned to eventually move into household budgeting.
Crucially, Ollie was one of the first mainstream apps that managed to achieve SOC 2, a privacy compliance standard that companies can attain via an independent audit. Unfortunately, user privacy has never been a hugely profitable aspect of the tech industry. If anything, many new digital assistants present unique privacy challenges for their users — as companies like Instinct have shown.
Ultimately, the pressures of the burgeoning AI industry took a toll on the company, Lennon said. “We got close, but ultimately couldn’t keep up,” he added. “With Muse, Instinct, and others entering the space, it became harder to stand out, grow, and raise the capital we needed to succeed.”
Ollie’s customers will receive instructions on how to export data and receive refunds in the coming days, Lennon added.

articles.title: PS5s Become Steam Machines with Unofficial Bazzite Linux Installer
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
PS5s Become Steam Machines with Unofficial Bazzite Linux Installer
While the PS5 Linux project appears to be moving ahead despite the original creator's departure, an enterprising group of developers has adapted that project and Bazzite to turn the PlayStation 5 into something approximating a Steam Machine. Being that it is built on the same foundations as the PS5 Linux loader, the same limitations apply, meaning that it will only work on jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles running on firmware versions 3.00-13.60, and there are other compatibility limitations documented in the installation guide on GitHub. 
The particular variant of Bazzite being used is Bazzite-deck, which was originally built as an alternative to SteamOS for other x86 gaming handhelds, like the Lenovo Legion Go and ASUS ROG Ally, so by default it boots into Steam Gaming Mode on the PS5. It also offers an optional desktop mode running a full installation of KDE Plasma, which would conceivably allow the PS5 to work as a desktop workstation, as well. Between the desktop mode and Bazzite's handheld gaming mode, consoles running this software mod would have access not only to Steam games but to other game libraries, like GOG and Epic Games.Another benefit of running Bazzite on the PS5 is that it allows users to unlock an additional four compute units in the PS5's GPU that come disabled in firmware as a binning strategy. These extra CUs can be re-enabled by running a script provided on the aforementioned GitHub repository, but there is no guarantee that it will result in a stable experience. The developer claims that unlocking the entire 40-CU stack should work on most consoles, but there is an unknown number of consoles that will produce "green dots and other artifacts" after enabling the extra compute units.
Sources:
				PS5 Bazzite Deck on GitHub, 				via u/VivaLaVent on Reddit

articles.title: Michael O’Leary (Ryanair): “Vamos a asistir al mayor aumento de las tarifas aéreas de la historia en Europa. Hasta un 20 %”
articles.text:
El CEO de Ryanair ha venido a avisar de que en el próximo año en Europa va a haber el mayor incremento de tarifas de toda la historia. El consejero delegado de Ryanair, Michael O’Leary, lo anunciaba el 20 de octubre en una rueda de prensa en Bruselas. El motivo es que en el sector aéreo la mayoría de las líneas no están protegidas de los aumentos del combustible de aviación.
“Van a ver subir las tarifas aéreas el próximo año en Europa, creo que entre un 10 %, un 15 % o quizá un 20 %. Vamos a asistir al mayor aumento de las tarifas aéreas de la historia en Europa durante los próximos 12 meses”. Además, según O’Leary, hay que tener en cuenta que el número de asientos también va a disminuir por quiebras y procesos de consolidación en el sector.
¿Por qué hay tantos problemas con el combustible? En primer lugar, porque ha aumentado mucho su precio por la guerra con Irán. Esto está afectando a los márgenes de las líneas que no tenían coberturas. O’Leary explica que Ryanair y otras líneas europeas están bien cubiertas para 2026.
Cuando comenzó el conflicto, a finales de febrero, Ryanair (que se define como la mayor compañía de Europa) tenía cubierto el 80 % de su combustible a 67 dólares por barril hasta marzo de 2027.
El problema viene después. A partir de abril de 2027, la mayoría de las líneas europeas tienen muy pocas coberturas contratadas. En el caso de Ryanair, solo tiene cubierto el 15 % de los costes de combustible para el próximo año a 85 dólares por barril. Los precios en el mercado spot rondan el doble.
Con un contrato de cobertura puedes determinar de antemano el precio del combustible que vas a comprar en el futuro.
Recortes en Bélgica y el Boeing 737 MAX 10
En Bruselas venía a anunciar que van a eliminar 20 rutas y más de un millón de plazas en su oferta de invierno en Bélgica. El motivo, según la aerolínea, es que el Gobierno belga ha decidido aumentar la tasa aérea (que según Ryanair pasa de 2 a 7 euros a partir de enero de 2027). Para Ryanair son 1,1 millones de asientos y seis aviones menos. También aprovechan para pedirle al primer ministro (Bart De Wever) que la suprima.
Adicionalmente, han hablado de los aviones. Son optimistas con la certificación en EE.UU. del Boeing 737 MAX 10 antes de finales de octubre. “Somos bastante optimistas y creemos que se cumplirá ese plazo”. El pasado 20 de octubre, Boeing informaba de que la Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA) había firmado la certificación del avión. Con él esperan recibir 16 aeronaves a principios de 2027.
Para saber qué hay detrás de esta previsión, podemos ver las cuentas del sector. En junio, la Asociación Internacional de Transporte Aéreo (IATA) reducía su previsión de beneficio neto para 2026 a 23.000 millones de dólares (con un margen neto del 2 %). Calculan que los gastos de las líneas crecerán un 13,1 % y los ingresos un 9,5 %. La factura de combustible ascenderá a 351.000 millones de dólares.
¿Se nota ya en el billete? En mayo los precios de transporte de pasajeros por vía aérea subieron respecto al año anterior (donde cayeron). Así lo explicaba el INE en su nota de junio. En septiembre han vuelto a caer (aunque menos que en septiembre de 2025), tal y como detalla en su nota del 14 de octubre. El grupo de transporte en general ha registrado un +10,5 % anual (sobre todo por los carburantes de los coches). La subida que anuncia O’Leary es una previsión de los próximos 12 meses.
Xataka ya lo adelantaba el 16 de mayo. Los vuelos de 20 euros pueden pasar a ser una especie de reliquia por el cierre del estrecho de Ormuz y por el alto precio del queroseno.
Cómo seguir el precio de un vuelo
En todo caso, siempre podemos estar pendientes de cómo va el precio de nuestro viaje. Existen diferentes opciones. Por ejemplo, en Google Flights podemos seguir una ruta o un vuelo en concreto.
Además, en la ayuda oficial nos indican que podemos configurarlo para que nos manden un email cuando los precios caigan significativamente. La opción de cualquier fecha funciona mediante la caída del precio mínimo de la ruta en un mes. También tenemos la posibilidad de recibir un aviso cuando es probable que los precios vayan a subir (con una estimación de cuánto y de la fiabilidad).
El último dato de la semana en el monitor semanal de IATA se sitúa en 196,70 dólares por barril (un 2,2 % más que la semana anterior). Este dato es una referencia de mercado (no es el que realmente paga Ryanair), pero da idea de la diferencia que existe con los 85 dólares con los que tienen cubierto el 15 % de su combustible para 2027.

articles.title: On a essayé le Li Auto Li 6, la voiture électrique chinoise au look de TGV qui arrive en Europe — Frandroid
articles.text:
Vous aussi, vous en avez marre de la horde de SUV électriques qui pullulent dans les concessions, mais vous avez besoin d’espace à bord ? La nostalgie des monospaces pointe le bout de son nez ? Li Auto a peut-être sa solution avec son Li 6, fraîchement dévoilé au Mondial de Paris.
    Pour aller plus loin
Li Auto Li 6 : on est montés dans le SUV chinois qui peut faire trembler BMW et Mercedes
            
Et c’est précisément en marge du Mondial que nous avons pu faire un court galop d’essai de ce Li 6 dans des rues parisiennes, avant son lancement européen en 2027.
Un style unique
Première voiture de la marque chinoise à fouler le sol européen, le Li Auto Li 6 n’est autre qu’un i6 rebadgé, déjà vendu en Chine – BMW a sûrement dû avoir son mot à dire dans ce rebranding.
Le style n’a en aucun cas été modifié, de quoi faire ressortir ce grand crossover (4,95 m de long pour 1,94 m de large et 1,66 m de haut) de la circulation parisienne.
La face avant concentre tous les regards ; j’ai tendance à la comparer au Shinkansen, d’autres à un TGV, sans oublier quelques allusions au Fiat Multipla. On aimera ou non, mais ce Li 6 favorise la créativité.
Dans le détail, le capot se retrouve dans la quasi-continuité du pare-brise, dont la base est ceinte d’un jonc lumineux sur toute la largeur ; les parties techniques, dont les projecteurs et les prises d’air, se retrouvent en partie basse.
Le profil est lui aussi assez unique : outre la silhouette quasi-monovolume, la ligne de toit plonge dès les portes avant pour finir sur un épais aileron arrière. Le bénéfice est avant tout aérodynamique, le Li 6 revendiquant un coefficient de pénétration dans l’air (Cx) de seulement 0,218 – encore mieux que le 0,22 d’un Tesla Model Y. D’immenses jantes de 21 pouces habillent des flancs autrement très simples.
C’est au final l’arrière qui est le plus convenu, avec un design bien plus standardisé et, il faut le dire, assez convenu. Le grand bandeau, la lunette arrière très inclinée allant se perdre dans le spoiler… pas de quoi se retourner. Un léger regret par rapport au reste de la carrosserie, bien plus spectaculaire.
Un habitacle ultra spacieux
La découverte de l’habitacle du Li Auto Li 6 se fait en trois temps. Le premier, c’est la découverte de la planche de bord, dont le seul élément semble être cette immense dalle de 29 pouces, regroupant l’écran central et l’écran passager en un seul et même écran tactile – les informations de conduite sont reléguées sur l’extrémité de gauche, comme une Tesla, mais aussi dans une très généreuse vision tête-haute.
À vrai dire, le temps m’a manqué pour comprendre les forces et les faiblesses de cette immense dalle, mais cet aperçu fut assez positif, avec la possibilité d’afficher plusieurs types d’informations les unes à côté des autres. Android Auto et Apple CarPlay étaient également de la partie.
Puis vient la banquette arrière – le Li 6 possédant cinq places. L’espace aux jambes, en bonne voiture électrique chinoise, est immense, avec des réglages d’assise, de dossier, de chauffage et de ventilation – le siège arrière droit peut même s’allonger, comme une limousine.
Pour s’occuper, les passagers ont droit à un écran rien qu’à eux de 21 pouces, de quoi regarder des films en autonomie. Notons en parallèle une commande vocale a priori très performante.
Enfin, les espaces de rangements sont à noter. Li Auto annonce 728 litres pour le coffre arrière – un chiffre qui nous paraît optimiste, nous faisant penser que le chiffre désigne le volume jusqu’au plafond, un peu à la manière de Tesla.
En cas de besoin, un coffre avant (frunk) de 91 litres arrive à la rescousse, doté d’une astuce qui m’a beaucoup plu : il suffit de toquer sur le capot pour l’ouvrir électroniquement. Pas besoin de tirer une gâchette ou de sortir son téléphone : un vrai plus au quotidien.
Un premier tour de quartier
Une fiche technique musclée
Pour son arrivée en Europe, le Li Auto Li 6 pourra bénéficier d’une fiche technique plutôt alléchante. Uniquement dédié au 100 % électrique (des SUV à prolongateur suivront), le crossover embarque une batterie de 96 kWh alimentant un moteur arrière développé en interne de 250 kW (340 ch). Un version à quatre roues motrices ajoute un moteur avant, de quoi promettre 400 kW (544 ch).
L’autonomie ? 640 km selon le cycle WLTP, un chiffre à vrai dire assez faible vu la taille de la batterie : un BMW iX3 propose 645 km WLTP avec une batterie de « seulement » 82,6 kWh. Le Li Auto se rattrape sur la recharge, avec la capacité d’accepter jusqu’à 500 kW de puissance, de quoi passer de 10 à 80 % en 10 minutes – c’est deux fois plus rapide que le BMW.
Un châssis revu pour l’Europe
Si la fiche technique est identique au i6 vendu en Chine, Li Auto a pris la peine de retravailler le châssis pour s’adapter aux goûts européens : direction, liaisons au sol, suspension pneumatique et réponses des commandes ont été revues, avec plus de fermeté que la version chinoise privilégiant la souplesse.
C’est précisément un Li 6 « Euro Spec » que nous récupérons pour un court trajet dans un Paris englué par les manifestations étudiantes. Loin d’être optimal pour se faire une idée définitive de la voiture, mais quelques éléments sont tout de même à retenir.
La première, c’est la douceur générale de la voiture. Tout semble aseptisé : direction hyper légère, réponse de l’accélérateur très progressive, suspensions moelleuses… Comme souvent sur les voitures chinoises, le passage en mode « Sport » des différents éléments permettra d’avoir une synthèse un peu plus consistante, même si la suspension devient bien plus sèche dans ces conditions.
En tout cas, la position de conduite est bonne, la vision tête-haute affiche des informations utiles et le silence général semble être de très bon niveau. Le GPS (un système dédié à l’Europe), en revanche, n’est pas encore au niveau de Google Maps pour proposer les itinéraires les plus rapides.
Les aides à la conduite, enfin, n’étaient pas disponibles sur notre exemplaire, mais la présence d’un LiDAR en compagnie de caméras et de radars laisse croire à un système sophistiqué. Et… c’est à peu près tout ce que je peux dire pour le moment.
Une arrivée en France pas encore décidée
Li Auto arrive donc en Europe au premier trimestre 2027, à commencer par une voiture (le Li 6) et deux marchés : Pays-Bas et Norvège. D’autres marchés et d’autres modèles (dont les SUV à prolongateur d’autonomie, véritable spécialité de Li Auto) suivront… mais la France n’est jamais mentionnée.
Ajoutons à cela que ce Li 6 n’a pas encore de tarification précise, et difficile de se projeter sur ce modèle. Nous estimons un tarif d’accès autour des 60 à 65 000 euros, de quoi le placer face aux Xpeng G9 et BYD Atto 8, sans oublier les concurrents européens type BMW iX3, Audi Q6 e-tron ou Mercedes-Benz GLC.
Rendez-vous dans quelques mois pour le lancement officiel du Li 6 en Europe, de quoi connaître sa fiche technique définitive et ses tarifs européens ; quant à son arrivée en France, il n’y a plus qu’à espérer. Si les clients « tech », déjà convaincus par les Tesla et Xpeng, pourraient être séduits par cette proposition alternative, il faudra bien plus d’arguments pour aller chercher le grand public.
