articles.title: The Netherlands risks losing its AgriTech crown, warns new report | EU-Startups
articles.text:
The Netherlands has long been regarded as a European leader in agricultural and food innovation, but that position appears to be under threat.
A new report published today by Dutch national investment institution Invest-NL warns that the country risks losing its competitive edge as other nations move faster to commercialise emerging agricultural technologies.
According to the report, Deep Dive Agrifood Biotech, addressing the barriers facing Dutch agrifood biotechnology companies could unlock approximately €17 billion in additional annual revenue by 2040. However, without coordinated action on regulation, financing and commercialisation, much of that opportunity could be captured elsewhere.
Based on interviews with more than 150 entrepreneurs, investors, researchers and policymakers, alongside investment data spanning 2010 to April 2026, the study examines three strategic areas: seed breeding and genetics, biological agricultural inputs, and biotech-derived food ingredients.
A strong start, a weaker finish
The Netherlands is home to notable agricultural research institutions, established seed breeders and a sophisticated food production ecosystem. Yet it seems scientific excellence is not necessarily translating into globally competitive businesses.
The report highlights a particularly telling imbalance: the Netherlands accounts for 3.3% of BioTech startups worldwide, but only 1.3% of scale-ups, according to broader BioTech data cited from the Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research (TNO). This suggests that while the country remains effective at generating innovation, it is less successful at helping young companies achieve meaningful commercial scale.
Invest-NL identifies three recurring weaknesses:
- too few promising technologies become scalable ventures
- regulatory and validation processes delay market entry
- insufficient financing prevents companies from reaching industrial production
The stakes extend beyond individual businesses. In a favourable scenario, Invest-NL estimates that annual Dutch agrifood BioTech revenues could reach approximately €25 billion by 2040, compared with just €8–9 billion if current conditions persist.
Crucially, the report argues that the Netherlands does not need to manufacture everything domestically. Instead, it should focus on retaining strategically valuable knowledge, intellectual property, companies and specialised capabilities, while taking advantage of European production networks where appropriate.
Ten years to say yes
One of the most striking obstacles concerns biological crop protection, where Dutch companies are developing alternatives to conventional chemical pesticides.
Obtaining European regulatory approval for a new biological crop protection product can take eight to ten years. Existing frameworks were largely designed around chemical products, making them less suited to certain biological innovations.
Consequently, some companies prioritise launching in markets such as Brazil and the United States, where commercialisation can proceed more quickly. Invest-NL warns that Europe risks losing ground in a biological crop protection market that could expand seven- to tenfold by 2040.
Food biotechnology faces similar difficulties. Regulatory approval for novel ingredients can take one to three years longer in Europe than in the United States, while building a first commercial production facility can require tens or even hundreds of millions of euros.
For fermentation-derived food ingredients alone, Invest-NL estimates that favourable conditions could support approximately €8 billion in annual Dutch revenues by 2040, compared with around €2 billion under existing policies.
The report stresses that faster approvals should not come at the expense of safety. Instead, regulators should offer earlier guidance, more predictable assessments and opportunities for companies to validate products under real-world conditions.
Innovation is not the issue
Recent EU-Startups coverage demonstrates that Dutch AgriTech entrepreneurs continue to attract investor interest across several areas identified in the report.
In August, Eindhoven-based VitalFluid secured €17.2 million to accelerate the commercialisation of its plasma-activated water technology, which offers growers an alternative to chemical crop protection. The investment was co-led by Invest-NL and Alder Tree Investments.
Meanwhile, Wageningen-based Aardaia raised €5 million in July to advance its genomics-driven crop breeding platform and develop a protein-rich tuber, while Nijmegen-based Gravity Gardens secured €2.6 million in September to scale its chemical-free seed activation technology.
Dutch food BioTech is also producing notable funding announcements. In June, Vivici received €12.5 million in European Innovation Council backing to expand the supply and commercial reach of its precision-fermented dairy proteins.
Last year, EU-Startups also reported on Revyve’s nearly €24 million Series B to expand production of yeast-based ingredients that can replace eggs in food manufacturing. Revyve had already commissioned a first-of-a-kind production facility in the Netherlands, illustrating that industrial scale-up is achievable with sustained backing.
Nevertheless, these successes do not eliminate the wider structural challenges. They illustrate the breadth of Dutch innovation, but also the importance of providing companies with appropriate financing and support beyond their initial funding rounds.
Europe will not wait
Across Europe, EU-Startups has reported comparable investment activity, illustrating how competition is developing around the same technologies.
In biological crop protection, France’s Agriodor raised €15 million in April to expand its natural scent-based pest management technology, while Denmark’s Mycoverse secured €2.4 million in March to develop fungal alternatives to chemical pesticides.
The competition is equally visible in food ingredients. French precision fermentation startups Verley raised €32 million and Standing Ovation secured €30 million in 2026, while Belgian fermentation company MAASH obtained a €12.15 million financing package combining equity and public financing to support industrial-scale mycoprotein production.
These announcements do not establish that the Netherlands has already lost its position. They do, however, show that European competitors are securing capital, developing production capacity and pursuing commercial opportunities in precisely the areas where Invest-NL sees significant Dutch potential.
To respond, Invest-NL proposes an indicative €650 million to €1.1 billion in public financing capacity between 2026 and 2030, spanning research, regulatory improvements, infrastructure and industrial scale-up.
Its ambitions for 2030 include doubling the number of agrifood BioTech ventures, reducing time to market by a factor of three, and developing five globally competitive companies capable of raising more than €100 million each.
For the Netherlands, the question is therefore becoming less about whether it can develop the next generation of agricultural technologies, and more about whether it can create the conditions for those technologies to become successful businesses.

articles.title: Policybazaar parent PB Fintech net profit rises 43% rise in Q2
articles.text:
Policybazaar parent PB Fintech net profit rises 43% rise in Q2
The revenues for PB Fintech at the end of second quarter of FY27 stood at Rs 2178 crore which was an year-on-year growth of 35%
PB Fintech, the parent company of digital insurance platform Policybazaar and credit aggregator platform Paisabazaar, reported a 42.5% rise in net profit for the second quarter of FY27 while revenue rose by 35% in the same period.
PB Fintech reported a net profit of Rs 192.4 crore in the second quarter of FY27 as compared to Rs 135 crore in the similar period of last fiscal. The revenues for the second quarter came in at Rs 2177.7 crore.
According to the company, it recorded a total insurance premium of Rs 9,385 crore for the second quarter which was a 38% year-on-year (YoY) growth. The core online insurance premium business grew 42% YoY and new health insurance premium rose by 46% YoY. The total lending disbursal by PB Fintech in the second quarter stood at Rs 4,739 crore.
The company has around 5.5 lakh insurance advisors, which grew by 1.3 lakh during the quarter. According to the company, these distributors helped expand insurance access across smaller towns and cities, which contributed to 76 percent of overall gross written premium for the quarter.
This performance comes in the backdrop of Insurance Regulatory Development Authority (IRDA) proposal to lower the commissions earned by insurance agents and this could have an impact on the overall growth trajectory of PB Fintech.
On leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) in its operations, the company said it has 10 crore customer interactions every day. Around 21 lakh calls are processed daily which are 100% AI processed where the talk time exceeds 60 seconds across 7 Indian languages. It does 17 lakh minutes of conversation per day with 8x deeper analysis with AI.
The company processes seven lakh documents per day and this resulted in savings of 1,000 hours daily.
The changes due to AI have seen 15% plus productivity improvement in insurance advisors through AI-driven intent calling and 20% improvement in conversion.

articles.title: Offering Free Wi-Fi to Customers Without Opening a Door Into Your Own Systems - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Growing Demand for Customer Wi-Fi and the Security Challenge
In today’s digital landscape, offering free Wi-Fi to customers has become more than a convenience-it’s a business expectation. Whether you run a café, retail store, or any customer-facing business, providing seamless internet access can significantly enhance the customer experience and even drive repeat visits. With smartphones, tablets, and laptops becoming ubiquitous, customers often decide where to spend their time based on internet availability. A recent study shows that 58% of customers expect free Wi-Fi in public venues, making it a key competitive advantage for businesses.
However, this convenience comes with a critical cybersecurity challenge: how to offer free Wi-Fi without exposing your own internal networks to potential risks. The risk is not hypothetical. Many businesses struggle to separate their guest networks from their sensitive internal systems, increasing the risk of cyberattacks, data breaches, and unauthorized access. Cybercriminals often target unsecured guest Wi-Fi networks as an entry point to launch attacks on business infrastructure. According to IBM’s 2023 Cost of a Data Breach Report, the average cost of a data breach in 2023 was $4.45 million. This staggering figure highlights the financial and reputational consequences of inadequate network security.
Why Segmentation Is Essential in Wi-Fi Network Setup
The fundamental principle in safely offering free Wi-Fi is network segmentation. Network segmentation means creating separate virtual networks-one dedicated to your internal business operations and another exclusively for guest access. By doing so, you ensure that customers can access the internet without gaining any visibility into your internal servers, databases, or critical business applications. This separation is typically achieved through technologies such as VLANs (Virtual Local Area Networks) and firewalls that enforce strict boundaries between networks.
Failing to implement such segmentation puts your business at significant risk. Cyber attackers frequently exploit insecure guest networks to gain footholds inside corporate environments, potentially leading to ransomware attacks, data theft, or service disruptions. Segmentation acts as a vital barrier that restricts unauthorized lateral movement within your network.
Implementing this segmentation effectively requires expertise and a well-structured IT approach. For organizations seeking to secure IT with Red Bigfoot, partnering with specialists who understand the complexities of network architecture and cybersecurity best practices is crucial. This approach not only protects your internal systems but also ensures compliance with data protection regulations that increasingly mandate secure network practices.
Best Practices for Offering Secure Guest Wi-Fi
- Use a Dedicated Guest Network
Always configure a separate SSID (Service Set Identifier) for guest Wi-Fi. This network should be isolated from your internal systems using firewalls and VLANs. This ensures that devices connected to the guest network cannot communicate with devices on your corporate network. By logically separating these networks, you minimize the risk that a compromised guest device can access sensitive business resources.
- Employ Strong Authentication and Encryption
While offering free Wi-Fi, you don’t want to make access cumbersome, but it’s important to enforce at least minimal authentication, such as a simple password or a captive portal where users must agree to terms of service before connecting. Additionally, ensure that the network uses WPA3 encryption to protect data transmission. WPA3 is the latest Wi-Fi security protocol that offers enhanced protection against password guessing and eavesdropping.
- Monitor and Limit Bandwidth
To prevent abuse and maintain quality of service, set bandwidth limits or session timeouts. This not only protects your internet resources but also helps maintain network performance for all users. Monitoring network traffic can also help identify suspicious activity, such as unusually high data usage that might indicate malicious behavior.
- Regularly Update Firmware and Security Patches
Wi-Fi access points and routers need to be regularly updated to patch known vulnerabilities. An outdated device can be a weak link that jeopardizes your entire network. Vendors often release firmware updates that fix security flaws and improve device stability, so staying current is essential.
For businesses looking to implement these recommendations, consulting with experts like Technology Advisory Group, a local tech company can ensure your guest Wi-Fi is both user-friendly and secure. Professional guidance helps tailor the network design to your specific business needs, balancing ease of access with robust security controls.
Advanced Security Measures to Consider
Beyond basic segmentation and encryption, there are more advanced security features that can further protect your business when offering free Wi-Fi:
– Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS): These systems monitor the network for unusual or suspicious activity and can alert administrators to potential threats early. IDS can detect attempts to scan the network, brute-force attacks, or malware communication.
– Network Access Control (NAC): NAC ensures that only compliant and trusted devices can connect to the internal network, even if users attempt to bridge from the guest network. NAC can enforce security policies such as requiring updated antivirus software or blocking unauthorized devices.
– Regular Security Audits: Conducting routine audits helps identify vulnerabilities and ensures compliance with industry standards such as PCI-DSS for retail or HIPAA for healthcare. Audits also provide actionable insights for continuous improvement.
These advanced measures complement the foundational practices and create a layered defense strategy, significantly reducing risk.
The Role of Employee Training and Policy Enforcement
Technology alone is not enough. Employees should be trained on the importance of maintaining network security, recognizing phishing attempts, and reporting suspicious activity. Phishing remains one of the most common attack vectors, and well-informed staff are a critical line of defense.
Additionally, clear policies regarding guest Wi-Fi use and internal network access should be established and communicated. For example, employees should understand that they must not connect their devices to the guest network when accessing sensitive company resources. Enforcement of these policies is essential to prevent accidental security lapses.
Balancing Convenience with Security: The Business Benefits
When implemented correctly, offering free Wi-Fi can result in tangible benefits beyond customer satisfaction. Businesses report increased dwell time, higher engagement, and valuable data collection opportunities through captive portals. According to a survey, 70% of consumers are more likely to visit a business that offers free Wi-Fi. This enhanced customer engagement can translate into increased sales and brand loyalty.
Moreover, captive portals can be used to gather customer insights such as email addresses or preferences, enabling targeted marketing campaigns. This data-driven approach helps businesses better understand their clientele and tailor services accordingly.
However, these benefits must never come at the expense of security. Compromised business systems can lead to operational downtime, reputational damage, and regulatory fines. For instance, the average downtime cost for a business after a cyberattack can exceed $300,000 per hour. Therefore, investing in secure guest Wi-Fi infrastructure is both a protective measure and a business enabler.
Conclusion
Providing free Wi-Fi to customers is a powerful tool for enhancing the customer experience and maintaining competitive advantage. Yet, the risks associated with exposing internal networks cannot be ignored. By adopting network segmentation, employing strong authentication, and partnering with experienced cybersecurity professionals, businesses can offer safe and reliable guest Wi-Fi without opening a door into their own systems.
For companies serious about safeguarding their digital assets while delivering excellent customer service, exploring solutions should be a top priority. Engaging trusted local experts can help tailor the right technology strategy for your unique business needs.
In the ever-evolving landscape of cybersecurity threats, proactive measures today will protect your business tomorrow. Offering free Wi-Fi securely is not just about technology-it’s about preserving trust and enabling growth in a connected world.

articles.title: Josep Albors, experto en ciberseguridad, sobre apagar el móvil como aconseja Sánchez: “Para la mayoría de los usuarios sirve de poco”
articles.text:
Pedro Sánchez ha hablado de apagar el móvil 5 minutos cada día. Fue en La Revuelta donde lo comentaba en el momento en que hablaba sobre el tema del espionaje con Pegasus. Josep Albors, responsable de Investigación y Concienciación de ESET España, comenta: “Para la mayoría de los usuarios, que nos enfrentamos a amenazas más mundanas, este consejo, en materia de ciberseguridad, sirve de poco”. Además, dependiendo de cómo se instale y active, el programa malicioso tendrá efecto o no.
“Solo se aplica para casos concretos en los que el malware está presente en la memoria RAM, que se borra cuando reinicias el dispositivo”, explica Albors. El problema de esta memoria es que es temporal y se vacía al apagar el teléfono. En el caso de que la infección solo se active en memoria (sin persistencia), puede ser interrumpida por el apagado.
El problema es que, si el software malicioso está instalado en el terminal, al apagar y encender el móvil no va a desinstalar la app maligna. Así pues, puede volver a activarse al encenderlo. Además, no podemos estar seguros de que la infección haya desaparecido por el hecho de que el móvil vuelva a funcionar correctamente. Es necesario conocer la naturaleza de la amenaza y trabajar sobre su causa.
Los límites del reinicio frente al malware
Por otro lado, en la Agencia de Seguridad Nacional de EE. UU. (NSA) se recomienda apagar/encender el dispositivo semanalmente. Esto puede ayudar a cortar ciertas infecciones. Sin embargo, esto no quiere decir que sea una forma generalizada de protegerse de malware. Además, no soluciona el problema de seguridad que se ha usado para acceder al móvil (como indica el informe de la agencia francesa de ciberseguridad).
El programa espía de NSO Group (Pegasus) permite acceder a la información del móvil. También puede usar la cámara o el micrófono. Existen algunas versiones que pueden activarse en memoria (sin persistencia). Esto complica su detección. De esta manera, apagar el dispositivo puede eliminar el programa activo. Aun así, el atacante puede conservar un medio de acceso para volver a entrar.
Hay que tener en cuenta que, aunque eliminemos el spyware con un reinicio, si no corregimos la vulnerabilidad que se ha explotado, simplemente con conocer el número de teléfono de la víctima, puede volver a infectarse este dispositivo. Además, existen ataques que no requieren que el dueño del móvil pulse ningún enlace o descargue ningún archivo.
También hay que destacar que no todas las versiones son iguales. Se han documentado versiones que son resistentes al reinicio. Además de esto, al hacer persistente el malware, puede dejarse más rastro en el sistema. Así pues, no podemos asegurar que, al apagar y encender el móvil, quedará eliminada esta clase de infección.
Este tipo de espionaje (con herramientas que emplean las agencias estatales en sus objetivos seleccionados) es muy diferente a lo que suele preocupar a la mayoría de los usuarios. Según Albors, frente a las amenazas habituales, poco ayuda el reinicio. Los usuarios deben preocuparse de amenazas como apps maliciosas o enlaces fraudulentos.
Qué hacer para proteger el móvil
Por otro lado, también puede ser útil apagar/reiniciar el móvil de vez en cuando. Por ejemplo, para cerrar apps en segundo plano o resolver problemas de memoria. Es útil en ciertas circunstancias para que el móvil funcione más fluido. Sin embargo, esto no quiere decir que esté limpio de malware.
Para ello es importante mantener actualizado el dispositivo (con las correcciones de seguridad). También es relevante no fiarse de enlaces que no hemos pedido. Además de esto, es muy recomendable no instalar apps que no provengan de los canales oficiales. También es interesante disponer de una solución de seguridad que analice el dispositivo y las conexiones. El alcance de estas herramientas depende del SO y de los permisos que tengan.

articles.title: Un sous-marin volé de 4 tonnes a été mis en vente sur Leboncoin pour 100 €
articles.text:
Aussi surprenant que cela puisse paraître, deux hommes ont eu l’idée de voler un sous-marin de quatre tonnes et de le mettre ensuite en vente sur Leboncoin. Heureusement, le véhicule a été rapidement retrouvé, comme le rapporte l’Est Républicain. Celui-ci était entreposé sur un terrain à découvert en l’attente d’un acheteur.
Un sous-marin de 4 tonnes volé
Entre le 1ᵉʳ et le 21 octobre, un sous-marin de quatre tonnes a été volé dans l’Ain (Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes). Bien entendu, les malfrats n’ont pas subtilisé l’engin dans les abysses, ce dernier servait de décoration dans un magasin de plongée. Ils ont tout simplement remorqué le sous-marin et sont repartis avec. Le gérant du magasin a immédiatement alerté la police lorsqu’il s’est rendu compte du vol, tout en débutant sa propre enquête qui l’a amené sur…. Leboncoin.
L’engin mis en vente sur Leboncoin pour 100 euros
Heureusement, le véhicule sous-marin a été retrouvé très rapidement par le gérant du magasin de plongée. Il faut dire que le véhicule avait été mis en vente sur le site Leboncoin pour la modique somme de 100 euros. Cette somme de 100 euros est en réalité un faux prix pour attirer ceux intéressés par ce sous-marin dont la valeur estimée avoisine plusieurs milliers d’euros. Les malfrats auraient ensuite effectué des négociations avec les potentiels acheteurs.
Les enquêteurs ont regroupé les différentes informations disséminées dans l’annonce et ont identifié le profil du vendeur. Ils ont ensuite placé le vendeur sous surveillance et sont ainsi parvenus à localiser le sous-marin volé. Le véhicule a finalement été retrouvé le 26 octobre à environ 120 kilomètres du magasin de plongée, dans le secteur de Planoise.
Deux hommes, âgés de 27 ans et 47 ans, ont été arrêtés. Le sous-marin était entreposé chez l’homme de 27 ans, sur un terrain à découvert. La police précise que leurs justifications concernant ce vol sont à l’heure actuelle « parcellaires ». Il faut dire que le vol d’un sous-marin de quatre tonnes doit être difficile à justifier. Quoi qu’il en soit, le gérant du magasin de plongée pourra bientôt récupérer son élément de décoration.

articles.title: Netflix Titus Adds Single-Tenant VM Isolation for Containers
articles.text:
Netflix has added single-tenant Titus, a mode that runs one task alone on its own right-sized EC2 instance. The Compute/Platform team still owns and patches the host, so application teams keep the same API and deployment path. First adopters include stateful, high-throughput streaming workloads. Here, a neighbor's interference can lead to minutes of checkpoint recovery.
Titus launches millions of containers a week across tens of thousands of EC2 instances and is multi-tenant by default. Netflix says that cgroups, seccomp, the iocost controller, and traffic shaping can’t split shared hardware. This includes resources like the last-level cache and memory bandwidth. Its HTB traffic shaper also takes a global lock. A container that floods the host with small packets can burn the kernel CPU and starve its neighbors. Predictive CPU pinning and eBPF-based detection helped, but Netflix concluded that shared-kernel tuning narrows the gap without closing it.
Netflix rejected the alternatives for specific reasons. MicroVMs such as Firecracker and Kata need bare-metal or nested virtualization, and nested virtualization was not ready on Netflix's instance types. They also meant running a hypervisor layer, added virtualization overhead, and lacked GPU support. gVisor added overhead on I/O-heavy paths, and a single vendor does most of its maintenance. Running containers on EC2 would hand host patching and fleet sizing back to application teams. Netflix argues that these workloads require performance isolation, not defense against hostile tenants.
The Titus federation layer does most of the work. An allowlist, maintained by the Compute/Platform team, controls eligibility and federation records, which instance families a task may use. The autoscaler launches the smallest instance that fits the task's CPU, memory, and GPU request. Pod anti-affinity, a non-preemptible priority class, and a node taint enforce one task per node. Netflix disables defragmentation, so nothing relocates the task. To measure isolation, Netflix runs a reference app alone, then beside a "havoc" container, and scores retained throughput and P99 latency. The post publishes no scores.
Launch latency is the main cost. A fresh instance needs tens of seconds to boot before the image pull begins. Warm pools help less than on the shared fleet, because right-sizing produces many instance shapes. Netflix keeps a small warm pool for the most latency-sensitive starts and limits the available sizes. It dropped metal instances for these pools. Disabling Kubernetes preemption removed a scheduling bottleneck that left new nodes idle. Lazy image pulling (stargz, SOCI) and CRIU checkpoint restore are longer-term fixes.
Efficiency can improve. Moving sensitive workloads off shared hosts removes the anti-affinity spreading and disruption budgets that left those hosts partly empty. Fixed overhead from sidecars and system services pulls the other way. Netflix says it can cost a small instance tens of percent of its resources, and the largest shapes only a couple of percent. Discrete EC2 sizes also leave bin-packing gaps on large shared hosts, which favored right-sizing in practice.
Early users include managed Apache Flink, streaming data connectors, and telemetry and logging pipelines. Then, there are some latency-sensitive GraphQL and edge services. The rollout continues. For the shared fleet, Netflix is working on eBPF-based Expected Departure Time shaping to replace HTB, plus cache and memory-bandwidth partitioning (Intel RDT, AMD PQoS), NVIDIA MIG, and the cgroup v2 IO controller. Its long-term goal is one Compute API that picks EC2 or Titus placement from declared intent.
Single-tenant Titus joins a broader set of approaches to the same problem. Instance-per-Pod Webhook, an open-source project from NTT’s Akihiro Suda, uses a Kubernetes admission webhook and the Cluster Autoscaler to create a tainted, dedicated instance for each pod. AWS Fargate makes the pod the unit of infrastructure, so customers do not create, patch, or scale worker nodes. GKE offers sole-tenant nodes, dedicated physical servers that run only a single project’s VMs, along with GKE Sandbox, which runs each pod in its own Kata Containers microVM. Azure’s Pod Sandboxing is also built on Kata and gives each pod its own lightweight VM, isolated from other pod VMs and the host kernel. Most of these target security isolation from untrusted code, while Netflix’s post focuses on performance isolation between trusted internal teams.
Teams running shared Kubernetes platforms can borrow the pattern: dedicated node pools with taints, anti-affinity, and repacking turned off. Netflix recommends it for large, long-running, disruption-sensitive workloads sized close to a node shape and not for small or bursty services. The allowlist keeps the mode from eroding multi-tenant density.

articles.title: Stablecoins gain ground in Africa but face hurdles to use
articles.text:
Stablecoins are giving African businesses an alternative way to pay overseas suppliers, but costs, security concerns and fragmented blockchain networks remain obstacles to wider use, industry executives told Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos.
Speaking on a panel titled, “Where Are Stablecoins Creating Real Value in Africa?”, representatives from Solana Superteam Nigeria, Obiex and Hyperbridge said demand was being driven by practical difficulties in accessing foreign currency and completing international payments.
Chinonso Obiefule, lead at Solana Superteam Nigeria, said some Nigerian businesses were already using stablecoins to pay suppliers in China when dollars were difficult to obtain through conventional channels.
“People want to access dollars, but they cannot do that because, obviously, dollars aren’t easily accessible, so the next best option is actually stablecoin,” he said.
The appeal extends beyond access to foreign currency. Businesses trading across time zones also need to move funds outside banking hours, said Odinaka Esiagu, head of customer success and operations at Obiex.
A company buying goods from a Chinese supplier might need to complete a payment while its bank was closed, she said. Stablecoins could allow it to transfer funds without waiting until the next banking day.
Esiagu said the technology would improve the flexibility of certain transactions rather than eliminate the need for banks.
The discussion reflected the growing role of dollar-linked digital assets in Nigeria’s financial system. The country received about $59 billion in crypto-asset inflows between July 2023 and June 2024, according to the IMF.
That figure covers crypto assets broadly, rather than stablecoins alone. The fund also estimates that Nigeria has accounted for roughly 60 per cent of stablecoin inflows into sub-Saharan Africa since 2019.
Costs and confidence
For businesses, however, a new payment channel must offer more than availability. Obiefule said developers needed to make international transfers cheaper, safer and easier to use.
“It should be cheaper to send money to somebody abroad or to get money from somebody abroad,” he said.
Low blockchain transaction fees were an important consideration for companies choosing which networks to use, he added. Lower costs could make stablecoin payments commercially viable for more businesses.
Trust remained another constraint. Esiagu said reports of cryptocurrency platforms being hacked continued to deter potential customers.
“Some people are still scared,” she said.
Obiex was developing a service to help businesses build stablecoin-based products by providing technical and compliance-related support, she added. The aim was to allow companies to focus on their customers without having to develop all the underlying capabilities themselves.
Connecting separate networks
Seun Lanlege, chief executive of Hyperbridge, said fragmentation across blockchains created a further challenge: funds available on one network were not necessarily readily accessible on another.
That limited users’ ability to draw on liquidity across platforms, complicating the promise of seamless transfers.
Lanlege said Hyperbridge provided infrastructure for moving tokens between networks, while its HyperFX product used those connections to facilitate transactions across blockchain ecosystems.
Such systems needed to prioritise security and decentralisation, he argued, warning that reliance on centralised intermediaries could create vulnerabilities.
Regulation also remains central to the market’s development. The IMF has called for clearer treatment of stablecoin issuers in Nigeria, alongside stronger oversight and better data on how digital assets interact with the domestic financial system.
It has warned that widespread use of dollar-denominated stablecoins could weaken monetary policy transmission and create financial integrity risks.

articles.title: Por qué el dolor de espalda crónico se siente tan personal: el cerebro lo trata como parte de quiénes somos
articles.text:
Las personas que conviven con el dolor de espalda crónico saben bien que, de un modo u otro, se ha convertido en parte de su personalidad. Despiertan cada mañana atentos a las sensaciones del nuevo día, cancelan planes por los dolores, dejan de practicar deportes que adoraban o incluso de coger en brazos a sus propios hijos… Es mucho más que un simple dolor. De hecho, está tan sumamente arraigado a la personalidad que, según un nuevo estudio, activa zonas del cerebro relacionadas con la autoconciencia. Es un descubrimiento interesante tanto por dar explicación a algo que en cierto modo intuíamos como porque puede abrir la puerta a nuevos y necesarios tratamientos.
Señales distintas en el cerebro. Para comprobar las diferencias entre el procesamiento cerebral de un dolor agudo o un dolor crónico, como puede ser el de espalda, un equipo de científicos de la Universidad de California San Diego reclutó a 114 personas que padecen dolor de espalda crónico. Es decir, un dolor lumbar que lleva más de 12 semanas sin resolución. Con el fin de provocar un episodio de dolor, se les hizo realizar una prueba de elevación de piernas. Pero también era necesario causar un dolor agudo en otra parte del cuerpo, así que se les aplicó un calor molesto en la pantorrilla.
Al estudiar su cerebro mediante resonancia magnética funcional, se vio que en el caso del dolor agudo disminuyó la actividad en un conjunto de regiones asociadas a la autoconciencia, conocido como red neuronal por defecto (DMN). En cambio, con el dolor lumbar ocurrió todo lo contrario: aumentó la actividad en dicha zona.
Los motivos. La DMN procesa todos esos pensamientos que forman parte de quiénes somos: las reflexiones sobre experiencias personales, los pensamientos sobre nuestra identidad, la observación de nuestras propias emociones… Son pensamientos casi constantes en nuestro día a día. Por su parte, el dolor agudo a menudo es una señal de alerta de que algo no va bien. Sentimos dolor al tocar algo muy caliente para poder apartar la mano y no quemarnos. Por eso, en casos de dolor agudo se desactiva temporalmente la DMN. Es necesario dejar espacio en el cerebro para procesar lo que ha causado la alerta.
En cambio, con el dolor crónico no hay nada externo a lo que haya que prestar atención. Forma parte de la persona y, además, puede traerle a la mente recuerdos de otras experiencias en las que sintió dolor o miedo a cómo lo percibirá en el futuro. Los autores del estudio creen que el dolor puede incluso generar un sentimiento de vergüenza por las actividades que no se pueden realizar. Todo eso lo procesa la DMN. Posiblemente esa es la causa por la que aumenta la actividad.
Aplicaciones. Los autores de este estudio han comenzado a realizar ensayos clínicos en los que se trata el dolor lumbar crónico mediante mindfulness y psilocibina. El primero es una técnica de meditación basada en la atención plena, mientras que el segundo es una sustancia psicodélica. Ninguno es capaz de eliminar el dolor, ni agudo ni crónico. Sin embargo, vistas las conclusiones de este estudio, sí que podrían tener aplicaciones interesantes en lo referente a la relación entre el dolor y la autoconciencia.
Por un lado, el mindfulness centra la atención en el ahora, de modo que la mente no vuela hacia experiencias de dolor pasadas o temores del futuro. Y, por otro, la psilocibina, como otros psicodélicos, es capaz de “abrir las puertas del cerebro” y modular su actividad. En este caso, se cree que podría reiniciar el sistema de dolor que integra traumas, experiencias pasadas y preocupaciones futuras para facilitar un reinicio. Todo esto, junto a los fármacos que sí van dirigidos directamente a la sensación de dolor, puede componer un tratamiento muy interesante para personas con dolor crónico.
Las cifras. Según una encuesta realizada por el INE en 2025, el dolor crónico lumbar afecta al 21,8% de las mujeres y al 13,6% de los hombres en España. Además, el barómetro de la lumbalgia de 2024 estimó que el 80% de los españoles tendrá algún episodio de dolor lumbar a lo largo de su vida, y que la edad media de los pacientes con dolor crónico y lumbalgia es de 51,3 años. Son muchísimas las personas que pueden verse beneficiadas por la comprensión de los mecanismos que están involucrados en este tipo de dolor. Solo así se podrán obtener tratamientos realmente transversales que no se centren únicamente en la sensación de dolor, sino también en cómo lo procesa nuestro cerebro.

articles.title: A University of Kentucky employee asked to be exempted from using AI for his 'religious' beliefs
articles.text:
Editor's take: Many research and enterprise organizations are trying to force staff to use AI tools wherever and whenever they can. Needless to say, the backlash is as strong as the C-suite's stubborn determination to push AI, even where there is absolutely no need for it.
David Durman might be the first employee to receive a special exemption from using AI tools on religious grounds. The 45-year-old research administrator at the University of Kentucky identifies as a humanist, a belief system that apparently requires him to avoid AI-based workflows. Durman's job doesn't require AI either, which is likely the main reason the university ultimately agreed to his unusual request.
Durman decided to take the religious route after his university's administrators began asking all employees to adopt AI in their work. In a recent interview, Durman said that he felt the request ran counter to his fundamental ideas about what it means to be human. In his view, the university was asking a fully conscious adult to offload his entire thought process to a chatbot to perform his daily duties.
Durman stated that "the process and work involved in thinking through situations, through my work, through my ethics, through the way I handle other people, is a key component in being able to develop myself as a moral person." Offloading that process to a commercial LLM tool was essentially undercutting his agency as a moral and conscious being.
Broadly speaking, humanism is neither a religion in the conventional sense nor a clearly defined philosophical movement. Rather, it is a philosophical stance shared by various intellectual traditions that emphasize universal human qualities, the pursuit of knowledge, and the improvement of individual and social conditions.
Durman's "quest" was supported by the American Humanist Association (AHA), with both parties seeking a religious accommodation from the University of Kentucky under Title VII. Federal law allows employees to request workplace accommodations that enable them to adhere to their religious beliefs.
The university agreed to Durman's request in September, granting the administrator special permission to avoid using Copilot, ChatGPT, and other LLM-based "stochastic parrots" in his work. Before working with the AHA, Durman sent a letter to university administrators in which he quoted the Humanist Manifesto III, which the organization first published in 2003.
In the interview, Durman confirmed that he could do his job without resorting to chatbots. At the university, he helps researchers with grant applications and related tasks. According to AHA attorney Alexandria Huiskens, the parties had a "very collegial" meeting during which Durman confirmed that avoiding AI would not burden his department or reduce its productivity.
Recent polls suggest that employees are increasingly stressed by organizations' efforts to fully integrate AI into their workflows. Durman argues that AI could have a very negative impact on society as a whole, while humanist principles run counter to what he sees as a turbo-capitalistic, nihilistic approach to exploiting human nature. In this regard, Huiskens said Durman's "religion" could be considered a "comprehensive way of life," much like Christianity and Islam.

articles.title: Reolink Argus MagiCam : on a testé la caméra polyvalente qui se fixe avec un aimant et ne nécessite aucun abonnement
articles.text:
| Ergonomie et installation |  | 
| Alimentation | Batterie | 
| Connexion | Wi-Fi | 
| Port microSD | Oui | 
| Compatibilité | Android, iOS | 
| Utilisation en extérieur | Oui | 
| Application |  | 
| Reconnaissance des visages | Non | 
| Abonnement | Non | 
| Qualité d'image |  | 
| Définition | 1920 x 1080 (Full HD) | 
| Angle de vision | NA | 
| Mode nuit | Oui | 
| Qualité audio |  | 
| Haut-parleur | Oui | 
| Microphone | Oui | 
| Fonction Alarme | Oui | 
Aussi à l’aise à l’intérieur qu’en extérieur, l’Argus MagiCam de Reolink mise sur sa simplicité d’utilisation et, surtout, sa grande flexibilité pour trouver sa place partout sans sortir le moindre tournevis.
Le catalogue de caméras de surveillance de Reolink ne cesse de s’étendre. Le constructeur chinois propose toujours plus de fonctionnalités avec des modèles conçus tantôt pour garder un œil sur les extérieurs, tantôt pour l’intérieur avec moult possibilités de réglages et de technologies embarquées. À l’autre bout du spectre, la marque propose aussi des caméras moins ambitieuses, mais qui séduisent par leur simplicité. C’est le cas de l’Argus MagiCam.
Cette petite caméra aligne en effet les bonnes idées pour faciliter non seulement son installation, mais aussi son utilisation au quotidien, tout en conservant un prix très abordable. Last but not least, elle n’est pas soumise à un abonnement obligatoire pour faire son office et signaler la présence d’intrus.
Avec un tarif de 59 €, elle compte bien faire de l’ombre à la Blink Outdoor 2K+ d’Amazon (99 €) au look presque similaire, mais qui reste associée à un abonnement obligatoire pour profiter de toutes ses fonctions.
Nous avons testé la Reolink Argus MagiCam sous la version 3.0.0, build 6362_26042310 du logiciel interne de l’appareil et les versions 4.630.3.20260924 (Android) et 4.64 (iOS) de l’app mobile.
Cette petite caméra de forme carrée ne mesure que 6,8 cm de côté pour une épaisseur de 2,9 cm. Elle se montre donc très discrète, à une exception près : sa couleur. Reolink a opté effectivement pour une robe blanche, un coloris qui ne réussit pas toujours à se fondre dans le décor.
En revanche, la marque a redoublé d’effort pour simplifier sa mise en place. Derrière le capot au dos de l’appareil se cache un aimant de bonne puissance. Grâce à lui, il est possible de plaquer la MagiCam sur n’importe quelle surface contenant du fer : une rambarde de balcon, une gouttière, un support de fenêtre, la porte du réfrigérateur, un pied de lampe, etc.
Les possibilités sont multiples et ne nécessitent aucun bricolage. Pas de trou à percer, pas de colle ! Une particularité qui offre une grande liberté, puisqu’il est possible de poser la MagiCam presque n’importe où et, surtout, de la déplacer à l’envi pour surveiller tantôt une zone, tantôt une autre en extérieur ou en intérieur.
Aucune surface métallique à l’horizon ? Pas de problème. Reolink livre dans la boîte un petit disque de métal affublé d’un adhésif. Il suffit de le coller à un mur ou sur toute autre surface plane et lisse pour y fixer la caméra.
Toujours dans la boîte, on trouve un pied doté lui aussi d’une plaque métallique pour accueillir la caméra. Il peut être posé sur un bureau, dans une bibliothèque, etc., et permet d’orienter la caméra sur 360° à l’horizontale et 180° à la verticale.
Il peut aussi se fixer au mur ou au plafond grâce à la visserie fournie elle aussi. Reolink a donc pensé à toutes les possibilités, de la plus simple à la plus complexe selon l’environnement et l’angle de vue souhaité, et c’est très appréciable.
Seconde particularité : la MagiCam propose deux modes d’alimentation. Elle peut tirer son énergie d’un câble USB-C (un exemplaire d’une longueur de 95 cm est fourni) branché à un chargeur de 5 V (non fourni) ou de deux piles AA. Reolink en livre une paire au lithium dans la boîte. Ce dispositif présente l’avantage de ne pas avoir de batterie à recharger, donc d’attendre avant de reprendre la surveillance.
Selon la marque, deux piles au lithium permettent d’envisager jusqu’à neuf mois d’autonomie. Attention, cela ne vaut que si la caméra n’est pas installée dans une zone à forts passages où les déclenchements d’enregistrements peuvent être nombreux. Quelques astuces permettent néanmoins de réduire la consommation d’énergie. Il suffit d’abaisser la sensibilité, activer la réduction des fausses alarmes (pour éviter que le vent dans les feuilles des arbres ne déclenche un enregistrement, par exemple), ou encore d’allonger l’intervalle de déclenchement du capteur PIR, réglé par défaut à 5 s.
Avant de placer les piles dans leur logement, il est recommandé de glisser d’abord la mémoire microSD (jusqu’à 256 Go) dans son slot. Elle permettra de stocker les vidéos en local, ce qui évite de souscrire un quelconque abonnement.
Le port USB-C placé sur le flanc gauche est protégé par une lamelle de silicone pour résister aux intempéries. La MagiCam revendique un indice IP67 lui permettant de passer sa vie dehors sous la pluie et la neige avec une plage de températures comprises entre -10 °C et +55 °C.
À l’opposé, sur le flanc droit, une grille protège le petit haut-parleur. Associé au micro installé en façade entre le capteur de mouvements PIR et l’objectif, il permet de mener des conversations.
Pour se connecter au réseau wifi du domicile, la MagiCam peut exploiter les deux bandes de fréquences 2,4 et 5 GHz. Néanmoins, Reolink a vu un peu léger dans le choix de la norme. Le réseau sans-fil exploite en effet la norme 802.11n au mieux, soit du wifi 4 (nous en sommes actuellement à la version 7). Autrement dit, il ne faudra pas trop éloigner la caméra du routeur ou de la box internet pour profiter d’une connexion solide. Un point à prendre en considération si la caméra doit siéger en extérieur.
Si l’Argus MagiCam offre une très grande souplesse pour son installation, celle-ci est à double tranchant. Comme elle peut être collée quasiment partout, elle peut aussi être dérobée facilement puisque l’appareil en lui-même n’est jamais fixé, mais juste retenu par un aimant. Heureusement pour les données stockées dans la carte mémoire, celles-ci sont chiffrées.
Simple dans l’installation, la MagiCam l’est aussi dans son utilisation. Et pour cause, puisqu’il ne s’agit pas du modèle le plus perfectionné du catalogue du constructeur. Quelques minutes suffisent ainsi pour en prendre le contrôle et opérer les réglages adéquats pour démarrer la surveillance.
L’application fournie par Reolink se révèle ainsi assez basique, mais comporte l’essentiel. La page d’accueil est constituée de la vue en direct et de quelques fonctions. Il est possible ici de déclencher une conversation, enregistrer une photo ou une vidéo saisie par la caméra directement sur le smartphone, activer la sirène, ou encore d’accéder aux séquences enregistrées sur la carte mémoire de l’appareil.
La présentation se révèle assez simple avec le choix du jour des enregistrements et la liste des séquences horodatées. Par contre, il n’est pas possible d’effectuer un tri par type d’événement (détection de personnes, d’animaux, de véhicules, etc.). Cette subtilité est réservée à ceux qui ont souscrit un abonnement au cloud de Reolink (à partir de 3,59 € mensuels).
La page des réglages permet d’affiner la détection. La MagiCam sait faire la distinction entre les silhouettes humaines, les animaux et les véhicules. Pour chacun de ces critères, il est possible d’ajuster la sensibilité et les dimensions à prendre en compte.
L’app propose également d’appliquer un masque de confidentialité afin de ne pas tenir compte de certaines zones de l’image. Pratique si une partie publique (voirie, palier, etc.) figure dans le champ. En revanche, la caméra étant démunie de clapet physique, la bascule vers un mode aveugle pour retrouver un peu d’intimité n’est que logicielle.
Le reste des réglages est réduit au strict minimum. Il n’est pas possible d’ajuster la qualité de l’image ou même le flux vidéo, limité à 15 images par seconde (i/s) lorsque la caméra fonctionne sur piles et à 20 lorsqu’elle est branchée en USB-C. On peut toutefois jouer sur différents réglages (luminosité, contrastes, etc.) et la puissance du haut-parleur, activer ou non la led d’état, donner les autorisations pour gérer la MagiCam depuis Google Home ou Alexa, etc.
Quant aux notifications, elles bénéficient de quelques ajustements pour ne pas en recevoir à tout bout de champ. On note au passage que seuls les abonnés au cloud de Reolink profitent de notifications comportant texte et images. Par ailleurs, aucune notification n’est expédiée si la caméra devient inaccessible en cas de déconnexion du réseau. En revanche, lorsque les piles montrent des signes de faiblesse, plusieurs notifications sont émises.
Reolink indique que sa caméra peut détecter les mouvements jusqu’à 10 m. Les tests effectués dans notre laboratoire montrent plutôt une détection fiable jusqu’à 7-8 m de distance, de jour comme de nuit. Avec la sensibilité du capteur PIR (capteur infrarouge passif) réglée au maximum, les résultats s’avèrent plutôt bons. La qualité de reconnaissance des éléments en déplacement est en revanche plus aléatoire.
Il faut tâtonner un peu pour définir les bons réglages (taille des éléments à prendre en compte et sensibilité) pour parvenir à un résultat correct. La caméra a toutefois pu différencier un être humain d’un animal jusqu’à 5 m. C’est plutôt confortable. En revanche, elle n’est jamais parvenue à identifier notre chat comme un animal, se contentant d’indiquer seulement la détection d’un mouvement.
De jour, il est possible de reconnaître aisément des visages jusqu’à 9 m. De nuit, l’affaire se complique au-delà de 5 m.
Pour mener sa surveillance et délivrer des preuves exploitables, la MagiCam se repose sur un unique objectif. Il s’agit bien sûr d’un ultra grand-angle offrant 113,9° à l’horizontale, 62,7° à la verticale et 132° en diagonale.
C’est suffisant pour surveiller une pièce ou un petit jardin. Derrière la lentille, un capteur CMOS 1/3,2 pouce est à la manœuvre, produisant des images en Full HD (1920 x 1080 pixels).
Avec son petit capteur de 2 Mpx, la MagiCam parvient à délivrer des images correctes, sans plus. Devant notre scène, elle éprouve quelques difficultés à restituer les détails. Les aplats sont nombreux et le lissage important. Néanmoins, l’image demeure assez nette au centre comme en périphérie. Les contrastes sont assez accentués et les contours de certains éléments bavent légèrement. Comparée à l’E1 Pro de Reolink sortie en 2025 et munie d’un capteur de 3 Mpx, elle se montre bien moins précise et présente des couleurs plus pâlichonnes. Un petit détour dans les réglages pour améliorer la netteté, la saturation, la luminosité ou encore le contraste permet d’obtenir un meilleur rendu.
La bascule vers le mode nocturne assisté des lampes infrarouges demande deux 2 s. Les images délivrées par la MagiCam perdent encore un peu en précision, mais le résultat demeure cohérent. La netteté reste au rendez-vous, mais la faiblesse du capteur pénalise encore un peu plus la lisibilité des petits éléments. La colonne de visages à gauche de notre scène conserve toutefois suffisamment de détails. L’ensemble souffre d’un aspect délavé face aux images produites par l’E1 Pro, sans pénaliser la lecture.
Parée d’un micro en façade et d’un haut-parleur sur le côté, la MagiCam permet de mener une conversation audio avec un interlocuteur situé à proximité d’elle. À deux 2 m tout au plus, car si le micro se montre assez efficace pour percevoir les voix jusqu’à 4 ou 5 m, ce n’est pas le cas du petit haut-parleur. La saturation se matérialise assez rapidement, accompagnée de crachotements et grésillements désagréables à l’oreille.
En mode surveillance, le son enregistré reste très correct et perceptible si l’intrus se situe jusqu’à 5 m de la caméra.
Reste la sirène dont la présence est plus symbolique qu’autre chose. Avec les 58 dB (A) mesurés à 1 m de distance, elle ne pourra pas effrayer d’éventuels intrus. Vos voisins pourront, s'ils l'entendent, aisément la confondre avec un réveil.
L’Argus MagiCam de Reolink ne manque pas d’atouts pour séduire. Son petit gabarit, son fonctionnement sur piles et sa facilité d’installation grâce à son système magnétique donnent toute latitude pour surveiller presque n’importe quelle zone sans se lancer dans des travaux. La détection se montre satisfaisante et la qualité d’image suffit pour mener une surveillance efficace. Il faudra tout de même garder un œil sur la consommation d’énergie s’il s’agit de surveiller un endroit très fréquenté, et ne pas compter sur la sirène pour effrayer qui que ce soit. Mais à ce tarif, et sans abonnement obligatoire, la MagiCam se présente comme une très bonne solution.
Peu de caméras de surveillance adoptent le principe de fonctionnement sur piles. À ce petit jeu, c’est la Blink Outdoor 2K+ d’Amazon qui se pose en meilleure candidate. Elle offre des images 2K, adopte presque le même gabarit et Blink promet deux ans d’autonomie avec des piles au lithium. Cependant, la caméra n’enregistre rien en local et un abonnement (à partir de 3 €/mois) est obligatoire pour bénéficier de toutes ses fonctions.

articles.title: Del tránsito a las inspecciones: cómo la inteligencia artificial empieza a cambiar las decisiones de los gobiernos
articles.text:
Las decisiones que hasta hace poco se resolvían con recorridas, planillas y criterios administrativos empiezan a pasar por sistemas capaces de cruzar el tránsito, el clima, los reclamos vecinales y los antecedentes de una inspección. La inteligencia artificial transforma la gestión pública en las ciudades, donde promete ordenar recursos y anticipar problemas, pero también obliga a responder quién define sus reglas y quién asume las consecuencias cuando falla.
El analista Emmanuel Ferrario situó ese cambio en la vida cotidiana de los gobiernos. “La IA está atravesando las ciudades”, afirmó en Infobae A las Nueve al enumerar aplicaciones vinculadas con el empleo, el transporte, las inspecciones y la seguridad.
Para Ferrario, la discusión ya no se limita a incorporar tecnología: alcanza a la forma en que el Estado decide usarla sobre servicios y trámites que afectan a la población.
Ese avance, explicó, parte de una diferencia visible entre los países que ya cuentan con capacidades estatales consolidadas y aquellos que todavía deben resolver problemas básicos de información.
Al citar un informe de Oxford Insights, señaló que Estados Unidos y Canadá rondan los 82 puntos sobre 100 en adopción gubernamental de inteligencia artificial, mientras Brasil, Chile y Uruguay se ubican cerca de los 60. “Los gobiernos deben definir cómo incorporan estas herramientas”, planteó.
La posibilidad de anticipar los efectos de una obra o de una modificación del tránsito aparece como uno de los usos más concretos. En Helsinki, según relató Ferrario, la ciudad desarrolló una representación digital que permite simular flujos de transporte y condiciones climáticas antes de decidir un desvío, una peatonalización o una intervención urbana.
Son sistemas conocidos como “gemelos digitales”, una herramienta que traslada parte de la planificación a un entorno virtual.
La simulación no sustituye la decisión política ni elimina la necesidad de evaluar el terreno, pero permite contrastar escenarios con información disponible.
Ferrario ubicó también a Singapur entre las ciudades que avanzaron con esta clase de modelos y advirtió que su funcionamiento exige recursos sostenidos. “Requieren inversión sostenida”, resumió sobre proyectos que dependen tanto de infraestructura tecnológica como de bases de datos actualizadas.
Chicago ordena inspecciones con reclamos
En Chicago, la inteligencia artificial se aplica sobre una tarea menos visible, aunque directamente ligada a la salud pública: la inspección de locales gastronómicos. El modelo reúne reclamos, antecedentes de higiene, fecha de la última visita, temperatura y otros indicadores para establecer un orden de prioridades. “El sistema reúne reclamos, antecedentes de higiene, fecha de la última visita, temperatura y otros indicadores”, explicó Ferrario al describir el mecanismo.
La diferencia está en que los inspectores no parten únicamente de un calendario o de controles al azar. Con esa combinación de variables, el sistema puede identificar establecimientos con posibles incumplimientos hasta “siete días antes” que los métodos basados solo en fechas o sorteos. El objetivo, sostuvo, consiste en destinar el tiempo de los equipos estatales hacia los casos con mayores señales de riesgo.
El tránsito ofrece otro ejemplo de esa lógica. En Singapur, dijo Ferrario, los sistemas que ajustan la circulación y articulan otros servicios urbanos ayudaron a reducir “15% el tráfico en la ciudad”. El dato muestra el alcance potencial de los modelos predictivos, aunque su resultado depende de la calidad de la información que reciben y de las decisiones que toman las autoridades a partir de sus recomendaciones.
Los datos dispersos limitan la capacidad de los gobiernos para usar modelos
Antes de llegar a esos resultados, los gobiernos deben resolver un obstáculo menos visible que un algoritmo: la organización de sus propios registros. Ferrario sostuvo que la adopción de inteligencia artificial no se explica solo por el presupuesto disponible; requiere infraestructura, sistemas que puedan intercambiar información y criterios claros para reunirla.
“Los gobiernos no tienen los datos”, afirmó, o no logran coordinarlos para entrenar herramientas que respondan a problemas específicos.
En muchos organismos, los registros permanecen separados entre áreas que usan formatos incompatibles. Esa fragmentación limita la posibilidad de cruzar información sobre servicios, controles o prestaciones y, a la vez, puede trasladar errores de origen a las decisiones automatizadas. Para Ferrario, “el resultado depende de los datos disponibles”, una condición que obliga a revisar de dónde proviene cada registro y qué sesgos puede contener.
La discusión sobre los datos lleva además al terreno legal. El uso de cámaras o de reconocimiento facial, por ejemplo, involucra información personal y puede requerir normas específicas antes de ponerse en marcha. “Las decisiones públicas requieren debates políticos y normas específicas”, señaló el analista, quien vinculó esa exigencia con los límites que deben establecerse para cada aplicación estatal.
La velocidad tecnológica choca con los tiempos de las instituciones
Ferrario también marcó una diferencia entre el ritmo de las empresas tecnológicas y el de la administración pública. Mientras una gestión puede tardar un año en aprobar un presupuesto, las compañías dedicadas a inteligencia artificial tienen margen para ampliar sus capacidades durante ese mismo período. “La velocidad tecnológica supera los tiempos institucionales”, resumió al describir una tensión que condiciona la capacidad de respuesta de los gobiernos.
En ese contexto, la responsabilidad sobre una decisión automatizada ocupa un lugar central. Los algoritmos pueden influir en controles, servicios y prestaciones, pero Ferrario remarcó que no deben convertirse en una instancia sin responsables identificables. “Tiene que haber un responsable”, afirmó al referirse a las autoridades que definen los criterios, supervisan los resultados y deben responder ante un perjuicio.
El antecedente de Países Bajos ilustra el alcance de ese problema. Allí, un sistema utilizado para asignar apoyos destinados al cuidado de menores perjudicó a personas con nacionalidades distintas de la holandesa. “El caso derivó en la renuncia de todo el gabinete”, indicó Ferrario, al recordar las consecuencias políticas que tuvo una herramienta aplicada sobre prestaciones estatales.
También mencionó el sistema usado en Australia para revisar seguros de desempleo. Según explicó, el modelo calculó de manera incorrecta los ingresos de personas sin trabajo y generó avisos de deuda ante la agencia de recaudación. “Cuatrocientas mil personas” recibieron esas notificaciones, señaló, en un caso que volvió visible el impacto que un error de cálculo puede tener cuando se traslada a la relación cotidiana entre el Estado y sus ciudadanos.
–

articles.title: Samsung se rinde ante Google Discover y mata una app instalada en millones de móviles Galaxy
articles.text:
A Samsung se le ha hecho costumbre matar varias de sus propias apps, incluyendo aquellas que están instaladas en millones de dispositivos Galaxy. La más reciente víctima de esta estrategia es Samsung News, una aplicación que, como bien lo indica su nombre, permite leer noticias, ver resultados deportivos y más.
Según recoge SamMobile, la app de Samsung News ha comenzado a mostrar un aviso de discontinuación en algunos países. El mismo indica que la plataforma cesará su funcionamiento el próximo 21 de diciembre. Una vez que esto ocurra, el widget y la página tipo Google Discover que se abre al deslizar desde el borde izquierdo de la pantalla principal, también pasarán al olvido.
El anuncio oficial no explica el porqué del final de Samsung News. Es cierto que la compañía coreana ha mutado esta aplicación en varias oportunidades, por lo que no sería raro que en el futuro reaparezca bajo otro nombre. Aunque también es lógico pensar que la hegemonía de Google Discover para ofrecer contenidos a un solo toque de distancia puede haber tenido que ver con la decisión.
Sea como sea, hacia finales de año finalizará el periplo de Samsung News en los móviles y las tablets Galaxy. Esto significa que próximos dispositivos de la marca coreana no traerán la app preinstalada, lo que seguramente sea una buena noticia para quienes prefieren una experiencia de software con menos bloatware.
Samsung News dejará de funcionar en los móviles Galaxy a fin de año
El cierre de Samsung News implica que la app, el widget y el apartado tipo Google Discover no se actualizarán con nuevos contenidos desde el 21 de diciembre. Samsung está invitando a los usuarios a borrar el widget en cuestión una vez que llegue la fecha mencionada.
Además, toda la información recopilada para el funcionamiento de la aplicación se eliminará de inmediato, excepto en los países donde exista una normativa de retención de datos por un tiempo determinado.
Samsung News llega al final de su periplo apenas tres años después de su lanzamiento. La aplicación debutó en abril de 2023 y fue la cuarta iteración de las plataformas de noticias de la marca coreana.
Recordemos que la primera versión se lanzó en 2017 bajo el nombre de Bixby Home y evolucionó en Samsung Daily en 2019, mientras que un año más tarde se transformó en Samsung Free. Por lo pronto, no hay detalles sobre si la empresa piensa relanzarlo bajo una denominación diferente.

articles.title: Meta pode pagar R$ 50 milhões por posts que incentivam demissão política • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Meta pode pagar R$ 50 milhões por posts que incentivam demissão política
Ministério Público do Trabalho pede remoção de publicações e multa de R$ 500 mil por conteúdo mantido nas redes sociais da empresa.
O Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) entrou com uma ação contra a Meta por permitir a circulação e ampliar o alcance de publicações que incentivam empresas a demitir funcionários por sua escolha eleitoral. O órgão federal pede R$ 50 milhões de indenização por danos morais coletivos, além de exigir a retirada de publicações do tipo em um prazo de 24 horas.
O MPT afirma ter recebido mais de 3.080 denúncias de assédio eleitoral durante o pleito, que reelegeu Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) à Presidência. Desde então, publicações nas redes sociais passaram a sugerir que empresários demitam funcionários que votaram no presidente. Parte desse conteúdo é atribuída a apoiadores do candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).
Em nota, o órgão alega que a Meta é responsável pela ampla disseminação desse tipo de conteúdo, que incentiva a “discriminação, retaliação ou punição de empregados por orientação política”. A empresa de Mark Zuckerberg também foi alvo de críticas durante as eleições por um possível tratamento desigual entre as candidaturas. O próprio TSE pediu explicações à Meta e ao X.
As publicações são apontadas como ilegais por incentivar o assédio eleitoral, convocando empregadores a vasculhar as redes sociais de funcionários para descobrir em quem votaram. Também há casos de trabalhadores expostos à “ridicularização, com nome e imagem”, além de comemorações por demissões já realizadas. Entre os autores das postagens estão empresários e parlamentares.
A responsabilização da Meta, por sua vez, iria além da permissão de conteúdo criminoso: o MPT aponta que ferramentas como a aba Explorar e as sugestões de Reels ampliam o alcance e o engajamento das postagens. Como exemplo, cita quatro publicações de um único perfil verificado, que tem 3,8 milhões de seguidores e cujos posts somavam mais de 2 milhões de curtidas.
O órgão também indica a existência de regras e sistemas automatizados da própria empresa que poderiam ser aplicadas para remover os conteúdos, o que não aconteceu. Segundo os procuradores responsáveis pela ação, a ausência de medidas por parte da Meta mostra que as decisões foram “por escolha, e não por impossibilidade técnica”. A Meta informou ao Tecnoblog que não irá comentar o caso.
O MPT pede R$ 50 milhões de indenização e a exclusão das postagens criminosas. Caso a empresa não acate, cada publicação que continuar disponível no Instagram, Facebook e Threads custará R$ 500 mil à Meta.
O órgão também pede uma retratação pública para os usuários brasileiros, afirmando que a companhia “não compactua com manifestações que incentivam a discriminiação, retaliação ou punição de empregados por orientação política”.
Outra exigência da ação cível é a notificação dos perfis que publicaram conteúdos criminosos e uma suspensão de 30 dias caso voltem a fazer isso, sob risco de desativação das contas em caso de reincidência. O MPT pede ainda a criação de uma “política permanente de prevenção ao assédio eleitoral” e que proiba “expressamente” esse publicações do tipo.

articles.title: AI law firm Crosby bids on disintegrating, famed firm Weil Gotshal | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Like a real-life episode of “Suits,” the demise of famed white-shoe Wall Street law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges has been the talk of the legal industry this week. And now Silicon Valley has entered the picture.
Two-year-old AI-first law firm Crosby has put in a bid to buy some of the assets of Weil Gotshal, including its trademark, its brand, and some unspecified internal data, TechCrunch has confirmed. Separately, it is also working to hire some of the firm’s 1,200 lawyers. The Information was first to report this offer.
The once-prestigious Weil Gotshal confirmed to the New York Times this week that it was preparing to vote on dissolution in the coming days. The wind-down is happening after the firm’s presumed leadership heir apparent turned down the role, a number of its top-producing lawyers left, and a hoped-for merger with its rival, Willkie Farr & Gallagher, was shelved, the Times reported.
Meanwhile, Crosby’s founders believe they are the future of law firms. Rather than selling their internally developed AI tech to existing firms like Harvey or Legora, Crosby is an actual law firm. It uses its AI to provide legal services at, the startup promises, a speed never before possible.
The startup has raised about $85 million, including a $60 million Series B round in March led by Lux and Index, with participation from its seed-lead Sequoia, Elad Gil, 01 Advisors, and Bain Capital Ventures. Crosby came out of stealth mode in 2025 armed with $5.8 million in seed money.
While no one has pointed to the rise of legal AI as a contributing factor to Weil Gotshal’s downfall, AI may be key to the legal industry’s future. Terms of the bid weren’t disclosed and there’s no guarantee that Crosby will prevail. But if it does, Weil Gotshal’s legacy could somehow rise from the ashes, transformed by an AI-first firm.

articles.title: Over 25% of people lie to get antibiotics—and their lies aren't even good
articles.text:
A significant number of patients in the US lie to their doctors to get antibiotics they likely don’t need, according to two new studies. While that may not be a startling revelation, the studies drills down on the phenomenon, finding that the lies patients tell are generally bad ones—and yet, they work almost all the time.
In the two linked studies published Friday in JAMA Network Open, a team of researchers led by Alistair Thorpe at the University of Utah analyzed online survey data from over 1,000 adults. They found that over a quarter of people reported having lied to a clinician at least once to get an antibiotic prescription for themselves or a child in their care. Patients lied by either exaggerating symptoms, making up symptoms, or—most often—both.
But interestingly, the lies people told to get antibiotics involved making up or exaggerating symptoms of infections that wouldn’t be treated with antibiotics. For example, the most common falsehoods were symptoms associated with colds, such as fever, cough, and sore throat. That’s despite the fact that colds are caused by viruses, not bacteria—which antibiotics treat.
Further, while the data suggests many patients were being dishonest, clinicians responded with what could be considered their own form of dishonesty; in most cases, the dubious fibs led to antibiotic prescriptions. Specifically, 77 percent of adult patients and 87 percent of caregivers said their lies worked, leading them to get the antibiotic prescriptions they wanted.
“These findings signal a significant issue for health professionals making antibiotic prescribing decisions and for the fields of antimicrobial stewardship and public health,” Thorpe and colleagues concluded.
Detailed deception
For the study, the researchers reviewed survey responses from 1,371 online respondents and found 959 responses that were valid and complete. Of those, 268 (28 percent) respondents reported misrepresenting their symptoms to get antibiotics. Of those, 108 reported exaggerating symptoms, 19 reported fabricating symptoms, and 141 reported doing both. In a separate analysis of 263 respondents who identified as caregivers, 63 (27 percent) reported misrepresenting symptoms of a child to get antibiotics.

articles.title: Cisco gives 27-year-old engineer unlimited AI tokens to rewrite 98% of the company's legacy code in 24 months — president plucks former startup founder, telling him to 'go nuts'
articles.text:
Cisco gives 27-year-old engineer unlimited AI tokens to rewrite 98% of the company's legacy code in 24 months — president plucks former startup founder, telling him to 'go nuts'
Cisco's president is betting on Gen Z to change the company
In a world where youth unemployment is growing as AI replaces more and more entry-level jobs, Cisco president and chief product officer Jeetu Patel is going for a different approach. According to a report by Fortune, he's given a 27-year-old ex-startup founder — brought into the company by an earlier acquisition, and previously languishing in a role five levels below — a new job to refactor 98% of the company's legacy code within 24 months.
The employee, Padmanabhan Krishnamurthy, joined Cisco after it acquired EzDubs, a translation startup that Krishnamurthy helped build in 2023. While having executive experience, Patel found that "Paddy" was left "buried away in the organization doing something unstrategic."
According to the report, Patel spoke to Krishnamurthy in Cisco's office in San Francisco, where Krishnamurthy told him that he could rewrite Cisco's legacy code in a team of just two people, and that "even the most AI-forward people on [Patel's] own team weren't thinking that way."
As a result, he's now been tasked with rewriting 98% of Cisco's legacy code within 24 months, with four weeks as a proof of concept. "I've given him unlimited tokens because he's going to refactor code," according to Patel, telling him "you can go nuts."
AI coding has skyrocketed in recent months, with GitHub forced to deploy 4 million extra CPU cores and 160 petabytes of storage to cope. However, the practice is not without its pitfalls, with rogue AI agents notorious for taking unsolicited actions including deleting entire company databases, TV show edits, and production setups.
Patel hopes that there are more young hires in the Krishnamurthy mould that he can find, both in the company and externally to hire. He's looking for hires to "challenge the system and the status quo," to be "an energizer bunny that just goes and kind of revs everyone up."
Patel believes that current corporate structures work against this kind of thinking. "If you don't hire the early-in-career [workers], and you just let your workforce continue the way that they were, where do fresh ideas get injected? How do you challenge the status quo?"
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
He acknowledges that this will create friction, putting Gen Z employees among decades-old employees. "Tension is good.... I actually try to create tension in the teams because you want to have enough friction on the ideas. You don't want to have friction with the people and personalities."
Patel believes that a combination of experienced, scale operators at Cisco, alongside external hires and "entrepreneurial founders, CEOs and engineers who are AI-native" will bring results. "Either of these groups by themselves aren't nearly as potent as when all three work together. It's what creates magic."
