articles.title: Opening a US Office From Australia: Phones, Power, Internet and Support in a New City - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Expanding Across the Pacific: Key Considerations
For Australian businesses eyeing expansion into the United States, establishing a physical office brings a multitude of logistical challenges and strategic opportunities. Successfully navigating this process requires a comprehensive understanding of the local environment, particularly when it comes to telecommunications, power infrastructure, internet connectivity, and technical support. Each of these elements plays a critical role in ensuring smooth daily operations and long-term growth in a new city.
This guide delves into the essential factors that Australian companies must consider when opening a US office, focusing on the practical aspects of phones, power, internet, and support services. By addressing these areas early in the planning process, businesses can avoid costly delays and position themselves for success in the competitive American market.
Navigating Communication: Phones in a New Market
One of the earliest hurdles in setting up a US office is establishing a reliable phone system tailored to local expectations. Unlike Australia, where telecom providers and numbering conventions are relatively consolidated, the US telecom landscape is vast and highly regionalized. Providers differ not only by state but often by city or neighborhood, making it essential to carefully select phone technologies and service plans that best fit the operational needs of the business.
Voice over IP (VoIP) has become the dominant choice for many companies due to its flexibility, cost-effectiveness, and integration capabilities. VoIP systems facilitate calls over the internet, often linking with customer relationship management (CRM) tools and enabling advanced call routing, analytics, and recording features. This integration enhances customer service and operational efficiency.
A crucial consideration is the use of local phone numbers. Research shows that 70% of customers are more likely to engage with a business that uses a local phone number, underscoring the importance of establishing a recognizable presence through localized communication. For example, a company opening an office in Philadelphia may want to leverage tech support in Philadelphia to ensure seamless integration and troubleshooting of their telephony systems. Having reliable, city-based tech support can quickly resolve any disruptions, minimizing downtime and maintaining customer trust.
Additionally, businesses should consider toll-free numbers for national reach, but these often lack the local familiarity that builds rapport. Combining local and toll-free numbers can provide a balanced communication strategy that supports both local clients and wider audiences.
Understanding Power Requirements and Standards
Power supply differences between Australia and the US are significant and must be carefully addressed to avoid equipment damage or operational interruptions. Australia operates on 230 volts at 50 Hz frequency, while the US standard is 120 volts at 60 Hz. This discrepancy means that most Australian office equipment, including computers, servers, and networking hardware, may require voltage converters or transformers to function correctly within a US office.
Beyond voltage differences, businesses must also plan for power reliability. The US electrical grid experiences regional variability; some cities are prone to frequent outages due to weather events, infrastructure age, or maintenance schedules. For example, cities in hurricane-prone areas or with older infrastructure may face more frequent disruptions.
To mitigate these risks, investing in uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) and backup generators is critical for protecting sensitive electronics and maintaining business continuity. These systems bridge short-term outages and provide time to safely shut down equipment if necessary.
Compliance with local electrical codes and safety standards is another vital aspect. The US has strict regulations enforced by state and local authorities, and non-compliance can lead to costly fines or insurance issues. Partnering with licensed local contractors familiar with these codes ensures that office power installations meet all legal requirements and operate safely.
Securing High-Speed Internet Connectivity
Internet connectivity is the backbone of modern business operations, enabling communication, cloud computing, data transfers, and customer interactions. While the US has extensive broadband coverage, the quality, speed, and availability of internet service providers (ISPs) can differ widely depending on the city and even the specific neighborhood.
According to the Federal Communications Commission, approximately 94% of Americans have access to broadband internet, but actual speeds vary significantly, with rural and some urban areas experiencing slower connections. For a business, choosing an office location with robust internet infrastructure is paramount.
Fiber-optic connections are often the preferred choice due to their high bandwidth and low latency, supporting demanding applications such as video conferencing, large file transfers, and cloud-based services. Cable and DSL remain options in areas where fiber is unavailable, but they generally offer lower speeds and less reliability.
When expanding into a city like Cleveland, companies should consider Cleveland’s top IT support to access local expertise in IT infrastructure and internet management. Local IT professionals can assist in evaluating ISP options, negotiating service agreements, and optimizing network configurations to ensure maximum uptime and performance.
Additionally, businesses should plan for redundancy by having backup internet connections or failover systems to avoid costly downtime caused by ISP outages.
Leveraging Local IT Support for Smooth Operations
Opening an office in a new city means entering an unfamiliar technology landscape with different vendors, service standards, and regulatory requirements. Local IT support is invaluable for bridging these gaps and ensuring that technology infrastructure is set up, maintained, and secured effectively.
Engaging with established local IT providers accelerates the onboarding process and helps navigate city-specific issues such as network architecture, software licensing, and compliance with US data protection laws. Cybersecurity is a particularly critical area where local expertise is essential. The US enforces stringent regulations such as the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), depending on the industry. Local IT providers are well-versed in these requirements and can assist with security audits, risk assessments, and implementing robust security protocols.
Furthermore, local support teams can provide training for staff, ensuring that employees understand best practices and the proper use of new systems.
Addressing Additional Operational Considerations
Beyond the core infrastructure, several other factors influence the success of opening a US office from Australia. Office location within the city can impact accessibility, proximity to clients, and employee convenience. Choosing a location near transport hubs or business districts can enhance networking and operational efficiency.
Time zone differences between Australia and the US pose challenges for communication and scheduling. Australian companies may need to establish flexible working hours or hire dedicated local staff to maintain consistent customer service and internal collaboration.
Compliance with US employment laws, tax codes, and business regulations also requires attention. Working with legal and financial advisors familiar with cross-border operations can prevent regulatory pitfalls and optimize tax strategies.
Cultural differences in business practices and customer expectations should inform marketing, sales, and customer service approaches. Hiring local talent or consultants provides valuable insights into American consumer behavior and business etiquette, which can improve market penetration and brand reception.
Conclusion: Planning for Success Across Borders
Opening a US office from Australia is a complex but rewarding endeavor that demands careful preparation across multiple dimensions. Telecommunications, power infrastructure, internet connectivity, and local technical support form the foundation on which operational success is built.
By partnering with trusted local providers and understanding the nuances of regional infrastructure, Australian businesses can establish resilient offices that meet customer expectations and regulatory requirements. Strategic choices about phone systems, power compatibility, and internet services – coupled with access to expert local IT support – equip companies to overcome common challenges.
Selecting the right city and building relationships with local IT support services like and can provide a competitive advantage and operational stability. With thorough planning and investment, businesses can bridge the geographic divide seamlessly and thrive in the dynamic US market.

articles.title: Aboyeji-backed AI engineering talent platform Talent Nation raises pre-seed funding - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian AI engineering talent platform Talent Nation, co-founded by serial entrepreneur Iyinoluwa Aboyeji, has raised an undisclosed pre-seed funding round as it looks to train and deploy one million African AI engineers over the next decade.
Co-founded by Aboyeji, who was behind Andela, Flutterwave and Moove, and South Africa-born lawyer Kesiah Valkin, who previously co-founded London-based 01 Founders, Talent Nation trains, certifies and deploys AI engineers into organisations looking to build their own AI capability.
The startup is betting that AI will increase demand for engineering talent rather than reduce it. As AI models generate more code, it argues, businesses need more engineers who can review, test and integrate that code into reliable systems.
“Talent is the final constraint to super intelligence. Engineers who can implement AI solutions are some of the most expensive talent to recruit anywhere. Talent Nation puts certified AI engineering talent within the reach of any organisation for a fraction of the cost of frontier labs and traditional consulting firms,” said Aboyeji, who serves as executive chairman.
The undisclosed round of funding was co-led by Enza Capital and UK-based LocalGlobe, with participation from Future Africa, Kaleo Ventures, Ajim Capital, Solving.org and Accelerate Africa.
Talent Nation’s academy, Learn2Earn, has received more than 63,000 applications in 18 months, assessed over 32,000 people, and now has around 1,400 fellows training across nine campuses in six cities. Fewer than three per cent of applicants are admitted.
Applicants first complete an online test on their phones, before progressing to weekly in-person trials at the company’s centres across Nigeria. Experienced engineers who meet the startup’s standards move straight to deployment, while others go through three-, six- or 12-month training programmes that include internships and practical work experience. Training is peer-led and project-based, with intensive build-athons held across its campuses.
Training carries no upfront fees. Revenue from enterprise clients is reinvested into developing more engineers, who in turn contribute towards future cohorts once employed. Its engineers are already working with clients including IHS Towers, and organisations can engage them on defined projects, as direct hires, or in embedded teams.
“The benefits of AI should extend far beyond the companies with the resources to develop and deploy it today. But technological breakthroughs alone will not deliver widespread adoption. That requires a fundamental shift in the cost and availability of AI engineering talent,” said Valkin, who is CEO.
Sir John Lazar, general partner at Enza Capital and president of the Royal Academy of Engineering, said engineering talent was a crucial bedrock of innovation.
“Enza is proud to co-lead this investment into Talent Nation because we believe the company’s remarkable founders can identify this talent, build pathways for African engineers into valuable work, not just in Lagos but in London, and hold their engineers to a global standard of excellence,” he said.

articles.title: Atomberg Technologies receives SEBI nod for IPO
articles.text:
Atomberg Technologies receives SEBI nod for IPO
The proceeds of the IPO will be used for repayment of debt, branding & marketing and R&D.
Consumer appliance maker Atomberg Technologies has received the approval from Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public offering (IPO).
The IPO will be a combination of fresh issue of shares and offer for sale. Atomberg plans to raise Rs 450 crore through the fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale of 76,542,051 equity shares of face value Rs 10 each.
The company proposes to utilise the proceeds from the IPO towards debt payment, investments into brand awareness & marketing, R&D and general corporate purposes.
Atomberg reported a revenue of Rs 1293.77 crore for FY26 as compared to Rs 959.51 crore recorded in FY25, registering a growth of 34.83%. It reported a loss of Rs 148.88 crore for FY26.
Founded in 2012, Atomberg manufactures a range of consumer appliances which include mixer grinders, water purifiers and cold-pressed juicers. The company also designs, manufactures and supplies proprietary and critical components, including motors and controllers, to enterprise customers such as Voltas, Godrej and BlueStar.
Atomberg sells its products through an omni-channel distribution model spanning offline channels such as general trade distributors, retailers, modern trade chains and institutional partners, and online channels including e-commerce marketplaces, quick-commerce platforms and its own website.
Its revenue from online channels increased to Rs 456.45 crore in FY2026 from Rs 234.51 crores in FY2024, while offline channel revenue rose to Rs 820.11 Crores from Rs 562.47 crores over the same period. The online channel contributed approximately 35.76% of the revenue from the consumer appliances business.
Atomberg operates two leased manufacturing facilities in Pune, Maharashtra, supporting its consumer appliances and proprietary components businesses. Its Chakan facility in Pune, which commenced operations in FY2022 manufactures ceiling fans, table, pedestal and wall fans, exhaust fans, mixer grinders, cold-pressed juicers and smart locks.

articles.title: Welche deutschen Unternehmen Bewerber transparent über den KI-Einsatz informieren – und welche nicht
articles.text:
KI im Recruiting: So findest du heraus, ob deine Bewerbung zuerst von einem Bot aussortiert wird
Zahlreiche Personaler:innen kämpfen mit einer Flut an Bewerbungen. Sie sind auf die Nutzung von KI zurückzuführen, die Anschreiben und Lebensläufe innerhalb kürzester Zeit ausspucken können und so die Hürde der Bewerbung minimieren. Um diesem Ansturm entgegenzuwirken, greifen viele Personalabteilungen mittlerweile selbst auf KI zurück. Wie jetzt eine Untersuchung des HR-Softwareanbieters Lucca zeigt, gehen aber gerade deutsche Unternehmen nicht flächendeckend transparent damit um.
Bewerbungen im KI-Zeitalter: Welche Unternehmen sind transparent?
Insgesamt wurden für den KI-Transparenz-Index 25 deutsche Unternehmen genauer unter die Lupe genommen. Es handelt sich dabei um die größten deutschen Arbeitgeber, gemessen an der Anzahl der Mitarbeiter:innen. Dabei untersuchte Lucca vier Bereiche genauer: die rechtliche Transparenz in Datenschutzhinweisen für Bewerber:innen, die Transparenz zum KI-Einsatz während des Bewerbungsablaufs sowie über die eingesetzte Recruiting-Software und die „unternehmensweite KI-Steuerung mitsamt Richtlinien, Ethik-Kodizes und Geschäfts-, Nachhaltigkeits- und Menschenrechtsberichten“.
Dabei konnten die deutschen Unternehmen insgesamt 30 Punkte sammeln. Je mehr Punkte, desto transparenter der Umgang mit KI. Die Allianz erreichte dabei mit einem Score von 26 die höchste Punktzahl. Auf den zweiten und dritten Platz kommen die Deutsche Telekom und SAP mit jeweils 20 Punkten. Auf dem letzten Platz liegt hingegen laut Lucca Aldi Nord mit nur einem Punkt. Siemens Energy landet mit fünf Punkten auf dem vorletzten Platz.
Laut Lucca nutzen 21 der untersuchten Unternehmen ihre Bewerbungen über eine Software, die zumindest theoretisch auch KI-Funktionen unterstützt. Lediglich vier Unternehmen kommunizieren diese KI-Funktionen auch offen. Dazu zählen Bayer, SAP, Allianz und Siemens. Bei anderen Unternehmen haben Bewerber:innen meist nur die Chance, über die Datenschutzhinweise etwas über die KI-Nutzung zu erfahren.
Marek Kraus, Country Manager Germany bei Lucca, sagt dazu: „Unsere Untersuchung zeigt: KI ist in den Systemen vieler Unternehmen angekommen, wird für Bewerber:innen aber oft erst im Datenschutztext sichtbar. Mittelfristig sollte der KI-Einsatz transparent dort offengelegt werden, wo Bewerber:innen sich tatsächlich informieren.“
Für Bewerber:innen empfiehlt Lucca deshalb, immer einen Blick auf die Datenschutzhinweise zu werfen. Darin wird dargelegt, welche personenbezogenen Daten während der Bewerbung verarbeitet werden. Anhand von KI-zugehörigen Begriffen wie „automatisierte Verarbeitung“ oder unscheinbaren Formulierungen wie „Vorauswahl“ lässt sich die KI-Nutzung erkennen.
Wer die KI-Nutzung frühzeitig sieht, kann sie auch für sich nutzen. Dabei sollten gezielt Schlagworte und Anforderungen aus der Stellenausschreibung im Lebenslauf und dem Anschreiben integriert und hervorgehoben werden, damit KI-Systeme sie schneller erkennen. Natürlich ist das nur dann empfehlenswert, wenn Bewerber:innen die nötigen Qualifikationen auch wirklich mitbringen.

articles.title: Sechs Wege zum ewigen Ich: Was Forscher mit Gehirnen anstellen, damit wir nie ganz verschwinden
articles.text:
Kopf ab, Gehirn rein, Geist hochladen: 6 waghalsige Experimente für ein Leben ohne Körper
Habt ihr schon einmal darüber nachgedacht, was euch zu dem macht, was ihr seid? Die Wissenschaft versichert uns, dass dies ausschließlich mit dem drei Pfund schweren Organ zwischen unseren Ohren zu tun hat – mit seinen Milliarden von Neuronen und Billionen feiner Verbindungen. Viel schwieriger ist es jedoch zu erklären, warum wir ein Selbstbewusstsein haben, oder genau zu bestimmen, wo diese erste Erinnerung an Mama tatsächlich gespeichert ist. Wenn wir älter werden, vergessen wir das meiste, was wir erlebt haben, und doch gibt es eine unbestreitbare Kontinuität: Mit 30, 50 oder 70 wirst du immer noch du selbst sein.
Um diese schwer fassbare Kontinuität des Selbst zu bewahren, arbeiten einige weitsichtige Technologen an Möglichkeiten, dein Gehirn am Laufen zu halten – sogar über den Tod hinaus. Nennen wir sie die „Mind Saver“. Sie erforschen alles, vom Einfrieren von Gehirnen in flüssigem Stickstoff über die Verbesserung lebender Gehirne bis hin zum Hochladen unserer Erinnerungen in die Cloud. Hier betrachten wir sechs mögliche und teilweise auch verrückte Wege, um euren Geist am Leben zu erhalten. Wir ordnen ein, wie realisierbar sie wären und welche Vorteile die heutige Forschung mit sich bringen könnte – selbst wenn die kognitive Unsterblichkeit nicht gelingen sollte.

articles.title: Delhivery reports net profit of Rs 41 crore in Q2 of FY27
articles.text:
Delhivery reports net profit of Rs 41 crore in Q2 of FY27
The logistics company sees performance improving in the second half of the fiscal year despite the challenges of inflation and labour supply.
Logistics company Delhivery reported a net profit of Rs 40.63 crore during the second quarter of FY27, compared to a loss of Rs 50.49 crore in the same quarter of the previous fiscal year. Revenue rose 19.8% to Rs 3,066.38 crore from Rs 2,559.3 crore in the year-ago period.
Delhivery, in a statement, said it could register a strong performance despite the pressure of inflation.
Express parcel volume recorded a 32% YoY growth touching 325 million shipments for the second quarter. The part truck load segment recorded a 14% YoY growth.
The logistics company said its new businesses are ramping up faster than originally planned.
Delhivery Local, an on-demand, intracity logistics and courier service, is now live across eight cities and is on track to exceed its previous guidance of an annual revenue run rate of Rs 250 crore by Q4FY27, along with improved contribution margins.
Financial Service has also begun early monetisation of its vendor ecosystem, and is developing co-lending partnerships to broaden financial access to vendor partners through an asset-light approach, the company said.
Delhivery said early investments in AI are beginning to bear fruit, with improved sales productivity and customer onboarding and faster resolution of claims and disputes and fraud detection.
Delhivery Robotics, an inhouse automation lab, has commenced production of customised autonomous vehicles for in-facility movement operations. It has also begun testing robotics systems across under-the-roof operations, in partnership with global leaders in the physical AI domain.
Delhivery expressed confidence going into the second half of the fiscal year, despite a volatile macro environment due to rising fuel prices, labour availability issues, and multiple statutory changes. It said its network service levels heading into the festive season have been the best, with improved profitability.

articles.title: Actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86, legendary star of Star Trek and X-Men
articles.text:
RIP Patrick Stewart, the actor best known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in the Star Trek franchise and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men movies, died Wednesday, October 28. He was 86. Stewart had Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, though neither diagnosis was made public until after his death.
After his longtime spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, formally announced his passing, tributes poured in from around the world. Fans and former colleagues recalled his iconic roles and marveled at how easily he moved between commercial cinema and classical Shakespearean theater.
Australian actor Hugh Jackman, who played Wolverine in the X-Men movies, called Stewart a "tremendous friend" and praised his contribution to the entertainment industry. "We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days," he wrote on Instagram.
 – Hugh Jackman (@RealHughJackman) October 29, 2026
Another former co-star, English actor Ian McKellen, also mourned Stewart's death, describing him as a proud Yorkshireman and one of the most respected and beloved actors of his generation. In a long, heartfelt message on Instagram, McKellen said Stewart was "a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love."
Star Trek co-star William Shatner also remembered Stewart fondly, calling him "a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor." In a social media post, Shatner wrote, "What a heartbreaking week it has been," an apparent reference to the death of Walter Koenig earlier in the week. Koenig, who played Pavel Chekov in Star Trek, died October 25 at 90.
Praising Stewart's diverse body of work, Shatner said: "From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work... He will be deeply missed."
 – William Shatner (@WilliamShatner) October 29, 2026
Born in Mirfield, England, in 1940, Stewart's career got a boost when he joined the prestigious Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966. He appeared on the long-running British soap Coronation Street in 1967 and made his Broadway debut in 1971 in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
Over the following decades, Stewart starred in a string of hit movies and TV shows, including Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol (1999), which earned him a Screen Actors Guild Award nomination for his portrayal of Ebenezer Scrooge. He also played Captain Ahab in the miniseries Moby Dick (1998) and King Henry II in the film The Lion in Winter (2003), for which he received a Golden Globe nomination.
Stewart turned up on Frasier in the show's 11th and final season in 2003, playing a gay Seattle socialite and opera director who mistakes Kelsey Grammer's title character for a potential love interest. He also appeared on Top Gear and lent his voice to multiple characters on Fox's animated sitcom Family Guy.
His career drew awards from both critics and peers. He won three Laurence Olivier Awards between 1979 and 2008, as well as a Grammy in 1996 for Best Spoken Word Album for Children for his recording of Prokofiev's Peter and the Wolf. He was also nominated for a Tony Award, three Golden Globes, four Emmys and three Screen Actors Guild Awards.
Queen Elizabeth II knighted Stewart in 2010 for his services to drama. He was also an ambassador for the International Rescue Committee. His final on-screen performance will be a return as Professor Charles Xavier in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, due in theaters in December.

articles.title: Corea del Norte se ha convertido en una superpotencia del ciberataque y lo está utilizando para autofinanciarse
articles.text:
Es uno de los países más aislados y herméticos del planeta. Su comercio exterior se limita a unos pocos países afines, arrastra sanciones desde hace años y casi nadie sabe qué ocurre realmente más allá de las fronteras. Aun así, Corea del Norte se ha revelado como una auténtica superpotencia en el cibercrimen.
Aunque todavía no se puede confirmar de forma oficial, algunos indicios y coincidencias apuntan Pyongyang podría estar tras el incidente de ciberseguridad que esta madrugada ha hecho desaparecer unos 6.360 millones de dólares de las carteras de Binance. No es el primer ataque de este estilo que se atribuye a grupos de ciberdelincuentes altamente especializados que actúan a las órdenes de Corea del Norte.
Binance, un robo récord con firma conocida. El impacto total del golpe a Binance se calcula cercano a los 6.300 millones de dólares, y podría haber sido mayor si no fuera porque la mitad quedó congelada. Tether bloqueó unos 1.600 millones y Circle más de 800 millones en USDC. Esta cifra cuadruplica la del anterior récord en el robo de criptomonedas: el de Bybit de 2025 en el que se esfumaron unos 1.500 millones de dólares en criptodivisas.
La firma de ciberseguridad TRM Labs tiene "alta confianza" en que el autor del robo es TraderTraitor, un grupo vinculado a la red de ciberdelincuentes Lazarus. Según TRM LAbs, "varias características de este ataque coinciden con robos anteriores vinculados a Corea del Norte". Otros investigadores apuntan en la misma dirección. Conviene ir con cautela ya que la atribución es todavía preliminar y el FBI no se ha pronunciado oficialmente al respecto.
Bybit y un régimen que cobra en cripto. Sin embargo, el precedente más reciente es Bybit. En febrero de 2025 se esfumaron 1.500 millones de dólares en Ether, y el FBI lo atribuyó a Corea del Norte días después. Los ladrones repartieron parte del botín obtenido entre miles de direcciones de varias cadenas de bloques para blanquearlo. Los investigadores han vinculado el ataque de Bybit con el de Binance porque algunas de las direcciones que se han utilizado en este último golpe, también se usaron en el de 2025.
Chainalysis calculó que los hackers vinculados al régimen habían robado unos 2.020 millones de dólares en criptodivisas solo en 2025, un 51% más que el año anterior y el mayor total registrado. El acumulado histórico llegaba a los 6.750 millones de dólares. Washington ya acusó en 2021 a tres programadores militares de robar 1.300 millones.
Cifrado poscuántico para esconder su rastro. Kaspersky documentó en una investigación la Operación FlashHole, activa desde al menos julio de 2025 y dirigida a empresas surcoreanas de software, construcción y telecomunicaciones. Los atacantes usaron un currículum falso con una foto probablemente creada con IA. Una artimaña bastante sencilla que sirve como señuelo para ataques Phishing. Sin embargo, la novedad es una herramienta de Lazarus que protege la descarga de nuevos programas con ML-KEM-1024, un algoritmo poscuántico.
Sojun Ryu, investigador de Kaspersky, dijo a El País que esta tecnología "se considera la criptografía del futuro, está diseñada para seguir siendo segura contra computadoras cuánticas". ML-KEM es uno de los tres estándares que NIST finalizó en agosto de 2024. Ningún ordenador cuántico conocido rompe aún el cifrado actual, así que Lazarus se cubre de un riesgo futuro. Para Ryu, eso revela que los ciberdelincuentes en nómina de Pyongyang tienen un nivel de conocimientos y especialización muy avanzado, y utilizan las tecnologías más vanguardistas para "que sus cargas maliciosas no queden expuestas ante defensores o investigadores".
El dinero tiene destino. La directora de Inteligencia Nacional de EE UU, Tulsi Gabbard, dijo ante el Congreso que esos robos ayudan a financiar al régimen de Kim Jong-un y a su programa de armas estratégicas. Un informe de la ONU de 2024 calculó que el robo de criptomonedas podía aportar hasta la mitad de las divisas que recibe el país.
Sin embargo, Corea del Norte cuenta con otra fuente de ingresos de divisas mucho más discreta: el teletrabajo. Informáticos norcoreanos consiguen empleo remoto con identidades robadas y usan portátiles de la empresa alojados en casas de cómplices en EEUU, las llamadas "granjas de portátiles". El Departamento de Justicia detalló un esquema que afectó a más de 70 empresas y generó unos 3 millones de dólares. En Texas, el FBI registró más de 40 viviendas y se incautó de unos 187 dispositivos.

articles.title: Hemos normalizado el uso del móvil en los estadios de fútbol. En Alemania, Vodafone está consiguiendo lo contrario
articles.text:
Hace tiempo que el móvil se convirtió en una extensión de nuestro cuerpo hasta el punto de que, en muchas ocasiones, vivimos las experiencias a través de su pantalla en vez de verlas con nuestros propios ojos. Si no sabéis a lo que me refiero, echad un vistazo a vuestro alrededor en un concierto o en cualquier otro tipo de espectáculo.
Fijaos, por ejemplo, qué hacen los aficionados en campo de fútbol cuando su equipo va a lanzar un penalti. O cuando va a levantar el trofeo de campeón (de la Champions, del Mundial o de lo que sea). Miles de teléfonos se alzan para capturar ese instante y compartirlo inmediatamente en redes sociales en lugar de disfrutar del momento.
Y eso es precisamente lo que se ha propuesto evitar el Borussia Dortmund en colaboración con Vodafone, su patrocinador. Para ello, el equipo alemán ha lanzado una solución que recompensa a los aficionados que no usen el móvil durante los partidos.
Camiseta, bufanda... y móvil. Qué tiempos aquellos cuando íbamos al estadio a animar a nuestro equipo. Hoy en día, gran cantidad de aficionados están más pendientes del móvil que de lo que sucede en el terreno de juego.
En 2023, Vodafone realizó una encuesta a mil personas que asisten habitualmente a los estadios y el 63% de ellos reconoció usar su teléfono regularmente durante los partidos. Hablamos de casi dos tercios de los aficionados y ese porcentaje ha aumentado aún más en los últimos años.
'Detox' digital en el fútbol. Utilizar constantemente en teléfono en el estadio no sólo provoca que los aficionados se pierdan goles y jugadas, sino que reduce la animación de la grada. Por eso, el Borussia Dortmund y Vodafone han decidido tomar cartas en el asunto.
Su solución ha sido incorporar el nuevo 'Fan Mode' (modo fan) en la aplicación oficial 'BVB' del club germano. Es una función que, básicamente, anima a dejar el móvil en el bolsillo durante los partidos en el Signal Iduna Park, el estadio del Borussia Dortmund. ¿Cómo? Con recompensas por usarlo, claro.
Ponte en 'Modo Fan' para ganar. Cuando vaya a empezar el partido, el usuario debe activar el nuevo modo 'Fan' dentro de la app 'BVB' y bloquear la pantalla del móvil. Mientras la pantalla permanezca bloqueada, irá sumando puntos, de manera que, cuantas menos veces desbloquees tu móvil durante el encuentro, más puntos ganarás.
En el descanso, está permitido usar el teléfono, pero cuando arranque la segunda parte, hay que volver al 'Fan Mode' para seguir acumulando puntos hasta el pitido final. Después, puedes canjearlos por tarjetas regalo para la tienda del club o por camisetas firmadas por los jugadores.
Todo un éxito. El 'Modo Fan' se utilizó por primera vez durante el partido en casa contra el Eintracht Frankfurt y ha tenido tan buena acogida que el club tiene previsto utilizarlo en todos los encuentros que el Borussia Dortmund dispute en su estadio.
La idea, según Carsten Cramer, CEO del Borussia Dortmund, es "proteger una experiencia que ninguna tecnología puede reemplazar. Más de 81.000 personas en el estadio, cantando, animando y conteniendo la respiración juntos". Muchas veces la tecnología debe pasar a un segundo plano, y no hay duda de que el deporte en directo es una de ellas. ¿No estáis de acuerdo?

articles.title: Tu Mac no tiene Face ID, pero esta aplicación permite desbloquearlo con tu cara
articles.text:
Una de las cosas que más me gustan de mi iPhone es que puedo desbloquear la pantalla con mi cara. Eso de poner el dedo en el sensor también es práctico, pero el Face ID es más cómodo y rápido. Además, también sirve para otras acciones como desbloquear aplicaciones, autorizar pagos con Apple Pay o comprar aplicaciones y juegos en la App Store. Sin embargo, no hay Face ID en Mac. Algo que se rumoreó en el pasado, pero que nunca se ha hecho realidad. Pero hay una buena noticia. Puedes desbloquear tu Mac con tu cara con una simple aplicación gratuita.
Primero llegó el Touch ID. Con tu huella dactilar, puedes desbloquear la pantalla de tu iPhone, iPad o Mac. Con los años ha ido cambiando de forma. Y, en la actualidad, en iPad es prácticamente invisible, integrado en el botón de encendido. Y en Mac puedes usarlo tanto en los modelos portátiles (MacBook Air, MacBook Neo y MacBook Pro) como en los de sobremesa. Estos segundos, a través del teclado Magic Keyboard con Touch ID.
Pero el Face ID en Mac sigue sin llegar. Y teniendo en cuenta que todos los Mac con pantalla (portátiles o iMac) tienen una cámara frontal integrada, es una lástima que no tengamos esta opción de desbloquear Mac con tu cara en vez de hacerlo con la contraseña, como se ha hecho siempre. Pero para eso están los desarrolladores de apps, para hacer posible lo que creías imposible.
Por qué no hay Face ID en Mac
Si Apple no hace algo, por algo será. Es decir, que si no puedes desbloquear el Mac con tu cara porque no hay Face ID en Mac es por algún motivo. Nos guste o no. Si echamos un vistazo a la hemeroteca, este tema no es nuevo. En 2020 se rumoreó sobre la posible llegada del Face ID a los Mac. Pero en 2021 nos cayó un jarro de agua fría. En una entrevista en The Wall Street Journal, Tom Boger, entonces vicepresidente de marketing de iPad y Mac, explicó que la razón por la que no tenían pensado implementar desbloquea de Mac por Face ID era porque el Touch ID era más conveniente en un portátil.
La explicación que dio Tom Boger es que, al abrir un MacBook, el usuario tiene las manos sobre el teclado, así que el sensor está a su alcance. Una explicación que también podemos extender a los teclados en un iMac, Mac mini o Mac Studio. Pero su argumentación chirría un poco, ya que también dijo que Face ID exige levantar la vista o ajustar la posición para que la cámara capte el rostro. Lo mismo podría argumentarse de un iPhone. Tanto en iPhone como en Mac, la pantalla es lo que mira el usuario principalmente. Teclado o no de por medio.
Otras razones de más peso para que no tengamos Face ID en Mac y no puedas desbloquear tu Mac con tu cara tienen que ver con el coste económico de esta tecnología frente a Touch ID, más económica y amortizada tras años y años de innovación. Pero, sobre todo, los motivos más serios tienen que ver con el diseño y fabricación de los Mac. Un artículo de 2022 de MacWorld explicaba que el grosor del módulo con el sensor TrueDepth impedía que la parte del MacBook con pantalla fuera tan fino como lo es hoy en día. Y si no podía estar presente en los portátiles, tampoco valía la pena añadirlo solamente al iMac. Aunque esto no impide que en el futuro se den las condiciones para incorporar Face ID en Mac si es barato y suficientemente pequeño.
Varios métodos para desbloquear tu Mac
Actualmente, si quieres desbloquear tu Mac, además de introducir la contraseña, tienes varias maneras de hacerlo. Ya hemos mencionado el método oficial con el Touch ID integrado en algunos teclados Magic Keyboard. Al encender el Mac tienes que iniciar sesión sí o sí con tu contraseña. Pero a partir de ahí, puedes desbloquear la pantalla con tu dedo y realizar otras acciones como instalar aplicaciones o hacer compras online.
Si tienes un Apple Watch, puedes desbloquear el Mac usando las conexiones wifi y Bluetooth. Es decir, que para que esto sea posible tienes que tener los dos dispositivos conectados al mismo punto wifi, tener Bluetooth activado y, en tercer lugar, tener iniciada la misma cuenta de Apple.
Y ya que hablamos de Bluetooth, hay métodos no oficiales para desbloquear el Mac. En esta ocasión, con tu iPhone. O, en general, con cualquier teléfono o dispositivo Bluetooth. Como vimos en este artículo, hay aplicaciones que permiten desbloquear tu Mac con tu iPhone. La que yo utilizo a diario se llama BLEUnlock. Es gratuita y de código abierto. Le indicas qué dispositivo hará de llave y, cuando el Mac lo detecte vía Bluetooth, se desbloqueará la pantalla.
Así que si Apple no permite desbloquear tu Mac con tu cara, vamos a hacerlo con una aplicación no oficial. Su nombre es Hey Mac. Esta app es gratuita, de código abierto y compatible con macOS 14 y superior. Puedes instalarla descargando su instalador o empleando Homebrew.
Desbloquear tu Mac con tu cara
El funcionamiento de Hey Mac es simple. Al bloquear el Mac, si miras a la cámara, se desbloqueará de nuevo. Lo que verás es una animación que se integra en la isla superior de la pantalla, donde está la cámara frontal de tu Mac. Y puedes cambiarla por otra animación más minimalista y menos intrusiva. Además, no solo sirve para desbloquear la pantalla del Mac. También puedes usar Hey Mac para bloquear aplicaciones de miradas curiosas. Así, con Hey Mac podrás añadir tu cara a otros métodos como la contraseña o el Touch ID.
Para instalar Hey Mac, tendrás que darle acceso a la cámara para que funcione correctamente. Y acceso al guardado de datos. Durante la configuración te explicará qué tienes que hacer para usarla correctamente. Básicamente, mirar a cámara o estar bien colocado frente a ella. Hay que tener en cuenta que la primera vez que abras la aplicación es probable que macOS la bloquee por seguridad. Para resolver este inconveniente, tendrás que ir a Configuración del Sistema > Privacidad y seguridad. Abajo del todo verás la opción Abrir de todas formas al lado de Hey Mac. Y volver a pedirlo de nuevo cuando te lo pida.
Sobre la seguridad de la app para desbloquear tu Mac con tu cara, es normal que te plantees qué hace o deja de hacer Hey Mac con la cámara. O con tu contraseña de usuario, que tendrás que facilitarle para que desbloquee el Mac por ti. Su página web afirma que el reconocimiento facial utiliza Apple Neural Engine. No hace fotos de tu cara, la información está cifrada y no envía datos fuera del Mac. Y, por descontado, al igual que Face ID, no sustituye del todo tu contraseña o Touch ID. Si Hey Mac no funciona bien, los demás métodos de seguridad seguirán estando ahí.

articles.title: Microsoft Edge
articles.text:
Microsoft's browser provides a fast, secure, and modern web experience. Browse the web anywhere with one seamless experience from your phone to your computer and other signed-in devices. Microsoft Edge is also a safe browser that gives you the tools to protect your privacy and security online.
How does Edge compare to Chrome and Firefox in terms of performance and usability?
Edge is built on the Chromium engine, similar to Chrome, and often offers comparable or better performance, especially regarding memory usage. It also supports Chrome extensions and includes features like vertical tabs and a built-in PDF viewer. However, some users prefer Firefox for its open-source nature and privacy features.
Is Microsoft Edge too bloated with unnecessary features?
Some users feel that Edge has become cluttered with features like the sidebar, shopping tools, games, and Microsoft Rewards integration. While these features can be disabled, the default experience may seem overwhelming to those seeking a minimalist browser.
Why does Microsoft Edge keep running in the background even after I close it?
Many users have reported that Edge continues to run in the background despite disabling settings like "Startup Boost" and "Continue running background apps when Microsoft Edge is closed." This issue can be particularly noticeable when using multiple profiles, where extensions from closed profiles may remain active.
Can Edge block autoplay media?
Yes, Microsoft Edge lets you block all the autoplay media by heading to edge://settings/content/mediaAutoplay and selecting "Block" from the drop-down menu. You can also add exceptions to websites using the "Add" tool in site permissions.
Why is Edge a Microsoft browser you should actually use?
Microsoft Edge is a well rounded browser based on Chromium with four key advantages:
- It offers solid integration with Windows and other Microsoft services, which allows for more direct communications between programs and thus a more fluent workflow.
- Performance and battery savings are improved upon Chrome and other Chromium-based browsers.
- You can access all Chrome extensions giving you a world of options to customize the browser.
- It adds enhanced privacy settings and track prevention measures that give you control over almost all aspects of the information you share. Microsoft promises that while using InPrivate tabs, your browsing and search data aren't saved on your device and any data collected will not be tied with your Microsoft account.
Features
Compose
With the power of AI, you can effortlessly transform your ideas into polished drafts, saving valuable time and ensuring the right tone, wherever you write online. Compose is available only with Copilot in the Edge browser. To open Compose, click the Copilot icon in the upper-right of Edge, and then click Compose at the top of the Copilot sidepane. Simply click the Re-generate draft button on the bottom of your draft, and Compose will rewrite it. You can also type input at the bottom of the Preview box, and have Compose rewrite your draft based on that feedback. To go back to your previous draft, click the Back button.
Making the web a better place for everyone
We've adopted the Chromium open source project in the development of Microsoft Edge to create better web compatibility for our customers, and less fragmentation of the web for all web developers.
Investing in open source
We've also started making contributions back to Chromium in areas like accessibility, touch, ARM64 and others. Our plan is to continue working in Chromium rather than creating a parallel project. We're working directly with the teams at Google, and we're looking forward to working even more with the open source community. To learn more about our contributions, see our Microsoft Edge "Explainers" on GitHub and check out our source code release.
We're listening!
The Microsoft Edge team wants to hear from you. In December we asked visitors to this site "if you could change one thing about the web, what would it be?". We've read your answers and have some thoughts to share. Head over to the Microsoft Edge Insider Forum to see what the community is saying about this and other topics.
Microsoft Edge now uses Mica material
Mica is an opaque, dynamic material that incorporates theme and desktop wallpaper to paint the background of long-lived windows such as apps and settings. You can apply Mica to your application backdrop to delight users and create visual hierarchy, aiding productivity, by increasing clarity about which window is in focus. Mica is specifically designed for app performance as it only samples the desktop wallpaper once to create its visualization. Mica is available for UWP apps that use WinUI 2 and apps that use Windows App SDK 1.1 or later, while running on Windows 11 version 22000 or later.
What's New
Edge is faster on Windows with Accelerated App Launches
We're excited to announce that Edge is the first browser to support accelerated app launches on Windows, delivering a faster and more consistent browser launch experience.
With accelerated app launch, most Windows users will see a 15% launch speed improvement, with wins of up to 33% under heavy multitasking!1 That means you can start browsing faster.
This has already rolled out starting with Microsoft Edge version 150 and later and is supported on Windows 11, versions 25H2, 26H2, 26H1 with the October 2026 non-security update (KB5127936) or later.
How does this work?
The Edge and Windows team partnered to bring this new Windows accelerated app launch capability to Edge users quickly. Edge, like many modern applications on Windows, is often already running. A visible Edge window might already be open, or Edge might already be running in the background through features such as Startup Boost.
Without accelerated app launches on Windows, when you click on a link or start Edge from the taskbar, Windows must first determine if Edge is already running. To do that, Windows starts an intermediary process that looks for the already-running browser and, if one is found, forwards the request.
On a PC that just started, you might barely notice. But in real multi-tasking scenarios, the extra work of having to look for an existing Edge process could make Edge feel slow.
Now, with accelerated app launches on Windows, when an Edge process starts, it sends a registration request to Windows. Windows checks and accepts the request. Later, when Edge is launched again, Windows can use the accelerated-launch registration to notify the already running Edge process directly.
Accelerated app launches are supported by the Start menu and the Taskbar and opening supported links that open in Edge by default.
For developers who are interested in supporting accelerated launches in their own Windows apps, see Register your application for accelerated app launches.
Making Edge work great on Windows
Accelerated app launches is part of our work to make Edge work great on Windows and we'll continue innovating in this area. We're working with Windows on adding other ways to utilize this feature, such as when opening PDF files.
We're also contributing this work to Chromium, the open-source project which Edge is based on, so other Chromium-based browsers can benefit from accelerated launches on Windows in the future.
Previous Release Notes:
Microsoft Edge supported operating systems for macOS. Microsoft Edge version 150 is the last release that supports macOS 12 (Monterey). Microsoft Edge version 151 or later requires macOS 13 (Ventura) or later. For more information, see Microsoft Edge supported operating systems.
Migration to improved V2 architecture for Workspaces. Workspaces, introduced in Edge in 2022, allows users to create durable sets of tabs that can be saved and shared with others. In order to improve reliability and performance of this feature, the following changes are being made:
- Migrating data for saved Workspaces from OneDrive/SharePoint to Edge Sync service
- Removing the collaboration/share functionality of this feature
For organizations who have disabled Sync through policy, the existing v1 Workspace data will still be migrated to the new architecture. New v2 Workspaces created after migration won't sync across devices and will remain local to each device. This update occurs on a progressive rollout beginning in Edge Stable v145 and continues rolling out through Edge v150. For more information, see Getting started with Microsoft Edge Workspaces.
Sidebar app list is being retired. We're simplifying Microsoft Edge. The sidebar app list will be retired in the near future. New apps can no longer be added to the sidebar, and apps currently pinned in the app tower will be removed in a future update. Sidebar app policies will no longer be supported, and any configured sidebar app policies will no longer be applied. For more information, see Streamline access to your favorite sites and apps with Sidebar in Microsoft Edge.
Feature Updates
Clarify choices surrounding third-party cookie settings. Language under 'Settings > Privacy, search, and services > Cookies' is updated to better describe the choices users have when managing third-party cookies.
Sign in to Edge with a Google account. Users can now sign in to Microsoft Edge using a Google account in addition to a Microsoft account from the profile menu and Edge sign-in screen. Available for Windows and macOS devices. Admins can control availability of this feature using the NonMicrosoftAccountSignInEnabled policy. Note: This is a controlled feature rollout. If you don't see this feature, check back as we continue our rollout.
Intune MAM Protected Downloads. The protected downloads feature for Intune MAM now saves downloaded files to the 'Documents > Microsoft Edge > Downloads' folder in OneDrive.
Enterprise WebView2 runtime downgrade via DowngradeVersion policy. Starting with Microsoft Edge version 150, enterprises can actively use the 'DowngradeVersion' policy to downgrade WebView2 applications. Administrators can temporarily roll back specific applications to a previous WebView2 Evergreen Runtime version (N-1 or N-2) using the new 'DowngradeVersion' policy in msedgewebview2.admx. The policy allows enterprises to mitigate critical regressions by specifying per-application executable-to-version mappings. The Edge Updater installs the target version side-by-side, and the WebView2 Loader redirects targeted applications accordingly. Downgrades automatically expire with each new WebView2 release. Applications pinned to N-1 remain on the same version (now becoming N-2) and automatically update in the next release, while applications pinned to N-2 revert to the current Evergreen Runtime. The policy applies only to enterprise-managed devices (domain-joined or MDM-enrolled). For more information, see Microsoft Edge WebView2 Policy Documentation.
Update to the "View in File Explorer" feature. When the ConfigureViewInFileExplorer policy is enabled, the View in File Explorer feature can be used in SharePoint document libraries. Microsoft Edge has updated the feature to enforce additional validation and restrictions when triggered by webpages to improve security.
Security Update Alerts in the Edge management service. Administrators can choose a severity threshold and receive alerts when a new Microsoft Edge update includes security fixes that meet or exceed that level, including zero-day fixes. This helps organizations quickly identify updates that may require attention while avoiding unnecessary notifications for routine releases. Note: This experience is in public preview and is available by opting in to Targeted Release in the Microsoft 365 admin center. For more information, see Monitoring dashboard.

articles.title: You can get up to $350 off the Pixel 11 series at Amazon today — I'd be surprised if this record-low is beaten over Black Friday
articles.text:
The Google Pixel 11 series just hit a record-low price ahead of Black Friday — and I'd be surprised if it gets cheaper
You can get up to $350 off an unlocked device
We're seeing the first round of 'early' Black Friday deals this week as retailers look to ease into the end-of-year madness. Both Amazon and Best Buy have some genuinely worthwhile listings right now, but a real highlight is the Google Pixel 11 for $699 (was $899).
This is a record-low price for Google's latest flagship, which is only a few months of as of writing. Up until now, we've seen $100 discounts and the usual trade-in rebates, but today's discount is arguably a Black Friday-quality deal if you're looking for a cheap(er) unlocked device.
I would be surprised if the device got any cheaper than this over November too, considering the Pixel 11 range came out back in late August this year. The Pixel 11 is definitely a real bargain at this price, considering it's packing the latest Tensor chipset, more RAM, and a few new eye-catching shades.
If you'd prefer a higher-end device, then you can also get the Pixel 11 Pro for $799 (was $1,099) and the Pixel 11 Pro XL for $949 (was $1,299), which are again record-low prices for either device. All these deals are also available at Best Buy today for the same price.
New record-low Google Pixel 11 deal at Amazon
We've been waiting for a decent price cut on the Google Pixel 11 — and here it is, finally. Available right now is a healthy $200 price cut across all color variations, which is a fantastic discount on this expensive device. The higher price was one of our main complaints about the Pixel 11, so this makes it an easy recommendation, considering you get the very latest chipset in this device, plus the interesting new HiLight feature.
What's new with the Google Pixel 11 series?
The Google Pixel 11 is definitely more of an iterative upgrade than some previous generations, but it's still an excellent option if you're looking for a flagship device that doesn't break the bank.
All devices in the range feature the Tensor G6 chip, plus 12GB of RAM, which should aid with both performance and efficiency. The standard Pixel 11 gets a larger 48MP main camera sensor, while the Pro devices get a 50MP main, 48MP ultrawide and 48MP telephoto cameras, with zoom extending to an ambitious 120x, assisted by AI processing. The Pro devices also get the new HiLight feature, which is an LED array around the flash that can glow in different colours.
If you'd like to read more about the Pixel 11 series, I'd recommend checking out our Google Pixel 11 Pro review and Google Pixel 11 Pro XL review pages.

articles.title: Former esports commentator builds his own custom mouse shell generator for 3D printing that doesn’t use AI — Mausstudio automatically detects buttons, screwholes, and sensor locations
articles.text:
Former esports commentator builds his own custom mouse shell generator for 3D printing that doesn’t use AI — Mausstudio automatically detects buttons, screwholes, and sensor locations
Mausstudio lets you design a 3D-printable gaming mouse shell without learning CAD.
Bastian Recha, “Unskilledcast,” is a German former CS:GO commentator, tech reviewer, and 3D printing enthusiast. On October 28, he posted a demo of his “Mausstudio” project on X that generates a customizable mouse shell around an imported 3D model of a mouse PCB intended for 3D printing — all running locally and not generated using AI.
Bastian posted on X after six days of inactivity, stating that he’s been busy working on Mausstudio, his custom 3D-printed mouse shell generator. His post shows a video of him demonstrating the software, playing around with the ways users can customize their mouse.
Mausstudio works by importing an STL 3D file of a mouse PCB, like the Razer Viper V2 Pro and Zaunkoenig M2K PCBs in Bastian’s demo, from which the software detects the location of several key components: Mouse button switch locations, sensor location, scroll wheel location, and screw hole locations. It then generates a shell around those key components, placing stems to reach the switches, cutouts for the scroll wheel, buttons for the side switches, and base cutouts for the sensor.
Bastian’s demo also showed how users can adjust the width, length, and height of the mouse, including the location of the hump. Further customizations include weight-reducing cutouts for the upper and lower shell, with options to have a fully enclosed shell without the cutouts. To demonstrate the level of customizability, Bastian also showed a battery shelf option, allowing you to customize the location of the battery and the shelf’s size by inputting the battery’s dimensions — this feature, Bastian emphasizes, is lacking in many custom 3D-printed mice, and battery placement is treated as an afterthought, often just using hot glue or double-sided tape to adhere it.
Bastian also boasts that Mausstudio runs completely locally and without generative AI, just math and algorithms.
Bastian has not yet announced a release date for this project, nor has he announced whether this is paid or free, but he has posted an update on what has been changed since his demo, including being able to edit detected component assignments, more side button control, saving shell designs to be used on other PCBs, and cleaner geometry. We’re not sure if it can handle split PCBs like on the G Pro X Superlight, but support for that may come in the future as well.
This project looks to be a great way for users to create a mouse that’s closer to their ideal shape; good gaming mice are not cheap, and it’s a costly endeavor to buy many mice just to try out various shapes. This project may be able to let users experiment with more shapes more affordably with their existing mouse without needing CAD skills or hoping that someone has designed a mouse shell for their PCB that fits their needs. We will have to see how good the software is when it releases, and how it will improve and mature with future updates.

articles.title: Basically no one is using AI agents for their DoorDash orders
articles.text:
As AI tools and agents have continued their march across all aspects of digital life, many companies are trying to use LLMs to improve the experience of purchasing goods and services on the Internet. Thus far, though, a vanishingly small number of people seem to be taking advantage of those capabilities, at least when it comes to using the popular food delivery app DoorDash with an outside AI agent.
In a third-quarter earnings call Thursday, DoorDash co-founder and CEO Tony Xu responded to an analyst question by noting that “AI agents are generating several hundred orders [on DoorDash] across the time that they’ve been up and running.” In a marked understatement, Xu called this a “very low use case” for a company that handled just shy of 1 billion orders total in the third quarter of 2026 alone.
Speaking generally, Xu said he sees the potential for AI agents to be genuinely helpful for “long consideration purchases” and major decisions where agents would be “doing work on your behalf proactively in the background.” However, Xu added, “when it comes to a task that’s as simple as ordering food, we tend to see that come directly to DoorDash.”
Give it time?
To be fair to the AI boosters, DoorDash only rolled out its Model Context Protocol (MCP) connector less than a month ago. The connector provides a standardized, open-standard way for third-party AI tools to easily order through DoorDash’s platform. Without that kind of linkup—which is still only available to a small number of “early beta partners” and mainly used to streamline corporate lunch orders—AI agents have to go through a bit more effort to access DoorDash through a web interface, for instance.

articles.title: Estos Galaxy Watch estarían a punto de quedarse sin nuevas funciones de Samsung
articles.text:
Samsung podría dejar sin actualizaciones a sus Galaxy Watch más antiguos. Una filtración asegura que la surcoreana está considerando no lanzar más actualizaciones de sistema para los relojes inteligentes más viejos, privándolos de nuevas funciones. El soporte para los Galaxy Watch antiguos estaría limitado a parches de seguridad, tal y como ocurre con los móviles.
La información proviene del conocido filtrador kro_roe, quien asegura que Samsung ya no lanzará nuevas versiones de Wear OS y One UI Watch para relojes antiguos. El reporte no menciona qué modelos entrarían en esta categoría ni cuáles serían los motivos de la decisión. Es probable que la medida afecte a los Galaxy Watch 4 y 5, que están a punto de alcanzar el número de actualizaciones prometido por el fabricante.
Que un dispositivo se quede sin soporte no es novedad. Samsung y otras compañías ofrecen algunos años de actualizaciones de sistema operativo y parches de seguridad. Una vez que se cumple el tiempo de vida útil, estos dispositivos ya no reciben nuevas funciones ni correcciones de errores. Aunque los relojes no dejarán de funcionar, los usuarios ya no podrán aprovechar las características más recientes del sistema operativo.
Los Galaxy Watch 4 y 5 se quedarían sin actualizaciones pronto
Los principales candidatos que encajan en este escenario son los Galaxy Watch 4 y Galaxy Watch 5, que ya llegaron al final del camino. El Watch 4 ya recibió las cuatro actualizaciones de sistema operativo conocido, por lo que cumple el compromiso de soporte de Samsung. En el caso del Galaxy Watch 5, el reloj está en la lista de dispositivos compatibles con One UI 9 Watch, que sería la última versión antes de ser discontinuado.
De confirmarse por el fabricante, estos relojes no quedarían abandonados de inmediato. Aquellos que tengan un Galaxy Watch 4 o Galaxy Watch 5 podrán utilizarlos sin problemas, ya que los dispositivos pasarán a la fase de mantenimiento. Las únicas descargas disponibles a partir de este punto serán las actualizaciones para corregir vulnerabilidades o mejorar la estabilidad del sistema.
La situación será distinta para generaciones más recientes como los Galaxy Watch 8 o el primer modelo Ultra, ya que estos todavía tienen garantizados más ciclos de soporte. En el caso de los recién lanzados Galaxy Watch 9 y Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, Samsung lanzó un programa más ambicioso que ofrece hasta cinco actualizaciones de sistema y cinco años de parches de seguridad.
Con el fin del soporte para los modelos viejos, los usuarios podrían buscar alternativas. La más evidente sería comprar un reloj más nuevo, pero si el tuyo funciona sin problemas y no tienes dinero, tal vez exista un truco para extender el soporte aún más. Muchos usuarios están usando la IA para eliminar funciones o devolver el soporte a dispositivos Samsung, sin depender de lo que tiene planeado la marca.

articles.title: Les lunettes Subvocal veulent vous faire écrire bouche fermée à 200 mots par minute
articles.text:
J’écris ces lignes avec un doigt cassé. Depuis sept semaines, chaque paragraphe me rappelle à quel point le clavier est une interface brutale et inefficace dès lors que l’on perd un membre, et la dictée vocale une solution gênante dès qu’on n’est pas seul dans la pièce. C’est exactement le créneau que vise Subvocal (bon, okay, pas moi, mais plutôt les vibecoders qui tiennent à se montrer au Starbucks).
« Taper est lent. Parler à son ordinateur est gênant. » C’est ainsi qu’Aarush Yadav, cofondateur de la start-up, a résumé son pitch sur X le 30 octobre 2026, en annonçant une levée de 1,3 million de dollars auprès de Y Combinator et du fonds Afore Capital. Le produit ? Des lunettes qui ressemblent aux dernières Meta Ray Ban et qui suivent les muscles de la parole intérieure grâce à un capteur sans contact, et traduisent en texte un mouvement de bouche silencieux, presque invisible. Le tout à plus de 200 mots par minute, selon l’entreprise.
Ce que promet Subvocal (et ce qu’on ignore)
D’après sa page de précommande, les lunettes n’ont pas besoin de caméra pour capter cette parole muette. Les préventes, malheureusement réservées aux États-Unis, demandent un acompte de 199 dollars sur un prix « early bird » de 499 dollars, pour des livraisons estimées au premier trimestre 2027. L’entreprise, issue de la promotion d’automne 2026 de Y Combinator, a été fondée par Aarush Yadav, passé par Georgia Tech, et Arnav Kumar.
Le chiffre de 200 mots par minute évoqué par l’entreprise est prometteur, mais pourrait tout autant être une promesse en l’air. Un bon dactylographe tourne autour de 40 à 60 mots par minute et une conversation normale, autour de 150. Subvocal promet donc d’écrire plus vite qu’on ne parle, sans émettre un son. Ce qui semble logique, si et seulement si tout fonctionne comme ils l’imaginent : l’écriture se passe avant le son.
On pourrait pourtant y croire, au vu des progrès de la dictée vocale boostés à l’IA. La parole dite subvocale est un vieux sujet de recherche. Quand on lit ou qu’on se parle intérieurement, la langue, la mâchoire et le larynx reçoivent des micro-signaux nerveux, même si rien ne bouge visiblement. En 2018, le chercheur Arnav Kapur (qui n’est pas Arnav Kumar de Subvocal), alors au MIT Media Lab, présentait AlterEgo, un dispositif à électrodes posées sur la mâchoire qui reconnaissait ces signaux avec environ 92 % de précision, en conditions contrôlées. Le projet est devenu une start-up en 2025 et a montré en septembre de la même année un appareil porté autour de l’oreille, toujours sans date de commercialisation. Meta, de son côté, mise sur l’électromyographie au poignet avec le bracelet Neural Band vendu avec ses lunettes Ray-Ban Display, qui permet notamment d’écrire en traçant les lettres du doigt.
Reste qu’aucune démonstration n’a été publiée par Subvocal. Les 200 mots par minute sont un chiffre maison, sans indication de taux d’erreur, de temps d’apprentissage nécessaire pour chaque utilisateur ou d’étendue du vocabulaire. Or en reconnaissance de la parole, la vitesse ne vaut rien sans la précision : 200 mots par minute avec un mot faux sur dix, c’est poubelle.
Et 1,3 million de dollars reste une somme modeste dans le matériel, même avec l’appui de Y Combinator : c’est tout juste de quoi financer des prototypes, mais pas du tout une chaîne de production. L’histoire des objets connectés est pavée de précommandes jamais honorées. Notre avis : attendre les premiers prototypes et les premiers tests avant de craquer.
Murmurer à nos machines
Depuis que l’IA générative a fait du langage naturel l’interface universelle, le goulot d’étranglement s’est déplacé : la machine comprend à peu près tout, encore faut-il lui parler. Le clavier hérite de la machine à écrire du XIXe siècle, la dictée vocale reste impraticable dans un open space ou un TGV. Entre les deux, et avant les implants cérébraux façon Neuralink, la parole silencieuse est la dernière marche non invasive.
Si Subvocal tient sa promesse, nous pourrons parler à nos machines sans bouger les lèvres.
