articles.title: Credit Direct wants to bring loans closer to Nigerians
articles.text:
Credit Direct, the consumer lending subsidiary of FCMB Group, a Nigerian financial services group, is expanding beyond traditional lending into embedded finance as it seeks to make credit and other financial services more accessible to individuals and businesses.
Victoria Arinze, product marketing lead at Credit Direct, said at Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos that Credit Direct wants to use partnerships with businesses and merchants to bring credit closer to these transactions.
Embedded finance involves integrating financial services into platforms where customers already make payments or conduct other transactions, allowing them to access services such as loans without having to approach a financial institution separately.
The continent’s 50 million small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face a funding gap estimated at more than $330 billion. Credit Direct aims to close this by extending its lending expertise and integrating financing into the platforms that businesses and people use.
“We are primarily a credit organisation, and that has not changed and will never change. Credit is still the core of what we do,” Arinze said “What we’ve realised, however, is that credit really is not the end of how a person’s finances is built. When you give them credit, they then need to live their life, and living their life means being able to pay for things when they want to or when they have to.”
Founded in 2007, Credit Direct has spent nearly two decades lending to Nigerians, including customers in markets traditional lenders have often been reluctant to serve. Its 2025 Nigeria Credit Landscape Report, which draws on data from more than 300,000 borrowers, found that the average loan amount on its platform increased by 23.5% to ₦449,178 ($326.75) in 2025, with rent, medical bills, and school fees being the three leading reasons customers borrowed.
Credit Direct is also expanding into SME financing through CreditDirect Business, one of its newer products. The product offers general-purpose loans, invoice-backed financing, and loan purchase order (LPO) contract financing, with loans of up to ₦50 million ($37,130) available to eligible businesses. Loan amounts depend on factors including cash flow, existing obligations, and the nature of the business. Arinze said it is still relatively new and that the company is using customer feedback and engagement to determine how its products should evolve.
“We’re not really looking to outbank the banks or out-fintech the fintechs. It’s really the people at the end of the day, and getting to that strength to partner with the persons that we have to when we need to,” she said.
Arinze said the company is now exploring expansion into other West African markets, with discussions currently ongoing. It did not disclose specific countries or timelines.

articles.title: 12 € pour GTA VI, 0,45 € pour un film : une taxe inédite sur les données adoptée à l'Assemblée
articles.text:
Netflix, Steam, cloud : vos abonnements et téléchargements bientôt plus chers à cause d'une nouvelle taxe ?
Malgré l’avis défavorable du gouvernement et du rapporteur général, les députés ont adopté un amendement socialiste créant une taxe au gigaoctet sur les fournisseurs de contenus en ligne. Une mesure aux répercussions potentielles étendues.
Le vote s'est joué à une voix près dans l'hémicycle : 11 voix contre 10. L'amendement n° I-1358 au projet de loi de finances, déposé par le groupe Socialistes et apparentés, entend instituer une contribution assise sur les volumes de données acheminés vers les utilisateurs français. Fixée à 0,055 euro par gigaoctet, cette fiscalité vise à générer jusqu'à 10 milliards d'euros de recettes en ciblant l'activité réelle des acteurs du numérique.
Un prélèvement au volume mesuré par les opérateurs télécoms
Le fonctionnement du dispositif confie aux fournisseurs d'accès à internet (FAI) la responsabilité de relever chaque trimestre les volumes émis par chaque acteur, sous le contrôle conjoint de l'Arcep et de la Direction générale des finances publiques. Le texte inclut également les réseaux de diffusion de contenu (CDN) afin de mesurer les flux issus des serveurs relais situés au plus près de l'utilisateur.
Pour éviter d'asphyxier les services à forte consommation de bande passante mais aux marges plus mesurées, un plafonnement a été intégré. Le montant réclamé ne pourra excéder 15 % du chiffre d'affaires réalisé en France, ou 2 % du chiffre d'affaires mondial. En complément de l'objectif budgétaire, les auteurs mettent en avant une dimension écologique, estimant que ce coût incitera les éditeurs à optimiser et compresser leurs flux.
De la vidéo aux jeux dématérialisés : les services dans le viseur
Si l'amendement précise que l'impôt est acquitté par les fournisseurs de contenus et non par les internautes, la liste des plateformes et services techniques susceptibles d'entrer dans le champ d'application couvre une part considérable des usages numériques quotidiens :
- Streaming vidéo et direct : Les plateformes comme Netflix, YouTube, Disney+, Prime Video, Twitch ou TikTok représentent l'essentiel du trafic descendant, aux côtés des plateformes de télévision et replay (TF1+, France.tv, MyCanal).
- Jeux vidéo et divertissement interactif : Les boutiques en ligne telles que Steam (Valve), l'Epic Games Store, le PlayStation Network ou le Xbox Network manipulent des fichiers d'installation et des mises à jour pesant fréquemment entre 50 et 150 gigaoctets.
- Intelligence artificielle et dépôts de code : Les services d'hébergement de modèles et jeux de données comme Hugging Face ou GitHub génèrent des transferts de plusieurs dizaines de gigaoctets par fichier, souvent distribués gratuitement.
- Services de cloud et synchronisation : Les espaces de stockage et de sauvegarde tels que Google Drive, OneDrive, iCloud ou Dropbox, ainsi que les infrastructures d'hébergement (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud).
- Réseaux sociaux et communication : Les applications comme Instagram, X, Discord ou les outils de visioconférence (Teams, Zoom).
- Réseaux de diffusion de contenu (CDN) : Les prestataires d'infrastructure comme Cloudflare, Akamai ou Fastly, expressément visés pour leurs points de livraison de données.
- Mises à jour de systèmes : La distribution des correctifs pour Windows, macOS, iOS ou les distributions Linux.
Des répercussions prévisibles pour les utilisateurs
Bien que les consommateurs ne soient pas directement taxés, les entreprises soumises à ce prélèvement pourraient adapter leur modèle économique. Pour compenser la charge financière ou éviter d'atteindre le plafond légal, certains acteurs pourraient répercuter le coût sur les prix des abonnements, restreindre la bande passante vers les connexions situées en France ou instaurer des limitations sur les téléchargements de fichiers très volumineux.
Adopté de justesse en séance publique à l'Assemblée, le texte doit encore poursuivre son parcours législatif. Il sera soumis à l'examen du Sénat et devra surmonter les réserves exprimées par l'exécutif avant une éventuelle intégration définitive dans la loi de finances.

articles.title: Anthropic just removed one of Claude’s biggest usage limits — but not for everyone
articles.text:
Anthropic just removed one of Claude’s biggest usage limits — but not for everyone
Claude Code users on Anthropic’s $200 plan will no longer face a rolling five-hour usage cap, provided their accounts are verified and they have weekly usage left.
Anthropic announced the change Friday as it renamed its two top consumer plans. Max 5x is now Max, and Max 20x becomes Ultra. They still cost $100 and $200 a month, respectively, and current subscribers don’t need to do anything to switch.
Max 5x is now Max, and Max 20x becomes Ultra.
Anthropic’s pricing page also lists monthly Claude Platform API credits: $100 with Max and $200 with Ultra. That adds another consideration for developers who use Claude Code while building applications against the API, with each plan bundling API credits equal to its monthly subscription price. Claude Code creator Boris Cherny highlighted the limit change in his own post.
What the five-hour cap meant
The five-hour limit capped usage within a rolling window, and a demanding task could burn through that allowance much sooner. Claude Code users could hit it midway through debugging or a large refactor and have to wait for a reset despite having weekly usage left.
Verification comes first
Some Ultra subscribers will have to wait for Anthropic to verify their accounts before the five-hour limit goes away. The company says the checks help prevent fraud and abuse, and it will email users when the cap is lifted.
Some Ultra subscribers will have to wait for Anthropic to verify their accounts before the five-hour limit goes away.
According to Anthropic’, verification happens automatically based on account and payment history. There’s no way to request it or speed it up so some users will just have to be patient.
The weekly cap remains
Ultra users still have the same weekly allowance, and they could use it up sooner without the five-hour limit forcing them to pause. The pricing page lists Ultra at 10 times Pro’s weekly usage, compared with five times Pro’s weekly usage on Max.
The pricing page lists Ultra at 10 times Pro’s weekly usage, compared with five times Pro’s weekly usage on Max.
Your chats with Claude count toward the same weekly limit as your Claude Code sessions, whether you’re on the web, desktop, or mobile. Once you use up that allowance, you can turn on usage credits to keep working at standard API rates, though you’ll pay extra on top of your subscription.
If you keep hitting the session limit with weekly usage to spare, avoiding those interruptions could make Ultra worth the extra $100 a month over Max, but if you already run out before the week is over, removing the session cap won’t give you more included usage.
OpenAI eases its limits
A day earlier, OpenAI’s Thibault Sottiaux announced higher usage limits for Pro subscribers and Business Premium.
OpenAI also dropped a planned cut for existing $200 Pro subscribers after customers objected. In a separate pricing decision, the company abandoned an idea to replace token-based billing with flat per-job fees after developers pushed back.

articles.title: Syrian Hacker Gets Prison Time in US After Over a Decade on the Run
articles.text:
A Syrian man tied to the Syrian Electronic Army (SEA) has received a 42-month prison sentence in the US, more than 12 years after he was first charged.
Ahmad Umar Agha, who used the online handle Th3Pr0, was sentenced on Thursday by a federal court in the Eastern District of Virginia. According to the Justice Department, he evaded US authorities for more than a decade.
Prosecutors say the hacking conspiracy Agha took part in was directed by figures close to Bashar al-Assad, among them the head of Syria’s General Intelligence Directorate. The scheme began as early as August 2011 and continued until January 2024.
The DOJ described Agha as a central figure in the operation. He compromised around 47 targets, a mix of Western news outlets, companies, NGOs, and government bodies in the US and allied countries.
Among the intrusions highlighted by prosecutors was the 2013 takeover of the Associated Press’s Twitter account. Agha used it to publish a fabricated report claiming that President Barack Obama had been hurt in two blasts at the White House. The fake post triggered a flash crash that briefly wiped $136 billion off the combined value of the Dow Jones Industrial Average’s component stocks.
Agha also gained access to the company hosting the Marine Corps’ recruiting website and sent its traffic to an image calling on Marines to defy their orders.
He twice went after the White House’s social media presence by targeting the email credentials of White House employees. In one case he obtained them, but his attempt to use that access to dupe other staffers into handing over the accounts did not work.
The intrusions left many victims with large bills for cleanup and security overhauls. A firm providing online publishers with content, advertising, and outbound links lost around $35,000 per day for about six months. A global NGO spent roughly $250,000 on new network monitoring tools, retrained more than 800 employees, and upgraded its security, with total losses of $480,000.
Agha and his alleged accomplice, Firas Dardar, were first charged by criminal complaint in June 2014. The case was unsealed in March 2016, when the FBI put both men on its Cyber’s Most Wanted list and offered a reward of up to $100,000 for information leading to Agha’s arrest.
A grand jury indicted the pair in May 2018. Dardar has yet to be caught.
Agha’s appearance in a federal courtroom in November 2025 was first reported by legal news outlet Court Watch. The DOJ’s announcement does not explain how or where he was taken into custody.

articles.title: Binance loses $6.3 billion in largest crypto heist ever
articles.text:
What we know so far: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, has suffered a cyberattack believed to be the largest crypto theft in history. Crypto worth more than $6 billion has been stolen from the platform, which initially suspended customer deposits and withdrawals. It's believed that a North Korean hacking unit was responsible for the attack.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs puts the haul at approximately $6.36 billion, taken from Binance wallets across ten blockchains on October 29. Most of the money was moved in about 20 minutes. The firm attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit, with high confidence.
There is some good news for customers. Binance says it has worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets and will cover all losses. Deposits are now operating normally, although withdrawals remain suspended. The exchange said on Friday that it expected withdrawals to resume within the next day or two.
The initial investigation pointed to a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer. Binance said this allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawals. It added that it had found no evidence that wallet private keys had leaked.
However, the company subsequently said investigators had uncovered additional points of breach, describing the incident as a complex attack – so the compromised laptop is unlikely to be the whole story. Binance has promised to release more technical details once its investigation is complete and the findings have been verified.
Elliptic also suspects North Korea was responsible. The blockchain analytics company says the attacker funded a wallet using small withdrawals from Tornado Cash, rehearsed the attack in advance, and executed previously signed transactions in a single burst.
The amount stolen is more than four times the $1.5 billion taken in the Bybit hack in February 2025, which was the largest crypto heist at the time. That attack targeted a cold wallet during a transfer, prompting a rush of customer withdrawals and assurances that the exchange could cover its losses.
Binance has been here before, albeit on a much smaller scale. In May 2019, hackers stole 7,000 bitcoins worth around $40.7 million from its hot wallet. The attackers also obtained user API keys and two-factor authentication codes. Binance used its emergency fund to cover that theft.

articles.title: Hackers vaciaron las billeteras de unos 700 usuarios de Polymarket y robaron al menos USD 2,7 millones
articles.text:
Polymarket suspendió durante cerca de una hora las operaciones de su plataforma internacional el 29 de octubre, después de que hackers vaciaran las billeteras de cientos de usuarios. Según firmas de análisis de datos cripto, unos 710 usuarios perdieron al menos USD 2,7 millones. La empresa prometió reembolsar a todos los afectados.
Polymarket es una plataforma donde los usuarios apuestan sobre el resultado de eventos, desde las elecciones legislativas de Estados Unidos hasta la fecha de lanzamiento de un videojuego. La versión internacional funciona con criptomonedas y está prohibida en Estados Unidos y en otros países, según Wired.
La empresa informó que uno de sus proveedores externos fue vulnerado y que derivó el caso a las autoridades. “Cualquiera que haya sido afectado será compensado”, escribió en un comunicado citado por BleepingComputer. Polymarket pasó a un modo en el que solo se permitía cancelar órdenes a las 14:05, hora del Este de Estados Unidos.
Las operaciones volvieron a la normalidad a las 15:05, según el relato de la propia empresa recogido por BleepingComputer. Los primeros reclamos de billeteras vaciadas aparecieron cerca de las 13:30, de acuerdo con The Washington Post, y varios traderes conocidos se quejaron de pérdidas en la red social X.
El código malicioso venía de una herramienta de medición web
Una persona al tanto del caso dijo a CNBC que el problema se originó en DebugBear, un servicio de monitoreo del rendimiento de sitios web con sede en el Reino Unido. DebugBear confirmó en X que sufrió un “incidente de seguridad” y pidió a sus clientes retirar su código de monitoreo de las páginas.
BleepingComputer analizó el script (un programa que se ejecuta en el navegador del usuario) y concluyó que fue alojado en la infraestructura de DebugBear. El código comprobaba si el visitante tenía una sesión abierta en Polymarket y, si era así, usaba esa sesión para operar en su nombre.
Según ese análisis, el programa intentaba vender las posiciones de los usuarios en los mercados de apuestas o transferir sus fichas a una billetera controlada por el atacante. También intentaba convertir las criptomonedas de la víctima en activos que pudieran enviarse a esa billetera.
La firma de seguridad Hudson Rock identificó la billetera del atacante. BleepingComputer rastreó que transfirió unos 28,6 millones de POL, una criptomoneda valuada en cerca de USD 2,57 millones, a otras tres billeteras. Hudson Rock también halló un cambio en el código de Polymarket, fechado a las 13:59, que eliminaba la integración con DebugBear.
Entre 700 y 710 afectados y un monto aún sin confirmar
Las firmas Betting Intelligence y Polysights, citadas por CNBC, calcularon que una cuenta retiró al menos USD 2,7 millones de 710 billeteras. La firma de análisis Bubblemaps estimó unos 700 afectados y la misma cifra de dinero, según Wired. BleepingComputer, por su parte, rastreó cerca de USD 2,5 millones hasta una billetera sospechosa.
Polymarket se negó a decirle a Wired cuántos usuarios se vieron afectados o cuánto dinero se perdió. La plataforma para usuarios dentro de Estados Unidos, que opera como un mercado financiero regulado y es independiente de la internacional, no sufrió el ataque.
Los usuarios a quienes se les retiraron menos de USD 10.000 recibirían la restitución de sus fondos el 30 de octubre, según lo que Polymarket comunicó a los usuarios en Discord, citado por CNBC. Quienes perdieron más de esa cifra deberán firmar un formulario de renuncia a reclamos para recibir el reembolso.

articles.title: Madrid's Talky raises €1.5 million to teach AI the unwritten rules of accounting | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Talky Labs, a Spanish startup developing AI-powered technology to automate accounting and financial operations, has raised €1.5 million in a pre-Seed funding round to support team expansion, further product development and improvements to the company’s technical infrastructure.
The investment, closed in September 2026, saw participation from venture capital firms HelloWorld, Silence VC, Motive Force, and Aera Capital. Alongside angel investors Sebastián Gunningham; CEO of Remitly, Paul Golbaum; CEO of Lightbase and former CTO of Seedtag, and Javier Morenés, among others.
“Two years ago, I met my co-founder Jorge Beamonte at a networking event. That night, I called my mom and told her: ‘Mom, today is the most important day of my life. Everything is about to change,‘” said Maximilian Letón in a public statement.
Talky’s funding comes amid a series of European investments in AI-powered accounting and financial operations during 2026.
In Belgium, Dytto raised €1.5 million to develop its AI assistant for accountants, while Denmark’s Plinto secured €2.9 million for automated financial controls. Germany’s mika raised €6 million for AI-powered accounting and tax services, and UK-based Zalos obtained €3.1 million for enterprise finance automation.
In Spain, Barcelona-based Dolfin secured €2.1 million for adjacent financial workflows.
Together these rounds amount to approximately €66.8 million, including Talky’s investment.
“Every company has its own way of doing accounting, and it’s almost never written down. Talky learns those criteria, applies them to the hard cases and turns them into information for better decisions,” adds Jorge Beamonte, co-founder and CEO of Talky.
Founded in 2025 by Jorge Beamonte; CEO, and Maximilian Letón (23); COO, Talky aims to help businesses automate financial processes that traditionally depend on accountants’ experience and knowledge of internal company practices. Despite operating with a team of just nine employees, the startup reports having processed more than 1.8 million documents and over €2 billion in client expenditure through its platform.
The company addresses a common challenge in corporate finance departments: accounting decisions often rely on information scattered across enterprise systems, spreadsheets, emails, contracts and individual employees’ knowledge. While conventional automation tools can process standard transactions, unusual invoices or exceptions frequently require manual intervention, creating delays and increasing the risk of errors.
Talky’s platform uses AI to learn from a company’s historical accounting records and the expertise of its financial teams. Rather than relying exclusively on predefined rules, its technology identifies how previous transactions were handled, extracts relevant accounting criteria and applies that knowledge to new financial operations.
When the system encounters an unfamiliar situation or lacks sufficient information to make a decision, it identifies the appropriate employee to consult.
According to the startup, its technology processes between 86% and 93% of accounting documents without human intervention. The platform can read invoices, suggest accounting entries, review tax information and reconcile bank transactions before recording the results in the client’s enterprise resource planning (ERP) system.
The funding comes as Talky looks to expand its presence among large enterprises and financial services providers managing high volumes of transactions. Its founders have identified recruitment as a central priority, with plans to grow the team while continuing to develop the platform alongside existing customers.

articles.title: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
articles.text:
Crater counts tell us that most of the Martian surface is more than 3 billion years old, but pieces of Mars we have on Earth tell a different story. The three main classes of Martian meteorites—shergottites, nakhlites, and chassignites—are all 2.4 billion years old or younger. Until now, only two genuinely ancient Martian meteorites were known: Allan Hills 84001, found in Antarctica, and a jumbled rock from northwest Africa nicknamed Black Beauty. Now we have a third one.
A team led by Yang Liu, a planetary scientist at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, has shown that a Martian meteorite called Teghaza 001, found in the Sahara Desert in Mali in 2022, formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. “It’s very old and similar to some of the oldest rocks on Earth,” Liu says.
A filtered collection
“We don’t fully understand why old Martian rocks are so rare on Earth,” Liu said. Part of the answer may lie in how a piece of Mars gets here. It takes a large impact to launch a rock off the planet, and not every rock can survive that. “If the impact hits into loose powder, it may not get cemented to become a rock and fly off Mars’ gravity,” Liu said. “So the natural impact already acts as a filter. Weak rocks do not make it off Mars.”
That left scientists with a biased collection.
“Even to date, none of our collected Martian meteorites are similar to what we found on the surface,” Liu said. The partial exception is Black Beauty, which has a bulk chemistry that matches orbital measurements. But Black Beauty is a mix of soil and many small rock fragments. Teghaza 001 is a single, intact igneous rock.
Teghaza 001 was acquired through the desert meteorite trade, where hunters comb the Sahara for dark stones that stand out against the sand. Its eight stones, weighing just under 800 grams in total, were bought by a private collector, who sent a piece to the University of New Mexico for classification. There, planetary scientists Carl Agee and Karen Ziegler measured its oxygen isotopes. “Each planetary body has a very characteristic oxygen isotope value,” Liu says. Teghaza 001’s values matched those of other Martian meteorites.
At first, the rock was classified as a shergottite, the most common (and young) type of Martian meteorite. But Agee noticed some oddities and reached out to Liu. One of Teghaza’s minerals had been altered on the inside while its outer part stayed pristine, the reverse of how weathering on Earth works. The oxygen isotopes looked a bit strange, and there was some manganese-rich material similar to what Liu had studied in Black Beauty.
“When I got to the sample, I looked around, I said, ‘That’s boring,’” Liu said. “The high-manganese material is actually terrestrial, but I quickly realized the sample is very different, very special.”
Teghaza 001 is made mostly of feldspar, a pale mineral common in the crusts of rocky planets. It has darker pyroxene crystals mixed in; according to Liu, those resemble some rocks exposed in the lunar highlands. Its crystals are rather big, up to a millimeter across, which scientists interpret as an indication it cooled down slowly. “For slow-cooled rock, they tend to have time to grow bigger,” Liu said.
By comparing the crystals with lab experiments and terrestrial rocks, the team estimated Teghaza 001 cooled by roughly 0.01° Celsius per year, indicating it formed from magma that never erupted but instead solidified inside the crust.
Clocks reset by water
The team dated the rock in several independent ways. Zircon grains gave about 4.11 billion years. Phosphate minerals and rubidium-strontium dating gave similar ages. “Doesn’t matter what type of zircon we are analyzing or what mineral we are analyzing, we get this very consistent age. And we didn’t expect that,” Liu said.
It is notoriously hard to reset the age of zircons, and the impact that launched the rock, while strong enough to forge high-pressure minerals, wasn’t hot enough to do it. “To change it, you really require some kind of hydrothermal fluid,” Liu said.
Sodium-rich rims on feldspar grains and sodium trapped in the zircons support the idea that hot water percolated through the rock shortly after it formed. So 4.1 billion years marks its last soaking, the youngest of what were probably several alteration events. “The crystallization age would be older than 4.1 billion years,” Liu said.
Teghaza 001 is also unusually rich in oxygen-18, a heavier form of oxygen, with about two parts per thousand more than other Martian meteorites. Neither crystallization nor gas escaping from magma can produce a difference that big. Because water that reacts with rock at low temperatures near the planet’s surface forms minerals rich in heavy oxygen, the team thinks the magma either swallowed bits of crust that had already interacted with surface water or reacted directly with fluids that had picked up the same heavy signature.
This implies that “There was active circulation of water through Martian crust,” Liu said. “When this rock was forming, we do have a hydrosphere on Mars, and that hydrosphere is reacting with Martian crust intensely.” The water must have been circulating through the crust and reacting with magma before it had even finished cooling. “It’s actually more dynamic and more active than we thought,” Liu said. She argues that this finding fits the picture of a wet early Mars and points to potentially habitable environments in its crust.
Teghaza 001 also reveals details about Mars’ interior. The rock crystallized near the surface, but the magma it formed from came from much deeper. Ratios of trace elements that resist alteration, like the zirconium to titanium ratio, differ from those in every other Martian meteorite. The team’s melting models matched the rock’s chemistry best when its mantle source contained garnet, a mineral that is stable in the Martian mantle only at depths of more than 160 kilometers.
Studies of other Martian meteorites suggest that as an early ocean of magma solidified on Mars roughly 4.5 billion years ago, the mantle separated into three to five reservoirs. Teghaza 001’s source does not match any of them. “In the first few hundred million years, the Martian mantle was evolving in a way that’s more complicated than we thought,” Liu said.
The orbital view
Comparing the rock’s chemistry with orbital maps, the team suggests it most likely came from the southern highlands, northwest of the giant Hellas impact basin. “No matter how many meteorite samples we have, we will always have this question: Where are they coming from on Mars?” Liu said.
Orbital data can narrow a source down to a patch of roughly 100 by 100 meters at best, which often amounts to one pixel in our remote sensing data. When Teghaza 001 left Mars is also an open question. “We only did the minimum required to make the world know this sample is special,” Liu said, adding that two or three groups are already studying it to get further insights.
The real game-changer, Liu said, would be samples collected with careful geological context, like those Perseverance has gathered in and around Jezero Crater. Liu would like to see some from terrains as old as Teghaza 001 or older. “If these samples come back, there are so many discoveries that can be made,” Liu said. “This could revolutionize our understanding of Mars and the early solar system.”
Jacek Krywko is a freelance science and technology writer who covers space exploration, artificial intelligence research, computer science, and all sorts of engineering wizardry.

articles.text:
Melhor Tablet TCL: 6 modelos para comprar em 2026
Tablets TCL são opções acessíveis para estudo, leitura e produtividade leve; veja a lista com os 6 melhores modelos à venda no Brasil
Os tablets TCL são indicados para quem busca preço acessível em um aparelho para o dia a dia. O portfólio da marca inclui modelos básicos e intermediários, que podem ser uma boa escolha para quem procura um dispositivo para leitura, estudos, produtividade leve ou assistir vídeos.
Entre as opções, estão tablets com tela grande, modelos com tecnologia Nxtpaper e dispositivos com suporte a redes móveis, para maior mobilidade.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog lista 6 modelos de tablets da TCL para comprar em 2026, com opções para todos os gostos e bolsos.
O TCL Nxtpaper 11 Plus pode ser a escolha ideal para leitura, estudos e produtividade. Seu principal destaque é a tela grande de 11,5 polegadas com resolução 2,2K e tecnologia Nxtpaper, que promete menos reflexos e entrega melhor conforto visual para usos prolongados, simulando a sensação do papel.
Por dentro, o TCL Nxtpaper 11 Plus é equipado com chip MediaTek Helio G100 de 2,2 GHz com litografia de 6 nanômetros, além de 8 GB ou 12 GB de memória RAM e 256 GB de armazenamento expansíveis via cartão microSD. A bateria não decepciona: são 8.000 mAh com suporte a carregamento rápido e duração de até 60 dias em modo de espera.
Outro destaque do TCL Nxtpaper 11 Plus é o som surround, com quatro auto-falantes e suporte a DTS. O tablet conta com recursos de inteligência artificial integrados no sistema, como auxílio de escrita, geração de atas de reuniões, legendas em tempo real e tradutor. O produto também tem suporte a caneta.
Se você procura um tablet para trabalho e estudos, vale a pena considerar o TCL Tab A1 Plus. Trata-se de um modelo com tela grande, de 12,2 polegadas com resolução 2,4K e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz. Ele tem a com tecnologia Nxtvision, que promete experiência visual mais confortável que reduz o cansaço ocular.
O TCL Tab A1 vem com chip octa-core Snapdragon 4 Gen 2, 6 GB de memória RAM e 128 GB de armazenamento, expansíveis para até 2 TB através de cartões de memória microSD. Sua bateria tem 8.000 mAh, com autonomia para até 15 horas de reprodução de vídeos.
Com sistema operacional Android 16, o TCL Tab A1 Plus conta com recursos de inteligência artificial do Google Gemini e tem suporte a multitarefa com tela dividia e janela flutuante. Outro recurso interessante é o suporte a modo estendido e modo espelho, que permite usar o tablet como segunda tela de um computador ou notebook.
O TCL Tab 10L Gen 3 LTE é indicado para quem precisa de um tablet barato com suporte a dados móveis. Um dos diferenciais desse produto é o suporte a redes 4G: basta inserir um chip de operadora com plano de dados e usar a internet, mesmo em locais onde não há Wi-Fi.
A tela IPS de 10,1 polegadas é apenas HD e entrega o básico na experiência visual, pecando um pouco em contrastes. Em filmes, desenhos e leitura, pode ser notável um efeito blur devido à baixa resolução.
O TCL Tab 10L Gen 3 LTE é equipado com processador Mediatek MT8768V octa-core, 4 GB de memória RAM, 64 GB de armazenamento e Android na versão 14. Sua bateria tem 6.000 mAh com promessa de autonomia para até 15 horas de uso.
Por ter especificações mais simples, o TCL Tab 10L Gen 3 não é indicado para quem quer rodar jogos pesados ou trabalhar em longas sessões de multitarefa, mas o tablet se mostra como uma opção econômica para quem precisa de um dispositivo auxiliar para produtividade leve e estudo.
O TCL Tab 10L Gen 4 é outra opção de tablet acessível da marca e pode ser a escolha ideal para quem busca um produto para tarefas do dia a dia com bom custo-benefício. Sua tela tem 10,1 polegadas com resolução HD e peso de apenas 430 g, o produto é fácil de transportar.
Por dentro, o TCL Tab 10L Gen 4 tem chip octa-core MediaTek Helio G37, 4 GB de memória RAM e 128 GB de armazenamento interno, expansíveis para até 1 TB através de cartão microSD. O sistema operacional é o Android 15.
Sua bateria tem capacidade de 6.000 mAh, com promessa de até 15 horas de reprodução de vídeo. O TCL Tab 10L Gen 4 tem câmera traseira de 8 megapixels e frontal de 5 megapixels para videochamadas.
Se você procura um tablet com bom custo-benefício com uma tela de maior qualidade, vale a pena considerar o TCL Tab 11 FE. O modelo intermediário se destaca por ter uma display IPS de 11 polegadas com resolução Full HD+ e preço não muito diferente dos modelos mais básicos da TCL.
O Tab 11 FE tem chip octa-core MediaTek G80, 4 GB de memória RAM e 128 GB de armazenamento interno, expansíveis para até 1 TB via cartões microSD. Com essas especificações, o tablet pode lidar bem com estudos e trabalho leves.
Falando de câmeras, o TCL Tab 11 FE tem uma frontal de 5 megapixels com foco fixo e traseira de 8 megapixel com foco automático, suficientes para sessões de videochamada. O sistema operacional de fábrica é o Android 14.
O Nxtpaper 11 Gen 2 é outro tablet da TCL ideal para leitura, graças à tecnologia que leva o próprio nome do produto. Sua tela de 11 polegadas tem resolução Full HD+ com acabamento fosco e taxa de atualização de 60 Hz, permitindo sessões de leitura em PDF mais fluidas em comparação com leitores de e-book.
Com chip MediaTek MT8786 e 8 GB de memória RAM, o TCL Nxtpaper 11 Gen 2 tem 128 GB de armazenamento expansíveis para até 1 TB através de cartão microSD. O tablet tem Android 15 com atualizações de segurança garantidas até julho de 2027.
Falando de software, o TCL Nxtpaper 11 Gen 2 tem recursos de IA integrados como auxílio de escrita, legendas em tempo real, gerador de atas de reuniões e tradutor inteligente. Já a bateria tem capacidade de 8.000 mAh com suporte a carregamento rápido.
A TCL conta com opções de tablets para diferentes perfis de uso no mercado. Para acertar na compra, vale focar em quatro pontos principais antes de decidir o modelo ideal:
O tablet de melhor custo-benefício da TCL é o TCL Tab 10L Gen 4. Geralmente encontrado por menos de R$ 1 mil, o modelo tem tela de 10,1 polegadas e bateria para até 15 horas de reprodução de vídeos.
O melhor tablet para leitura dessa lista é o TCL Nxtpaper 11 Plus. Ele tem tela IPS LCD com acabamento fosco antirreflexo, que suaviza a o brilho excessivo, além de modo de software que simula a experiência de um leitor de e-books com tecnologia e-ink, deixando a tela em preto e branco.
Sim, vale a pena. A TCL é uma marca que oferece tablets com foco em custo-benefício, tem diferentes modelos para atender maior quantidade de público e oferece garantia no Brasil de 12 meses contados a partir da emissão da nota fiscal.
A tela Nxtpaper é, na verdade, uma tela LCD convencional, mas com acabamento fosco antirreflexo que ajuda a reduzir o brilho excessivo que gera fadiga ocular. Os tablets da TCL com essa tecnologia têm um modo de software que simula a experiência de uma tela com tecnologia e-ink, deixando o display monocromático.
O Kindle pode ser a melhor escolha se seu objetivo for ler apenas livros convencionais devido ao tamanho, duração de bateria e, principalmente, por ter uma tela e-ink. No entanto, se você precisa ler PDFs, HQs, gráficos e deseja fazer anotações durante as sessões de leitura, escolher um tablet TCL com tela Nxtpaper é a escolha ideal em comparação com o leitor de e-books da Amazon.

articles.title: Benchmarking Nvidia’s Vera CPU for the data center — standalone Vera tested against Granite Rapids-AP and EPYC Turin
articles.text:
Benchmarking Nvidia’s Vera CPU for the data center — standalone Vera tested against Granite Rapids-AP and EPYC Turin
Vera debuts with strong Python performance and unmatched memory bandwidth.
Nvidia’s Vera CPU is an important next step in the company’s years-long spearheading of AI infrastructure buildout. It’s arriving just as the shift to agentic AI workflows has created unprecedented demand for data center CPUs, and it’s designed specifically for this moment, at least according to Nvidia’s marketing bullet points. Although the idea that anyone developed a CPU for a shift in demand that arose just six months ago is reaching, as our benchmarks below show, Nvidia’s claims about Vera aren’t full of hot air.
Based on the workloads we have now — there aren’t standardized end-to-end agentic benchmarks focused on the CPU right now — Vera has strong indicators about its usefulness in agentic workflows. It offers chart-topping performance in Python, for instance, which makes up much of the backbone of the AI software ecosystem.
It also shows commanding memory bandwidth, both at the socket level and system level, with the high-speed C2C interconnect between Vera chips. In contentious agentic environments where agents may be querying large databases, that bandwidth is critical.
Specialization is one thing, but Vera is arriving in a hotly contested server market with custom Arm chips penetrating the data center and the old guard of x86 chips from AMD and Intel, which not only have a foundation in the data center, but also an extensive list of clients that work with their systems. Regardless of how Vera performs, that’s no small undertaking.
What’s surprising about Vera isn’t that it performs well in these agentic-adjacent workloads, but that it offers competent performance in general-purpose server workloads as well, often managing to match or beat the comparable AMD Turin and Intel Granite Rapids-AP chips. The scales are more balanced when looking at frontend workloads, with the core density available on x86 CPUs often the winner, but Vera trades that density for strong performance in backend, data-rich operations.
| Nvidia Vera specifications |  | 
|---|---|
| Cores / Threads | 88 / 176 | 
| L2 cache | 2 MB per core | 
| L3 cache | 164 MB per CPU | 
| Memory | Up to 1.5 TB SOCAMM2 LPPDDR5X | 
| Memory speed | Up to 9600 MT/s | 
| Memory bandwidth | Up to 1.2 TB/s (aggregate), 14 GB/s (per core) | 
| PCIe | 88 PCIe 6.4 lanes (CPU only), 96 PCIe 6.4 lanes (Vera Rubin), bifurcation down to x2, CXL 3.1 | 
| Configurable TDP | 250W - 450W | 
It’s an impressive showing for Nvidia's first custom core, called Olympus, and a stark improvement in nearly all aspects over Grace, which used an off-the-shelf Arm core design. The 88-core CPU is built on the Armv9.2-A architecture, including two threads per core through Nvidia’s “spatial multithreading.”
The chip is characterized by a 10-wide decode, similar to Arm’s AGI, as well as Nvidia’s second-gen Scalable Coherency Fabric (SCF). You can read more about the SCF and the Olympus core in our Vera deep dive, but SCF is critical to Vera’s performance. It’s a mesh that distributes L3 across the die, offering up to 3.4 TB/s of bandwidth across the die.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Vera has high memory bandwidth as well, leveraging replaceable SOCAMM2 LPDDR5X at 9600 MT/s, offering up to 1.2 TB/s of total memory bandwidth or around 14 GB/s per core, more than double that of AMD’s dense Turin designs.
We’ve heard a lot about the speeds and feeds of Vera, however. It’s time to understand its role in the modern AI data center, as well as see how it performs in our benchmarks against the x86 competition before AMD’s Venice and Intel’s Diamond Rapids start rolling out.
| Test platforms |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Test Platform | Memory | Tested Processors | 
|---|---|---|
| 2P Nvidia MGX Vera reference platform | 16 x 96 GB (1.5 TB) Samsung LPDDR5-9600 ECC SOCAMM2 | Nvidia Vera | 
| 2P Supermicro SYS-222HA | 24 x 64GB (1.5 TB) Micron DDR5-8800 ECC MRDIMM | Intel Xeon 6980P | 
| 2P AMD Volcano reference platform | 24 x 64 GB (1.5 TB) SK hynix DDR5-6000 ECC RDIMM | AMD EPYC 9965, EPYC 9755 | 
Understanding the CPU's role in agentic AI
Depending on where you’re at in the fast-moving world of agentic AI, you probably have a different definition of what exactly an agentic CPU is. Given the rise in prominence of agentic CPUs, the understanding of what makes a CPU tick for this type of workload has been largely defined by two companies: AMD and Nvidia. Although the points they’ve driven about concurrency and the varied work of agents are correct, it’s useful to derive a definition from how we’re seeing agentic platforms deployed right now.
Let’s back up from there and look at real agentic workflows in action to better understand where CPUs fit into this chain. As we’ve seen with Meta Muse and OpenAI Dots, there’s a class of persistent agent that gives you a slice of compute in the cloud. These CPU-only racks communicate with inference servers to actually run the models, but their workload is defined by concurrency. It’s not about the performance of an individual sandbox but instead how each sandbox performs when the chip is fully loaded.
Concurrency provides important context to some of the workloads companies like Nvidia and AMD have described. Some tool calls are more demanding, like code compilation and large database queries, but reading/writing files, running code tests, and going online in a headless browser is not demanding CPU work in isolation. When the chip is handling potentially thousands of these tool calls, however, slight advantages start to pile up. And, the CPU topology plays a bigger role in how performance is sustained as agent sessions increase.
That’s one major tenet of an agentic CPU, one that can maintain performance with high concurrency. The other is variability, which touches on the CPU, but also the larger infrastructure available. Mark Lohmeyer, VP/GM of AI and computing infrastructure at Google Cloud, described an example to Tom’s Hardware about planning a vacation with an agent. Using AI to plan a vacation is just about as trite as examples get, but Lohmeyer sheds some light on the unique challenge of agentic workloads from the hyperscaler perspective.
In the example, Lohmeyer described planning a vacation over the course of a month, where he would suddenly prompt the agent to do a bunch of work, but may not return to prompt again for another week. “The actual use of the underlying compute, it's happening in basically bursts, right? There's like a burst of use at the start, maybe for an hour, and then it goes away, and then a couple days later, [it] bursts again for some other purpose and goes away,” Lohmeyer said. “They're very long-running workloads, effectively long-running, but often idle, basically.”
Agentic calls for a lot of power on demand, as the right alignment of this bursty work on a server with hardware contention can bring everyone’s sessions to a crawl. This factors into the type of work the CPU is doing, as well, which can include heavy code compilation, graph traversal, and large database queries. Scale that up across several agents, all with their own independent loops that don’t neatly align with each other, and the CPU problem for agentic AI becomes clear.
In the August 2026 study, Architectural Implications of Agentic AI Workflows, from researchers at The University of Texas at Austin and Microsoft Azure, the paper describes three tasks of the CPU in an agentic flow. In addition to a scheduler for GPU inference, which is how CPUs function in one-shot-style LLM queries, CPUs also serve as orchestrators for maintaining agent states and communication, and as runners that call tools and execute agent logic (often in Python).
The paper also shows this contention that can happen when multiple agents are running at once, passing requests to the GPU, receiving responses, acting, and then passing requests back. We’re looking at a cross-section of four agents over less than half a minute, and you can already see how small CPU-based tasks can align, as well as create hangs between GPU time.
Nvidia has been clear that Vera is an agentic CPU, though defining the performance of an agentic loop is still a work in progress. “The industry built a pretty good way to benchmark traditional workloads,” Lohmeyer said. “I think this is happening now for GPUs and TPUs for inference, for example. I think we're going to need the same type of industry-level benchmarks for agentic workloads that are probably still emerging.”
Standardized benchmarks that look at the full agentic loop aren’t available yet. We have our own internal tests that we’re running and hope to have data for soon, and we’ve seen some vendor-level benchmarking from companies like Modal, but the broader industry hasn’t come forth with a set of benchmarks for the end-to-end agentic loop along the lines of a SPEC or TPC yet.
Although those tests aren’t available yet, we can still look at CPU performance through the lens of an agentic workflow, prioritizing aspects of performance that are important for agentic loops. We can also look at common workflows for agents, including code compilation for coding agents and database performance for retrieval agents. We can look at things like JSON parsing through the simdjson library, evaluating how these CPUs parse the large JSON files agents use to communicate. And we can look at the foundation of much of the AI ecosystem with Python performance.
That’s the focus of our benchmarking here, to establish where Vera stands among the x86 competition from AMD and Intel in well-known benchmarks. Hopefully we’ll have the opportunity for further testing in the near future to evaluate full agentic loops once that testing procedure is finalized.
Although we’re evaluating performance through an agentic lens here, Nvidia did not limit what tests we could run nor place any stipulations on our coverage. We’re thankful to Nvidia for providing us with remote access to a dual-socket Vera system for the purposes of testing, but beyond configuration checks to ensure the platform was operating as expected, we were left to run the tests we wanted to run. That includes several tests that are applicable to agentic workflows, but also tests from our general server CPU benchmarking suite, including Java, cryptography, compression, and rendering performance.
A gentle reminder for readers
Servers are not client PCs. You have much smarter operators with deeper access to the hardware, and often a software stack that’s unique to the specific workload at minimum, and highly tweaked and optimized for that workload at a maximum. With client CPUs, we can say that an AMD X3D chip is the best for gaming, or that Intel’s latest flagship offers the highest single-threaded performance. Servers depend much more on use cases.
In a typical review, we’d say that X is better than Y for Z purpose, and back that up with data. Here, that commentary is more muted. The reality is that hyperscalers maintain large fleets with a variety of hardware that can fit any purpose, and enterprises need to choose the hardware best suited not only for their operations, but also for TCO and a list of at least a dozen other variables that are specific to that business.
Nvidia Vera SPEC CPU 2026 estimates
So far, the primary benchmark we’ve had for Vera is SPEC CPU 2026 intrate, so we ran the full SPEC CPU 2026 suite to check Nvidia’s performance claims, as well as look at floating point performance. For anyone who hasn’t read SPEC CPU benchmarks before, there are a few disclaimers before heading into the results.
All of the runs here are estimates, and that’s due to how SPEC reporting works. There are strict reporting rules, and we’re not reporting these results to SPEC directly. The charts say “estimated,” but the numbers aren’t a guess. We ran SPEC CPU 2026 following the standard testing procedure, using the same compiler and flags for each CPU.
For the compiler, we used GCC 15.2 with a few common flags, including link-time optimization and march/mcpu to expose the correct instruction support to the compiler. We also used the general-purpose jemalloc memory allocator across all of the tests we ran.
Starting with the overall intrate, this is a series of applications primarily dealing with integer operations instead of floats, and the SOP is to run a copy of the application on each thread available. The test looks at what a CPU is capable of with many applications running at once, measuring throughput.
Nvidia’s numbers aren’t dissimilar from our own. In the company’s white paper, it showed Vera ahead of the EPYC 9755 by 3%, and with our tests, Vera is ahead by 1.5%. Keep in mind the considerably higher 512-thread count of the 9755 system here against the 352-thread Vera system. Vera absolutely runs away with performance when breaking down the score per-core.
Despite the core density of Intel’s 512-thread Xeon 6980P in a two-socket configuration, it’s not in the conversation here. Retesting with oneAPI represented an impressive 10% increase in performance with Intel-optimized binaries, but even against optimized code, Vera is 8.6% ahead with generic GCC.

No one is realistically running a single application on servers utilizing every thread available like this, but the numbers are there to browse if you’re interested.
Nvidia Vera Python and AI benchmarks
If there’s any direct benchmark for agentic AI right now, it’s Python performance. There isn’t one universal language for AI agents, but Python (and, to a lesser extent, TypeScript) make up the foundational agentic frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. A strong agentic CPU right now is defined in part by strong Python performance, and Vera has exactly that.
Starting with a broad overview, you can see the total average test times for PyBench above, with Vera leading the pack. It’s 4% ahead of the EPYC 9755, which itself leads Intel’s Xeons and the larger 9965. The AI ecosystem right now is largely built on Python, so strong performance here is a good early indicator of strong AI performance in the data center. For prompt processing, much of the process is handled on the GPU, so this pure-CPU benchmark isn’t totally representative of a real deployment. However, the CPU still plays a role here, particularly in tokenization.
Unsurprisingly, we can see the single 6980P topping the charts in prompt processing, with a 2P Xeon 6980P coming up in second place, likely on the back of Intel’s AI-specific ISA extensions. We expect AMD to further extend support for these instructions in Zen 6, which should level the playing field.

Nvidia has touted the memory bandwidth of Vera as one of the chip’s strongest points, and the industry-standard STREAM memory bandwidth benchmark backs up those claims. Vera comes with a memory bus width more than twice as large as Grace, plus a large jump up to LPDDR5X-9600. It’s capable of up to 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth through the LPDDR5X interface, and up to 1.8 TB/s of bandwidth between Vera sockets.
AMD’s support for DDR5-6000 is relatively slow, and although Intel offers more bandwidth with MRDIMMs reaching up to 8,800 MT/s, Vera is in a league of its own here. That’s true without optimization, as well. After my initial STREAM pass, Nvidia suggested passing the OpenMP “spread” policy, which distributes processes as far away from each other as possible to reduce cache/memory contention.
With AMD and Intel, we see a slight regression with this setting, but it offers Vera a massive jump in memory bandwidth. Undoubtedly, the scales will start to level off as AMD and Intel roll out their next-gen Venice and Diamond Rapids parts, both of which tout much higher memory bandwidth than their predecessors.

7-Zip traditionally favors Zen, so it’s no surprise to see both Turin configurations at the top of the charts. Vera loses out to the dual 6980P system in both compression and decompression performance via 7-Zip.

ClickHouse provides some interesting data that goes beyond a steady-state SQL database.

In Discrete Fourier Transforms (DFT) using FFTE, Vera tops the charts, as it does in Octave and CloverLeaf. Although not strictly HPC, Vera falls in the middle of the pack in intensive mathematical operations like m-queens, and it trails chips with massive core arrays in the heavily threaded Primesieve.

Code compilation is a more contentious workload, with Vera trading blows against AMD and Intel depending on the workload. Starting with the compilers themselves, Vera takes a strong lead in a timed GCC compilation, beating out a dual 9755 system by 12%. It falls into last place in our LLVM compilation tests, however, both using standard Makefiles and Ninja. These tests measure the time it takes to compile the compiler itself, not the time it takes to compile an application with it.
Elsewhere, Vera shows up strongly in ImageMagick and PHP compiles while losing out slightly to the dual 9755s in Godot. Compiler performance is important to agentic AI given the prominence of coding agents, which often need to build software from source as part of an agentic coding workflow.
Nvidia Vera encoding and rendering benchmarks
Encoding and rendering workloads aren’t the focus of Vera, but we ran our standard list of benchmarks, which includes some rendering and encoding tests. Vera has strong performance here in some applications, though it certainly takes a backseat to the headline Python and memory performance shared earlier in this article.

We normally run Blender, though there isn’t an official Arm Linux version available, so we skipped the test here. Instead, we have the cross-platform C-Ray and POV-Ray. Vera manages to outclass even the 768 threads available on a 2P EPYC 9965 server, both at 1080p and 4K. Vera also leads in POV-Ray, though on a technicality. Every server we tested was tightly coupled short of the 2P 6980P server.
For a more granular look, we have OSPRay, where Vera tops the charts in real-time path tracing, though falls short of the AMD and Intel flagships in real-time scientific visualization. The “dim_512” subset is worth drawing attention to. Strong AVX-512 performance allows AMD to offer three or even four times the performance of Vera in this workload.
Nvidia makes a delayed debut
Although Vera isn’t Nvidia’s first data center CPU, it’s the first one that the company is aggressively pursuing with the same fervor that it carries with its accelerators. It’s an impressive chip, often punching far above its weight class, especially in those workloads that can show off its unique capabilities and topology.
Still, it’s a single 88-core chip arriving in a market characterized by granular SKU lists to meet a wide range of specific workloads. Vera won’t be the right choice for all of them, which is something that Nvidia itself has already stated. “The world is not going to be served by one SKU of CPU. And that's not our intention,” said Nvidia’s Ian Buck when Vera was revealed in March.
That’s not the intention with Vera, but the performance against contemporary x86 CPUs shows that Nvidia’s new push into standalone data center CPUs has legs, more so than the various building-block-style Arm chips we’ve seen from hyperscalers, certainly. If nothing else, Vera demands some attention from AMD and Intel.
The x86 crew is responding shortly, with Zen 6 queued up to roll out through the end of the year and Intel’s Diamond Rapids targeting a 2027 release. As you can imagine, we'll be putting those chips through their paces as well.

articles.title: 'It’s 100 percent a national security threat': Accenture contractor connected an AI agent to the Pentagon’s secure network, and then sent data to a high-risk website
articles.text:
'It’s 100 percent a national security threat': Accenture contractor connected an AI agent to the Pentagon’s secure network, and then sent data to a high-risk website
Stop giving AI agents your credentials
- An AI agent was connected to a secure internal Defense Department network
- The agent was given login details to allow it to perform coding tasks, but also allowed it to bypass security controls
- The agent sent sensitive information, including the credentials, to a high-risk third party website
An Accenture contractor at the Department of Defense is in hot water over an AI agent that was given access to the Pentagon’s secure internal network.
The Claude Code agent then collected data from the network - which is used by multiple intelligence agencies - and sent it to a third-party website.
Login credentials were confirmed to have been leaked by the agent, with other controlled unclassified information potentially put at risk.
Don’t connect unauthorized agents to secure networks
According to a source familiar with the matter who spoke to Wired, “It puts all the data that’s in there at risk. There could be somebody out there with the ability to log into a secure environment without anyone knowing,” the source said.
“It’s 100 percent a national security threat and could cause irreparable harm.”
Despite Claude currently being banned from use for Defense Department staff due to Anthropic's supply chain risk designation, the Accenture employee is alleged to have given their personal Claude account access to a secure production environment in order to write and deploy code.
For two months, the AI agent had access to the secure internal network before the risk was identified and patched - but sources say once the connection was discovered it was not treated as severe or urgent by Accenture employees.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The contractor is alleged to have given the AI agent login credentials to the DoD’s Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet) in order to allow it to write code. But in order to function properly, the AI agent also needed the internet to perform its tasks.
The login credentials give the AI agent the ability to bypass the security controls enforced by the login process, and the AI agent then sent the credentials and a map of NIPRNet to a third party website.
“We are in a conflict with Iran right now,” the source added. “It’s the worst time to be having this kind of cavalier attitude.”
Both employees and contractors for the DoD are required to report any cybersecurity incidents within 72 hours, but according to the source, the Accenture employee did not raise the alarm.
“The Department does not comment on the status of its networks or systems,” the DoD told Wired.
“We take all concerns seriously. These allegations were thoroughly and independently investigated and found to be without merit. We fully complied with our legal and contractual obligations,” an Accenture spokesperson said.

Benedict is a Senior Security Writer at TechRadar Pro, where he has specialized in covering the intersection of geopolitics, cyber-warfare, and business security.
Benedict provides detailed analysis on state-sponsored threat actors, APT groups, and the protection of critical national infrastructure, with his reporting bridging the gap between technical threat intelligence and B2B security strategy.
Benedict holds an MA (Distinction) in Security, Intelligence, and Diplomacy from the University of Buckingham Centre for Security and Intelligence Studies (BUCSIS), with his specialization providing him with a robust academic framework for deconstructing complex international conflicts and intelligence operations, and the ability to translate intricate security data into actionable insights.

articles.title: Tiny magnetic vortices could help computers work more like your brain
articles.text:
Tiny magnetic vortices could help computers work more like your brain
- Date:
- October 26, 2026
- Source:
- Norwegian University of Science and Technology
- Summary:
- Scientists have filmed tiny magnetic vortices called skyrmions melting out of an organized lattice for the first time, revealing new ways to manipulate these unusual structures. The breakthrough could help make brain-like computers a reality, potentially enabling dramatically smaller and more energy-efficient technology.
- Share:
Tiny magnetic structures called skyrmions could help pave the way for a new generation of computers that process information more like the human brain while using far less electricity. Although most people have never heard of skyrmions, these microscopic magnetic vortices may eventually play an important role in how computers store and process data.
A study published in the journal Nature Nanotechnology provides new insights into how skyrmions behave and how scientists can control them. The findings could help researchers develop smaller, more efficient computing systems and advance emerging quantum technologies.
Most of the research was conducted at the Institute of Physics at Johannes Gutenberg University in Mainz, Germany, with contributions from a professor at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU).
"Skyrmions are small, magnetic vortices that can store information in a completely new way," explained Asle Sudbø, who leads NTNU's Centre for Quantum Spintronics (QuSpin).
Unlike conventional technologies, which require increasing amounts of space and energy to handle growing quantities of data, skyrmions could offer a much more efficient alternative.
"Instead of the current technology, where we constantly need more space and energy to process data, skyrmions could make it possible to build much smaller and more energy-efficient data storage systems," explained Sudbø.
Tiny Magnetic Vortices Could Enable Brain-Like Computers
The potential applications of skyrmions extend well beyond conventional data storage. They are also important to spintronics, which explores ways to use the magnetic properties of electrons in electronic devices, and to research involving topological quantum effects.
One particularly promising possibility is the development of computers that operate in ways similar to biological brains.
"These nanoscale vortices could help develop computers that resemble biological brains," said Sudbø.
Rather than relying on conventional transistor-based computing, such systems could use magnetism to process information. In principle, this approach could dramatically reduce electricity consumption, potentially allowing future computers to perform complex tasks with very little energy.
Turning that possibility into practical technology, however, requires scientists to understand exactly how skyrmions behave and how to manipulate them reliably.
The latest research represents an important advance toward that goal.
Scientists Film Magnetic Skyrmion Lattices Melting for the First Time
Skyrmions do not always exist as isolated magnetic structures. Under certain conditions, they organize themselves into repeating patterns known as lattices, resembling the orderly arrangement of atoms in a crystal, but on a much smaller scale.
Scientists can manipulate these arrangements, a capability that could be essential for using skyrmions in future computing devices.
In the new study, researchers achieved something that had not been demonstrated before. They recorded the melting of a magnetic skyrmion lattice as it happened while simultaneously controlling individual skyrmions.
"For the first time, researchers have managed to film how a magnetic skyrmion lattice melts in real time, while simultaneously being able to manipulate each individual skyrmion directly as they film it. For example, both their shape and size can be changed 'on the fly'," said Sudbø.
The ability to observe this process directly provides a clearer picture of how skyrmions respond when their organized structures break apart. It also allows researchers to study how changing the size and shape of individual magnetic vortices affects their behavior.
A New Step Toward Energy-Efficient Computing
Understanding how skyrmions behave during the breakdown of their lattices could help scientists develop more precise ways to control them. That control is particularly important if these magnetic structures are to become useful components in future computer systems.
The findings therefore offer more than a new way to observe an unusual magnetic phenomenon. They provide information that could help researchers overcome challenges involved in developing practical skyrmion-based technologies.
"The findings give us new insight into how these types of particles behave. This could therefore become important for the development of more energy-efficient computer technology in the future," said Sudbø.
Although substantial development is still needed before skyrmions can be used in everyday computing devices, the research highlights their potential for improving data storage, enabling new computing architectures, and supporting advances in quantum technology.
By learning to observe and manipulate these tiny magnetic vortices in real time, scientists are gaining capabilities that could eventually help reshape the design of computers.
"This could revolutionize the way we think about computers," concluded Sudbø.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Norwegian University of Science and Technology. Original written by Steinar Brandslet. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Raphael Gruber, Jan Rothörl, Simon M. Fröhlich, Maarten A. Brems, Fabian Kammerbauer, Maria-Andromachi Syskaki, Elizabeth M. Jefremovas, Sachin Krishnia, Asle Sudbø, Peter Virnau, Mathias Kläui. Real-time observation of topological defect dynamics mediating two-dimensional skyrmion lattice melting. Nature Nanotechnology, 2025; 20 (10): 1405 DOI: 10.1038/s41565-025-01977-2

articles.title: Esta nueva memoria promete resolver uno de los mayores problemas creados por la IA
articles.text:
La industria de los semiconductores atraviesa una de las peores crisis desde la pandemia. La explosión de la IA ha disparado la demanda de memoria a niveles nunca antes vistos, lo cual generó una escasez y aumento de precios que han golpeado a todos los segmentos, incluidos los móviles. Este escenario podría cambiar gracias a la Z2RAM, una nueva tecnología impulsada por el antiguo jefe de Intel, Pat Gelsinger.
De acuerdo con un reporte de The Register, la propuesta de la Z2RAM intenta combinar las ventajas de las tres tecnologías que dominan el mercado: SRAM, DRAM y NAND.
La SRAM es extremadamente rápida y se utiliza en las memorias caché de los procesadores, pero ocupa mucho espacio y es costosa de escalar. Mientras tanto, la DRAM ofrece una mayor densidad y es la base de la memoria RAM convencional, aunque es más lenta. Por último, la NAND, que se usa en los SSD, se distingue por su capacidad y fabricación en múltiples capas verticales.
Nagare Labs, una startup respaldada por Geslinger, intenta reunir lo mejor de estos tres mundos. Según la compañía, Z2RAM podría ofrecer la velocidad de la SRAM, la densidad de la DRAM y la arquitectura de la NAND en un mismo paquete. Esta nueva memoria sería escalable y tendría un consumo energético mucho menor, convirtiéndose en una alternativa para las empresas de IA.
¿Qué es la Z2RAM, la nueva memoria que podría acabar con el RAMaggeddon?
Una de las claves de la Z2RAM está en su diseño. Mientras que la DRAM convencional usa un transistor y un condensador para almacenar cada bit de información, Z2RAM emplea dos transistores. Esto le permite usar la capacitancia de la compuerta del segundo para almacenar la carga eléctrica, eliminando la necesidad de un condensador independiente. Además, los datos no necesitan reescribirse tras cada acceso, que es una de las limitaciones de la DRAM.
Según sus desarrolladores, la Z2RAM ha sido concebida para apilarse verticalmente como las NAND y otras tecnologías de encapsulado 3D. La memoria se vale de semiconductores de óxido y técnicas de unión híbrida tridimensional, lo que le permitiría alcanzar más de cinco veces la densidad de bits de una memoria SRAM manteniendo un ancho de banda parecido. Nagare Labs dice que un espacio capaz de albergar 64 MB de SRAM podría alojar 320 MB de Z2RAM.
La nueva memoria podría ayudar a combatir la demanda de memoria que exige la industria de la IA. Además de la potencia de cálculo, uno de los cuellos de botella de los aceleradores gráficos es la capacidad de mover y almacenar los datos con suficiente rapidez. Cuanta más memoria rápida se integre cerca de los procesadores, menos chips serán necesarios para ejecutar los modelos avanzados.
Las primeras memorias comerciales podrían lanzarse en 10 años
La Z2RAM no reemplazaría a la memoria convencional, pero si podría reducir la cantidad de aceleradores que se necesitan en los centros de datos. Esto disminuiría la presión sobre la cadena de suministro, traduciéndose en una mejor disponibilidad de componentes y una baja de precio en toda la industria.
Todo suena muy bien, excepto porque la Z2RAM se encuentra en una fase preliminar de desarrollo. Los ingenieros de Nagare Labs ya desarrollaron los primeros prototipos, pero la producción comercial podría tardar una década. La empresa tiene que resolver algunos problemas de fiabilidad y estandarización de interfaces, por lo que el camino es largo.
Aún así, la Z2RAM podría convertirse en una de las innovaciones más importantes del hardware moderno, siempre y cuando cumpla sus promesas.

articles.title: PHP2Shell Attacks Root Palo Alto Firewalls but Fail Against WordPress
articles.text:
Threat actors have been hammering servers vulnerable to PHP2Shell for over a week, but only a few successful compromises have been confirmed to date.
Standing out are Palo Alto Networks firewalls, which have been rooted by a China-linked hacking group in attacks chaining PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia kernel privilege escalation bug.
Assisted by AI, the hackers chained two separate exploits: one specifically targeting the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 on Palo Alto Networks’ PAN-OS devices, and another one for Fragnesia to deploy webshells with root privileges.
Cybersecurity outfit Dream flagged the campaign earlier this week, noting that at least 25 firewalls out of a pool of hundreds were hacked. Palo Alto Networks has since confirmed the findings.
“Dream Research has reported a campaign in which attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation vulnerability to gain root access. Unit 42 has independently verified the same attacker’s tooling and confirmed the reported results,” Palo Alto Networks said.
The company has rolled out patches that resolve the PHP2Shell flaws in PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1, and 10.2 for PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls, and for Panorama (virtual and M-Series).
“No special configuration is required to be affected by this issue. Active exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet,” the company notes in its advisory.
Palo Alto Networks says that by default the management interface is not exposed to the internet and urges customers to immediately restrict access to it and apply the available fixes.
“Only a small fraction of a percent (approximately .02%) of our global installed base has internet-facing management interfaces configured and was impacted. Each of these customers has been individually contacted by our teams. We will continue to investigate and provide any necessary updates as they become available,” Palo Alto Networks notes.
22.6 million exposed PHP instances
According to the company, as of October 29, its telemetry has identified over 22.6 million exposed PHP instances that are potentially vulnerable to the PHP2Shell bugs.
That is not surprising, given that PHP is widely used across servers and content management systems, including WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and many others.
The mass PHP2Shell exploitation has been targeting those as well, but remained largely unsuccessful, at least when it comes to WordPress, web security firm Defiant says.
As of October 28, it was not aware of any WordPress site being compromised via PHP2Shell exploitation, although it has recorded over 77,000 related requests from more than 2,000 IP addresses.
However, Defiant points out that testing has revealed the exploits often need to be adjusted to work on targeted servers, influenced by ASLR, PHP build, running extensions, memory limits, and the server’s request handling.
“Attackers are still changing their tools. A successful attack could give them access to your site’s files, database, and passwords, so updating PHP remains essential,” Defiant warned.
A handful of IPs
Despite the broad PHP2Shell exploitation attempts, success has been attributed to very few threat actors.
According to Cato Networks, roughly 96% of the attacks it has blocked targeted CVE-2026-109618, and 41% of them attempted remote code execution (RCE), while the remaining were scanning or invalid PoC attempts.
The attempts originated from a handful of IPs in the US, the Netherlands, and Germany, repeating proof-of-concept (PoC) style requests. Most of them focused on command execution, followed by deserialization attempts.
According to Cato, healthcare organizations were targeted the most, followed by technology and security services, professional services, automotive, education and non-profit, and manufacturing, construction, and retail.
The attacks, however, were not targeted, but appeared opportunistic, as the same source was seen sending requests to organizations in the healthcare, technology, and software sectors during the same day.
WatchTowr says it has observed successful PHP2Shell exploitation from a single IP address in Germany, despite the large volume of attempts and variety of payloads.
“In every case, it executes a simple ‘curl’ command to prove exploitation was successful, and stops there, with no additional post-exploitation activity,” WatchTowr head of threat intelligence Jake Knott said.
“New techniques, inventive payloads, and better appliance-specific exploits are being thrown around as more reliable exploits are worked on, and we’re likely to only see public reporting of highly targeted successful exploitation of specific edge appliances keep growing,” Knott added.

Related: Drupal Commerce Core Vulnerability Exploited Against Online Stores
Related: Max-Severity GitLab Vulnerability Exploited Against Alpine Linux
