articles.title: Elon Musk's SpaceXSI offers to buy hundreds of homes near its data centers, as long as owners don't sue
articles.text:
Winners & losers: It appears that Elon Musk's recently renamed SpaceXSI has found a way to stop local residents joining a noise-pollution class-action suit against its data centers: buy up their homes on the condition they don't sue.
Real estate agents have been going door to door in the Colonial Hills neighborhood of Southaven, Mississippi, on behalf of the tech giant, offering to buy residents' homes if they don't join the ongoing lawsuit, writes The Guardian.
One realtor told a resident that the plan is to buy 418 homes, and that 18 homeowners have already agreed to sell. The realtor and local mayor say the homes will house SpaceXSI staff.
In January, the EPA closed a loophole that xAI had relied on by treating off-grid turbines like temporary "non-road engines." Federal regulators clarified that such turbines must meet the same Clean Air Act requirements as stationary power plants. But the Colossus 1 and 2 sites continue to use gas turbines without the required air-pollution permits. The EPA has said the permit requirements are a matter for the state to enforce.
SpaceXSI has since promised that it will remove all its unpermitted turbines in a year, but noise pollution is still angering residents.
"It sounds like an airplane engine but it's continuous, it's incredibly loud," Elizabeth Rose, a piano teacher who lives about two miles from the site, told The Guardian. "I've been woken up at 2am by it, I've been woken up at 3am by it. I sometimes have to just get away from it because it makes me so angry."
 – SemiAnalysis (@SemiAnalysis_) September 17, 2025
"There's a high-pitched hum and then another sound like an airplane over your house. It's been so torturous I can't sleep; I just leave the house or turn on some music until I fall asleep completely exhausted," said Jason Haley, one of the suit's three plaintiffs. "It drives you insane. You also lose hope because you're being ignored or dismissed. There's no escape."
The homes are being offered for purchase at market value – the average house price in the area is $180,000. Musk himself spends up to four nights a week in an Airstream trailer in the Memphis area as he personally oversees the construction.
A class-action lawsuit was filed against the company in June over claims of near-constant noise, vibrations and other nuisance-level harms from the facilities.
SpaceXSI denies the claims, arguing that has adjusted its power output and installed sound-dampening walls to reduce the impact on the neighborhood.
Southaven mayor Darren Musselwhite said city monitors have recorded no noise levels above the local limit of 70 decibels, though some experts warn that sustained noise at even 50 decibels can harm health.
Musselwhite added that the buyouts won't turn Colonial Hills into a company town. "The buyout has multiple purposes which are to provide homes for some employees and a goodwill gesture from a good corporate citizen for those who perceive the industrial development near them as a negative," he said.
This isn't the first time SpaceXSI has tried to appeal to residents. It tried offering 50% discounts on its Starlink satellite internet service to locals earlier this year, but only around 2,000 people out of 250,000 signed up.

articles.title: Thousands of “ghost students” use AI to steal millions in student loans, DOJ says
articles.text:
The US has charged five individuals as part of the first broad federal crackdown on “ghost students”—fraudsters who steal the identities of hundreds of Americans to pose as fake college students and steal student loans.
In a press release Thursday, the Department of Justice said it had uncovered a large-scale scheme relying partly on AI. The DOJ seized more than $750,000 in cryptocurrency from “a network associated with Kenyan nationals” after data analysis helped flag likely fraudsters. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the DOJ’s National Fraud Enforcement Division credited new fraud-detection measures implemented by the Trump administration for the arrests. He said that “this is the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya,” while warning fraudsters that the crackdown has only just begun.
“If you steal American identities, if you steal taxpayer dollars, if you exploit programs meant to help students build a future—we will find you,” McDonald said. “Whether you are in Nebraska, New Jersey, Virginia, or Nairobi, we will pursue you.”
At a press conference, McDonald was joined by FBI and Department of Education officials to explain how the scheme works.
It starts with bad actors purchasing personally identifiable information (PII) of Americans—most frequently targeting high school graduates who never attended college and went straight into the workforce.
Once they have that sensitive data, they fill out the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) while seeking to enroll in universities and community colleges. If accepted, student aid is distributed first to schools to cover tuition and fees, but any leftover money is deposited into bank accounts controlled by the fraudsters. Dozens of Americans have opened bank accounts to act as money mules for fraudsters, the DOJ said.
To keep money flowing, bad actors use AI to fill out applications, complete coursework, and even make it appear that a student is attending virtual sessions.
“It looks like the ghost student is actually completing the class,” McDonald said at the press conference. “Some even create the appearance of a fake student in an online classroom to trick schools into believing a real person is present. The goal is to keep the ghost student in school for as long as possible, semester after semester after semester.”
Oblivious Americans stuck with bills
So far, the DOE has “identified over 830,000 potentially fraudulent federal student aid accounts created by using this PII of US citizens,” officials said at the press conference. If all those accounts are ghost students, total losses come close to $130 million, the DOJ said.
For Americans whose data is stolen, there’s little opportunity to discover the scheme until the government comes collecting on loans years later. In the meantime, victims’ credit can be damaged. Once they detect the scheme, they’re stuck defending against demands to repay inflated student loans, which McDonald admitted is messy.
“The Department of Education does a great job to help unravel that mess, but it is a mess that no one should have to endure,” he said.
In connection with the arrests, officials said they “identified more than $32 million in actual loss tied to these specific subjects” and “we believe that actual total is substantially higher,” with “millions more suspected.”
The DOE’s Office of Inspector General first detected the fraud patterns that brought the alleged scheme to light. The FBI then helped identify how many accounts were impacted, tracing money to US and foreign bank accounts and crypto wallets. In one case, a defendant “used multiple bank accounts across several financial institutions to receive over 700 fraudulently obtained federal student aid refund deposits, totaling approximately $1,439,548,” the DOJ said. In another, “one person received more than $1 million in deposits that were linked to more than 300 fraudulent student accounts,” Inside Higher Ed reported.
At the press conference, First Assistant US Attorney Theophani K. Stamos for the Eastern District of Virginia said that data analysis “identified unusual, suspicious patterns of behavior” that the FBI said indicated “coordinated fraud was happening involving FAFSA.” Those patterns gave investigators “a solid basis and a solid lead to open further inquiries that have led to indictments,” Stamos said.
To keep the crackdown going, his office has sent “approximately 50 referrals to 26 FBI field offices across the country” to hunt down stolen taxpayer funds.
“We are just getting started. Working with partners around the world, we are sending a clear message: student aid belongs to real students, the data always leaves a trail, and we will follow it wherever it leads,” Stamos said.
Automated fraud detection isn’t perfect
The DOJ suspects this scam has been running since at least 2021, growing increasingly sophisticated as AI opens new avenues for loan theft.
“These fraudsters are exploiting Americans who have never been to college before, preventing the Department of Education from cross-checking applicants,” the DOJ said. “Many known victims have reported attaining only high school diplomas—and are shocked by their faked attendance at an institution hundreds of miles away.”
At the press conference, Undersecretary of Education Nicholas Kent accused the Biden administration of leaving Americans unprotected.
“When we walked in the door last January, we were extremely troubled to find that the Biden administration had turned off nearly every fraud detection measure,” Kent said.
Trump’s DOE said it introduced online identity verification requirements that Kent claimed would stop ghost students from ever receiving funds. Relying on automated systems to flag behaviors and reject fraudulent FAFSA applications, Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, vice chair of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, insisted that fraud could be easily stopped without allocating staff and resources or overly burdening the US government.
“The computers help us find it, and we keep the money in the agency,” Ferguson said.
The automated system isn’t perfect, however, and advocates have warned that false flags burden schools, meaning students’ access to aid could be delayed as administrators work through the added identity-verification processes.
Glitches have already affected fraud detection and student applications. In August, the DOE confirmed a technical issue from June 29 to July 6 prevented fraud evaluation results from being shared with certain FAFSA forms. After detecting the glitch, the DOE reprocessed those applications.
Real students may be flagged as fakes
Colleges and universities are also considering adding fees to stop the ghost student fraud.
Some advocates have acknowledged that the fraud deprives real students of funds. But they’re concerned that both the fees and online identity verification could become barriers to access to higher education for low-income students.
To verify their identities through the online FAFSA portal, students are expected to have government-issued IDs on hand in “real time.” They hold the IDs up to their cameras, and automated systems review them. A senior DOE official told Insider Higher Ed that the systems are “similar to the ones used by financial services companies like banks” and that he believed they are the same ones used by rental car companies.
Automated systems then assign a risk rating to the student, and anyone flagged as “high risk” is rejected. Once a student is rejected for aid, it’s up to the university to conduct any follow-up to verify if the application was real.
MorraLee Keller, a senior consultant for the National College Attainment Network, told Inside Higher Ed that “a lot of low-economic kids may not have secured, for example, a driver’s license” and may be set back in the application process while trying to obtain alternative IDs. That could also add fees during the application process.
Students may also be subject to automated fraud detection when seeking to make corrections to their FAFSA, which could delay fund distribution if a false rejection is issued.
“We want to make sure that timing doesn’t interrupt the aid getting credited to their account to pay their bills on time so that they could start classes, get refunds to go get their books, and all those kinds of things,” Keller said.
The Trump administration has said that it expects the number of real students flagged as fraudulent to be low. But the president of the National Association of Student Financial Aid Administrators, Melanie Storey, pushed back “a little bit” on that claim during a podcast from the association recently, asking “the department to quantify the volume of in-person verification that will remain,” Inside Higher Ed reported in April. At the time, Aaron Lemon-Strauss, executive director of the FAFSA program, replied, “I’m not going to be able to give you a number yet.”
Storey noted that many people complete the FAFSA form at in-person events, further narrowing potential false positives as the government expands its ghost student crackdown. For any students who “accidentally get caught in the net,” Lemon-Strauss recommended that universities remain vigilant and take action to ensure support goes to Americans who need it most.
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

articles.title: Vai chover no feriadão de Finados? Confira a previsão do tempo
articles.text:
Sol, calor e pancadas de chuva. Esta é a previsão do tempo para grande parte do Brasil entre este sábado (31) e segunda-feira (02), Dia de Finados.
Temporais devem atingir áreas do Sul, Sudeste e Centro-Oeste neste feriadão, segundo a Climatempo.
O deslocamento de áreas de baixa pressão e a presença de umidade na atmosfera favorecem a formação de nuvens carregadas. Isso pode provocar temporais país afora.
Sol, calor e pancadas de chuva: a previsão do tempo para o feriado de Finados
Confira abaixo os destaques da previsão do tempo para o feriado prolongado, organizados por região:
Sul
Períodos com sol devem ser maiores no Rio Grande do Sul. Pancadas de chuva estão previstas principalmente para áreas ao norte e leste do estado.
Paraná e Santa Catarina devem ter períodos com sol pela manhã e pancadas de chuva com raios à tarde e à noite no domingo (1º).
Na segunda-feira, as áreas de chuva podem começar a se formar pela manhã no centro-oeste do Paraná e de Santa Catarina. E devem se espalhar para outras áreas dos estados ao longo da tarde.
Sudeste
Há risco de fortes pancadas de chuva nos três dias do fim de semana prolongado em áreas de todos os estados do Sudeste.
A presença de uma área de baixa pressão atmosférica na costa do Sudeste deve facilitar a formação de nuvens carregadas por toda a região durante este sábado (31).
No domingo e na segunda-feira, após o afastamento desta área de baixa pressão, os períodos com sol serão maiores pela manhã em todo o Sudeste. Mas há previsão de pancadas de chuva com raios à tarde e à noite.
As praias do Sudeste devem ter períodos com sol principalmente no domingo e na segunda. No entanto, não há expectativa de calorão.
Centro-Oeste
Mato Grosso, Goiás e o Distrito Federal devem ter várias horas de sol forte durante o fim de semana prolongado.
No entanto, com o calor e o ar úmido que predomina sobre o Centro-Oeste, e condições especiais da circulação de ventos em níveis elevados da atmosfera, nuvens carregadas devem se formar.
Por isso, existe previsão de pancadas de chuva com raios em muitas áreas da região, principalmente durante a tarde e à noite.
A chuva não deve se prolongar por muitas horas, mas poderá cair com forte intensidade em vários locais, acompanhada por raios e eventualmente por rajadas de vento moderadas a fortes.
O risco de chuva pela manhã é maior no feriado de 2 de novembro, incluindo as capitais Brasília e Goiânia.
Nordeste
A previsão é de sol forte durante todo o fim de semana prolongado.
Algumas pancadas de chuva devem ocorrer no interior, em áreas do oeste e sudoeste da Bahia, Maranhão e Piauí. Nas demais áreas do Nordeste, a chance de chuva é pequena.
Norte
Amazonas, Acre e Rondônia devem passar o fim de semana prolongado com muitas nuvens, períodos com sol e pancadas de chuva, que poderão ocorrer a qualquer hora.
A possibilidade de chuva é baixa durante o fim de semana prolongado em Roraima, no Amapá e no extremo norte do Pará.
O Tocantins e outras áreas do Pará terão várias horas com sol forte durante o fim de semana prolongado e pancadas de chuva isoladas à tarde e à noite.
Pedro Spadoni é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de Piracicaba. Já escreveu para sites, revistas e jornal.

articles.title: Bloatware in Aftermarket Auto Parts - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
Bloatware in Aftermarket Auto Parts
This story is interesting:
One Civic owner purchased a cheap aftermarket head unit off Amazon, and decided to have Claude work its magic on it, like it would a smart TV. What was reportedly discovered isn’t surprising, but is worth knowing about.
Among the pre-installed bloatware—or spyware, if you’re being less charitable—was a voice assistant equipped with WebView, an Android system component that lets apps display content off the web. This apparently always used about a third of processing power, even while idle, which isn’t great. There were also Baidu location services, a call recorder (!), a DAB radio client that is pretty much useless in the U.S., and Adobe Acrobat, presumably so your passenger can entertain themselves with PDFs on the go.
It’s interesting because it exposes all the insecurities in this piece of IoT software. But I think the real story is that a random person was able to do this reverse-engineering with the help of AI. Expect a lot more stories like this in the future.
Rontea • October 30, 2026 1:06 PM
Cheap aftermarket devices—especially ones running Android variants—are the definition of untrusted hardware. They’re loaded with services and apps you didn’t ask for, phone home to places you don’t control, and often keep running even when you think they’re idle.
Stick to reputable vendors, keep them segmented, and if you must tinker, know exactly what firmware you’re flashing and where it came from. Trust is earned, not assumed.

articles.title: James Gunn quiere a Margot Robbie como Harley Quinn en el Universo DC
articles.text:
El Universo DC de James Gunn (o DCU) busca hacer borrón y cuenta nueva respecto de adaptaciones previas de sus personajes principales. Por supuesto que existen unas pocas excepciones, siendo la más notoria la del Peacemaker de John Cena. Y el propio cineasta ha reconocido que le encantaría que Margot Robbie se una a la saga como Harley Quinn.
Durante su participación en un pódcast, James Gunn confirmó que su idea es, eventualmente, introducir a Harley Quinn dentro del Universo DC que lidera. También reconoció que Margot Robbie es su opción número 1 para darle vida al personaje, considerando el trabajo que ya hizo con el personaje en tres películas previas.
Sin embargo, el jefe de DC Studios también reconoció que no está del todo convencido de cómo podría justificar un potencial regreso de la actriz australiana a este rol. Gunn mencionó que aún es difícil determinar si las películas de Escuadrón Suicida son canon o no en la actual franquicia que lidera.
A esto se suma otro detalle no menor: que James Gunn aún no introdujo al Joker en su Universo DC. La existencia del villano es fundamental para que Harley Quinn pueda tener su espacio, sea o no con Margot Robbie como intérprete.
"Creo que, en este contexto, Harley Quinn es uno de los elementos más difíciles de justificar como parte del canon del DCU. La relación de Harley con el Joker es muy particular, ¿verdad? Pues bien, todavía no hemos introducido al Joker en el DCU. A Batman sí lo hemos establecido; ya sabemos que existe. Lo hemos visto brevemente en Creature Commandos, pero no sabemos si el Joker existe ya. Y, obviamente, el Joker forma parte del pasado de Harley", explicó el cineasta.
¿Puede Margot Robbie sumarse al DCU como Harley Quinn?
Gunn ratificó que su plan es, tarde o temprano, incorporar a Harley Quinn a su Universo DC. También sostuvo que la primera opción para interpretarla estará en manos de Margot Robbie. El cineasta incluso mencionó que la decisión de considerar canon o no al Escuadrón Suicida va a depender de lo que haga la actriz.
"Margot Robbie es una de mis actrices favoritas con las que he trabajado. [...] Me encanta su interpretación de Harley. No sé si ella quiere volver a interpretar a Harley; puede que ya haya pasado página. Se ha convertido en una de las estrellas femeninas más grandes del mundo. Por eso, no sé qué piensa al respecto de todo esto", indicó el guionista y director, y agregó: "Harley es un personaje que, casi con total seguridad, voy a utilizar en el DCU. Si Margot quiere interpretarla, haré lo imposible por encajarla en ese universo. Pero si no es así, entonces podría optar por otra persona, sin necesidad de estar condicionado por lo que le ocurre a Harley en esta película. En resumen: es Margot quien debe decidir si Escuadrón Suicida forma parte del canon o no".
Será interesante ver si en el futuro Margot Robbie desea regresar al rol de Harley Quinn como parte del Universo DC de James Gunn y Peter Safran. Hasta aquí, la actriz dio vida al personaje en tres películas: Escuadrón Suicida (2016), de David Ayer, Aves de presa (2020) y El Escuadrón Suicida (2021), esta última de James Gunn.

articles.title: Here’s why you can’t shake those unhinged political texts
articles.text:
“Its James Talarico. Can you please please please please pretty pretty please rush in even just $1?”
Here’s why you can’t shake those unhinged political texts
You might be receiving political texts even if you’ve never made a political donation.
“Who’s working to elect James Talarico? Marxists.”
“Wow! Wow! Wow! Mark Kelly just made a HUGE announcement!”
“We asked Ben Verlander, MLB analyst and former Tigers prospect, to record a quick video about the election this Tuesday, November 3rd.”
“See which of your friends or family members have voted in the past and remind them to vote this year.”
If any of these messages sound familiar, it’s likely because they’re part of the massive stream of text messages flooding your phone leading up to the US midterm elections on Tuesday. The scale of the issue is not entirely clear, but call-blocking company Robokiller found that 15 billion political texts were sent in 2022, thanks in part to a Supreme Court decision the year prior that made it easier to send some mass calls and texts without consent. Alex Quilici, CEO of spam protection service YouMail, has an even higher estimate of 25 billion to 30 billion political texts this year, but caveats it’s an informal approximation. The volume is about the same to 10 percent higher than in 2024, he says.
There’s some good news and some bad news about these messages, says PIRG consumer watchdog director Teresa Murray. “The bad news is that political calls and political texts are exempt from the do-not-call-list rules,” Murray says. “The good news is that the election is next Tuesday, and hopefully within a few days after that, we’ll know what the results are and there won’t be any need to have any texts, or calls, or emails anymore after that.”
There are still some things consumers can try to stem the flow of these messages blowing up their phones — but it likely won’t significantly reduce it before Tuesday.
“In between all of the ‘legitimate’ political texts … there are going to be some scams in there”
The simplest thing you can do is send “stop” or block and report the messages as spam, which will notify your service provider of a likely spam number. That probably won’t result in any immediate change, Murray says, but if enough people report the same number in a certain period of time, the provider might begin to block it or label it as spam. You can also file a complaint with the Federal Communications Commission or your state attorney general if you believe a number is using an autodialer without your consent — something that even the people behind political texts are not supposed to do. Whatever you do, Murray says, do not click any links you receive from numbers you don’t know.
“In between all of the ‘legitimate’ political texts that are going out to support this candidate, or vote against that candidate, or vote for this issue, or whatever, there are going to be some scams in there,” Murray says. “If you want to donate money at this point, I would recommend going directly to the website for that political candidate, or for that PAC, and donating it that way.”
How did all of these campaigns get your number in the first place? If you’ve donated to a political candidate or issue group, that might seem obvious. But campaigns are also likely getting your information — including details about whether you might be likely to contribute to or vote for their candidate or issue — through data brokers that have nothing to do with politics. Data brokers collect and sell information from both public and private sources, such as public voter rolls, your online behavior observed by advertising web trackers, and loyalty programs. By collating all of this information, campaigns can try to infer your behavior, though they also might end up with outdated info, like old addresses that lead you to getting texts about a state you no longer live in (or even erroneous info that invites them for states you never lived in).
“As a consumer protection advocate, it’s so frustrating to have to say, ‘What can each individual person do?’”
“Errors in the processing of this information and the identification of individuals are very prevalent,” says Sara Geoghegan, consumer privacy program director of the Electronic Privacy Information Center. “Sometimes multiple people use the same device. Sometimes people have similar names. Sometimes people move. And this is such an unregulated ecosystem that there aren’t really rules in place to make sure that this is being effective and accurate, let alone free from bias, discrimination, and verified for privacy impact before processing this information.
“As a consumer protection advocate, it’s so frustrating to have to say, ‘What can each individual person do, and how many numbers do they need to block, and what are the toggle and privacy settings that they should toggle on?’” Geoghegan says. Meanwhile, “the companies that are trading in our most sensitive information are the ones who should stop harmful surveillance and the use of harmful technologies to have us better engage civically with our society, and not the other way around,” she says.
“I’ve spoken to people, someone last week who said, ‘Why would I even donate again when I get put on all these lists?’”
Geoghegan worries that the harm of being bombarded with unwanted political texts isn’t just that people get annoyed, but that they stop engaging civically as a result. “Having this surveillance apparatus that invades people’s privacy and really annoys them actually pushes people away from this,” she says. “I’ve spoken to people, someone last week who said, ‘Why would I even donate again when I get put on all these lists?’”
Unfortunately, you might get on some political text lists whether you engage in the civic process or not because of data brokers. Murray says the best long-term solution to minimize these spam messages is to limit how frequently you give out your phone number in general, like in an online shopping portal. If you need to give a number, you might consider using a VoIP number like a free Google Voice number, so at least you can silo those messages into another app you don’t need to frequently check or get notifications from.
Murray says she rarely gives out her personal number and limits where she gives out her Google Voice number, too. But even she has seen an uptick in political texts over the past couple of weeks. That’s likely in part because some groups may try to dial numbers in order in a certain area code, or her number could still be floating around on lists from long ago. “You can’t really do anything about the people or the businesses or the political entities that you have already shared your number with in the past,” Murray says. “But I would encourage people to just draw a line in the sand.”
Murray and Geoghegan encourage consumers to take the actions available to them to help limit the unwanted texts they receive, but they say the real solutions to the broader issue will likely come from Congress or regulators. Geoghegan says greater enforcement of existing laws could limit robocalls and texts, and Murray says concerned voters could contact their representatives about putting more pressure on the FCC to address the problems.
“Don’t get just frustrated with what you can’t change in four days, but you may be able to make a difference for the future,” Murray says. “By all means, reply to a text and say, ‘Stop.’ … But just don’t make it your life’s quest because it’s probably a fool’s errand.”

articles.title: Desk Phones vs Apps: Choosing a Business Phone System When Everyone Already Has a Mobile - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Evolution of Business Communication
In today’s digitally connected world, business communication has undergone a profound transformation. The proliferation of smartphones and high-speed internet means nearly every employee carries a mobile device capable of voice, video, and messaging. Yet, despite this ubiquity, many organizations continue to rely on traditional desk phones or explore app-based communication platforms to meet their needs. Choosing between desk phones and mobile app-based systems is complex, especially when balancing cost, reliability, security, and user experience.
Understanding these options is crucial for companies aiming to optimize communication efficiency and employee productivity. This article explores the advantages and challenges of desk phones and app-based systems, offering insights to help businesses select the most effective phone system in an era where mobile devices are already in everyone’s hands.
Understanding the Role of Desk Phones in Modern Offices
Desk phones have been the backbone of business communication for decades. Their dedicated hardware and infrastructure provide a reliable, consistent calling experience valued by many professionals. These devices are designed for high call volumes in environments like call centers, customer service departments, and executive offices where call clarity and uninterrupted connectivity are paramount.
A key advantage of desk phones is their ability to maintain high-quality voice transmission without relying heavily on fluctuating internet connections. This reliability translates into fewer dropped calls and less interference, critical for customer-facing roles. Additionally, desk phones project a professional presence with features like customizable caller ID and dedicated buttons for frequent contacts or emergency numbers.
However, desk phones come with challenges. Physical installation requires wired connections, which can be costly and time-consuming to set up and maintain. Scaling the system as the company grows may involve significant expenses. To address these issues, many businesses partner with a managed IT provider in New Hampshire, which streamlines installation, maintenance, and integration with existing IT infrastructure. These providers handle hardware procurement, software updates, and network management, ensuring minimal downtime and optimal performance.
Despite the rise of mobile communication, desk phones remain a staple in many organizations due to their reliability, ease of use for frequent callers, and the familiarity they offer employees accustomed to traditional telephony.
The Rise of App-Based Phone Systems
The rapid advancement of mobile technology and cloud computing has paved the way for app-based phone systems, also known as Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) or Unified Communications (UC) platforms. These systems enable voice and video calls, instant messaging, and collaboration through file sharing-all within a single app accessible on smartphones, tablets, and desktops.
App-based systems offer unparalleled flexibility. Employees can communicate seamlessly whether in the office, working remotely, or on the go. This adaptability is especially valuable in today’s hybrid work models, where staying connected from any location is a critical business requirement.
According to a recent survey, 85% of businesses have adopted some form of mobile or app-based communication tools to support remote workforces. This shift reflects the growing recognition that app-based platforms enhance employee mobility and foster real-time collaboration beyond voice calls.
Moreover, app-based systems often come with rich features such as video conferencing, screen sharing, call recording, and integration with business applications like Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software. These capabilities can significantly boost team productivity and streamline workflows.
Nevertheless, app-based phone systems depend heavily on internet connectivity quality. Network congestion, low bandwidth, or unstable Wi-Fi can lead to poor call quality or dropped connections. To mitigate these challenges, companies can leverage resources such as NetAccess’ on-demand tech support, which provide rapid technical assistance, network optimization, and troubleshooting services. These support structures are vital for maintaining smooth communication and minimizing disruptions in mission-critical operations.
Key Considerations When Choosing Between Desk Phones and Apps
Cost Efficiency
Cost is often a primary consideration when evaluating phone systems. Desk phones require upfront investment in hardware, wiring, and installation. Ongoing maintenance and upgrades add to the total cost of ownership. Conversely, app-based systems usually operate on subscription models, offering lower initial costs but recurring monthly fees depending on users or features.
Businesses must conduct a thorough cost-benefit analysis, factoring in direct expenses and indirect costs such as employee training, system downtime, and scalability. For small to medium-sized enterprises, app-based systems may offer a more budget-friendly and flexible solution, while larger organizations with stable office environments might find desk phones more cost-effective over time.
User Experience and Productivity
User experience is pivotal for communication effectiveness. Desk phones provide a tactile interface with physical buttons, which many employees find intuitive, especially for frequent or complex calls. Features like dedicated hold buttons, speakerphones, and headset compatibility contribute to efficient call management.
App-based platforms unify multiple communication channels-voice, video, messaging-into a single interface. This integration can enhance productivity by reducing tool switching and enabling quicker decision-making through instant collaboration.
A study by McKinsey found that companies using integrated communication apps experienced a 32% improvement in team collaboration. This often translates into faster project turnaround times and better customer service.
Security and Compliance
Security is paramount, especially for industries handling sensitive or regulated information like healthcare, finance, and legal services. Desk phones can operate on isolated, private networks, limiting exposure to cyber threats. Physical control over hardware and connections simplifies compliance with regulations such as HIPAA or GDPR.
In contrast, app-based systems transmit data over the internet and rely on encryption protocols to safeguard communications. While many platforms offer robust security features, including end-to-end encryption and multi-factor authentication, cyber risks remain a consideration.
Engaging a managed IT provider ensures the chosen phone system incorporates tailored security measures and complies with industry-specific regulations. This partnership can include regular security audits, employee training, and rapid incident response.
Scalability
Scalability is essential for businesses anticipating growth or fluctuating workforce sizes. App-based phone systems excel here, allowing companies to add or remove users easily without physical hardware changes. This flexibility supports dynamic teams and seasonal staffing variations.
Desk phone systems may require purchasing additional hardware, rewiring, or upgrading network infrastructure to accommodate expansion. While this provides predictable control over communication, it can result in higher capital expenditures and longer deployment timelines.
Integrating Mobile Devices Into the Business Phone System
Since employees already rely heavily on mobile devices, integrating these tools into the broader business communication strategy is vital. Many modern phone systems support “bring your own device” (BYOD) policies, enabling secure access to company communication apps on personal smartphones while maintaining separation between personal and corporate data.
This integration facilitates seamless communication across devices and locations, empowering employees to switch between desk phones, mobile apps, and computers without losing call continuity or collaboration features.
Hybrid communication models combining desk phones, app-based platforms, and mobile integration offer the best of all worlds. They accommodate diverse working styles, from office-centric roles needing desk phones to remote employees relying exclusively on mobile apps. Such flexibility promotes inclusivity and ensures all team members remain connected regardless of location.
Future Trends in Business Phone Systems
The communication landscape continues to evolve rapidly, influenced by emerging technologies and changing workplace dynamics. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning are beginning to play roles in phone systems, offering features like automated call routing, voice transcription, sentiment analysis, and virtual assistants.
Cloud-based communication platforms are expected to dominate, driven by scalability, cost-effectiveness, and integration capabilities. The global cloud telephony market is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 15.9% from 2021 to 2028.
Moreover, the rise of 5G networks promises to improve mobile connectivity quality, potentially narrowing the gap between desk phones and app-based systems in terms of call reliability and latency.
Businesses should stay informed about these trends and adapt their communication infrastructure to leverage new capabilities that enhance operational efficiency and employee satisfaction.
Making the Right Choice for Your Business
Choosing between desk phones and app-based systems is not one-size-fits-all. It depends on factors including company size, industry requirements, workforce distribution, budget, and security needs.
Engaging technology partners, managed service providers, and communication consultants can provide valuable insights. These experts assess unique organizational needs, evaluate existing infrastructure, and recommend solutions aligned with strategic goals.
While mobile devices offer unprecedented flexibility, desk phones still hold value by providing reliability, professionalism, and dedicated hardware functionality. Meanwhile, app-based systems bring flexibility, integration, and scalability suited to modern, mobile-first workforces. A thoughtful balance of these options, supported by expert guidance and tailored to operational realities, ensures effective communication channels that drive growth and productivity.

Au lieu de 1 089 euros, le pack Xiaomi 17T pro est actuellement affiché à 749 euros au lieu de 1 089 euros sur le site de Boulanger.

Le Dreame Tasti reprend l’idée de l’air fryer modulaire en verre proposé par le Ninja Crispi, avec un écran tactile en façade en plus, et pour moins cher pendant le Black Friday.
Ce qu’il faut retenir du Dreame Tasti
- Un écran tactile en façade pour suivre la cuisson
- Une plage de 60 à 200 °C et cinq programmes
- Deux récipients en verre borosilicate de 2,5 et 4,5 litres
Vendu habituellement 119 euros, le Dreame Tasti s’affiche en promotion à 94 euros chez Boulanger en pack avec 2 récipients.
Nintendo Switch
Sortie en mars 2017, la Switch originale est en passe de devenir la console la plus vendue au monde. Pour Nintendo, ce pack à moins de 200 euros avec Mario Kart 8 Deluxe est une bonne façon d’écouler les derniers stocks.
Pourquoi choisir ce pack Switch ?
- Un format hybride avec tablette, dock TV et Joy-Con détachables
- Le jeu Mario Kart 8 Deluxe inclus
- Une fabrication robuste malgré le Joy Con Drift
La Nintendo Switch avec Mario Kart 8 Deluxe est aujourd’hui proposée à 199,99 euros au lieu de 299,99 euros chez Boulanger.
Google Pixel Watch 4
La Google Pixel Watch 4 a apporté une nette évolution par rapport à la Google Pixel Watch 3 à bien des égards, notamment au niveau de l’écran et de la puce qui l’anime. Avec aussi un cheval de bataille en matière d’intelligence artificielle puisqu’on passe de l’assistant Google à Gemini, avec notamment la fonction « lever pour parler » qui permet de ne pas avoir à donner de mot déclencheur.
Les points forts de la Pixel Watch 4
- Pour son écran Actua 360 lumineux et 10 % plus grand
- Pour ses finitions impeccables avec son boîtier en alu recyclé
- Pour la fiabilité de son capteur de suivi cardiaque
Au lieu de 449 euros, la Google Pixel Watch 4 version 45 mm est actuellement en promotion à seulement 249 euros chez Boulanger.
Acer Swift Air 14″
L’Acer Swift Air 14 est un ultraportable de 14 pouces qui s’adresse avant tout aux utilisateurs en quête de mobilité sans se ruiner. Léger et pratique à transporter, il propose une fiche technique suffisante pour la bureautique et la navigation, mais qui peut montrer ses limites en multitâche intensif. Noté 7/10 dans notre test, c’est une option solide à considérer, surtout à ce prix.
Les points forts de l’Acer Swift Air 14″
- Châssis aluminium léger à 1,19 kg
- Une configuration solide sous Intel Core 5
- Ne chauffe pas, reste silencieux
L’Acer Swift Air 14 passe de 899 euros à 599 euros chez Boulanger, soit 300 euros de remise immédiate.
Samsung Galaxy Book 6
Si vous cherchez un ordinateur portable pour le travail ou les cours, le Samsung Galaxy Book 6 mérite votre attention. Ce 14 pouces sous Windows mise sur l’endurance : sa batterie de 61,2 Wh revendique jusqu’à 25 heures d’autonomie, ce qui le place parmi les mieux armés de sa catégorie. Les fonctions Galaxy AI sont embarquées pour ceux qui gravitent dans l’écosystème Samsung et à ce prix-là, c’est une machine qui vaut le coup.
Le Samsung Galaxy Book 6 en résumé
- Autonomie annoncée jusqu’à 25 heures
- Dalle IPS 14″ 1920 x 1200 anti-reflets
- Fonctions Galaxy AI intégrées
De base à 899 euros, le Samsung Galaxy Book 6 tombe à 599 euros chez Boulanger, soit 300 euros d’économie.
Asus ROG XG27AQWMG
L’Asus ROG XG27AQWMG cible les joueurs qui veulent franchir le cap de l’OLED sans débourser le prix d‘un écran de compétition haut de gamme. Ce moniteur de 27 pouces en QHD (2560 x 1440), avec un taux de rafraîchissement de 280 Hz et un temps de réponse de 0,03 ms ne dépasse pas les 500 euros grâce à cette offre.
Les avantages de l’Asus ROG XG27AQWMG
- Écran OLED en QHD
- 280 Hz et 0,03 ms
- Deux ports HDMI 2.1 et G-Sync compatible
L’Asus ROG XG27AQWMG passe de 599 euros à 469 euros chez Boulanger, soit 130 euros de remise.
Sony Bravia Theatre Quad
Le Sony Bravia Theatre Quad est un système d’exception qui embarque quatre enceintes compactes et sans fil, idéales pour transformer votre salon sans défigurer votre déco. Grâce à la technologie 360 Spatial Sound Mapping, il crée jusqu’à 12 enceintes virtuelles pour une immersion totale en Dolby Atmos et DTS:X. Certifié Hi-Res et IMAX Enhanced, il s’intègre parfaitement à votre installation (HDMI eARC, AirPlay 2, VRR/ALLM pour le jeu vidéo). Une solution haut de gamme clé en main, parfaite si vous cherchez le rendu d’une vraie salle de cinéma sans la contrainte des câbles.
La Sony Bravia Theatre Quad, c’est quoi ?
- Quatre enceintes sans fil, placement libre
- 360 Spatial Sound Mapping, Dolby Atmos, DTS:X
- Calibrage automatique via BRAVIA Connect
La Sony Bravia Theatre Quad coûte initialement 1 999 euros, mais en ce moment elle revient à 1 490 euros chez Boulanger, soit 509 euros de remise.
JBL Partybox Club 120
La JBL Partybox Club 120 est une enceinte festive parfaite pour animer une fête dans le jardin ou le salon. Notée 9/10 dans notre test, elle se distingue nettement des enceintes de sono classiques par son équilibre général. Trois zones d’éclairage dynamiques rythment la musique, et la connectique est complète – entrées ligne, micro et guitare au programme. Avec 37 % de moins, elle devient plus recommandable.
Ce qu’on apprécie de la JBL Partybox Club 120

Le JBL Quantum 950 plaît pour…

- Ses deux batteries amovibles, 25 h d’autonomie chacune
Habituellement proposé à 299 euros, le JBL Quantum 950 passe à 199 euros chez Boulanger dans le cadre du Black Friday.

TCL cherche avec le X11L à s’imposer sur le segment très haut de gamme des téléviseurs, et la fiche technique est à la hauteur de l’ambition. Ce 75 pouces mise sur la technologie SQD-Mini LED. articles.title: Ma maison est à la fois connectée et idiote : voilà pourquoi c'est le meilleur des deux mondes
articles.text:
Il existe un test très simple pour savoir si votre maison connectée est réussie. Invitez quelqu’un à dîner et regardez-le aller aux toilettes. S’il allume la lumière du premier coup, sans même y penser, bravo. S’il appuie deux fois sur l’interrupteur, puis revient vers vous en haussant les sourcils, vous avez une maison connectée mal conçue : un bouton ne fait pas ce que l’utilisateur attend. Je suis bien placé pour en parler : j’en ai eu une pendant des années.
Les plus anciens d’entre vous connaissent mon cheminement, j’en avais déjà parlé dans cette newsletter. Pour les autres, un petit rappel des faits. Quand Philips a lancé ses ampoules Hue, fin octobre 2012, elles n’étaient vendues que dans les Apple Store : 199 euros le kit de départ, pour trois ampoules et un petit pont à brancher sur la box. J’étais, je crois, quelques années après (je penche sur 2014 si ma mémoire ne me fait pas défaut), l’un des premiers en France à en avoir partout chez moi. Ont suivi un Google Home, puis un HomePod que j’avais fait importer des États-Unis pour l’avoir avant tout le monde, puis des volets roulants connectés, un Google Nest Hub, une Apple TV, des prises connectées… Je disais « Dis Siri, bonne nuit » et l’appartement s’éteignait et se fermait tout seul. J’adorais ça. Honnêtement, j’adore toujours l’idée.
Le problème, c’est que cette maison avait été conçue pour un seul utilisateur, qui en connaissait toutes les règles parce qu’il les avait écrites (moi). Et puis j’ai eu une vie sociale un peu plus riche, et surtout, j’ai, plus tard, partagé mon appartement avec ma femme.
Appuyez deux fois
Pour comprendre ce qui a coincé, il faut regarder où se trouve l’intelligence dans une installation à base d’ampoules connectées. Elle est dans l’ampoule. Le reste de votre installation électrique n’est au courant de rien (pardon pour la vanne). L’interrupteur mural continue de faire ce qu’il fait depuis un siècle : couper ou laisser passer le courant. Vous avez donc deux autorités qui commandent la même lumière sans jamais se parler.
Si j’éteins depuis l’application, l’interrupteur reste en position allumée, et pour rallumer il faut l’éteindre puis le rallumer. Si quelqu’un coupe au mur, l’ampoule n’est plus alimentée et ne répond plus ni à l’application ni aux automatisations que j’avais minutieusement réglées. Le va-et-vient du couloir est devenu une loterie à deux joueurs dont un seul connaissait les règles.
Pour ma femme, qui n’avait rien demandé, la situation était ubuesque. Elle vivait dans un appartement où la chose la plus simple du monde, allumer la lumière, demandait de deviner l’état d’un système invisible sur lequel elle n’avait aucune prise – même en lui partageant l’accès à la Maison dans Apple Home, cela ne réglait qu’un problème, le sien, et pas celui de nos invités.
Bref, chaque bug devenait mon bug, que je devais réparer en ayant l’air d’un type qui défend son jouet. Je l’ai compris plus tard : une technologie qui oblige les autres à changer leurs gestes pour me faire plaisir est une technologie impolie.
Alors, quand nous avons déménagé, j’ai tranché. Plus de lumière connectée, ou le strict minimum : quelques petites lumières sous le lit pour faire un halo, des choses sans conséquence qui ne touchent pas au comportement des vrais boutons. Le mur reprenait le pouvoir. J’étais assez fier de cette sagesse retrouvée.
Le cerveau dans le mur
Avec un peu de recul, je me suis rendu compte que j’avais simplement changé d’extrême. J’étais passé du tout connecté au rien connecté avec la même absence de nuance, celle du converti qui brûle ce qu’il a adoré. C’est Nicolas Lellouche, qui suit ces sujets à Numerama, qui m’a sorti de ma posture, avec un conseil qui tient en une phrase : « arrête de mettre l’intelligence dans l’ampoule, mets-la dans le mur ».
Mi-octobre, j’ai installé un Shelly 2L Gen4 derrière un interrupteur (ouais je me suis planté de modèle, je n’ai besoin que d’un 1L), dans la boîte d’encastrement. C’est un petit module à deux canaux, qui peut donc piloter deux circuits de lumière séparément. L’ampoule redevient une ampoule bête, le bouton reste un bouton, et le module, glissé entre les deux, fait le lien avec l’app Maison d’Apple via Matter. Le bouton ne coupe plus le courant de la lumière : il envoie un ordre au module, exactement comme l’application ou Siri. Il n’y a plus qu’une seule autorité, et elle écoute tout le monde.
J’ai testé ça dans la pièce la plus démocratique de l’appartement, celle où passent absolument tous les invités : les toilettes. J’y ai ajouté un détecteur de mouvement Aqara P1, gros comme une balle de ping-pong coupée en deux. Quand quelqu’un entre, la lumière s’allume seule, puis s’éteint dix minutes après le départ du dernier occupant. Si vous sortez en oubliant la lumière, elle s’éteint quand même. Si vous l’éteignez au bouton, elle s’éteint, et l’automatisation repart normalement au passage suivant. Si vous appuyez sur l’interrupteur avant que le capteur vous ait repéré, la lumière s’allume et rien ne se contredit. Si je change quelque chose depuis l’application, ça marche aussi. J’ai cherché le cas qui casse. Je ne l’ai pas trouvé.
C’est la découverte qui m’enthousiasme le plus depuis longtemps dans ce domaine : une maison peut être connectée pour moi et parfaitement normale pour tous les autres. Vos invités appuient sur un bouton, la lumière s’allume. Ils ne sauront jamais qu’un module infrarouge les a aussi vus entrer.
Matter, ou presque
Évidemment, il y a un prix d’entrée, et il est double.
Le premier est physique. Tout se joue au niveau des fils : derrière les interrupteurs, ou directement dans le tableau électrique, où l’on peut installer des modules sur rail à côté des disjoncteurs. Cela veut dire couper le courant, ouvrir des boîtes et parfois appeler un électricien. Bref, faire des travaux. Ce n’est pas plug and play.
Souvent, il faut aussi regarder si un fil neutre arrive jusqu’à l’interrupteur, ce qui est loin d’être garanti dans les logements anciens. C’est justement l’intérêt du 2L : il s’en passe, moyennant un petit composant fourni dans la boîte, le bypass, à brancher en parallèle de la lampe. On ne fait pas ça un dimanche après-midi en dévissant une ampoule, mais on ne refait pas non plus l’électricité de l’appartement. Et puis on va pas se mentir, avec l’IA, tout est devenu plus simple : une photo, une description du projet et Gemini vous fait les étapes.
Le second est logiciel, et là, on ne va pas se mentir, c’est encore le Far West. L’application Shelly est un bordel sans nom. Quant à Matter, la norme lancée fin 2022 avec la promesse que tous les objets parleraient enfin la même langue, elle n’a tenu son engagement qu’à moitié. Mon capteur Aqara en est un parfait exemple. Je l’ai ajouté directement à l’app Maison, en Matter, avec le HomePod comme contrôleur : il fonctionne très bien. Mais pour régler sa sensibilité ou son délai de détection, l’application Aqara réclame un hub Aqara. Sans lui, je suis coincé sur le réglage d’usine. La norme universelle, en 2026, consiste donc à acheter une deuxième box pour régler un curseur sur un objet qui marche déjà. Yay! Interoperability!
Alors pourquoi je vous en parle avec enthousiasme ? Parce que ces frictions sont désormais celles de l’installateur, une fois, et plus celles des habitants. Pendant des années, la maison connectée m’a fait payer sa complexité chaque fois que quelqu’un touchait un interrupteur. Aujourd’hui, je la paie un samedi, un tournevis à la main et un tutoriel sur les genoux. Ensuite, plus personne ne la remarque.
J’ai longtemps cru que le défaut de ma maison connectée était d’être trop connectée. Son vrai défaut, c’est qu’elle n’obéissait qu’à moi. Une maison bien faite obéit au bouton, parce que le bouton est la seule interface que tout le monde sait utiliser, de l’ami de passage à la belle-mère.
Si vous hésitez à franchir le pas, ou à revenir en arrière comme moi, commencez par une seule pièce et une question bête : comment j’automatise sans que personne ne s’en aperçoive ? La réponse décide du module à acheter, et tout le reste en découle. Et la prochaine fois que vous recevez, regardez vos invités utiliser la salle de bain sans vous poser de question. Vous n’aurez même pas à leur faire un tunnel pour leur expliquer Matter.

articles.title: Polymarket piraté : un simple chargement de page a suffi pour vider des centaines de portefeuilles
articles.text:
Une simple visite sur la plateforme de paris prédictifs aurait suffi à exposer l’argent de certains utilisateurs. Polymarket annonce avoir résolu l’incident et promet de rembourser les victimes.
Les utilisateurs de Polymarket n’avaient apparemment pas besoin de cliquer sur un lien douteux pour se faire voler leur argent. Le danger venait d’un script chargé par le site lui-même. Selon l’analyse des chercheurs de Hudson Rock, ce code malveillant cherchait à exploiter une session déjà ouverte pour vendre les positions de l’utilisateur ou transférer ses actifs vers un portefeuille contrôlé par les pirates. Des victimes rapportent des opérations effectuées sans leur accord, mais les conditions exactes dans lesquelles les transactions ont pu être validées restent à préciser.
Un prestataire compromis, la plateforme mise en pause
Pour interrompre les opérations pendant son enquête, Polymarket a basculé sa plateforme internationale en mode « annulation uniquement ». Les utilisateurs pouvaient encore supprimer leurs ordres alors que les opérations des relayers étaient suspendues (services techniques qui transmettent certaines transactions des utilisateurs à la blockchain, cf. FAQ en fin d'article). Une trentaine de minutes plus tard, l’entreprise annonçait avoir corrigé le problème et attribuait l’incident à la compromission d’un prestataire tiers. Les échanges ont repris environ une heure après leur suspension.
D'après CNBC, il s’agirait de DebugBear, une société britannique spécialisée dans la mesure des performances des sites web. Au moment des faits, celle-ci a reconnu un incident de sécurité sur X et demandé aux clients de son outil RUM de retirer le code intégré à leurs pages. Elle n’a pas apporté davantage de précisions. Polymarket indique pour sa part avoir alerté les autorités britanniques.
Une indemnisation promise, mais sous conditions pour les plus grosses pertes
La plateforme n’a pas explicitement confirmé le montant des pertes, mais s’est engagée à indemniser intégralement les personnes lésées. Selon la société d’analyse Bubblemaps, plus de 700 utilisateurs auraient été touchés, pour un total de 2,7 millions de dollars dérobés.
Les modalités de remboursement ont été précisées sur Discord. Pour les victimes ayant perdu moins de 10 000 dollars, Polymarket annonçait un versement au plus tard le 30 octobre. Au-delà de ce seuil, les utilisateurs devront d’abord signer une décharge juridique. La promesse d’un remboursement intégral s’accompagne donc d’une formalité supplémentaire pour ceux qui ont subi les pertes les plus lourdes.
Cet incident ajoute aux difficultés d’une plateforme déjà mise en cause dans l’État de New York pour son activité de jeux d’argent. En France, son site est bloqué par les principaux fournisseurs d’accès à la demande de l’Autorité nationale des jeux, qui considère son offre comme illégale.
Sources : Polymarket, Hudson Rock et CNBC
Une attaque supply chain côté Web survient quand un service externe intégré à une page (analytics, performance, chat, etc.) est compromis et sert du code malveillant à la place du code légitime. Comme ce script s’exécute dans le navigateur avec les mêmes droits que le site, il peut lire des données de session, interagir avec la page et déclencher des actions à la place de l’utilisateur. Ce n’est pas une faille locale sur l’ordinateur : l’attaque se produit dans la chaîne de dépendances du site. Dans le cas d’un service financier ou crypto, cela peut suffire à initier des ordres, modifier des adresses de destination ou pousser l’utilisateur à valider une transaction sans s’en rendre compte. La gravité dépend ensuite de ce qui protège l’action (revalidation, confirmation wallet, 2FA, etc.).
Le mode « annulation uniquement » consiste à bloquer la création et l’exécution de nouveaux ordres tout en laissant la possibilité d’annuler ceux qui existent déjà. C’est une mesure de confinement : elle limite la surface d’attaque et évite d’amplifier des opérations potentiellement frauduleuses pendant l’enquête. Techniquement, cela revient à désactiver les fonctions d’exécution/matching et à n’autoriser que les actions de retrait/cancellation. Ce mode est fréquent sur les plateformes d’échange ou de trading quand l’intégrité des transactions ou des sessions n’est plus garantie. Il permet aussi de stabiliser l’état du système avant de remettre les services en ligne.
Un relayer est un service qui transmet des transactions ou des messages signés par l’utilisateur vers la blockchain, souvent pour simplifier l’usage (moins de frais directs, exécution plus rapide, abstraction technique). Dans certains systèmes, l’utilisateur signe une intention (ordre, autorisation) et le relayer se charge de la publier on-chain au bon moment. Suspendre les relayers, c’est interrompre ce canal de diffusion : les ordres ne partent plus vers la blockchain via cette infrastructure, ce qui peut stopper une partie des opérations. Cela ne gèle pas la blockchain elle-même, mais coupe un maillon opérationnel utilisé par la plateforme. En situation de crise, c’est une façon de limiter l’exécution de transactions tant que l’origine des requêtes n’est pas jugée fiable.

articles.title: Waiting for an AI law is a poor compliance strategy
articles.text:
Waiting for an AI law is a poor compliance strategy
India's courts and sectoral regulators have already begun assigning liability for AI failures. Businesses that are holding out for a statute are preparing for the wrong deadline.
A bank has an AI system in place to flag suspicious transactions and take the call to freeze accounts. While the workflow has a human sign-off in place, clearing around 400 cases a day has resulted in the approval system becoming a formality. So, when a wrongly-frozen account takes the system to court, the bank becomes unable to prove what the human actually reviewed. This, unfortunately, is no longer a hypothetical scenario.
On July 2, 2026, the Supreme Court of India quashed orders passed by the National Company Law Tribunal and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal in the Pooja Ramesh Singh v. Jammu and Kashmir Bank Ltd. case. The orders had rested on citations generated by an AI tool and attributed to the Supreme Court itself. This directed the Bar Council of India to constitute a committee to prescribe disciplinary norms for advocates who file AI-generated citations.
This is a business story as much as a legal one. Despite two tribunals and several rounds of proceedings, the parties had to carry the cost of a machine error that no human caught before filing. No AI statute was required to reach that outcome. Ordinary law, applied by judges, did the work.
The regulators are moving faster than the legislature
For most Indian companies, the sharper edge is coming from sectoral regulators rather than from the bench.
In early June this year, the Reserve Bank of India gave banks and other regulated entities until June 30 to submit gap assessments on frontier-AI cyber risk. Instead of having the CISO to file the note, the RBI had asked the board to sign one.
Later, on June 24, the RBI publicly released a draft 'Guidance on Regulatory Principles for Model Risk Management' to establish a comprehensive enterprise-wide model governance framework for the financial sector. Here 'models' extend to third-party models, AI, and machine learning (ML) systems used by commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, NBFCs, and other financial institutions. So if a lending decision is influenced by a model licensed from a vendor, the model risk sits on the one putting the AI system to use and not the vendor who built it.
Meanwhile, India's legislative position is still a work-in-progress. On October 8, 2026, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had assured that the time has come for India to get an AI law. In a first step towards this, the government will be launching a consultation paper on regulating artificial intelligence.
However, any business that is treating a pending law as its compliance milestone has their sequencing backwards. Even when the statute arrives, it can only land on top of existing case laws and sectoral circulars, not in place of them. Regardless of what law comes into place, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act takes full effect on May 13, 2027. Businesses will be held accountable even if the data is being processed by an external vendor as the DPDPA will be applicable wherever an AI system handles personal data.
What does this ask of a business?
Behind all the legal vocabulary, the requirements across all the domains are the same—one needs to show their working.
For any consequential decision made by an AI system, organisations must be able to have the visibility regarding which model produced the output, what data it drew on, whether a retrieval step was involved, who reviewed it before it went out, and whether that record still exists six months later.
Multiple Indian firms have written a policy, appointed a committee, and deployed systems but can still not answer any of the above questions. This is clearly an architecture question before it is a policy-related one. Recording the model version, prompt, retrieved data and human sign-off for every AI decision is only cheap if it is thoughtfully designed for. It can, however, become close to impossible to reconstruct afterwards.
It is important for businesses to question an AI vendor before procuring a model. Does the system record which model version handled each request? Can that record be exported and retained? Where does inference physically happen? What happens to inputs after processing? Where in the workflow is a human required to act? Vendors that cannot answer plainly are transferring risk to the buyer.
Build the record now
There is not much point in waiting for an AI law. AI adoption is already in full swing, and when unprepared, the chain is only waiting to break. In the case of the tribunal matter, that chain broke at the review step. In an RBI-regulated entity, the chain is most likely to break earlier, at provenance, if nobody logged which version of which model scored the application.
The current strategy, albeit unglamorous, is to ensure that the record of every AI-assisted decision made can survive being read aloud. So while the law may still be pending, the question is not. When it does come, the answer will have to exist already.
(The article has been authored by Ramprakash Ramamoorthy, Director - AI Research, Zoho Corporation)

articles.title: Critical Linux kernel flaw allows remote root attacks on MPTCP servers
articles.text:
Security researchers at Anthropic have developed an exploit for a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute commands as root on servers running Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listeners.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, also affects ordinary TCP connections, although remote code execution has not been publicly demonstrated on servers without an MPTCP listener.
Multipath TCP (MPTCP) is a TCP feature that lets a single connection use multiple network paths at the same time to improve performance and reliability. It is commonly used in environments where devices have multiple network connections, such as Wi-Fi and cellular networks.
CVE-2026-98432 is a use-after-free vulnerability in the kernel's IPv4 TCP networking code that received a severity score of 9.8 out of 10 from the Linux kernel CVE team.
The vulnerability affects Linux kernels dating back to version 4.4, including widely used distributions such as Ubuntu, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and Rocky Linux.
According to the Linux kernel advisory, the vulnerability stems from a race condition in how the kernel handles TCP connection requests, potentially causing a use-after-free condition.
"tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it," reads the advisory.
"Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req(). tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice."
A similar issue can occur during TCP request socket migration when net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req is enabled, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE program is used.
Although triggering the vulnerability requires no authentication, Red Hat says exploiting the race condition is more complex than just sending a malicious network packet.
Red Hat classifies the vulnerability as a potential denial-of-service issue that could cause a kernel crash, assigning it a lower severity score of 5.9 because exploitation is complex.
However, researchers at Anthropic demonstrated that the vulnerability could be exploited for remote code execution under specific conditions.
An Anthropic report explained that an unreleased Claude AI model developed an exploit that bypassed kernel address space layout randomization (KASLR) and executed arbitrary commands as root on a Linux server running an MPTCP listener.
According to Anthropic, the exploit took about 53 minutes to achieve remote root code execution, showing the vulnerability could be exploited for more than denial-of-service attacks.
While MPTCP is not typically enabled by default in applications, some software enables it automatically.
Beginning in Go 1.24, the programming language enables MPTCP by default for TCP listeners on Linux as long as the kernel supports the feature. Due to this, some Go-based network services may enable MPTCP listeners without administrators knowing.
Linux distros begin releasing patches
The vulnerability was fixed in the upstream Linux kernel and backported to maintained kernel branches. However, security updates have not yet been pushed out to all affected Linux distributions.
According to Canonical's security tracker, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, 26.04 LTS, and 26.10 remain vulnerable, with kernel fixes in progress as of October 30.
Red Hat also lists RHEL 8, 9, and 10 as affected, with fixes planned for future updates. RHEL 7 is not affected because its kernel does not contain the vulnerable code.
In mitigation guidance, Rocky Linux support provider CIQ confirms Rocky Linux 8, 9, and 10 are also affected and shared temporary firewall protections for affected systems.
According to Debian's security tracker, the vulnerability was fixed in kernel package version 6.1.190-1 for Debian 12 (Bookworm) and 6.12.113-1 for Debian 13 (Trixie). Fixed packages are also available for Debian testing and unstable.
Other Linux vendors, including Oracle Linux, Amazon Linux, and SUSE, have also released fixes for some affected kernel versions.
The vulnerability does not affect macOS, which uses Apple's XNU kernel rather than the Linux kernel.
Administrators are advised to check their distribution's security advisories and install updated kernel packages as they become available.
For systems where patches are not yet available, restricting access to trusted networks or IP addresses can reduce the risk.
CIQ also recommends temporarily blocking IPv4 TCP packets containing IP options before they reach the vulnerable TCP processing code, and shared examples of nftables rules that can block this type of traffic.
The company cautions that disabling MPTCP alone is insufficient because the underlying vulnerability can still be triggered through ordinary TCP traffic.
There are currently no confirmed reports of CVE-2026-98432 being exploited in the wild.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked

articles.title: How Grey plans to turn FX paychecks into credit
articles.text:
Grey, the Y Combinator-backed cross-border payments company, is looking to use foreign currency salary records to help remote workers access credit, addressing a gap in how traditional lenders assess professionals earning internationally.
Speaking on the Moonshot Podcast at Moonshot by TechCabal 2026 in Lagos, Nigeria, Idorenyin Obong, Grey’s co-founder and chief executive officer, said many remote workers struggle to establish creditworthiness because conventional credit bureaus have limited visibility into income earned from foreign employers.
He said Grey plans to use income and transaction data accumulated over the past six years to develop credit services for these customers.
“This is built on our own data and income intelligence from the last five to six years,” Obong said.
The planned offering forms part of Grey’s expansion into salary management following the launch of Paycheck on Wednesday.
The product allows professionals earning in US dollars, British pounds, and euros to automatically divide their salaries between spending, savings, and emergency funds.
With Paycheck, Obong said that a customer receiving $1,000 monthly could choose to allocate 20% to savings, another 10% to other financial needs, and retain 70% for immediate expenses. Users can adjust these allocations rather than follow a fixed spending formula.
Eligible Paycheck customers can also earn up to 3% annual interest on their US dollar Pouch, Grey’s savings feature. The product includes an emergency fund designed to help users work towards saving three months’ salary over a year, alongside salary tracking and other account benefits.
“We need to build a bit more around the lifestyle of salary customers; if a customer wants to save, we can help them with that, and then offer them interest. If a customer wants to travel, we can help them with that,” Obong said, adding that Grey is looking to support flight bookings and provide eSIMs for customers travelling internationally.
“That was where the thinking came from. We still saw a gap here because I think there’s a lot of innovation we could still build for our customers; we saw that gap and decided to start with it.”
Grey’s move underscores the changing needs of remote workers who initially used cross-border fintech platforms primarily to receive foreign payments.
As international employment becomes more established, these customers increasingly need tools to manage their earnings, build savings, and potentially access loans.
However, Grey has not announced when the credit feature will become available or disclosed its proposed lending rates and borrowing limits.
For now, Paycheck is starting with customers earning at least $300 in foreign-currency salaries.
While salary management and savings benefits are already available, Grey’s planned credit offering could extend those services to remote workers whose international earnings are often overlooked by traditional lenders.

articles.title: El BCE elige a Telefónica e Indra para desarrollar una parte clave de la infraestructura del futuro euro digital
articles.text:
El euro digital lleva años sobre la mesa del Banco Central Europeo (BCE), pero cada vez conocemos mejor qué hace falta para convertirlo en realidad. La institución aspira a estar preparada para una posible primera emisión en 2029, siempre que se apruebe a tiempo la legislación europea necesaria. Y no hablamos únicamente de dar luz verde a una nueva forma de dinero: también hay que construir la infraestructura tecnológica que permitiría utilizarlo en la práctica. Es un trabajo que involucra a numerosos participantes y en el que dos empresas españolas acaban de asegurarse un papel destacado.
Se trata de Telefónica y Minsait, la compañía tecnológica de Indra Group, que han formado un consorcio seleccionado por el BCE. Su encargo consiste en desplegar y operar una infraestructura de comunicaciones seguras para conectar la plataforma del euro digital con bancos y otros proveedores de servicios de pago. Eso sí, el organismo también ha elegido al consorcio formado por Nexi Payments y Deutsche Telekom Business Solutions, cuyo contrato ya está en vigor y cubrirá inicialmente las necesidades del programa piloto. El acuerdo con las compañías españolas comenzará el 3 de mayo de 2027 y tendrá una duración de diez años.
Para entender la dimensión del proyecto, primero debemos distinguir entre pagar digitalmente y utilizar dinero digital del banco central. Cuando hacemos una compra con tarjeta, normalmente estamos utilizando dinero depositado en una entidad bancaria. El euro digital, en cambio, sería una versión electrónica del efectivo, emitida y respaldada por el Eurosistema. Su diseño contempla pagos en establecimientos, compras por Internet y transferencias entre particulares, tanto con conexión como sin ella. Y hay dos diferencias fundamentales respecto a otras alternativas: no sería una criptomoneda y tampoco estaría pensado para reemplazar los billetes y las monedas.
La infraestructura que necesita el euro digital
Pero hay una distinción importante en el trabajo adjudicado: una cosa es conectar a los participantes externos con la plataforma y otra permitir que los componentes de esta se comuniquen entre sí. Pensemos en un banco que necesita acceder a sus servicios: deberá intercambiar información mediante una conexión protegida. Al mismo tiempo, la plataforma puede distribuir sus sistemas entre centros de datos diferentes, que también necesitan estar conectados. El contrato cubre precisamente estas dos necesidades de conectividad.
En ese reparto de tareas, Telefónica aportará su experiencia en redes y conectividad a través de áreas como Telefónica Global Solutions y Telefónica Tech. Según detallan las compañías en su nota de prensa, su trabajo incluirá el despliegue de una red privada MPLS, soluciones SD-WAN para conectar distintas sedes y servicios de ciberseguridad. Minsait, por su parte, proporcionará las herramientas para integrar aplicaciones y sistemas mediante API, además de soluciones de identidad digital y certificados electrónicos. Todo ello estará respaldado por un centro de operaciones de seguridad (SOC), encargado de detectar amenazas y responder ante posibles incidentes.
¿Cuánto dinero supone este encargo para las empresas españolas? Los documentos de contratación del BCE permiten conocer las cifras, pero también obligan a introducir algunos matices. El lote adjudicado tiene un valor estimado de 81,42 millones de euros, sin IVA, y contempla un máximo contractual de 177,66 millones, una cantidad que no debe confundirse con ingresos garantizados. La facturación efectiva dependerá de los servicios prestados durante la ejecución del contrato y, por ahora, tampoco conocemos cómo se repartirán los ingresos entre las firmas.
El euro digital no sería la primera moneda digital de banco central del mundo, pero Europa aspira a llevar este modelo a una escala considerable: los 21 países que comparten la moneda única. La iniciativa persigue además otro objetivo, reducir la dependencia de proveedores extranjeros en los pagos cotidianos. Según el BCE, dos tercios de las operaciones con tarjeta dependen de redes internacionales y 13 países de la zona euro carecen de un sistema nacional propio de tarjetas. Sin embargo, el proyecto también genera resistencias entre entidades financieras preocupadas por los costes de adaptación y sus posibles consecuencias económicas.
El siguiente paso llegará previsiblemente en la segunda mitad de 2027, cuando el Eurosistema tiene previsto iniciar un ejercicio piloto de doce meses con 36 proveedores de servicios de pago, comerciantes seleccionados y personal del BCE y de 19 bancos centrales nacionales. El objetivo será comprobar cómo funcionaría una versión de prueba del euro digital en situaciones cotidianas, aunque todavía no estaría disponible para el público en general. Mientras tanto, las instituciones europeas deberán completar el marco legislativo y el BCE tendrá que decidir sobre su emisión. Los preparativos tecnológicos avanzan, pero la puesta en circulación de esta moneda sigue sin estar garantizada.
