articles.title: Password Managers for Teams: Sharing Logins Safely Without a Sticky Note in Sight - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Growing Need for Secure Team Password Management
In today’s fast-paced business environment, teams often need to share access to various digital tools and platforms. From project management software to customer relationship management (CRM) systems, multiple team members require login credentials to collaborate effectively. However, this convenience comes with a significant risk: insecure password sharing practices. Writing passwords on sticky notes, emailing them unencrypted, or sharing them verbally can expose critical business data to cyber threats, leading to costly breaches and operational disruptions.
According to a 2023 report by Verizon, 81% of hacking-related breaches involve stolen or weak passwords, highlighting the urgent need for more secure methods of managing login credentials. This widespread vulnerability emphasizes how traditional password-sharing methods are no longer sufficient in the face of sophisticated cyber attacks. Businesses, especially those operating with distributed or remote teams, must rethink how they manage and share access to sensitive accounts.
Furthermore, a recent survey by Cybersecurity Ventures found that the average cost of a data breach involving compromised credentials reached $4.35 million in 2023, up 15% from previous years. These alarming figures underscore the financial and reputational risks associated with poor password management and sharing practices.
What Makes Password Managers Essential for Teams?
Password managers are software solutions designed to store, generate, and manage complex passwords in an encrypted vault. For teams, these tools offer a centralized platform to securely share login credentials without exposing the actual passwords. This eliminates the need for risky practices, such as sharing passwords verbally or jotting them down on physical notes. The tech managed by iTi Communications can help businesses implement robust cybersecurity strategies, including setting up and managing password managers tailored for team use.
Beyond simple storage, password managers enable teams to generate strong, unique passwords for each account, reducing the risk that a breach of one service compromises others. They also allow administrators to set granular access controls, ensuring that only authorized team members can view or use certain credentials. This is particularly important for businesses that deal with sensitive client data or intellectual property.
Integrating a reliable password manager can significantly reduce the risk of unauthorized access and data breaches. Businesses that leverage password managers report a 50% reduction in security incidents related to credential theft. This statistic reflects how implementing proper password management solutions can transform an organization’s security posture and foster safer collaboration among team members.
Moreover, password managers streamline workflows by enabling auto-fill features and seamless cross-device synchronization, reducing the friction often associated with password entry. This convenience encourages team members to adopt stronger security habits without sacrificing productivity.
How Experts at The KR Group Facilitate Secure Team Access
The experts at The KR Group specialize in integrating password management tools within broader IT infrastructure. They assist organizations in selecting the right platform based on team size, business needs, and security requirements. By leveraging their insights, companies can establish role-based access controls, ensuring that only authorized personnel can view or share specific credentials.
This approach not only protects sensitive information but also simplifies auditing and compliance-key considerations for industries governed by stringent data protection regulations such as GDPR, HIPAA, or PCI-DSS. The KR Group’s expertise extends to tailoring password management workflows that align with regulatory mandates, helping organizations avoid costly fines and reputational damage.
Moreover, The KR Group supports seamless integration of password managers with Single Sign-On (SSO) solutions and identity management systems, creating a unified and user-friendly authentication experience for teams. This integration reduces password fatigue and improves overall security hygiene across the organization.
Key Features to Look for in Team Password Managers
While numerous password managers exist, selecting the right tool for your team involves evaluating several critical features:
– Shared Vaults and Access Controls: Enables teams to share credentials securely with defined permissions, limiting exposure to only those who need access.
– Password Generation and Auto-Fill: Helps create strong, unique passwords and reduces manual entry errors, which are common sources of security vulnerabilities.
– Audit Trails and Reporting: Tracks access history for accountability and compliance purposes, allowing administrators to monitor who accessed what and when.
– Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): Adds an additional security layer beyond just passwords, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized access.
– Cross-Platform Compatibility: Ensures seamless access across desktops, mobile devices, and browsers, supporting diverse work environments.
– Emergency Access and Password Recovery: Allows designated team members to regain access in case of emergencies without compromising security.
– Integration Capabilities: Ability to integrate with existing IT infrastructure such as SSO, identity providers, and security information and event management (SIEM) tools.
Implementing a password manager with these capabilities can lead to a 33% decrease in time spent on password-related support requests, freeing IT teams to focus on strategic initiatives. (https://www.lastpass.com/resources/password-security-report) This efficiency gain translates to cost savings and enhanced operational effectiveness, making password managers a valuable investment beyond just security.
Overcoming Common Challenges in Team Password Management
Despite the clear benefits, some organizations hesitate to adopt password managers due to concerns about complexity, cost, or user adoption. To address these challenges, companies should invest in user training and choose intuitive platforms that integrate well with existing workflows. This reduces resistance and accelerates adoption across all team members.
Developing a clear password-sharing policy aligned with the organization’s security framework reinforces responsible behavior. Policies should define who can access shared credentials, how passwords are updated, and the procedures for onboarding or offboarding team members. Combining technology with governance ensures that password sharing is both safe and efficient.
Another common challenge is ensuring that password managers remain up-to-date and patched against vulnerabilities. Partnering with managed IT services can alleviate this burden by providing regular maintenance and security assessments.
Furthermore, organizations should consider scalability when selecting a password manager. As teams grow or change, the solution should accommodate new users and evolving security requirements without disruption.
Future Trends in Password Management for Teams
Looking ahead, passwordless authentication methods such as biometrics and hardware tokens are gaining traction. Technologies like FIDO2 and WebAuthn standards are enabling secure, phishing-resistant login experiences that eliminate the need for traditional passwords in some contexts.
However, password managers remain indispensable as they bridge the gap during this transition, especially for legacy systems and third-party applications that do not yet support passwordless methods. They also continue to evolve by integrating AI-driven features that detect anomalous login behaviors, automate credential rotation, and provide real-time security alerts.
Moreover, advancements in AI are enabling smarter password management solutions that can detect anomalies and automate security tasks, further protecting teams from credential-related threats. For example, AI-powered systems can identify unusual access patterns that may indicate compromised accounts and prompt immediate action.
As remote and hybrid work models persist, the need for secure, flexible, and user-friendly password management will only increase. Organizations that proactively adopt advanced password management solutions position themselves to mitigate risks and maintain operational resilience.
Conclusion
Securely sharing passwords within teams is no longer a luxury but a necessity in safeguarding business assets. By adopting modern password management tools and partnering with trusted IT experts, organisations can eliminate risky practices like sticky notes and unprotected emails. Investing in the right password management solution today is a proactive step toward a safer, more efficient future for any team. With the right technology, policies, and expert support in place, businesses can foster a security-conscious culture that empowers teams to collaborate confidently without compromising sensitive information.

articles.title: Govt notifies National Social Security Board for gig, platform workers
articles.text:
Govt notifies National Social Security Board for gig, platform workers
The Board is mandated to design, monitor, and recommend targeted welfare schemes to bridge the social security gap for millions of gig and platform workers, alongside traditional unorganised workers.
The government has notified the National Social Security Board for unorganised workers and gig and platform workers, which will design, monitor, and recommend targeted welfare schemes to bridge the social security gap.
Gig workers are those who perform work or participate in a work arrangement and earn from such activities outside the traditional employer-employee relationship.
Platform workers are those who engage in work through or with online platforms.
In a move towards ensuring comprehensive social security for India's massive informal workforce, the Ministry of Labour & Employment has notified the constitution of the National Social Security Board for Unorganised Workers and Gig & Platform Workers, a ministry statement said.
Established under the statutory framework of the Code on Social Security, this marks a historic shift by integrating digital gig and platform professionals into India's formal welfare architecture, the ministry said.
The Board will be presided over by the Union Minister for Labour & Employment and comprise representatives from the Central and state governments, prominent aggregator companies, employers, civil society organisations, workers' unions, and gig and platform worker associations.
The Board is mandated to design, monitor, and recommend targeted welfare schemes to bridge the social security gap for millions of gig and platform workers, alongside traditional unorganised workers.
The National Social Security Board shall meet at least thrice a year and observe the rules of procedure relating to the transaction of business at its meetings, as prescribed by the Central government.
The National Social Security Board shall recommend to the Central government the framing of suitable schemes for different sections of unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers.
The board will advise the Central government on such matters arising out of the administration of this Code as may be referred to; It will monitor such social welfare schemes for unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers administered by the Central government.
It will review the record keeping functions performed at the state level and also review the expenditure from the fund and account.
It will also undertake other functions as are assigned to it by the Central government from time to time.

articles.title: Windows 11 : plus besoin d’Adobe Acrobat, Microsoft Edge va devenir le meilleur lecteur de PDF
articles.text:
Il existe plusieurs façons d’ouvrir des documents PDF dans Windows 11. La première, en passant par un outil dédié, comme SumatraPDF, Foxit Reader ou encore Adobe Reader.
Il est également possible de faire appel à des services en ligne, mais la manœuvre est généralement déconseillée, d’autant plus s’il s’agit de PDF contenant des données sensibles.
Enfin, la dernière option existante pour ouvrir vos PDF est d’utiliser tout simplement votre navigateur Web. Qu’il s’agisse de Chrome, Edge ou encore de Firefox, tous les navigateurs Web actuels sont capables d’ouvrir ces fichiers. Certains proposent même quelques outils d’édition basiques qui permettent de remplir, signer ou encore d’annoter vos documents.
Mais jusqu’à présent, pour la gestion même de ces documents et des pages qui les composent, seules les applications dédiées étaient dotées du nécessaire. Les choses devraient toutefois changer, puisque Microsoft prévoit d’intégrer de nouvelles fonctions pour gérer plus facilement vos PDF directement depuis son navigateur Web Microsoft Edge.
Comme l’ont repéré nos confrères de Windows Latest, Microsoft prépare une importante mise à jour du lecteur PDF intégré à son navigateur Web Microsoft Edge. D’après la feuille de route mise en ligne par la firme de Redmond, cette mise à jour introduira, entre autres, une fonction pour fusionner et organiser vos documents de manière native, sans avoir à passer par un logiciel tiers, à utiliser de service en ligne tiers, ou à payer pour Adobe Acrobat.
Microsoft Edge pourra bientôt organiser vos pages et fusionner vos documents
Concrètement, Microsoft Edge va intégrer un outil qui vous permettra de fusionner plusieurs documents PDF entre eux. Vous pourrez ainsi combiner un document ouvert avec d’autres fichiers PDF, ouverts dans d’autres onglets ou stockés localement sur votre PC, pour en faire un document unique.
Microsoft Edge vous autorisera par ailleurs à organiser manuellement les pages qui composent votre document. Vous pourrez a priori sélectionner des pages pour les extraire, les supprimer, modifier leur ordre d’apparition dans le document, ou encore pour les faire pivoter si elles ne sont pas affichées dans le bon sens.
Le lecteur PDF intégré à Edge fournira par ailleurs un outil d’extraction de contenu (texte, images, etc.) qui fonctionnera même sur les documents ayant été numérisés, grâce au module de reconnaissance optique de caractères (OCR) intégré nativement dans Windows 11.
Microsoft prévoit également d’afficher un nouveau volet dédié aux outils d’annotation dans lequel seront centralisés les commentaires, notes manuscrites et autres surlignages. Vous pourrez ainsi rechercher facilement dans vos annotations, les filtrer, ou encore ajouter ou modifier vos commentaires.
Autre nouveauté qui devrait avoir son importance, le lecteur PDF de Microsoft Edge prendra en charge la traduction de vos documents PDF (jusqu’à 62 langues). Comble de l’ironie, pour proposer cette fonctionnalité gratuitement et vous éviter d’acheter Adobe Acrobat, Microsoft s’appuie sur les technologies d’Adobe. La firme de Redmond avait en effet abandonné, en 2023, son moteur PDF historique au profit du moteur Adobe Acrobat PDF Engine.
Des documents traités localement
Toutes ces nouvelles fonctionnalités de gestion de PDF dans Microsoft Edge seront traitées entièrement localement sur votre PC. Toutes les opérations de modification, de fusion ou d’annotation seront exécutées directement sur votre ordinateur, sans qu’aucune donnée ne transite par les serveurs de Microsoft, d’Adobe ou de tout autre service cloud.
Et la bonne nouvelle, c’est que les opérations réalisées sur vos documents PDF sont non destructrices. Les fichiers PDF sources ne seront pas modifiés. Le module PDF intégré à Microsoft Edge générera automatiquement un nouveau fichier PDF dès qu’une modification sera apportée.

articles.title: El Ayuntamiento de Madrid abre concurso para privatizar por 35 años el auditorio abandonado del parque Juan Carlos I
articles.text:
Ya hay luz verde. O ambar, más bien: el Ayuntamiento de Madrid ha abierto el concurso para entregar en concesión el auditorio del parque Juan Carlos I, el mayor al aire libre de la capital. Han propuesto una fórmula demanial, de 35 años prorrogable a otros cinco más. Es decir, aunque el recinto seguirá siendo de dominio y titularidad pública, lo explotará un operador privado. Ya se intentó en 2021 y no fue a parar a ningún lugar. Esta vez, el plazo de ofertas termina el 24 de noviembre.
Inaugurado en 1992 en un proyecto de Antonio Fernández-Alba, el último concierto de su historia fue el de Guns N’ Roses, en 2006. Desde entonces se ha ido convirtiendo en una reliquia ruinosa. Hace ahora nueve años, en noviembre de 2017, el equipo de Ahora Madrid presionó a la competencia para su rehabilitación. Pero no fue hasta junio de 2021 cuando el Ayuntamiento anunció su estudio de viabilidad y la promesa de reformarlo. Nunca se cumplió: durante 2024 y 2025 llegaron iniciativas privadas, hasta diciembre de ese mismo año, cuando la Junta de Barajas rechazó una propuesta del PSOE para rehabilitarlo y gestionarlo con Madrid Destino.
Qué piden a cambio. Ahora mismo, sobre el papel, el adjudicatario deberá programar al menos un 60% de actividad cultural, deportiva o de ocio para el público general. El 40% restante sería para eventos privados, como congresos o ferias.
Más: tendrá que abrir un espacio de restauración accesible, y podrá levantar edificios nuevos compatibles con la actividad. El pliego exige un informe acústico, pero permite superar los niveles ordinarios de ruido hasta 30 días al año y abrir el parque fuera de su horario habitual. El aforo de referencia (teórico) son 9.813 personas.
El canon. 446.000 euros al año más un 2% por cada año de explotación, esa es la cuota. Según el Ayuntamiento, las obras van a costar al menos 15,7 millones de euros (correrán a cargo del concesionario). Las instalaciones que se van a ceder están valoradas en 35,9 millones. Por comparar, un informe de Patrimonio Cultural que desveló Madridiario cifraba en 5,7 millones la inversión mínima para rehabilitarlo.
Un año de trámites. El Área de Cultura ya había adelantado que el auditorio volvería a usarse. Según la resolución municipal, dos particulares presentaron iniciativas de reforma y explotación, como decíamos al arranque del artículo. La primera del 3 de abril de 2024 preveía 14,6 millones de inversión (o 21,7 millones con equipamiento).
La segunda, del 2 de julio de 2025, hacía una oferta más baja, de 15,9 millones. A falta de pan, ambas fueron valoradas positivamente. En enero de 2026, el BOCM abrió un plazo de 30 días para recibir alternativas, y Somos Madrid contó que había dos ofertas más, de identidad secreta.
Del zombi al “estado aceptable”. Durante años se han publicado reportajes de saqueos, de zonas sin butacas, cables robados, grafitis y vegetación invadiendo los espacios. De las casi 10.000 butacas “solo quedaba una”, documentaba un reportaje de ElEspañol. Los informes del anteproyecto, de los primeros años de Almeida, hablan de un estado de conservación aceptable, con carencias que subsanar y sin daños estructurales importantes. ¿En qué quedamos? En que el diagnóstico exacto depende de qué se mida a día de hoy, ya casi metidos en noviembre de 2027.
Las dos posturas. El Ayuntamiento sostiene que Madrid carece de recintos de entre 5.000 y 10.000 personas sin problemas de ruido para los vecinos. En el parque Tierno Galván, el único comparable, los vecinos llevan un tiempo quejándose de saturación de festivales.
Borja Carabante, delegado de Urbanismo, consideraba una buena noticia este movimiento de explotación. La idea de recuperar un recinto que lleva casi dos décadas sin uso parece lo más inteligente; el interrogante a resolver son las garantías de descanso y medio ambiente. Y Más Madrid calificó de “totalmente intolerable” la gestión privada, al entender que se pierde el control de la programación cultural. La palabra “privatización”, por cierto, es un término que el Ayuntamiento ni usa ni recoge en ningún apartado.
El precedente. Este modelo ya se aplicó en el antiguo IMAX del Tierno Galván, cedido durante 42 años a la multinacional de musicales Stage Entertainment, un gigantesco propietario del espectáculo con regular prensa que ahora mismo tiene los cines en reforma, tras el “extraño” derrumbe de su cúpula central. Aquel cine cerró en 2014 por deudas, y el edificio estuvo años vacío hasta su rehabilitación.
Qué viene ahora. Tras el 24 de noviembre, el Ayuntamiento evaluará las ofertas y adjudicará la concesión final, un proceso del que no consta calendario público. Todavía queda saber cuánto subirá el canon sobre el mínimo y cómo se compaginará el ruido con los vecinos del distrito de Barajas. El auditorio ha cumplido la mayoría de edad (lleva 18 años sin ofrecer ningún espectáculo) y los estudios de acústica. Por comparar, algunas viviendas registraron unos 75 decibelios de media durante los entrenamientos libres del Gran Premio de Fórmula 1 en Madring. El umbral está limitado en 45.

articles.title: Doom n’a jamais tourné comme ça : un Raspberry Pi, deux IA et aucun moteur de jeu
articles.text:
Après les calculatrices, les imprimantes et même les tests de grossesse, Doom continue de s'inviter un peu partout. Cette fois, un développeur a fait fonctionner une version simplifiée du célèbre FPS sur un Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W. Sa particularité ? Le jeu n'est pas exécuté par un moteur classique, mais recréé image après image par une intelligence artificielle.
Faire tourner Doom sur à peu près n'importe quoi est devenu une tradition chez les bidouilleurs. En 2020, Foone Turing avait même réussi à le rendre jouable sur un test de grossesse numérique, après en avoir remplacé l'écran et le processeur.
Avec son projet Tinyworldformer, le développeur SheepSeb pousse l'expérience dans une autre direction. Plutôt que d'adapter le code d'un jeu à une machine peu puissante, il a entraîné une IA à reproduire son fonctionnement. Le tout sur un Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W, une carte à quelques euros équipée d'une puce RP2350, de deux cœurs pouvant atteindre 150 MHz et de seulement 520 Ko de mémoire vive. Doom avait déjà été porté sur un Raspberry Pi Pico en 2022, mais cette fois, l'expérience ne repose plus sur l'exécution du jeu original.
Un Doom lite sans moteur de jeu, mais avec deux IA
Tinyworldformer repose sur deux petits réseaux neuronaux. Le premier est un world model, ou modèle de monde : entraîné à partir de parties enregistrées, il reçoit une image et une action du joueur, puis prédit l'image suivante. Il ne calcule donc pas les conséquences des actions à partir des règles originales du jeu, mais tente de les reproduire grâce à ce qu'il a appris.
Le second réseau se charge de jouer. Il observe les images produites par le premier et décide des actions à effectuer. Les deux modèles peuvent ainsi fonctionner ensemble sans exécuter le programme original.
Attention toutefois, il ne s'agit pas du Doom de 1993, mais de Doom-lite, une adaptation très simplifiée : un labyrinthe de 8 × 8 cases en pseudo-3D, avec un ennemi à affronter. L'expérience fonctionne également avec des versions miniatures de Pong, Breakout, Flappy Bird et Pac-Man.
L'idée n'est d'ailleurs pas entièrement nouvelle. En 2024, des chercheurs de Google avaient déjà présenté GameNGen, un modèle génératif capable de simuler le véritable Doom en temps réel, grâce aux TPU de Google. SheepSeb, lui, fait tenir son modèle de Doom-lite dans seulement 55 000 paramètres, sur un microcontrôleur dépourvu de GPU et d'accélérateur IA dédié. Les deux réseaux fonctionnent sur l'un des cœurs de la puce, tandis que l'autre gère notamment l'affichage et les communications USB.
Une IA imagine le jeu, l'autre apprend à y jouer
L'expérience ne consiste pas seulement à regarder deux IA jouer ensemble. Une pression sur un bouton permet de reprendre les commandes et d'interagir avec le monde généré par le modèle.
Plus intéressant encore, SheepSeb a intégré un mode d'apprentissage directement sur le Pico 2 W. Un agent peut ainsi apprendre progressivement à jouer dans l'environnement imaginé par l'autre réseau neuronal, sans nécessiter d'ordinateur puissant pour cette phase d'apprentissage.
Les résultats ne sont évidemment pas parfaits. Sur les transitions réservées à l'évaluation de Doom-lite, le modèle reproduit exactement l'image suivante dans 83,6 % des cas, selon les mesures de son créateur, en excluant les événements aléatoires impossibles à prédire précisément. Ce critère est particulièrement exigeant : un seul élément graphique incorrect suffit à considérer toute l'image comme erronée, même lorsque la partie reste jouable.
Tinyworldformer ne cherche donc pas à remplacer les moteurs de jeu traditionnels. Il démontre surtout qu'une IA capable de simuler un petit univers interactif, et même d'y apprendre à agir, peut fonctionner sur un matériel extrêmement modeste.
Après avoir fait tourner Doom sur toutes sortes d'appareils, les bidouilleurs explorent ainsi une nouvelle possibilité : jouer sans même exécuter les règles originales du jeu. Et nul besoin de posséder un Raspberry Pi pour découvrir le résultat : SheepSeb propose une démonstration interactive accessible depuis un navigateur, ainsi que le code source du projet sur GitHub.

articles.title: Ce smartphone Android en promo à moins de 200 € est une bonne affaire du Black Friday — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le Moto G67 fait partie des smartphones Motorola à petit prix. Dans cette gamme, on cherche surtout un grand écran, de la place pour ses photos et une batterie qui suit. Auchan n’a pas attendu fin novembre pour baisser les prix, comme plusieurs marchands que nous suivons dans notre sélection des meilleures offres du Black Friday en avant-première, et le G67 en profite pour chuter sous les 200 euros.
Les atouts du Motorola Moto G67
- Un écran OLED de 6,78 pouces en 2 772 x 1 272 pixels à 120 Hz
- 256 Go de stockage, extensibles par microSD jusqu’à 2 To
- Une batterie de 5200 mAh avec une charge filaire de 30 watts
Le Moto G67 en version 4 + 256 Go passe de 299,99 euros à 199,99 euros chez Auchan, soit 100 euros de moins que le prix barré de l’enseigne. Ce prix barré dépasse toutefois le tarif de lancement fixé par Motorola en janvier, 259 euros. Par rapport à ce prix officiel, l’économie réelle est de 59 euros, soit environ 23 %. On trouve la même offre chez Boulanger.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le Motorola Moto G67. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Un grand écran OLED pour les séries, et 256 Go pour tout garder
La dalle OLED de 6,78 pouces est le gros argument de ce Moto G67. Sa définition de 2 772 x 1 272 pixels dépasse le Full HD+ qu’on croise souvent à ce prix. L’OLED apporte aussi des noirs profonds, et la dalle monte à 120 Hz pour un défilement plus fluide. Pour regarder une série dans le métro ou faire défiler YouTube au lit, c’est franchement confortable. Le tout pèse 182 grammes, ce qui reste raisonnable pour un écran de cette taille. Motorola annonce une certification IP64 qui assure une protection contre la poussière et les projections d’eau, mais pas contre l’immersion. On évitera donc de l’emmener à la piscine.
Le stockage suit. Avec 256 Go, vous pouvez entasser photos, vidéos et applications sans faire le ménage tous les deux mois. Si ça ne suffit pas, le smartphone accepte une carte microSD jusqu’à 2 To. La connectivité coche les cases attendues (5G, double SIM avec nanoSIM et eSIM, NFC pour le paiement sans contact, Bluetooth 5.4), avec lecteur d’empreintes et reconnaissance faciale pour le déverrouillage. Petit regret quand même, le Wi-Fi s’arrête à la norme Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac).
Un Dimensity 6300 pensé pour le quotidien plus que pour le jeu
À l’intérieur, Motorola a installé un MediaTek Dimensity 6300. C’est une puce à huit cœurs pensée pour l’entrée de gamme 5G. Elle est accompagnée de 4 Go de RAM, avec Android 16 au démarrage. Pour WhatsApp, les réseaux sociaux, le GPS ou le streaming, cette configuration fait le taf. Honnêtement, il ne faut pas lui en demander beaucoup plus. Avec 4 Go de mémoire vive, le multitâche intensif et les jeux 3D gourmands vont vite montrer leurs limites. Si vous jouez beaucoup, mieux vaut regarder ailleurs.
La batterie de 5200 mAh offre une capacité confortable sur le papier. La recharge filaire grimpe jusqu’à 30 watts en USB Power Delivery. Attention, le chargeur n’est pas fourni dans la boîte, et la charge sans fil est absente. Pour la photo, on trouve à l’arrière un capteur principal de 50 mégapixels et un ultra grand-angle de 8 mégapixels (le troisième rond du module n’est qu’un capteur de luminosité), plus une caméra frontale de 32 mégapixels pour les selfies et les appels vidéo.

articles.title: Black Friday : À moins de 100 €, ce pack de deux routeurs Wi-Fi 7 couvre un logement jusqu'à 130 m²
articles.text:
La box internet est souvent installée dans le salon, juste à côté de la prise fibre. Le signal Wi-Fi, lui, s’affaiblit dès qu’il doit traverser un ou deux murs porteurs, et la chambre du fond devient une zone où les vidéos chargent mal. Les systèmes maillés, aussi appelés mesh, règlent ce problème en ajoutant des bornes Wi-Fi à différents endroits du logement, afin d’étendre la couverture réseau.
Boulanger a lancé ses offres Black Friday en avance, dès ce vendredi 30 octobre, et le pack de deux bornes Deco BE22 de TP-Link en fait partie. Ce kit Wi-Fi 7 passe à 99,99 € au lieu de 119,99 €, soit 20 € d’économie, ou un peu moins de 50 € par borne.
C’est quoi, le TP-Link Deco BE22 ?
Le pack contient deux bornes identiques. La première se branche à la box internet en Ethernet, tandis que la seconde se place plus loin dans le logement, à un endroit où le signal reste suffisamment bon. Ensemble, elles diffusent un seul réseau Wi-Fi, avec un nom et un mot de passe uniques. Votre smartphone peut ainsi passer d’une borne à l’autre sans que vous ayez à vous reconnecter. TP-Link met en avant une itinérance pilotée par l’intelligence artificielle, censée orienter chaque appareil vers la borne la plus adaptée.
Côté débits, TP-Link annonce jusqu’à 2 882 Mbit/s sur la bande 5 GHz et 688 Mbit/s sur la bande 2,4 GHz, soit 3,6 Gbit/s cumulés. Ce sont des maximums théoriques. Il prend en charge le MLO (Multi-Link Operation), une fonction du Wi-Fi 7 qui permet à un appareil compatible d’utiliser plusieurs liaisons en même temps. TP-Link en promet un meilleur débit et une connexion plus stable. TP-Link annonce la prise en charge de plus de 150 appareils connectés en simultané, et recommande ce kit pour les logements allant jusqu’à 130 m². Les anciens appareils Wi-Fi 5 ou Wi-Fi 6 restent compatibles.
À ce prix, le pack TP-Link Deco BE22 est-il une bonne affaire ?
À 99,99 € les deux bornes, le Deco BE22 vise un cas d’usage précis : un appartement ou une maison où la box couvre mal certaines pièces. Si votre logement est petit et que le signal passe partout, un kit maillé n’apportera pas grand-chose. En revanche, si le Wi-Fi peine à atteindre une chambre éloignée ou un bureau situé à l’étage, cette solution peut améliorer sensiblement la couverture, à condition de placer correctement les deux bornes.
Boulanger a lancé ses offres Black Friday en avance et prolonge sa période de retour jusqu’au 31 janvier 2027 pour les achats concernés par l’opération. De quoi prendre le temps de vérifier si le kit améliore réellement la couverture Wi-Fi de votre logement.
Black Friday 2026 : tout ce qu’il faut savoir
Depuis une dizaine d’années, le Black Friday s’est infiltré dans le calendrier commercial des grandes marques et enseignes françaises. Avec l’expérience, on peut vous dire que cet événement fait partie des meilleurs moments pour faire de bonnes affaires.
Les dates du Black Friday
Bien qu’il porte encore le nom du vendredi noir, le Black Friday s’étend désormais sur un mois chez de nombreux revendeurs. Un format moins typique qui lui retire un peu son petit côté FOMO. On dirait presque les soldes, finalement. Mais c’est aussi moins le rush, ce qui est une bonne chose pour ceux qui veulent faire des achats plus raisonnés. Globalement, on peut résumer ce Black Friday en quatre temps forts :
- Début novembre : les avant-premières Black Friday.
- Autour du 20 novembre, selon les enseignes : la Black Week commence généralement plusieurs jours avant le jour J.
- 27 novembre : la date du Black Friday, même si les offres commencent généralement avant et se prolongent le week-end des 28 et 29 novembre.
- 30 novembre : le Cyber Monday.

Pour les produits phares comme les AirPods, la PS5, la Switch 2, un iPhone ou un Samsung Galaxy, sachez que nos tests sont là pour vous aider à savoir s’ils méritent votre argent.

articles.title: Trezor warns of suspected crypto-theft implant in hardware wallet
articles.text:
Hardware wallet device maker Trezor has received credible reports about a suspected hardware crypto-theft implant in a Trezor Safe 5 sold by its reseller CryptoBilis in Southeast Asia.
Although the company has not yet received the device to examine it and confirm whether there is a malicious implant, it has warned potentially affected users to move their private keys and digital assets to known safe wallets.
Trezor wallets are physical devices that store cryptocurrency private keys and authorize transactions. Safe 5 is one of its latest models and is currently available for purchase from the official store.
According to Trezor, the concerns arose after it received a report from an Indonesian user who purchased a Safe 5 device from CryptoBilis through Tokopedia in August 2026.
The user opened it and found an extra circuit board between the wallet's main board and screen, equipped with a cellular module and antenna.
Based on unconfirmed information supplied by that customer, the implant appears capable of reading information displayed on the screen, including the wallet recovery phrase, and transmitting it over a mobile network when plugged in.
CryptoBilis is the same retailer implicated in a Ledger implant incident that unfolded earlier this month, and the implants on the two devices appear to be similar in form and function.
Ledger later confirmed the compromise and asked resellers and distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to halt all sales until the investigation confirms their safety.
In response to the Ledger incident, and before it had any indication it was impacted, Trezor immediately stopped device sales through CryptoBilis on October 9, 2026. The company later announced it would restructure and tighten its reseller network globally to maintain higher levels of security.
Trezor says it is unaware of any funds being stolen as a result of a supply-chain attack, and promised to provide updates once it receives the device, which is currently being shipped to it.
Meanwhile, multiple reports of losses by Ledger users have emerged since earlier this month, and a recent Singapore police announcement added another $3,500,000 to the tally.
For now, Trezor recommends not setting up or using any device bought via CryptoBilis from March 2026 onward.
Users who have already done so are advised to move their funds to a newly created wallet with a new recovery phrase.
Buyers holding proof of purchase may contact Trezor for a replacement device or a voucher for a new device.
Trezor underlined that weighing devices is not a reliable way to determine if they have been tampered with.

articles.title: Kubernetes just formed a workload conformance group. Here’s why it matters for AI teams.
articles.text:
Kubernetes just formed a workload conformance group. Here’s why it matters for AI teams.
Welcome to the final edition of Road to KubeCon, where we track the Kubernetes and cloud-native ecosystem each week on The New Stack as we head into KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, November 9-12 in Salt Lake City, Utah.
This week we explore how Kubernetes is getting new guidance for running AI workloads, including a new book from TNS, a dedicated Kubernetes working group, and advice on running LLMs across multiple GPUs.
Also in this day-before-Halloween-timed column, we’ve got OTel operators speaking a new language, security horrors from the latest AGNTCon + MCPCon, and untangling the dark webs of Kubernetes pod troubleshooting gone awry.
Join the conversation with HPE at KubeCon
HPE will have a big presence at KubeCon NA this year. The gold sponsor will be at Booths 151 and 145, where they’ll present live sessions throughout the day on topics spanning vSphere, HPE Kubernetes Service (HKS), distributed inference, setting up cloud storage for Kubernetes, and more.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is a presenting sponsor of Road to KubeCon. HPE Software helps IT organizations modernize infrastructure, streamline operations, and accelerate AI initiatives across hybrid, multi-vendor environments.
This year, the focus is on gaining visibility and control across Kubernetes environments across VMs, infrastructure, and clouds. If you’d like to schedule a meeting with an HPE representative, contact jennifer.osuna@hpe.com.
TNS publishes Kubernetes guidebook for 2027
In partnership with HPE, The New Stack has published a helpful book containing ten checks for teams running AI workloads on Kubernetes. The book, Kubernetes in 2027: Building Platforms for AI, Autonomy, and Scale, is available for download now.
Written by contributing writer Chris J. Preimesberger, the guide spans the full lifecycle, covering how to stress-test infrastructure before launch, how to meet the nuanced demands of agentic AI, what to watch for, and how to develop stronger permissioning models for agents.
Since agentic AI is prone to bursty, unpredictable behavior, arming your infrastructure with the right approach on Kubernetes is an important first step to production stability and success with AI at scale.
Kubernetes gets a Workload Conformance Working Group
Workload types have been expanding for years. And AI undoubtedly adds more variety. Against this backdrop, on Tuesday, October 27, the Kubernetes community announced a dedicated Workload Conformance Working Group.
According to Broadcom’s Nabarun Pal, writing on behalf of WG Workload Conformance on the Kubernetes blog, “The working group is writing a shared standard for how workloads behave at runtime on Kubernetes.” To do so, they’ll need community input, Pal adds.
The Kubernetes AI Conformance test already determines whether a cluster can run AI or machine learning (ML) workloads. Yet none currently exists for workloads, requiring workarounds, manual exploration, or monitoring for signs like node drain or permission issues. So the new WG aims to create a similar standard for workloads.
It’s a significant step forward as the Kubernetes community grapples with a growing variety of workloads, including AI. Interested parties can read the working group proposal for more information, join the Slack channel, or attend biweekly meetings to get involved.
OpenTelemetry Transformation Language reaches v1
Earlier this week, the OpenTelemetry (OTel) project reached a milestone: the OpenTelemetry Transformation Language (OTTL) has reached v1. It’s stable for traces, metrics, and logs, and is included within Collector Contrib v0.164.0 and onward.
As Grafana Labs’ Tyler Helmuth recounts on the OTel blog, OTTL was created in 2022 as the configuration language for the transform processor. The domain-specific language lets you modify, filter, and enrich telemetry data directly at the collector level.
Longevity-thinkers will like this: They’ve also made a big backward-compatibility promise for OTTL. “If you write OTTL statements, the syntax and the standard functions stay backward compatible,” says Helmuth.
As Kubernetes evolves, so do the demands on the teams running it. Presenting sponsor HPE helps teams address that complexity with software spanning virtualization, cloud management, observability, and automation.
Solving LLMs on shared GPUs
Putting all AI workloads on a single GPU is expensive and inefficient. But how do we pack multiple LLMs on shared GPUs safely, without a bunch of guesswork or manual toil?
Ratnopam Chakrabarti, a senior solutions architect at AWS, took to X to share an early preview of his upcoming joint Nvidia–AWS session, which will seemingly answer this question for KubeCon attendees.
He says his KubeCon session will “demonstrate an agent pipeline that profiles workloads and handles model colocation on GPUs, all in real time.” It’s one of many KubeCon sessions this year tackling AI optimization on Kubernetes.
Troubleshooting GKE workloads with VPC Flow Logs
This week on the Google Cloud blog, Google Cloud product managers Nishant Kumar and Whitney Jenkins describe a common issue for cloud operators: Kubernetes pods are ephemeral, making them hard to troubleshoot.
As they describe, “In a standard cloud network, flow logs provide that view by recording connections between IP addresses, ports, and protocols.” In Kubernetes, however, pods are temporary; they add, and by the time you track them down, they’ve often already vanished — leaving little evidence or records to inform troubleshooting.
The workaround, at least for those using Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), is its built-in VPC Flow Logs. This feature uses Google’s virtualized network to log every sampled flow with metadata like pod, workload, namespace, and service.
It’s one example of how cloud-native platforms are continuing to advance the infrastructure around Kubernetes to increase its visibility and usability.
AGNTCon + MCPCon prioritizes agent security
Is your agent installing malware without your knowledge? It’s a real possibility.
The latest AGNTCon + MCPCon event this month in San Jose, California, featured plenty of interesting talks that might resonate with the cloud-native community looking at the agent trend with big, worried eyes.
For instance, Snyk’s Liran Tal gave a talk entitled Your AI Agent Installed Malware Because a SKILL.md Told It To. Tal covered how agents often get tricked into running malware and offered some guidance on how to prevent it.
Vstorm’s Antoni Kozelski and Bartosz Adam Gonczarek also presented how they built an e-commerce MCP server and let the agent experiment with purchases across four different hosts. It behaved drastically differently in each scenario.
The session opened a conversation about where authorization rules that allow or disallow agents from taking irreversible steps should live. For Vstorm, it meant placing them on the server, not locally. They’re also following up with a webinar on the subject soon.
These stories are just two examples of what we’re seeing a lot: the unintended consequences of giving AI agents the keys to the kingdom. Cloud-native operators should watch for stories like this as they build the foundational infrastructure to support agents.
See you at KubeCon
Road to KubeCon is an eight-part series presented by HPE. Before you go, explore how HPE Software helps IT teams do more with less complexity.
And that’s a wrap for this year’s Road to KubeCon series! It’s been a privilege and an adventure profiling the top movements in the cloud-native world over the past two months.
In this weekly column, we covered many areas across eight editions, spanning updates to Kubernetes itself, like the Kubernetes 1.37 update and the move to cgroup v2.
Much of the discussion centered around how cloud-native technology is evolving for AI. We looked at case studies around Kubernetes inference at scale, and how agent harnesses are evolving.
Another recurring theme was increasing operator visibility. We saw how OpenTelemetry and Prometheus are converging and how to spot idle GPUs and optimize.
Arguably, the biggest takeaway is that the Kubernetes ecosystem is facing major shifts to meet the challenges of running AI workloads at scale. Is it up for the task?
KubeCon NA is anticipated to tackle this question head-on, from discussion at the co-located events to the main keynotes, sessions, and the showcase floor.
View the Road to KubeCon archive for all editions in this series, along with other insights from the TNS and HPE teams. A big thank you to the column’s sponsor, HPE, for making this column possible, and to the community members who shared their insights.
Now, we’re excited to continue the conversation in person at KubeCon NA!
See you there.

articles.title: Breet makes the case for simpler crypto payments at Moonshot
articles.text:
Making cryptocurrency payments easier to use is as much a challenge as building the infrastructure behind them, Breet chief operating officer Vivian Mbene told Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos on Wednesday.
Mbene said the company’s biggest task was making a complicated product appear simple to customers, allowing businesses to accept digital assets without taking on the operational demands of managing them.
Breet, founded in 2019, converts cryptocurrency into cash for individuals in Nigeria and Ghana. It also offers an application programming interface that allows businesses to accept crypto payments and receive settlement in local currency.
The proposition separates the payment method from the currency a merchant ultimately wants to hold. Customers can pay with digital assets, while businesses receive local money without having to build a crypto operation of their own.
For Mbene, the objective is to reduce the work required to complete that transaction. “We’re just obsessed with simplicity,” she said.
That approach places much of the complexity behind the scenes. Functions such as monitoring transactions, routing deposits and converting currencies need to work together without requiring merchants to manage each step themselves.
But making the process look straightforward can create a different problem: convincing customers and business partners to trust it.
“Sometimes simplicity brings suspicion, and when it’s powered by crypto, the suspicion kind of doubles,” Mbene said.
Her remarks highlighted a tension for crypto payment providers. A simpler interface can reduce the effort involved in using a service, but it does not necessarily remove doubts about the technology underneath it.
Breet’s pitch is that businesses should be able to use crypto as a payment channel while continuing to manage their finances in familiar currencies. For providers pursuing that model, the commercial test is whether they can make accepting digital assets both straightforward and credible to merchants.

articles.title: Sam Altman, creador de ChatGPT: "El mundo debería aceptar que sucedan algunas cosas malas" en aras de los beneficios de la IA
articles.text:
Sam Altman, director ejecutivo de OpenAI, cree que el mundo tendrá que convivir con algunos daños de la inteligencia artificial para aprovechar sus ventajas, y lo presenta como uno de los puntos que le separan de Anthropic. "Creemos que el mundo debería aceptar que sucedan algunas cosas malas a cambio de los beneficios de esta tecnología y de que la gente tenga capacidad de decisión", explicó en una entrevista el 4 de octubre de 2026. Y es que entre su empresa y la de Dario Amodei hay, según él, "mucha distancia".
Dos caminos desde OpenAI. OpenAI lanzó ChatGPT a finales de 2022, un lanzamiento que desató el auge comercial de la IA. Pero a finales de mayo de 2026 Anthropic, fundada en 2021 por antiguos directivos de OpenAI, superó la última valoración conocida de la empresa de Altman.
Además, según Politico, Anthropic lleva tiempo considerada la defensora más firme de la regulación dentro de la industria, algo que hasta hace poco chocaba con el enfoque más ligero de la creadora de ChatGPT.
Más cerca de lo que parece. Y eso que sus posiciones se han ido acercando. En septiembre de 2026, Altman respaldó la petición de Amodei de frenar el desarrollo de los modelos más avanzados. Según contaba Forbes el 12 de septiembre, esa propuesta pasaba por permitir auditorías externas y alertaba de riesgos como los ciberataques o la toma de internet por parte de bots autónomos.
La acusación de captura regulatoria. Eso sí, Altman aprovechó una crítica que asesores cercanos a Donald Trump lanzan contra Anthropic, a la que reprochan utilizar la regulación para blindar su posición, para marcar distancias con su rival. Es la acusación de "captura regulatoria" que formuló David Sacks, responsable de IA de la Casa Blanca.
Altman no se sumó a ella, pero tampoco a la postura que atribuye a quienes piden más control: "No estoy de acuerdo, pero entiendo el punto de vista de quienes piensan: 'Esta tecnología va a ser tan potente y tan peligrosa que un único laboratorio de San Francisco debería tenerla para asegurarse de que no pase nada malo y, en cierto modo, decidir cómo repartir los beneficios'". Para él, eso sería "una contrapartida completamente inaceptable", contraria a la "postura reguladora más ligera" que defiende OpenAI.
De la extinción al optimismo. Durante años, Altman advirtió de los riesgos existenciales de la IA, hasta el punto de firmar en 2023 una declaración sobre el riesgo de extinción que pedía tratarlo como una prioridad global. En Decoded, en cambio, defendió que "la gente hará muchísimas más cosas buenas que malas, órdenes de magnitud más".
Pero esa tolerancia tiene un límite, y Altman lo dejó claro más adelante en la conversación: no acepta "los riesgos realmente catastróficos", entre ellos "una grave pérdida de control a manos de la IA".

articles.title: Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
articles.text:
Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
- Date:
- October 22, 2026
- Source:
- University of Cambridge
- Summary:
- Cambridge researchers have created a groundbreaking $10 optical sensor that delivers the precision of laboratory equipment in a device small enough for wearable technology. It identified foods, plastics, and medicines with 100% accuracy in tests and demonstrated the ability to monitor blood glucose, alcohol, and other health markers without invasive procedures.
- Share:
A new optical sensor costing just $10 could bring laboratory-level precision to wearable health monitors, potentially allowing people to track blood glucose without needles. The technology could also transform food testing, industrial quality control, and environmental monitoring.
Researchers at the University of Cambridge and GlitterinTech (a start-up founded by the same research group) have developed a new type of optical spectrometer that combines exceptional accuracy with a remarkably small size and low cost. Measuring just centimeters across, the device could be incorporated into portable electronics and wearable health technology. Its potential applications range from monitoring important health markers in real time to identifying materials and detecting changes in chemical composition.
Optical spectrometers work by analyzing light to reveal information about the substances it interacts with. They are essential tools in medicine, manufacturing, chemical testing, and environmental research. However, making these instruments smaller has traditionally meant compromising their performance. Compact spectrometers often have limited measurement ranges, reduced resolution, or lower accuracy, making them better suited to identifying substances than performing precise measurements.
The researchers believe their new design could overcome these limitations. Known as a convolutional spectrometer, it uses a mathematical principle called the convolution theorem to analyze light in a fundamentally different way. According to the team, this approach delivers performance that surpasses existing types of spectrometers in several key areas, including designs based on light dispersion, Fourier transforms, and computational reconstruction.
A New Way to Analyze Light With Extraordinary Precision
Traditional spectrometers generally separate incoming light into its component wavelengths or use complex calculations to reconstruct its spectrum. The new device takes another approach by performing a mathematical operation called convolution directly on the incoming light.
To accomplish this, the researchers arranged optical components with repeating spectral responses in a sequence. These components can include unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers or micro-ring resonators. By adjusting them in proportion to one another, the system can shift its response to different wavelengths in a controlled, linear fashion. Fast Fourier transforms are then used to accurately recover the light spectrum.
"The key insight was to go back to the mathematics and ask whether there was a fundamentally cleaner way to retrieve spectra," said Dr. Chunhui Yao, a lead author of the study. "By using the convolution theorem directly in the optical domain, we avoid many of the limitations that have held miniaturized spectrometers back. This gives us high precision, strong noise tolerance, and very low computational overhead, all in a compact and low-cost system."
The researchers built the spectrometer using a silicon nitride photonic platform and integrated it with onboard electronics. It operates across a broad range of near-infrared wavelengths (1200-1700 nm) and can collect and process measurements in less than a second.
Another important advantage is its ability to expand its measurement capabilities without major hardware changes. Because the system uses repeating optical patterns, its spectral bandwidth can theoretically be extended almost without limit. Adding more optical components in sequence can also increase its resolution exponentially.
A $10 Sensor That Could Transform Food Testing and Healthcare
To evaluate the device outside purely theoretical measurements, the researchers tested it on a variety of materials and substances. The results demonstrated its potential for applications that normally depend on larger, more expensive laboratory instruments.
When used to identify plastics, pharmaceuticals, coffee, flour, and tea, the spectrometer achieved a 100% classification success rate in the reported tests. It also measured concentrations in water-based and organic solutions with accuracies of approximately 0.01%, exceeding the performance of commercial benchtop spectrometers in those experiments.
The healthcare demonstrations were particularly promising. Under conditions designed to reflect real physiological environments, the device accurately measured several human biomarkers, including skin moisture, blood alcohol, blood lactate, and blood glucose.
The researchers also demonstrated noninvasive glucose tracking over an extended period in one participant. Although further testing would be needed before the technology could become a practical medical product, the finding suggests a possible route toward monitoring blood sugar without repeatedly piercing the skin.
"These biomedical demonstrations are particularly exciting," said Prof. Qixiang Cheng, who led the project. "What makes this work stand out is not just performance in the lab, but technical readiness. Dr. Chunhui Yao's contribution was crucial in translating a mathematical concept into a fully packaged, robust system that operates reliably across temperature extremes and real-world conditions. That combination is what opens the door to practical deployment."
The sensor also demonstrated impressive resistance to temperature changes. It continued operating reliably between -20°C and 80°C, an unusually wide temperature range for a miniature spectrometer. This durability could be especially valuable for wearable devices, factory equipment, and sensors operating outdoors.
Why a Simpler Design Could Be a Major Breakthrough
The new spectrometer's advantages extend beyond its accuracy, size, and price. Its internal design also reduces the amount of computing power needed to analyze incoming light.
Many existing miniature spectrometers depend on complicated calibration procedures and demanding algorithms to reconstruct spectral information. These methods can become unreliable when measurements contain noise, and they often require substantial processing resources.
The Cambridge team's convolution-based approach avoids much of this complexity. Because the measurements follow a linear mathematical relationship, the system can recover spectra rapidly and consistently while using relatively little computational power.
"This is a beautiful example of how elegant engineering can unlock real impact," said Prof. Richard Penty, who contributed to the photonic system design and integration. "The architecture is simple, scalable, and manufacturable, yet it delivers precision that rivals or exceeds much larger instruments. Dr. Chunhui Yao played a central role in bringing together the photonic design, system integration, and experimental validation that made this possible."
Its relatively simple construction could also make the technology easier to manufacture on a large scale, potentially bringing sophisticated optical measurements to devices where conventional spectrometers would be too bulky or expensive.
Bringing Laboratory-Grade Measurements to Everyday Devices
The researchers envision a future in which accurate optical sensing becomes a routine feature of everyday technology rather than something largely confined to specialized laboratories.
In industrial settings, inexpensive spectrometers could be installed throughout manufacturing facilities to continuously check material composition and product quality. Similar sensors could monitor food freshness, identify substances, and analyze environmental conditions on a much larger scale than is currently practical.
Healthcare could see equally significant changes. Compact sensors might eventually enable wearables to measure hydration levels, detect signs of alcohol intoxication, track biomarkers related to physical fitness, or continuously monitor glucose levels for people managing diabetes.
"Our vision is to make spectrometry as ubiquitous as temperature or motion sensing," added Prof. Qixiang Cheng. "This work shows that high-quality spectral information doesn't have to be confined to the laboratory -- it can be embedded directly into the technologies people use every day."
As photonic technology becomes smaller and more advanced, the convolutional spectrometer provides a promising example of how mathematical insights and practical engineering can make sophisticated scientific instruments simpler, cheaper, and more accessible. By combining high precision with a device that costs around $10, the researchers have opened a potential path toward a new generation of smart sensors capable of measuring the hidden chemistry of our bodies and surroundings.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Cambridge. Original written by Michael Shuff. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

articles.text:
Android 17 sur Nothing : les Phone (3a) et (4a) reçoivent une mise à jour anticipée
Bonne nouvelle pour les possesseurs de smartphones Nothing : le constructeur a décidé de déployer un peu en avance la nouvelle version de Nothing OS, permettant de profiter d'Android 17 et de multiples améliorations.
Nothing Phone (4a) Pro
Depuis plusieurs semaines, les mises à jour se multiplient chez les différents constructeurs de smartphones Android pour y apporter Android 17 via leurs différentes surcouches. Mais l'un d'eux était un peu à la traîne sur la concurrence, à savoir Nothing. C'est peut-être pour cela que le constructeur anglais semble avoir décidé de légèrement bousculer son calendrier de déploiement initial.
Nothing déploie Android 17 un peu en avance sur quatre appareils
En bêta depuis août dernier, la surcouche Nothing OS 5.0 basée sur Android 17 était initialement attendue pour début novembre sur de nombreux terminaux. Mais à en croire la mise en ligne récente de changelogs, le déploiement semble en cours pour les Phone 3a, Phone 3a Pro, Phone 4a et Phone 4a Pro. Le Nothing Phone 3 a déjà reçu la mise à jour.
Comme d'habitude, si la mise à jour ne vous est pas proposée automatiquement, direction Paramètres > Système > Mise à jour du système. Si toujours rien n'apparait, patience, cela ne devrait pas tarder.
De nombreuses nouveautés pour les smartphones Nothing
Outre les nouveautés apportées par Android 17, Nothing OS 5.0 est une mise à jour majeure à plus d'un titre. Visuellement tout d'abord, l'interface atypique de Nothing profite d'un bon coup de pinceau, adoptant un thème translucide glacé pour ses widgets et menus, une nouvelle police ou encore des icônes mises à jour. Des Paramètres repensés, des animations plus rapides et fluides ou encore plus d'options de personnalisation pour l'écran de verrouillage sont également là.
Les notifications et paramètres rapides peuvent désormais être séparés en deux panneaux comme c'est déjà le cas chez la plupart des concurrents, tandis que Nothing améliore la plupart de ses outils (nouveau Glyph Timer, contrôle Bluetooth plus rapide, nouveaux widgets Collector et Away Time...). L'appareil photo profite également d'enrichissements variés (effets, presets, interface…).
Pour les Phone 2a et Phone 2a Plus il faudra (normalement) attendre mi-novembre. Le Phone 3a Lite sera concerné lui fin décembre, tandis qu'il faudra attendre mi-janvier pour les Phone 4b et CMF Phone 2 Pro.

articles.title: Flock can't seem to take no for an answer, as its cameras reappear in another city that rejected them
articles.text:
A hot potato: It's fair to say that Flock is one of the most hated companies in the US right now. So, what better way to improve its public image than to ignore a city's instructions and reinstall two cameras when explicitly told not to – and it's not the first time this has happened.
The surveillance giant's latest PR disaster took place in Dayton, Minnesota, reports The Drive. The city's local government posted on Facebook that the Police Department was made aware of a maintenance work order produced by Flock on September 17, 2026.
The city notified Flock a day later, informing it that the program was on hold and no work orders were to be completed. But the company appeared to just ignore this, reinstalling its cameras and putting them into service.
Local residents spotted the cameras and informed police, who were directed to remove the devices.
In August, Dayton voted to cancel its contract with Flock, joining hundreds of US communities that have removed or stopped using the company's cameras.
Dayton City Administrator Zach Doud later said Flock took five days to acknowledge the city's contract cancellation and informed officials that removing its surveillance equipment would take 60 days.
This isn't the first time Flock has seemingly ignored a city's orders to remove its cameras. In September, Grass Valley, California, which had also canceled Flock's contract and removed its cameras, was shocked to find that two of them had been reinstalled.
Flock essentially blamed the city. It said the company handles the removal of the cameras as part of the cancellation process, but because the city took them down before the process was complete, the system assumed there was an equipment failure. This caused it to generate replacement work orders, resulting in crews being dispatched.
There have been numerous negative stories about Flock and its privacy-invading cameras since reports emerged that police officers were using its technology to stalk former partners, prompting cities to drop the cameras at a rapid pace.
But while you may see fewer Flock cameras lining the streets, the company's surveillance technology might instead be flying through the air. The company said in August that its Drone as First Responder, or DFR, tech – which can also read license plates from the air – is its fastest-growing segment. The aircraft can fly at 400 feet and reach 60 mph, while a 40x optical zoom allows operators to see details from a distance.

articles.title: Crean una pantalla táctil integrada en la ropa: puede reproducir videos y resistir hasta 50 lavados
articles.text:
Investigadores de la Universidad Nacional de Singapur (NUS) desarrollaron una pantalla táctil que puede integrarse directamente en la tela de una prenda de vestir. La tecnología permite mostrar imágenes, reproducir vídeos, utilizar aplicaciones sencillas y controlar algunas funciones mediante el contacto con los dedos, sin necesidad de llevar un celular o una pantalla adicional.
El prototipo fue incorporado en la manga de una prenda y también cuenta con sensores capaces de medir la temperatura corporal, detectar movimientos y ajustar automáticamente el brillo de la pantalla. El avance fue anunciado por la universidad el 22 de octubre, un día después de que la investigación se publicara en la revista científica Nature.
La propuesta busca combinar las funciones de los dispositivos electrónicos con la ropa de uso cotidiano. Aunque todavía se encuentra en fase experimental, sus desarrolladores consideran que podría tener aplicaciones en ámbitos como la salud, el deporte y el monitoreo de las condiciones físicas de las personas.
Cómo funciona la pantalla táctil integrada en la ropa
El equipo de investigación, dirigido por el profesor adjunto Tural Khudiyev, de la Facultad de Diseño e Ingeniería de la NUS, desarrolló fibras electrónicas especiales capaces de emitir luz y detectar el contacto de los usuarios.
Cada fibra tiene aproximadamente un milímetro de grosor e incorpora 96 pequeñas luces. Para construir la pantalla, los investigadores entrelazaron 54 de estas fibras hasta formar una superficie de aproximadamente 17 por 11 centímetros, integrada directamente en la manga de una prenda.
El resultado es una pantalla flexible que permite mostrar fotografías, reproducir vídeos, utilizar una calculadora y funcionar como brújula. También puede recibir imágenes desde otros dispositivos mediante una conexión Bluetooth y responder a comandos de voz.
Una de sus características principales es que admite múltiples puntos de contacto simultáneos. Esto significa que el usuario puede interactuar con la superficie textil utilizando los dedos, de manera similar a como lo haría con la pantalla de un smartphone.
Sin embargo, la calidad de imagen todavía está por debajo de la que ofrecen los celulares actuales. La investigación se concentra principalmente en demostrar que es posible integrar componentes electrónicos y funciones táctiles en un material flexible sin perder las propiedades habituales de una prenda.
Una pantalla que puede lavarse y doblarse
Uno de los principales desafíos de esta tecnología consiste en conseguir que los componentes electrónicos resistan las condiciones habituales de uso de la ropa. A diferencia de un teléfono o una tableta, una prenda está expuesta constantemente a movimientos, dobleces, humedad y lavados.
Para comprobar su resistencia, los investigadores sometieron el prototipo a 50 ciclos de lavado en una lavadora convencional con detergente. También realizaron 1.000 pruebas de doblado para evaluar si la estructura podía soportar deformaciones repetidas.
Según los resultados comunicados por la Universidad Nacional de Singapur, tanto el brillo de la pantalla como su sensibilidad táctil se mantuvieron prácticamente sin cambios después de las pruebas.
Además, el equipo comprobó que el tejido conservaba una transpirabilidad comparable con la de materiales textiles convencionales, como el algodón, el poliéster y la mezclilla. Este aspecto resulta importante porque una prenda tecnológica debe permitir que el usuario la lleve puesta sin generar las incomodidades asociadas a materiales rígidos o poco ventilados.
La ropa inteligente podría utilizarse para monitorear la salud
Más allá de mostrar imágenes y ejecutar funciones básicas, los investigadores consideran que la tecnología podría tener aplicaciones en el seguimiento de la salud. Los sensores integrados permiten recopilar información sobre la temperatura corporal y el movimiento, mientras que la propia pantalla ofrece una superficie para consultar esos datos.
“La atención médica es una aplicación particularmente prometedora”, explicó Khudiyev en el comunicado de la universidad. Según el investigador, una prenda podría recopilar información fisiológica de manera continua y permitir que el usuario interactúe con esos registros directamente desde la ropa.
La combinación con inteligencia artificial también podría ampliar sus posibilidades. En el futuro, estos sistemas podrían analizar los datos recopilados y ofrecer información personalizada sobre el estado físico de una persona. No obstante, estas aplicaciones todavía forman parte de las posibilidades que estudia el equipo y no de funciones comerciales disponibles.
Cuándo llegará al mercado la pantalla táctil textil
Por ahora, la pantalla desarrollada por la NUS es un prototipo de investigación. El equipo trabaja en mejorar la calidad de imagen, incorporar sensores más avanzados y añadir capacidades relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial.
La universidad no ha anunciado una fecha para su comercialización ni ha informado cuánto podría costar fabricar prendas con esta tecnología.
El desarrollo representa un avance en el campo de los textiles inteligentes, que busca incorporar sensores y componentes electrónicos en materiales utilizados habitualmente para fabricar ropa. Si consigue superar los desafíos de producción, podría abrir la puerta a prendas capaces de mostrar información, controlar dispositivos y monitorear variables físicas sin depender de una pantalla externa.

articles.title: Berlin’s Greentech Alliance to acquire Intermobility to connect mobility startups with investors and cities | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Greentech Alliance (GTA), a Berlin-based global connection network for sustainable technology businesses, has agreed to acquire Intermobility, a Paris-based transport and mobility network connecting more than 1,000 companies, public authorities, and ecosystem players.
The combined entity will span more than 5,000 members and partners across 25 countries on six continents. The network links climate investors, startups, corporates, and policymakers in one of Europe’s most challenging sectors to decarbonise.
“Europe does not have a mobility technology problem, it has a coordination problem. The capital, the startups and the cities are all there, but they rarely meet. Bringing Intermobility into Greentech Alliance puts the people who build, fund and buy mobility solutions in one network, and we are inviting investors and companies who want a seat at that table to join us,” said Charles Newton Price, CEO, Greentech Alliance.
The acquisition, whose financial terms were not disclosed, comes as Europe grapples with transport emissions that have remained stubbornly above 1990 levels and as startup funding continues to decline. According to the European Environment Agency, transport emissions were 25.3% above 1990 levels in 2023 and accounted for around 31% of total EU emissions.
Transport & Environment, a Brussels-based clean-transport advocacy group, estimates the sector needs €310 billion in annual investment by 2030 to meet climate targets. However, data from Via ID and Dealroom show European mobility startups closed 654 funding rounds in 2025, down from 785 the year before, raising $10.1 billion in total private funding. Greentech Alliance says the acquisition is designed to bridge this gap.
Founded in Berlin in May 2020 by Lubomila Jordanova, Simon Thies, Hannah Kromminga, and Jan-Jaap Verhoeve, Greentech Alliance is a curated global network for ventures, investors, educators and partners building what it describes as a more regenerative economy. The organisation is incorporated as both a Canadian not-for-profit and a German for-profit company.
It currently counts more than 3,000 community members and partners across six continents, including more than 700 investor members, and has facilitated more than 2,000 introductions.
Intermobility was founded in 2022 by François Hoehlinger as a European network of transport and mobility players spanning private companies and public institutions. By bringing Intermobility’s operators, cities and public authorities into the same network as GTA’s climate investors, startups, and corporates, the deal paves the way for a mobility solution to mature from pilot to scale.
For investors, GTA membership will now offer curated access to mobility ventures from both communities, alongside introductions to co-investors, corporates and public buyers. For companies. It opens direct channels to customers, pilots and capital across Europe and beyond.
The two organisations will also explore joint ventures and financing projects, including work linked to GTA’s Climate Zero programmes, subject to separate approval. Hoehlinger will join GTA’s board to help shape the Alliance’s direction as it scales internationally.
“Mobility only changes when founders, investors, operators and public authorities move together. Intermobility built that table in Europe. Greentech Alliance gives it international reach and access to capital, while keeping a grounded European perspective at its heart,” said Hoehlinger, founder, Intermobility.
Since its inception, GTA has successfully connected members on its network and with the acquisition of Intermobility, it has an opportunity to move beyond connection. Using its proven model of trusted introductions and curated membership, the alliance will aim to bridge the gap between climate solutions and funding shortfall.

articles.title: Bulletproof Host Virtualine Loses Its Domain to FBI Seizure
articles.text:
The FBI has seized virtualine.net, the domain of a Russian-speaking bulletproof hosting services provider associated with various cybercriminal operations.
According to court documents, Virtualine, also known as Secury, Massgod, Spamhouse, Lanedo, and Omegatech, has been hosting customers’ illicit services and helped them evade law enforcement takedown attempts.
In posts on cybercrime forums, Virtualine promoted support for various types of cybercriminal activity, including phishing, spam, carding, and more; advertised its ability to move customer services to unaffiliated infrastructure; and claimed it intentionally ignored abuse.
It also allowed users to post and sell explicit images and videos of minors and adults, and supported at least one customer that offered a hack-for-hire service aimed at stealing sexually explicit content from online accounts.
Despite receiving numerous takedown requests from law enforcement agencies in several countries, Virtualine continued to aid the customer and even helped them create a new website for uploading the illicit content. The provider continues to host the new website.
According to blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs, Virtualine has been used, among others, by ransomware groups and an infostealer operator.
“Virtualine received more illicit-attributed cryptocurrency than any other TRM-labeled bulletproof hosting provider, despite receiving less total value than several peers,” the company says.
The bulletproof hosting provider first emerged on the cybercrime forum Exploit in 2024, but claims to have been operating since 2019. It claimed to have had the largest collection of autonomous system numbers for malware and botnet hosting in 2025.
Most of the payments Virtualine’s labeled Bitcoin addresses have received came from a Russian drug marketplace (44%) and a large sextortion scheme (17%). A cryptocurrency mixer accounted for 13% of them and ransomware for 5%. In 2026, Virtualine also received payments from the StealC infostealer operators.
“A domain seizure disrupts how customers find and access a service. It does not, by itself, establish that the operator has stopped working, or that customers have lost access to all underlying infrastructure,” TRM notes.
