articles.title: Katzenkopf im Weltall: Diese Formation aus dem Carinanebel hat ein leuchtend rotes Auge
articles.text:
Nasa zeigt Katzenkopf im Weltall: Was es mit der Nebelformation auf sich hat
Der Carinanebel ist etwa 7.500 Lichtjahre von der Erde entfernt. Trotz der enormen Entfernung können Weltraumteleskope wie das Hubble- und das James-Webb-Teleskop solche Gegenden beobachten und davon atemberaubende Aufnahmen schießen. Das beweist jetzt auch ein Fund, den die Nasa in einem Beitrag näher erklärt und zeigt. Die Aufnahmen zeigen einen gigantischen Katzenkopf im All.
Katzenkopfnebel: So kam er womöglich zustande
Natürlich handelt es sich nicht um einen echten Katzenkopf, sondern um einen Nebel innerhalb des Carinanebels, der wie eine Katze geformt ist. Von der Position der Weltraumteleskope macht ein leuchtender Stern den Eindruck perfekt, da er genau an der Position des vermeintlichen Auges der Nebelkatze durchscheint. Die Aufnahmen des Hubble-Teleskops zeigen dabei Rückstände von Sauerstoff, Wasserstoff und Schwefel, während das James-Webb-Teleskop Infrarotaufnahmen liefert.
Der ungewöhnliche Nebel kommt laut Nasa durch ultraviolette Strahlung und Winde zustande. Während leichteres Material schnell abgetragen wird, verbleibt ein dichterer Nebel in Form eines Katzenkopfes. Aktuell trotz dieser noch den weiteren Abtragungen. Durch die Infrarotaufnahmen des James-Webb-Teleskops können die Forscher:innen aber auch hinter das Material schauen und dort das Licht zahlreicher Sterne einfangen.
Dazu zählt auch das vermeintliche Auge des Katzenkopfnebels. Die Nasa-Forscher:innen gehen aktuell davon aus, dass es sich um das Licht eines vergleichsweise jungen Sternes handelt, der womöglich teilweise in der Nebelwolke steckt. Durch die Aufnahmen erhoffen sich die Forscher:innen, mehr über die Sterne, aber auch über den „chaotischen und komplexen Prozess, der als Sternenentstehung bekannt ist“, zu lernen.

articles.title: South Korea clamps down on Tesla drivers for unlocking restricted full self-driving feature, $15,000 fines and prison possible sentences — suspects imported hardware from Europe and China, then traded tips on concealing activation logs
articles.text:
South Korea clamps down on Tesla drivers for unlocking restricted full self-driving feature, $15,000 fines and prison possible sentences — suspects imported hardware from Europe and China, then traded tips on concealing activation logs
Tesla’s FSD jailbreak crackdown comes with a $15,000 sting and possible prison time
South Korean authorities have identified 80 Tesla drivers who allegedly forced Full Self-Driving (FSD) onto cars that were never cleared for it, Electrek reports. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency says it confiscated 21 of the devices used to switch the feature on. The unlock modules reportedly connect to the car’s CAN bus (the internal network that links its electronic control units) and get around the regional software lock that keeps FSD disabled. That works because Tesla builds the same computer into every car, whether or not the feature is approved locally.
Some suspects bought ready-made units from Europe and China, and one reportedly plugged a European-made module into his own Tesla. Others skipped the shopping. One suspect, an IT worker, built his device using information he found on GitHub, which suggests the barrier to entry for this kind of modification is lower than it sounds. The group also traded tips online, including how to stop the car from keeping any record that FSD had been activated. Concealing the activation history is likely an attempt to avoid detection by Tesla, which has been looking for these devices itself.
Then there is the legal risk, where prosecutors are using the Motor Vehicle Management Act, which bans unauthorized software changes that could affect vehicle safety. In Korea, the maximum penalty is two years in prison or a fine of up to 20 million won, or roughly $15,000, a steep price for a driver-assistance feature that many of these owners had already paid for.
South Korea’s transport ministry first flagged suspicious activations to police in April. “Safety risks were confirmed, including the possibility that FSD may fail to properly recognize driving conditions or operate differently from the driver’s intentions,” a police official said then.
Notably, the root of the problem is a certification gap. Tesla began offering FSD (Supervised) in South Korea in late 2025, but only on US-built Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck units, which skip local safety certification under the Korea-US free trade agreement. The Model 3 and Model Y arrive from Giga Shanghai and have yet to pass. Nobody agrees on how many Korean Teslas are eligible, although Carisyou Data Lab figures cited by MK last month indicate 47,458 of 229,311 cars (20.7%).
The South Korean investigation follows Tesla’s own efforts to stop unauthorized activation. In April, the company began remotely detecting unlock devices and disabling FSD access on affected vehicles. It has also warned owners that unauthorized modifications could void warranty coverage and leave them liable for crashes. Moreover, the restrictions are not the first time Tesla’s software protections have come under scrutiny. In August 2023, researchers exploited a hardware security flaw in the AMD processor powering Tesla’s media control unit to unlock certain paid features. The exploit targeted the car’s AMD-based system-on-chip, although researchers did not confirm that every premium feature could be unlocked.
Tesla has also faced regulatory scrutiny over software restrictions. In December 2021, the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration investigated the company after an over-the-air update allowed drivers to play certain games while their vehicles were moving. The case highlighted how software changes can raise safety concerns when features are accessible under conditions regulators consider unsafe. Hardware reliability is another challenge for Tesla. Last year, the company detailed how it identifies defective processor cores in its Dojo AI supercomputers, where a single faulty component can compromise lengthy training runs.

articles.title: Canada to join European supercomputer program, collaborate on tech priorities
articles.text:
Canada will gain access to a European supercomputer program and align upcoming real-time payment systems as the Canadian government forges closer ties with Europe on a broad array of issues, including the digital economy.
The Destination Earth program is “one of Europe’s most strategic data assets.”
Henna Virkkunen
European Commission
Prime Minister Mark Carney and the European Commission announced their intention to work together on several economic and trade priorities on Friday, through a so-called “Alliance for the Future.” In addition to collaborating on energy exports, defence contracts, and student exchange programs, Canada and Europe are partnering to share access to supercomputing infrastructure—high in demand in the age of AI—and to work on digital climate modelling.
Canada has joined the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking, a network of compute infrastructure that includes 14 supercomputers, 10 quantum computers, and 19 “AI factories” across Europe. Researchers and businesses in Canada will be able to apply to access JUPITER, a powerful supercomputer located in Germany, the government said.
“It means access to a compute power no one can build alone,” AI and digital innovation minister Evan Solomon said at the announcement in Montréal on Friday.
Canada is also building its own public AI supercomputer under an $890-million program. The government hasn’t yet announced which non-profit, post-secondary institution, or consortium will be selected to lead the project. Solomon said this would come “early in the new year.”
In an interview with BetaKit, the minister indicated that Canada would be open to having its new supercomputer be part of the European network once it’s built.
Another project Canada will contribute to is Destination Earth, a climate modelling initiative by the European Commission that aims to develop a digital twin of the Earth. With highly accurate geographical data, the European Union-funded project could offer tools to predict extreme weather events and inform policy to adapt to the effects of climate change.
“This is one of Europe’s most strategic data assets,” said Henna Virkkunen, the European Commission’s executive vice-president for tech sovereignty, security and democracy.
Several other items outlined in Carney’s announcement concerned the tech sector. Canada and Europe said they would take the first steps toward a new transatlantic data cable that would “give Canada and Europe a direct, secure route for rapid data exchange” and for internet traffic. Currently, roughly 80 percent of Canada’s internet traffic gets routed through the US, according to the Centre for International Governance Innovation.
On payments technology, the announcement said the European Commission would support connecting instant payment systems to allow Canadians and Europeans to send money instantly. After years of delay, Canada’s Real-Time Rail system is still forthcoming but expected to launch a first phase this fall.
Officials considering AI regulatory body
On day one of the Canada-EU Summit on Thursday, Canada announced it was taking a financial stake in Toronto AI company Cohere, which is partnering with and effectively acquiring Germany’s AI leader Aleph Alpha. The further alignment on tech comes as the Canadian government has floated the idea of spearheading a “technology stability board,” akin to the Financial Stability Board, to regulate AI models internationally.
While Solomon said there were several ways such a body might come into being—through G7 or G20 countries, for example—he told BetaKit there is a “profound, shared interest that Canada and the EU have to make sure that citizens are safe, and that frontier models…are regulated to keep our critical infrastructure safe.”
Virkkunen added that Europe already has the AI Act, which it has begun to enforce this year.
“The challenge is that we don’t have these kinds of rules internationally, but the risks are very global,” she said.
Feature image courtesy Madison McLauchlan for BetaKit.

articles.title: Sam Altman says it’s better for RAM to be in a data center than on your desk
articles.text:
Asked about supply chain shortages, like the ongoing RAM shortage, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in an interview that it’s “terrible” to have RAM in personal PCs instead of data centers. During his appearance on the Cheeky Pint podcast, where he also commented on AI’s impact on math, Altman said:
Sam Altman says it’s better for RAM to be in a data center than on your desk
As OpenAI’s buying spree squeezes the world’s supply of RAM, its CEO explains why he needs so much.
“A lot of people want local inference. And somehow, they assume that the problem is solved now because we are going to have open-source models, we’re going to be able to run them on our computers, and so we’re not going to need all the stuff in the data center.
But from a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used five percent of the time.
You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you’re trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment. And somehow everyone’s— many people’s intuition is the opposite of that.”
Whether Altman meant your gaming PC or developers working with something like the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box or the new touchscreen MacBook Pro, the outcome is the same. Right now, memory companies Samsung and SK Hynix have long term deals with cloud service operators and projects like OpenAI’s Stargate that have reserved much of the world’s RAM output over the next few years. And the billions they’re willing to lay out for chips is why the laptops, phones, and other tech you use are getting more expensive right now.

articles.title: Hubble a une chance sur deux de s'écraser d'ici 2033, alors la Nasa cherche un plan de sauvetage - Numerama
articles.text:
Hubble travaille toujours, mais il y a un problème : le télescope descend. S’il n’est pas menacé à très court terme, l’observatoire spatial voit en revanche son horizon s’assombrir dans les années à venir. Une analyse datée de juillet 2026 évalue même le risque d’une chute vers la Terre à une chance sur dix en septembre 2032 et une sur deux avant décembre 2033.
Perdre Hubble ne serait pas seulement la mort d’un symbole de l’aventure spatiale, ce serait aussi une terrible perte pour la communauté scientifique. L’engin reçoit en effet sept fois plus de demandes d’observation qu’il ne peut en traiter, malgré son ancienneté notable. Le télescope a été lancé en 1990, soit plus de 35 ans.
C’est dans ce contexte que la question d’une mission d’assistance s’est de nouveau posée dernièrement. Le centre Goddard de la Nasa, qui s’occupe de l’observatoire, a publié une demande d’informations, c’est-à-dire un appel à idées, sans engagement. Objectif : recenser les industriels pouvant proposer une solution pour remonter Hubble en orbite.
Cette sollicitation a été repérée le 29 octobre par Irene Klotz, rédactrice au sein de la revue Aviation Week.
Pousser, réparer ou faire tomber proprement Hubble
Dans le document de la Nasa, trois pistes sont proposées : la première est la capture de Hubble pour le hisser au-delà de 600 kilomètres d’altitude ; la seconde est une mission d’entretien pour prolonger sa vie ; la troisième se présente sous la forme d’une rentrée atmosphérique contrôlée. Et, donc, de la fin du satellite.
Quel que soit le chemin retenu, le lancement doit avoir lieu d’ici 2032. Pour les deux premiers scénarios, il s’agira de ne pas abîmer le télescope, pour qu’il puisse encore opérer le temps imparti. Goddard fournira les données techniques. Le lanceur, le vaisseau et l’éventuel équipage restent à la charge de l’industriel.
Ce n’est évidemment pas si simple. On l’a vu avec la tentative de la mission LINK qui devait venir en aide au télescope Swift, qui lui aussi connaît une lente mais inexorable chute vers la Terre. Un petit robot aurait dû rejoindre Swift, s’agripper à lui et le remonter. Hélas, les choses ne se sont pas bien passées et Swift est désormais perdu.
L’idée d’une mission de sauvetage ne date pas d’hier.
En 2022, la Nasa et SpaceX avaient étudié une mission Crew Dragon. En juin 2024, l’agence l’a refusée, jugeant le risque trop élevé pour le télescope. Le 1er juin 2026, devant un comité consultatif, Shawn Domagal-Goldman, directeur de la division astrophysique de la Nasa, s’est dit ouvert à un rehaussement de l’orbite, à condition que les coûts de fonctionnement de Hubble baissent.
Cette demande d’informations ne vaut pas commande, mais cela donnera à la Nasa du grain à moudre pour la suite. La Nasa prévoit de lancer un appel d’offres formel une fois les réponses des industriels analysées. Il ne faudra cependant pas trop tarder, car la mise en route industrielle d’une telle mission prendra des mois.

articles.title: C’est déjà le Black Friday chez Boulanger : le Samsung Galaxy S25 FE s’affiche avec 250€ de moins sur le site
articles.text:
Avec son grand écran AMOLED et son équipement photo polyvalent, le Samsung Galaxy S25 FE se présente comme un smartphone attractif, surtout si l’on tient compte de la remise de 250 € dont il bénéficie chez Boulanger pour le lancement du Black Friday.
Boulanger n’a pas de temps à perdre : le Black Friday a déjà démarré sur le site de l’enseigne. Parmi les premières offres intéressantes, on trouve celle qui concerne le smartphone Samsung Galaxy S25 FE de 128 Go, disponible à 499 € au lieu de 749 €. Ce modèle équipé d’un processeur Exynos 2400 et de 8 Go de RAM se destine aux utilisateurs en quête d’un mobile polyvalent et abordable sous Android 16.
Le Samsung Galaxy S25 FE 128 Go est à 499 € au lieu de 749 € au lancement du Black Friday chez Boulanger.
Pourquoi choisir le Samsung Galaxy S25 FE ?
- Pour son grand écran : la dalle AMOLED de 6,7 pouces à 120 Hz est idéale pour lire, regarder des séries et naviguer.
- Pour son zoom optique : le téléobjectif 3x complète le capteur principal de 50 mégapixels et l’ultra grand-angle.
- Pour son suivi logiciel : Samsung prévoit sept générations de mises à jour du système et sept ans de correctifs de sécurité, à compter du lancement du modèle.
Un smartphone confortable pour les loisirs et la photo
L’écran AMOLED de 6,7 pouces qui équipe le Galaxy S25 FE est son premier atout. Il offre une surface d’affichage généreuse pour regarder des vidéos, surfer sur les réseaux sociaux et utiliser de nombreuses applications, dont des jeux mobiles. Côté photo, on trouve trois capteurs de 50, 12 et 8 mégapixels. La qualité des prises de vue en extérieur fait partie des points forts relevés au sein de notre test, qui accorde la note de 8 sur 10 au Samsung Galaxy S25 FE. Sa batterie de 4 900 mAh accepte une recharge filaire jusqu’à 45 W, mais l’adaptateur secteur est vendu séparément.
Une porte d’entrée dans la gamme Galaxy S
À 499 €, le Galaxy S25 FE se présente comme une porte d’entrée abordable au sein de la gamme Samsung Galaxy S. Son téléobjectif et ses fonctions Galaxy AI sont notamment appréciables. En revanche, il embarque une puce Exynos 2400 moins puissante que le Snapdragon 8 Elite des Galaxy S25 et S25+, ce qui le rend notamment moins adapté aux jeux mobiles les plus gourmands avec les réglages poussés au maximum.
✅ Les points forts
- Écran AMOLED de 6,7 pouces à 120 Hz.
- Téléobjectif avec zoom optique 3x.
- Suivi logiciel longue durée annoncé par Samsung.
❌ Les limites
- Stockage de 128 Go non extensible.
- SoC vieillissant.
Boulanger fait passer le prix du Samsung Galaxy S25 FE de 749 € à 499 € à l’occasion du Black Friday.
Si vous disposez d’un budget de moins de 500 € et que vous désirez changer de smartphone pour un modèle Samsung récent, alors le Samsung Galaxy S25 FE de 128 Go pourrait bien correspondre à ce que vous recherchez.
En revanche, les amateurs de petits smartphones, de stockage abondant ou les joueurs souhaitant pousser les réglages au maximum devraient se mettre à la recherche d’un terminal un peu plus adapté à leurs besoins. Après tout, le Black Friday ne fait que commencer.

articles.title: OPINION: You can’t scale with a startup mindset | EU-Startups
articles.text:
The best advice once your company achieves product-market fit? Don’t get stuck on things that got you there, keep adjusting your architecture and workflow to fit your new realities and sizes.
Starting strong is one thing, but the real point is pushing past the growth ceiling without crashing: McKinsey found 78% of products launched successfully only to fail later on. Having worked in international expansion, I have seen how the practices that help a startup gain traction can cause troubles as it grows. Here is my top-5 of what’s better to be changed once a company is too big for a startup mode, and what habits are worth keeping in mind.
Money moves faster than decisions
Congratulations, it’s been your big funding round. Having more capital can feel like you have almost unlimited freedom to chase everything at once. This money mostly goes to ideas that already work, more on tests, all at once. In a ten-person startup, the founder knows every ongoing experiment. In a 100-person company, nobody does. Tests overlap, compete for the same target audience, and rarely get switched off. Meanwhile, decision-making slows down as more people have something to say. More money won’t fix messy operations, it just makes the mistakes more expensive.
The Turkish quick-commerce company Getir expanded to nine countries by the end of 2021 and bought Berlin rival Gorillas for €1.13 billon ($1.2 billion) in December 2022. Yet, in a few years the company chose to exit Germany, the UK and the Netherlands to focus back on its core Turkish business. Having enough money to go global doesn’t automatically mean it’s the right move. Sustainable scaling requires strong research: diving into local consumer behavior, understanding specific market nuances, and adapting your model to what local buyers actually want.
To grow without burning capital, build a fixed and transparent framework of your experiments: a single log where every project has one owner, a set budget, a clear deadline, and kill criteria agreed before launch. Each ongoing test should be backed by a specific hypothesis and (ideally) data. If an experiment went great in one market, don’t hurry to move forward – assess whether the conditions that made it work still apply in other regions.
Customer behaviour, channel preferences, and acquisition costs vary from country to country, so goals need to be tailored to actual team capacity and adapted market by market.
Hiring and ownership need a system
In a startup mode, team members do everything at once, no matter the difficulty level. Quite often, juniors jump in wherever they’re needed, keep going, and naturally become team leads. Loyalty is important, but management requires a different skillset. Wharton professor Peter Cappelli points out that top individual contributors who get promoted often make the weakest managers.
The same applies at the executive level. When founders are responsible for each new decision, they’re likely to slow down processes in their own business. Getting advice and seeing fresh perspectives from someone who has their own area of responsibility creates a clear structure with solid boundaries.
Bringing in senior leadership only works if you fix how responsibility is assigned. As headcount grows, each person assumes someone else is handling it. Psychologists call this diffusion of responsibility. Every project needs one named owner with the authority to execute, and clear processes for who decides and who reports progress. If a project has two owners, in practice, it has none.
AI will not replace everyone
Every company that’s actively growing now feels pressure to automate more and hire less. But implementation itself is a huge project, and for plenty of everyday tasks, a skilled person is still faster, cheaper, and far less painful to manage.
In May 2025, Klarna backtracked their earlier beliefs that AI has a potential to replace human work. A bit more than a year earlier, the company paused hiring customer service agents in favour of their AI assistant. The bot took 75% of the company’s customer chats in more than 35 languages. It sounded high-potential at first, but then there was: lower quality of support. Klarna began recruiting human agents again, while AI keeps handling simpler requests.
The point is to define for your business when to use AI, and when human touch is a super power. Everything repetitive and predictable can go to the AI team, and situations that win from empathy and critical thinking, are better left for people. The next step is to start educating your team to make sure they’re staying flexible and are using modern solutions for the new way of living.
AI is way more than just right prompting. Show employees how they can make their own simple tools for their daily workflows – through online courses, internal bootcamps, hackathons, or any other solutions that work best for your business. Developers can then turn the most promising ideas into advanced solutions.
Plan beyond the next quarter
Startups live month-over-month. Meanwhile, scaling needs a longer horizon, with a solid six-month and a year plan, all while maintaining a flexible approach. Your core metrics have to evolve, too.
A longer perspective also offers you a unique view of which temporary fixes no longer work and need to be redone in favour of a stronger infrastructure. Spreadsheets and manual workarounds are fine at a hundred orders a day, not at a hundred thousand. A McKinsey survey revealed that about 30% of CIOs said more than 20% of their new-product budget is diverted to fixing tech debt.
To keep everything aligned, run a strategy session every six months. On a more routine basis, make it a norm to have bi-weekly leadership syncs to review progress, track unit economics, and adjust tactics before small operational cracks can turn into a real problem.
Growth makes centralisation a necessity
As you grow, your operational architecture has to go through changes, including a call on what stays central and what lives in-market. Having worked in international expansion, I’ve seen how companies hit a ceiling when they try to manage global growth from two extreme ends: either micro-managing every local solution or letting regional teams operate like separate startups.
Core product decisions, CRM, brand guidelines, and customer support standards require consistency, so they are best managed centrally. Where you can really leave room for local teams is in what they know best: local landscape, relationships and competitors, regional traditions, preferences, and behaviors. The real challenge here is finding the right balance. Centralization cuts out messy duplication and keeps your brand cohesive, but excessive control from the top will blindside you to market-specific realities.
Scale up, but keep the best of the startup mindset. Stay adaptable. Keep testing (but make it wisely and don’t waste resources). Count money the way you did when there was very little of it, because the budget is never infinite, no matter how big the last round was.

articles.title: When the Internet Drops Mid-Shift: Backup Connections and Failover for Small Offices - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Critical Role of Internet Connectivity in Small Offices
In today’s fast-paced business environment, reliable internet connectivity is no longer a luxury but a fundamental necessity, especially for small offices. These businesses often depend heavily on cloud-based applications, VoIP phone systems, video conferencing, and real-time communication tools that require continuous internet access to function effectively. When the internet unexpectedly drops mid-shift, it can disrupt workflows, delay customer service, and ultimately impact revenue and reputation.
Recent studies reveal that 35% of small businesses experience internet outages several times a year, with each outage lasting an average of four hours. This kind of downtime can lead to significant losses, not only in employee productivity but also in customer satisfaction and trust. Moreover, 60% of small businesses that suffer a major data loss or extended downtime close within six months. These statistics underscore how critical it is for small offices to prepare for unexpected internet disruptions.
Understanding Backup Connections and Failover Systems
To mitigate the risks associated with internet downtime, small offices must implement robust backup connections and failover solutions. A backup connection is a secondary internet link that automatically activates when the primary connection fails. Failover systems are designed to monitor the health of the primary connection continuously and switch to the backup without manual intervention, ensuring seamless business continuity.
For example, a local business like Lakeside Motors for BMW Vehicles understands the importance of maintaining constant communication with customers and suppliers. By having a failover system in place, they avoid potential revenue losses and maintain service quality even during internet outages. This proactive approach ensures that critical operations such as order processing, customer support, and internal communications remain uninterrupted.
Failover technology can be as simple as a router configured to switch to a cellular network when the primary broadband fails, or as advanced as multi-WAN load balancing systems that distribute traffic across multiple connections for both redundancy and performance improvements.
Types of Backup Internet Connections
Small offices have several viable options when it comes to backup internet connections, each with its own advantages and limitations:
– DSL or Cable as Primary, Cellular as Backup: Many small businesses use a fixed broadband connection as their primary internet source and a cellular connection via 4G or 5G as backup. Cellular failover is popular due to its ease of setup, mobility, and widespread coverage. It provides an automatic switch during outages, minimizing disruption.
– Dual Broadband Connections: Some offices opt for two broadband providers, such as cable and fiber, to eliminate dependence on a single ISP. This approach lowers the risk of simultaneous outages since each provider typically uses different physical infrastructure.
– Satellite Internet: Although satellite connections have higher latency and can be affected by weather conditions, they serve as an emergency backup in remote or rural areas where terrestrial options are limited or unavailable.
– Fixed Wireless Access (FWA): This option uses radio signals to provide internet service and can be a reliable backup in areas with good line-of-sight to a wireless tower.
Each option comes with trade-offs regarding speed, reliability, latency, and cost. For instance, while cellular backup is convenient, data caps and variable speeds may limit its use during prolonged outages. Small businesses should evaluate their specific operational needs, budget constraints, and geographic location when selecting a backup solution.
The Importance of Professional IT Support
Implementing and managing backup connections and failover systems can be complex and requires technical expertise to ensure they function correctly when needed. Many small offices lack the in-house IT resources to design, configure, and maintain these solutions effectively. This is where professional IT services become invaluable.
For instance, InfoTECH for Lafayette businesses offers managed IT services tailored for businesses in Lafayette, providing continuous monitoring, rapid response to connectivity issues, and regular failover testing. Partnering with such providers ensures that failover systems are properly configured, tested regularly, and updated as technology evolves, substantially reducing the risk of unexpected downtime.
Professional IT support can also help small offices assess their network vulnerabilities, recommend the most cost-effective backup solutions, and provide training to staff on best practices during outages. This partnership enables businesses to focus on their core operations without worrying about internet reliability.
Cost Considerations and Return on Investment (ROI)
While the upfront costs of backup internet connections and failover equipment might seem significant, the return on investment (ROI) often justifies the expenditure. According to a Gartner study, the average cost of network downtime for small businesses is approximately $8,000 per hour. Avoiding even a single extended outage can save substantial amounts of money.
Additionally, uninterrupted internet service improves customer trust and satisfaction, which are critical for small businesses competing in crowded markets. Reliable connectivity also enhances employee productivity by minimizing frustration and downtime. These intangible benefits can lead to increased customer retention, positive word-of-mouth, and new business opportunities.
When calculating ROI, businesses should consider both direct costs, such as lost sales and labor, and indirect costs, including damage to brand reputation and employee morale. Investing in backup internet and failover solutions is a strategic move to protect against these risks.
Best Practices for Backup Internet and Failover Implementation
To maximize the benefits of backup connections, small offices should follow these best practices:
- Assess Bandwidth Needs: Determine the minimum bandwidth required during failover to maintain essential operations. This ensures that the backup connection can handle critical applications like VoIP calls, email, and cloud access.
- Choose Diverse Providers: Avoid using ISPs that share the same physical infrastructure to reduce the risk of simultaneous outages caused by cable cuts or local disruptions.
- Regular Testing: Schedule periodic failover tests to ensure automatic switching works correctly and that staff know how to respond during outages.
- Monitor Network Health: Use monitoring tools that provide real-time alerts on connection status, enabling proactive troubleshooting before issues escalate.
- Plan for Scalability: As the business grows, ensure that backup solutions can accommodate increased internet usage without compromising performance.
- Secure Failover Connections: Implement security measures such as firewalls and VPNs on backup connections to protect sensitive data during failover.
- Document Procedures: Maintain clear documentation of failover configurations and response protocols accessible to IT staff and relevant employees.
Additional Considerations for Small Offices
Beyond technology, small offices should consider the human factor in managing internet disruptions. Training employees on contingency plans during outages can reduce panic and confusion. For example, staff can be instructed on how to switch to alternative communication channels or access offline resources.
Moreover, reviewing and updating internet service contracts can sometimes provide options for service level agreements (SLAs) that guarantee minimum uptime or faster repair times. Engaging with ISPs about these options can provide additional peace of mind.
Finally, staying informed about emerging technologies such as 5G and software-defined WAN (SD-WAN) can offer new opportunities for more resilient and flexible network architectures in the near future.
Conclusion
Internet outages can severely disrupt small office operations, but with strategic planning and the right technology, businesses can safeguard against downtime. Backup internet connections and failover systems provide a safety net that keeps workflows running smoothly, even when the unexpected occurs.
By understanding available options, leveraging professional IT support, and investing wisely, small offices can protect their productivity and reputation. In an era where connectivity is king, being prepared for internet disruptions is essential for any business aiming to thrive.
Ensuring your small office has a robust backup and failover strategy is not just a technical decision-it’s a business imperative that supports growth, customer satisfaction, and long-term success.

articles.title: India needs a digital goods marketplace and control of its distribution layer, say Indus Appstore and Eloelo
articles.text:
India needs a digital goods marketplace and control of its distribution layer, say Indus Appstore and Eloelo
Priya Narasimhan of Indus Appstore and Sagar Gaonkar of Eloelo Group argued that India’s next 500 million users will come through AI-ready, locally priced platforms, and that sovereignty must extend beyond chips and models to app distribution, billing and data.
India’s app-first economy still lacks a thriving marketplace for digital goods, and fixing that is as much a question of sovereignty as of technology, according to speakers at the 17th edition of YourStory’s TechSparks.
Speaking on a panel titled “India’s digital economy 2.0: Public tech, AI sovereignty, and the next 500 million”, Priya Narasimhan, Chief Business Officer at Indus Appstore, said the country’s mobile-first habits should have produced a large digital goods market, but have not. She blamed distribution monopolies held by Google and Apple and the economics of their 15% to 30% billing commissions, which make lower-priced digital products unviable. Web stores, the other route, suffer from user friction and low reach, she said.
Narasimhan argued that digital sovereignty is about how and where consumers meet technology. She named three layers India must control: discovery and distribution through app marketplaces, monetisation and billing, and a data trust and consent framework. She pointed to the Epic Games and Google dispute in the US as proof of what happens when developers depend on gatekeepers. She stressed, however, that sovereignty does not mean rebuilding every base layer. The aim, she said, is to plug into global technology on India’s terms.
Sagar Gaonkar, CTO of Eloelo Group, said India’s strengths lie in its data, its cultural variety and its creative and platform-building talent. Chips and large language models can be built upon, he said, with value added for India and then exported. He added that security cannot be an afterthought as more tools are hosted outside the country.
On AI, Gaonkar said it helps microdrama platforms decide what to greenlight before a frame is shot, and personalise what viewers see. He also pointed to stories that adapt to a viewer’s preferences. Narasimhan said app stores must become hybrid platforms: simple and familiar on the surface for most Indians, and addressable by AI agents at the back end, so that developers can scale whether users tap an icon or ask a chatbot.
Both speakers challenged the idea that Bharat is a low-spending audience. Narasimhan recalled that PhonePe’s gold category scaled only after it allowed purchases of Rs 10 a day. Gaonkar said Indian users are value-conscious rather than unwilling to pay, and need a softer landing to experience a product before paying. Narasimhan also urged founders to talk to users rather than rely only on analytics.
Responding to audience questions, Narasimhan said Indus aims to cut the commission burden on developers, and rejected the suggestion that Indians do not value digital goods, citing microdramas, OTT and gaming. She said platforms should not let discovery become purely pay-to-play. On fraudulent installs, she said vetting combines automated checks with human review and constant monitoring, but admitted that no system is foolproof.

articles.title: Piratage de Binance : plus de 6 milliards de dollars de cryptos ont été volés, que s’est-il passé ?
articles.text:
Dans la soirée du jeudi 29 octobre, des pirates ont siphonné les portefeuilles de Binance, la plus grande plateforme d’échange de cryptomonnaies au monde, sur la blockchain. Binance estime le préjudice à 6,3 milliards de dollars, soit près de 5,5 milliards d’euros. C’est quatre fois plus que le précédent hack record, à savoir le vol de 1,5 milliard de dollars chez Bybit en février 2025.
« Un potentiel problème de sécurité »
D’après les investigations de la société d’analyse TRM Labs, les pirates sont passés à l’action vers 21 heures, heure de Paris. Les cybercriminels ont vidé les portefeuilles de Binance connectés à Internet. En une vingtaine de minutes, tous les fonds ont été transférés vers des adresses crypto contrôlées par les pirates. Dans un premier temps, Binance s’est montré prudent en indiquant avoir « connaissance de signalements concernant un potentiel problème de sécurité ». L’exchange s’engageait alors à mener une enquête. Changpeng Zhao, le fondateur de la plateforme, parle rapidement de la possibilité d’une « cyberattaque contre Binance ».
 Binance’s initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified.
The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B. We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far.
Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. User funds are safe. We will also publish an updated Proof of Reserves once the remediation is complete.
As an immediate precaution, Binance has:
– temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks are completed;
– revoked the affected address authorisation;
– engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds.
Our teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly. We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice.
Please rely only on official Binance channels for updates. Please feel free to contact Binance Customer Support if you have any further questions.
https://t.co/ywB2mKFy0p
— Binance (@binance) October 30, 2026
À lire aussi : 351 millions de dollars de cryptos dérobées – la plateforme Bitget a été piratée par des hackers nord-coréens
Trois milliards de dollars gelés
Face à la cyberattaque qui frappe Binance, tout l’écosystème crypto s’est rapidement mobilisé. Tether, l’émetteur du stablecoin USDT, parvient à bloquer environ 1,56 milliard de dollars volés par les truands. Circle, l’émetteur de l’USDC, gèle quant à lui plus de 800 millions. L’objectif est d’empêcher les pirates d’exfiltrer les fonds sur des mixeurs, des outils qui vont mélanger les cryptos de façon à ce que Binance en perde la trace.
De son côté, Binance assure d’abord que les fonds de ses clients sont « totalement à l’abri », avant de promettre qu’il couvrira « toutes les pertes ». Dos au mur, l’exchange finit par suspendre tous les dépôts et les retraits, avant de confirmer une perte de 6,3 milliards de dollars. Trois milliards d’entre eux ont pu être gelés avant qu’il ne soit trop tard.
Binance découvre rapidement que l’attaque repose sur un ordinateur portable compromis, appartenant à un ingénieur chargé de l’infrastructure informatique. Les pirates se sont servis de la machine vulnérable pour accéder à un service interne de Binance. De fil en aiguille, ils ont pu lancer des retraits non autorisés sur les portefeuilles.
« Cela met en évidence à quel point la sécurité d’une plateforme financière dépend des appareils du quotidien et des personnes y ayant accès, ainsi que de la technologie protégeant ses portefeuilles », souligne Marijus Briedis, responsable chez NordVPN, dans une réaction adressée à 01net.
Bonne nouvelle, Binance n’a trouvé « aucune preuve de fuite de clés privées depuis les portefeuilles ». En clair, les pirates n’ont pas volé les clés des coffres, ce qui limite les dégâts.
À lire aussi : Crypto-crime – pourquoi 2025 a pulvérisé tous les records
La Corée du Nord à l’origine de la cyberattaque
Les chercheurs de TRM Labs attribuent le vol « avec une confiance élevée » à TraderTraitor, un gang lié à la Corée du Nord. Rattaché au groupe Lazarus, le gang est déjà accusé d’être à l’origine du casse de Bybit l’année dernière. Il est aussi soupçonné d’avoir piraté la plateforme Bitget en septembre. C’est également l’avis de l’enquêteur ZachXBT, qui a découvert qu’une même adresse est exploitée par les hackers de Bitget et ceux de Binance.
Binance promet de rembourser l’intégralité des pertes des utilisateurs. Les investisseurs sont couverts par SAFU, le fonds d’urgence de la plateforme, mis en place dans le sillage de la chute de FTX en 2022. Désormais, « les fonds des utilisateurs sont en sécurité », insiste la plateforme. Les dépôts sont d’ailleurs de nouveau ouverts. Toutefois, les retraits sont toujours bloqués, mais ils devraient reprendre dans les 48 heures.

articles.title: Una gran explosión sacude la fábrica de municiones más antigua de España, en Granada, en plena fiebre del rearme
articles.text:
Una explosión en el quemadero de la Fábrica de Municiones de Granada ha hecho temblar esta mañana el barrio de El Fargue, en Granada. Como si fuera un terremoto, los vecinos llamaron al 112 en una treintena de ocasiones y la planta, que emplea a unas 260 personas, fue desalojada y se llenó de especialistas. Granada Digital informaba de al menos cinco heridos, dos por problemas auditivos y tres por heridas leves.
El grupo CSG, propietario de FMG, ha situado la explosión en la zona de desmilitarización de la fábrica, donde se elimina munición antigua, dañada o inutilizable. La empresa tampoco espera que el accidente tenga consecuencias a largo plazo sobre la actividad de la planta. Porque sí, son proveedores clave en la Guerra de Rusia contra Ucrania, un conflicto bélico que se remonta a 2014, tras las protestas contra el presidente Víktor Yanukóvich.
Los hechos. A las 8:58 de este viernes, el 112 empezó a recibir llamadas por una explosión en El Fargue, el barrio granadino donde se levanta la Fábrica de Municiones de Granada (FMG). Fueron una treintena. El estallido se produjo en el quemadero, la zona donde se destruyen restos de pólvora y explosivos, y vecinos de otros barrios sintieron un temblor semejante al de un seísmo. Al filo de las 9:30 de la mañana ya estaban por allí la Policía Nacional, operativos de los Tedax, Seguridad Ciudadana, Policía Judicial, Científica y de Subsuelo.
Diecisiete días antes. Recordemos también que el 13 de octubre un camión de la fábrica perdió granadas de mortero. Fue en la carretera del barrio. La Junta activó entonces la preemergencia, la policía apuntó a una carga mal sujeta y la empresa abrió una investigación interna.
Y ya ves las fotos: tras la explosión se levantó una columna de humo, se declaró un pequeño fuego en el monte y se estableció un perímetro de seguridad de varios kilómetros. Entretanto, la planta fue desalojada. Varios trabajadores recibieron atención por problemas de oído, sin que se registraran heridos graves. Y la causa está en investigación. Una de las primeras versiones apunta a una quema controlada que se habría ido de madre, aunque no está confirmado.
Qué se fabrica en El Fargue. LA FMG Granada Company es actualmente un fabricante integral de propelentes, cargas propulsoras de una y dos bases, produce pólvora, granadas de mortero y munición de artillería y de carros de combate. Es la única fábrica española de munición para carros y vende sobre todo a países europeos y de la OTAN. Es decir, una interrupción prolongada de su actividad tendría consecuencias graves en el actual proceso de rearme.
Siete siglos de pólvora. La web de la empresa presume de más de 700 años de historia, de fabricar pólvora desde 1324 “de forma ininterrumpida”. No es mentira, pero conviene precisar: es el primer uso documentado de pólvora en la península, cuando el sultán Ismail I tomó el castillo de Huéscar. El edificio de El Fargue, por su parte, se levantó en 1786, y el cronista Valladar ya señalaba en 1908 que no existían indicios de un origen oficial nazarí, sino únicamente de producción de pólvora en la Alhambra.
La sociedad actual, de hecho, se fundó en 2019. Pero si hacemos caso a los libros, el emplazamiento se eligió por la acequia de Aynadamar, cuya pendiente movía las ruedas de los molinos. En 1812, los franceses, al abandonar Granada, incendiaron esos mismos molinos. En 1897 salió de allí el primer lote de pólvora sin humo de España. Es más, en 1906 se estrenó un pasodoble en honor de la fábrica, compuesto para la Banda de Obreros Polvoristas, agrupación motivada por la visita del rey Alfonso XIII. Pero menos baile y más historia: en 1936, varios de sus obreros fueron ejecutados en represalia por varios bombardeos.
De Santa Bárbara a Praga. Muchas manos han pasado por la munición. En 1960, la escritura de la empresa estaba en manos y gestión estatal de Santa Bárbara. Se privatizó en 2001, cuando pasó a manos de General Dynamics, y en 2019 se constituyó FMG como sociedad independiente. El 21 de mayo de 2020 el dinero y las balas cambiaron de bando: se vendió a la eslovaca MSM Group, con autorización del Consejo de Ministros. MSM depende de Czechoslovak Group (CSG), propiedad de Michal Strnad, de 34 años, cuyo padre comenzó en los años noventa comerciando con material militar soviético.
Crecimiento desde Ucrania. Como era de esperar, la guerra de Ucrania viró por completo la situación de la fábrica. FMG pasó de 125 empleados en 2020 a triplicar su plantilla y en 2024 facturó unos 163 millones, un 126% más que el año anterior. Ese mismo año anunció una ampliación de unos 50 millones. La empresa estima que un 26% de todo su operativo se vende a Ucrania.
CSG ingresó 6.741 millones en 2025 y el 23 de enero debutó en Ámsterdam con una valoración de 25.000 millones, 3.800 recaudados y 2.550 para Strnad, la mayor salida a bolsa de defensa registrada hasta la fecha. Hace una semana, representantes de la empresa llevaron a la Exposición Anual de la Asociación del Ejército de los Estados Unidos sus mejores obuses y productos más avanzados. En el contexto del asesinato de su hijo, decía Julio Anguita “Malditas sean las guerras y los canallas que las hacen”.
La suspensión de la OTAN. El 31 de julio de 2025, la agencia de compras de la OTAN (NSPA) suspendió a FMG de sus licitaciones por “graves acusaciones” de prácticas sancionables. La medida se enmarca en una investigación sobre la propia agencia, con sospechas de sobornos y filtraciones, y alcanzó también a la israelí Elbit Systems, la segunda empresa privada con el mayor porfolio en sistemas PULS (lanzacohetes polivalentes) y tanques de guerra. Se hizo pública en marzo de 2026 y no figuraba en el folleto de la salida a bolsa.
CSG lo negó: sostiene que su auditoría no halló irregularidades, que la suspensión carece de fundamento y que FMG puede seguir vendiendo directamente a los países miembros. A las pocas semanas, un informe de corte bajista cuestionó la capacidad de producción del grupo, que también lo calificó de infundado. En mayo, las acciones se hundieron, aunque ya se han recuperado.
Como fuera, nada vincula estas polémicas con la explosión y lo importante es que ningún empleado haya sufrido daños severos. Quedan por esclarecer la causa, el alcance de daños materiales y balance definitivo, para estimar si la planta detendrá su actividad. La empresa aún no ha emitido un comunicado oficial.

articles.title: « Vous ne comprenez rien » : VLC chiffre à 1 million d'euros par an la nouvelle taxe sur le Gigaoctet — Frandroid
articles.text:
VLC, le lecteur vidéo français qui a franchi le cap des 7 milliards de téléchargements, s’invite dans le débat sur le budget 2027. Ce vendredi 30 octobre, VideoLAN, l’association loi 1901 qui développe et distribue gratuitement VLC, a affirmé sur X que la nouvelle taxe au gigaoctet lui coûterait plus d’un million d’euros par an.
Elle interpelle directement Laurent Lhardit, le député socialiste qui a porté le texte, et se demande si lui et ses collègues ne sont pas « probablement les politiciens les plus ignorants sur Terre ». Comme nous l’expliquions lors du vote, l’amendement adopté le même jour fait payer 5,5 centimes par gigaoctet aux entreprises qui envoient des données vers les abonnés français.
Pourquoi une association sans but lucratif se sent-elle visée ? Le texte de l’amendement n° I-1358 ne prévoit aucune exemption, ni pour les associations ni pour les logiciels libres, et aucun seuil minimum. Il vise tout « fournisseur de contenu » que les fournisseurs d’accès identifient. Or VLC envoie beaucoup de données vers la France : chaque téléchargement compte dans la base de calcul de la taxe, tout comme chaque mise à jour publiée pour corriger une faille de sécurité.
À 5,5 centimes le gigaoctet, un million d’euros correspond à un peu plus de 18 millions de gigaoctets par an, ce que VLC estime envoyer chaque année.
Une taxe sur les revenus et non les profits
Laurent Lhardit a répondu sur X. Pour le député du groupe Socialistes et apparentés, « VideoLAN raconte n’importe quoi » : la taxe est plafonnée et ne s’appliquerait pas du tout à l’association, qu’il invite à « lire l’amendement avant de suivre la meute ».
Le plafond existe bel et bien. Le texte limite la taxe à 15 % du chiffre d’affaires réalisé en France ou à 2 % du chiffre d’affaires total. Le tweet du député a été marqué d’une note de communauté des utilisateurs de X qui rappelle qu’aucune exemption ne protège VideoLAN ni les associations.
VideoLAN a répliqué dans un second message, où l’association accuse l’élu de confondre revenu et profit, c’est-à-dire ce qu’une structure encaisse et ce qui lui reste une fois ses dépenses payées. L’association a beau être à but non lucratif, elle perçoit tout de même des revenus.
Pour une association qui ne fait pas de bénéfice, prélever 15 % des recettes revient à retirer 15 % de son budget. VideoLAN reproche aussi au député de ne rien comprendre au non-lucratif, aux modèles économiques du numérique, à la sécurité et aux mises à jour.
L’association s’en prend enfin à son raisonnement sur Facebook et Instagram, des services gratuits qu’il jugerait à tort non concernés. Elle se moque aussi de la « souveraineté technologique » que revendiquent les défenseurs de la taxe, alors que VLC est l’un des rares logiciels libres français connus dans le monde entier.
D’autres projets gratuits dans le même cas ?
Rien dans l’amendement ne distingue VLC des autres services gratuits qui envoient beaucoup de données vers la France. La Wikimedia Foundation, l’organisation à but non lucratif qui héberge Wikipédia, pourrait entrer dans la même définition.
Ce serait aussi le cas des distributions Linux comme Debian, dont les serveurs diffusent des mises à jour tous les jours, et des éditeurs de logiciels libres qui mettent à jour leurs programmes automatiquement.
Le texte prévoit même que si un émetteur passe par un réseau de diffusion de contenus, c’est le volume sorti de ce réseau qui est compté. L’exposé de l’amendement, lui, ne cite que Google, Meta, Amazon, Netflix et Akamai, qui représentent selon lui la moitié du trafic mesuré par l’Arcep. Il justifie le plafond par le cas de la vidéo à la demande et du jeu vidéo, qui envoient beaucoup de données pour chaque euro de chiffre d’affaires.
Pour l’instant, la taxe n’est pas en vigueur. Les députés doivent encore voter l’ensemble de la partie recettes du budget 2027 avant son passage au Sénat. Le gouvernement, opposé à la mesure, peut aussi l’écarter s’il utilise le 49.3. Si elle passe toutes ces étapes, un décret devra encore fixer comment mesurer les flux de chaque émetteur.

articles.title: Una pareja con cuatro hijos construye una casa de 232 m² en el desierto: usaron más de 360 toneladas de tierra
articles.text:
Después de pasar cinco años recorriendo Estados Unidos en caravana, Jonathan y Ashley Longnecker decidieron instalarse en el desierto de Arizona con sus cuatro hijos y levantar allí su propia casa utilizando sobre todo tierra. La vivienda tendrá 232 metros cuadrados y, en una de las fases de la obra, ya se habían empleado en ella más de 360 toneladas de tierra. Además, también tienen la ambiciosa la idea de que funcione sin las conexiones tradicionales de agua y electricidad.
De la caravana al desierto. Según explica la propia familia en la web de su proyecto, llamado Tiny Shiny Home, fueron esos años de viajes a tiempo completo los que los llevaron a buscar algo diferente, y acabaron comprando un terreno sin urbanizar de unas 4,45 hectáreas. Ese terreno está en el condado de Cochise, en el sureste de Arizona. Allí están construyendo la Hyperadobe Roundhouse, una casa formada por círculos cuyo avance van están documentando paso a paso con fotos y muchos vídeos.
Tierra metida en mallas. La técnica que da nombre a la casa es el hyperadobe, que consiste en rellenar largos tubos de malla con tierra húmeda y apisonarla capa a capa hasta formar muros resistentes, según detalla la guía que han publicado los Longnecker. Vamos, que el ladrillo se sustituye por tierra apisonada, a ser posible la del propio terreno.
Con este método los muros alcanzan unos 40 centímetros de grosor, según recoge El Imparcial en su reportaje sobre la casa. Y cuando completaron la vigésima hilada de sacos, la familia contabilizaba 400 toneladas estadounidenses de tierra, que equivalen a unas 363 toneladas métricas.
Cuatro círculos unidos. La vivienda está formada por cuatro círculos de diferentes tamaños conectados mediante muros rectos, siempre según el mismo diario mexicano. ¿Y por qué tanta curva? Pues porque, como explican los Longnecker en esa misma guía, los muros circulares son de por sí más resistentes que los rectos, ya que la propia forma estabiliza la pared frente a la gravedad.
Y antes de meterse con la casa practicaron con construcciones más pequeñas, como una oficina y un gallinero, para ir haciéndose con el método, algo que cuentan tanto en su guía como en el reportaje de faircompanies.
Agua de lluvia y sol. El proyecto contempla recoger el agua de lluvia a través del tejado y llevarla hasta un depósito con capacidad para unos 114.000 litros, desde donde una bomba la filtrará y la distribuirá por la casa, de nuevo según El Imparcial. Y la electricidad tampoco llegará de la red, porque está prevista la instalación de paneles solares y baterías para generarla y almacenarla.
A principios de octubre de 2026 la obra seguía avanzando, como muestra el diario de construcción del tejado que publica la familia, y su objetivo es demostrar que se puede levantar una vivienda con materiales del entorno y sin depender de los servicios convencionales.

articles.title: Fresh WordPress Vulnerability in Attackers’ Crosshairs
articles.text:
Threat actors started exploiting a new high-severity WordPress vulnerability within hours of patches rolling out, Defiant warns.
Patched on October 28 in WordPress 7.1.4, the security defect impacts the WordPress update process and can be exploited for remote code execution.
According to Defiant, it is a race condition in WordPress’s Core update process that can be exploited without authentication. The attack complexity, however, is high. No CVE identifier has been assigned to the vulnerability yet.
The weakness stems from predictable, web-accessible staging paths during the upgrades. New files are unpacked into a predictable directory that is accessible from the web on many servers.
“The attacker needs a full-package update containing the installer files, public web and PHP access to the staging tree, a predictable or discovered staging path, and enough time to complete the attack before WordPress cleans up the temporary files,” Defiant explains.
According to the web security firm, threat actors are already attempting to exploit the vulnerability, polling the vulnerable paths repeatedly in their attempts to hit the seconds-long exploitability window.
While an attacker does not need an account on the site to exploit the flaw, they do need “to hit a very narrow window while WordPress is unpacking a complete Core update,” Defiant says.
To address the security bug, WordPress now randomizes the staging directory, adds an index guard, and prevents the unsafe promotion of staged configuration data.
“Wordfence telemetry shows that threat actors are already actively attempting to exploit the vulnerability. The first match for our new firewall rule arrived nine minutes after deployment. During the first 21 hours, we recorded more than 18,500 requests targeting staged setup-config.php installer paths,” Defiant says.
Wordfence has not reported successful compromises.
Fixes for the vulnerability were included in WordPress 7.1.4 and backported to branches through WordPress 4.7.
WordPress 7.1.4 includes patches for 22 security defects, including several XSS flaws, interactivity API issues, an unauthenticated information disclosure bug, and an authorization weakness, and also updates the bundled root certificates to reflect the recent eMudhra revocation.

articles.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
articles.text:
People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science
- Summary:
- Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates. The findings differ from clinical trial results and highlight how AI could help identify potential drug safety signals that warrant further investigation.
- Share:
An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting users willing to obtain unapproved versions online. Now, scientists are using artificial intelligence to investigate their experiences, uncovering unexpected symptom reports that differ from those documented in clinical trials.
The drug, retatrutide, belongs to a new generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight. Although it remains under investigation and is not approved for use, people are purchasing unapproved formulations that are not intended for human consumption and discussing their experiences on internet forums.
Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts. Their study, published in JAMA Network Open, provides the first systematic examination of potential side effects reported by people claiming to use unapproved retatrutide.
One finding stood out. Among users whose reported symptoms could be classified, increased appetite was the most common complaint. That was particularly unexpected because retatrutide is designed to suppress hunger, and its Phase 2 clinical trials primarily identified digestive problems as the most frequent side effects.
AI Uncovers Unexpected Weight-Loss Drug Reports
"Our goal is to identify hypotheses in online conversations that we could test. AI helps us find recurring patterns in people's self-reports, including experiences that may be missed by conventional drug-safety monitoring," says Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Research Associate Professor in Computer and Information Science (CIS), Director of Penn's Computational Social Listening Lab and senior author of the study.
However, the researchers emphasize that the findings should not be interpreted as proof of previously unknown side effects. Reddit users represent a very different population from clinical trial participants, and their accounts cannot establish whether the drug caused the symptoms they described.
There is also considerable uncertainty about what these individuals are actually taking. Products sold outside regulated medical channels may differ from the genuine experimental medication in their ingredients, purity, and dosage.
"We can't say that retatrutide is causing these symptoms, or even that Reddit users are actually taking genuine retatrutide, since the drug is not legally available, and gray market formulations vary," says Lyle Ungar, Professor in CIS and a co-author of the study.
Rather than confirming new risks, the research offers scientists an opportunity to identify questions that warrant more rigorous investigation.
"This is the first glimpse into the experiences of a population that is otherwise outside conventional drug safety monitoring because they are taking unapproved versions of a drug that has yet to finish clinical trials," says Neil Sehgal, the study's first author and a doctoral student in CIS.
How Researchers Analyzed 150,000 Reddit Posts
The project builds on previous research by the University of Pennsylvania team. In that earlier investigation, scientists used large language models (LLMs), the type of artificial intelligence that powers many modern chatbots, to examine more than 400,000 Reddit posts discussing semaglutide and tirzepatide.
That analysis revealed reports of possible side effects, including menstrual irregularities, that may not have been fully documented in clinical trials or official drug safety records.
"We wanted to apply the same methodology to gray-market retatrutide," says Sehgal.
Retatrutide is particularly interesting because it works differently from existing GLP-1 medications. Semaglutide acts on one hormone receptor involved in blood sugar control and appetite regulation, while tirzepatide targets two. Retatrutide activates three receptors, potentially producing a different combination of effects throughout the body.
To investigate what people were experiencing, the researchers used AI to examine nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments. They identified approximately 14,000 users who claimed to have personally taken an unapproved version of retatrutide.
The AI systems then extracted descriptions of symptoms that users associated with the medication and translated those descriptions into standardized medical terminology. This allowed researchers to compare reports even when different people used different words to describe similar experiences.
After excluding expected effects such as weight loss and reduced appetite, the team identified 7,823 users who reported at least one symptom that could be medically classified.
"A researcher might be able to examine a few thousand Reddit posts by hand, but looking at nearly 150,000 would be an enormous undertaking," says Sehgal. "AI makes it possible to analyze these conversations at scale, identifying patterns in what people are sharing that would otherwise be difficult to recognize."
A Surprising Appetite Paradox Emerges
The most striking difference involved hunger.
In retatrutide's Phase 2 clinical trials (the drug is currently in Phase 3 trials, the final step before FDA approval), participants most commonly experienced gastrointestinal complaints, including nausea. These effects are familiar concerns with medications that influence appetite and digestion.
But among Reddit users who reported taking unapproved retatrutide, the pattern looked different. Increased appetite emerged as the most frequently described classifiable symptom, despite the substantial weight-loss effects demonstrated in clinical testing.
The researchers also compared the new findings with their earlier analysis of semaglutide and tirzepatide.
Compared with those earlier Reddit reports, discussions involving unapproved retatrutide contained proportionally more mentions of appetite-related changes, sleep disturbances, increased heart rate, and muscle-related symptoms. Reports of nausea and other digestive complaints were proportionally less common.
These differences could reflect how retatrutide interacts with the body. However, they could also result from differences between the groups of people discussing the medications, their other drug use, or the contents of the unapproved products.
"Retatrutide works differently from existing GLP-1 drugs, so it's possible that its effects on the body are different, too," says Jena Shaw Tronieri, Senior Research Investigator at Penn's Center for Weight and Eating Disorders and a co-author of the study.
"But the people discussing it on Reddit also may be different," she notes. "Users willing to obtain an unapproved medication on the gray market likely differ from other clinical populations. Some may be taking multiple experimental peptides, and we can't verify exactly what they're taking. We need more research to understand what, if anything, these differences in self-reported symptoms mean."
Can AI Detect Drug Safety Concerns Earlier?
Beyond the findings about retatrutide, the study demonstrates how AI could potentially improve the early detection of drug safety concerns.
Traditional monitoring systems depend heavily on clinical trials, reports submitted to regulators, and information collected by healthcare professionals. People obtaining experimental medications through unapproved channels may not be represented in those systems.
Social media offers another source of information, allowing researchers to identify recurring experiences that might otherwise escape attention. However, these reports must be independently investigated before they can be considered reliable evidence of a drug-related problem.
The Penn team has already seen an example of how this approach can help guide further research.
In their previous investigation of semaglutide and tirzepatide, researchers identified online reports of menstrual irregularities. Those findings subsequently encouraged another scientific team to examine similar symptoms using the FDA's database of reported adverse drug events.
The follow-up study, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology, also detected disproportionate reports of certain menstrual changes. Although those findings did not establish causation, they provided additional reasons to investigate the potential connection.
The researchers hope their retatrutide findings will lead to similar independent studies, particularly as the drug advances through clinical development.
"That's what we hope will happen with this study," says Sehgal. "Other researchers can take what we find on Reddit and look for the same patterns in other datasets, using entirely different methods. Whether those signals hold up or not, the goal is to build a better understanding of what people are actually experiencing."
The research was conducted through the University of Pennsylvania's School of Engineering and Applied Science and Perelman School of Medicine. Benjamin Rader of Boston Children's Hospital also contributed as a co-author. Funding was provided in part by the University of Pennsylvania's Penn Medical Communication Research Institute. Tronieri disclosed receiving an investigator-initiated grant from Novo Nordisk on behalf of the University of Pennsylvania, along with consulting fees from Currax Pharmaceuticals, LLC. No conflicts of interest were reported by the other authors.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Neil K. R. Sehgal, Jena Shaw Tronieri, Benjamin Rader, Lyle Ungar, Sharath Chandra Guntuku. Self-Reported Adverse Effects Among Social Media Users Taking Nonapproved Retatrutide. JAMA Network Open, 2026; 9 (10): e2638929 DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.38929

articles.title: CISA says max severity GitLab flaw now exploited in the wild
articles.text:
Attackers have started exploiting a maximum-severity GitLab vulnerability patched earlier this month, according to the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).
Tracked as CVE-2026-97229, this critical security flaw was discovered by a security researcher using the 'joaxcar' handle in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses, compiles, and evaluates regular expressions in pipeline configuration files.
CVE-2026-97229 stems from an integer overflow weakness and could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on targeted instances via a maliciously crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient expression validation.
"GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation," it said.
GitLab addressed the security issue in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8 and urged admins to patch their servers immediately.
The company has also released threat detections to support customers with self-managed instances after detecting exploitation attempts.
On Thursday, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed active exploitation and added CVE-2026-97229 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog. CISA also ordered federal agencies to secure their servers by Sunday, as mandated by Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
Although BOD 26-04 targets only federal agencies, the cybersecurity agency encouraged all security teams, including those in the private sector, to prioritize patching this flaw to protect their networks against ongoing attacks.
Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver tracks nearly 2,800 Internet-exposed GitLab Community Edition instances, but it doesn't say how many have already been secured against attacks.
CVE-2026-97229 is the latest in a string of security issues GitLab has addressed since the start of the year. In January, it patched a high-severity two-factor authentication bypass (CVE-2026-0723) that lets attackers who know the target's account ID circumvent two-factor authentication.
Earlier this month, it also fixed a maximum-severity Regular Expression Compiler flaw (CVE-2026-110264) that could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on targeted instances.
Almost two weeks later, GitLab addressed another maximum-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-85706) in the repository commits API that can be abused to read sensitive data, such as credentials and other secrets, from vulnerable servers.
One day later, CISA added CVE-2026-85706 to its list of actively exploited flaws after cybersecurity firm watchTowr reported that attackers had already begun scanning the Internet for unpatched GitLab servers.
CISA has tagged six GitLab vulnerabilities as exploited in the wild since November 2021, including two (tracked as CVE-2021-22175 and CVE-2021-39935) in February this year.
GitLab's DevSecOps platform is used by over 50% of Fortune 100 companies and has more than 70 million registered users worldwide.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked

articles.title: Why the MacBook Neo is my Laptop of the Year award winner — how many new devices instantly changed the industry around them this year?
articles.text:
We've crowned our Laptop of the Year, and there really was only one choice: the Apple MacBook Neo
A real trendsetter
I reviewed the MacBook Neo way back in March, and even then I knew there was very little chance that I'd be giving our Laptop of the Year award to any other device at the TechRadar Product of the Year 2026 Awards.
It's not necessarily the best choice for everyone — many far more powerful laptops have been released this year, and if you want to play PC games on your laptop don't even think of buying the Neo — but what Apple did with the MacBook Neo is pretty incredible, and it set the tone for a lot of other laptops that have come out this year.
Apple has always been seen as a premium brand, offering expensive devices that (usually, but not always) justify their price tags with superior build quality, and the kind of lifespans that owners of Windows laptops, who feel they have to upgrade every five years, can only dream of.
With the MacBook Neo, however, Apple has produced a (relatively) cheap laptop that manages to keep a lot of what we love about Apple's more expensive MacBooks, while making it affordable for more people.
The timing couldn't have been better, as a global cost-of-living crisis has meant that more people are struggling to afford day-to-day essentials, let alone 'luxury' purchases like laptops. At a time when a lot tech is also increasing in price because of the RAM crisis, it was very welcome to see a company like Apple release a relatively inexpensive new device.
Before the Neo's announcement, rumors had been swirling that Apple was planning on announcing a cheaper MacBook, but I don't think any of us were expecting the earthquake of its $599 / £599 / AU$1,049 starting price.
I say 'earthquake' because not only was it a lot cheaper than expected, it changed the landscape of the laptop market, shaking Apple's competitors, and leaving them scrambling to come up with a response.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
And respond they did, with the likes of Dell and Acer releasing laptops at a similar price point that were explicitly pitched as competitors to the MacBook Neo when I discussed them with the makers.
A victim of its own success?
The fact that the MacBook Neo has had such an influence on the laptop market is one of the key reasons why I've picked it as TechRadar's Laptop of the Year. The likes of the Dell XPS 13 (2026) and Acer Swift Air 14 have made affordable Windows 11 laptops worth buying again, and the higher price of the new Googlebook laptops have a more difficult time justifying their price tags when the MacBook Neo, and the laptops it inspired, offer such good value.
In fact, you could almost argue that the MacBook Neo proved a bit too successful in inspiring its competitors, especially given that, a few months after launch, Apple increased the price of the MacBook Neo by $100 / £100. Not only did this make the MacBook Neo less groundbreaking value (and less of an 'instant recommendation' when people asked me which laptop they should buy), but its competitors seem to have mostly held steady with their initial pricing.
All of a sudden, Apple appeared to have inspired its competitors to make rival products that were cheaper than the MacBook Neo. Whoops.
Despite that price bump, the MacBook Neo remains an excellent laptop that continues to offer plenty of value. If you're looking for a dependable, well-built laptop for day-to-day tasks that doesn't cost a fortune, it's still one of the best laptops you can buy — and it remains the cheapest way to get into the Mac ecosystem.
The MacBook Neo proved that, at a time when hardware prices appear to be rising inexorably, it's still possible to make an impressive, affordable device, without making too many sacrifices — and that's exactly what we need in 2026.

And of course you can also follow TechRadar on TikTok for news, reviews, unboxings in video form, and get regular updates from us on WhatsApp too.
Matt is TechRadar's Managing Editor for Core Tech, looking after computing and mobile technology. Having written for a number of publications such as PC Plus, PC Format, T3 and Linux Format, there's no aspect of technology that Matt isn't passionate about, especially computing and PC gaming. He’s personally reviewed and used most of the laptops in our best laptops guide - and since joining TechRadar in 2014, he's reviewed over 250 laptops and computing accessories personally.
